# Rebel 0.1.0: every package, for a program that uses it

Rebel is the library a Heroes program takes or leaves, never the language's own. This index names every face of its version 0.1.0, the modules a program names with `use <rebel>/<face>`: 190 faces in 10 layers, with every one of their 6,150 functions, 1,064 records, 414 variants and 1,607 constants. Every word of it is read from what `heroes doc` prints of each face, so a name it gives is one the face declares, and a call it shows is one the checker accepts: write no name it does not give.

## How to take Rebel

A program names a package of Rebel through its catalogue, `heroes.toml`, which stands beside the file it compiles and which `heroes add` writes, run in the program's folder: nobody types a catalogue. A program takes Rebel today from a clone of its repository, read where it stands:

    heroes add --path <clone>/rebel/library/0.1.0/files --as rebel
    heroes add rebel/csv

No index publishes Rebel yet, so `heroes add rebel` by its name, which asks an index, waits for one that does; a `path` entry is read where it stands, and nothing verifies it.

`heroes add rebel/<face>` adds a face to the entry's `packages` line, which names every face the program uses: a `use` of a face the line does not name is refused, and an entry fetched from an index places the faces it names and the modules they use, nothing else. A module then writes `use <rebel>/csv` and calls the face by the last part of its path: `csv.parse(text)`.

## How to read this index

- The faces stand by layer, from 0: a package uses only packages of a lower layer (`rebel/examples/README.md` § A1). The list below names each with its purpose, the first sentence of its module comment; then each face has a section of its own, headed `### <face>`, in the same order.
- A section opens with the face's layer, the `use` line that names it, and its reference page, which shows every declaration whole: each parameter, its edges and its examples. `heroes doc <rebel>/<face>`, run in a program's folder, prints the same text.
- Then each declaration of the face, in the order the face writes it, on one line:
  - a function: its signature as `heroes doc` prints it, the call a program writes (each argument its parameter's name, with a label exactly where the call needs one, `@` where the function changes the caller's place), the first sentence of its comment, and the codes its comment names from its `Fails` on, or, where it names none, its `Fails` sentence whole, a failure handed on from what it calls;
  - a record: its fields in their declared order, written as the call that builds one, `record Name(field: type, ...)`; where a field's type is a private module's (`stream.State`), only the face's functions build it, as its comment says;
  - a variant: its cases as a program writes them, `variant Name = .case | .case(field: type)`;
  - a constant: its declaration, then its value where it is written on one line; a failure code is one of them.
- A type another face declares is written qualified, `io.Stream`, as the face writes it.
- A failure's code is one word of a closed vocabulary, the same in every package (`rebel/examples/README.md` § A4): `not_found`, `file_not_found`, `exists`, `permission`, `not_a_directory`, `is_a_directory`, `not_empty`, `invalid`, `does_not_fit`, `not_text`, `closed`, `timeout`, `stopped`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`.

## The faces by layer

### Layer 0

- [`unicode`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/): What a character is: its code point, its classes, its case, and how UTF-8 and UTF-16 write it.
- [`math`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/): The functions of mathematics over `f64`, and the integer helpers that answer where the language's own arithmetic aborts.
- [`lists`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/lists/): What the built-ins do not do for a `[T]`: its ends, its parts, a list built or edited, a value searched for, a stable sort by an order, a sorted list searched by halving, the smallest or largest few by an order, and the arrangements of its elements.
- [`maps`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/maps/): What the built-ins do not do for a `{K: V}`: its values, a map built from lists, keys removed, kept and put in an order, two maps merged, the elements of a list counted and grouped.
- [`numbers`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/numbers/): A number read from text and written as text: integers of every width and base, floats in decimal and hexadecimal, booleans, sizes in bytes written for people, and the width, sign and grouping of a number's text.
- [`path`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/path/): A path as text, by POSIX's rules and by Windows', touching no disk: what a path's parts are, where it begins, how two paths stand to each other, and a path cleaned, joined or changed, a path matched against a pattern, and whether gitignore files ignore a path.
- [`os`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/os/): The process's world: its environment, its working folder, the folders the system keeps for a program's data, state, cache, settings and sockets, who it runs as and on what machine, the machine's processes listed, users and groups found and the user changed, the signals it counts, a URL or a file handed to the application the user's system keeps for it, and a file shown selected in the system's file manager.
- [`hash`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/hash/): Checksums and fast hashes that are not cryptographic, computed over bytes or over text, all at once or in steps: CRC-32 by the IEEE polynomial, by Castagnoli's or by one of the caller's; CRC-64 by ISO's polynomial, by ECMA's or by one of the caller's; Adler-32; FNV-1 and FNV-1a in 32 and 64 bits; and xxHash's XXH32 and XXH64, with a seed, the checksums of LZ4's and Zstandard's frames.
- [`sets`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sets/): Sets of values, kept in a `{K: bool}`: the language has no set type, and a map's keys are already distinct and found by hashing, so a set is a map whose keys are its elements, each under `true`.
- [`errors`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/errors/): Failures told well: words added to a failure as it travels up, its code kept; several failures joined into one; a failure told to a person, in one line or as an indented chain; and one dropped on purpose where it cannot matter.
- [`threads`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/threads/): A function run on another thread and waited for, through the language's own `spawn` and `t.wait()` (spec § 11), under names of this package's own and with a pool that bounds how many run at once.
- [`containers/ordered`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/ordered/): An ordered map and an ordered set: keys kept in the order a function of the program gives, each found, added and taken out at a cost of the logarithm of the size, with the keys at or around a bound, a range walked in order, and the key of a rank and the rank of a key.
- [`containers/deque`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/deque/): A double-ended queue: items put in and taken out at either end in constant time over many calls, read and written by their place from the front, and, where it is bounded, the oldest dropped as new ones come.
- [`containers/bits`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/bits/): A set of bits of a fixed size: bits set, cleared and turned over one at a time or a run at a time, counted, combined with another set, scanned for the next set or clear one, and read and written as places, bytes, words or text.
- [`containers/cache`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/cache/): A cache of a capacity that forgets the entry used least recently to make room and, where it has a time to live, every entry written longer ago than that.
- [`containers/indexed`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/indexed/): A map that keeps its keys in the order they were first put, each at a position from 0, as Rust's indexmap and Python's `dict` do: an entry found by its key or by its position, taken out by swapping the last one in or by shifting the rest, moved, swapped and sorted.
- [`containers/heap`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/heap/): A heap, the priority queue: a plain `[T]` the program owns, kept so that its element at 0 is one nothing goes before by the program's order, an element going in or coming out at a cost of the logarithm of the length.
- [`graphs`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/graphs/): The orders and the paths of a graph: a topological order, all at once or handed out in stages, the cycle that forbids one, the strongly connected components, the nodes a node reaches, and the paths of least weight.
- [`qr`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/qr/): QR codes made by ISO/IEC 18004: a text or bytes written in numeric, alphanumeric, byte and kanji segments, every version from 1 to 40 and every level of error correction, the mask chosen by the standard's penalty rules, and the symbol written as a matrix of modules, as SVG text, as text for a terminal, or as pixels a program hands to `image` and `image/png`.
- [`containers/trie`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/trie/): A prefix tree of texts: keys found, added and taken out at a cost of their length whatever the number held, with what a trie alone answers quickly: whether some key begins with a text, every key that does in byte order and how many, and the longest or the shortest key that begins a text, which is what a router asks of a path and a tokenizer of the text still to read.
- [`containers/disjoint`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/containers/disjoint/): Union-find: elements gathered into sets that only ever merge, each set answered by one element that stands for it, so that whether two elements stand in one set is known at once.

### Layer 1

- [`unicode/normalize`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/normalize/): A text put in one of Unicode's four normal forms, so that two texts that write the same characters in different code points compare equal: "é" as one character and "e" followed by a combining acute accent are the same text in NFC and in NFD.
- [`unicode/segment`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/segment/): A text cut where Unicode says its parts end: into graphemes, what a reader sees as one character (UAX #29); into words and sentences (UAX #29); at the places a line may break (UAX #14).
- [`unicode/names`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/names/): What the Unicode Character Database tells of a character beyond its class and its case: its name and the character a name gives, its aliases, its script and the scripts it is used with, its block, the properties Unicode lists by name, the number it writes and its direction in text written right to left.
- [`strings`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/strings/): Text searched, cut, trimmed, replaced, padded, indented and cased.
- [`bytes`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/bytes/): A `[u8]` searched, cut, joined and compared, and bytes written as text and read back from it: as UTF-8, as hexadecimal, as base 32 and as base 64.
- [`regex`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/regex/): A regular expression compiled once and matched in time linear in the text, for every pattern: the pattern becomes an automaton, and a search runs the automaton over the text with every state at once and never goes back.
- [`random`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/random/): Numbers drawn at random from a seeded generator the caller holds: whole numbers below a bound or in a range without bias, floats in [0, 1), bytes, a list shuffled, an element chosen, a sample drawn without replacement, a choice by weights, and numbers drawn from a distribution: uniform, normal, lognormal, exponential, gamma, beta, von Mises, Pareto, Weibull, triangular, binomial and Zipf's; and from the system's generator for keys, a number below a bound, an element chosen, and a token written as text.
- [`stats`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/stats/): The statistics of a list of floats: means, medians, modes, spread, quantiles, and the covariance, correlation and fitted line of two lists.
- [`math/complex`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/complex/): Complex numbers, `re + im i`, and their functions as C11's Annex G computes them: arithmetic, the size and the angle, the polar form, the exponential, the logarithms and the powers, and the circular and hyperbolic functions with their inverses, each branch cut on an axis.
- [`math/linear`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/linear/): Vectors of two, three and four floats, matrices of two, three and four columns, quaternions, and the transforms of graphics built from them: the geometry of games and of the screen, in `f64`, every value a copy.
- [`math/sparse`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/sparse/): Matrices of any size of `f64` whose entries are mostly zero, held as compressed sparse rows (CSR): built from triplets, read, transposed, multiplied by a vector, their rows summed and normalized, and the steady states two power iterations find on them, a Markov chain's and PageRank's.
- [`image`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/): Images in memory: a grid of pixels of one format, made, read and written pixel by pixel, converted between formats, cut, scaled, turned, combined, drawn on, measured, and reduced to a palette.

### Layer 2

- [`io`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/io/): The stream: the one handle a program reads and writes through, whatever stands behind it (a file, a pipe, a terminal, the process's own input and outputs, a child's ends, a socket), and the buffered reader over one that reads lines, characters and bytes up to a byte.
- [`json`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/json/): JSON read and written: the text of RFC 8259 read into a tree a program matches on, the tree written back as text, and the functions that read a value out of it.
- [`xml`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/xml/): XML read, walked, built and written: a text read by XML 1.0 (fifth edition) and Namespaces in XML 1.0 into a tree a program matches on, the tree walked by names, built by a program, and written back as text, or as the one text Canonical XML 1.0, 1.1 or Exclusive XML Canonicalization gives it, the text XML Signature digests (`xmldsig`).
- [`html`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/html/): HTML read as a browser reads it: any text, however broken, read into the tree a browser builds from it, by the WHATWG HTML Living Standard's tokenizer and tree construction (insertion modes, the adoption agency algorithm, foster parenting, implied end tags), as fetched from html.spec.whatwg.org on 2026-11-16.
- [`url`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/url/): A URL parsed, built and escaped, by RFC 3986 and touching no network: this module reads a text into the parts of a `Url`, writes the parts back, resolves a reference against a base, escapes and unescapes what a part holds, and reads a query as its keys and values in their order.
- [`crypto`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/crypto/): Cryptographic digests, the MACs and key derivations over them, password hashing, and the comparison of two byte lists in constant time: MD5, SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 (FIPS 180-4 and RFC 1321) and SHA3-224 to SHA3-512 (FIPS 202), all at once or in steps; SHAKE128, SHAKE256 and cSHAKE read to any length (FIPS 202, SP 800-185); BLAKE2b and BLAKE2s keyed or not (RFC 7693) and BLAKE3 in its three modes; HMAC (RFC 2104); HKDF (RFC 5869); PBKDF2 (RFC 8018) and scrypt (RFC 7914); Argon2 (RFC 9106) and bcrypt, with the PHC and modular crypt strings a password's hash is stored in; one-time passwords, HOTP (RFC 4226) and TOTP (RFC 6238), with the otpauth URI that hands their key to an authenticator app.
- [`big`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/big/): Numbers of any size, held exactly: integers, decimals and fractions, their arithmetic, and their text in any base.
- [`flags`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/flags/): The arguments of a program read against a declaration: options long and short, with a value and without, given once or many times, positionals, subcommands, defaults, and a help page made from the declaration itself.
- [`ini`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ini/): INI read and written: sections in brackets, each holding keys and their values, in the order they were written, as Python's `configparser` reads them.
- [`java_properties`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/java_properties/): Java's properties files read and written as `java.util.Properties` reads and writes them: Spring Boot's `application.properties`, a resource bundle, Gradle's and Maven's settings.
- [`semver`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/semver/): Versions by Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (semver.org), read, written and ordered, and ranges of versions as Cargo reads them: which versions a requirement such as `^1.2`, `~1.4.3` or `>=1.2, <1.5` admits, and the highest of a list it admits.
- [`diff`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/diff/): The differences of two lists: of lines, of words, of characters, of bytes or of any values, as an edit script a program walks, cut into hunks, and written in the unified and context formats of `diff -u` and `diff -c`; and how alike two lists are, as Python's `difflib` measures it.
- [`pem`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/pem/): PEM, the text that carries binary data between a `-----BEGIN <label>-----` line and a `-----END <label>-----` line, read and written by RFC 7468: certificates, keys, requests, any DER a program keeps as text.
- [`unicode/encodings`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/encodings/): Bytes in the encodings of the WHATWG Encoding Standard read as text and text written back as bytes, as a browser reads a page: the 40 encodings of the standard (UTF-8, UTF-16, the 28 single-byte ones from IBM866 to windows-1258, gb18030 and GBK, Big5 with Hong Kong's extensions, EUC-JP, ISO-2022-JP, Shift_JIS, EUC-KR, and the two of its own), every label it reads them by, its byte order marks, and its two error modes each way; and the encoding of bytes nobody declared, guessed with a confidence.
- [`keyring`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/keyring/): Secrets kept in the system's own keyring: a password, a token or a key stored under a service and an account, read back, replaced, removed, and the accounts of a service listed, so a program keeps no secret in a file of its own.
- [`printing`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/printing/): The system's printers: the printers this machine knows listed with their state, the papers each takes and what it can do, a PDF document submitted to one as a job with the settings a print dialog asks (copies, paper, orientation, sides, colour, pages, collation), the job's state and pages told while it runs and when it ends, waited for, and cancelled.
- [`scanner`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/scanner/): A configurable lexer: a text read into its tokens one after another, as Go's text/scanner reads one, each token with its kind, its text and its place, the byte offset, line and column where it begins and where it ends.
- [`property`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/property/): Property-based testing inside a `test` block: a property, a top-level function from a generated value to a `bool` or a `()?`, checked over many cases a generator makes from a seed, and the first case that fails it shrunk to a smallest one, which the report prints with the seed that reproduces the run.
- [`vectors`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/vectors/): Vectors of `f32` compared and searched: the dot product, the cosine, the euclidean and manhattan distances, a vector normalized, added or averaged, the nearest of a list found by exact search, and an HNSW index in memory that finds them fast, deterministic from its seed and saved as bytes.
- [`tokenizer`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tokenizer/): Text made tokens and tokens made text by byte-pair encoding, as OpenAI's tiktoken does it, so that a program counts what a model of OpenAI's reads before it sends it, keeps a text within a model's window, or reads back the tokens a model wrote.
- [`search`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/search/): Texts indexed in memory by their words and searched, the best first: an inverted index ranked by BM25 with the `k1` and `b` the program gives, and queries of words, of words required or refused, of phrases and of prefixes.
- [`http/suffixes`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/http/suffixes/): The Public Suffix List: which part of a domain name the public registers under, `co.uk` of `example.co.uk`, so that a cookie set for `co.uk` is refused and the registrable domain of a host is known.
- [`image/jpeg`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/jpeg/): JPEG read and written, by ITU-T T.81 and JFIF: baseline and progressive files of 8 bits a sample read, gray or colour, every sampling of the colour, with restart intervals; their EXIF orientation read; baseline files written at a quality the caller picks, with the tables of T.81's Annex K.
- [`image/gif`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/gif/): GIF read and written, by the GIF89a specification: every frame of an animation read with its palette, place, delay and disposal, interlaced or not; the frames laid one over another as a viewer shows them; an animation or a single image written with its palettes.
- [`image/bmp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/bmp/): BMP read and written: Windows' device-independent bitmaps of 1, 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32 bits a pixel, under every header from OS/2's core header to BITMAPV5HEADER, bottom up or top down, plain, with bit fields, or run-length coded (RLE8 and RLE4).
- [`image/netpbm`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/netpbm/): The netpbm formats read and written: PBM (P1, P4), PGM (P2, P5), PPM (P3, P6) and PAM (P7), plain or raw, of any maximum value from 1 to 65,535, comments anywhere the format allows them.
- [`image/colorspace`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/colorspace/): Colours in other spaces than red, green and blue: HSV and HLS (a colour picker's hue, how much of it and how bright), CMYK (print's inks, as Go's `color.RGBToCMYK` computes them), YCbCr (JPEG's, JFIF's equations) and YIQ (NTSC's), each way for one colour, and a whole image split into the planes of a space and put together again.
- [`image/vector`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/vector/): Paths of lines and curves drawn into an image: a path built from moves, lines, quadratic and cubic curves and arcs, or read from SVG's path data, moved by an affine matrix, filled under the non-zero or the even-odd rule, stroked with a width, caps, joins and dashes, and a region painted from a point.
- [`image/webp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/webp/): WebP read and written: still pictures and animations, lossless and lossy, with the ICC profile, EXIF and XMP chunks of the extended format.
- [`url/idna`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/url/idna/): Host names between Unicode and ASCII by IDNA: UTS #46's processing for Unicode 17.0.0 (its mapping table, its validity criteria, RFC 5892's ContextJ rules and RFC 5893's bidi rule), ToASCII and ToUnicode over it, and Punycode (RFC 3492) on its own.
- [`i18n`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/): A program spoken in its reader's language: the language a reader asked for named and matched (BCP 47 tags), the languages and the formats the person chose in the system's settings, the plural rules of every language CLDR knows, and the translations of a program's messages read from gettext's `.po` and `.mo` files and looked up with their context and plural forms.
- [`font`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/font/): TrueType and OpenType fonts read: the glyph a character has, a glyph's advance, its bounds and its outline as a path, a font's names and metrics, the width of a text, and a TrueType font cut down to the glyphs a document uses (a PDF embeds such a subset).

### Layer 3

- [`time`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/time/): Time as a program counts it: an instant, a duration, the calendar, the text of a time, sleeping, and time zones.
- [`net`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/net/): The network: TCP connections and listeners, UDP datagrams, names looked up, an echo asked by ICMP (`ping`), and addresses as values.
- [`yaml`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/yaml/): YAML read and written: a YAML 1.2 stream read into the tree `json` holds, `json.Value`, and a value written back as a document in block style.
- [`cbor`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/cbor/): CBOR, the Concise Binary Object Representation of RFC 8949: bytes decoded into a value a program matches on, and a value encoded as bytes, in the deterministic encoding of its section 4.2 unless the program asks for another key order.
- [`term`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/term/): The terminal: colours and styles that fall back to plain text, the cursor and the screen, one key read as it is pressed, a secret read with nothing echoed, a line read with editing and a history, a progress bar and a spinner drawn on a stream, and tables and columns of text aligned by the cells their characters take.
- [`csv`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/csv/): Comma-separated values read and written by RFC 4180: a text or a stream of rows, each row fields between separators, a field holding a separator, a quote or a line end written inside quotes with its quotes doubled.
- [`image/text`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/text/): Text drawn into an image: a line set in a font, its glyph outlines filled anti-aliased through `image/vector`, kerned and spaced as asked, measured before it is drawn, cut into lines no wider than a width and aligned.
- [`compress`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/): DEFLATE compressed and decompressed, bare (RFC 1951) or wrapped as zlib (RFC 1950) or gzip (RFC 1952) with their checksums: all at once over a `[u8]`, piece by piece in memory, or through an `io.Stream`.
- [`template`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/template/): Text made from a template and a value: a template is text holding actions between `{{` and `}}`, which write the value's parts, choose, loop and run another template, and its HTML mode escapes every value by the place it stands in the page, as Go's `html/template` does.
- [`markdown`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/markdown/): Markdown read as CommonMark 0.31.2 reads it, every rule of the specification, with GFM's tables, strikethrough, extended autolinks and task list items; the document a tree of nodes a program walks and changes; and HTML written from it as the specification's reference renderer writes it, so that each of the specification's 652 examples comes out byte for byte.
- [`html/sanitize`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/html/sanitize/): HTML from outside cleaned by an allow-list policy: a fragment someone the page does not trust wrote is read as a browser reads it, by `html`, every element, attribute, URL and style property the policy does not allow is taken out, and the tree is written back, so that the answer can stand inside an element of the page and run nothing.
- [`json/schema`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/json/schema/): JSON Schema validation, in the dialects of 2020-12 and of draft 7: a schema compiled once from a `json.Value`, its references resolved, and any number of instances validated against it, each error with its place in the instance and in the schema.
- [`json/patch`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/json/patch/): JSON Patch (RFC 6902) and JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386): a list of changes to a `json.Value` held as values, read and written as JSON, applied whole or not at all, and made from two values; and a merge patch, a value shaped like the document it changes, applied and made.
- [`json/path`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/json/path/): JSONPath as RFC 9535 defines it: a query read once, checked against the RFC's grammar and its rules of types, and run against a `json.Value` to select the values it names, each with its place as a normalized path and as a JSON pointer; and the places a query selects given new values.
- [`json/jq`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/json/jq/): The jq language run over a `json.Value`: a filter read once and run against any number of values, each run answering every value the filter outputs.
- [`math/matrix`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/matrix/): Dense matrices of any size: of `f64`, multiplied, solved, inverted and decomposed by the published algorithms of floating point (LU with partial pivoting, Householder QR, Cholesky, the Jacobi methods for a symmetric matrix's eigenvalues and for singular values, least squares by QR); and of `big`'s fractions, eliminated exactly by Gauss-Jordan (solve, inverse, determinant, rank, reduced row echelon form), so a result a program must trust to the last digit carries no rounding at all.
- [`serial`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/serial/): Serial ports: the ports this machine has, a port opened as an `io.Stream` that `io`'s functions read and write, its settings (speed, size of a character, parity, stop bits, flow control) set and read back, its timeouts, its modem lines, a break sent, its buffers emptied or waited for, and a pseudo-terminal that stands for a port where there is no hardware.
- [`i18n/numbers`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/numbers/): Numbers written and read as a language writes them: "1.234,5" in German and "1,234.5" in English, percentages, amounts of money with their currency's symbol and digits, compact forms ("1.2K", "1,2 Mio."), and CLDR's number patterns, from the data of CLDR release `i18n.CLDR_VERSION` for every locale it holds.
- [`i18n/collate`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/collate/): Texts ordered as a language orders them, by the Unicode Collation Algorithm (UTS #10) over CLDR's root collation and the tailorings CLDR gives the languages: "ä" after "z" in Swedish and beside "a" in German, "ch" after "h" in Czech, accents ignored or weighed, case first or last, numbers by their value.
- [`i18n/locales`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/locales/): What CLDR knows of the languages a tag names: the script and region a language is most likely written in (`en` is `en-Latn-US`, `zh-TW` is `zh-Hant-TW`), and the tags old names are replaced by (`iw` is `he`, `sh` is `sr-Latn`).
- [`i18n/names`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/names/): Languages, scripts, regions and whole locales named in words in a language, as a language menu or a settings window lists them: German is "German" in English, "Deutsch" in German and "tedesco" in Italian; `en-GB` is "British English" or "English (United Kingdom)".
- [`crypto/seal`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/crypto/seal/): Authenticated encryption by the system's own cryptography: a text sealed under a secret key, so that nobody without the key reads it and nobody changes a byte of it, or of the associated data beside it, unseen.
- [`crypto/keypairs`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/crypto/keypairs/): Key pairs, signatures, key agreement and encryption to a public key, by the system's own cryptography: Ed25519 (RFC 8032), ECDSA on P-256 and P-384 (FIPS 186-5, signatures in X9.62's DER), RSA-PSS and RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 signatures and RSA-OAEP encryption (RFC 8017), X25519 (RFC 7748) and ECDH on P-256 and P-384 (SEC 1).
- [`scram`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/scram/): Both sides of SCRAM (RFC 5802, RFC 7677), the login that proves a password to a server without sending it, by SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512: the client's messages and its check of the server, and the server's verifier made from a password, its messages and its check of the client's proof; and SASLprep (RFC 4013), the preparation of a password SCRAM asks.
- [`tokenizer/tables`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tokenizer/tables/): The encodings of OpenAI's models by name, and which encoding a model reads, as tiktoken 0.14.0 answers: `o200k_base` (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5, o1, o3, o4-mini), `cl100k_base` (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, the embeddings of 2022 and 2024) and `o200k_harmony` (gpt-oss).
- [`tokenizer/tables/cl100k_base`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tokenizer/tables/cl100k_base/): The table of `cl100k_base`, the encoding of GPT-4, GPT-3.5 and the embedding models `text-embedding-ada-002` and `text-embedding-3-*`, alone: a program that uses this module carries this table and no other, where one that uses `tokenizer/tables`, which also finds an encoding by its name or its model, carries all three.
- [`tokenizer/tables/o200k_base`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tokenizer/tables/o200k_base/): The table of `o200k_base`, the encoding of GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5 and the models o1, o3 and o4-mini, alone: a program that uses this module carries this table and no other, where one that uses `tokenizer/tables`, which also finds an encoding by its name or its model, carries all three.
- [`tokenizer/tables/o200k_harmony`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tokenizer/tables/o200k_harmony/): The table of `o200k_harmony`, the encoding of OpenAI's gpt-oss models, alone: a program that uses this module carries this table and `o200k_base`'s tokens and no other, where one that uses `tokenizer/tables`, which also finds an encoding by its name or its model, carries all three.

### Layer 4

- [`fs`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/): Files and folders by path: a file read or written whole, a file opened as an `io.Stream`, the facts of a path, folders made, read and removed, trees walked, globbed and copied, links made, read and resolved, temporaries made, a path's times, length, permission and owner set, a file written atomically, locked, or mapped in memory and read and written by copy, and a walk that leaves out what a tree's gitignore files ignore.
- [`msgpack`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/msgpack/): MessagePack, the binary format of msgpack.org's specification: bytes decoded into a value a program matches on, and a value encoded as bytes, each object in the smallest format that holds it as the specification asks.
- [`plist`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/plist/): Apple property lists, the two forms every Apple platform reads: the XML form of `PropertyList-1.0.dtd` and the binary form, `bplist00`.
- [`poll`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/poll/): Waiting on many connections, listeners, datagram sockets, streams and timers at once, and being told which are ready and for what, so one thread serves many connections: what an event loop gives a program (Rust's `tokio` and `mio`, Go's network poller, Python's `selectors`), without a coroutine, which the language refuses (design.md Part 6).
- [`tls`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tls/): TLS: a connection whose bytes are encrypted and whose peer is checked, as an `io.Stream` that `io` reads, writes and closes like any other, so `http`, `sql/postgres` and any program use it unchanged.
- [`log`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/log/): Lines with a time and a level, written to a stream: a logger is a record that says where its lines go, the lowest level it writes, a prefix, the line's form and the fields every line carries, built by `to` and passed along.
- [`uuid`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/uuid/): Universally unique identifiers (RFC 9562): versions 4 and 7 made, any version read from text or bytes and written back, the nil and the max values, and the version, the variant and a version 7's time read.
- [`toml`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/toml/): TOML 1.1.0 read and written: a document of tables, keys and values, read into a tree a program matches on and written back as text that reads as the same tree.
- [`sql`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/): What a program does with a database whatever the database is: the values that travel to it and back, the rows a query answers and the reads of their columns by place and by name, what a statement that changes rows answers, the codes a database failure is told with, and an identifier quoted.
- [`protobuf`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/protobuf/): Protocol Buffers: the wire format read and written field by field, `.proto` files read at run time into a schema, messages held as a tree a program matches on and encoded or decoded by that schema, the proto3 JSON mapping to and from a `json.Value`, and the well-known types.
- [`mail`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mail/): E-mail messages read and written: a message's header fields (RFC 5322), folded and unfolded with their order kept; addresses, address lists and groups; dates; encoded words (RFC 2047); MIME (RFC 2045 to 2049) with its content types and their parameters (RFC 2231), multipart messages read as a tree and written with a boundary none of their parts holds, quoted-printable and base 64; attachments and inline parts; and UTF-8 in header fields and addresses (RFC 6532).
- [`asn1`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/asn1/): ASN.1 values read and written in the encodings of ITU-T X.690: DER read and written exactly, BER read.
- [`i18n/dates`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/dates/): Dates and times written as a language writes them: "Tuesday, March 5, 2024" and "5 mars 2024", the names of its months and days, its patterns for full, long, medium and short dates, times relative to now, "3 days ago", "in 2 hours", "yesterday", in a unit the program names or one chosen for the span, and durations in words, "3 hours, 5 minutes", from the data of CLDR release `i18n.CLDR_VERSION` for every locale it holds, over the instants and zones of `time`.
- [`dns`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/dns/): A DNS client: messages of RFC 1035 read from their bytes and written to them exactly, every common kind of record as a value, and questions asked of name servers over UDP, and over TCP where an answer comes truncated, with a deadline on every try.
- [`bench`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/bench/): A function measured: called in rounds after a warm-up, each round repeating the call until it lasts long enough for the monotonic clock to read it well, and the time a call took told by the rounds kept: their median, their best, their spread, their quartiles and the rounds far from the others.
- [`chunks`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/chunks/): A text cut into pieces for retrieval: each piece small enough for a model or an index to take, cut where the text's own structure allows, paragraphs first, then sentences, words and last characters, with an overlap between neighbours so that a sentence cut in two is still read whole somewhere.
- [`bson`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/bson/): BSON, the binary documents of MongoDB as bsonspec.org specifies them: bytes decoded into a `Document` a program reads and matches on, and a document encoded as bytes, every one of BSON's types held exactly, the deprecated ones included, so a document read and written again is the same bytes but where the specification asks one form (a regex's options in alphabetical order, an array's names `0`, `1`, ...).
- [`tui`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tui/): Full-screen terminal programs in immediate mode, as Rust's `ratatui` draws them: the program keeps its own state; each frame it asks for a blank buffer of the screen's size, cuts it into areas by constraints, draws widgets into those areas, and hands the buffer to `flush`, which writes only the cells that changed since the frame before; then it reads the next event, a key, a click, a paste or a new size, and changes its state.
- [`webauthn`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/webauthn/): A relying party of W3C Web Authentication Level 3: the options of a registration and of an authentication written as the JSON a browser hands `navigator.credentials`, and the responses verified: the client data's type, challenge and origin, the authenticator data's RP ID, flags and counter, the attestation, and the assertion's signature.
- [`image/png`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/png/): PNG read and written, by the W3C's PNG specification (third edition): every colour type and bit depth, interlaced or not, read into an `image.Image`; an image written with the filter and compression level the caller picks; the chunks a program does not need dropped or kept, and text chunks read and made.
- [`retries`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/retries/): The waits of a retry loop and circuit breakers: how long a program waits before it tries a failed call again, spread by chance so that clients that failed together do not try again together, when it gives up, and the wait an HTTP `Retry-After` asks; and a breaker that stops calling a service that keeps failing, then lets a trial through.
- [`compress/zstd`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/zstd/): Zstandard (RFC 8878) compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: every frame read, its blocks stored, repeated or compressed with Huffman-coded literals and FSE-coded sequences, its checksum checked, skippable frames passed over, with or without a dictionary; and frames written at a basic level.
- [`compress/brotli`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/brotli/): Brotli (RFC 7932) compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: every stream read whole, its meta-blocks stored or compressed, block types and their switches, context modes and maps, every prefix code, the distances and the 121 transforms of the static dictionary's 122,784 bytes (carried here, so only the programs that use this package carry them); and streams written at a basic level.
- [`compress/bzip2`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/bzip2/): bzip2 compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: the Burrows-Wheeler transform, the move to front, the runs and the Huffman codes of Julian Seward's format, each block's CRC and the stream's.
- [`process`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/process/): Another program run, fed, read and waited for: a command built as a record, run to its end with what it writes captured, or started as a child whose pipes are `io.Stream`s, waited for, asked to end or ended at once; a program looked up on PATH; a text quoted for a POSIX shell.
- [`compress/lz4`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/lz4/): LZ4 compressed and decompressed: its blocks bare, and its frames (the magic 04 22 4D 18, a header, blocks of up to 64 KiB to 4 MiB that stand alone or reach back into the blocks before them, an xxHash32 checksum of each block and of the content, the content's size, a dictionary's id), all at once over a `[u8]`, piece by piece in memory, or through an `io.Stream`; skippable frames passed over, and legacy frames read and written.
- [`compress/xz`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/xz/): xz and LZMA compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: the xz container (its blocks, index, footer and checks, several streams one after another with their padding) holding LZMA2 data, and the older `.lzma` format of a header and LZMA data.
- [`template/sanitized`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/template/sanitized/): A page of `template`'s HTML mode that places HTML from outside where its template says: each `clean` action writes the text its value names as markup, cleaned by an `html/sanitize` policy inside the element it lands in, so a note written in Markdown and made HTML, or a visitor's comment, stands in its layout as one template, inside a loop as anywhere, and runs nothing.
- [`ical`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ical/): iCalendar (RFC 5545), the format every calendar program imports and exports, and the content lines it shares with vCard (RFC 6350).
- [`barcode`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/barcode/): Barcodes made: EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A and UPC-E with their two- and five-digit add-ons (ISO/IEC 15420 and the GS1 General Specifications), Code 128 and GS1-128 (ISO/IEC 15417), Data Matrix ECC 200 and GS1 Data Matrix (ISO/IEC 16022), and PDF417 and compact PDF417 (ISO/IEC 15438), each with its check characters or error correction and its quiet zones, and written as SVG text or drawn into an `image`, the digits a person reads set under a linear symbol's bars.
- [`chart`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/chart/): Plots and charts made: lines, points and areas over two axes, bars side by side or stacked, upright or lying, histograms, pies and donuts, each with its axes' ticks computed (nice numbers, logarithmic scales, the calendar's steps for dates), a grid, a legend, a title and the axes' labels, its text set in a `font.Font` and its colours from a palette made in `image/colorspace`; written as SVG text or drawn into an `image` through `image/vector`, the same drawing either way.

### Layer 5

- [`jobs`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jobs/): Background work kept in a store and run by workers, as Celery, Sidekiq and river do it: a job is a value (a kind, a JSON payload, a queue, a priority, a time to start, its attempts), a worker claims the next one ready, runs the program's own function for its kind, and marks it completed or failed; a failed attempt runs again after a wait that grows, until its attempts are spent and it is kept, failed, with every error.
- [`jose`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jose/): JSON Web Signatures, Keys, Tokens and Encryption (RFC 7515, 7517, 7519 and 7516, the algorithms of RFC 7518 and RFC 8037): a payload signed and verified in the compact and the JSON serializations, a key read from and written as its JSON or as DER and PEM, a JWT's claims checked, and a plaintext encrypted where the system's cryptography allows it.
- [`archive`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/archive/): Archives of many files in one: tar (ustar, with PAX records and GNU's long names read) plain or gzip, and zip (stored and deflated members, ZIP64 for large ones), read entry by entry, listed, extracted into a folder, written entry by entry or from files on the disk; and read from, or written as, bytes held in memory (`decode_tar`, `encode_tar`, `decode_zip`, `encode_zip`), with no file on the way.
- [`sql/postgres`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/postgres/): A PostgreSQL client written in Heroes: it speaks the database's own frontend/backend protocol, version 3.0, over a TCP connection of `net`, and links no library of PostgreSQL.
- [`sql/sqlite`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/sqlite/): SQLite from Heroes: a database in a file or in memory, run inside the program through SQLite's own C library, with the API every driver of Rebel keeps over `sql`'s types, name for name, as `sql`'s opening comment writes it: `open`, `close`, `is_closed`, `ping`, `exec`, `query`, `query_one`, `exec_script`, `prepare`, `exec_prepared`, `query_prepared`, `close_statement`, `begin`, `commit`, `rollback` and `in_transaction`.
- [`sql/mysql`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/mysql/): A MySQL and MariaDB client written in Heroes: it speaks the servers' own client/server protocol, 4.1, over a TCP connection of `net`, and links no library of either.
- [`redis`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/redis/): A Redis client written in Heroes: it speaks RESP, the Redis serialization protocol, versions 2 and 3, over a TCP connection of `net` or a TLS connection of `tls`, and links no library.
- [`sql/build`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/build/): Queries as values: a SELECT, an INSERT, an UPDATE or a DELETE built by functions and composed as any value is, then written by `to_sql` as the text and the parameters a driver of Rebel runs, with each database's own placeholders: `$1` for PostgreSQL, `?1` for SQLite.
- [`http2`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/http2/): HTTP/2 (RFC 9113) and its header compression HPACK (RFC 7541), client and server, over a `tls` stream whose ALPN chose `h2` or over a plain stream by prior knowledge (h2c): many requests at once on one connection, each on a stream of its own.
- [`mail/imap`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mail/imap/): Mail read from a server by IMAP (RFC 9051, IMAP4rev2, and RFC 3501, IMAP4rev1): a client that connects in plain text, by STARTTLS or by TLS from the first byte (RFC 8314, port 993), logs in by LOGIN or by AUTHENTICATE with PLAIN, XOAUTH2 or OAUTHBEARER, enables IMAP4rev2 where the server offers it, lists, makes, renames and selects mailboxes, fetches messages whole or in parts (envelopes, body structures, sections, partial fetches, BINARY), searches, changes flags, copies, moves, appends and expunges, by message number or by UID, and waits for news with IDLE.
- [`mail/smtp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mail/smtp/): Mail sent by SMTP (RFC 5321): a client that connects in plain text, by STARTTLS (RFC 3207) or by TLS from the first byte (RFC 8314, port 465), reads the extensions EHLO names, logs in by AUTH PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5 or XOAUTH2, and sends a message to its recipients with SIZE, 8BITMIME, SMTPUTF8 and PIPELINING where the server offers them; each step bounded by a deadline, every reply a value with its code.
- [`x509`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/x509/): Certificates of X.509 read as RFC 5280 writes them: the subject and the issuer with their attributes, the validity, the serial, the public key, the signature's algorithm and bytes, and every common extension decoded, an unknown one kept with its criticality; certificate requests (PKCS #10, RFC 2986) and revocation lists (RFC 5280 § 5) read; a signature checked by the system's own cryptography through `crypto/keypairs`; a chain put in order from a leaf and a pool, and checked; a host name and an address matched against a certificate as RFC 6125 says; and certificates, requests and revocation lists made and signed through `crypto/keypairs`.
- [`fs/acl`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/acl/): Who may do what to a file or a folder beyond its permission bits: its access control list read, written whole, copied to another path, and the id of a user or a group found by name, so a backup restores a folder with who may read it and a program grants one user or group a right.
- [`fs/watch`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/watch/): A folder, a folder's whole tree or one file watched, and every change the system tells of it handed to the program as an `Event`, in order: an entry created, removed, written, its facts changed, or renamed with both its names; events lost told as one `overflow`; the watched folder itself gone.
- [`fs/xattr`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/xattr/): The extended attributes of a file or a folder: named values it carries beside its bytes, listed, read, written, removed and copied to another path, so a backup keeps a macOS file's tags (`com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags`) and quarantine (`com.apple.quarantine`), a Linux file's SELinux label (`security.selinux`), and what a program stored beside a file of its own.
- [`sql/odbc`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/odbc/): Any database the system's ODBC driver manager reaches, through the API every driver of Rebel keeps over `sql`'s types, name for name, as `sql`'s opening comment writes it: `open`, `close`, `is_closed`, `ping`, `exec`, `query`, `query_one`, `exec_script`, `prepare`, `exec_prepared`, `query_prepared`, `close_statement`, `begin`, `commit`, `rollback` and `in_transaction`.
- [`ldap`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ldap/): An LDAP client written in Heroes: it speaks LDAPv3 (RFC 4511) to a directory server over a TCP connection of `net` or a TLS connection of `tls`, every message BER of `asn1`, and links no library.
- [`config`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/config/): Settings read in layers: defaults, files in TOML, YAML, JSON, INI or Java's properties, `.env` files, the environment and the command line, each a `Layer` holding an object of `json.Value`, merged by `merge` in the order the program lists them, each over the ones before it, into `Settings` read by dotted path with typed getters.
- [`amqp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/amqp/): An AMQP 0-9-1 client written in Heroes, as RabbitMQ speaks it, over a TCP connection of `net` or TLS of `tls`, linking no library.
- [`kafka`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/kafka/): A Kafka client written in Heroes, speaking the wire protocol over TCP connections of `net` or TLS of `tls`, linking no library.
- [`mongodb`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mongodb/): A MongoDB client written in Heroes: it speaks MongoDB's wire protocol (OP_MSG) over a TCP connection of `net` or a TLS connection of `tls`, and links no library.
- [`log/files`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/log/files/): A logger's lines written to a file that is rotated: when the next line would take the file past a size, or is of a later day, the file is set aside under an old file's name and a new one begun at the same path; the oldest old files are removed past a count or an age, and the others gzipped where asked.
- [`image/ico`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/ico/): ICO and CUR read and written: the directory of images that Windows keeps an icon or a cursor in, each stored as a PNG or as a bitmap with a mask, every one an RGBA image here, with a cursor's hot spot.
- [`image/tiff`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/tiff/): TIFF read and written: every page of a file, classic or BigTIFF in either byte order, in strips or tiles, coded by PackBits, LZW, Deflate (with the horizontal predictor), Zstandard, JPEG or CCITT's fax codings, with 1 to 16 bits a sample as gray, RGB, a palette, CMYK or YCbCr (its chroma shared by blocks of pixels), with an alpha channel, in one plane or several, and the bits of a byte in either fill order; and written in every one of those codings but JPEG, as strips or tiles, at 8 or 16 bits or at one bit a pixel.
- [`pdf`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/pdf/): PDF documents written and read.
- [`ipc`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ipc/): Communication between the processes of one machine: a local channel by name, read and written as an `io.Stream`, and messages whole over one; memory shared by name, read and written by copies; a semaphore and a lock between processes, named, every wait with a bound.
- [`audio`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/audio/): Sound for a program: frames of samples held in memory, converted between encodings, channel counts and rates, read from WAV files and written to them; and the system's devices, listed with their formats, a sound played on one and frames recorded from one, paused, resumed, stopped and its end told, a stream waited on in a `poll.Set`, the microphone's permission asked, and the system's beep.
- [`mdns`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mdns/): Multicast DNS (RFC 6762) and DNS-based service discovery (RFC 6763): the devices, printers and peers of the local network found by name, and a program's own service made known to them.
- [`ui`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ui/): Windows holding the system's own widgets, in the manner of wxWidgets: a button is an `NSButton` on macOS, a Win32 button on Windows, a GTK button on Linux, never one this package draws, so a program looks and behaves as the system's own programs do, its keys, its accessibility and its languages included.
- [`ical/vcard`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ical/vcard/): vCard (RFC 6350, and RFC 2426's version 3.0): a contact read from and written as the `VCARD` components of a document, over the content lines `ical` reads and writes.
- [`ssh`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ssh/): A client of SSH 2 (RFC 4250 to 4254): a server reached, its host key checked against a `known_hosts` file the program names, a sign-in by a key or a password, programs run with their output, errors and exit status, a shell or a subsystem in a terminal or without, and connections forwarded both ways; with SSH's key formats, public key lines, OpenSSH's private key files and `known_hosts` lines, read and written.
- [`syslog`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/syslog/): The system's own log: a daemon's lines where the system keeps its log and its tools read it.
- [`service/manage`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/service/manage/): A service of the system installed, started, stopped, asked and removed by another program: a systemd unit, `--user` or the system's, on Linux; a launchd agent of the user's or a daemon of the system's on macOS; a service of the Service Control Manager on Windows.

### Layer 6

- [`service`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/service/): The program as a service of the system that starts it.
- [`http`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/http/): HTTP/1.1, client and server, over `net` and over `tls`: a request and a response as values, read from and written to an `io.Stream` by RFC 9112; a client that sends a request to an `http://` or `https://` URL and follows its redirects; and a server that answers each request of each connection, plain or TLS, with a function of the program.
- [`sql/migrate`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/migrate/): Numbered migrations of a database's schema: read from the SQL files of a folder or given as values, checked against a table of the versions already applied, and planned as steps, each applying or undoing one migration in its own transaction, that the program runs with its driver.
- [`grpc`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/grpc/): gRPC over HTTP/2: calls of the four kinds (unary, a stream from the server, a stream from the client, and both ways at once), client and server, as the gRPC over HTTP/2 protocol writes them: each message framed by its length, a call's status and its message in the trailers, metadata as header fields (`-bin` keys carried in base 64), a deadline sent as `grpc-timeout`, and messages compressed by gzip where both ends allow it.
- [`xlsx`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/xlsx/): Spreadsheets of Office Open XML, the `.xlsx` files of Excel, read and written.
- [`jobs/postgres_store`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jobs/postgres_store/): Jobs kept in PostgreSQL, in a table of the program's own database, as river keeps them: a job enqueued in the program's own transaction is kept exactly where that transaction commits, a worker claims the next job ready with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so any number of workers each claim a job once without waiting on each other, and a job completed in the program's own transaction is completed exactly where the work it did commits.
- [`jobs/redis_store`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jobs/redis_store/): Jobs kept in Redis, as Sidekiq, asynq and RQ keep them: each job a hash, each queue sorted sets of the jobs ready, waiting, running and finished, and every change a Lua script the server runs whole, so any number of workers each claim a job once and never see one half moved.
- [`ui/webview`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ui/webview/): A web page as a program's interface, in the manner of Tauri: the system's own web view, shown as a widget of a `ui` app, whose page is the HTML, CSS and scripts the program carries, and the program its logic, the two speaking through a bridge of texts and through nothing else.
- [`xmldsig`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/xmldsig/): XML Signature, checked and made: a `ds:Signature` of XML Signature 1.1 (W3C, 2013) read and checked against the key a program trusts, its references to the document itself digested over Canonical XML, and an enveloped or detached signature made by a key pair or an HMAC secret.
- [`x509/pkcs12`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/x509/pkcs12/): PKCS #12 (RFC 7292), the `.pfx` and `.p12` files Windows, macOS, Java, OpenSSL and load balancers import and export a key and its certificates in, read and written: the keys, the certificates, the revocation lists and the secrets of a file, each with its name and its key identifier; the key and the chain that belong together; and a file made of a key and its chain, or of trusted certificates alone, as Java's trust stores are.
- [`sftp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sftp/): A client of SFTP, the SSH File Transfer Protocol version 3 (draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-02) as OpenSSH's `sftp-server` speaks it, over a channel of an `ssh` client: files opened, read and written, their attributes read and set, folders listed, made and removed, paths renamed, linked and resolved, with OpenSSH's extensions where the server announces them, each checked by the version OpenSSH's `PROTOCOL` gives it: `posix-rename@openssh.com`, `hardlink@openssh.com`, `fsync@openssh.com`, `lsetstat@openssh.com`, `statvfs@openssh.com`, `fstatvfs@openssh.com`, `limits@openssh.com`, `expand-path@openssh.com`, `copy-data`, `home-directory` and `users-groups-by-id@openssh.com`.

### Layer 7

- [`web`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/web/): Routes for an HTTP server in the manner of Go's Echo: explicit routes, values, no magic.
- [`websocket`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/websocket/): WebSocket (RFC 6455), client and server: a connection that carries whole messages of text or of bytes both ways, framed and masked as the RFC asks, compressed by permessage-deflate (RFC 7692) where both ends agree, and ended by its closing handshake.
- [`oauth2`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/oauth2/): An OAuth 2.0 client (RFC 6749 as RFC 9700 hardens it) and OpenID Connect: the authorization code grant with PKCE, the client credentials, device authorization (RFC 8628), JWT bearer (RFC 7523) and refresh grants, a token's revocation (RFC 7009) and introspection (RFC 7662), an authorization server's metadata (RFC 8414, OpenID Connect Discovery), a protected resource's (RFC 9728), resource indicators (RFC 8707), the issuer of a redirect checked (RFC 9207), a client's metadata document whose URL is its id, and an ID token verified through `jose`.
- [`saml`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/saml/): SAML 2.0's service provider (OASIS, 2005): a program signs its users in through a company's identity server.
- [`s3`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/s3/): The S3 API spoken over HTTP and HTTPS with Signature Version 4: objects put, read whole or by a range, asked about, copied, deleted and listed; buckets made, listed and removed; uploads in parts; presigned URLs and browser forms; checksums; and any other request of the API signed and sent.
- [`jsonrpc`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jsonrpc/): JSON-RPC 2.0, exactly as its specification of 2013-01-04 writes it: requests, notifications, answers and errors with their codes, batches, and ids of every kind the specification allows, read from text and written as text; carried over a stream one message a line (as MCP's standard streams and JSON Lines carry it) or each after a `Content-Length` header (as the Language Server Protocol carries it), and over HTTP through `http`.
- [`acme`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/acme/): A client of ACME, RFC 8555: the directory read, an account made, found, changed or deactivated, an order placed for names, its authorizations answered by HTTP-01 or DNS-01, the order finalized with a certificate request, and the certificate chain downloaded, revoked, or asked when to renew (RFC 9773).
- [`x509/ocsp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/x509/ocsp/): OCSP (RFC 6960): whether a certificate is revoked, asked of the responder its issuer names and the answer checked.
- [`llm/anthropic`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/llm/anthropic/): Claude's Messages API spoken over `http`, with no SDK: a conversation sent and its answer read whole or as it streams, tools whose calls the program runs itself, tokens counted, batches of requests, the models listed, and every failure the API answers told with its status, its type, its request id and the wait it advises.
- [`llm/openai`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/llm/openai/): OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs spoken over `http`, with no SDK, and every server that speaks them: Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp's and LM Studio's servers, reached by their base URL.
- [`graphql`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/graphql/): GraphQL, as its specification of October 2021 writes it and as its working draft has settled since (`@oneOf` input objects, Unicode escapes past U+FFFF, the check that an operation's kind exists): a document's text parsed into operations and fragments, a schema's text parsed into a schema, a document validated against a schema by every rule of the specification's section 5, and an operation executed with the program answering every field, its result and its errors the specification's JSON response.
- [`otlp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/otlp/): OpenTelemetry's protocol, OTLP 1.x over HTTP with protobuf: the attributes, the resource and the instrumentation scope every signal's request carries; an exporter, which posts a request to a collector and sends it again as OTLP's specification asks; and the pieces a signal's request is written with, on `protobuf`'s wire, so the bytes are those Python's `opentelemetry-proto` writes for the same message.

### Layer 8

- [`metrics`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/metrics/): Counters, gauges, histograms and summaries, each with labels, kept in a registry the program holds as a value; written in Prometheus's text format 0.0.4 and in OpenMetrics 1.0 as Prometheus's own Go client writes them, served to a scraper by `respond`, pushed to a Pushgateway, sent as StatsD and DogStatsD lines over UDP, and written as OTLP's request for an OpenTelemetry collector, which `otlp.export` posts.
- [`tracing`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tracing/): Spans of work with a parent, attributes, events, links and a status, kept by a tracer the program holds as a value; their context carried from one program to the next in HTTP requests by the W3C Trace Context fields `traceparent` and `tracestate`; traces sampled by a ratio of their ids; and spans and log records exported to an OpenTelemetry collector as OTLP over HTTP, a log record carrying the trace and the span it was written in.
- [`nats`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/nats/): A NATS client written in Heroes: it speaks NATS's text protocol over a TCP connection of `net`, a TLS connection of `tls` or a WebSocket of `websocket`, and links no library.
- [`mqtt`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mqtt/): An MQTT client written in Heroes: MQTT 3.1.1 and 5.0 spoken over a TCP connection of `net`, TLS of `tls` or a WebSocket of `websocket`, linking no library.
- [`sse`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sse/): Server-sent events, read and served: a reader that connects again as a browser's `EventSource` does (the WHATWG HTML standard, § 9.2), and a hub that keeps the clients of an event stream, tells each of them what happens, remembers what it told so a client that connects again is told what it missed, and keeps a silent connection from being closed by a proxy.
- [`mcp`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mcp/): The Model Context Protocol, revision 2026-07-28, followed as that revision writes it: a server that offers a model tools (listed with the JSON Schema of their inputs, and called), resources and resource templates, prompts, completions, and change notifications on `subscriptions/listen`; that asks the user for more through elicitation, by multi round-trip requests; that tells progress and hears cancellation; over standard streams one message a line, and over Streamable HTTP.
- [`openapi`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/openapi/): OpenAPI 3.1 documents built as data, written as JSON and YAML, read back, checked, served beside a program's routes, and requests and responses validated against them.
- [`web/proxy`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/web/proxy/): A reverse proxy in the manner of nginx's `proxy_pass` and Go's `httputil.ReverseProxy`: each request a client sends passed to one of its upstreams, `http://` or `https://`, and the answer passed back, the bodies both ways in pieces as they come and never held whole.
- [`web/chain`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/web/chain/): The steps a request runs on its way to a `web` router's answer, in the manner of Echo's middleware: a step every route runs (Echo's `e.Use`), a group's (`g.Use`) and one route's own, each a function of the program's that answers before the handler (a check refusing 401) or wraps it (a log line reading the response and the time).

### Layer 9

- [`web/steps`](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/web/steps/): The usual steps of a `web/chain` chain, ready for a program to bind, in the manner of Echo's `middleware` package: a log line for each request with its status and the time it took, a request id kept or made, CORS, a Basic check against the program's own accounts, a body's limit, helmet's security headers and gzip.
## Each face

### unicode

Layer 0, named `use <rebel>/unicode`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/).

What a character is: its code point, its classes, its case, and how UTF-8 and UTF-16 write it.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a failure on input that is not what the function reads: a number that is no code point of a character, a byte that begins no character.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of a failure on bytes that are not UTF-8, the language's own.
- `constant UNICODE_VERSION: str`, value `"17.0.0"`: The version of Unicode the tables hold.
- `constant MAX_CODE_POINT: i64`, value `0x10ffff`: The largest code point, U+10FFFF.
- `constant REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER: str`, value `"�"`: The character U+FFFD, written where a character could not be read.
- `constant MAX_UTF8_LEN: i64`, value `4`: The most bytes one character takes in UTF-8.
- `variant Category = .uppercase_letter | .lowercase_letter | .titlecase_letter | .modifier_letter | .other_letter | .nonspacing_mark | .spacing_mark | .enclosing_mark | .decimal_number | .letter_number | .other_number | .connector_punctuation | .dash_punctuation | .open_punctuation | .close_punctuation | .initial_punctuation | .final_punctuation | .other_punctuation | .math_symbol | .currency_symbol | .modifier_symbol | .other_symbol | .space_separator | .line_separator | .paragraph_separator | .control | .format | .surrogate | .private_use | .unassigned`: A character's general category, one of Unicode's thirty, in the order Unicode lists them; `letter_of` gives its two letters.
- `function code_point(c: str) -> i64`, called `unicode.code_point(c)`: The code point of `c`, one character.
- `function from_code_point(n: i64) -> str?`, called `unicode.from_code_point(n)`: The character whose code point is `n`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function code_points(s: str) -> [i64]`, called `unicode.code_points(s)`: The code points of `s`, one for each character, in order.
- `function from_code_points(points: [i64]) -> str?`, called `unicode.from_code_points(points)`: The text that `points` write, one character for each. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_scalar_value(n: i64) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_scalar_value(n)`: Whether `n` is a scalar value, a code point a character can have: 0 to `MAX_CODE_POINT`, the surrogates U+D800 to U+DFFF left out.
- `function is_letter(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_letter(c)`: Whether `c` is a letter: its general category is one of the five that begin with `L`.
- `function is_alphabetic(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_alphabetic(c)`: Whether `c` is alphabetic, Unicode's Alphabetic property: a letter, a number written as a letter, or a sign a script writes as part of a word, a vowel sign among them.
- `function is_digit(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_digit(c)`: Whether `c` is a decimal digit, general category `Nd`: one of the ten digits of some script.
- `function is_number(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_number(c)`: Whether `c` is a number of any kind, a general category that begins with `N`: a decimal digit, a Roman numeral, a fraction, a circled number.
- `function is_alphanumeric(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_alphanumeric(c)`: Whether `c` is alphabetic or a number: `is_alphabetic` or `is_number`.
- `function is_space(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_space(c)`: Whether `c` is white space, Unicode's White_Space property: space, tab, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, carriage return, U+0085, U+00A0, and the spaces and separators above them, 25 code points in all.
- `function is_upper(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_upper(c)`: Whether `c` is upper case, Unicode's Uppercase property: an upper case letter, or a sign that is one by its use, as a Roman numeral or a circled capital.
- `function is_lower(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_lower(c)`: Whether `c` is lower case, Unicode's Lowercase property: a lower case letter, or a sign that is one by its use, as the ordinal indicators.
- `function is_title_letter(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_title_letter(c)`: Whether `c` is a title case letter, general category `Lt`: one character that writes two letters, the first upper case.
- `function is_cased(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_cased(c)`: Whether `c` has a case, Unicode's Cased property: `is_upper`, `is_lower` or `is_title_letter`.
- `function is_case_ignorable(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_case_ignorable(c)`: Whether `c` is passed over when the letters around it are asked their case, Unicode's Case_Ignorable property: a mark, a modifier, an apostrophe, a full stop.
- `function is_punctuation(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_punctuation(c)`: Whether `c` is punctuation, a general category that begins with `P`.
- `function is_symbol(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_symbol(c)`: Whether `c` is a symbol, a general category that begins with `S`: a sign of mathematics, of a currency, a modifier such as `^`, or any other symbol.
- `function is_mark(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_mark(c)`: Whether `c` is a mark, a general category that begins with `M`: an accent or a sign that combines with the character before it.
- `function is_control(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_control(c)`: Whether `c` is a control code, general category `Cc`: U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F to U+009F.
- `function is_graphic(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_graphic(c)`: Whether `c` is drawn or leaves a space: a letter, a mark, a number, punctuation, a symbol, or a space of category `Zs`.
- `function is_printable(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_printable(c)`: Whether `c` may be printed as itself: `is_graphic`, with U+0020 the only space.
- `function is_ascii(c: str) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_ascii(c)`: Whether `c` is ASCII, a code point below 128.
- `function category(c: str) -> Category`, called `unicode.category(c)`: The general category of `c`.
- `function letter_of(kind: Category) -> str`, called `unicode.letter_of(kind)`: Unicode's two letters for the category `kind`, the major class first: `Lu` for `.uppercase_letter`, `Zs` for `.space_separator`.
- `function digit_value(c: str) -> i64?`, called `unicode.digit_value(c)`: The value of `c`, a decimal digit of any script, 0 to 9. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_digit(c: str, base: i64) -> i64?`, called `unicode.to_digit(c, base)`: The value of `c` as a digit of `base`, 0 to `base` less one: `0` to `9`, then the letters `a` to `z`, of either case, for ten to thirty-five. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_digit(value: i64, base: i64) -> str?`, called `unicode.from_digit(value: value, base: base)`: The character that writes `value` as a digit of `base`: `0` to `9`, then a letter in lower case. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_upper(c: str) -> str`, called `unicode.to_upper(c)`: The upper case of `c`, one character, as a text of one to three characters: the upper case of `ß` is `SS`.
- `function to_lower(c: str) -> str`, called `unicode.to_lower(c)`: The lower case of `c`, one character, as a text of one or two characters.
- `function to_title(c: str) -> str`, called `unicode.to_title(c)`: The title case of `c`, one character, as a text of one to three characters: the form a word's first letter takes, where the title case of `ǆ` is `ǅ` and its upper case is `Ǆ`.
- `function to_casefold(c: str) -> str`, called `unicode.to_casefold(c)`: The folded form of `c`, one character, as a text of one to three characters: two texts are the same ignoring case where their characters fold to the same texts.
- `function simple_fold(n: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.simple_fold(n)`: The next code point that is the same letter as `n` ignoring case, one to one: the smallest such above `n`, or the smallest of all where `n` is the largest.
- `function simple_upper(n: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.simple_upper(n)`: The upper case of the code point `n` where that is one code point, by Unicode's simple mapping, which leaves `ß` as it is.
- `function simple_lower(n: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.simple_lower(n)`: The lower case of the code point `n` where that is one code point, by Unicode's simple mapping.
- `function simple_title(n: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.simple_title(n)`: The title case of the code point `n` where that is one code point, by Unicode's simple mapping.
- `record Decoded(code_point: i64, len: i64)`: What `decode_at` and `decode_before` answer: one character read from bytes.
- `function to_utf8(n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `unicode.to_utf8(n)`: The bytes that write the code point `n` in UTF-8, one to four. Fails `invalid`.
- `function utf8_len(n: i64) -> i64?`, called `unicode.utf8_len(n)`: How many bytes write the code point `n` in UTF-8, 1 to 4. Fails `invalid`.
- `function utf8_len_of_first(first: u8) -> i64?`, called `unicode.utf8_len_of_first(first)`: How many bytes the character takes whose first byte is `first`, 1 to 4. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_utf8(bytes: [u8]) -> [i64]?`, called `unicode.from_utf8(bytes)`: The code points that `bytes` write in UTF-8, in order. Fails `not_text`.
- `function decode_at(bytes: [u8], index: i64) -> Decoded?`, called `unicode.decode_at(bytes, index)`: The character that begins at `index` of `bytes`. Fails `not_text`.
- `function decode_before(bytes: [u8], end: i64) -> Decoded?`, called `unicode.decode_before(bytes, end)`: The character that ends just before `end` in `bytes`: its last byte is `bytes[end - 1]`. Fails `not_text`.
- `function is_utf8(bytes: [u8]) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_utf8(bytes)`: Whether `bytes` are UTF-8 from the first to the last.
- `function utf8_prefix_len(bytes: [u8]) -> i64`, called `unicode.utf8_prefix_len(bytes)`: How many bytes at the start of `bytes` are whole characters of UTF-8.
- `function is_utf8_prefix(bytes: [u8]) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_utf8_prefix(bytes)`: Whether `bytes` are the beginning of UTF-8: they are UTF-8, or they stop inside a last character that more bytes could complete.
- `function is_continuation(byte: u8) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_continuation(byte)`: Whether `byte` continues a character, 0x80 to 0xBF: in UTF-8 no such byte begins one, and every byte of a character after its first is one.
- `function code_point_at(s: str, index: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.code_point_at(s, index)`: The code point of the character that begins at `index` of `s`.
- `function len_at(s: str, index: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.len_at(s, index)`: How many bytes the character takes that begins at `index` of `s`, 1 to 4, so the next begins at `index` plus it.
- `function char_count(s: str) -> i64`, called `unicode.char_count(s)`: How many characters `s` holds, where `s.len()` counts its bytes.
- `function is_char_boundary(s: str, index: i64) -> bool`, called `unicode.is_char_boundary(s, index)`: Whether `index` is where a character of `s` begins, or the end of `s`: where a slice may cut.
- `function floor_char_boundary(s: str, index: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.floor_char_boundary(s, index)`: The nearest index at or before `index` where a character of `s` begins, or the end of `s`: the largest that `is_char_boundary` accepts and is not above `index`.
- `function ceil_char_boundary(s: str, index: i64) -> i64`, called `unicode.ceil_char_boundary(s, index)`: The nearest index at or after `index` where a character of `s` begins, or the end of `s`: the smallest that `is_char_boundary` accepts and is not below `index`.
- `function to_utf16(n: i64) -> [u16]?`, called `unicode.to_utf16(n)`: The units that write the code point `n` in UTF-16: one, or the two surrogates of a code point above U+FFFF, the high one first. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_utf16(units: [u16]) -> [i64]?`, called `unicode.from_utf16(units)`: The code points that `units` write in UTF-16, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_surrogates(high: i64, low: i64) -> i64?`, called `unicode.from_surrogates(high: high, low: low)`: The code point that the surrogates `high` and `low` write together, U+10000 or above. Fails `invalid`.


### math

Layer 0, named `use <rebel>/math`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/).

The functions of mathematics over `f64`, and the integer helpers that answer where the language's own arithmetic aborts.
