- `function subtract_vec2(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2`, called `linear.subtract_vec2(a: a, b: b)`: The difference `a - b`, part by part: the vector from the point `b` to the point `a`.
- `function negate_vec2(v: Vec2) -> Vec2`, called `linear.negate_vec2(v)`: `v` pointing the other way: every part negated.
- `function scale_vec2(v: Vec2, by: f64) -> Vec2`, called `linear.scale_vec2(v, by)`: `v` times the number `by`, every part.
- `function multiply_vec2(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> Vec2`, called `linear.multiply_vec2(a: a, b: b)`: The product of `a` and `b` part by part, Hadamard's: not the dot product, which is `dot_vec2`.
- `function dot_vec2(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> f64`, called `linear.dot_vec2(a: a, b: b)`: The dot product of `a` and `b`: the sum of their parts' products, the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them.
- `function length_vec2(v: Vec2) -> f64`, called `linear.length_vec2(v)`: The length of `v`, computed so that it overflows or underflows only where the answer does.
- `function length_squared_vec2(v: Vec2) -> f64`, called `linear.length_squared_vec2(v)`: The squared length of `v`, its dot product with itself: what compares two lengths without a square root.
- `function distance_vec2(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> f64`, called `linear.distance_vec2(a: a, b: b)`: The distance between the points `a` and `b`: the length of `a - b`.
- `function normalize_vec2(v: Vec2) -> Vec2?`, called `linear.normalize_vec2(v)`: `v` scaled to length 1, its direction: first scaled by a power of two, exactly, so that a vector of huge or tiny parts has its direction too. Fails `invalid`.
- `function lerp_vec2(from: Vec2, to: Vec2, t: f64) -> Vec2`, called `linear.lerp_vec2(from: from, to: to, t)`: The point a fraction `t` of the way from `from` to `to`: `(1 - t) * from + t * to`, part by part, exactly `from` at 0 and exactly `to` at 1.
- `function angle_vec2(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> f64?`, called `linear.angle_vec2(a: a, b: b)`: The angle between `a` and `b`, in radians from 0 to pi, by Kahan's `2 atan2(|u - v|, |u + v|)` of their directions, which keeps its digits where the vectors are nearly parallel or nearly opposite, as the arc cosine of the dot product does not. Fails `invalid`.
- `function cross_vec2(a: Vec2, b: Vec2) -> f64`, called `linear.cross_vec2(a: a, b: b)`: The cross product of two vectors of the plane, a number: `a.x * b.y - a.y * b.x`, the signed area of their parallelogram, positive where `b` turns counterclockwise from `a`.
- `function reflect_vec2(v: Vec2, normal: Vec2) -> Vec2?`, called `linear.reflect_vec2(v: v, normal: normal)`: `v` reflected off a surface whose normal is `normal`: `v - 2 (v . n) n` with `n` the normal's direction. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.add_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The sum `a + b`, part by part.
- `function subtract_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.subtract_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The difference `a - b`, part by part: the vector from the point `b` to the point `a`.
- `function negate_vec3(v: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.negate_vec3(v)`: `v` pointing the other way: every part negated.
- `function scale_vec3(v: Vec3, by: f64) -> Vec3`, called `linear.scale_vec3(v, by)`: `v` times the number `by`, every part.
- `function multiply_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.multiply_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The product of `a` and `b` part by part, Hadamard's: not the dot product, which is `dot_vec3`.
- `function dot_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> f64`, called `linear.dot_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The dot product of `a` and `b`: the sum of their parts' products, the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them.
- `function length_vec3(v: Vec3) -> f64`, called `linear.length_vec3(v)`: The length of `v`, computed so that it overflows or underflows only where the answer does.
- `function length_squared_vec3(v: Vec3) -> f64`, called `linear.length_squared_vec3(v)`: The squared length of `v`, its dot product with itself: what compares two lengths without a square root.
- `function distance_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> f64`, called `linear.distance_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The distance between the points `a` and `b`: the length of `a - b`.
- `function normalize_vec3(v: Vec3) -> Vec3?`, called `linear.normalize_vec3(v)`: `v` scaled to length 1, its direction: first scaled by a power of two, exactly, so that a vector of huge or tiny parts has its direction too. Fails `invalid`.
- `function lerp_vec3(from: Vec3, to: Vec3, t: f64) -> Vec3`, called `linear.lerp_vec3(from: from, to: to, t)`: The point a fraction `t` of the way from `from` to `to`: `(1 - t) * from + t * to`, part by part, exactly `from` at 0 and exactly `to` at 1.
- `function angle_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> f64?`, called `linear.angle_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The angle between `a` and `b`, in radians from 0 to pi, by Kahan's `2 atan2(|u - v|, |u + v|)` of their directions, which keeps its digits where the vectors are nearly parallel or nearly opposite, as the arc cosine of the dot product does not. Fails `invalid`.
- `function cross_vec3(a: Vec3, b: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.cross_vec3(a: a, b: b)`: The cross product `a x b`: perpendicular to both, of the length of their parallelogram's area, pointing by the right-hand rule.
- `function reflect_vec3(v: Vec3, normal: Vec3) -> Vec3?`, called `linear.reflect_vec3(v: v, normal: normal)`: `v` reflected off a surface whose normal is `normal`: `v - 2 (v . n) n` with `n` the normal's direction. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_vec4(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4`, called `linear.add_vec4(a: a, b: b)`: The sum `a + b`, part by part.
- `function subtract_vec4(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4`, called `linear.subtract_vec4(a: a, b: b)`: The difference `a - b`, part by part: the vector from the point `b` to the point `a`.
- `function negate_vec4(v: Vec4) -> Vec4`, called `linear.negate_vec4(v)`: `v` pointing the other way: every part negated.
- `function scale_vec4(v: Vec4, by: f64) -> Vec4`, called `linear.scale_vec4(v, by)`: `v` times the number `by`, every part.
- `function multiply_vec4(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> Vec4`, called `linear.multiply_vec4(a: a, b: b)`: The product of `a` and `b` part by part, Hadamard's: not the dot product, which is `dot_vec4`.
- `function dot_vec4(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> f64`, called `linear.dot_vec4(a: a, b: b)`: The dot product of `a` and `b`: the sum of their parts' products, the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them.
- `function length_vec4(v: Vec4) -> f64`, called `linear.length_vec4(v)`: The length of `v`, computed so that it overflows or underflows only where the answer does.
- `function length_squared_vec4(v: Vec4) -> f64`, called `linear.length_squared_vec4(v)`: The squared length of `v`, its dot product with itself: what compares two lengths without a square root.
- `function distance_vec4(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> f64`, called `linear.distance_vec4(a: a, b: b)`: The distance between the points `a` and `b`: the length of `a - b`.
- `function normalize_vec4(v: Vec4) -> Vec4?`, called `linear.normalize_vec4(v)`: `v` scaled to length 1, its direction: first scaled by a power of two, exactly, so that a vector of huge or tiny parts has its direction too. Fails `invalid`.
- `function lerp_vec4(from: Vec4, to: Vec4, t: f64) -> Vec4`, called `linear.lerp_vec4(from: from, to: to, t)`: The point a fraction `t` of the way from `from` to `to`: `(1 - t) * from + t * to`, part by part, exactly `from` at 0 and exactly `to` at 1.
- `function angle_vec4(a: Vec4, b: Vec4) -> f64?`, called `linear.angle_vec4(a: a, b: b)`: The angle between `a` and `b`, in radians from 0 to pi, by Kahan's `2 atan2(|u - v|, |u + v|)` of their directions, which keeps its digits where the vectors are nearly parallel or nearly opposite, as the arc cosine of the dot product does not. Fails `invalid`.
- `function identity_mat2() -> Mat2`, called `linear.identity_mat2()`: The identity matrix of size 2: ones on the diagonal, which changes nothing it multiplies.
- `function add_mat2(a: Mat2, b: Mat2) -> Mat2`, called `linear.add_mat2(a: a, b: b)`: The sum `a + b`, entry by entry.
- `function subtract_mat2(a: Mat2, b: Mat2) -> Mat2`, called `linear.subtract_mat2(a: a, b: b)`: The difference `a - b`, entry by entry.
- `function scale_mat2(m: Mat2, by: f64) -> Mat2`, called `linear.scale_mat2(m, by)`: `m` times the number `by`, every entry.
- `function multiply_mat2_vec2(m: Mat2, v: Vec2) -> Vec2`, called `linear.multiply_mat2_vec2(m, v)`: The product `m * v`: the vector `v` sent by `m`, its columns weighed by `v`'s parts.
- `function multiply_mat2(a: Mat2, b: Mat2) -> Mat2`, called `linear.multiply_mat2(a: a, b: b)`: The product `a * b`, the map that applies `b` first, then `a`: each column of `b` sent by `a`.
- `function transpose_mat2(m: Mat2) -> Mat2`, called `linear.transpose_mat2(m)`: `m` with its rows made its columns.
- `function determinant_mat2(m: Mat2) -> f64`, called `linear.determinant_mat2(m)`: The determinant of `m`: the factor by which it scales areas, negative where it turns the space over.
- `function inverse_mat2(m: Mat2) -> Mat2?`, called `linear.inverse_mat2(m)`: The inverse of `m`, the matrix that undoes it, by Gauss and Jordan's elimination with partial pivoting. Fails `invalid`.
- `function identity_mat3() -> Mat3`, called `linear.identity_mat3()`: The identity matrix of size 3: ones on the diagonal, which changes nothing it multiplies.
- `function add_mat3(a: Mat3, b: Mat3) -> Mat3`, called `linear.add_mat3(a: a, b: b)`: The sum `a + b`, entry by entry.
- `function subtract_mat3(a: Mat3, b: Mat3) -> Mat3`, called `linear.subtract_mat3(a: a, b: b)`: The difference `a - b`, entry by entry.
- `function scale_mat3(m: Mat3, by: f64) -> Mat3`, called `linear.scale_mat3(m, by)`: `m` times the number `by`, every entry.
- `function multiply_mat3_vec3(m: Mat3, v: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.multiply_mat3_vec3(m, v)`: The product `m * v`: the vector `v` sent by `m`, its columns weighed by `v`'s parts.
- `function multiply_mat3(a: Mat3, b: Mat3) -> Mat3`, called `linear.multiply_mat3(a: a, b: b)`: The product `a * b`, the map that applies `b` first, then `a`: each column of `b` sent by `a`.
- `function transpose_mat3(m: Mat3) -> Mat3`, called `linear.transpose_mat3(m)`: `m` with its rows made its columns.
- `function determinant_mat3(m: Mat3) -> f64`, called `linear.determinant_mat3(m)`: The determinant of `m`: the factor by which it scales areas and volumes, negative where it turns the space over.
- `function inverse_mat3(m: Mat3) -> Mat3?`, called `linear.inverse_mat3(m)`: The inverse of `m`, the matrix that undoes it, by Gauss and Jordan's elimination with partial pivoting. Fails `invalid`.
- `function identity_mat4() -> Mat4`, called `linear.identity_mat4()`: The identity matrix of size 4: ones on the diagonal, which changes nothing it multiplies.
- `function add_mat4(a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4`, called `linear.add_mat4(a: a, b: b)`: The sum `a + b`, entry by entry.
- `function subtract_mat4(a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4`, called `linear.subtract_mat4(a: a, b: b)`: The difference `a - b`, entry by entry.
- `function scale_mat4(m: Mat4, by: f64) -> Mat4`, called `linear.scale_mat4(m, by)`: `m` times the number `by`, every entry.
- `function multiply_mat4_vec4(m: Mat4, v: Vec4) -> Vec4`, called `linear.multiply_mat4_vec4(m, v)`: The product `m * v`: the vector `v` sent by `m`, its columns weighed by `v`'s parts.
- `function multiply_mat4(a: Mat4, b: Mat4) -> Mat4`, called `linear.multiply_mat4(a: a, b: b)`: The product `a * b`, the map that applies `b` first, then `a`: each column of `b` sent by `a`.
- `function transpose_mat4(m: Mat4) -> Mat4`, called `linear.transpose_mat4(m)`: `m` with its rows made its columns.
- `function determinant_mat4(m: Mat4) -> f64`, called `linear.determinant_mat4(m)`: The determinant of `m`: the factor by which it scales areas and volumes, negative where it turns the space over.
- `function inverse_mat4(m: Mat4) -> Mat4?`, called `linear.inverse_mat4(m)`: The inverse of `m`, the matrix that undoes it, by Gauss and Jordan's elimination with partial pivoting. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rotation_mat2(angle: f64) -> Mat2`, called `linear.rotation_mat2(angle)`: The rotation of the plane by `angle`, counterclockwise.
- `function scaling_mat2(by: Vec2) -> Mat2`, called `linear.scaling_mat2(by)`: The scaling of the plane by `by.x` along x and `by.y` along y.
- `function translation_mat3(by: Vec2) -> Mat3`, called `linear.translation_mat3(by)`: The translation of the plane by `by`, as an affine map: a 3 by 3 matrix acting on `(x, y, 1)`, its translation in `z_axis`.
- `function transform_point2(m: Mat3, p: Vec2) -> Vec2`, called `linear.transform_point2(m, p)`: The point `p` of the plane sent by the affine map `m`: `m * (p.x, p.y, 1)`, its third part dropped, so the translation applies.
- `function transform_vector2(m: Mat3, v: Vec2) -> Vec2`, called `linear.transform_vector2(m, v)`: The direction `v` of the plane sent by the affine map `m`: `m * (v.x, v.y, 0)`, so the translation does not apply.
- `function scaling_mat3(by: Vec3) -> Mat3`, called `linear.scaling_mat3(by)`: The scaling of space by `by.x`, `by.y` and `by.z` along the three axes; with `by.z` 1, the scaling of the plane as an affine map.
- `function rotation_mat3(axis: Vec3, angle: f64) -> Mat3?`, called `linear.rotation_mat3(axis, angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about `axis`, counterclockwise as seen from the axis's tip: Rodrigues' matrix, `1 - cos(angle)` taken as `2 sin^2(angle / 2)` so a small angle keeps its digits. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rotation_x_mat3(angle: f64) -> Mat3`, called `linear.rotation_x_mat3(angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about the x axis, turning y toward z.
- `function rotation_y_mat3(angle: f64) -> Mat3`, called `linear.rotation_y_mat3(angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about the y axis, turning z toward x.
- `function rotation_z_mat3(angle: f64) -> Mat3`, called `linear.rotation_z_mat3(angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about the z axis, turning x toward y: also the rotation of the plane as an affine map.
- `function extend_mat3(m: Mat3) -> Mat4`, called `linear.extend_mat3(m)`: The 3 by 3 matrix `m` as a transform of space: in the upper left of the identity of size 4, which translates nothing.
- `function upper_mat3(m: Mat4) -> Mat3`, called `linear.upper_mat3(m)`: The upper left 3 by 3 of `m`: a transform's linear part, its rotation and scaling without its translation.
- `function translation_mat4(by: Vec3) -> Mat4`, called `linear.translation_mat4(by)`: The translation of space by `by`.
- `function scaling_mat4(by: Vec3) -> Mat4`, called `linear.scaling_mat4(by)`: The scaling of space by `by.x`, `by.y` and `by.z` along the three axes.
- `function rotation_mat4(axis: Vec3, angle: f64) -> Mat4?`, called `linear.rotation_mat4(axis, angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about `axis`, as a transform. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rotation_x_mat4(angle: f64) -> Mat4`, called `linear.rotation_x_mat4(angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about the x axis, as a transform.
- `function rotation_y_mat4(angle: f64) -> Mat4`, called `linear.rotation_y_mat4(angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about the y axis, as a transform.
- `function rotation_z_mat4(angle: f64) -> Mat4`, called `linear.rotation_z_mat4(angle)`: The rotation of space by `angle` about the z axis, as a transform.
- `function transform_point3(m: Mat4, p: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.transform_point3(m, p)`: The point `p` sent by the transform `m`: `m * (p, 1)`, its weight dropped, so the translation applies and no division is made; for an affine `m`, whose last row is `(0, 0, 0, 1)`.
- `function transform_vector3(m: Mat4, v: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.transform_vector3(m, v)`: The direction `v` sent by the transform `m`: `m * (v, 0)`, so the translation does not apply.
- `function project_point3(m: Mat4, p: Vec3) -> Vec3?`, called `linear.project_point3(m, p)`: The point `p` sent by the projection `m` and divided by its weight: `m * (p, 1)` over its `w`, the point in normalized device coordinates. Fails `invalid`.
- `function look_at(eye: Vec3, target: Vec3, up: Vec3, hand: Hand) -> Mat4?`, called `linear.look_at(eye: eye, target: target, up: up, hand)`: The view matrix of a camera at `eye` looking at `target`: it sends `eye` to the origin and the direction of view to minus z in a right-handed frame, plus z in a left-handed one, with `up` as near to plus y as it can be. Fails `invalid`.
- `function perspective(fov_y: f64, aspect: f64, near: f64, far: f64, hand: Hand, depth: Depth) -> Mat4?`, called `linear.perspective(fov_y: fov_y, aspect: aspect, near: near, far: far, hand, depth)`: The perspective projection of a camera that sees `fov_y` radians from its bottom edge to its top one: it sends the near plane to the depth's near end and the far plane to its far end, and leaves the division by `w` to `project_point3` or to the graphics card. Fails `invalid`.
- `function orthographic(left: f64, right: f64, bottom: f64, top: f64, near: f64, far: f64, hand: Hand, depth: Depth) -> Mat4?`, called `linear.orthographic(left: left, right: right, bottom: bottom, top: top, near: near, far: far, hand, depth)`: The orthographic projection of the box from `left` to `right`, `bottom` to `top` and `near` to `far` in front of the camera: it sends the box to the cube of normalized device coordinates, the near face to the depth's near end and the far one to its far end, with no perspective. Fails `invalid`.
- `function identity_quat() -> Quat`, called `linear.identity_quat()`: The quaternion of no rotation, `1 + 0i + 0j + 0k`.
- `function rotation_quat(axis: Vec3, angle: f64) -> Quat?`, called `linear.rotation_quat(axis, angle)`: The unit quaternion of the rotation by `angle` about `axis`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function axes_of(order: EulerOrder) -> [i64]`, called `linear.axes_of(order)`: The axes of `order`, 0 for x, 1 for y and 2 for z, in the order of the turns.
- `function euler_quat(angles: Euler) -> Quat`, called `linear.euler_quat(angles)`: The unit quaternion of the rotation `angles` names: the turn by `angles.first` about the order's first axis, then `angles.second` about its second as the first turn left it, then `angles.third` about its third.
- `function to_euler(q: Quat, order: EulerOrder) -> Euler`, called `linear.to_euler(q, order)`: The three angles of the rotation `q` stands for, in the order `order`: the outer two from -pi to pi, the middle one from -pi/2 to pi/2 for Tait and Bryan's orders and from 0 to pi for the proper ones.
- `function arc_quat(from: Vec3, to: Vec3) -> Quat?`, called `linear.arc_quat(from: from, to: to)`: The shortest rotation that turns the direction of `from` into the direction of `to`, about their common perpendicular; for opposite directions, a half turn about an axis perpendicular to `from`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_axis_angle(q: Quat) -> AxisAngle`, called `linear.to_axis_angle(q)`: The rotation `q` stands for, as an axis and an angle from 0 to pi.
- `function to_mat3(q: Quat) -> Mat3`, called `linear.to_mat3(q)`: The rotation matrix of `q`.
- `function to_mat4(q: Quat) -> Mat4`, called `linear.to_mat4(q)`: The rotation of `q` as a transform.
- `function to_quat(m: Mat3) -> Quat`, called `linear.to_quat(m)`: The unit quaternion of the rotation matrix `m`, by Shepperd's method, its real part never negative.
- `function multiply_quat(a: Quat, b: Quat) -> Quat`, called `linear.multiply_quat(a: a, b: b)`: The product `a * b`, Hamilton's: the rotation `b`, then the rotation `a`.
- `function rotate_vec3(q: Quat, v: Vec3) -> Vec3`, called `linear.rotate_vec3(q, v)`: The vector `v` turned by the rotation `q`.
- `function conjugate_quat(q: Quat) -> Quat`, called `linear.conjugate_quat(q)`: The conjugate of `q`, its vector part negated: the inverse rotation, for a unit quaternion.
- `function inverse_quat(q: Quat) -> Quat?`, called `linear.inverse_quat(q)`: The inverse of `q`, its conjugate over its squared length, so `multiply_quat` of the two is 1. Fails `invalid`.
- `function normalize_quat(q: Quat) -> Quat?`, called `linear.normalize_quat(q)`: `q` scaled to length 1, a rotation's own quaternion. Fails `invalid`.
- `function dot_quat(a: Quat, b: Quat) -> f64`, called `linear.dot_quat(a: a, b: b)`: The dot product of `a` and `b` as four numbers: the cosine of half the angle between their rotations, for unit quaternions, up to its sign.
- `function length_quat(q: Quat) -> f64`, called `linear.length_quat(q)`: The length of `q` as four numbers, computed so that it overflows or underflows only where the answer does.
- `function slerp(from: Quat, to: Quat, t: f64) -> Quat`, called `linear.slerp(from: from, to: to, t)`: The rotation a fraction `t` of the way from `from` to `to` along the shorter arc, at a constant speed: spherical linear interpolation, its angle taken as `2 atan2(|a - b|, |a + b|)`, which keeps its digits for close rotations.


### math/sparse

Layer 1, named `use <rebel>/math/sparse`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/math/sparse/).

Matrices of any size of `f64` whose entries are mostly zero, held as compressed sparse rows (CSR): built from triplets, read, transposed, multiplied by a vector, their rows summed and normalized, and the steady states two power iterations find on them, a Markov chain's and PageRank's.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a shape below 0, a triplet outside its matrix, a vector of the wrong length, a matrix that is not square or not a chain's, and a setting of an iteration out of its range: `from_triplets`, `multiply_vector`, `scale_rows`, `steady_state`, `pagerank`.
- `record Matrix(rows: i64, columns: i64, starts: [i64], indices: [i64], values: [f64])`: A matrix of `rows` rows and `columns` columns, its entries that are not zero kept row by row.
- `record Triplet(row: i64, column: i64, value: f64)`: One entry of a matrix, at a row and a column.
- `function from_triplets(rows: i64, columns: i64, triplets: [Triplet]) -> Matrix?`, called `sparse.from_triplets(rows: rows, columns: columns, triplets)`: The matrix of `rows` rows and `columns` columns that `triplets` write, every other place zero; two triplets of one place summed, as SciPy's `coo_matrix` sums them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function identity(n: i64) -> Matrix`, called `sparse.identity(n)`: The identity matrix of `n` rows and columns: ones on its diagonal.
- `function entries_of(m: Matrix) -> [Triplet]`, called `sparse.entries_of(m)`: The entries `m` keeps, row by row and by column within a row.
- `function value_at(m: Matrix, row: i64, column: i64) -> f64`, called `sparse.value_at(m, row: row, column: column)`: The value at `row` and `column` of `m`: an entry's, or 0 where `m` keeps none there.
- `function count_of_entries(m: Matrix) -> i64`, called `sparse.count_of_entries(m)`: How many entries `m` keeps, a place's two triplets counted once.
- `function transpose(m: Matrix) -> Matrix`, called `sparse.transpose(m)`: `m` transposed: its rows made columns.
- `function multiply_vector(m: Matrix, v: [f64]) -> [f64]?`, called `sparse.multiply_vector(m, v)`: The product `m * v`, a vector of `m.rows` values. Fails `invalid`.
- `function row_sums(m: Matrix) -> [f64]`, called `sparse.row_sums(m)`: The sum of each row of `m`, `m.rows` values.
- `function column_sums(m: Matrix) -> [f64]`, called `sparse.column_sums(m)`: The sum of each column of `m`, `m.columns` values.
- `function scale_rows(m: Matrix, factors: [f64]) -> Matrix?`, called `sparse.scale_rows(m, factors)`: `m` with each row multiplied by its factor. Fails `invalid`.
- `function normalize_rows(m: Matrix) -> Matrix`, called `sparse.normalize_rows(m)`: `m` with each row divided by its sum, so that every row that sums to anything but 0 sums to 1: the links of a graph made a chain's probabilities of moving.
- `function norm_l1(v: [f64]) -> f64`, called `sparse.norm_l1(v)`: The sum of the absolute values of `v`: its manhattan norm.
- `function norm_l2(v: [f64]) -> f64`, called `sparse.norm_l2(v)`: The square root of the sum of the squares of `v`: its euclidean norm, computed over the values divided by the largest, so that no square passes the range of an `f64` where the norm does not.
- `function norm_max(v: [f64]) -> f64`, called `sparse.norm_max(v)`: The largest absolute value of `v`: its maximum norm.
- `record Settled(vector: [f64], iterations: i64, change: f64)`: What a power iteration settled on: the vector, how many rounds it took, and how far the last round moved it, so that a program reads whether it settled.
- `function steady_state(p: Matrix, tolerance: f64, most_iterations: i64) -> Settled?`, called `sparse.steady_state(p, tolerance, most_iterations)`: The steady state of the Markov chain whose probabilities of moving are `p`, row `i` holding the chances of moving from state `i` to each: the vector `x` that `x = x p` keeps, found by power iteration from the uniform vector. Fails `invalid`.
- `function pagerank(links: Matrix, damping: f64, tolerance: f64, most_iterations: i64) -> Settled?`, called `sparse.pagerank(links, damping: damping, tolerance: tolerance, most_iterations)`: The PageRank of every page of a graph whose links are `links`, row `i` holding the weight of the link from page `i` to each page: the steady state of a surfer who follows a link with the chance `damping`, chosen by its weight, and jumps to any page with the rest; a page with no link out jumps to any page. Fails `invalid`.


### image

Layer 1, named `use <rebel>/image`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/).

Images in memory: a grid of pixels of one format, made, read and written pixel by pixel, converted between formats, cut, scaled, turned, combined, drawn on, measured, and reduced to a palette.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an input that is not what the call reads: a file that is not its format, a pixel buffer of the wrong length, a rectangle outside an image, a palette of no colour or of more than 256.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of an image larger than the caller allows: a width, height or count of pixels past `Limits`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a file of a known format in a form no decoder here reads (a JPEG coded arithmetically, a PNG of an unknown compression method), and of an image a format has no form for (an alpha channel in JPEG).
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH: i64`, value `65536`: The widest image `default_limits` allows, in pixels.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_HEIGHT: i64`, value `65536`: The tallest image `default_limits` allows, in pixels.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_PIXELS: i64`, value `67108864`: The most pixels `default_limits` allows in all the images one call answers: 8192 by 8192, 256 MiB as RGBA of 8 bits.
- `record Limits(max_width: i64, max_height: i64, max_pixels: i64)`: How large an image a decoder may answer.
- `function default_limits() -> Limits`, called `image.default_limits()`: Limits of `DEFAULT_MAX_WIDTH`, `DEFAULT_MAX_HEIGHT` and `DEFAULT_MAX_PIXELS`: an image of 8192 by 8192 passes, one of 65,536 by 65,536 does not.
- `function check_limits(limits: Limits, width: i64, height: i64) -> ()?`, called `image.check_limits(limits, width: width, height: height)`: Nothing where an image of `width` by `height` is within `limits`. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `variant Format = .gray | .gray_alpha | .rgb | .rgba | .gray16 | .gray_alpha16 | .rgb16 | .rgba16`: How a pixel is held: which channels, and 8 or 16 bits for each sample.
- `record Color(r: u8, g: u8, b: u8, a: u8)`: A colour of 8 bits a channel, alpha straight.
- `function channels_of(format: Format) -> i64`, called `image.channels_of(format)`: How many samples a pixel of `format` holds: 1, 2, 3 or 4.
- `function bits_of(format: Format) -> i64`, called `image.bits_of(format)`: How many bits a sample of `format` holds: 8 or 16.
- `function pixel_bytes_of(format: Format) -> i64`, called `image.pixel_bytes_of(format)`: How many bytes a pixel of `format` holds: its channels times 1 or 2.
- `function has_alpha(format: Format) -> bool`, called `image.has_alpha(format)`: Whether a pixel of `format` holds an alpha sample.
- `function format_of(channels: i64, bits: i64) -> Format?`, called `image.format_of(channels: channels, bits: bits)`: The format of `channels` samples of `bits` bits: 1 gray, 2 gray and alpha, 3 RGB, 4 RGBA. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Image(width: i64, height: i64, format: Format, pixels: [u8])`: An image: `width` by `height` pixels of one `format`, held row after row from the top, each row from the left.
- `function blank(width: i64, height: i64, format: Format) -> Image?`, called `image.blank(width: width, height: height, format)`: An image of `width` by `height` pixels of `format`, every sample 0: black, and transparent where the format has alpha. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function from_pixels(width: i64, height: i64, format: Format, pixels: [u8]) -> Image?`, called `image.from_pixels(width: width, height: height, format, pixels)`: An image of `width` by `height` pixels of `format` holding `pixels`, row after row from the top. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function is_valid(img: Image) -> bool`, called `image.is_valid(img)`: Whether `img` holds as many bytes as its width, height and format say, none of them negative: whether the other functions accept it.
- `function color_at(img: Image, x: i64, y: i64) -> Color`, called `image.color_at(img, x: x, y: y)`: The colour of the pixel at column `x` and row `y` of `img`, in 8 bits a channel: a gray sample stands for red, green and blue alike, a format without alpha answers alpha 255, and a 16-bit sample keeps its high byte.
- `function set_color(@img: Image, x: i64, y: i64, color: Color)`, called `image.set_color(@img, x: x, y: y, color)`: Writes `color` into the pixel at column `x` and row `y` of `img`, converted to its format: a gray format takes the colour's luma (Go's `color.GrayModel`), a format without alpha drops the alpha, a 16-bit one takes each value times 257.
- `function samples_at(img: Image, x: i64, y: i64) -> [u16]`, called `image.samples_at(img, x: x, y: y)`: The samples of the pixel at column `x` and row `y` of `img`, exactly as held: `channels_of(img.format)` of them, each 0 to 255 or, at 16 bits, 0 to 65,535.
- `function set_samples(@img: Image, x: i64, y: i64, samples: [u16])`, called `image.set_samples(@img, x: x, y: y, samples)`: Writes `samples` into the pixel at column `x` and row `y` of `img`, exactly.
- `function convert(img: Image, to: Format) -> Image`, called `image.convert(img, to)`: `img` held in format `to`, pixel by pixel.
- `function flatten(img: Image, background: Color) -> Image`, called `image.flatten(img, background)`: `img` blended over `background`, its alpha dropped: each pixel's colour weighted by its alpha, the background's by the rest.
- `function crop(img: Image, x: i64, y: i64, width: i64, height: i64) -> Image?`, called `image.crop(img, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height)`: The rectangle of `img` whose top left corner is column `x`, row `y`, of `width` by `height` pixels, as a new image. Fails `invalid`.
- `function flip_horizontal(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.flip_horizontal(img)`: `img` mirrored left to right: the first column becomes the last.
- `function flip_vertical(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.flip_vertical(img)`: `img` mirrored top to bottom: the first row becomes the last.
- `function rotate_90(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.rotate_90(img)`: `img` turned a quarter counter-clockwise: its first row becomes the first column, read from the bottom, and width and height swap.
- `function rotate_180(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.rotate_180(img)`: `img` turned half a turn: the top left pixel becomes the bottom right.
- `function rotate_270(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.rotate_270(img)`: `img` turned a quarter clockwise, three quarters counter-clockwise: its first row becomes the last column, and width and height swap.
- `function transpose(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.transpose(img)`: `img` mirrored across its main diagonal: the pixel at column x, row y goes to column y, row x, and width and height swap.
- `function transverse(img: Image) -> Image`, called `image.transverse(img)`: `img` mirrored across its other diagonal: the top left pixel becomes the bottom right, and width and height swap.
- `function apply_orientation(img: Image, orientation: i64) -> Image?`, called `image.apply_orientation(img, orientation)`: `img` as an EXIF orientation says to show it: 1 as it is, 2 mirrored, 3 turned half, 4 flipped, 5 transposed, 6 turned a quarter clockwise, 7 transversed, 8 turned a quarter counter-clockwise, as Pillow's `ImageOps.exif_transpose` applies them. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Resampling = .nearest | .box | .bilinear | .hamming | .bicubic | .lanczos`: How a pixel is computed from the pixels around the place it comes from.
- `function resize(img: Image, width: i64, height: i64, resampling: Resampling) -> Image?`, called `image.resize(img, width: width, height: height, resampling)`: `img` scaled to `width` by `height` pixels, each output pixel weighted from the input pixels under its filter. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function thumbnail(img: Image, max_width: i64, max_height: i64, resampling: Resampling) -> Image?`, called `image.thumbnail(img, max_width: max_width, max_height: max_height, resampling)`: `img` scaled down to fit inside `max_width` by `max_height`, its proportions kept, each side rounded to the nearest pixel and held to 1 and the bound; an image that fits already answers a copy, never enlarged. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rotate(img: Image, degrees: f64, resampling: Resampling, expand: bool, background: Color) -> Image`, called `image.rotate(img, degrees, resampling, expand, background)`: `img` turned `degrees` counter-clockwise about its centre, each pixel computed from the input under `resampling`.
- `function paste(@onto: Image, source: Image, x: i64, y: i64)`, called `image.paste(onto: @onto, source: source, x: x, y: y)`: Writes `source` into `onto` with its top left corner at column `x`, row `y`, replacing what was there, alpha and all (Pillow's `paste` with no mask, Go's `draw.Src`).
- `function composite(@onto: Image, source: Image, x: i64, y: i64)`, called `image.composite(onto: @onto, source: source, x: x, y: y)`: Blends `source` over `onto` with its top left corner at column `x`, row `y`, by `source`'s alpha (Porter and Duff's "over", Pillow's `alpha_composite`, Go's `draw.Over`).
- `function blend(first: Image, second: Image, amount: f64) -> Image?`, called `image.blend(first: first, second: second, amount)`: `first` and `second` mixed, each sample `first` × (1 - `amount`) + `second` × `amount`, rounded: Pillow's `Image.blend`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function draw_line(@img: Image, from_x: i64, from_y: i64, to_x: i64, to_y: i64, color: Color)`, called `image.draw_line(@img, from_x: from_x, from_y: from_y, to_x: to_x, to_y: to_y, color)`: Draws the line from column `from_x`, row `from_y`, to column `to_x`, row `to_y`, both ends included, one pixel wide: each column (or each row, where the line is steeper) gets the pixel nearest to the true line.
- `function draw_rect(@img: Image, x: i64, y: i64, width: i64, height: i64, color: Color)`, called `image.draw_rect(@img, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height, color)`: Draws the border of the rectangle whose top left pixel is column `x`, row `y`, of `width` by `height` pixels, one pixel wide and inside the rectangle.
- `function fill_rect(@img: Image, x: i64, y: i64, width: i64, height: i64, color: Color)`, called `image.fill_rect(@img, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height, color)`: Fills the rectangle whose top left pixel is column `x`, row `y`, of `width` by `height` pixels with `color`, written with no blending; what falls outside `img` is dropped.
- `function draw_circle(@img: Image, center_x: i64, center_y: i64, radius: i64, color: Color)`, called `image.draw_circle(@img, center_x: center_x, center_y: center_y, radius: radius, color)`: Draws the circle of `radius` pixels about column `center_x`, row `center_y`: the pixels of the disc of `fill_circle` that touch a pixel outside it above, below, left or right, so the line is one pixel wide and closed.
- `function fill_circle(@img: Image, center_x: i64, center_y: i64, radius: i64, color: Color)`, called `image.fill_circle(@img, center_x: center_x, center_y: center_y, radius: radius, color)`: Fills the disc of `radius` pixels about column `center_x`, row `center_y`: every pixel whose distance from the centre, dx² + dy², is at most radius × (radius + 1), the disc whose edge passes half a pixel past `radius`.
- `function histogram(img: Image) -> [i64]`, called `image.histogram(img)`: How many samples of `img` hold each value, channel after channel: 256 counts for the first channel, then 256 for the next, as Pillow's `histogram` lays them out.
- `record Indexed(width: i64, height: i64, palette: [Color], indices: [u8])`: An image of colours chosen from a palette: one byte a pixel, each the index of its colour.
- `function palette_of(img: Image, most: i64) -> [Color]?`, called `image.palette_of(img, most)`: At most `most` colours that stand for those of `img`, by median cut: the colours are split in two at the median of the channel they spread most along, again and again, and each part answers the mean of its colours, each weighted by how many pixels hold it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_indexed(img: Image, palette: [Color], dither: bool) -> Indexed?`, called `image.to_indexed(img, palette, dither)`: `img` as indices into `palette`: each pixel the nearest colour, by the sum of the squared differences of its four channels, the first where two are as near. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_indexed(ix: Indexed) -> Image?`, called `image.from_indexed(ix)`: `ix` as an image of its colours: RGBA where an entry of its palette is not opaque, RGB otherwise. Fails `invalid`.
- `function web_safe_palette() -> [Color]`, called `image.web_safe_palette()`: The 216 colours of the web-safe palette, every mix of red, green and blue at 0, 51, 102, 153, 204 and 255, blue changing fastest: Go's `palette.WebSafe`, each colour opaque.
- `variant Kind = .png | .jpeg | .gif | .bmp | .netpbm | .tiff | .ico | .webp`: Which format a file is in, from its first bytes.
- `function kind_of(data: [u8]) -> Kind?`, called `image.kind_of(data)`: The kind of file `data` begins as, read from its signature alone; the rest is not checked, so a decoder may still fail `invalid`. Fails `invalid`.


### io

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/io`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/io/).

The stream: the one handle a program reads and writes through, whatever stands behind it (a file, a pipe, a terminal, the process's own input and outputs, a child's ends, a socket), and the buffered reader over one that reads lines, characters and bytes up to a byte.

- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `failure.CLOSED`: The stream, or its other end, is closed: a stream closed by `close`, a write to a pipe or a socket whose reader is gone, or a stream that ended before the count `read_exact` promised.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `failure.NOT_TEXT`: Bytes read as text are not UTF-8.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `failure.INVALID`: A count below 0, or an argument the layer refuses; the message says which.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `failure.PERMISSION`: The system refuses this to the program: a read of a stream opened to write, a write of one opened to read, a file's permissions.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `failure.LIMIT`: The process or the machine has no descriptor, room or memory left.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `failure.UNSUPPORTED`: The stream has no such thing: a position, a size or a sync on a pipe, a terminal or a socket.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `failure.TIMEOUT`: The time a socket's stream was allowed ran out while a call waited on it (`net` sets the deadline).
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `failure.STOPPED`: The program was asked to stop while a call waited on a socket's stream.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `failure.FAILED`: The system refused for a reason none of the other codes names; the message carries the system's own number.
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `failure.FILE_NOT_FOUND`: A path names nothing: what `last_failure` answers after a floor's `open`.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `failure.EXISTS`: The file is there already: what `last_failure` answers after a floor's `open` that must create it.
- `constant IS_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `failure.IS_A_DIRECTORY`: A path names a folder: what `last_failure` answers after a floor's `open`.
- `constant NOT_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `failure.NOT_A_DIRECTORY`: A name on a path's way is a file: what `last_failure` answers after a floor's `open`.
- `record Stream(handle: hero_stream.Stream, borrowed: bool, name: str)`: A stream open to read, to write, or both.
- `record Pipe(reader: Stream, writer: Stream)`: The two ends of a pipe, which `pipe` answers: what is written to `writer` is read from `reader`, in order.
- `variant Origin = .start | .current | .end`: Where `seek` counts its offset from.
- `function stdin() -> Stream`, called `io.stdin()`: The process's own input, as a stream.
- `function stdout() -> Stream`, called `io.stdout()`: The process's own output, as a stream, borrowed as `stdin` is.
- `function stderr() -> Stream`, called `io.stderr()`: The process's own error output, as a stream, borrowed as `stdin` is.
- `function pipe() -> Pipe?`, called `io.pipe()`: A new pipe's two ends, each closed by its own `close`. Fails `limit`.
- `function close(@s: Stream) -> ()?`, called `io.close(@s)`: Closes `s` and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(s: Stream) -> bool`, called `io.is_closed(s)`: Whether `close` has emptied this place.
- `function read(s: Stream, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `io.read(s, n)`: Up to `n` bytes of `s`, waiting for one: at most 65,536 at once, and fewer where fewer are there. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `permission`.
- `function read_exact(s: Stream, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `io.read_exact(s, n)`: Exactly `n` bytes of `s`, waiting for each. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function read_all(s: Stream) -> [u8]?`, called `io.read_all(s)`: Every byte of `s` from where it stands to its end, waiting for the end: an empty list where it is at its end already. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function read_all_text(s: Stream) -> str?`, called `io.read_all_text(s)`: Every byte of `s` to its end, as text. Fails `not_text`.
- `function write(s: Stream, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `io.write(s, data)`: Writes every byte of `data` to `s`, as many times as the system needs. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function write_text(s: Stream, text: str) -> ()?`, called `io.write_text(s, text)`: Writes every byte of `text` to `s`, as `write` does. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function write_line(s: Stream, line: str) -> ()?`, called `io.write_line(s, line)`: Writes `line` and a line feed to `s` in one write, as `write` does. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function write_lines(s: Stream, lines: [str]) -> ()?`, called `io.write_lines(s, lines)`: Writes each of `lines` followed by a line feed, in one write, as `write` does. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function copy(from: Stream, to: Stream) -> i64?`, called `io.copy(from: from, to: to)`: Copies everything `from` holds, to its end, into `to`, and answers how many bytes, 65,536 at a time. Fails as `read` and `write` do; the bytes copied before a failure stay written.
- `function copy_n(from: Stream, to: Stream, n: i64) -> i64?`, called `io.copy_n(from: from, to: to, n)`: Copies at most `n` bytes of `from` into `to` and answers how many, fewer where `from` ends first. Fails `invalid`.
- `function seek(s: Stream, offset: i64, from: Origin) -> i64?`, called `io.seek(s, offset, from)`: Moves where the next read or write of `s` begins to `offset` bytes from `from`, and answers that position counted from the start. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function position(s: Stream) -> i64?`, called `io.position(s)`: Where the next read or write of `s` begins, counted in bytes from the start. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function size(s: Stream) -> i64?`, called `io.size(s)`: The size in bytes of the file `s` stands on, as the system holds it now. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function truncate(s: Stream, length: i64) -> ()?`, called `io.truncate(s, length)`: Makes the file `s` stands on `length` bytes long, cutting what is past it or adding zero bytes to reach it; where `s` stands does not move. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`.
- `function sync(s: Stream) -> ()?`, called `io.sync(s)`: Answers once the system says every byte written to the file `s` stands on is on the storage itself. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function is_terminal(s: Stream) -> bool?`, called `io.is_terminal(s)`: Whether `s` is a terminal, or a Windows console. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_seekable(s: Stream) -> bool?`, called `io.is_seekable(s)`: Whether `s` has positions, which only a file has: `seek`, `position`, `size` and `truncate` fail `unsupported` on the rest. Fails `closed`.
- `record Reader(stream: Stream, held: buffer.Held)`: A buffered reader over a stream: it reads the stream 65,536 bytes at a time and gives them out by line, by character, up to a byte or by count.
- `function reader(s: Stream) -> Reader`, called `io.reader(s)`: A reader over `s`, holding nothing yet.
- `function read_line(@r: Reader) -> str?`, called `io.read_line(@r)`: The next line of `r` as text, without its end: a line feed, or a carriage return and a line feed. Fails `not_text`.
- `function read_line_with_end(@r: Reader) -> str?`, called `io.read_line_with_end(@r)`: The next line of `r` as text, with its end as it was, "\n" or "\r\n", or none for a last line with no end: "" only at the end. Fails `not_text`.
- `function read_lines(@r: Reader) -> [str]?`, called `io.read_lines(@r)`: Every line left in `r`, each without its end as `read_line` reads it: an empty list at the end. Fails `not_text`.
- `function read_until(@r: Reader, byte: u8) -> [u8]?`, called `io.read_until(@r, byte)`: The bytes of `r` up to and including the first `byte`, or to the end where no `byte` comes: an empty list at the end. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function read_char(@r: Reader) -> str?`, called `io.read_char(@r)`: The next character of `r`, of one to four bytes: "" at the end. Fails `not_text`.
- `function read_n(@r: Reader, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `io.read_n(@r, n)`: At most `n` bytes of `r`, waiting until `n` have come or the stream ends: fewer only at the end, and an empty list there. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_rest(@r: Reader) -> [u8]?`, called `io.read_rest(@r)`: Every byte left in `r`, what it holds first, then its stream to the end. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function read_rest_text(@r: Reader) -> str?`, called `io.read_rest_text(@r)`: Every byte left in `r`, as text. Fails `not_text`.
- `function peek(@r: Reader, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `io.peek(@r, n)`: The next `n` bytes of `r` without reading them: the next call gives them out again. Fails `invalid`.
- `function skip(@r: Reader, n: i64) -> i64?`, called `io.skip(@r, n)`: Reads and drops at most `n` bytes of `r`, and answers how many: fewer only at the end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function at_end(@r: Reader) -> bool?`, called `io.at_end(@r)`: Whether `r` has no byte left, waiting for one where it holds none and the stream has not ended. Fails `closed`, `permission`.
- `function buffered(r: Reader) -> [u8]`, called `io.buffered(r)`: The bytes `r` holds and has not given out, read from its stream already: what a read of the stream itself would no longer see.
- `function of_handle(handle: hero_stream.Stream, name: str) -> Stream`, called `io.of_handle(handle, name)`: The stream over `handle`, a handle of the floor `io/hero_stream` that the caller owns, called `name` in messages: how `fs`, `process` and `net` hand out what they open.
- `function last_failure<T>(asked: str) -> T?`, called `io.last_failure(asked)`: The failure the floor's last call on this thread left, as a `T?` whose message begins with `asked`: how `fs`, `process` and `net` turn a `nullptr` or a -1 of `io/hero_stream` into a code of README § A4. Fails `file_not_found`, `exists`, `is_a_directory`, `not_a_directory`, `permission`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `closed`, `timeout`, `stopped`, `invalid`, `failed`.


### json

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/json`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/json/).

JSON read and written: the text of RFC 8259 read into a tree a program matches on, the tree written back as text, and the functions that read a value out of it.

- `variant Value = .null_value | .boolean(v: bool) | .number(v: f64) | .text(v: str) | .list(items: [Value]) | .object(members: {str: Value})`: One JSON value.
- `function equals(a: Value, b: Value) -> bool`, called `json.equals(a: a, b: b)`: Whether `a` and `b` are the same JSON value: numbers by value, texts by bytes, lists element by element, objects member by member whatever their order.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text that is not JSON, of a value that is not of the kind asked for, and of a pointer that is not one.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a value that holds a `nan` or an infinity, which no JSON says: `format`, `format_indented`, `format_with` unless its options ask for Python's words, and `format_canonical`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a key an object does not hold and of an index past a list's end.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a number past what its type holds: a number in a text that no `f64` reaches, an integer past `MAX_EXACT_INT` where an exact one was asked.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `512`: The deepest nesting `parse` reads: `1` is 0 deep, `[]` is 1, `[[]]` is 2.
- `constant MAX_EXACT_INT: i64`, value `9007199254740991`: The largest integer an `f64` holds with no other integer reading to the same `f64`: 2^53 - 1.
- `record ParseOptions(max_depth: i64, duplicate_keys: bool, control_characters: bool, lone_surrogates: bool, non_finite: bool, exact_integers: bool)`: How a text is read.
- `record Parsed(value: Value, next: i64)`: What `parse_next` answers.
- `function strict_parse_options() -> ParseOptions`, called `json.strict_parse_options()`: The options that read RFC 8259 and nothing wider: nesting no deeper than `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`, and every other field `false`.
- `function parse(text: str) -> Value?`, called `json.parse(text)`: The value `text` writes, read as `strict_parse_options` reads. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function parse_with(text: str, options: ParseOptions) -> Value?`, called `json.parse_with(text, options)`: The value `text` writes, read as `options` say. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function parse_next(text: str, from: i64, options: ParseOptions) -> Parsed?`, called `json.parse_next(text, from, options)`: The one value that begins at byte `from` of `text`, after any white space, and where the next begins. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_valid(text: str) -> bool`, called `json.is_valid(text)`: Whether `text` is JSON: true exactly where `parse` succeeds.
- `variant Cut = .whole | .empty | .container | .key | .member | .text | .number | .word`: What a JSON text that has not finished arriving stopped inside, as `parse_partial` says it.
- `record Partial(value: Value, cut: Cut, pointer: str)`: What `parse_partial` answers: the value a text holds so far, and where it stopped.
- `function parse_partial(text: str) -> Partial?`, called `json.parse_partial(text)`: The value a JSON text holds so far, where the text has not finished arriving: the arguments of a tool as a model streams them, read again as each piece comes. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `record FormatOptions(multiline: bool, indent: str, prefix: str, spaced: bool, sort_keys: bool, ascii_only: bool, escape_html: bool, escape_js: bool, non_finite: bool)`: How a value is written.
- `function compact_format_options() -> FormatOptions`, called `json.compact_format_options()`: The options of the shortest text: one line, no white space, the members in the order the object holds them, and no escape RFC 8259 does not oblige.
- `function format(v: Value) -> str?`, called `json.format(v)`: `v` as JSON on one line with no white space. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function format_indented(v: Value, width: i64) -> str?`, called `json.format_indented(v, width)`: `v` as JSON over several lines, one element or member a line and `": "` after a key. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_with(v: Value, options: FormatOptions) -> str?`, called `json.format_with(v, options)`: `v` as JSON, written as `options` say. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function format_canonical(v: Value) -> str?`, called `json.format_canonical(v)`: `v` as the one text RFC 8785 gives it, so that two programs that hold equal values write equal bytes. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function quote(s: str) -> str`, called `json.quote(s)`: `s` as a JSON string, between its quotes.
- `function unquote(token: str) -> str?`, called `json.unquote(token)`: The text a JSON string writes, its quotes taken off and its escapes read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_compact(text: str) -> str?`, called `json.to_compact(text)`: `text` on one line with no white space between its tokens, each token kept as it was written. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_indented(text: str, width: i64) -> str?`, called `json.to_indented(text, width)`: `text` over several lines, laid out as `format_indented` lays a value out, each token kept as it was written. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_html_safe(text: str) -> str`, called `json.to_html_safe(text)`: `text` with `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 written as `\u003c`, `\u003e`, `\u0026`, `\u2028` and `\u2029`, so that it may stand inside an HTML script element.
- `function kind_of(v: Value) -> str`, called `json.kind_of(v)`: The name of the kind `v` is: `null`, `boolean`, `number`, `text`, `list` or `object`.
- `function is_null(v: Value) -> bool`, called `json.is_null(v)`: Whether `v` is JSON's `null`.
- `function bool_of(v: Value) -> bool?`, called `json.bool_of(v)`: The `bool` of a boolean. Fails `invalid`.
- `function number_of(v: Value) -> f64?`, called `json.number_of(v)`: The `f64` of a number. Fails `invalid`.
- `function int_of(v: Value) -> i64?`, called `json.int_of(v)`: The integer of a number that is one. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function text_of(v: Value) -> str?`, called `json.text_of(v)`: The `str` of a text. Fails `invalid`.
- `function items_of(v: Value) -> [Value]?`, called `json.items_of(v)`: The elements of a list, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function members_of(v: Value) -> {str: Value}?`, called `json.members_of(v)`: The members of an object by key, `keys` giving them in the order they were written. Fails `invalid`.
- `function member(v: Value, key: str) -> Value?`, called `json.member(v, key)`: The member of the object `v` whose key is `key`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function text_at(v: Value, key: str) -> str?`, called `json.text_at(v, key)`: The text of the member `key` of the object `v`: `member`, then `text_of`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function int_at(v: Value, key: str) -> i64?`, called `json.int_at(v, key)`: The integer of the member `key` of the object `v`: `member`, then `int_of`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function bool_at(v: Value, key: str) -> bool?`, called `json.bool_at(v, key)`: The boolean of the member `key` of the object `v`: `member`, then `bool_of`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function items_at(v: Value, key: str) -> [Value]?`, called `json.items_at(v, key)`: The elements of the list in the member `key` of the object `v`, in order: `member`, then `items_of`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function element(v: Value, index: i64) -> Value?`, called `json.element(v, index)`: The element of the list `v` at `index`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function value_at(v: Value, pointer: str) -> Value?`, called `json.value_at(v, pointer)`: The value inside `v` that `pointer` reaches. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function from_int(n: i64) -> Value?`, called `json.from_int(n)`: The number `n` as a value. Fails `does_not_fit`.
- `function pointer_of(tokens: [str]) -> str`, called `json.pointer_of(tokens)`: The pointer whose tokens are `tokens`, in RFC 6901's text.
- `function pointer_tokens(pointer: str) -> [str]?`, called `json.pointer_tokens(pointer)`: The tokens of `pointer`, its escapes read. Fails `invalid`.


### xml

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/xml`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/xml/).

XML read, walked, built and written: a text read by XML 1.0 (fifth edition) and Namespaces in XML 1.0 into a tree a program matches on, the tree walked by names, built by a program, and written back as text, or as the one text Canonical XML 1.0, 1.1 or Exclusive XML Canonicalization gives it, the text XML Signature digests (`xmldsig`).

- `record Name(prefix: str, local: str, space: str)`: A name as XML writes it, and the namespace it stands in.
- `record Attribute(name: Name, value: str)`: One attribute of an element: its name and its value, the value's references read and its white space normalised as XML 1.0 says.
- `record Element(name: Name, attributes: [Attribute], children: [Node])`: One element: its name, its attributes in the order they were written, and what it holds in order.
- `variant Node = .element(v: Element) | .text(v: str) | .comment(v: str) | .instruction(target: str, data: str)`: One thing an element holds.
- `variant Misc = .comment(v: str) | .instruction(target: str, data: str)`: What may stand before and after a document's root: a comment or a processing instruction.
- `variant Declaration = .absent | .present(version: str, encoding: str, standalone: str)`: Whether a document opens with an XML declaration, `<?xml version="1.0"?>`, and what it says.
- `record Document(declaration: Declaration, before: [Misc], root: Element, after: [Misc])`: A whole document: its declaration, the comments and instructions around its one root, and the root.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text that is not well-formed XML, of a tree that would not read back as itself, and of a path that is not one: `parse`, `format`, `element_at` and the escapes fail with it.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of bytes that are not UTF-8: `decode` fails with it.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a declaration naming another encoding than UTF-8: `parse` fails with it.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a text past the depth or the size its reading allows: `parse` fails with it.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a name an element does not hold: `child`, `child_in`, `element_at`, `attribute` and `attribute_in` fail with it.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `512`: The deepest nesting `parse` reads: the root is 1 deep, an element inside it 2.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES: i64`, value `67108864`: The longest text `parse` reads, in bytes: 64 MiB.
- `constant XML_SPACE: str`, value `"http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace"`: The namespace the prefix `xml` stands for, in every document, declared or not.
- `constant XMLNS_SPACE: str`, value `"http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/"`: The namespace of a declaration's own name, `xmlns` and `xmlns:p`.
- `record ParseOptions(max_depth: i64, max_bytes: i64)`: How a text is read: XML 1.0 is read whole either way, and these are the limits the caller sets.
- `function default_options() -> ParseOptions`, called `xml.default_options()`: The options `parse` reads with: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH` and `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`.
- `function parse(text: str) -> Document?`, called `xml.parse(text)`: The document `text` writes, read with `default_options`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function parse_with(text: str, options: ParseOptions) -> Document?`, called `xml.parse_with(text, options)`: The document `text` writes, read with the limits `options` set. Fails `limit`.
- `function decode(bytes: [u8], options: ParseOptions) -> Document?`, called `xml.decode(bytes, options)`: The document `bytes` write, read with the limits `options` set. Fails `not_text`.
- `function is_well_formed(text: str) -> bool`, called `xml.is_well_formed(text)`: Whether `text` is well-formed XML: true exactly where `parse` succeeds.
- `record FormatOptions(multiline: bool, indent: str, self_closing: bool)`: How a tree is written.
- `function compact_format_options() -> FormatOptions`, called `xml.compact_format_options()`: The options of the shortest text: one line, no white space added, and an element with no children written `<a/>`.
- `function format(doc: Document) -> str?`, called `xml.format(doc)`: `doc` as XML on one line, with no white space added. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_indented(doc: Document, width: i64) -> str?`, called `xml.format_indented(doc, width)`: `doc` as XML over several lines, each element of element content on its own line. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_with(doc: Document, options: FormatOptions) -> str?`, called `xml.format_with(doc, options)`: `doc` as XML, written as `options` say. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_element(e: Element, options: FormatOptions) -> str?`, called `xml.format_element(e, options)`: `e` alone as XML, with no declaration, written as `options` say. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_name(n: Name) -> str`, called `xml.format_name(n)`: `n` as XML writes it: `prefix:local`, or `local` where it has no prefix.
- `function escape_text(s: str) -> str?`, called `xml.escape_text(s)`: `s` escaped to stand as an element's text: `&`, `<` and `>` written `&amp;`, `&lt;` and `&gt;`, and a carriage return `&#13;`, so that reading gives back `s` itself. Fails `invalid`.
- `function quote_attribute(s: str) -> str?`, called `xml.quote_attribute(s)`: `s` between `"` as an attribute's value: `&`, `<`, `>` and `"` written `&amp;`, `&lt;`, `&gt;` and `&quot;`, and tab, line feed and carriage return `&#9;`, `&#10;` and `&#13;`, so that reading gives back `s` itself. Fails `invalid`.
- `function unescape(s: str) -> str?`, called `xml.unescape(s)`: `s` with its references read: `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&amp;`, `&quot;` and `&apos;`, and every character reference, `&#65;` and `&#x41;`. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Canonical = .inclusive | .inclusive_11 | .exclusive(prefixes: [str])`: Which Canonical XML `canonicalize` writes: the three XML Signature names, each a W3C Recommendation.
- `record CanonicalOptions(method: Canonical, comments: bool)`: How `canonicalize` writes: which Canonical XML, and whether comments stay.
- `function canonical_options(method: Canonical) -> CanonicalOptions`, called `xml.canonical_options(method)`: The options of `method` without comments, the form XML Signature uses unless it names the other.
- `function canonicalize(doc: Document, options: CanonicalOptions) -> str?`, called `xml.canonicalize(doc, options)`: `doc` as Canonical XML: the one text every document of the same content gives, whatever its quotes, empty-element tags, attribute order and redundant declarations, the text XML Signature digests. Fails `invalid`.
- `function canonicalize_at(doc: Document, place: [i64], options: CanonicalOptions) -> str?`, called `xml.canonicalize_at(doc, place, options)`: The element at `place` in `doc` as Canonical XML, standing where it stands: the document subset of that element and everything inside it, as XML Signature digests an element a reference names. Fails `invalid`.
- `function document(root: Element) -> Document`, called `xml.document(root)`: A document of `root` alone, opening with `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`.
- `function element(name: str) -> Element`, called `xml.element(name)`: An element named `name`, in no namespace, with no attributes and no children.
- `function element_in(space: str, name: str) -> Element`, called `xml.element_in(space: space, name: name)`: An element named `name` in the namespace `space`, with no attributes and no children.
- `function with_attribute(e: Element, name: str, value: str) -> Element`, called `xml.with_attribute(e, name: name, value: value)`: A copy of `e` with the attribute `name` set to `value`: in its place where `e` has one of that name, after the others where not.
- `function with_attribute_in(e: Element, space: str, name: str, value: str) -> Element`, called `xml.with_attribute_in(e, space: space, name: name, value: value)`: A copy of `e` with the attribute `name` of the namespace `space` set to `value`: in its place where `e` has one of that namespace and local name, after the others where not.
- `function without_attribute(e: Element, name: str) -> Element`, called `xml.without_attribute(e, name)`: A copy of `e` without its attribute `name`: `e` itself where it has none.
- `function with_namespace(e: Element, prefix: str, space: str) -> Element`, called `xml.with_namespace(e, prefix: prefix, space: space)`: A copy of `e` declaring `prefix` for the namespace `space`: `xmlns:prefix`, or `xmlns` for the empty prefix, in its place where `e` declares that prefix already, after its attributes where not.
- `function with_text(e: Element, text: str) -> Element`, called `xml.with_text(e, text)`: A copy of `e` with `text` after its children.
- `function with_child(e: Element, inner: Element) -> Element`, called `xml.with_child(e: e, inner: inner)`: A copy of `e` with `inner` after its children.
- `function without_node(doc: Document, place: [i64]) -> Document?`, called `xml.without_node(doc, place)`: A copy of `doc` without the node at `place` and everything inside it, the nodes beside it kept as they are: two texts it parted stand side by side. Fails `invalid`.
- `function child(e: Element, name: str) -> Element?`, called `xml.child(e, name)`: The first child element of `e` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function child_in(e: Element, space: str, local: str) -> Element?`, called `xml.child_in(e, space: space, local: local)`: The first child element of `e` of the namespace `space` and the local name `local`, whatever its prefix. Fails `not_found`.
- `function children_named(e: Element, name: str) -> [Element]`, called `xml.children_named(e, name)`: Every child element of `e` named `name`, in order.
- `function children_in(e: Element, space: str, local: str) -> [Element]`, called `xml.children_in(e, space: space, local: local)`: Every child element of `e` of the namespace `space` and the local name `local`, whatever its prefix, in order.
- `function child_elements(e: Element) -> [Element]`, called `xml.child_elements(e)`: Every child element of `e`, in order, its text, comments and instructions left out.
- `function elements_named(e: Element, name: str) -> [Element]`, called `xml.elements_named(e, name)`: Every element inside `e` named `name`, at any depth, in document order: an element before the elements inside it.
- `function descendants_in(e: Element, space: str, local: str) -> [Element]`, called `xml.descendants_in(e, space: space, local: local)`: Every element inside `e` of the namespace `space` and the local name `local`, at any depth, in document order.
- `function descendants(e: Element) -> [Element]`, called `xml.descendants(e)`: Every element inside `e`, at any depth, in document order.
- `function element_at(e: Element, path: str) -> Element?`, called `xml.element_at(e, path)`: The first element, in document order, that `path` reaches from `e`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function elements_at(e: Element, path: str) -> [Element]?`, called `xml.elements_at(e, path)`: Every element `path` reaches from `e`, in document order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function attribute(e: Element, name: str) -> str?`, called `xml.attribute(e, name)`: The value of the attribute of `e` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function attribute_in(e: Element, space: str, local: str) -> str?`, called `xml.attribute_in(e, space: space, local: local)`: The value of the attribute of `e` of the namespace `space` and the local name `local`, whatever its prefix. Fails `not_found`.
- `function has_attribute(e: Element, name: str) -> bool`, called `xml.has_attribute(e, name)`: Whether `e` has an attribute named `name`.
- `function text_of(e: Element) -> str`, called `xml.text_of(e)`: Every text inside `e`, at any depth, in document order and joined: `<p>a <b>b</b> c</p>` holds `a b c`.
- `function places_with_attribute(doc: Document, name: str, value: str) -> [[i64]]`, called `xml.places_with_attribute(doc, name: name, value: value)`: The places of every element of `doc` whose attribute `name` holds `value`, in document order: each the indices of the children walked from the root, empty for the root, as `element_at_place` and `canonicalize_at` read one.
- `function element_at_place(doc: Document, place: [i64]) -> Element?`, called `xml.element_at_place(doc, place)`: The element at `place` in `doc`. Fails `invalid`.


### html

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/html`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/html/).

HTML read as a browser reads it: any text, however broken, read into the tree a browser builds from it, by the WHATWG HTML Living Standard's tokenizer and tree construction (insertion modes, the adoption agency algorithm, foster parenting, implied end tags), as fetched from html.spec.whatwg.org on 2026-11-16.

- `variant Space = .html | .svg | .mathml`: Which namespace an element stands in: HTML, or the SVG or MathML a document holds inside an `svg` or a `math` element.
- `variant AttributeSpace = .none | .xlink | .xml | .xmlns`: Which namespace an attribute stands in: none, or one of the three the standard gives an attribute of an SVG or MathML element.
- `record Attribute(space: AttributeSpace, name: str, value: str)`: One attribute of an element: its namespace, its local name and its value.
- `variant Quirks = .no_quirks | .quirks | .limited_quirks`: How a document is laid out by a browser, which its doctype decides: the standard's three modes.
- `variant Node = .document | .fragment | .doctype(name: str, public_id: str, system_id: str) | .element(space: Space, name: str, attributes: [Attribute]) | .text(v: str) | .comment(v: str) | .instruction(target: str, data: str)`: One node of a tree.
- `record Document(tree: dom.Tree)`: A document or a fragment: its nodes, each named by its number.
- `record Parsed(document: Document, errors: [ParseError])`: What `parse_with` answers: the document, and every parse error met reading it, in the order they were met.
- `record ParseError(code: str, tag: str, line: i64, column: i64)`: One parse error: where the text breaks a rule of the standard, which reading recovered from.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a selector that cannot be read, and of a change that would put a node inside itself: `select`, `select_all`, `is_match`, `closest`, `append_child`, `insert_before`, `insert_after` and `replace_node` fail with it.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a search that finds nothing, a node with no parent or sibling, and an attribute an element does not hold: `select`, `closest`, the `element_` searches, `name_of`, `attribute`, `parent`, `first_child`, `last_child`, `next_sibling` and `previous_sibling` fail with it.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a text longer than the reading allows: `parse_with` fails with it.
- `constant ROOT: i64`, value `0`: The number of the document node of a tree `parse` reads, and of the fragment node of one `parse_fragment` reads: 0.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `512`: How deep an element nests before reading keeps what is deeper flat: 512, as Chromium reads.
- `record ParseOptions(max_depth: i64, max_bytes: i64, scripting: bool, context: str, context_space: Space)`: How a text is read: the limits the caller sets, the scripting flag, and the element a fragment is read inside.
- `function default_options() -> ParseOptions`, called `html.default_options()`: The options `parse` reads with: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`, no limit on the length, scripting set as in a browser, and a whole document.
- `function parse(text: str) -> Document`, called `html.parse(text)`: The document `text` writes, read as a browser reads it.
- `function parse_fragment(text: str, context: str) -> Document`, called `html.parse_fragment(text: text, context: context)`: A fragment `text` writes, read inside an HTML element named `context`, as a browser reads it into an element's `innerHTML`.
- `function parse_with(text: str, options: ParseOptions) -> Parsed?`, called `html.parse_with(text, options)`: The document or fragment `text` writes, read as `options` say, with every parse error met. Fails `limit`.
- `function quirks_of(doc: Document) -> Quirks`, called `html.quirks_of(doc)`: The mode the doctype of `doc` set.
- `function node_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> Node`, called `html.node_of(doc, node)`: What node number `node` of `doc` is.
- `function is_element(doc: Document, node: i64) -> bool`, called `html.is_element(doc, node)`: Whether node `node` of `doc` is an element.
- `function name_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> str?`, called `html.name_of(doc, node)`: The local name of the element `node`: `p`, `svg`, `foreignObject`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_named(doc: Document, node: i64, name: str) -> bool`, called `html.is_named(doc, node, name)`: Whether `node` is an element named `name`.
- `function attribute(doc: Document, node: i64, name: str) -> str?`, called `html.attribute(doc, node, name)`: The value of the attribute `name` of the element `node`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function has_attribute(doc: Document, node: i64, name: str) -> bool`, called `html.has_attribute(doc, node, name)`: Whether the element `node` has an attribute `name`.
- `function attributes_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [Attribute]`, called `html.attributes_of(doc, node)`: Every attribute of the element `node`, in the order they were written.
- `function classes_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [str]`, called `html.classes_of(doc, node)`: The classes of the element `node`: its `class` attribute split at ASCII white space, in order, a class written twice kept twice.
- `function has_class(doc: Document, node: i64, name: str) -> bool`, called `html.has_class(doc, node, name)`: Whether the element `node` has the class `name`.
- `function parent(doc: Document, node: i64) -> i64?`, called `html.parent(doc, node)`: The node that holds `node`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function children(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [i64]`, called `html.children(doc, node)`: Every child of `node`, in order: elements, text, comments and the rest.
- `function child_elements(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [i64]`, called `html.child_elements(doc, node)`: Every child of `node` that is an element, in order.
- `function first_child(doc: Document, node: i64) -> i64?`, called `html.first_child(doc, node)`: The first child of `node`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function last_child(doc: Document, node: i64) -> i64?`, called `html.last_child(doc, node)`: The last child of `node`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function next_sibling(doc: Document, node: i64) -> i64?`, called `html.next_sibling(doc, node)`: The node after `node`, held by the same parent. Fails `not_found`.
- `function previous_sibling(doc: Document, node: i64) -> i64?`, called `html.previous_sibling(doc, node)`: The node before `node`, held by the same parent. Fails `not_found`.
- `function next_siblings(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [i64]`, called `html.next_siblings(doc, node)`: Every node after `node` held by the same parent, the nearest first.
- `function previous_siblings(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [i64]`, called `html.previous_siblings(doc, node)`: Every node before `node` held by the same parent, the nearest first.
- `function ancestors(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [i64]`, called `html.ancestors(doc, node)`: Every node that holds `node`, its parent first and `ROOT` last.
- `function descendants(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [i64]`, called `html.descendants(doc, node)`: Every node inside `node`, at any depth, in document order: a node before the nodes inside it.
- `function text_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> str`, called `html.text_of(doc, node)`: Every text inside `node`, at any depth, in document order and joined: `<p>a <b>b</b> c</p>` holds `a b c`.
- `function texts_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [str]`, called `html.texts_of(doc, node)`: Every text node inside `node`, at any depth, in document order, each as it is.
- `function stripped_texts_of(doc: Document, node: i64) -> [str]`, called `html.stripped_texts_of(doc, node)`: Every text node inside `node`, at any depth, in document order, ASCII white space taken off both ends, and those left empty left out.
- `function element_named(doc: Document, within: i64, name: str) -> i64?`, called `html.element_named(doc, within, name)`: The first element inside `within` named `name`, in document order. Fails `not_found`.
- `function elements_named(doc: Document, within: i64, name: str) -> [i64]`, called `html.elements_named(doc, within, name)`: Every element inside `within` named `name`, in document order.
- `function element_with_attribute(doc: Document, within: i64, name: str, value: str) -> i64?`, called `html.element_with_attribute(doc, within, name: name, value: value)`: The first element inside `within` whose attribute `name` is `value`, in document order. Fails `not_found`.
- `function elements_with_attribute(doc: Document, within: i64, name: str, value: str) -> [i64]`, called `html.elements_with_attribute(doc, within, name: name, value: value)`: Every element inside `within` whose attribute `name` is `value`, in document order.
- `function element_with_class(doc: Document, within: i64, name: str) -> i64?`, called `html.element_with_class(doc, within, name)`: The first element inside `within` that has the class `name`, in document order. Fails `not_found`.
- `function elements_with_class(doc: Document, within: i64, name: str) -> [i64]`, called `html.elements_with_class(doc, within, name)`: Every element inside `within` that has the class `name`, in document order.
- `function element_with_id(doc: Document, id: str) -> i64?`, called `html.element_with_id(doc, id)`: The first element of `doc` whose `id` is `id`, in document order. Fails `not_found`.
- `function select(doc: Document, within: i64, selector: str) -> i64?`, called `html.select(doc, within, selector)`: The first element inside `within` that `selector` matches, in document order. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function select_all(doc: Document, within: i64, selector: str) -> [i64]?`, called `html.select_all(doc, within, selector)`: Every element inside `within` that `selector` matches, in document order, each once. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_match(doc: Document, node: i64, selector: str) -> bool?`, called `html.is_match(doc, node, selector)`: Whether `selector` matches the element `node`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function closest(doc: Document, node: i64, selector: str) -> i64?`, called `html.closest(doc, node, selector)`: The nearest element, `node` itself first and then its ancestors, that `selector` matches. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function set_attribute(@doc: Document, node: i64, name: str, value: str)`, called `html.set_attribute(@doc, node, name: name, value: value)`: Sets the attribute `name` of the element `node` to `value`: in its place where it has one of that name, after the others where not.
