- `function highest_admitted(r: Range, versions: [Version]) -> Version?`, called `semver.highest_admitted(r, versions)`: The highest version of `versions` that `r` admits: the one a package manager picks. Fails `not_found`.
- `function lowest_admitted(r: Range, versions: [Version]) -> Version?`, called `semver.lowest_admitted(r, versions)`: The lowest version of `versions` that `r` admits. Fails `not_found`.
- `function lowest_possible(r: Range) -> Version?`, called `semver.lowest_possible(r)`: The lowest version of all that `r` admits, as npm's `minVersion` answers it, read by Cargo's rule. Fails `not_found`.
- `function intersects(a: Range, b: Range) -> bool`, called `semver.intersects(a: a, b: b)`: Whether some version is admitted by both `a` and `b`, by Cargo's rule.
- `function is_subset(a: Range, b: Range) -> bool`, called `semver.is_subset(a: a, b: b)`: Whether every version `a` admits, `b` admits too, by Cargo's rule.


### diff

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/diff`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/diff/).

The differences of two lists: of lines, of words, of characters, of bytes or of any values, as an edit script a program walks, cut into hunks, and written in the unified and context formats of `diff -u` and `diff -c`; and how alike two lists are, as Python's `difflib` measures it.

- `variant Tag = .equal | .delete | .insert | .replace`: What a run of an edit script does.
- `record Op(tag: Tag, old_from: i64, old_to: i64, new_from: i64, new_to: i64)`: One run of an edit script, as Python's `get_opcodes` writes one: the old elements `old_from` to `old_to` become the new elements `new_from` to `new_to`.
- `record Block(old_at: i64, new_at: i64, size: i64)`: A run of elements the two lists share, as Python's `Match`.
- `variant Algorithm = .myers | .patience | .ratcliff`: How an edit script is found.
- `function lines_of(text: str) -> [str]`, called `diff.lines_of(text)`: The lines of `text`, each with its line feed: what a difference of texts compares, and what `format_unified` writes.
- `function words_of(text: str) -> [str]`, called `diff.words_of(text)`: The words of `text` and the runs of white space between them, each an element of its own: what a difference of words compares.
- `function edits(old: [str], new: [str]) -> [Op]`, called `diff.edits(old: old, new: new)`: The shortest edit script that turns `old` into `new`, by Myers's algorithm: lines, words, characters or any texts.
- `function edits_with(old: [str], new: [str], algorithm: Algorithm) -> [Op]`, called `diff.edits_with(old: old, new: new, algorithm)`: The edit script that turns `old` into `new`, found by `algorithm`.
- `function edits_of_bytes(old: [u8], new: [u8]) -> [Op]`, called `diff.edits_of_bytes(old: old, new: new)`: The shortest edit script that turns the bytes `old` into the bytes `new`, by Myers's algorithm.
- `function edits_by<T>(old: [T], new: [T], same: (function(left: T, right: T) -> bool)) -> [Op]`, called `diff.edits_by(old: old, new: new, same)`: The shortest edit script that turns `old` into `new`, lists of any values, by Myers's algorithm.
- `function distance(ops: [Op]) -> i64`, called `diff.distance(ops)`: How many elements an edit script inserts, deletes or replaces: a `replace` counts its longer side, as go-diff's `DiffLevenshtein` counts.
- `function hunks(ops: [Op], context: i64) -> [[Op]]`, called `diff.hunks(ops, context)`: The hunks of an edit script: its changes, each with up to `context` equal elements before and after, as Python's `get_grouped_opcodes` cuts them.
- `record Options(old_name: str, old_date: str, new_name: str, new_date: str, context: i64, algorithm: Algorithm)`: How a difference is written: the files' names and dates in the headers, the context around each change, and the algorithm.
- `function default_options(old_name: str, new_name: str) -> Options`, called `diff.default_options(old_name: old_name, new_name: new_name)`: The options `diff -u` writes with: the two names, no dates, 3 lines of context, Myers's algorithm.
- `function format_unified(old: [str], new: [str], options: Options) -> str`, called `diff.format_unified(old: old, new: new, options)`: The difference of `old` and `new` in the unified format, as `diff -u` writes it: `---` and `+++` headers, then each hunk, `@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@` and its lines after ` `, `-` or `+`.
- `function format_context(old: [str], new: [str], options: Options) -> str`, called `diff.format_context(old: old, new: new, options)`: The difference of `old` and `new` in the context format, as `diff -c` writes it: `***` and `---` headers, then each hunk after `***************`, its old lines under `*** 1,4 ****` and its new under `--- 1,4 ----`, marked `  `, `- `, `+ ` or `! `.
- `function ratio(a: [str], b: [str]) -> f64`, called `diff.ratio(a: a, b: b)`: How alike `a` and `b` are, from 0 to 1, as Python's `SequenceMatcher(None, a, b).ratio()` answers: twice the elements of the Ratcliff and Obershelp matching over the elements of both.
- `function quick_ratio(a: [str], b: [str]) -> f64`, called `diff.quick_ratio(a: a, b: b)`: An upper bound of `ratio`, quickly: the elements the two share counted with no regard to their order, as Python's `quick_ratio`.
- `function real_quick_ratio(a: [str], b: [str]) -> f64`, called `diff.real_quick_ratio(a: a, b: b)`: An upper bound of `quick_ratio`, at once: from the two lengths alone, as Python's `real_quick_ratio`.
- `function matching_blocks(a: [str], b: [str]) -> [Block]`, called `diff.matching_blocks(a: a, b: b)`: The runs `a` and `b` share by Ratcliff and Obershelp's matching, as Python's `get_matching_blocks`: in order in both, those that touch joined.
- `function longest_match(a: [str], b: [str], a_from: i64, a_to: i64, b_from: i64, b_to: i64) -> Block`, called `diff.longest_match(a: a, b: b, a_from: a_from, a_to: a_to, b_from: b_from, b_to: b_to)`: The longest run `a` and `b` share inside the given ranges, as Python's `find_longest_match`: of several, the one that begins first in `a`, then first in `b`.
- `function close_matches(word: str, possibilities: [str], n: i64, cutoff: f64) -> [str]`, called `diff.close_matches(word, possibilities, n, cutoff)`: The texts of `possibilities` most like `word`, best first, as Python's `get_close_matches` answers: those whose `ratio` against `word`, by characters, is `cutoff` or more, at most `n` of them.


### pem

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/pem`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/pem/).

PEM, the text that carries binary data between a `-----BEGIN <label>-----` line and a `-----END <label>-----` line, read and written by RFC 7468: certificates, keys, requests, any DER a program keeps as text.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The text is not PEM where a block was expected, or a block cannot be written: `parse`, `parse_all`, `parse_strict`, `parse_next`, `format`, `format_all`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No block where one was asked for: `parse`, `parse_strict`, `parse_next`; and no header of the name asked: `header_of`.
- `record Header(name: str, value: str)`: One header of RFC 1421's form, `Proc-Type: 4,ENCRYPTED`, as a block read holds it.
- `record Block(label: str, headers: [Header], data: [u8])`: One PEM block: its label, its headers, and the bytes its base 64 holds.
- `record Found(block: Block, start: i64, end: i64)`: A block found by `parse_next`, with where it stands in the text.
- `variant Reading = .lax | .strict`: Which of RFC 7468's two grammars a block is read by.
- `function parse(text: str) -> Block?`, called `pem.parse(text)`: The first PEM block in `text`, read by the lax grammar; text before and after it passed over. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function parse_all(text: str) -> [Block]?`, called `pem.parse_all(text)`: Every PEM block in `text`, in order, read by the lax grammar. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_strict(text: str) -> Block?`, called `pem.parse_strict(text)`: The first PEM block in `text`, read by the strict grammar. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function parse_next(text: str, from: i64, reading: Reading) -> Found?`, called `pem.parse_next(text, from, reading)`: The next PEM block in `text` from byte `from`, read by `reading`, with where it begins and ends. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function header_of(block: Block, name: str) -> str?`, called `pem.header_of(block, name)`: The value of the first header of `block` named `name`, the names compared with ASCII case ignored, as RFC 1421's names are. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_label(s: str) -> bool`, called `pem.is_label(s)`: Whether `s` is a label RFC 7468 allows: printable ASCII but the hyphen, with single hyphens or spaces between its characters, or empty.
- `function format(block: Block) -> str?`, called `pem.format(block)`: `block` written as PEM: its BEGIN line, its headers and a blank line where it has any, its data in base 64 in lines of 64 characters, its END line, each line ending in `\n`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_all(blocks: [Block]) -> str?`, called `pem.format_all(blocks)`: Every block of `blocks` written by `format`, one after the other. Fails as `format` does for the first block it refuses.


### unicode/encodings

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/unicode/encodings`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/unicode/encodings/).

Bytes in the encodings of the WHATWG Encoding Standard read as text and text written back as bytes, as a browser reads a page: the 40 encodings of the standard (UTF-8, UTF-16, the 28 single-byte ones from IBM866 to windows-1258, gb18030 and GBK, Big5 with Hong Kong's extensions, EUC-JP, ISO-2022-JP, Shift_JIS, EUC-KR, and the two of its own), every label it reads them by, its byte order marks, and its two error modes each way; and the encoding of bytes nobody declared, guessed with a confidence.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a label the standard reads as no encoding: every function that takes an encoding fails with it, and `sniff_bom` where no byte order mark begins the bytes.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of bytes an encoding cannot read, where the call is strict: `decode_strict` and `decode_chunk_strict`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a character an encoding has no bytes for, where the call is strict (`encode`, `encode_chunk`, `encode_isomorphic`), and of writing in the encoding `replacement`.
- `function name_of(label: str) -> str?`, called `encodings.name_of(label)`: The name of the encoding `label` names, as the standard writes it: `latin1` answers `windows-1252`, `sjis` answers `Shift_JIS`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function labels_of(encoding: str) -> [str]?`, called `encodings.labels_of(encoding)`: Every label the standard reads as `encoding`, in lower case and in the order of their bytes. Fails `not_found`.
- `function names() -> [str]`, called `encodings.names()`: The name of every encoding of the standard, 40, in its order: UTF-8, the single-byte ones, the Chinese, the Japanese, the Korean, then `replacement`, UTF-16BE, UTF-16LE and x-user-defined.
- `function output_encoding(encoding: str) -> str?`, called `encodings.output_encoding(encoding)`: The encoding a page in `encoding` writes a form or a URL in: UTF-8 in place of `replacement` and the two UTF-16s, which a browser never writes, and `encoding` itself otherwise. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_single_byte(encoding: str) -> bool?`, called `encodings.is_single_byte(encoding)`: Whether `encoding` writes every character it has in one byte: the 28 single-byte encodings and x-user-defined. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_ascii_compatible(encoding: str) -> bool?`, called `encodings.is_ascii_compatible(encoding)`: Whether `encoding` writes the ASCII characters as their own bytes and uses no byte below 0x80 for anything else, so that bytes in it may be searched for `<`, `"` or a line feed as ASCII: every encoding but ISO-2022-JP, `replacement` and the two UTF-16s. Fails `not_found`.
- `function can_encode_everything(encoding: str) -> bool?`, called `encodings.can_encode_everything(encoding)`: Whether `encoding` has bytes for every character: UTF-8, UTF-16BE and UTF-16LE. gb18030 has bytes for every character but U+E5E5, which the standard leaves out so that bytes read and written back stay the same. Fails `not_found`.
- `function sniff_bom(data: [u8]) -> str?`, called `encodings.sniff_bom(data)`: The encoding the byte order mark at the start of `data` names, as the standard reads one: `UTF-8` for EF BB BF, `UTF-16BE` for FE FF, `UTF-16LE` for FF FE. Fails `not_found`.
- `function bom_of(encoding: str) -> [u8]?`, called `encodings.bom_of(encoding)`: The byte order mark `encoding` begins a text with, or no bytes: EF BB BF for UTF-8, FE FF for UTF-16BE, FF FE for UTF-16LE, none for the others. Fails `not_found`.
- `function decode(data: [u8], encoding: str) -> str?`, called `encodings.decode(data, encoding)`: `data` read as text in `encoding`, as a browser reads a page: a byte order mark at the start chooses the encoding in its place and is dropped, and what cannot be read is U+FFFD. Fails `not_found`.
- `function decode_without_bom(data: [u8], encoding: str) -> str?`, called `encodings.decode_without_bom(data, encoding)`: `data` read as text in `encoding` and no other: a byte order mark is read as the character it writes, U+FEFF, and what cannot be read is U+FFFD. Fails `not_found`.
- `function decode_strict(data: [u8], encoding: str) -> str?`, called `encodings.decode_strict(data, encoding)`: `data` read as text in `encoding`, failing where a byte cannot be read: what an XML reader or a protocol that refuses bad input asks. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function valid_prefix_len(data: [u8], encoding: str) -> i64?`, called `encodings.valid_prefix_len(data, encoding)`: How many bytes at the start of `data` read in `encoding` with no error: the length of `data` where all of them do, else the index where the first wrong sequence begins. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Decoder(encoding: str, state: machine.State)`: A text read from bytes that come in pieces, a file read a block at a time or a body read from a socket: what is cut at the end of one piece is held and read with the next.
- `function new_decoder(encoding: str) -> Decoder?`, called `encodings.new_decoder(encoding)`: A decoder of `encoding` that reads a byte order mark first, as `decode` does. Fails `not_found`.
- `function new_decoder_without_bom(encoding: str) -> Decoder?`, called `encodings.new_decoder_without_bom(encoding)`: A decoder of `encoding` that reads a byte order mark as a character, as `decode_without_bom` does. Fails `not_found`.
- `function decode_chunk(@decoder: Decoder, data: [u8], last: bool) -> str`, called `encodings.decode_chunk(@decoder, data, last)`: The text the next piece of the bytes writes, what cannot be read U+FFFD.
- `function decode_chunk_strict(@decoder: Decoder, data: [u8], last: bool) -> str?`, called `encodings.decode_chunk_strict(@decoder, data, last)`: The text the next piece of the bytes writes, failing where a byte cannot be read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode(s: str, encoding: str) -> [u8]?`, called `encodings.encode(s: s, encoding: encoding)`: `s` written as bytes in `encoding`, failing at the first character it has no bytes for. Fails `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_html(s: str, encoding: str) -> [u8]?`, called `encodings.encode_html(s: s, encoding: encoding)`: `s` written as bytes in `encoding`, a character it has no bytes for written as an HTML numeric reference, `&#` its code point in decimal and `;`, as a browser writes a form. Fails `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `record Encoder(encoding: str, state: machine.Shift)`: A text written as bytes in pieces, the state of ISO-2022-JP kept between them.
- `function new_encoder(encoding: str) -> Encoder?`, called `encodings.new_encoder(encoding)`: An encoder of `encoding`. Fails `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_chunk(@encoder: Encoder, s: str, last: bool) -> [u8]?`, called `encodings.encode_chunk(@encoder, s, last)`: The bytes the next piece of the text writes, failing at the first character the encoding has no bytes for. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function encode_chunk_html(@encoder: Encoder, s: str, last: bool) -> [u8]`, called `encodings.encode_chunk_html(@encoder, s, last)`: The bytes the next piece of the text writes, a character the encoding has no bytes for written as an HTML numeric reference, as `encode_html` does.
- `function decode_isomorphic(data: [u8]) -> str`, called `encodings.decode_isomorphic(data)`: `data` read as the characters whose code points are their numbers, U+0000 to U+00FF: the Infra standard's isomorphic decoding, which HTTP's headers ask, and what other libraries call Latin-1.
- `function encode_isomorphic(s: str) -> [u8]?`, called `encodings.encode_isomorphic(s)`: The bytes whose numbers are the code points of `s`: the Infra standard's isomorphic encoding. Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Guess(encoding: str, confidence: f64)`: What `detect` and `detect_all` answer: an encoding the bytes may be in, and how sure the guess is.
- `function detect(data: [u8]) -> Guess`, called `encodings.detect(data)`: The likeliest encoding of `data`, whose encoding nobody declared, and how sure the guess is.
- `function detect_all(data: [u8]) -> [Guess]`, called `encodings.detect_all(data)`: Every encoding that reads `data` with no error, the likeliest first, each with its confidence, as `detect` scores them.
- `constant UTF_8: str`, value `"UTF-8"`: UTF-8, the encoding every new text is written in.
- `constant IBM866: str`, value `"IBM866"`: IBM866, the DOS code page of Russian.
- `constant ISO_8859_2: str`, value `"ISO-8859-2"`: ISO-8859-2, Latin-2, of Central Europe.
- `constant ISO_8859_3: str`, value `"ISO-8859-3"`: ISO-8859-3, Latin-3, of Maltese and Esperanto.
- `constant ISO_8859_4: str`, value `"ISO-8859-4"`: ISO-8859-4, Latin-4, of the Baltic languages.
- `constant ISO_8859_5: str`, value `"ISO-8859-5"`: ISO-8859-5, of Cyrillic.
- `constant ISO_8859_6: str`, value `"ISO-8859-6"`: ISO-8859-6, of Arabic.
- `constant ISO_8859_7: str`, value `"ISO-8859-7"`: ISO-8859-7, of Greek.
- `constant ISO_8859_8: str`, value `"ISO-8859-8"`: ISO-8859-8, of Hebrew written in the order it is shown.
- `constant ISO_8859_8_I: str`, value `"ISO-8859-8-I"`: ISO-8859-8-I, of Hebrew written in the order it is read: ISO-8859-8's bytes, which a browser lays out by the bidirectional algorithm.
- `constant ISO_8859_10: str`, value `"ISO-8859-10"`: ISO-8859-10, Latin-6, of the Nordic languages.
- `constant ISO_8859_13: str`, value `"ISO-8859-13"`: ISO-8859-13, Latin-7, of the Baltic languages.
- `constant ISO_8859_14: str`, value `"ISO-8859-14"`: ISO-8859-14, Latin-8, of the Celtic languages.
- `constant ISO_8859_15: str`, value `"ISO-8859-15"`: ISO-8859-15, Latin-9: Latin-1 with the euro sign.
- `constant ISO_8859_16: str`, value `"ISO-8859-16"`: ISO-8859-16, Latin-10, of South-Eastern Europe.
- `constant KOI8_R: str`, value `"KOI8-R"`: KOI8-R, of Russian.
- `constant KOI8_U: str`, value `"KOI8-U"`: KOI8-U, of Ukrainian.
- `constant MACINTOSH: str`, value `"macintosh"`: The Mac OS Roman encoding.
- `constant WINDOWS_874: str`, value `"windows-874"`: windows-874, of Thai.
- `constant WINDOWS_1250: str`, value `"windows-1250"`: windows-1250, of Central Europe.
- `constant WINDOWS_1251: str`, value `"windows-1251"`: windows-1251, of Cyrillic.
- `constant WINDOWS_1252: str`, value `"windows-1252"`: windows-1252, of Western Europe: the encoding `latin1`, `iso-8859-1` and `ascii` name.
- `constant WINDOWS_1253: str`, value `"windows-1253"`: windows-1253, of Greek.
- `constant WINDOWS_1254: str`, value `"windows-1254"`: windows-1254, of Turkish, which `iso-8859-9` names.
- `constant WINDOWS_1255: str`, value `"windows-1255"`: windows-1255, of Hebrew.
- `constant WINDOWS_1256: str`, value `"windows-1256"`: windows-1256, of Arabic.
- `constant WINDOWS_1257: str`, value `"windows-1257"`: windows-1257, of the Baltic languages.
- `constant WINDOWS_1258: str`, value `"windows-1258"`: windows-1258, of Vietnamese.
- `constant X_MAC_CYRILLIC: str`, value `"x-mac-cyrillic"`: The Mac OS Cyrillic encoding, with the euro sign.
- `constant GBK: str`, value `"GBK"`: GBK, of simplified Chinese: gb18030 read, and written without its four-byte sequences.
- `constant GB18030: str`, value `"gb18030"`: gb18030, of Chinese: GB18030-2022, which has bytes for every character.
- `constant BIG5: str`, value `"Big5"`: Big5, of traditional Chinese, with the Hong Kong Supplementary Character Set read.
- `constant EUC_JP: str`, value `"EUC-JP"`: EUC-JP, of Japanese, with JIS X 0212 read.
- `constant ISO_2022_JP: str`, value `"ISO-2022-JP"`: ISO-2022-JP, of Japanese in seven bits, switched by escape sequences.
- `constant SHIFT_JIS: str`, value `"Shift_JIS"`: Shift_JIS, of Japanese, with the extensions of Windows code page 932.
- `constant EUC_KR: str`, value `"EUC-KR"`: EUC-KR, of Korean, with the Unified Hangul Code of Windows code page 949.
- `constant REPLACEMENT: str`, value `"replacement"`: The encoding `replacement`, which reads any bytes as one U+FFFD and writes nothing: the labels of ISO-2022-KR, ISO-2022-CN and HZ name it, so that text in them cannot slip markup past a filter.
- `constant UTF_16BE: str`, value `"UTF-16BE"`: UTF-16 with the high byte of each unit first.
- `constant UTF_16LE: str`, value `"UTF-16LE"`: UTF-16 with the low byte of each unit first: the encoding `utf-16` names.
- `constant X_USER_DEFINED: str`, value `"x-user-defined"`: x-user-defined: ASCII, and each byte from 0x80 as U+F780 plus its number less 0x80.


### keyring

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/keyring`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/keyring/).

Secrets kept in the system's own keyring: a password, a token or a key stored under a service and an account, read back, replaced, removed, and the accounts of a service listed, so a program keeps no secret in a file of its own.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A service empty, a name holding a zero byte or past `MAX_NAME_BYTES` bytes, or a secret past `MAX_SECRET_BYTES` bytes.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No secret stands under the service and account.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The keyring refuses this to the program: it is locked and may not be opened here, the person refused the system's dialog, or the secret belongs to another program.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system has no memory or no room left in its store.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This machine has no keyring the package reaches: on Linux no libsecret, no session bus, or no Secret Service on it (a container, a server with no desktop); on Windows a logon that keeps no credentials (a service's, a network logon's).
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The secret read is not UTF-8.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The keyring refused for a reason none of the above names; the message carries the system's words.
- `constant MAX_NAME_BYTES: i64`, value `1024`: The most bytes a service or an account holds.
- `constant MAX_SECRET_BYTES: i64`, value `2560`: The most bytes a secret holds, on every platform: Windows' Credential Manager holds no more.
- `function system() -> str?`, called `keyring.system()`: The name of the keyring this machine offers: "macOS Keychain", "Windows Credential Manager" or "Secret Service". Fails `unsupported`, `permission`, `failed`.
- `function store(service: str, account: str, secret: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `keyring.store(service: service, account: account, secret)`: Stores `secret` under `service` and `account`, replacing the secret that stood there. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function store_text(service: str, account: str, secret: str) -> ()?`, called `keyring.store_text(service: service, account: account, secret: secret)`: Stores the text `secret` under `service` and `account`, as its UTF-8, replacing the secret that stood there. Fails as `store` fails.
- `function read(service: str, account: str) -> [u8]?`, called `keyring.read(service: service, account: account)`: The secret stored under `service` and `account`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `permission`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function read_text(service: str, account: str) -> str?`, called `keyring.read_text(service: service, account: account)`: The secret stored under `service` and `account`, as text. Fails `not_text`.
- `function remove(service: str, account: str) -> ()?`, called `keyring.remove(service: service, account: account)`: Removes the secret stored under `service` and `account`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `permission`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function accounts(service: str) -> [str]?`, called `keyring.accounts(service)`: The accounts that hold a secret under `service`. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function remove_all(service: str) -> ()?`, called `keyring.remove_all(service)`: Removes every secret stored under `service`, whatever its account; done also where none stood. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `unsupported`, `failed`.


### printing

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/printing`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/printing/).

The system's printers: the printers this machine knows listed with their state, the papers each takes and what it can do, a PDF document submitted to one as a job with the settings a print dialog asks (copies, paper, orientation, sides, colour, pages, collation), the job's state and pages told while it runs and when it ends, waited for, and cancelled.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument refused: a name empty where it may not be, holding a zero byte or past `MAX_NAME_BYTES`; bytes that are not a PDF; settings outside their values; a wait below `FOREVER`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No printer of that name, no paper of that name on the printer, no job of that number on the printer, or no default printer.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The system refuses this to the program: the job is another user's, or the print service asks for credentials.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system has no memory, or the printer no room for another job.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This machine has no print system the package reaches (Linux with no CUPS library, or no scheduler running), or the printer takes no such setting (two sides on a printer of one, colour on one of grey).
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The job had not ended when the time given ran out.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program's stop was asked while the call waited.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names, a printer that takes no job now among them; the message carries the system's words.
- `constant MAX_NAME_BYTES: i64`, value `255`: The most bytes a printer's name, a paper's name or a job's title holds: IPP's bound on a name.
- `constant MAX_COPIES: i64`, value `999`: The most copies a job asks.
- `constant MAX_RANGES: i64`, value `100`: The most page ranges a job names.
- `constant FOREVER: i64`, value `-1`: No bound on a wait, in milliseconds: `wait` waits until the job ends.
- `record Printer(name: str, description: str, location: str, model: str, state: State, reasons: [str], message: str, accepting: bool, is_default: bool)`: A printer this machine knows.
- `variant State = .idle | .processing | .stopped`: What a printer is doing.
- `function printers() -> [Printer]?`, called `printing.printers()`: The printers this machine knows, in the system's order; none where it knows none. Fails `unsupported`, `permission`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `function default_printer() -> Printer?`, called `printing.default_printer()`: This machine's default printer. Fails `not_found`.
- `function printer_named(name: str) -> Printer?`, called `printing.printer_named(name)`: The printer named `name`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `record Paper(name: str, label: str, width_mm: f64, height_mm: f64, left_mm: f64, right_mm: f64, top_mm: f64, bottom_mm: f64, is_default: bool)`: A paper a printer takes.
- `function papers(printer: str) -> [Paper]?`, called `printing.papers(printer)`: The papers `printer` takes, in the system's order; none where it names none. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `function default_paper(printer: str) -> Paper?`, called `printing.default_paper(printer)`: The paper `printer` prints on where a job names none. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Capabilities(two_sided: bool, color: bool, copies_most: i64)`: What a printer can do, which `submit` holds a job to.
- `function capabilities(printer: str) -> Capabilities?`, called `printing.capabilities(printer)`: What `printer` can do. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `variant Orientation = .portrait | .landscape | .reverse_landscape | .reverse_portrait`: Which way up a page prints on the paper.
- `variant Sides = .one_sided | .two_sided_long_edge | .two_sided_short_edge`: Which sides of a sheet a job prints.
- `variant ColorMode = .printer_default | .color | .monochrome`: The colour a job prints in.
- `record PageRange(first: i64, last: i64)`: Pages of a document, `first` to `last`, both printed.
- `record Settings(printer: str, copies: i64, paper: str, orientation: Orientation, sides: Sides, color: ColorMode, pages: [PageRange], collate: bool)`: What a job asks of its printer: what a print dialog answers, and what `submit` takes.
- `function default_settings(printer: str) -> Settings`, called `printing.default_settings(printer)`: The settings a job on `printer` starts from: one copy, the printer's paper, upright, one side, the printer's colour, every page, collated.
- `function format_settings(settings: Settings) -> str?`, called `printing.format_settings(settings)`: The text of `settings`: UTF-8 lines `<key>=<value>`, each ended by a line feed, the keys and values IPP's own job-template attributes (RFC 8011, 5.2): `printer`, `copies`, `media`, `orientation-requested` (3 to 6), `sides`, `print-color-mode` (`auto` for the printer's own), `multiple-document-handling` and `page-ranges` (`1-3,5-5`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_settings(s: str, printer: str) -> Settings?`, called `printing.parse_settings(s: s, printer: printer)`: The settings `s` writes, as `format_settings` writes them. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Job(printer: str, id: i64)`: A job on a printer: what `submit` and `jobs` answer.
- `variant JobState = .pending | .held | .processing | .stopped | .cancelled | .aborted | .completed`: The state of a job.
- `record Status(state: JobState, reasons: [str], message: str, pages_printed: i64)`: How a job goes.
- `function submit(settings: Settings, title: str, pdf: [u8]) -> Job?`, called `printing.submit(settings, title, pdf)`: Submits the PDF `pdf` to the printer `settings` names as one job titled `title`, and answers it once the system holds the whole document: what is printed is the system's from then on, and `status_of` tells how it goes. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `function status_of(job: Job) -> Status?`, called `printing.status_of(job)`: How `job` goes now. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `failed`.
- `function is_ended(state: JobState) -> bool`, called `printing.is_ended(state)`: Whether `state` is an end: `cancelled`, `aborted` or `completed`.
- `function jobs(printer: str) -> [Job]?`, called `printing.jobs(printer)`: The jobs on `printer` that have not ended, oldest first: this program's, other programs' and other users' as far as the system shows them. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `failed`.
- `function cancel(job: Job) -> ()?`, called `printing.cancel(job)`: Cancels `job`; a job that had already ended stays as it ended, and is no failure. Fails `not_found`, `permission`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `constant SLICE_MS: i64`, value `250`: The milliseconds one wait of the layer takes at most, between which the program's stop is asked.
- `function wait(job: Job, within_ms: i64) -> Status?`, called `printing.wait(job, within_ms)`: Waits at most `within_ms` milliseconds for `job` to end, asking its state every quarter of a second, and answers how it ended. Fails `timeout`, `stopped`, `invalid`.


### scanner

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/scanner`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/scanner/).

A configurable lexer: a text read into its tokens one after another, as Go's text/scanner reads one, each token with its kind, its text and its place, the byte offset, line and column where it begins and where it ends.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code `scan_checked` fails with at the first malformed token, and the functions of values where a token is not of their kind.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code `next_char` and `peek_char` fail with at the end of the text.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code `int_of` fails with where the integer is outside `i64`.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code `text_of` fails with where the escapes of a literal spell bytes that are not UTF-8.
- `variant Kind = .identifier | .keyword | .integer | .float | .string | .raw_string | .character | .comment | .whitespace | .newline | .operator | .custom(index: i64) | .other | .invalid(reason: str) | .end`: What a token is.
- `record Place(offset: i64, line: i64, column: i64)`: Where a token begins or ends in its text.
- `record Token(kind: Kind, text: str, start: Place, end: Place)`: One token of a text.
- `record Rules(identifiers: bool, identifier_char: (function(str, i64) -> bool), keywords: [str], integers: bool, floats: bool, string_quotes: str, raw_quotes: str, char_quotes: str, multiline_strings: bool, line_comments: [str], block_comment_open: str, block_comment_close: str, nested_comments: bool, keep_comments: bool, whitespace: str, keep_whitespace: bool, keep_newlines: bool, operators: [str], classes: [regex.Regex])`: What a scanner reads: which kinds, by which characters, and the program's own keywords, operators and classes.
- `function go_rules() -> Rules`, called `scanner.go_rules()`: The rules of Go's text/scanner as `Init` sets them: identifiers by `is_identifier_char`, integers, floats, strings between double quotes, raw strings between backquotes, character literals between single quotes, comments after "//" and between "/*" and "*/" skipped, and space, tab, line feed and carriage return skipped; no keyword, operator or class.
- `function is_identifier_char(c: str, at: i64) -> bool`, called `scanner.is_identifier_char(c, at)`: Whether `c` may stand at index `at` of an identifier by Go's rule: a letter or `_` anywhere, a decimal digit anywhere but first.
- `record Scanner(source: str, rules: Rules, compiled: config.Config, cursor: cursor.Cursor)`: A text being read into tokens: what `new_scanner` makes and `next_token` reads on from.
- `function new_scanner(source: str, rules: Rules) -> Scanner`, called `scanner.new_scanner(source, rules)`: A scanner at the start of `source`.
- `function next_token(@scanner: Scanner) -> Token`, called `scanner.next_token(@scanner)`: The next token, and the scanner past it.
- `function peek_token(scanner: Scanner lent) -> Token`, called `scanner.peek_token(scanner)`: The token `next_token` would answer, the scanner left where it stands.
- `function next_char(@scanner: Scanner) -> str?`, called `scanner.next_char(@scanner)`: The next character of the text, and the scanner past it, whatever the rules would read there: white space and comments included. Fails `not_found`.
- `function peek_char(scanner: Scanner lent) -> str?`, called `scanner.peek_char(scanner)`: The character `next_char` would answer, the scanner left where it stands. Fails `not_found`.
- `function place_of(scanner: Scanner lent) -> Place`, called `scanner.place_of(scanner)`: Where the scanner stands: the place of the next character it reads.
- `function set_rules(@scanner: Scanner, rules: Rules)`, called `scanner.set_rules(@scanner, rules)`: The scanner reading on by `rules` from where it stands, as a lexer that enters another language in the middle of a text.
- `function scan(source: str, rules: Rules) -> [Token]`, called `scanner.scan(source, rules)`: Every token of `source`, read by `rules`, the `end` token last.
- `function scan_checked(source: str, rules: Rules) -> [Token]?`, called `scanner.scan_checked(source, rules)`: Every token of `source`, read by `rules`, the `end` token last, or the first malformed one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function kind_name(kind: Kind) -> str`, called `scanner.kind_name(kind)`: The name of a kind, for a message: "identifier", "integer", "raw string", "end of text"; a custom class is "custom 2", an invalid token "invalid".
- `function format_place(place: Place) -> str`, called `scanner.format_place(place)`: `place` written as its line and its column, "3:14", as Go and most compilers write one after a file's name.
- `function text_of(token: Token) -> str?`, called `scanner.text_of(token)`: The text a string, raw string or character literal spells: its quotes taken off, and in a string or character literal Go's escapes read: `\a`, `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\v`, `\\`, the quote itself, three octal digits, `\x` and two hexadecimal digits, `\u` and four, `\U` and eight. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function int_of(token: Token) -> i64?`, called `scanner.int_of(token)`: The integer an integer token spells, in any of Go's forms. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function float_of(token: Token) -> f64?`, called `scanner.float_of(token)`: The float a float or integer token spells, the nearest `f64`, ties going to the even one. Fails `invalid`.


### property

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/property`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/property/).

Property-based testing inside a `test` block: a property, a top-level function from a generated value to a `bool` or a `()?`, checked over many cases a generator makes from a seed, and the first case that fails it shrunk to a smallest one, which the report prints with the seed that reproduces the run.

- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `drawing.LIMIT`: The code a draw fails with where its case has drawn every choice its settings allow (`Settings.choices`); the case is rejected, not failed.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `drawing.INVALID`: The code `assume` fails with, and the code a generator or a `()?` property answers to reject its case: the case is not one the property reads.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `runner.NOT_FOUND`: The code `smallest` fails with where no case was accepted.
- `constant HELD: str`, value `runner.HELD`: The `report` of an `Outcome` whose property held on every case, alone, so a test writes `assert outcome.report == property.HELD` and a failure prints the whole report beside it.
- `record Settings(seed: u64, cases: i64, rejects: i64, shrinks: i64, choices: i64)`: How a run is made: its seed and its bounds.
- `function seeded(seed: u64) -> Settings`, called `property.seeded(seed)`: Settings with `seed` and the bounds of every run that names no other: 100 cases, 1,000 rejects, 2,000 shrinking candidates, 8,192 choices a case.
- `function seeded_by_system() -> Settings?`, called `property.seeded_by_system()`: Settings as `seeded` makes them with a seed drawn from the system's generator for keys, different on every call: for runs that look at new cases each time, the report naming the seed that makes them again. Fails with the code of `random.from_system` where the system's generator refuses.
- `function with_cases(settings: Settings, cases: i64) -> Settings`, called `property.with_cases(settings, cases)`: A copy of `settings` asking `cases` cases.
- `function with_rejects(settings: Settings, rejects: i64) -> Settings`, called `property.with_rejects(settings, rejects)`: A copy of `settings` allowing `rejects` rejected cases.
- `function with_shrinks(settings: Settings, shrinks: i64) -> Settings`, called `property.with_shrinks(settings, shrinks)`: A copy of `settings` allowing `shrinks` candidates while shrinking.
- `function with_choices(settings: Settings, choices: i64) -> Settings`, called `property.with_choices(settings, choices)`: A copy of `settings` allowing `choices` choices a case.
- `record Source(state: drawing.State)`: Where a generator draws one case from: the case's choices and how many it has drawn.
- `function source_of(choices: [u64]) -> Source`, called `property.source_of(choices)`: A source that draws `choices` in turn, and 0 past them: to test a generator's own helpers, which take `@source`, on chosen choices, and to read what a draw makes of them.
- `function int_between(@source: Source, least: i64, most: i64) -> i64?`, called `property.int_between(@source, least: least, most: most)`: A whole number from `least` to `most`, both included: a range's ends, 0, 1 and -1 among its edges, and on each side of its target (0, or the end nearer 0 where the range leaves 0 out) nearer the target the smaller its choices, the side above the simpler: where numbers fail on both sides, the smallest case is the least above the target that fails. Fails `limit`.
- `function u64_between(@source: Source, least: u64, most: u64) -> u64?`, called `property.u64_between(@source, least: least, most: most)`: A `u64` from `least` to `most`, both included, nearer `least` the smaller its choices, its edges the two ends and their neighbours. Fails `limit`.
- `function float(@source: Source) -> f64?`, called `property.float(@source)`: Any float, its edges the special values: zeros of both signs, `nan`, both infinities, the largest and smallest finite floats, the smallest normal one, 1, -1, 0.5, the machine's epsilon and 2^53. Fails `limit`.
- `function float_between(@source: Source, least: f64, most: f64) -> f64?`, called `property.float_between(@source, least: least, most: most)`: A finite float from `least` to `most`, both included: the ends, 0 of both signs where the range holds it, the neighbours of the ends, 1 and -1 and the tiny and huge floats it holds are its edges; the rest are small whole numbers, floats spread over the range and floats of any size it holds, nearer 0 the smaller its choices. Fails `limit`.
- `function boolean(@source: Source) -> bool?`, called `property.boolean(@source)`: `true` or `false`, as likely, `false` the simpler. Fails `limit`.
- `function character(@source: Source, alphabet: str) -> str?`, called `property.character(@source, alphabet)`: One character of `alphabet`, the first of it the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `function any_character(@source: Source) -> str?`, called `property.any_character(@source)`: Any character, a Unicode scalar value: its edges the zero character, a line feed, a space, the last of every width of UTF-8 and the first of the next, characters of two, three and four bytes, a combining mark, a right-to-left override, a byte order mark, U+FFFD, a noncharacter and the last scalar value; the rest printable ASCII, the Basic Multilingual Plane or any plane, `0` the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `function text(@source: Source, alphabet: str, least: i64, most: i64) -> str?`, called `property.text(@source, alphabet, least: least, most: most)`: A text of characters of `alphabet`, from `least` to `most` characters long, shorter the smaller its choices. Fails `limit`.
- `function any_text(@source: Source, least: i64, most: i64) -> str?`, called `property.any_text(@source, least: least, most: most)`: A text of any characters, as `any_character` draws them, from `least` to `most` characters long. Fails `limit`.
- `function bytes(@source: Source, least: i64, most: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `property.bytes(@source, least: least, most: most)`: From `least` to `most` bytes, each any byte, 0, 255, 127, 128, a line feed, a carriage return and a space its edges, and 0 the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `record Many(count: collections.Count)`: How long a list a generator is drawing may grow, and how long it has grown: the count `more` keeps.
- `function many(least: i64, most: i64) -> Many`, called `property.many(least: least, most: most)`: The count of a list from `least` to `most` elements long, for `more`; on average about five elements above `least`, or half the way to `most` where that is nearer.
- `function more(@source: Source, @count: Many) -> bool?`, called `property.more(@source, @count)`: Whether the list `count` counts takes one more element, and if so counts it: a generator draws one element each time it answers `true`. Fails `limit`.
- `function one_of(@source: Source, count: i64) -> i64?`, called `property.one_of(@source, count)`: Which of `count` alternatives a generator takes, from 0, the first the simplest, every one as likely. Fails `limit`.
- `function frequency(@source: Source, weights: [i64]) -> i64?`, called `property.frequency(@source, weights)`: Which of the alternatives `weights` weighs a generator takes, from 0, each as likely as its weight against their sum, the first of weight above 0 the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `function choose<T>(@source: Source, xs: [T]) -> T?`, called `property.choose(@source, xs)`: An element of `xs`, the first the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `function shuffled<T>(@source: Source, xs: [T]) -> [T]?`, called `property.shuffled(@source, xs)`: The elements of `xs` in a drawn order, their own order the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `function subsequence<T>(@source: Source, xs: [T]) -> [T]?`, called `property.subsequence(@source, xs)`: Some elements of `xs`, each kept or left as likely, in their order, none the simplest. Fails `limit`.
- `function random_generator(@source: Source) -> random.Generator?`, called `property.random_generator(@source)`: A seeded generator of `random`, its two words drawn, for code under test that takes one: what it draws is part of the case and shrinks with it. Fails `limit`.
- `function assume(condition: bool) -> ()?`, called `property.assume(condition)`: Nothing where `condition` holds, else a failure `invalid` that rejects the case: a generator writes `property.assume(x != 0)?`, and a `()?` property the same, so a case outside what the property reads is drawn again and not counted. Fails `invalid`.
- `function ints(source: Source) -> i64?`, called `property.ints(source)`: A generator of any `i64`, for `check`: `int_between` over the whole width of `i64`, so its edges are the type's ends. Fails `limit`.
- `function floats(source: Source) -> f64?`, called `property.floats(source)`: A generator of any float, for `check`: `float`, its special values among the edges. Fails `limit`.
- `function texts(source: Source) -> str?`, called `property.texts(source)`: A generator of texts of any characters, up to 20 long, for `check`: `any_text`. Fails `limit`.
- `function int_lists(source: Source) -> [i64]?`, called `property.int_lists(source)`: A generator of lists of up to 20 numbers, each any `i64`, for `check`. Fails `limit`.
- `function byte_lists(source: Source) -> [u8]?`, called `property.byte_lists(source)`: A generator of up to 64 bytes, each any byte, for `check`: `bytes`. Fails `limit`.
- `function booleans(source: Source) -> bool?`, called `property.booleans(source)`: A generator of `true` and `false`, for `check`: `boolean`. Fails `limit`.
- `variant Verdict = .held | .failed(failure: Failure) | .gave_up(last: str)`: What a run of a property ended with.
- `record Failure(found_at: i64, choices: [u64], shown: str, answer: str, shrinks: i64, tries: i64)`: A failing case, as shrinking left it.
- `record Outcome(verdict: Verdict, report: str, seed: u64, passed: i64, rejected: i64)`: What `check` and its kin found: the verdict, the counts, and a paragraph a reader reads.
- `function check<T>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), holds: (function(T) -> bool), show: (function(T) -> str), settings: Settings) -> Outcome`, called `property.check(generate, holds, show, settings)`: Whether `holds` answers `true` on every case `generate` makes, checked over the cases `settings` asks; the first case it answers `false` on is shrunk to a smallest one, which the report shows.
- `function check_result<T>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), holds: (function(T) -> ()?), show: (function(T) -> str), settings: Settings) -> Outcome`, called `property.check_result(generate, holds, show, settings)`: Whether `holds` answers `ok()` on every case `generate` makes, as `check` does; a failure's code and message are its words in the report, and a failure `invalid` rejects the case instead.
- `function check_equal<T, R>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), left: (function(T) -> R), right: (function(T) -> R), same: (function(left: R, right: R) -> bool), show: (function(T) -> str), settings: Settings) -> Outcome`, called `property.check_equal(generate, left: left, right: right, same, show, settings)`: Whether `left` and `right` answer the same, by `same`, on every case `generate` makes, as `check` checks a property: a function against a simpler one that is known right, an old version against a new.
- `function smallest<T>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), accepts: (function(T) -> bool), settings: Settings) -> T?`, called `property.smallest(generate, accepts, settings)`: The smallest case `generate` makes that `accepts` accepts: the first accepted over the run's cases, shrunk as a failure is. Fails `not_found`.
- `function sample<T>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), count: i64, settings: Settings) -> [T]?`, called `property.sample(generate, count, settings)`: `count` cases `generate` makes, in the order a run makes them: the simplest first, then edges, then at random. Fails `limit`.
- `function label_counts<T>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), label: (function(T) -> str), settings: Settings) -> {str: i64}?`, called `property.label_counts(generate, label, settings)`: How many of the run's cases `label` gives each label: how the cases a generator makes spread, to see that it reaches what the property needs. Fails `limit`.
- `function replay<T>(generate: (function(Source) -> T?), choices: [u64], settings: Settings) -> T?`, called `property.replay(generate, choices, settings)`: The case `generate` makes from `choices`: a failure's smallest case made again, from the `choices` of its `Failure`. Fails where `generate` fails on that case, with its code.


### vectors

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/vectors`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/vectors/).

Vectors of `f32` compared and searched: the dot product, the cosine, the euclidean and manhattan distances, a vector normalized, added or averaged, the nearest of a list found by exact search, and an HNSW index in memory that finds them fast, deterministic from its seed and saved as bytes.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of a vector a function cannot read: two vectors of different lengths, a component that is a nan or an infinity where distances are ordered, a vector of zeros where it has no direction, a setting out of its range, bytes that are not an index.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `codes.NOT_FOUND`: The code of an id an index does not hold, which `remove`, `restore` and `vector_of` fail with.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `codes.EXISTS`: The code of an id an index already holds, which `insert` fails with.
- `function dot(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.dot(a: a, b: b)`: The dot product of `a` and `b`: the sum of the products of their components taken in pairs. Fails `invalid`.
- `function norm(v: [f32]) -> f32`, called `vectors.norm(v)`: The length of `v`: the square root of the sum of the squares of its components.
- `function cosine_similarity(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.cosine_similarity(a: a, b: b)`: The cosine of the angle between `a` and `b`, from -1 to 1: their dot product over the product of their lengths. Fails `invalid`.
- `function cosine_distance(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.cosine_distance(a: a, b: b)`: One less the cosine similarity of `a` and `b`, from 0 for one direction to 2 for opposite ones: pgvector's `<=>`, hnswlib's `cosine` space. Fails `invalid`.
- `function euclidean_distance(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.euclidean_distance(a: a, b: b)`: The straight-line distance between `a` and `b`: the length of their difference, pgvector's `<->`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function squared_euclidean_distance(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.squared_euclidean_distance(a: a, b: b)`: The square of the straight-line distance between `a` and `b`, which faiss's and hnswlib's `l2` answer: the same order, without the root. Fails `invalid`.
- `function manhattan_distance(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.manhattan_distance(a: a, b: b)`: The sum of the absolute differences of the components of `a` and `b`, pgvector's `<+>`. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Metric = .euclidean | .cosine | .inner_product | .manhattan`: How the distance between two vectors is measured, where a search orders them: the smaller the distance, the nearer.
- `function distance(a: [f32], b: [f32], metric: Metric) -> f32?`, called `vectors.distance(a: a, b: b, metric)`: The distance between `a` and `b` as `metric` measures it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function distances(query: [f32], vectors: [[f32]], metric: Metric) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.distances(query, vectors, metric)`: The distance from `query` to each of `vectors`, in their order, as `metric` measures it: faiss's `pairwise_distances` for one query. Fails `invalid`.
- `function normalize(v: [f32]) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.normalize(v)`: `v` scaled to length one: each component divided by the length. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.add(a: a, b: b)`: The sum of `a` and `b`, component by component. Fails `invalid`.
- `function subtract(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.subtract(a: a, b: b)`: `a` less `b`, component by component. Fails `invalid`.
- `function multiply(a: [f32], b: [f32]) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.multiply(a: a, b: b)`: The product of `a` and `b`, component by component, pgvector's `*`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function scale(v: [f32], by: f32) -> [f32]`, called `vectors.scale(v, by)`: `v` with each component multiplied by `by`.
- `function sum(vectors: [[f32]]) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.sum(vectors)`: The sum of `vectors`, component by component, pgvector's `sum`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function mean(vectors: [[f32]]) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.mean(vectors)`: The mean of `vectors`, component by component: their centre, pgvector's `avg`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function quantize_binary(v: [f32]) -> [u8]`, called `vectors.quantize_binary(v)`: `v` reduced to one bit a component, set where the component is above zero, eight to a byte, the first component in the highest bit of the first byte: pgvector's `binary_quantize`.
- `function hamming_distance(a: [u8], b: [u8]) -> i64?`, called `vectors.hamming_distance(a: a, b: b)`: How many bits differ between `a` and `b`, pgvector's `<~>`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function jaccard_distance(a: [u8], b: [u8]) -> f32?`, called `vectors.jaccard_distance(a: a, b: b)`: One less the share of the bits set in either of `a` and `b` that are set in both, pgvector's `<%>`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Neighbor(id: i64, distance: f32)`: A vector found near a query: which one, and how far.
- `function nearest(query: [f32], vectors: [[f32]], limit: i64, metric: Metric) -> [Neighbor]?`, called `vectors.nearest(query, vectors, limit, metric)`: The `limit` vectors of `vectors` nearest to `query`, the nearest first, by measuring every one: faiss's `IndexFlat`. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function within(query: [f32], vectors: [[f32]], radius: f32, metric: Metric) -> [Neighbor]?`, called `vectors.within(query, vectors, radius, metric)`: Every vector of `vectors` whose distance from `query` is `radius` or less, the nearest first: faiss's `range_search`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Options(links: i64, ef_construction: i64, seed: u64)`: The settings an `Index` is made with, built directly or by `default_options`.
- `record Index(graph: graph.Graph, visits: walk.Visits)`: An index of vectors that finds the nearest to a query by walking a graph of layers, Malkov and Yashunin's Hierarchical Navigable Small World: hnswlib's `Index`, faiss's `IndexHNSWFlat`.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `vectors.default_options()`: hnswlib's defaults: 16 links, 200 candidates at construction, seed 100.
- `function new_index(dimension: i64, metric: Metric, options: Options) -> Index?`, called `vectors.new_index(dimension, metric, options)`: An empty index of vectors of `dimension` components, measured by `metric`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function insert(@index: Index, id: i64, vector: [f32]) -> ()?`, called `vectors.insert(@index, id, vector)`: Adds `vector` to `index` under `id`, linking it to its nearest on each layer it reaches. Fails `exists`, `invalid`.
- `function remove(@index: Index, id: i64) -> ()?`, called `vectors.remove(@index, id)`: Marks the vector under `id` deleted: no search answers it, and the graph still walks through it, as hnswlib's `mark_deleted`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function restore(@index: Index, id: i64) -> ()?`, called `vectors.restore(@index, id)`: Takes back the mark of `remove` on the vector under `id`, as hnswlib's `unmark_deleted`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function search(index: Index lent, query: [f32], limit: i64, ef: i64) -> [Neighbor]?`, called `vectors.search(index, query, limit: limit, ef: ef)`: The `limit` vectors of `index` nearest to `query` as its walk finds them, the nearest first. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function search_where(index: Index lent, query: [f32], limit: i64, ef: i64, accepts: (function(i64) -> bool)) -> [Neighbor]?`, called `vectors.search_where(index, query, limit: limit, ef: ef, accepts)`: The `limit` vectors of `index` nearest to `query` among those whose id `accepts` takes, as `search` finds them: a filter on what the program knows of each vector. Fails `invalid`.
- `function size(index: Index lent) -> i64`, called `vectors.size(index)`: How many vectors `index` holds that are not removed.
- `function contains(index: Index lent, id: i64) -> bool`, called `vectors.contains(index, id)`: Whether `index` holds a vector under `id` that is not removed.
- `function vector_of(index: Index lent, id: i64) -> [f32]?`, called `vectors.vector_of(index, id)`: The vector `index` holds under `id`, normalized where its metric is `.cosine`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function ids_of(index: Index lent) -> [i64]`, called `vectors.ids_of(index)`: The ids of the vectors `index` holds that are not removed, in the order they were inserted.
- `function dimension_of(index: Index lent) -> i64`, called `vectors.dimension_of(index)`: The length of every vector `index` holds.
- `function metric_of(index: Index lent) -> Metric`, called `vectors.metric_of(index)`: The measure `index` orders its vectors by.
- `function compact(index: Index lent) -> Index`, called `vectors.compact(index)`: A new index holding the vectors of `index` that are not removed, inserted again in the order they were first inserted, with its options and seed: what is removed stops costing memory.
- `function to_bytes(index: Index lent) -> [u8]`, called `vectors.to_bytes(index)`: `index` written as bytes: its settings, the state of its seed, its vectors and its links, so `from_bytes` reads back the same index.
- `function from_bytes(bytes: [u8]) -> Index?`, called `vectors.from_bytes(bytes)`: The index `bytes` hold, as `to_bytes` wrote it. Fails `invalid`.


### tokenizer

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/tokenizer`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tokenizer/).

Text made tokens and tokens made text by byte-pair encoding, as OpenAI's tiktoken does it, so that a program counts what a model of OpenAI's reads before it sends it, keeps a text within a model's window, or reads back the tokens a model wrote.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of what a function does not read: a token, a special token's text where it is not allowed, a file of ranks, a table.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a token, a special token or bytes that the encoding does not hold.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a pattern that holds what `regex` cannot match as fancy-regex does.
- `record Encoding(name: str, core: assemble.Core)`: An encoding: its ordinary tokens, its pattern and its special tokens.
- `function new(name: str, pattern: str, ranks: [[u8]], specials: {str: i64}) -> Encoding?`, called `tokenizer.new(name: name, pattern: pattern, ranks, specials)`: The encoding of the ordinary tokens `ranks`, the pattern `pattern` and the special tokens `specials`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function parse_ranks(text: str) -> [[u8]]?`, called `tokenizer.parse_ranks(text)`: The ordinary tokens a file of tiktoken's `.tiktoken` format writes, each at its rank: one line a token, the standard base 64 of its bytes, a space, and its rank as a decimal number, empty lines passed over. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_ranks(ranks: [[u8]]) -> str`, called `tokenizer.format_ranks(ranks)`: The ordinary tokens `ranks` written as a `.tiktoken` file: one line a token, in rank order, the standard base 64 of its bytes, a space and its rank, every line ended by a line feed.
- `function pattern_of(encoding: Encoding lent) -> str`, called `tokenizer.pattern_of(encoding)`: The pattern of `encoding`, as it was given to `new`.
- `function vocabulary_size(encoding: Encoding lent) -> i64`, called `tokenizer.vocabulary_size(encoding)`: How many numbers the tokens of `encoding` may take: its largest token plus 1, tiktoken's `n_vocab`.
- `function max_token(encoding: Encoding lent) -> i64`, called `tokenizer.max_token(encoding)`: The largest number of a token of `encoding`, ordinary or special.
- `function ranks_of(encoding: Encoding lent) -> [[u8]]`, called `tokenizer.ranks_of(encoding)`: The bytes of every ordinary token of `encoding`, its rank its index.
- `function special_tokens(encoding: Encoding lent) -> [str]`, called `tokenizer.special_tokens(encoding)`: The text of every special token of `encoding`, in the order of its number.
- `function is_special(encoding: Encoding lent, token: i64) -> bool`, called `tokenizer.is_special(encoding, token)`: Whether `token` is a special token of `encoding`.
- `function end_of_text(encoding: Encoding lent) -> i64?`, called `tokenizer.end_of_text(encoding)`: The number of the special token `<|endoftext|>` of `encoding`, tiktoken's `eot_token`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function encode(encoding: Encoding lent, text: str) -> [i64]?`, called `tokenizer.encode(encoding, text)`: The tokens of `text`, every special token's text in it refused, as tiktoken's `encode` does by default. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_ordinary(encoding: Encoding lent, text: str) -> [i64]`, called `tokenizer.encode_ordinary(encoding, text)`: The tokens of `text`, a special token's text in it encoded as ordinary text, as tiktoken's `encode_ordinary` does.
- `function encode_with_specials(encoding: Encoding lent, text: str, allowed: [str], refused: [str]) -> [i64]?`, called `tokenizer.encode_with_specials(encoding, text, allowed: allowed, refused: refused)`: The tokens of `text`, the special tokens `allowed` encoded as special tokens wherever their text stands in it, and those `refused` failing. Fails `invalid`.
- `function count(encoding: Encoding lent, text: str) -> i64`, called `tokenizer.count(encoding, text)`: How many tokens `encode_ordinary` makes of `text`.
- `function truncate(encoding: Encoding lent, text: str, most: i64) -> str`, called `tokenizer.truncate(encoding, text, most)`: The longest beginning of `text` that encodes to at most `most` tokens, never cutting inside a character.
- `function token_of(encoding: Encoding lent, piece: [u8]) -> i64?`, called `tokenizer.token_of(encoding, piece)`: The token of `encoding` that is exactly the bytes `piece`, ordinary or special, tiktoken's `encode_single_token`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function encode_piece(encoding: Encoding lent, piece: [u8]) -> [i64]`, called `tokenizer.encode_piece(encoding, piece)`: The tokens of the bytes `piece` merged whole, as one piece, with no pattern cutting them first and no special token read: tiktoken's `_encode_single_piece`.
- `function pieces_of(encoding: Encoding lent, text: str) -> [str]`, called `tokenizer.pieces_of(encoding, text)`: The pieces the pattern of `encoding` cuts `text` into, which are then merged into tokens each apart.
- `function decode(encoding: Encoding lent, tokens: [i64]) -> str?`, called `tokenizer.decode(encoding, tokens)`: The text the tokens `tokens` write, each byte that is no part of UTF-8 replaced by U+FFFD, as tiktoken's `decode` does. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_bytes(encoding: Encoding lent, tokens: [i64]) -> [u8]?`, called `tokenizer.decode_bytes(encoding, tokens)`: The bytes the tokens `tokens` write, end to end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_token(encoding: Encoding lent, token: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `tokenizer.decode_token(encoding, token)`: The bytes of the token `token`, tiktoken's `decode_single_token_bytes`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_tokens(encoding: Encoding lent, tokens: [i64]) -> [[u8]]?`, called `tokenizer.decode_tokens(encoding, tokens)`: The bytes of each token of `tokens`, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function offsets_of(encoding: Encoding lent, tokens: [i64]) -> [i64]?`, called `tokenizer.offsets_of(encoding, tokens)`: Where each token of `tokens` begins in the bytes `decode_bytes` answers, as a byte index, which is its place in the text it was encoded from. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_next(encoding: Encoding lent, @held: [u8], token: i64) -> str?`, called `tokenizer.decode_next(encoding, @held, token)`: The text `token` completes, after the bytes `held` keeps of the tokens before it: a model's answer decoded token by token as it streams. Fails `invalid`.


### search

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/search`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/search/).

Texts indexed in memory by their words and searched, the best first: an inverted index ranked by BM25 with the `k1` and `b` the program gives, and queries of words, of words required or refused, of phrases and of prefixes.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of what a function cannot read: a query whose quote is not closed, a setting out of its range, bytes that are not an index.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `codes.NOT_FOUND`: The code of an id an index does not hold, which `remove` fails with.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `codes.EXISTS`: The code of an id an index already holds, which `insert` fails with.
- `variant Formula = .standard | .okapi(epsilon: f64) | .bm25l(delta: f64) | .bm25_plus(delta: f64)`: How a term's weight and its count in a text make a score, a text scoring only for the terms it holds.
- `record Options(k1: f64, b: f64, formula: Formula, stop_words: [str])`: The settings an `Index` is made with, built directly or by `default_options`.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `search.default_options()`: Lucene's and tantivy's settings: `k1` 1.2, `b` 0.75, the standard formula, and no stop word.
- `function english_stop_words() -> [str]`, called `search.english_stop_words()`: The 33 English words tantivy's `stopword("english")` filter leaves out, in alphabetical order: articles, conjunctions, prepositions and the forms of "to be" a search rarely needs.
- `function terms(text: str, stop_words: [str]) -> [str]`, called `search.terms(text, stop_words)`: The terms of `text`, in the order they stand: each run of letters and digits in lower case, the words of `stop_words` left out.
- `record Index(engine: engine.Engine)`: An inverted index: each term with the texts that hold it and its places in each, and each text's length in terms, so a query reaches only the texts that hold its words.
- `function new_index(options: Options) -> Index?`, called `search.new_index(options)`: An empty index ranked by `options`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function insert(@index: Index, id: i64, text: str) -> ()?`, called `search.insert(@index, id, text)`: Adds `text` to `index` under `id`. Fails `exists`.
- `function remove(@index: Index, id: i64) -> ()?`, called `search.remove(@index, id)`: Takes the text under `id` out of `index`: no query finds it, and the counts every score reads leave it out. Fails `not_found`.
- `function contains(index: Index lent, id: i64) -> bool`, called `search.contains(index, id)`: Whether `index` holds a text under `id`.
- `function size(index: Index lent) -> i64`, called `search.size(index)`: How many texts `index` holds.
- `function document_frequency(index: Index lent, term: str) -> i64`, called `search.document_frequency(index, term)`: How many texts of `index` hold `term`.
- `function terms_with_prefix(index: Index lent, prefix: str) -> [str]`, called `search.terms_with_prefix(index, prefix)`: The terms of `index` that begin with `prefix`, held by at least one text, in the order of their bytes: what a search box completes a word to.
- `function compact(index: Index lent) -> Index`, called `search.compact(index)`: A new index holding the texts of `index`, with its options, without what `remove` left in memory.
- `function to_bytes(index: Index lent) -> [u8]`, called `search.to_bytes(index)`: `index` written as bytes: its options and each text's id and terms with their places, so `from_bytes` reads back an index that scores alike.
- `function from_bytes(bytes: [u8]) -> Index?`, called `search.from_bytes(bytes)`: The index `bytes` hold, as `to_bytes` wrote it. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Hit(id: i64, score: f64)`: A text a query found, and how well it matched.
- `function search(index: Index lent, query: str, limit: i64) -> [Hit]?`, called `search.search(index, query, limit)`: The texts of `index` that match `query`, the best first, at most `limit`. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.


### http/suffixes

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/http/suffixes`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/http/suffixes/).

The Public Suffix List: which part of a domain name the public registers under, `co.uk` of `example.co.uk`, so that a cookie set for `co.uk` is refused and the registrable domain of a host is known.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a name that is no domain name.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a name with no registrable domain.
- `constant VERSION: str`, value `rules.VERSION`: The version of the list the rules are made from, as it writes it: the instant it was cut.
- `record Suffix(name: str, icann: bool)`: A name's public suffix, and whether the list's ICANN section says it.
- `function suffix_of(host: str) -> Suffix?`, called `suffixes.suffix_of(host)`: The public suffix of `host` by the list's algorithm: the longest rule it matches, a wildcard's label taken for any, an exception's rule less its first label, and the last label alone where no rule matches. Fails `invalid`.
- `function registrable_domain_of(host: str) -> str?`, called `suffixes.registrable_domain_of(host)`: The registrable domain of `host`: its public suffix and the one label before it, `example.co.uk` of `www.example.co.uk`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function is_public_suffix(domain: str) -> bool`, called `suffixes.is_public_suffix(domain)`: Whether `domain` is a public suffix itself, as a cookie's `Domain` is asked before it is taken: `co.uk` and `com` are, `example.co.uk` is not.


### image/jpeg

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/image/jpeg`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/jpeg/).

JPEG read and written, by ITU-T T.81 and JFIF: baseline and progressive files of 8 bits a sample read, gray or colour, every sampling of the colour, with restart intervals; their EXIF orientation read; baseline files written at a quality the caller picks, with the tables of T.81's Annex K.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code `orientation_of` fails with where an EXIF directory holds no orientation.
- `record Jpeg(image: image.Image, orientation: i64, progressive: bool, exif: [u8], icc: [u8])`: What `decode` answers: the image and what the file says of it.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> Jpeg?`, called `jpeg.decode(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, and its orientation. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `constant MAX_SCANS: i64`, value `reading.MAX_SCANS`: The most scans `decode` reads in one file: a progressive file has about ten, and each scan walks every block of its components, so more would only cost time.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `jpeg.decode_image(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, alone: what a program that reads any of the formats asks of each, by one call of one shape in `image/bmp`, `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/netpbm` and `image/png`. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `record Info(width: i64, height: i64, components: i64, progressive: bool)`: What the frame header of a JPEG file says, read without its scans.
- `function info_of(data: [u8]) -> Info?`, called `jpeg.info_of(data)`: The size of the image `data` holds, read from its segments up to the frame header, nothing decoded: Go's `jpeg.DecodeConfig`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function orientation_of(exif: [u8]) -> i64?`, called `jpeg.orientation_of(exif)`: The orientation the EXIF data `exif` holds: tag 274 of its first image directory, 1 to 8. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `variant Subsampling = .full | .half | .quarter`: How the colour is sampled against the brightness when writing.
- `record EncodeOptions(quality: i64, subsampling: Subsampling)`: How `encode` writes a file.
- `function default_encode_options() -> EncodeOptions`, called `jpeg.default_encode_options()`: Options of quality 75 and 4:2:0, Go's default quality and sampling.
- `function encode(img: image.Image, options: EncodeOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `jpeg.encode(img, options)`: `img` as a baseline JPEG file in JFIF: one component for gray, three for RGB as YCbCr, Huffman-coded with the tables of Annex K. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.


### image/gif

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/image/gif`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/gif/).

GIF read and written, by the GIF89a specification: every frame of an animation read with its palette, place, delay and disposal, interlaced or not; the frames laid one over another as a viewer shows them; an animation or a single image written with its palettes.

- `variant Disposal = .unspecified | .keep | .background | .previous`: What a viewer does with a frame's rectangle before the next frame is drawn.
- `record Frame(image: image.Indexed, left: i64, top: i64, delay: i64, disposal: Disposal, interlaced: bool)`: One frame: an indexed image placed on the screen.
- `record Gif(width: i64, height: i64, palette: [image.Color], background: i64, loop_count: i64, frames: [Frame])`: A GIF file: a screen and the frames drawn on it.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> Gif?`, called `gif.decode(data, limits)`: Every frame of the GIF `data` holds, and its screen. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `gif.decode_image(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, alone: what a program that reads any of the formats asks of each, by one call of one shape in `image/bmp`, `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/netpbm` and `image/png`. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `record Info(width: i64, height: i64)`: What the header of a GIF file says.
- `function info_of(data: [u8]) -> Info?`, called `gif.info_of(data)`: The size of the screen of the GIF `data`, read from its first 13 bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function composite(g: Gif, limits: image.Limits) -> [image.Image]?`, called `gif.composite(g, limits)`: Every frame of `g` as a viewer shows it: the screen in RGBA, transparent at first, each frame drawn over what its predecessors left, a transparent index leaving what was under it, then disposed of as it says before the next. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function encode(g: Gif) -> [u8]?`, called `gif.encode(g)`: `g` as a GIF89a file: its global palette where it has one, each frame's palette written as its own where it differs from the global one, its place, delay and disposal, the first entry of alpha 0 of its palette as its transparent index, and a NETSCAPE2.0 block where `loop_count` is 0 or more. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_image(img: image.Image, dither: bool) -> [u8]?`, called `gif.encode_image(img, dither)`: `img` as a GIF file of one frame: its colours reduced to 256 by `image.palette_of`, or to 255 and a transparent entry where a pixel's alpha is below 128, which becomes transparent. Fails `invalid`.


### image/bmp

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/image/bmp`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/bmp/).

BMP read and written: Windows' device-independent bitmaps of 1, 4, 8, 16, 24 and 32 bits a pixel, under every header from OS/2's core header to BITMAPV5HEADER, bottom up or top down, plain, with bit fields, or run-length coded (RLE8 and RLE4).

- `record Info(width: i64, height: i64, bits: i64, format: image.Format)`: What the header of a BMP file says.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `bmp.decode(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `bmp.decode_image(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, alone: what a program that reads any of the formats asks of each, by one call of one shape in `image/bmp`, `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/netpbm` and `image/png`. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `function info_of(data: [u8]) -> Info?`, called `bmp.info_of(data)`: The size, depth and format of the BMP `data`, read from its headers. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode(img: image.Image) -> [u8]?`, called `bmp.encode(img)`: `img` as a BMP file, bottom up: gray as 8 bits of a gray palette, RGB as 24 bits, RGBA (and gray with alpha, made RGBA) as 32 bits under a BITMAPV4HEADER whose bit fields give the alpha. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.


### image/netpbm

Layer 2, named `use <rebel>/image/netpbm`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/netpbm/).

The netpbm formats read and written: PBM (P1, P4), PGM (P2, P5), PPM (P3, P6) and PAM (P7), plain or raw, of any maximum value from 1 to 65,535, comments anywhere the format allows them.

- `record Info(width: i64, height: i64, maxval: i64, depth: i64, plain: bool)`: What the header of a netpbm file says.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `netpbm.decode(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds: its first one. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `netpbm.decode_image(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, alone: what a program that reads any of the formats asks of each, by one call of one shape in `image/bmp`, `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/netpbm` and `image/png`. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `function info_of(data: [u8]) -> Info?`, called `netpbm.info_of(data)`: The size, maximum value and depth of the netpbm `data`, read from its header. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
