- `variant KeyOrder = .as_written | .bytewise`: The order an encoded map's entries stand in.
- `function encode(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `msgpack.encode(v)`: `v` encoded, each object in the smallest format that holds it, a map's entries in the order they stand. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_with(v: Value, order: KeyOrder) -> [u8]?`, called `msgpack.encode_with(v, order)`: `v` encoded as `encode` encodes it, a map's entries in the order `order` names. Fails as `encode` fails.
- `function to_json(v: Value) -> json.Value?`, called `msgpack.to_json(v)`: `v` as a `json.Value`, where JSON can hold every object of it. Fails `unsupported`, `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function from_json(v: json.Value) -> Value`, called `msgpack.from_json(v)`: `v` as a MessagePack object.
- `function from_int(n: i64) -> Value`, called `msgpack.from_int(n)`: The integer `n` as an object: `unsigned` from 0 up, `negative` below.
- `function int_of(v: Value) -> i64?`, called `msgpack.int_of(v)`: The integer `v` holds, as an `i64`. Fails `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function member(v: Value, key: str) -> Value?`, called `msgpack.member(v, key)`: The value `v`, a map, holds under the string key `key`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function kind_of(v: Value) -> str`, called `msgpack.kind_of(v)`: The name of `v`'s case, as a `match` on it writes it: `nil_value`, `boolean`, `unsigned`, `negative`, `float`, `text`, `binary`, `list`, `pairs` or `extension`.
- `function bool_of(v: Value) -> bool?`, called `msgpack.bool_of(v)`: The `bool` of `false` or `true`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function float_of(v: Value) -> f64?`, called `msgpack.float_of(v)`: The number of a float, encoded as a float 32 or a float 64. Fails `invalid`.
- `function text_of(v: Value) -> str?`, called `msgpack.text_of(v)`: The characters of a string (MessagePack's `str`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function bytes_of(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `msgpack.bytes_of(v)`: The bytes of a binary (MessagePack's `bin`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function items_of(v: Value) -> [Value]?`, called `msgpack.items_of(v)`: The items of an array, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function entries_of(v: Value) -> [Entry]?`, called `msgpack.entries_of(v)`: The entries of a map, its keys of any kind, in the order they were read or built. Fails `invalid`.
- `function instant_of(v: Value) -> time.Instant?`, called `msgpack.instant_of(v)`: The instant the timestamp `v` holds. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function from_instant(t: time.Instant) -> Value`, called `msgpack.from_instant(t)`: The timestamp of `t`, in the smallest of the specification's three layouts that holds it: 4 bytes for whole seconds from 1970 to 2106, 8 for nanoseconds from 1970 on, and 12, which only an instant before 1970 needs, since a `time.Instant` ends in 2262.


### plist

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/plist`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/plist/).

Apple property lists, the two forms every Apple platform reads: the XML form of `PropertyList-1.0.dtd` and the binary form, `bplist00`.

- `variant Value = .nil_value | .boolean(v: bool) | .unsigned(v: u64) | .negative(v: i64) | .real(v: f64) | .text(v: str) | .date(v: time.Instant) | .data(v: [u8]) | .uid(v: u64) | .list(items: [Value]) | .dictionary(entries: [Entry])`: One property list value.
- `record Entry(key: str, value: Value)`: One entry of a dictionary: a key, always a string, and its value.
- `variant Format = .xml | .binary`: The two forms a document is written in.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a document that is not a property list of the form it claims, of a dictionary that holds a key twice, and of a value of the wrong kind.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of bytes that are not UTF-8, where the XML form is read from them.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of an integer past what `int_of` holds, and of a date past a `time.Instant`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a key a dictionary does not hold and of a place an array or a path does not reach, which `member`, `item` and `value_at` fail with.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a value the form asked for cannot hold: a null in XML, a form a version of the binary header names that this reading does not know.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a document past the depth, the size or the count of values its reading allows.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `512`: The deepest nesting `decode` reads: a value that is no container is 1 deep, `[]` is 1, `[[]]` is 2.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS: i64`, value `4194304`: The most values `decode` reads, counted as the tree they make: an object a binary list refers to twice counts twice.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES: i64`, value `268435456`: The longest document `decode` reads, in bytes.
- `record DecodeOptions(max_depth: i64, max_items: i64, max_bytes: i64, duplicate_keys: bool)`: How a document is read: the limits and what a dictionary may hold.
- `function default_decode_options() -> DecodeOptions`, called `plist.default_decode_options()`: The options `decode` reads with: `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`, `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS` and `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES`, and no key twice in a dictionary.
- `function format_of(data: [u8]) -> Format?`, called `plist.format_of(data)`: The form `data` is written in: binary where it opens with `bplist`, XML where it opens, after a byte order mark and white space, with `<`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode(data: [u8]) -> Value?`, called `plist.decode(data)`: The value a document holds, read as `default_decode_options` reads it, from either form. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`, `unsupported`, `does_not_fit`, `limit`.
- `function decode_with(data: [u8], options: DecodeOptions) -> Value?`, called `plist.decode_with(data, options)`: The value a document holds, read as `options` asks. Fails `limit`.
- `function parse_xml(text: str) -> Value?`, called `plist.parse_xml(text)`: The value an XML property list writes. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function decode_binary(data: [u8]) -> Value?`, called `plist.decode_binary(data)`: The value a binary property list writes. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function format_xml(v: Value) -> str?`, called `plist.format_xml(v)`: `v` written as an XML property list, as `plutil -convert xml1` writes one: the declaration, the document type, `<plist version="1.0">`, a tab for each level, a date to the second in UTC, data in base 64 lines of 68 characters, a real in 17 significant digits, `nan` and `+infinity`. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function encode_binary(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `plist.encode_binary(v)`: `v` written as a binary property list, `bplist00`: each distinct string, number, date and datum once, however many times it stands, an integer in the fewest bytes its size allows, a string in ASCII where it is, in UTF-16 otherwise. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function encode(v: Value, format: Format) -> [u8]?`, called `plist.encode(v, format)`: `v` written in `format`, an XML list as UTF-8 bytes. Fails as the function of `format` does.
- `function from_int(n: i64) -> Value`, called `plist.from_int(n)`: The integer `n`, in the case that holds it.
- `function int_of(v: Value) -> i64?`, called `plist.int_of(v)`: The `i64` an integer value holds. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function member(dict: Value, key: str) -> Value?`, called `plist.member(dict, key)`: The value `dict` holds under `key`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function item(list: Value, index: i64) -> Value?`, called `plist.item(list, index)`: The value `list` holds at `index`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function value_at(root: Value, path: str) -> Value?`, called `plist.value_at(root, path)`: The value at a path of keys and places, as `plutil -extract` takes one: `CFBundleURLTypes.0.CFBundleURLSchemes`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.


### poll

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/poll`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/poll/).

Waiting on many connections, listeners, datagram sockets, streams and timers at once, and being told which are ready and for what, so one thread serves many connections: what an event loop gives a program (Rust's `tokio` and `mio`, Go's network poller, Python's `selectors`), without a coroutine, which the language refuses (design.md Part 6).

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument out of its range: a size, a time below zero, an interest a timer cannot have.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The set, or the connection, listener or stream handed, is closed.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A key that names no entry of the set: removed already, or another set's.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The set holds the most entries it was made for, or the process has no room for another set.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This system cannot wait on what the stream stands on: a pipe or a console on Windows, a device such as `/dev/null`.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop (`os.catch_stop`, `os.ask_stop`).
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system's wait failed for a reason none of the above names; the message carries its number.
- `record Set(handle: hero_poll.Set, most: i64)`: A set of entries waited on together.
- `variant Interest = .read | .write | .read_write`: What an entry waits for.
- `record Event(key: i64, readable: bool, writable: bool, hangup: bool, error: bool, due: i64)`: One entry found ready by a wait, and what for.
- `function make(most: i64) -> Set?`, called `poll.make(most)`: A new set that holds at most `most` entries. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function close(@set: Set) -> ()?`, called `poll.close(@set)`: Closes the set and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`; what it held is let go and none of it closed, being the program's. Fails `closed`.
- `function count(set: Set) -> i64?`, called `poll.count(set)`: How many entries the set holds. Fails `closed`.
- `function add_conn(set: Set, c: net.Conn, interest: Interest) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_conn(set, c, interest)`: Adds the connection `c` to the set, waiting for what `interest` says, and answers the key every event of it carries. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function add_listener(set: Set, l: net.Listener) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_listener(set, l)`: Adds the listener `l` to the set, told readable when a connection waits to be accepted, and answers the entry's key. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function add_udp(set: Set, u: net.UdpSocket, interest: Interest) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_udp(set, u, interest)`: Adds the datagram socket `u` to the set, waiting for what `interest` says, and answers the entry's key. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function add_stream(set: Set, s: io.Stream, interest: Interest) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_stream(set, s, interest)`: Adds the stream `s` to the set, waiting for what `interest` says, and answers the entry's key: a connection's stream is waited on as its socket, a pipe, a terminal, a serial port, a pseudo-terminal's controlling side and a local channel of `ipc` as what they stand on, and a regular file is ready at every wait. Fails `closed`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function add_timer(set: Set, first: time.Duration, every: time.Duration) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_timer(set, first: first, every: every)`: Adds a timer to the set, due once `first` has passed and then every `every`, and answers its key; a timer fallen due is told by `wait` with `due`, the times it fell due. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `limit`.
- `function add_signals(set: Set) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_signals(set)`: Adds the signals the program counts to the set, and answers the entry's key: told readable while a signal `os.count_signal` counts has come and `os.take_signals` has not taken it, so a loop that takes every count it keeps at each event waits again quietly, and one that leaves a count is told it again at every wait, as everything still ready is. Fails `closed`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function add_mailbox<T>(set: Set, m: (mailbox T)) -> i64?`, called `poll.add_mailbox(set, m)`: Adds a mailbox to the set, so a thread waiting on sockets, streams and timers is woken by a value another thread sends: told `readable` while a receive on it would not wait, because it holds a value, is closed or answers `stopped`, and told again at every wait until the program takes what it holds. Fails `closed`, `limit`, `failed`, `invalid`. What each call must give its type parameters: `T` reaches no `ptr` and no `cstr`: `(mailbox T)` makes it cross between threads, line 319; `T` is not `()`: `(mailbox T)` is a mailbox of it, line 319.
- `function reset_timer(set: Set, key: i64, first: time.Duration, every: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `poll.reset_timer(set, key, first: first, every: every)`: Sets the timer `key` again from now, as `add_timer` sets one. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `closed`.
- `function change(set: Set, key: i64, interest: Interest) -> ()?`, called `poll.change(set, key, interest)`: Makes the entry `key` wait for what `interest` says from now. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `closed`.
- `function remove(set: Set, key: i64) -> ()?`, called `poll.remove(set, key)`: Takes the entry `key` out of the set, letting go of what it held, which stays open and the program's. Fails `not_found`, `closed`.
- `function wait(set: Set, limit: time.Duration) -> [Event]?`, called `poll.wait(set, limit)`: The entries of the set found ready, waiting until one is, a timer falls due, `limit` passes, or the stop is asked. Fails `stopped`, `invalid`, `limit`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function wait_forever(set: Set) -> [Event]?`, called `poll.wait_forever(set)`: The entries of the set found ready, waiting as long as it takes: until one is ready, a timer falls due, or the stop is asked. Fails `stopped`, `closed`, `failed`.


### tls

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/tls`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tls/).

TLS: a connection whose bytes are encrypted and whose peer is checked, as an `io.Stream` that `io` reads, writes and closes like any other, so `http`, `sql/postgres` and any program use it unchanged.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument the layer refuses, or a certificate the client refused: every function that takes text, `connect` and `client_over` for a certificate.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: Nothing listens there, the peer closed the connection, or the stream or the listener is closed: `connect`, `accept`, `close_listener`, `client_over`, `server_over`, `version_of`, `protocol_of`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A host name with no address: `connect`.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The time allowed ran out: `connect`, `accept`.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while the call waited (`os.ask_stop`): `connect`, `accept`.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: Something listens at that address and port already: `listen`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The system refuses the address or the port to this program: `listen`.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system has no memory, socket or stream left: every function that makes a connection or a listener.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This platform has no such thing: TLS over a stream the program holds on macOS, or no TLS library on a Linux machine.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The handshake failed, or no route reaches the host; the message carries the system's own words.
- `record Client(roots: str, protocols: [str])`: What a client trusts and offers.
- `record Server(chain: str, key: str, protocols: [str])`: What a server presents.
- `variant Step = .send(data: [u8]) | .expect(answer: [u8]) | .expect_line(prefix: str)`: One step of an exchange in plain text before TLS begins on the same connection, as Postgres's SSLRequest, SMTP's and IMAP's STARTTLS and a proxy's CONNECT need: `connect_after` and `listen_after` run a list of them, in order, and TLS begins once the last is met.
- `record Listener(handle: hero_tls.Listener, port: i64)`: A socket listening for TLS connections, made only by `listen`.
- `function is_available() -> bool`, called `tls.is_available()`: Whether this machine has the platform's TLS library: false only on a Linux machine with no `libssl.so.3`, where every other function fails `unsupported`.
- `function connect(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, client: Client) -> net.Conn?`, called `tls.connect(host, port, deadline, client)`: A TLS connection to `host` at `port`, its peer's certificate checked against `client`'s roots and `host`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `not_found`, `timeout`, `stopped`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function connect_unchecked_for_tests(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, protocols: [str]) -> net.Conn?`, called `tls.connect_unchecked_for_tests(host, port, deadline, protocols)`: FOR TESTS ONLY: a TLS connection to `host` at `port` whose peer's certificate is not checked at all, neither its authority, nor its dates, nor its host, so anybody between the two ends reads and changes every byte. Fails as `connect` does, but never for a certificate.
- `function client_over(@inner: io.Stream, host: str, client: Client) -> io.Stream?`, called `tls.client_over(@inner, host, client)`: TLS as the client of `host` over `inner`, a stream already connected to it: what Postgres's `sslmode` and a proxy's tunnel need, where a protocol of their own comes before TLS. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function connect_after(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, client: Client, steps: [Step]) -> net.Conn?`, called `tls.connect_after(host, port, deadline, client, steps)`: A TLS connection to `host` at `port` whose `steps` are run in plain text on the connection before TLS begins, as Postgres's SSLRequest or SMTP's STARTTLS: on every platform, macOS included, since the exchange runs below TLS inside the connection this call makes. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `timeout`.
- `function listen(host: str, port: i64, server: Server) -> Listener?`, called `tls.listen(host, port, server)`: A socket listening for TLS connections on `host` at `port`, each presenting `server`'s chain and key. Fails `invalid`, `exists`, `permission`, `unsupported`.
- `function listen_after(host: str, port: i64, server: Server, steps: [Step]) -> Listener?`, called `tls.listen_after(host, port, server, steps)`: A socket listening for TLS connections on `host` at `port`, each running `steps` from the server's side in plain text before TLS begins: a server that speaks Postgres's or SMTP's exchange before its TLS. Fails `invalid`.
- `function accept(l: Listener, deadline: time.Duration) -> net.Conn?`, called `tls.accept(l, deadline)`: The next connection `l` holds, once its handshake has ended: its TLS stream and its two ends' addresses, the listener's own and the client's. Fails `closed`, `timeout`, `invalid`, `stopped`, `failed`.
- `function close_listener(@l: Listener) -> ()?`, called `tls.close_listener(@l)`: Closes `l` and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`; an `accept` another thread waits in ends at once. Fails `closed`.
- `function server_over(@inner: io.Stream, server: Server) -> io.Stream?`, called `tls.server_over(@inner, server)`: TLS as the server over `inner`, a stream already connected to a client, presenting `server`'s chain and key. Fails `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_deadline(s: io.Stream, deadline: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `tls.set_deadline(s, deadline)`: Makes every later and waiting read and write of `s` end by `deadline` from now, failing `timeout`: a TLS stream's by its own layer, and a connection's stream that is no TLS stream by `net.set_deadline`, so a program holding either kind moves its deadline by this one call. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_accept_deadline(l: Listener, deadline: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `tls.set_accept_deadline(l, deadline)`: Makes every `accept` on `l` waiting for a client, and every later one, end by `deadline` from now, failing `timeout`; a handshake's own time stays `accept`'s. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function version_of(s: io.Stream) -> i64?`, called `tls.version_of(s)`: The version of TLS `s` speaks: 12 for TLS 1.2, 13 for TLS 1.3. Fails `closed`.
- `function protocol_of(s: io.Stream) -> str?`, called `tls.protocol_of(s)`: The application protocol the two ends chose (ALPN), "" where none was. Fails `closed`, `not_text`.
- `constant TEST_ROOT: str`, value `fixture.ROOT`: FOR TESTS ONLY: a test authority's certificate, EC on P-256, valid from 2019 to 2125, which signed every certificate below but `TEST_SELF_CHAIN`.
- `constant TEST_LOCALHOST_CHAIN: str`, value `fixture.LOCALHOST_CHAIN`: FOR TESTS ONLY: a certificate for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` signed by `TEST_ROOT`.
- `constant TEST_LOCALHOST_KEY: str`, value `fixture.LOCALHOST_KEY`: FOR TESTS ONLY: `TEST_LOCALHOST_CHAIN`'s key, as PKCS #8.
- `constant TEST_WRONG_CHAIN: str`, value `fixture.WRONG_CHAIN`: FOR TESTS ONLY: a certificate for `wrong.example` alone, signed by `TEST_ROOT`, which a client of `localhost` refuses for its host.
- `constant TEST_WRONG_KEY: str`, value `fixture.WRONG_KEY`: FOR TESTS ONLY: `TEST_WRONG_CHAIN`'s key.
- `constant TEST_EXPIRED_CHAIN: str`, value `fixture.EXPIRED_CHAIN`: FOR TESTS ONLY: a certificate for `localhost` signed by `TEST_ROOT` and valid in 2020 alone, which a client refuses as past its last day.
- `constant TEST_EXPIRED_KEY: str`, value `fixture.EXPIRED_KEY`: FOR TESTS ONLY: `TEST_EXPIRED_CHAIN`'s key.
- `constant TEST_SELF_CHAIN: str`, value `fixture.SELF_CHAIN`: FOR TESTS ONLY: a certificate for `localhost` signed by its own key, which no authority vouches for.
- `constant TEST_SELF_KEY: str`, value `fixture.SELF_KEY`: FOR TESTS ONLY: `TEST_SELF_CHAIN`'s key.


### log

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/log`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/log/).

Lines with a time and a level, written to a stream: a logger is a record that says where its lines go, the lowest level it writes, a prefix, the line's form and the fields every line carries, built by `to` and passed along.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text that names no level, from `parse_level`.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a write to a stream that is closed, or whose reader is gone, from `write` and the four functions named after a level.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a write to a stream not opened to write, from `write` and the four functions named after a level.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of a write the system refused for another reason, its message the system's words, and of a clock the system cannot read, from `write` and the four functions named after a level.
- `constant TIME_KEY: str`, value `"time"`: The key of a line's time in the JSON form, `time`.
- `constant LEVEL_KEY: str`, value `"level"`: The key of a line's level in the JSON form, `level`.
- `constant MESSAGE_KEY: str`, value `"msg"`: The key of a line's message in the JSON form, `msg`.
- `variant Level = .debug | .info | .warn | .error`: How much a line matters, from the least to the most.
- `function level_name(level: Level) -> str`, called `log.level_name(level)`: The name a line writes for `level`: `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARN` or `ERROR`.
- `function level_number(level: Level) -> i64`, called `log.level_number(level)`: The number Python's `logging` gives `level`: 10, 20, 30 or 40, a larger number for a line that matters more.
- `function parse_level(name: str) -> Level?`, called `log.parse_level(name)`: The level `name` names, as a setting or an environment variable writes it. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Field(key: str, value: Value)`: A value a line carries beside its message: a key and its value.
- `variant Value = .text(v: str) | .integer(v: i64) | .number(v: f64) | .boolean(v: bool) | .duration(v: time.Duration) | .instant(v: time.Instant) | .group(fields: [Field])`: What a field holds.
- `function text(key: str, value: str) -> Field`, called `log.text(key: key, value: value)`: The field `key` holding the text `value`.
- `function integer(key: str, value: i64) -> Field`, called `log.integer(key, value)`: The field `key` holding the whole number `value`.
- `function number(key: str, value: f64) -> Field`, called `log.number(key, value)`: The field `key` holding the float `value`.
- `function boolean(key: str, value: bool) -> Field`, called `log.boolean(key, value)`: The field `key` holding `value`, `true` or `false`.
- `function duration(key: str, value: time.Duration) -> Field`, called `log.duration(key, value)`: The field `key` holding the length of time `value`.
- `function instant(key: str, value: time.Instant) -> Field`, called `log.instant(key, value)`: The field `key` holding the moment `value`.
- `function group(key: str, fields: [Field]) -> Field`, called `log.group(key, fields)`: The field `key` holding `fields` as a group.
- `variant Form = .text | .json`: The two forms of a line.
- `record Logger(stream: io.Stream, level: Level, prefix: str, form: Form, fields: [Field], clock: (function() -> time.Instant?))`: Where a logger's lines go and what each holds.
- `function to(stream: io.Stream) -> Logger`, called `log.to(stream)`: A logger writing to `stream`: lines at `info` and above, no prefix, the text form, no fields, the time from `time.now`.
- `function with_level(logger: Logger, level: Level) -> Logger`, called `log.with_level(logger, level)`: A copy of `logger` that writes the lines at `level` and above.
- `function with_prefix(logger: Logger, prefix: str) -> Logger`, called `log.with_prefix(logger, prefix)`: A copy of `logger` whose messages open with `prefix`.
- `function with_form(logger: Logger, form: Form) -> Logger`, called `log.with_form(logger, form)`: A copy of `logger` that writes its lines in `form`.
- `function with_fields(logger: Logger, fields: [Field]) -> Logger`, called `log.with_fields(logger, fields)`: A copy of `logger` whose lines carry `fields` after the ones it carries already.
- `function with_clock(logger: Logger, clock: (function() -> time.Instant?)) -> Logger`, called `log.with_clock(logger, clock)`: A copy of `logger` that asks `clock` for each line's time: how a test makes every line the same on every run.
- `function is_enabled(logger: Logger, level: Level) -> bool`, called `log.is_enabled(logger, level)`: Whether `logger` writes a line at `level`: where `level` is the logger's own or above it.
- `function write(logger: Logger, level: Level, msg: str, fields: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `log.write(logger, level, msg, fields)`: Writes one line at `level` to `logger`'s stream, at the time its clock reads, where the logger writes that level; else does nothing. Fails `closed`, `permission`, `failed`.
- `function debug(logger: Logger, msg: str, fields: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `log.debug(logger, msg, fields)`: Writes one line at `debug`, as `write` does. Fails as `write` fails.
- `function info(logger: Logger, msg: str, fields: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `log.info(logger, msg, fields)`: Writes one line at `info`, as `write` does. Fails as `write` fails.
- `function warn(logger: Logger, msg: str, fields: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `log.warn(logger, msg, fields)`: Writes one line at `warn`, as `write` does. Fails as `write` fails.
- `function error(logger: Logger, msg: str, fields: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `log.error(logger, msg, fields)`: Writes one line at `error`, as `write` does. Fails as `write` fails.
- `function format_line(logger: Logger, level: Level, at: time.Instant, msg: str, fields: [Field]) -> str`, called `log.format_line(logger, level, at, msg, fields)`: The line `write` writes for these, without its line feed, whatever the logger's level: what a program checks a line against, or sends somewhere a stream does not reach.


### uuid

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/uuid`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/uuid/).

Universally unique identifiers (RFC 9562): versions 4 and 7 made, any version read from text or bytes and written back, the nil and the max values, and the version, the variant and a version 7's time read.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `text.INVALID`: The code a function fails with where its input is not a UUID: a text, bytes that are not 16, a time version 7 cannot hold, a UUID that is not of version 7 asked its time, or a version RFC 9562 does not define.
- `record Uuid(high: u64, low: u64)`: A UUID: 128 bits, held as two halves.
- `function nil_uuid() -> Uuid`, called `uuid.nil_uuid()`: The nil UUID, every bit 0 (RFC 9562 5.9): Python's `uuid.NIL`.
- `function max_uuid() -> Uuid`, called `uuid.max_uuid()`: The max UUID, every bit 1 (RFC 9562 5.10): Python's `uuid.MAX`.
- `variant Variant = .ncs | .rfc | .microsoft | .future`: Which layout a UUID's bits follow, read from its first bits of byte 8.
- `function new_v4() -> Uuid?`, called `uuid.new_v4()`: A new UUID of version 4: 122 bits from the system's generator for keys, the version and the variant set, as RFC 9562 5.4 asks. Fails with the code of `random.secure_below` where the system's generator refuses.
- `function new_v7() -> Uuid?`, called `uuid.new_v7()`: A new UUID of version 7 for this moment: the milliseconds since 1970 in its first 48 bits and 74 random bits after (RFC 9562 5.7), so it sorts after one made a millisecond before. Fails `invalid`.
- `function new_v7_at(unix_milliseconds: i64) -> Uuid?`, called `uuid.new_v7_at(unix_milliseconds)`: A new UUID of version 7 for the moment `unix_milliseconds`: what `new_v7` makes, at a time of the caller's. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_version(id: Uuid, version: i64) -> Uuid?`, called `uuid.with_version(id, version)`: `id` marked as a UUID of `version`: its four version bits set to `version` and its variant to RFC 9562's, its other 122 bits kept, as Python's `uuid.UUID(bytes=..., version=...)` makes one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse(s: str) -> Uuid?`, called `uuid.parse(s)`: The UUID `s` writes: the standard form of 36 characters in either case, the same 32 digits with no hyphen, either of these inside braces, or the standard form after `urn:uuid:`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format(id: Uuid) -> str`, called `uuid.format(id)`: `id` in the standard form, lower case: `f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6`.
- `function format_urn(id: Uuid) -> str`, called `uuid.format_urn(id)`: `id` as a URN: `urn:uuid:` and the standard form.
- `function format_hex(id: Uuid) -> str`, called `uuid.format_hex(id)`: `id` as its 32 hexadecimal digits in lower case, with no hyphen: Python's `hex`.
- `function from_bytes(data: [u8]) -> Uuid?`, called `uuid.from_bytes(data)`: The UUID the 16 bytes `data` hold, the first byte the highest, as a database or a protocol stores it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_bytes(id: Uuid) -> [u8]`, called `uuid.to_bytes(id)`: The 16 bytes of `id`, the first the highest: RFC 9562's order, Python's `bytes`.
- `function version_of(id: Uuid) -> i64`, called `uuid.version_of(id)`: The version of `id`, the four bits RFC 9562 gives it, from 0 to 15: 4 for one made by `new_v4`, 7 for one made by `new_v7`.
- `function variant_of(id: Uuid) -> Variant`, called `uuid.variant_of(id)`: The layout `id` follows, read from the first bits of its byte 8.
- `function compare(a: Uuid, b: Uuid) -> i64`, called `uuid.compare(a: a, b: b)`: Which of `a` and `b` orders first: -1 where `a` does, 1 where `b` does, 0 where they are the same, by their bytes as numbers; for version 7, the order they were made in, to the millisecond.
- `function time_of(id: Uuid) -> time.Instant?`, called `uuid.time_of(id)`: The moment a UUID of version 7 was made, to the millisecond. Fails `invalid`.


### toml

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/toml`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/toml/).

TOML 1.1.0 read and written: a document of tables, keys and values, read into a tree a program matches on and written back as text that reads as the same tree.

- `variant Value = .text(v: str) | .integer(v: i64) | .float(v: f64) | .boolean(v: bool) | .date_time(at: time.DateTime, offset_minutes: i64) | .local_date_time(at: time.DateTime) | .local_date(at: time.DateTime) | .local_time(since_midnight: time.Duration) | .array(items: [Value]) | .table(members: {str: Value})`: One TOML value.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text that is not TOML 1.1.0, of a value that is not of the kind asked for, and of a value no TOML writes.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of an integer past what an `i64` holds.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a key a table does not hold: `value_at`, `value_of`, `remove_value`.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a table added where something stands already: `add_table`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a value one side has no form for: a `nan` or an infinity, which `to_json` fails with, and JSON's `null`, which `from_json` fails with.
- `constant MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `512`: The deepest a value may stand below the document: the keys of its path and the arrays and inline tables around it counted together.
- `function parse(text: str) -> Value?`, called `toml.parse(text)`: The document `text` holds, as a `table`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function value_at(v: Value, path: [str]) -> Value?`, called `toml.value_at(v, path)`: The value under `path` in `v`, each step a key of a table or the index of an item of an array, read as `value_of` reads a document's path. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function text_at(v: Value, key: str) -> str?`, called `toml.text_at(v, key)`: The text of the member `key` of the table `v`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function int_at(v: Value, key: str) -> i64?`, called `toml.int_at(v, key)`: The integer of the member `key` of the table `v`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function bool_at(v: Value, key: str) -> bool?`, called `toml.bool_at(v, key)`: The boolean of the member `key` of the table `v`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function items_at(v: Value, key: str) -> [Value]?`, called `toml.items_at(v, key)`: The items of the array in the member `key` of the table `v`, in order. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function instant_of(v: Value) -> time.Instant?`, called `toml.instant_of(v)`: The instant a `date_time` names. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function format(v: Value) -> str?`, called `toml.format(v)`: `v`, a document, written as TOML 1.1.0 text that `parse` reads back as `v`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Document(text: str)`: A TOML document held as its text, so that an edit changes only the bytes of what it touches: its comments, blank lines, order, quotes and spacing kept everywhere else, as a program that writes a file a person also edits needs.
- `function parse_document(text: str) -> Document?`, called `toml.parse_document(text)`: The document `text` holds, to be edited in place. Fails where `parse` fails on `text`, with its code and message.
- `function format_document(d: Document) -> str`, called `toml.format_document(d)`: The text of `d`: what was read, every byte an edit did not touch the same.
- `function value_of(d: Document, path: [str]) -> Value?`, called `toml.value_of(d, path)`: The value under `path` in `d`, each step a key of a table or the index of an item of an array. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function set_value(@d: Document, path: [str], value: Value) -> ()?`, called `toml.set_value(@d, path, value)`: Sets the value under `path` in `d` to `value`, written as `format` writes it, every other byte of `d` kept. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function remove_value(@d: Document, path: [str]) -> ()?`, called `toml.remove_value(@d, path)`: Takes what `path` names out of `d`, with its own bytes and no others. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function add_table(@d: Document, path: [str]) -> ()?`, called `toml.add_table(@d, path)`: Adds an empty table at `path` to `d`: a section `[...]` after the last section of the table that holds it, or `{}` inside an inline table. Fails `exists`.
- `function add_table_entry(@d: Document, path: [str], entry: Value) -> i64?`, called `toml.add_table_entry(@d, path, entry)`: Appends `entry` to the array of tables `path` names in `d`, and answers the index it takes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_json(v: Value) -> json.Value?`, called `toml.to_json(v)`: `v` as a `json.Value`: a table an object, an array a list, and a date or a time the RFC 3339 text TOML writes for it. Fails `unsupported`, `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function from_json(v: json.Value) -> Value?`, called `toml.from_json(v)`: `v` as a TOML value: an object a table, a list an array. Fails `unsupported`.


### sql

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/sql`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/).

What a program does with a database whatever the database is: the values that travel to it and back, the rows a query answers and the reads of their columns by place and by name, what a statement that changes rows answers, the codes a database failure is told with, and an identifier quoted.

- `variant Value = .null_value | .boolean(v: bool) | .integer(v: i64) | .float(v: f64) | .text(v: str) | .blob(v: [u8]) | .instant(v: time.Instant)`: A value as it travels to a database and back.
- `record Column(name: str, type_name: str)`: What a driver knows of one column of a query's answer.
- `record Row(names: [str], values: [Value])`: One row of a query's answer: its values in the order of the columns, each under the column's name.
- `record Rows(columns: [Column], rows: [Row])`: Everything a query answered: its columns and its rows, in the order the database gave them.
- `record Result(rows_affected: i64, last_id: i64?)`: What a statement that changes rows answers.
- `function value_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> Value?`, called `sql.value_at(row, index)`: The value of the column at `index` of `row`, counted from 0. Fails `not_found`.
- `function value_named(row: Row, name: str) -> Value?`, called `sql.value_named(row, name)`: The value of the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_null_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> bool?`, called `sql.is_null_at(row, index)`: Whether the column at `index` of `row` is `NULL`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_null_named(row: Row, name: str) -> bool?`, called `sql.is_null_named(row, name)`: Whether the first column of `row` named `name` is `NULL`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function boolean_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> bool?`, called `sql.boolean_at(row, index)`: The truth value of the column at `index` of `row`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function boolean_named(row: Row, name: str) -> bool?`, called `sql.boolean_named(row, name)`: The truth value of the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function integer_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> i64?`, called `sql.integer_at(row, index)`: The whole number in the column at `index` of `row`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function integer_named(row: Row, name: str) -> i64?`, called `sql.integer_named(row, name)`: The whole number in the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function float_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> f64?`, called `sql.float_at(row, index)`: The floating-point number in the column at `index` of `row`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function float_named(row: Row, name: str) -> f64?`, called `sql.float_named(row, name)`: The floating-point number in the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function text_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> str?`, called `sql.text_at(row, index)`: The text in the column at `index` of `row`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function text_named(row: Row, name: str) -> str?`, called `sql.text_named(row, name)`: The text in the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function blob_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `sql.blob_at(row, index)`: The bytes in the column at `index` of `row`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function blob_named(row: Row, name: str) -> [u8]?`, called `sql.blob_named(row, name)`: The bytes in the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function instant_at(row: Row, index: i64) -> time.Instant?`, called `sql.instant_at(row, index)`: The moment in the column at `index` of `row`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function instant_named(row: Row, name: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `sql.instant_named(row, name)`: The moment in the first column of `row` named `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function kind_of(v: Value) -> str`, called `sql.kind_of(v)`: The name of the case `v` is: `null`, `boolean`, `integer`, `float`, `text`, `blob` or `instant`, as a failure's message names it.
- `function quote_identifier(name: str) -> str?`, called `sql.quote_identifier(name)`: `name` as a quoted identifier of standard SQL, which PostgreSQL and SQLite both read: inside double quotes, each double quote in it doubled. Fails `invalid`.
- `function quote_qualified(parts: [str]) -> str?`, called `sql.quote_qualified(parts)`: The parts of a qualified name, each quoted as `quote_identifier` quotes it, joined by dots: `["app", "users"]` gives `"app"."users"`. Fails `invalid`.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a value read as a kind it is not, and of a statement, a name or a parameter the database refuses as written: a syntax error, a value of the wrong type, a constraint a row breaks other than a unique one.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a column a row does not hold, of a query that answers no row where one was asked for, and of a table, a column, a function or a database the database does not know.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a row a unique key already holds, and of a table, a column or another object made where one of its name is already there.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a login the database refuses, and of a statement the user may not run.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a value past what its column's type holds: a number out of its range, a text longer than its column allows.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a connection that is closed, or that the database or the network closed while the call waited.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a call whose time ran out: a connection's deadline, or a limit of the database's own on how long a session may wait.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The code of a statement the database cancelled while it ran, and of a call that ended because the program was asked to stop.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a database that has no more of what the statement needs: disk, memory, connections, or a limit of its own on a statement's size.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of what this database or this driver does not do: a feature the database does not have, a protocol the driver does not speak.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of every other failure of a database, a deadlock and a transaction that could not be serialized among them: the message carries the database's own code and words.
- `function failure_message(database_code: str, message: str) -> str`, called `sql.failure_message(database_code: database_code, message: message)`: The message of a failure a database reported: its own code in brackets, then its own words, `[23505] duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_pkey"`.
- `function database_code_of(msg: str) -> str?`, called `sql.database_code_of(msg)`: The database's own code in the message of a failure `failure_message` made: `23505` in `[23505] duplicate key value violates unique constraint`. Fails `not_found`.


### protobuf

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/protobuf`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/protobuf/).

Protocol Buffers: the wire format read and written field by field, `.proto` files read at run time into a schema, messages held as a tree a program matches on and encoded or decoded by that schema, the proto3 JSON mapping to and from a `json.Value`, and the well-known types.

- `variant Value = .boolean(v: bool) | .int32(v: i32) | .int64(v: i64) | .uint32(v: u32) | .uint64(v: u64) | .float(v: f32) | .double(v: f64) | .text(v: str) | .binary(v: [u8]) | .enumeration(number: i32) | .message(m: Message) | .list(items: [Value]) | .entries(entries: [Entry])`: One value of a field: a `match` on it answers all thirteen cases.
- `record Entry(key: Value, value: Value)`: One entry of a map field.
- `record Message(type_name: str, fields: {i64: Value}, unknown: [u8])`: A message of any type the schema holds, as a tree: the fields it holds by number, and the bytes of those its type does not declare.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of bytes, a `.proto` text or JSON that is not what the function reads, and of a value not of its field's kind.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a type, a field, a file or a name the schema does not hold.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a number past what its field's kind holds.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of a `string` field whose bytes are not UTF-8 where its file asks them to be.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `100`: The deepest nesting `decode` and `from_json` read: a message inside a message is 2 deep.
- `constant MAX_FIELD_NUMBER: i64`, value `536870911`: The largest field number, 2^29 - 1.
- `constant TYPE_URL_PREFIX: str`, value `"type.googleapis.com/"`: The prefix `pack_any` writes before a type's full name, as every runtime writes it.
- `variant Syntax = .proto2 | .proto3 | .editions(edition: str)`: How a `.proto` file is written: proto2, proto3, or an edition.
- `variant Kind = .double | .float | .int32 | .int64 | .uint32 | .uint64 | .sint32 | .sint64 | .fixed32 | .fixed64 | .sfixed32 | .sfixed64 | .boolean | .text | .binary | .enumeration | .message | .group`: The kind of a field, as its `.proto` names it.
- `variant Cardinality = .optional | .required | .repeated`: How many values a field holds.
- `variant Constant = .identifier(v: str) | .number(text: str) | .quoted(v: [u8]) | .aggregate(text: str)`: The value of an option, as the file wrote it.
- `record OptionSetting(name: str, value: Constant)`: One option a declaration sets.
- `record Range(first: i64, last: i64)`: A range of numbers, both ends included, as `reserved 9 to 11;` writes it.
- `record Field(name: str, full_name: str, json_name: str, number: i64, kind: Kind, cardinality: Cardinality, type_name: str, has_presence: bool, packed: bool, is_map: bool, oneof: str, proto3_optional: bool, default_value: Value, has_default: bool, validate_utf8: bool, closed_enum: bool, extendee: str, options: [OptionSetting])`: A field of a message, or an extension.
- `record Oneof(name: str, full_name: str, synthetic: bool, fields: [str], options: [OptionSetting])`: A oneof: fields of which a message holds at most one.
- `record MessageType(name: str, full_name: str, file: str, fields: [Field], oneofs: [Oneof], nested_messages: [str], nested_enums: [str], extension_ranges: [Range], reserved_ranges: [Range], reserved_names: [str], is_map_entry: bool, options: [OptionSetting])`: A message type: what `new_message`, `decode` and the JSON mapping read.
- `record EnumValue(name: str, number: i32, options: [OptionSetting])`: One value of an enum.
- `record EnumType(name: str, full_name: str, file: str, values: [EnumValue], closed: bool, reserved_ranges: [Range], reserved_names: [str], options: [OptionSetting])`: An enum type.
- `record Method(name: str, full_name: str, input_type: str, output_type: str, client_streaming: bool, server_streaming: bool, options: [OptionSetting])`: One method of a service, what `grpc` calls.
- `record Service(name: str, full_name: str, file: str, methods: [Method], options: [OptionSetting])`: A service.
- `record File(name: str, package: str, syntax: Syntax, dependencies: [str], public_dependencies: [str], weak_dependencies: [str], messages: [str], enums: [str], services: [str], extensions: [str], options: [OptionSetting])`: A `.proto` file, read.
- `record Schema(files: {str: File}, messages: {str: MessageType}, enums: {str: EnumType}, services: {str: Service}, extensions: {str: Field}, compiled: model.Schema)`: Every file a program read and everything they declare, each name resolved: made only by `parse_schema` and `parse_schema_text`.
- `function parse_schema(names: [str], open: (function(str) -> str?)) -> Schema?`, called `protobuf.parse_schema(names, open)`: The schema the files `names` and every file they import declare, each file's text given by `open`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_schema_text(name: str, text: str) -> Schema?`, called `protobuf.parse_schema_text(name: name, text: text)`: The schema the one file `text` declares, read under the name `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function parse_schema_texts(texts: {str: str}) -> Schema?`, called `protobuf.parse_schema_texts(texts)`: The schema the files `texts` declare, each file's text given by its name, imports read among them. Fails `not_found`.
- `function field_of(schema: Schema, type_name: str, field: str) -> Field?`, called `protobuf.field_of(schema, type_name: type_name, field: field)`: The field `field` of the message type `type_name`, an extension's full name included. Fails `not_found`.
- `function message_named(schema: Schema, name: str) -> MessageType?`, called `protobuf.message_named(schema, name)`: The message type whose full name is `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function enum_named(schema: Schema, name: str) -> EnumType?`, called `protobuf.enum_named(schema, name)`: The enum whose full name is `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function service_named(schema: Schema, name: str) -> Service?`, called `protobuf.service_named(schema, name)`: The service whose full name is `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function file_named(schema: Schema, name: str) -> File?`, called `protobuf.file_named(schema, name)`: The file read under the name `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function extension_named(schema: Schema, name: str) -> Field?`, called `protobuf.extension_named(schema, name)`: The extension whose full name is `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function field_named(t: MessageType, name: str) -> Field?`, called `protobuf.field_named(t, name)`: The field of `t` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function field_numbered(t: MessageType, number: i64) -> Field?`, called `protobuf.field_numbered(t, number)`: The field of `t` whose number is `number`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function method_named(s: Service, name: str) -> Method?`, called `protobuf.method_named(s, name)`: The method of `s` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function enum_value_named(e: EnumType, name: str) -> EnumValue?`, called `protobuf.enum_value_named(e, name)`: The value of `e` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function enum_value_numbered(e: EnumType, number: i32) -> EnumValue?`, called `protobuf.enum_value_numbered(e, number)`: The first value of `e` whose number is `number`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function new_message(schema: Schema, type_name: str) -> Message?`, called `protobuf.new_message(schema, type_name)`: An empty message of the type `type_name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function get(schema: Schema, m: Message, field: str) -> Value?`, called `protobuf.get(schema, m, field)`: The value of `m`'s field `field`, or its default where it is unset. Fails `not_found`.
- `function has(schema: Schema, m: Message, field: str) -> bool?`, called `protobuf.has(schema, m, field)`: Whether `m` holds a value for `field`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function set(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, value: Value) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.set(schema, @m, field, value)`: Sets `m`'s field `field` to `value`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function set_int(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, n: i64) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.set_int(schema, @m, field, n)`: Sets `m`'s integer field `field` to `n`, at the field's own width and sign. Fails `does_not_fit`, `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function set_uint(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, n: u64) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.set_uint(schema, @m, field, n)`: Sets `m`'s unsigned field `field` to `n`. Fails as `set_int` fails.
- `function set_float(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, x: f64) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.set_float(schema, @m, field, x)`: Sets `m`'s `float` or `double` field `field` to `x`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function set_enum(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.set_enum(schema, @m, field: field, name: name)`: Sets `m`'s enum field `field` to the value its enum names `name`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function enum_name_of(schema: Schema, m: Message, field: str) -> str?`, called `protobuf.enum_name_of(schema, m, field)`: The name of the value `m`'s enum field `field` holds. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function clear(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.clear(schema, @m, field)`: Takes `m`'s field `field` back to unset. Fails `not_found`.
- `function which_oneof(schema: Schema, m: Message, oneof: str) -> str?`, called `protobuf.which_oneof(schema, m, oneof)`: The name of the field of the oneof `oneof` that `m` holds. Fails `not_found`.
- `function add_item(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, item: Value) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.add_item(schema, @m, field, item)`: Adds `item` at the end of `m`'s repeated field `field`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function put_entry(schema: Schema, @m: Message, field: str, key: Value, value: Value) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.put_entry(schema, @m, field, key: key, value: value)`: Puts `value` under `key` in `m`'s map field `field`, in place of any value the key held. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.

- `function check_required(schema: Schema, m: Message) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.check_required(schema, m)`: Checks that `m`, and every message inside it, holds each field its type requires. Fails `invalid`.
- `function clear_unknown(schema: Schema, @m: Message) -> ()?`, called `protobuf.clear_unknown(schema, @m)`: Takes away the unknown bytes of `m` and of every message inside it. Fails as `encode_partial` fails.
- `function kind_of(v: Value) -> str`, called `protobuf.kind_of(v)`: The name of `v`'s case: `boolean`, `int32`, `int64`, `uint32`, `uint64`, `float`, `double`, `text`, `binary`, `enumeration`, `message`, `list` or `entries`.
- `function bool_of(v: Value) -> bool?`, called `protobuf.bool_of(v)`: The `bool` of a `.boolean`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function int_of(v: Value) -> i64?`, called `protobuf.int_of(v)`: The integer of an integer value, or an enum's number. Fails `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function uint_of(v: Value) -> u64?`, called `protobuf.uint_of(v)`: The integer of an integer value that is not negative. Fails `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function float_of(v: Value) -> f64?`, called `protobuf.float_of(v)`: The number of a `.float` or a `.double`, as an `f64`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function text_of(v: Value) -> str?`, called `protobuf.text_of(v)`: The text of a `.text`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bytes_of(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `protobuf.bytes_of(v)`: The bytes of a `.binary`, or of a `.text` as UTF-8. Fails `invalid`.
- `function message_of(v: Value) -> Message?`, called `protobuf.message_of(v)`: The message of a `.message`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function items_of(v: Value) -> [Value]?`, called `protobuf.items_of(v)`: The values of a `.list`, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function entries_of(v: Value) -> [Entry]?`, called `protobuf.entries_of(v)`: The entries of an `.entries`, in the order of their keys. Fails `invalid`.
- `function entry_value(v: Value, key: Value) -> Value?`, called `protobuf.entry_value(v: v, key: key)`: The value an `.entries` holds under `key`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `record DecodeOptions(max_depth: i64, allow_partial: bool, discard_unknown: bool)`: How bytes are decoded.
- `record Decoded(message: Message, next: i64)`: What `decode_delimited` answers.
- `function strict_decode_options() -> DecodeOptions`, called `protobuf.strict_decode_options()`: The options of the protocol's own reading: nesting to `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`, required fields checked, unknown fields kept.
- `function encode(schema: Schema, m: Message) -> [u8]?`, called `protobuf.encode(schema, m)`: `m` encoded, its fields in the order of their numbers. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function encode_partial(schema: Schema, m: Message) -> [u8]?`, called `protobuf.encode_partial(schema, m)`: `m` encoded as `encode` encodes it, a required field unset allowed. Fails as `encode` fails, but for a required field.

- `function decode_with(schema: Schema, type_name: str, data: [u8], options: DecodeOptions) -> Message?`, called `protobuf.decode_with(schema, type_name, data, options)`: The message `data` encodes, read as `options` say. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `function encode_delimited(schema: Schema, m: Message) -> [u8]?`, called `protobuf.encode_delimited(schema, m)`: `m` encoded after its length as a varint, as a stream of messages holds it. Fails as `encode` fails.

- `record JsonOptions(use_proto_names: bool, use_enum_numbers: bool, emit_defaults: bool)`: How a message is written as JSON.
- `record JsonReadOptions(ignore_unknown: bool, max_depth: i64)`: How JSON is read.

- `function default_json_read_options() -> JsonReadOptions`, called `protobuf.default_json_read_options()`: The options of the mapping's own reading: an unknown member refused, nesting to `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`.

- `function format_duration(m: Message) -> str?`, called `protobuf.format_duration(m)`: The text the JSON mapping writes for a `google.protobuf.Duration`: seconds with 0, 3, 6 or 9 digits of fraction and `s`, `-1.5s`. Fails `invalid`.

- `function push_fixed32(@to: [u8], v: u32)`, called `protobuf.push_fixed32(@to, v)`: Writes `v` as four bytes, the lowest first, at the end of `to`.
- `function push_fixed64(@to: [u8], v: u64)`, called `protobuf.push_fixed64(@to, v)`: Writes `v` as eight bytes, the lowest first, at the end of `to`.
- `function push_length_delimited(@to: [u8], v: [u8])`, called `protobuf.push_length_delimited(to: @to, v: v)`: Writes the length of `v` as a varint, then `v`, at the end of `to`.

- `function decode_uvarint(data: [u8], at: i64) -> WireNumber?`, called `protobuf.decode_uvarint(data, at)`: The varint that begins at byte `at` of `data`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function decode_fixed32(data: [u8], at: i64) -> WireNumber?`, called `protobuf.decode_fixed32(data, at)`: The four bytes that begin at byte `at` of `data`, the lowest first. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_fixed64(data: [u8], at: i64) -> WireNumber?`, called `protobuf.decode_fixed64(data, at)`: The eight bytes that begin at byte `at` of `data`, the lowest first. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_length_delimited(data: [u8], at: i64) -> WireBytes?`, called `protobuf.decode_length_delimited(data, at)`: The length-delimited value that begins at byte `at` of `data`: a varint length, then that many bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function skip_field(data: [u8], tag: WireTag) -> i64?`, called `protobuf.skip_field(data, tag)`: The index past the value of the field whose tag `tag` is, a group's end tag included: the way past a field a program does not read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_zigzag(n: i64) -> u64`, called `protobuf.to_zigzag(n)`: `n` in zig-zag form, as `sint32` and `sint64` write it: 0, -1, 1, -2 become 0, 1, 2, 3.
- `function from_zigzag(n: u64) -> i64`, called `protobuf.from_zigzag(n)`: The number whose zig-zag form `n` is.
- `function size_of_uvarint(v: u64) -> i64`, called `protobuf.size_of_uvarint(v)`: How many bytes `push_uvarint` writes for `v`, 1 to 10.
- `record RawField(number: i64, value: RawValue)`: One field read with no schema: its number and its value as the wire holds it, which says nothing of the kind its `.proto` declares.
- `variant RawValue = .varint(v: u64) | .fixed64(v: u64) | .length_delimited(v: [u8]) | .group(fields: [RawField]) | .fixed32(v: u32)`: A field's value as the wire holds it.
- `function decode_raw(data: [u8]) -> [RawField]?`, called `protobuf.decode_raw(data)`: The fields `data` holds, read with no schema, as `protoc --decode_raw` reads them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_raw(fields: [RawField]) -> [u8]`, called `protobuf.encode_raw(fields)`: `fields` written on the wire, in their order.


### mail

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/mail`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mail/).

E-mail messages read and written: a message's header fields (RFC 5322), folded and unfolded with their order kept; addresses, address lists and groups; dates; encoded words (RFC 2047); MIME (RFC 2045 to 2049) with its content types and their parameters (RFC 2231), multipart messages read as a tree and written with a boundary none of their parts holds, quoted-printable and base 64; attachments and inline parts; and UTF-8 in header fields and addresses (RFC 6532).

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A text, a field or a value that is not what the function reads, the message saying where: every `parse_` function, and the writers for a name or a value a message may not hold.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A field, a part or a parameter asked for is not there: `value_of`, `disposition_of`, `filename_of`, `body_of`, `date_of`.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: Bytes that are not UTF-8 where text is asked: `text_of`, `decode_header`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A charset or a transfer encoding this package does not read, or a header that needs UTF-8 written where the options forbid it: `text_of`, `content_of`, `decode_header`, `encode_message`.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: A date outside what a `time.Instant` holds: `parse_date`.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system gave no random bytes for a new identifier: `make_message_id`.
- `constant MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `64`: How deep multiparts are read as a tree: 64 levels.
- `record Field(name: str, value: str)`: A header field: a name and its value, as one line of a message's header holds it once unfolded.
- `record Message(fields: [Field], body: [u8], parts: [Message], preamble: [u8], epilogue: [u8], defects: [str])`: A message, or one part of a MIME message, which has the same shape: header fields, then a body, or parts where it is a multipart.
- `record WriteOptions(utf8: bool, line_length: i64, line_end: str)`: How a message is written.
- `function standard_options() -> WriteOptions`, called `mail.standard_options()`: The options a message is sent with: header text above ASCII as encoded words, lines folded at 78 bytes, every line ending `"\r\n"`.
- `function utf8_options() -> WriteOptions`, called `mail.utf8_options()`: The options of a message sent to a server that took SMTPUTF8: header text written as UTF-8, lines folded at 78 bytes, every line ending `"\r\n"`.
- `function decode_message(data: [u8]) -> Message`, called `mail.decode_message(data)`: The message `data` holds, read whole: its header fields, then its body, a multipart read as a tree of parts.
- `function read_message(s: io.Stream) -> Message?`, called `mail.read_message(s)`: The message `s` holds from where it stands to its end, read as `decode_message` reads it. Fails where `s` fails, with its code.
- `function encode_message(m: Message, options: WriteOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `mail.encode_message(m, options)`: The bytes of `m`, its header fields folded and its parts written with a boundary none of them holds. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function write_message(s: io.Stream, m: Message, options: WriteOptions) -> ()?`, called `mail.write_message(s, m, options)`: Writes `m` to `s`, as `encode_message` writes it. Fails as `encode_message` fails, and where `s` fails, with its code.
- `function split_mbox(data: [u8]) -> [[u8]]`, called `mail.split_mbox(data)`: The messages of an mbox file, each as bytes `decode_message` reads.
- `function decode_fields(data: [u8]) -> [Field]`, called `mail.decode_fields(data)`: The header fields at the start of `data`, up to the first empty line, each unfolded.
- `function encode_fields(fields: [Field], options: WriteOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `mail.encode_fields(fields, options)`: `fields` written as a message's header, each folded, without the empty line that ends it. Fails as `encode_message` fails for a field.
- `function format_field(field: Field, options: WriteOptions) -> str?`, called `mail.format_field(field, options)`: `field` written as one header field, folded, with its line end. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function unfold(value: str) -> str`, called `mail.unfold(value)`: `value` with its line breaks taken out: every `"\r\n"` or `"\n"` that a space or a tab follows is removed, the space kept.
- `function value_of(m: Message, name: str) -> str?`, called `mail.value_of(m, name)`: The value of the first field of `m` named `name`, unfolded and not decoded. Fails `not_found`.
- `function values_of(m: Message, name: str) -> [str]`, called `mail.values_of(m, name)`: The values of every field of `m` named `name`, in order: [] where there is none.
- `function decoded_value_of(m: Message, name: str) -> str?`, called `mail.decoded_value_of(m, name)`: The value of the first field of `m` named `name`, its encoded words decoded. Fails `not_found`.
- `function has_field(m: Message, name: str) -> bool`, called `mail.has_field(m, name)`: Whether `m` has a field named `name`.
- `function with_field(m: Message, name: str, value: str) -> Message`, called `mail.with_field(m, name: name, value: value)`: A copy of `m` whose field `name` holds `value`: the first field of that name takes it and any other of that name is removed, or one is added at the end where there is none.
- `function with_field_added(m: Message, name: str, value: str) -> Message`, called `mail.with_field_added(m, name: name, value: value)`: A copy of `m` with one more field at the end of its header, whatever fields of that name it has: `Received`, `Comments`.
- `function without_field(m: Message, name: str) -> Message`, called `mail.without_field(m, name)`: A copy of `m` with no field named `name`.
- `record ContentType(media_type: str, params: {str: str})`: The media type of a part's content and its parameters, as `Content-Type` writes them: `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.
- `record Disposition(kind: str, params: {str: str})`: How a part is shown, as `Content-Disposition` writes it: `attachment; filename="a.pdf"`.
- `function content_type_of(m: Message) -> ContentType`, called `mail.content_type_of(m)`: The content type of `m`: its `Content-Type`, or the one RFC 2045 gives a part without a valid one, `text/plain; charset=us-ascii`.
- `function disposition_of(m: Message) -> Disposition?`, called `mail.disposition_of(m)`: The disposition of `m`, from its `Content-Disposition`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function transfer_encoding_of(m: Message) -> str`, called `mail.transfer_encoding_of(m)`: The transfer encoding of `m`'s body in lower case: `7bit` where it names none.
- `function filename_of(m: Message) -> str?`, called `mail.filename_of(m)`: The name of the file `m` carries: its disposition's `filename`, else its content type's `name`, encoded words in it decoded. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_multipart(m: Message) -> bool`, called `mail.is_multipart(m)`: Whether `m` is a multipart: its content type's is `multipart/`.
- `function is_attachment(m: Message) -> bool`, called `mail.is_attachment(m)`: Whether `m` is an attachment: its disposition is `attachment`.
- `function content_of(m: Message) -> [u8]?`, called `mail.content_of(m)`: The content of `m`: its body with its transfer encoding undone. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function text_of(m: Message) -> str?`, called `mail.text_of(m)`: The content of `m` as text, decoded from the charset its content type names, and from UTF-8, which holds US-ASCII, where it names none. Fails `unsupported`, `not_text`.
- `function walk(m: Message) -> [Message]`, called `mail.walk(m)`: Every part of `m`, `m` first, then each part before its own parts: the order Python's `walk` and a reader's tree give.
- `function attachments_of(m: Message) -> [Message]`, called `mail.attachments_of(m)`: The parts of `m` a reader shows as files, in order: every part whose disposition is `attachment`, and every other part under `m` that is no multipart, is not `inline`, has no `Content-ID` (an HTML body shows it), and is no text or names a file.
- `function body_of(m: Message, preferring: [str]) -> Message?`, called `mail.body_of(m, preferring)`: The part of `m` a reader shows as its text, as Python's `get_body` finds it: the text part whose subtype stands first in `preferring`, looked for in every part of a multipart, but in a `multipart/related` only in its start part, and never in an attachment. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Attachment(filename: str, media_type: str, data: [u8], content_id: str)`: A file attached to a message `compose` builds.
- `function text_part(text: str, subtype: str) -> Message?`, called `mail.text_part(text: text, subtype: subtype)`: A part holding `text`, of type `text/<subtype>`: charset US-ASCII where the text is ASCII and UTF-8 otherwise, and the transfer encoding that keeps it within ASCII and lines of 76 bytes, `7bit`, quoted-printable or base 64, the shorter of the last two. Fails `invalid`.
- `function data_part(data: [u8], media_type: str) -> Message?`, called `mail.data_part(data, media_type)`: A part holding `data`, of type `media_type`, in base 64. Fails `invalid`.
- `function media_type_of(name: str) -> str?`, called `mail.media_type_of(name)`: The media type of a file named `name`, by its extension compared without case, as an attachment gives it: `application/pdf` for `report.PDF`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function attachment_part(data: [u8], media_type: str, filename: str) -> Message?`, called `mail.attachment_part(data, media_type: media_type, filename: filename)`: A part holding a file attached, in base 64, named `filename`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function inline_part(data: [u8], media_type: str, content_id: str) -> Message?`, called `mail.inline_part(data, media_type: media_type, content_id: content_id)`: A part holding a file shown inside an HTML body that names it `cid:<content_id>`, in base 64. Fails `invalid`.
- `function multipart(subtype: str, parts: [Message]) -> Message?`, called `mail.multipart(subtype, parts)`: A multipart of `parts`, of type `multipart/<subtype>`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function message_part(m: Message) -> Message?`, called `mail.message_part(m)`: A part of type `message/rfc822` holding `m`, as a message forwarded whole. Fails as `encode_message` fails.
- `function compose(text: str, html: str, attachments: [Attachment]) -> Message?`, called `mail.compose(text: text, html: html, attachments)`: A message with a text body, an HTML body, or both, and files: the structure every mail reader expects. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Address(name: str, local: str, domain: str)`: A mailbox: an address and the name shown with it.
- `variant Recipient = .one(address: Address) | .group(name: str, members: [Address])`: One entry of an address list: a mailbox, or a group of them under a name.
- `function parse_address(s: str) -> Address?`, called `mail.parse_address(s)`: The mailbox `s` writes: `Ana Lima <ana@example.org>`, `ana@example.org`, `"Lima, Ana" <ana@example.org>`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_address_list(s: str) -> [Address]?`, called `mail.parse_address_list(s)`: The mailboxes of the address list `s`, a group's members in its place. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_recipients(s: str) -> [Recipient]?`, called `mail.parse_recipients(s)`: The entries of the address list `s`, each group kept as one. Fails as `parse_address_list` fails.
- `function format_address(a: Address) -> str`, called `mail.format_address(a)`: `a` as a mailbox in a header: its name quoted where it must be and as encoded words where it is above ASCII, then its address in angle brackets; its address alone where it has no name.
- `function format_address_list(addresses: [Address]) -> str`, called `mail.format_address_list(addresses)`: `addresses` as an address list: each as `format_address` writes it, a comma and a space between them.
- `function format_recipients(recipients: [Recipient]) -> str`, called `mail.format_recipients(recipients)`: `recipients` as an address list, a group as `Name: a, b;`.
- `function format_addr_spec(a: Address) -> str`, called `mail.format_addr_spec(a)`: The address of `a` alone, `local@domain`, its local part quoted where it is no dot-atom: what SMTP's envelope names.
- `function addresses_of(m: Message, name: str) -> [Address]?`, called `mail.addresses_of(m, name)`: The mailboxes of every field of `m` named `name`, in order. Fails as `parse_address_list` fails.
- `function is_ascii_address(a: Address) -> bool`, called `mail.is_ascii_address(a)`: Whether `a`'s address is ASCII, so a server that did not take SMTPUTF8 accepts it; its name does not count, being written as encoded words.
- `record Word(text: str, charset: str, data: [u8], is_decoded: bool)`: One piece of a header's text as `decode_words` reads it: plain text, or the content of encoded words of one charset.
- `variant WordEncoding = .b | .q`: How an encoded word writes its bytes.
- `function decode_header(s: str) -> str?`, called `mail.decode_header(s)`: `s` with its encoded words decoded: `=?utf-8?q?caf=C3=A9?=` is `café`. Fails `unsupported`, `not_text`.
- `function decode_words(s: str) -> [Word]`, called `mail.decode_words(s)`: The pieces of `s`: its plain text, and its encoded words decoded where their charset is read and kept as bytes where it is not, so nothing is lost.
- `function encode_words(text: str, encoding: WordEncoding) -> str`, called `mail.encode_words(text, encoding)`: `text` as encoded words of UTF-8 where it needs them, each at most 75 bytes, a space between two; `text` itself where it is printable ASCII.
- `function parse_content_type(s: str) -> ContentType?`, called `mail.parse_content_type(s)`: The content type `s` writes, as `Content-Type` holds it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_content_type(ct: ContentType) -> str?`, called `mail.format_content_type(ct)`: `ct` written as a `Content-Type` value: its parameters in their order, a value quoted where it must be, and written by RFC 2231 in UTF-8 where it is above ASCII, in continuations where it is long. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_disposition(s: str) -> Disposition?`, called `mail.parse_disposition(s)`: The disposition `s` writes, as `Content-Disposition` holds it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_disposition(d: Disposition) -> str?`, called `mail.format_disposition(d)`: `d` written as a `Content-Disposition` value, its parameters as `format_content_type` writes them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_quoted_printable(data: [u8], binary: bool) -> str`, called `mail.format_quoted_printable(data, binary)`: `data` in quoted-printable (RFC 2045): a byte outside printable ASCII, and `=`, written `=XX`; lines at most 76 bytes, a longer one broken by `=` at its end.
- `function parse_quoted_printable(s: str) -> [u8]`, called `mail.parse_quoted_printable(s)`: The bytes the quoted-printable `s` writes.
- `function format_base64_lines(data: [u8]) -> str`, called `mail.format_base64_lines(data)`: `data` in base 64, in lines of 76 characters each ended by `"\r\n"`, as a part's body holds it.
- `function parse_base64_lines(s: str) -> [u8]?`, called `mail.parse_base64_lines(s)`: The bytes the base 64 `s` writes, across lines. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Date(instant: time.Instant, offset_minutes: i64, offset_known: bool)`: A moment as a message's `Date` writes it: the instant, and the offset from UTC its writer's clock kept.
- `function parse_date(s: str) -> Date?`, called `mail.parse_date(s)`: The date `s` writes: `Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 -0700`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function format_date(d: Date) -> str`, called `mail.format_date(d)`: `d` as a `Date` field writes it: `Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 -0700`, in its own offset, `-0000` where it is unknown.
- `function date_at(t: time.Instant, zone: time.Zone) -> Date`, called `mail.date_at(t, zone)`: `t` as a date in `zone`'s offset at that moment.
- `function date_of(m: Message) -> Date?`, called `mail.date_of(m)`: The date of `m`'s `Date` field. Fails `not_found`.
- `function make_message_id(domain: str) -> str?`, called `mail.make_message_id(domain)`: A new `Message-ID`, `<...@domain>` with angle brackets, unique by 128 random bits from the system. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function parse_message_ids(s: str) -> [str]?`, called `mail.parse_message_ids(s)`: The identifiers of a `Message-ID`, `In-Reply-To` or `References` value, in order and without their angle brackets. Fails `invalid`.


### asn1

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/asn1`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/asn1/).

ASN.1 values read and written in the encodings of ITU-T X.690: DER read and written exactly, BER read.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: Bytes that are not an element of the encoding read, or a value that has no DER form: every reading and writing function, the message saying at which byte or of what.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: A UTF8String whose bytes are not UTF-8, or a string of another type whose characters are not its type's: `decode_der`, `decode_ber`, `decode_with`, `decode_next`, `decode_content`, `to_universal`.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: A number outside the type asked for: an ENUMERATED or an arc of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER past 64 bits, a REAL no `f64` holds exactly, a BER time whose offset moves it outside an `Instant`; and `int_of` and `arcs_of`.
- `variant Value = .boolean(v: bool) | .integer(v: i64) | .big_integer(v: big.Integer) | .enumerated(v: i64) | .real(v: f64) | .bit_string(v: BitString) | .octet_string(v: [u8]) | .null_value | .oid(v: Oid) | .relative_oid(v: Oid) | .text(kind: TextKind, v: str) | .utc_time(v: time.DateTime) | .generalized_time(v: time.DateTime) | .sequence(items: [Value]) | .set(items: [Value]) | .primitive(tag: Tag, content: [u8]) | .constructed(tag: Tag, items: [Value])`: One ASN.1 value.
- `variant TextKind = .utf8 | .numeric | .printable | .teletex | .videotex | .ia5 | .graphic | .visible | .general | .universal | .bmp | .object_descriptor`: The type of a character string, and the characters it holds.
- `record BitString(bytes: [u8], bit_len: i64)`: The bits of a BIT STRING.
- `record Oid(dotted: str)`: An OBJECT IDENTIFIER, held as its dotted text: `1.2.840.113549`.
- `variant Encoding = .der | .ber`: How bytes are read.
- `record Options(encoding: Encoding, max_depth: i64)`: How `decode_with` and `decode_next` read.
- `record Decoded(value: Value, next: i64)`: What `decode_next` answers: the value read and where the next element begins.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `64`: The deepest nesting `decode_der` and `decode_ber` read: 64 constructed elements, where a certificate nests about ten.
- `function decode_der(data: [u8]) -> Value?`, called `asn1.decode_der(data)`: The value DER `data` holds: one element and nothing after it. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`, `does_not_fit`.
