- `function decode_ber(data: [u8]) -> Value?`, called `asn1.decode_ber(data)`: The value BER `data` holds: one element and nothing after it. Fails as `decode_der` does, with BER's rules.
- `function decode_with(data: [u8], options: Options) -> Value?`, called `asn1.decode_with(data, options)`: The value `data` holds, read as `options` says: one element and nothing after it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_next(data: [u8], from: i64, options: Options) -> Decoded?`, called `asn1.decode_next(data, from, options)`: The element that begins at byte `from` of `data`, and where the next begins: the way through elements written one after another. Fails as `decode_with` does, bytes after the element excepted.
- `function decode_content(number: i64, content: [u8], encoding: Encoding) -> Value?`, called `asn1.decode_content(number, content, encoding)`: The value of the universal type numbered `number` whose content octets are `content`: what an IMPLICIT tag hides. Fails as `decode_der` does for the content.
- `record Element(tag: Tag, start: i64, content_start: i64, content_end: i64, end: i64)`: Where one element stands in some bytes, read without its content: the way to the exact bytes of a part, as a signature covers them.
- `function element_at(data: [u8], at: i64, options: Options) -> Element?`, called `asn1.element_at(data, at, options)`: The element that begins at byte `at` of `data`: its tag and where its parts stand, its content unread. Fails `invalid`.
- `function elements_of(data: [u8], element: Element, options: Options) -> [Element]?`, called `asn1.elements_of(data, element, options)`: The elements inside the constructed `element` of `data`, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_der(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `asn1.encode_der(v)`: `v` encoded in DER. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_content(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `asn1.encode_content(v)`: The content octets of `v` in DER: its encoding without its tag and length, what an IMPLICIT tag keeps. Fails as `encode_der` does.
- `function with_tag(v: Value, tag: Tag) -> Value?`, called `asn1.with_tag(v, tag)`: `v` written under `tag` in place of its own: ASN.1's IMPLICIT tagging. Fails as `encode_content` does.
- `function tagged(v: Value, number: i64) -> Value`, called `asn1.tagged(v, number)`: `v` inside the context-specific tag `[number]`: ASN.1's EXPLICIT tagging.
- `function items_of(v: Value) -> [Value]?`, called `asn1.items_of(v)`: The elements of `v`, a SEQUENCE or a SET. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bool_of(v: Value) -> bool?`, called `asn1.bool_of(v)`: The truth value of `v`, a BOOLEAN. Fails `invalid`.
- `function int_of(v: Value) -> i64?`, called `asn1.int_of(v)`: The integer `v` holds, an INTEGER or an ENUMERATED that fits an `i64`. Fails `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function integer_of(v: Value) -> big.Integer?`, called `asn1.integer_of(v)`: The integer `v` holds, an INTEGER of any size. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_integer(n: big.Integer) -> Value`, called `asn1.from_integer(n)`: The INTEGER `n`: an `integer` where it fits an `i64`, a `big_integer` otherwise, as decoding answers it.
- `function bytes_of(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `asn1.bytes_of(v)`: The bytes of `v`, an OCTET STRING. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bits_of(v: Value) -> BitString?`, called `asn1.bits_of(v)`: The bits of `v`, a BIT STRING. Fails `invalid`.
- `function oid_of(v: Value) -> Oid?`, called `asn1.oid_of(v)`: The identifier `v` holds, an OBJECT IDENTIFIER. Fails `invalid`.
- `function text_of(v: Value) -> str?`, called `asn1.text_of(v)`: The characters of `v`, a string of any of the twelve types. Fails `invalid`.
- `function time_of(v: Value) -> time.DateTime?`, called `asn1.time_of(v)`: The moment `v` holds, a UTCTime or a GeneralizedTime, in UTC. Fails `invalid`.
- `function untagged(v: Value, number: i64) -> Value?`, called `asn1.untagged(v, number)`: The value inside `v`, the context-specific tag `[number]` around one value: ASN.1's EXPLICIT tagging read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_universal(v: Value, number: i64, encoding: Encoding) -> Value?`, called `asn1.to_universal(v, number, encoding)`: `v`, read under an IMPLICIT tag, read again as the universal type numbered `number`: a `primitive`'s content decoded, or a `constructed`'s elements made a SEQUENCE or a SET, or under BER a constructed string's segments joined. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Class = .universal | .application | .context_specific | .private`: The class of a tag, X.690 § 8.1.2.2.
- `record Tag(kind: Class, number: i64, constructed: bool)`: The tag of an element: its class, its number, and whether its content is made of elements.
- `constant BOOLEAN: i64`, value `1`: The universal number of BOOLEAN.
- `constant INTEGER: i64`, value `2`: The universal number of INTEGER.
- `constant BIT_STRING: i64`, value `3`: The universal number of BIT STRING.
- `constant OCTET_STRING: i64`, value `4`: The universal number of OCTET STRING.
- `constant NULL: i64`, value `5`: The universal number of NULL.
- `constant OBJECT_IDENTIFIER: i64`, value `6`: The universal number of OBJECT IDENTIFIER.
- `constant OBJECT_DESCRIPTOR: i64`, value `7`: The universal number of ObjectDescriptor.
- `constant EXTERNAL: i64`, value `8`: The universal number of EXTERNAL, kept as a constructed element.
- `constant REAL: i64`, value `9`: The universal number of REAL.
- `constant ENUMERATED: i64`, value `10`: The universal number of ENUMERATED.
- `constant EMBEDDED_PDV: i64`, value `11`: The universal number of EMBEDDED PDV, kept as a constructed element.
- `constant UTF8_STRING: i64`, value `12`: The universal number of UTF8String.
- `constant RELATIVE_OID: i64`, value `13`: The universal number of RELATIVE-OID.
- `constant TIME: i64`, value `14`: The universal number of TIME, kept as its content.
- `constant SEQUENCE: i64`, value `16`: The universal number of SEQUENCE and SEQUENCE OF.
- `constant SET: i64`, value `17`: The universal number of SET and SET OF.
- `constant NUMERIC_STRING: i64`, value `18`: The universal number of NumericString.
- `constant PRINTABLE_STRING: i64`, value `19`: The universal number of PrintableString.
- `constant TELETEX_STRING: i64`, value `20`: The universal number of TeletexString, also called T61String.
- `constant VIDEOTEX_STRING: i64`, value `21`: The universal number of VideotexString.
- `constant IA5_STRING: i64`, value `22`: The universal number of IA5String.
- `constant UTC_TIME: i64`, value `23`: The universal number of UTCTime.
- `constant GENERALIZED_TIME: i64`, value `24`: The universal number of GeneralizedTime.
- `constant GRAPHIC_STRING: i64`, value `25`: The universal number of GraphicString.
- `constant VISIBLE_STRING: i64`, value `26`: The universal number of VisibleString.
- `constant GENERAL_STRING: i64`, value `27`: The universal number of GeneralString.
- `constant UNIVERSAL_STRING: i64`, value `28`: The universal number of UniversalString.
- `constant CHARACTER_STRING: i64`, value `29`: The universal number of CHARACTER STRING, kept as a constructed element.
- `constant BMP_STRING: i64`, value `30`: The universal number of BMPString.
- `constant DATE: i64`, value `31`: The universal number of DATE, kept as its content.
- `constant TIME_OF_DAY: i64`, value `32`: The universal number of TIME-OF-DAY, kept as its content.
- `constant DATE_TIME: i64`, value `33`: The universal number of DATE-TIME, kept as its content.
- `constant DURATION: i64`, value `34`: The universal number of DURATION, kept as its content.
- `constant OID_IRI: i64`, value `35`: The universal number of OID-IRI, kept as its content.
- `constant RELATIVE_OID_IRI: i64`, value `36`: The universal number of RELATIVE-OID-IRI, kept as its content.
- `function format_tag(tag: Tag) -> str`, called `asn1.format_tag(tag)`: `tag` as ASN.1's notation writes it: a universal type by its name, `INTEGER`, `SEQUENCE`; another as `[0]`, `[APPLICATION 1]`, `[PRIVATE 2]`; a universal number with no type as `[UNIVERSAL 99]`.
- `function tag_of(v: Value) -> Tag`, called `asn1.tag_of(v)`: The tag `v` is written with by `encode_der`.
- `function parse_oid(s: str) -> Oid?`, called `asn1.parse_oid(s)`: The identifier `s` writes: arcs in decimal with dots between, `2.5.4.3`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_arcs(arcs: [u64]) -> Oid?`, called `asn1.from_arcs(arcs)`: The identifier of the arcs `arcs`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function arcs_of(oid: Oid) -> [u64]?`, called `asn1.arcs_of(oid)`: The arcs of `oid`, in order. Fails `does_not_fit`, `invalid`.
- `function bit_at(b: BitString, index: i64) -> bool`, called `asn1.bit_at(b, index)`: Whether the bit at `index` of `b` is set, the first bit 0.


### i18n/dates

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/i18n/dates`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/i18n/dates/).

Dates and times written as a language writes them: "Tuesday, March 5, 2024" and "5 mars 2024", the names of its months and days, its patterns for full, long, medium and short dates, times relative to now, "3 days ago", "in 2 hours", "yesterday", in a unit the program names or one chosen for the span, and durations in words, "3 hours, 5 minutes", from the data of CLDR release `i18n.CLDR_VERSION` for every locale it holds, over the instants and zones of `time`.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code a function fails with where a pattern, a skeleton or a text to read is not what it reads.
- `variant DateStyle = .full | .long | .medium | .short`: How much of a date or a time is written, CLDR's four lengths.
- `variant Width = .wide | .abbreviated | .narrow | .short`: How long a name is written.
- `variant NameContext = .format | .standalone`: Where a name stands, which changes it in some languages: in Russian a month inside a date is "марта" and alone "март".
- `variant RelativeUnit = .year | .quarter | .month | .week | .day | .hour | .minute | .second`: A unit of a relative time.
- `variant RelativeStyle = .long | .short | .narrow`: How long a relative time is written: "in 3 days", "in 3 days" or "in 3d" in English.
- `variant DurationUnit = .year | .month | .week | .day | .hour | .minute | .second | .millisecond | .microsecond | .nanosecond`: A unit a duration is written in.
- `variant DurationStyle = .long | .short | .narrow`: How long a duration's words are: "3 hours, 5 minutes", "3 hr, 5 min" or "3h 5m" in English.
- `record DurationPart(unit: DurationUnit, count: i64)`: One unit of a duration written in words, and how many of it.
- `function format_date(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, zone: time.Zone, style: DateStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_date(locale, t, zone, style)`: `t` in `zone` written as a date in `locale`'s language: "Tuesday, March 5, 2024" in full English, "05.03.24" short in German.
- `function format_time(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, zone: time.Zone, style: DateStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_time(locale, t, zone, style)`: `t` in `zone` written as a time of day in `locale`'s language: "3:04 PM" short in English, "15:04" in German.
- `function format_date_time(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, zone: time.Zone, date_style: DateStyle, time_style: DateStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_date_time(locale, t, zone, date_style: date_style, time_style: time_style)`: `t` in `zone` written as a date and a time in `locale`'s language, joined as the language joins them: "March 5, 2024 at 3:04 PM".
- `function format_pattern(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, zone: time.Zone, pattern: str) -> str?`, called `dates.format_pattern(locale, t, zone, pattern)`: `t` in `zone` written by a CLDR date pattern in `locale`'s language, as ICU's `SimpleDateFormat` reads one: `EEEE, d MMMM y`, `HH:mm`, `h:mm a`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_skeleton(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, zone: time.Zone, skeleton: str) -> str?`, called `dates.format_skeleton(locale, t, zone, skeleton)`: `t` in `zone` written with the fields `skeleton` asks for, in the order and the form `locale`'s language writes them: `yMMMd` is "Mar 5, 2024" in English and "5. Fails `invalid`.
- `function skeleton_pattern(locale: i18n.Locale, skeleton: str) -> str?`, called `dates.skeleton_pattern(locale, skeleton)`: The pattern `locale`'s language writes a skeleton's fields with, the closest of CLDR's available formats with each field widened to the skeleton's: `yMMMd` is `MMM d, y` in English. Fails `invalid`.
- `function date_pattern(locale: i18n.Locale, style: DateStyle) -> str`, called `dates.date_pattern(locale, style)`: The pattern `locale`'s language writes a date with: `EEEE, MMMM d, y` full in English.
- `function time_pattern(locale: i18n.Locale, style: DateStyle) -> str`, called `dates.time_pattern(locale, style)`: The pattern `locale`'s language writes a time with: `h:mm a` short in English, `HH:mm` in German.
- `function date_time_pattern(locale: i18n.Locale, date_style: DateStyle, time_style: DateStyle) -> str`, called `dates.date_time_pattern(locale, date_style: date_style, time_style: time_style)`: The pattern `locale`'s language writes a date and a time with, the two joined.
- `function parse_pattern(locale: i18n.Locale, text: str, zone: time.Zone, pattern: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `dates.parse_pattern(locale, text: text, zone, pattern: pattern)`: A date or time written in `locale`'s language by `pattern`, read back as an instant: the reverse of `format_pattern`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function month_names(locale: i18n.Locale, width: Width, context: NameContext) -> [str]`, called `dates.month_names(locale, width, context)`: The names of the months in `locale`'s language, January first.
- `function weekday_names(locale: i18n.Locale, width: Width, context: NameContext) -> [str]`, called `dates.weekday_names(locale, width, context)`: The names of the days of the week in `locale`'s language, Monday first as `time.Weekday` counts them.
- `function quarter_names(locale: i18n.Locale, width: Width, context: NameContext) -> [str]`, called `dates.quarter_names(locale, width, context)`: The names of the quarters of the year in `locale`'s language, the first quarter first.
- `function day_period_names(locale: i18n.Locale, width: Width) -> [str]`, called `dates.day_period_names(locale, width)`: The names of the morning and the afternoon in `locale`'s language, "AM" and "PM" in English.
- `function era_names(locale: i18n.Locale, width: Width) -> [str]`, called `dates.era_names(locale, width)`: The names of the two eras of the Gregorian calendar in `locale`'s language, the one before the year 1 first: "BC" and "AD" in English.
- `function first_weekday(locale: i18n.Locale) -> time.Weekday`, called `dates.first_weekday(locale)`: The day a week begins on in `locale`'s region: Sunday in the United States, Monday in Germany, Saturday in Egypt.
- `function minimal_days(locale: i18n.Locale) -> i64`, called `dates.minimal_days(locale)`: The fewest days of a new year that the first week of the year must hold in `locale`'s region: 1 in the United States, 4 in Germany as ISO 8601 says.
- `function uses_12_hour_clock(locale: i18n.Locale) -> bool`, called `dates.uses_12_hour_clock(locale)`: Whether `locale`'s region writes the time with a 12-hour clock, as the United States does, rather than a 24-hour one.
- `function format_relative(locale: i18n.Locale, amount: i64, unit: RelativeUnit, style: RelativeStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_relative(locale, amount, unit, style)`: `amount` units of time from now written in `locale`'s language, always with its number: "in 3 days", "3 days ago", "in 0 days".
- `function format_relative_named(locale: i18n.Locale, amount: i64, unit: RelativeUnit, style: RelativeStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_relative_named(locale, amount, unit, style)`: `amount` units of time from now written as `locale`'s language names it where it has a word, "yesterday", "tomorrow", "next year", "now", and with a number where it has none, "in 3 days".
- `function format_relative_duration(locale: i18n.Locale, d: time.Duration, style: RelativeStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_relative_duration(locale, d, style)`: `d` from now written in `locale`'s language in the one unit chosen for it, always with its number: "in 5 minutes", "3 hours ago", "in 0 seconds".
- `function format_relative_duration_named(locale: i18n.Locale, d: time.Duration, style: RelativeStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_relative_duration_named(locale, d, style)`: `d` from now written in `locale`'s language in the one unit chosen for it, as the language names it where it has a word: "yesterday", "last week", "now", and "in 5 minutes" where it has none.
- `function format_relative_instant(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, now: time.Instant, style: RelativeStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_relative_instant(locale, t: t, now: now, style)`: `t` written in `locale`'s language relative to `now`, in the one unit chosen for the span between them, always with its number: "5 minutes ago", "in 2 hours".
- `function format_relative_instant_named(locale: i18n.Locale, t: time.Instant, now: time.Instant, style: RelativeStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_relative_instant_named(locale, t: t, now: now, style)`: `t` written in `locale`'s language relative to `now`, in the one unit chosen for the span between them, as the language names it where it has a word: "yesterday", "tomorrow", "now".
- `function format_duration(locale: i18n.Locale, parts: [DurationPart], style: DurationStyle) -> str`, called `dates.format_duration(locale, parts, style)`: `parts` written in `locale`'s language as one duration, each part in its unit's words and the parts joined as the language joins a list of units: "3 hours, 5 minutes" in English, "3 Stunden, 5 Minuten" in German, "3 heures et 5 minutes" in French, from CLDR's unit and list patterns.
- `function duration_parts(d: time.Duration, largest: time.Unit, smallest: time.Unit) -> [DurationPart]`, called `dates.duration_parts(d, largest: largest, smallest: smallest)`: `d` broken into whole units from `largest` down to `smallest`, each unit that holds none left out: 3 hours and 5 minutes is a part of 3 hours and a part of 5 minutes.


### dns

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/dns`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/dns/).

A DNS client: messages of RFC 1035 read from their bytes and written to them exactly, every common kind of record as a value, and questions asked of name servers over UDP, and over TCP where an answer comes truncated, with a deadline on every try.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `failure.NOT_FOUND`: A name that names nothing, a name with no record of the type asked, or a parameter or a type absent from what was searched.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `failure.INVALID`: The input is not what the function reads: a name too long or holding an empty label, a message cut short or whose counts its bytes do not hold, a compression pointer that does not point back, a field outside its range; the message says where.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `failure.NOT_TEXT`: A text read from a message that is not UTF-8, where a function answers it as `str`.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `failure.FAILED`: A server answered that it failed (`SERVFAIL`), refused (`REFUSED`) or could not do what was asked (`NOTIMP`, `FORMERR`), or answered with another code a lookup cannot read as an answer; the message names the code.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `failure.UNSUPPORTED`: This system holds its name servers where this package cannot read them: Windows, where no file names them.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `failure.TIMEOUT`: No server answered in the time allowed, on any try.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `failure.CLOSED`: The connection was closed or refused by the server.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `failure.STOPPED`: The program was asked to stop while a call waited (`os.catch_stop`).
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `failure.LIMIT`: The system has no socket, descriptor or memory left.
- `record Resolver(servers: [net.Address], search: [str], ndots: i64, timeout: time.Duration, attempts: i64, rotate: bool, tcp: bool, udp_size: i64, dnssec_ok: bool, recursion: bool)`: How questions are asked: of which servers, under which search list, within which time.
- `function system() -> Resolver?`, called `dns.system()`: The resolver the system is configured with: on POSIX systems what `/etc/resolv.conf` says, as `parse_resolv_conf` reads it, and the loopback servers `127.0.0.1` and `::1` where the file is not there, as Go and glibc take them. Fails `unsupported`, `not_text`, `failed`.
- `function parse_resolv_conf(text: str) -> Resolver`, called `dns.parse_resolv_conf(text)`: The resolver `text`, the content of a `resolv.conf`, describes: its `nameserver` lines, at most three, as glibc reads them; its `search` or `domain` line, the last one counting; and its `options` `ndots:`, `timeout:` (seconds), `attempts:`, `rotate`, `use-vc` and `edns0`.
- `function resolver(servers: [str]) -> Resolver?`, called `dns.resolver(servers)`: A resolver asking `servers` with the defaults `parse_resolv_conf` takes: no search list, `ndots:1`, five seconds a try, two attempts, recursion desired, EDNS(0) at `DEFAULT_UDP_SIZE`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function exchange(r: Resolver, m: Message) -> Message?`, called `dns.exchange(r, m)`: The answer to `m` from the servers of `r`: sent over UDP, and again over TCP where the answer comes truncated, or over TCP alone where `r.tcp` says so, each server tried in turn `r.attempts` times, each try within `r.timeout`. Fails `timeout`, `closed`, `invalid`, `stopped`, `limit`.
- `function exchange_stream(s: io.Stream, m: Message) -> Message?`, called `dns.exchange_stream(s, m)`: The answer to `m` over `s`, a stream the program opened to a server and closes: DNS over TLS, `tls.connect` to port 853 (RFC 7858), or any stream that frames messages as TCP does, each after its length in two bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function query(r: Resolver, name: str, type_code: i64) -> Message?`, called `dns.query(r, name, type_code)`: The answer of `r`'s servers to the question `name` and `type_code` in class IN, whatever its code: `name` is asked as it is, absolute, with no search list, as `r` says to ask it. Fails as `new_query` and `exchange` fail.
- `record Answer(name: str, canonical: str, records: [Record], message: Message)`: What a lookup found: the name that answered, the end of its aliases, and the records.
- `function lookup(r: Resolver, name: str, type_code: i64) -> Answer?`, called `dns.lookup(r, name, type_code)`: The records of type `type_code` that `name` has, asked of `r`'s servers through its search list, the aliases of the answer followed. Fails `not_found`, `failed`.
- `function lookup_addresses(r: Resolver, name: str) -> [net.Host]?`, called `dns.lookup_addresses(r, name)`: The IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of `name`, asked of `r`'s servers: its A records then its AAAA records, none twice. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Mx(host: str, preference: i64)`: A mail exchanger, as `lookup_mx` answers it.
- `function lookup_mx(r: Resolver, name: str) -> [Mx]?`, called `dns.lookup_mx(r, name)`: The mail exchangers of `name`, by preference from the lowest, in the server's order within one. Fails as `lookup` fails.
- `function lookup_txt(r: Resolver, name: str) -> [str]?`, called `dns.lookup_txt(r, name)`: The texts of `name`, one for each TXT record, its character strings joined with nothing between them, as Go's `LookupTXT` joins them. Fails `not_text`.
- `record Srv(target: str, port: i64, priority: i64, weight: i64)`: A server of a service, as `lookup_srv` answers it.
- `function lookup_srv(r: Resolver, service: str, protocol: str, name: str) -> [Srv]?`, called `dns.lookup_srv(r, service: service, protocol: protocol, name: name)`: The servers of the service `service` over `protocol` for `name`, asked as `_service._protocol.name`, by priority from the lowest and within one by weight from the largest. Fails as `lookup` fails.
- `function lookup_ns(r: Resolver, name: str) -> [str]?`, called `dns.lookup_ns(r, name)`: The names of the name servers of the zone `name`, in the server's order. Fails as `lookup` fails.
- `function lookup_cname(r: Resolver, name: str) -> str?`, called `dns.lookup_cname(r, name)`: The canonical name of `name`, every alias followed: `name` itself, made absolute, where it is no alias but has addresses. Fails `not_found`.
- `function lookup_reverse(r: Resolver, a: net.Host) -> [str]?`, called `dns.lookup_reverse(r, a)`: The names the address `a` has by its PTR records, asked under `in-addr.arpa.` or `ip6.arpa.`, in the server's order. Fails as `lookup` fails.
- `function transfer(r: Resolver, zone: str) -> [Record]?`, called `dns.transfer(r, zone)`: The records of the zone `zone`, asked of the first of `r`'s servers over TCP (AXFR, RFC 5936), in the order the server sends them: the zone's SOA first and last. Fails `failed`, `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `record Message(id: i64, response: bool, opcode: i64, authoritative: bool, truncated: bool, recursion_desired: bool, recursion_available: bool, authenticated_data: bool, checking_disabled: bool, rcode: i64, questions: [Question], answers: [Record], authorities: [Record], additionals: [Record], edns: Edns?)`: A DNS message, a query or a response, as RFC 1035 § 4 lays it out.
- `record Question(name: str, type_code: i64, class_code: i64)`: A question: a name, a type, a class.
- `record Edns(udp_size: i64, version: i64, dnssec_ok: bool, options: [EdnsOption])`: What EDNS(0)'s OPT record carries (RFC 6891).
- `record EdnsOption(code: i64, data: [u8])`: One option of an OPT record.
- `record Record(name: str, class_code: i64, ttl: i64, data: Data)`: A resource record: an owner name, a class, a time to live and the data, whose case says the record's type (`type_of`).
- `variant Data = .a(address: net.Host) | .aaaa(address: net.Host) | .ns(host: str) | .cname(target: str) | .dname(target: str) | .ptr(target: str) | .mx(preference: i64, exchange: str) | .txt(texts: [[u8]]) | .srv(priority: i64, weight: i64, port: i64, target: str) | .soa(primary: str, mailbox: str, serial: i64, refresh: i64, retry: i64, expire: i64, minimum: i64) | .hinfo(cpu: [u8], system: [u8]) | .caa(flags: i64, tag: str, value: [u8]) | .naptr(order: i64, preference: i64, flags: [u8], services: [u8], regexp: [u8], replacement: str) | .svcb(priority: i64, target: str, params: [SvcParam]) | .https(priority: i64, target: str, params: [SvcParam]) | .ds(key_tag: i64, algorithm: i64, digest_type: i64, digest: [u8]) | .dnskey(flags: i64, protocol: i64, algorithm: i64, key: [u8]) | .rrsig(type_covered: i64, algorithm: i64, labels: i64, original_ttl: i64, expiration: i64, inception: i64, key_tag: i64, signer: str, signature: [u8]) | .nsec(next: str, types: [i64]) | .tlsa(usage: i64, selector: i64, matching_type: i64, association: [u8]) | .sshfp(algorithm: i64, fingerprint_type: i64, fingerprint: [u8]) | .unknown(type_code: i64, data: [u8])`: What a record says, one case per type.
- `record SvcParam(key: i64, value: [u8])`: One parameter of a service binding.
- `function new_query(name: str, type_code: i64) -> Message?`, called `dns.new_query(name, type_code)`: A query for `name` and `type_code` in class IN, recursion desired and EDNS(0) offering `DEFAULT_UDP_SIZE`, its ID 0 as RFC 8484 asks of DNS over HTTPS. Fails `invalid`.
- `function reply_to(asked: Message) -> Message`, called `dns.reply_to(asked)`: A response begun for `asked`: its ID, operation, questions and wish for recursion copied, its sections empty, its code `RCODE_NO_ERROR`, and EDNS where the query had it, at `DEFAULT_UDP_SIZE`.
- `function decode(data: [u8]) -> Message?`, called `dns.decode(data)`: The message `data` holds, its names decompressed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode(m: Message) -> [u8]?`, called `dns.encode(m)`: The bytes of `m`, its names compressed where RFC 3597 § 4 allows it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function canonical_name(name: str) -> str?`, called `dns.canonical_name(name)`: `name` in the form two names are compared by: absolute, its ASCII letters in lower case, its escapes as dig writes them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function labels_of(name: str) -> [str]?`, called `dns.labels_of(name)`: The labels of `name`, each written as a name writes it, from the first: none for the root. Fails as `canonical_name` fails.
- `function is_subdomain(name: str, of: str) -> bool`, called `dns.is_subdomain(name: name, of: of)`: Whether `name` is `of` or a name under it, their letters compared without case.
- `function parse_reverse_name(name: str) -> net.Host?`, called `dns.parse_reverse_name(name)`: The address the reverse name `name` names, as `net.to_reverse_name` writes one: `4.3.2.1.in-addr.arpa.` or 32 hexadecimal digits under `ip6.arpa.`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_record(r: Record) -> str?`, called `dns.format_record(r)`: `r` as a zone file writes it and dig prints it, its fields parted by one space: `example.com. 300 IN MX 10 mail.example.com.`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_data(d: Data) -> str?`, called `dns.format_data(d)`: The data `d` as a zone file writes it: a character string in quotes with `"` and `\` escaped and every byte outside printable ASCII as `\DDD`, keys and signatures in base 64, digests in upper-case hexadecimal, an RRSIG's times as `YYYYMMDDHHmmSS` in UTC, and an `unknown` as `\# <length> <hex>` (RFC 3597 § 5). Fails `invalid`.
- `function param_of(params: [SvcParam], key: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `dns.param_of(params, key)`: The value of the parameter `key` among `params`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function alpn_of(value: [u8]) -> [str]?`, called `dns.alpn_of(value)`: The protocol identifiers an `alpn` value lists, `h2` and `h3`, in order. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function port_of(value: [u8]) -> i64?`, called `dns.port_of(value)`: The port a `port` value holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function hints_of(value: [u8], v6: bool) -> [net.Host]?`, called `dns.hints_of(value, v6)`: The addresses an `ipv4hint` or an `ipv6hint` value lists, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function alpn_param(ids: [str]) -> SvcParam?`, called `dns.alpn_param(ids)`: The `alpn` parameter listing `ids`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function port_param(port: i64) -> SvcParam?`, called `dns.port_param(port)`: The `port` parameter for `port`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function hints_param(addresses: [net.Host]) -> SvcParam?`, called `dns.hints_param(addresses)`: The `ipv4hint` or `ipv6hint` parameter listing `addresses`, of one kind. Fails `invalid`.
- `function key_tag_of(d: Data) -> i64?`, called `dns.key_tag_of(d)`: The key tag of a DNSKEY's data, the number a DS and an RRSIG name it by (RFC 4034 appendix B). Fails `invalid`.
- `function type_of(r: Record) -> i64`, called `dns.type_of(r)`: The type of a record, which its data's case says: `TYPE_MX` for an `mx`, the type kept for an `unknown`.
- `function type_name(type_code: i64) -> str`, called `dns.type_name(type_code)`: The mnemonic of the record type `type_code`, `MX`, or `TYPE` and its number where it has none here, `TYPE65280` (RFC 3597 § 5).
- `function parse_type(s: str) -> i64?`, called `dns.parse_type(s)`: The record type `s` names: a mnemonic `type_name` writes, in either case, or `TYPE` and a number 0 to 65535. Fails `invalid`.
- `function class_name(class_code: i64) -> str`, called `dns.class_name(class_code)`: The mnemonic of the class `class_code`, `IN`, `CH`, `HS`, `NONE`, `ANY`, or `CLASS` and its number (RFC 3597 § 5).
- `function parse_class(s: str) -> i64?`, called `dns.parse_class(s)`: The class `s` names: a mnemonic `class_name` writes, in either case, or `CLASS` and a number 0 to 65535. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rcode_name(rcode: i64) -> str`, called `dns.rcode_name(rcode)`: The mnemonic of the response code `rcode`, `NXDOMAIN`, or `RESERVED` and its number where it has none, as dig writes it.
- `constant PORT: i64`, value `53`: The port a name server listens on, UDP and TCP.
- `constant DEFAULT_UDP_SIZE: i64`, value `1232`: The size of a datagram a query offers to read, 1,232 bytes, the size of DNS Flag Day 2020, which fits a path of IPv6 without fragments.
- `constant TYPE_A: i64`, value `1`: The type of an IPv4 address (A).
- `constant TYPE_NS: i64`, value `2`: The type of a name server of a zone (NS).
- `constant TYPE_CNAME: i64`, value `5`: The type of an alias, the canonical name it stands for (CNAME).
- `constant TYPE_SOA: i64`, value `6`: The type of a zone's start of authority (SOA).
- `constant TYPE_PTR: i64`, value `12`: The type of a name an address or another name points to (PTR).
- `constant TYPE_HINFO: i64`, value `13`: The type of a host's processor and system (HINFO, RFC 8482).
- `constant TYPE_MX: i64`, value `15`: The type of a mail exchanger (MX).
- `constant TYPE_TXT: i64`, value `16`: The type of texts (TXT).
- `constant TYPE_AAAA: i64`, value `28`: The type of an IPv6 address (AAAA).
- `constant TYPE_SRV: i64`, value `33`: The type of a service's server (SRV, RFC 2782).
- `constant TYPE_NAPTR: i64`, value `35`: The type of a naming authority pointer (NAPTR, RFC 3403).
- `constant TYPE_DNAME: i64`, value `39`: The type of an alias for a whole subtree (DNAME, RFC 6672).
- `constant TYPE_OPT: i64`, value `41`: The type of EDNS(0)'s pseudo-record (OPT, RFC 6891), which `decode` reads into a message's `edns` and never into a `Record`.
- `constant TYPE_DS: i64`, value `43`: The type of a delegation signer (DS, RFC 4034).
- `constant TYPE_SSHFP: i64`, value `44`: The type of an SSH key's fingerprint (SSHFP, RFC 4255).
- `constant TYPE_RRSIG: i64`, value `46`: The type of a signature over a set of records (RRSIG, RFC 4034).
- `constant TYPE_NSEC: i64`, value `47`: The type of the next name of a signed zone (NSEC, RFC 4034).
- `constant TYPE_DNSKEY: i64`, value `48`: The type of a zone's public key (DNSKEY, RFC 4034).
- `constant TYPE_TLSA: i64`, value `52`: The type of a TLS certificate's association (TLSA, RFC 6698).
- `constant TYPE_SVCB: i64`, value `64`: The type of a service binding (SVCB, RFC 9460).
- `constant TYPE_HTTPS: i64`, value `65`: The type of a service binding for HTTPS (HTTPS, RFC 9460).
- `constant TYPE_AXFR: i64`, value `252`: The type of a question asking for a whole zone (AXFR).
- `constant TYPE_ANY: i64`, value `255`: The type of a question asking for every record of a name (ANY, `*`), which many servers answer with one record alone (RFC 8482).
- `constant TYPE_CAA: i64`, value `257`: The type of the authorities allowed to issue a certificate (CAA, RFC 8659).
- `constant CLASS_IN: i64`, value `1`: The class of the Internet (IN), every class but a handful of tools use.
- `constant CLASS_CH: i64`, value `3`: The class of Chaos (CH), where servers answer questions about themselves: `version.bind.` and `id.server.`.
- `constant CLASS_HS: i64`, value `4`: The class of Hesiod (HS).
- `constant CLASS_NONE: i64`, value `254`: The class of none, in a dynamic update (RFC 2136).
- `constant CLASS_ANY: i64`, value `255`: The class of any, in a question (`*`).
- `constant RCODE_NO_ERROR: i64`, value `0`: The answer is what was asked (NOERROR).
- `constant RCODE_FORMAT_ERROR: i64`, value `1`: The server could not read the query (FORMERR).
- `constant RCODE_SERVER_FAILURE: i64`, value `2`: The server failed to answer (SERVFAIL).
- `constant RCODE_NAME_ERROR: i64`, value `3`: The name asked names nothing (NXDOMAIN).
- `constant RCODE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: i64`, value `4`: The server does not do what was asked (NOTIMP).
- `constant RCODE_REFUSED: i64`, value `5`: The server refuses to answer (REFUSED).
- `constant RCODE_NAME_EXISTS: i64`, value `6`: A name that should not exist does, in an update (YXDOMAIN).
- `constant RCODE_RRSET_EXISTS: i64`, value `7`: A set of records that should not exist does, in an update (YXRRSET).
- `constant RCODE_RRSET_MISSING: i64`, value `8`: A set of records that should exist does not, in an update (NXRRSET).
- `constant RCODE_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE: i64`, value `9`: The server is not authoritative for the zone (NOTAUTH).
- `constant RCODE_NOT_IN_ZONE: i64`, value `10`: A name of an update is outside its zone (NOTZONE).
- `constant RCODE_BAD_VERSION: i64`, value `16`: The server does not speak the EDNS version asked (BADVERS, RFC 6891).
- `constant RCODE_BAD_COOKIE: i64`, value `23`: The server refused the client's cookie (BADCOOKIE, RFC 7873).
- `constant OPCODE_QUERY: i64`, value `0`: A query, the operation of every question here (QUERY).
- `constant OPCODE_STATUS: i64`, value `2`: A question about the server's state (STATUS).
- `constant OPCODE_NOTIFY: i64`, value `4`: A zone's change told to its secondaries (NOTIFY, RFC 1996).
- `constant OPCODE_UPDATE: i64`, value `5`: A dynamic update (UPDATE, RFC 2136).
- `constant SVC_MANDATORY: i64`, value `0`: The keys a client must understand to use the binding (`mandatory`).
- `constant SVC_ALPN: i64`, value `1`: The application protocols offered, `h2`, `h3` (`alpn`).
- `constant SVC_NO_DEFAULT_ALPN: i64`, value `2`: That the default protocol is not offered (`no-default-alpn`).
- `constant SVC_PORT: i64`, value `3`: The port to connect to (`port`).
- `constant SVC_IPV4_HINT: i64`, value `4`: IPv4 addresses the target may be reached at (`ipv4hint`).
- `constant SVC_ECH: i64`, value `5`: An encrypted ClientHello's configuration (`ech`).
- `constant SVC_IPV6_HINT: i64`, value `6`: IPv6 addresses the target may be reached at (`ipv6hint`).
- `constant SVC_DOH_PATH: i64`, value `7`: The path of a DNS over HTTPS template (`dohpath`, RFC 9461).
- `constant EDNS_NSID: i64`, value `3`: The server's identifier, asked by an empty option (NSID, RFC 5001).
- `constant EDNS_CLIENT_SUBNET: i64`, value `8`: The client's subnet (ECS, RFC 7871).
- `constant EDNS_COOKIE: i64`, value `10`: A cookie (RFC 7873).
- `constant EDNS_PADDING: i64`, value `12`: Padding, zeros that hide a message's length (RFC 7830).
- `constant EDNS_EXTENDED_ERROR: i64`, value `15`: An extended error: a code and a text saying why (EDE, RFC 8914).


### bench

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/bench`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/bench/).

A function measured: called in rounds after a warm-up, each round repeating the call until it lasts long enough for the monotonic clock to read it well, and the time a call took told by the rounds kept: their median, their best, their spread, their quartiles and the rounds far from the others.

- `constant FAILED: str`, value `clock.FAILED`: The code `measure` and `compare_versions` fail with where the monotonic clock or the process's processor time cannot be read.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `clock.TIMEOUT`: The code `measure` and `compare_versions` fail with where the time allowed ran out before a round, or a pair, could be kept: every one waited.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `figures.INVALID`: The code `summarize` and `compare_pairs` fail with where the times are empty, of two lengths, negative or not numbers.
- `record Settings(warmups: i64, rounds: i64, most: time.Duration, round: time.Duration, waiting: f64, floor: f64)`: How a measurement is made.
- `function default_settings() -> Settings`, called `bench.default_settings()`: The settings of a measurement no program changed: one warm-up, 20 rounds of at least 100 milliseconds within 10 seconds, a round discarded as waiting past a tenth, and a floor of effect of 0.5 %, the project's own.
- `function with_warmups(settings: Settings, warmups: i64) -> Settings`, called `bench.with_warmups(settings, warmups)`: A copy of `settings` running `warmups` warm-up rounds.
- `function with_rounds(settings: Settings, rounds: i64) -> Settings`, called `bench.with_rounds(settings, rounds)`: A copy of `settings` keeping `rounds` rounds at most.
- `function with_time(settings: Settings, most: time.Duration) -> Settings`, called `bench.with_time(settings, most)`: A copy of `settings` measuring for `most` at most: with many `rounds`, a measurement for a time.
- `function with_round(settings: Settings, round: time.Duration) -> Settings`, called `bench.with_round(settings, round)`: A copy of `settings` whose rounds last at least `round`.
- `function with_waiting(settings: Settings, share: f64) -> Settings`, called `bench.with_waiting(settings, share)`: A copy of `settings` discarding a round as waiting past `share`.
- `function with_floor(settings: Settings, share: f64) -> Settings`, called `bench.with_floor(settings, share)`: A copy of `settings` whose floor of effect is `share`.
- `record Round(calls: i64, wall_ns: i64, processor_ns: i64, kept: bool, reason: str)`: One round of a measurement.
- `record Outliers(low_severe: i64, low_mild: i64, high_mild: i64, high_severe: i64)`: How many times stand far from the others, by Tukey's fences: a fence stands 1.5 interquartile ranges beyond a quartile, and a far fence 3.
- `record Summary(count: i64, best: f64, worst: f64, median: f64, mean: f64, spread: f64, deviation: f64, median_deviation: f64, lower_quartile: f64, upper_quartile: f64, outliers: Outliers)`: The figures of a list of times, each in nanoseconds a call.
- `record Report(calls: i64, rounds: [Round], summary: Summary, text: str)`: What `measure` found: every round, the figures of the kept rounds' times a call, and a line a reader reads.
- `variant Change = .slower | .faster | .same | .unknown`: Which way a comparison found the second version to have moved.
- `record Comparison(change: Change, pairs: i64, slower: i64, faster: i64, median_change: f64, share: f64, tail: f64, floor: f64, before: Summary, after: Summary, text: str)`: What `compare_versions` and `compare_pairs` found.
- `function measure<T, R>(work: (function(T) -> R), input: T, settings: Settings) -> Report?`, called `bench.measure(work, input, settings)`: How long `work` takes on `input`, a call: its calls in a round settled so a round lasts `settings.round`, the warm-ups run and discarded, then rounds until `settings.rounds` are kept or `settings.most` has passed, each round that waited discarded. Fails `failed`, `timeout`.
- `function compare_versions<T, R>(before: (function(T) -> R), after: (function(T) -> R), input: T, settings: Settings) -> Comparison?`, called `bench.compare_versions(before: before, after: after, input, settings)`: Whether `after` is slower or faster than `before` on `input`: rounds of the two run in pairs, alternately and in turns of order, the first pair discarded and every pair in which a round waited dropped, and the pairs read by `compare_pairs` against `settings.floor`. Fails `failed`, `timeout`.
- `function summarize(times: [f64]) -> Summary?`, called `bench.summarize(times)`: The figures of `times`, each the time of a call in nanoseconds: for a program that times its own work, a setup left out, as Go's `StopTimer` and criterion's `iter_custom` let one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compare_pairs(before: [f64], after: [f64], floor: f64) -> Comparison?`, called `bench.compare_pairs(before: before, after: after, floor)`: Whether the second version is slower or faster, read from pairs of times the program made itself, alternately in one sitting: `before[i]` and `after[i]` are a pair. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_nanoseconds(ns: f64) -> str`, called `bench.format_nanoseconds(ns)`: `ns` nanoseconds written for a reader, three figures in the unit that keeps them above 1: `ns`, `µs`, `ms` or `s`.
- `function throughput(summary: Summary, per_call: f64) -> f64`, called `bench.throughput(summary, per_call)`: How many units a second the work handles at the median of `summary`: bytes a second where a call handles `per_call` bytes, elements where elements.


### chunks

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/chunks`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/chunks/).

A text cut into pieces for retrieval: each piece small enough for a model or an index to take, cut where the text's own structure allows, paragraphs first, then sentences, words and last characters, with an overlap between neighbours so that a sentence cut in two is still read whole somewhere.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a size or an overlap that no piece can have, and of an empty separator among others.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a Markdown heading this package cannot place in the text.
- `record Chunk(text: str, start: i64, end: i64, path: [str])`: A piece of a text: a slice of it and where it stands.
- `variant Measure = .characters | .bytes | .tokens(encoding: tokenizer.Encoding)`: What a piece's size counts.
- `record Options(size: i64, overlap: i64, measure: Measure, trims: bool)`: How a text is cut: the largest size of a piece, the overlap, and what they count.
- `function by_characters(size: i64, overlap: i64) -> Options?`, called `chunks.by_characters(size: size, overlap: overlap)`: The options of pieces of at most `size` characters, each beginning with at most `overlap` characters of the one before, white space trimmed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function by_bytes(size: i64, overlap: i64) -> Options?`, called `chunks.by_bytes(size: size, overlap: overlap)`: The options of pieces of at most `size` bytes, each beginning with at most `overlap` bytes of the one before, white space trimmed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function by_tokens(encoding: tokenizer.Encoding, size: i64, overlap: i64) -> Options?`, called `chunks.by_tokens(encoding, size: size, overlap: overlap)`: The options of pieces of at most `size` tokens of `encoding`, each beginning with at most `overlap` tokens of the one before, white space trimmed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function size_of(text: str, measure: Measure) -> i64`, called `chunks.size_of(text, measure)`: The size of `text` by `measure`.
- `variant Level = .paragraphs | .lines | .sentences | .words | .graphemes`: Where a text may be cut, from the coarsest to the finest.
- `function split(text: str, options: Options) -> [Chunk]`, called `chunks.split(text, options)`: The pieces of `text`, none larger than `options.size`: cut at paragraphs, a paragraph too large cut at its sentences, a sentence too large at its words, a word too large at its graphemes, LangChain's recursive splitter and LlamaIndex's sentence splitter with Unicode's boundaries.
- `function split_at(text: str, level: Level, options: Options) -> [Chunk]`, called `chunks.split_at(text, level, options)`: The pieces of `text` cut only at the boundaries of `level`, parts joined up to `options.size`.
- `function split_separators(text: str, separators: [str], options: Options) -> [Chunk]?`, called `chunks.split_separators(text, separators, options)`: The pieces of `text` cut at the separators `separators`, the first that the text holds tried first and each next one inside a part still too large, then at graphemes: LangChain's recursive splitter with the separators a program gives, for code or any text of its own shape. Fails `invalid`.
- `function split_tokens(text: str, encoding: tokenizer.Encoding, size: i64, overlap: i64) -> [Chunk]?`, called `chunks.split_tokens(text, encoding, size: size, overlap: overlap)`: The pieces of `text` that are runs of its own tokens in `encoding`, at most `size` a piece, each beginning with the last `overlap` of the one before: LangChain's token splitter, cut only where a token ends at a grapheme's end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function split_markdown(text: str, options: Options) -> [Chunk]?`, called `chunks.split_markdown(text, options)`: The pieces of the Markdown document `text`, one for each heading and the blocks under it before the next heading, each piece's `path` the headings above it and its own; a section larger than `options.size` is cut by `split`, each piece keeping the section's path. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function boundaries(text: str, level: Level) -> [i64]`, called `chunks.boundaries(text, level)`: Where `text` may be cut at `level`, as byte indices, ascending, 0 and the length of `text` among them.


### bson

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/bson`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/bson/).

BSON, the binary documents of MongoDB as bsonspec.org specifies them: bytes decoded into a `Document` a program reads and matches on, and a document encoded as bytes, every one of BSON's types held exactly, the deprecated ones included, so a document read and written again is the same bytes but where the specification asks one form (a regex's options in alphabetical order, an array's names `0`, `1`, ...).

- `variant Value = .double(v: f64) | .text(v: str) | .document(doc: Document) | .array(items: [Value]) | .binary(subtype: u8, data: [u8]) | .undefined | .object_id(id: ObjectId) | .boolean(v: bool) | .datetime(ms: i64) | .null_value | .regex(pattern: str, options: str) | .db_pointer(namespace: str, id: ObjectId) | .javascript(code: str) | .symbol(v: str) | .javascript_with_scope(code: str, scope: Document) | .int32(v: i32) | .timestamp(v: Timestamp) | .int64(v: i64) | .decimal128(v: Decimal128) | .min_key | .max_key`: One BSON value.
- `record Document(fields: [Field])`: A BSON document: its fields in order.
- `record Field(name: str, value: Value)`: One field of a document: a name and its value.
- `record ObjectId(bytes: [u8])`: A MongoDB ObjectId: twelve bytes, the first four the seconds since 1970 of its making, big-endian.
- `record Decimal128(bytes: [u8])`: A Decimal128, IEEE 754-2008's 128-bit decimal in its binary integer encoding, as BSON holds it.
- `record Timestamp(seconds: u32, increment: u32)`: A timestamp of MongoDB's replication: seconds and an ordinal within them.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of bytes that are not one well-formed BSON document, of Extended JSON that is not, of a value of another kind than the one asked for, and of a name or a regex holding a zero byte.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of a name or a string whose bytes are not UTF-8.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a number past its type, a document past 2 GiB, and a time past what its form holds.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a field a document does not hold: `member`, `value_at`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a Decimal128 infinity or NaN asked for as a `big.Decimal`.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `512`: The deepest nesting `decode` reads: an empty document is 1 deep, one holding an empty document 2, an array and a scope each a level.
- `constant SUBTYPE_GENERIC: u8`, value `0`: Generic binary data, subtype 0.
- `constant SUBTYPE_FUNCTION: u8`, value `1`: A function, subtype 1.
- `constant SUBTYPE_BINARY_OLD: u8`, value `2`: The old binary subtype 2, its bytes after an inner length, deprecated.
- `constant SUBTYPE_UUID_OLD: u8`, value `3`: A UUID in a legacy byte order, subtype 3.
- `constant SUBTYPE_UUID: u8`, value `4`: A UUID in its standard byte order, subtype 4.
- `constant SUBTYPE_MD5: u8`, value `5`: An MD5 digest, subtype 5.
- `constant SUBTYPE_ENCRYPTED: u8`, value `6`: Encrypted BSON of client-side encryption, subtype 6.
- `constant SUBTYPE_COLUMN: u8`, value `7`: A compressed time-series column, subtype 7.
- `constant SUBTYPE_SENSITIVE: u8`, value `8`: Sensitive data a server leaves out of its logs, subtype 8.
- `constant SUBTYPE_VECTOR: u8`, value `9`: A dense vector of numbers, subtype 9.
- `constant SUBTYPE_USER_DEFINED: u8`, value `128`: The first of the subtypes a program defines, 128 to 255.
- `record DecodeOptions(max_depth: i64, lossy_text: bool)`: How bytes are decoded.
- `record Decoded(doc: Document, next: i64)`: What `decode_next` answers.
- `function strict_decode_options() -> DecodeOptions`, called `bson.strict_decode_options()`: The options `decode` uses: nesting no deeper than `DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`, and text that must be UTF-8.
- `function decode(data: [u8]) -> Document?`, called `bson.decode(data)`: The one document `data` holds. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function decode_with(data: [u8], options: DecodeOptions) -> Document?`, called `bson.decode_with(data, options)`: The one document `data` holds, decoded as `options` asks. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `function decode_next(data: [u8], from: i64, options: DecodeOptions) -> Decoded?`, called `bson.decode_next(data, from, options)`: The document that begins at `from` of `data`, and where it ends: the documents of a stream or a file of `mongodump`, read one after another. Fails as `decode` fails, bytes after the document aside.
- `function decode_all(data: [u8]) -> [Document]?`, called `bson.decode_all(data)`: Every document `data` holds, one after another, as `mongodump` writes a collection. Fails as `decode_next` fails on the first document that is not well-formed.
- `function is_valid(data: [u8]) -> bool`, called `bson.is_valid(data)`: Whether `data` is exactly one well-formed BSON document, as `decode` reads one.
- `function lookup(data: [u8], name: str) -> Value?`, called `bson.lookup(data, name)`: The value of the first field named `name` at the top of the document `data` holds, read without decoding the fields before it: Go's `Raw.Lookup`, Rust's `RawDocument::get`, pymongo's `RawBSONDocument`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function encode(doc: Document) -> [u8]?`, called `bson.encode(doc)`: The bytes of `doc`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function member(doc: Document, name: str) -> Value?`, called `bson.member(doc, name)`: The value of the first field of `doc` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function has_member(doc: Document, name: str) -> bool`, called `bson.has_member(doc, name)`: Whether `doc` has a field named `name`.
- `function with_member(doc: Document, name: str, value: Value) -> Document`, called `bson.with_member(doc, name, value)`: `doc` with its first field named `name` holding `value`, in its place, or with that field added at the end where none has the name.
- `function without_member(doc: Document, name: str) -> Document`, called `bson.without_member(doc, name)`: `doc` without any field named `name`.
- `function names_of(doc: Document) -> [str]`, called `bson.names_of(doc)`: The names of the fields of `doc`, in order; a name that stands twice is there twice.
- `function value_at(doc: Document, path: str) -> Value?`, called `bson.value_at(doc, path)`: The value a dotted path names in `doc`, as MongoDB's queries name one: `"a.b.0"` is field `b` of the document in field `a`, then its element 0. Fails `not_found`.
- `function kind_of(v: Value) -> str`, called `bson.kind_of(v)`: The name of the type of `v`, as MongoDB's `$type` operator spells it: `double`, `string`, `object`, `array`, `binData`, `undefined`, `objectId`, `bool`, `date`, `null`, `regex`, `dbPointer`, `javascript`, `symbol`, `javascriptWithScope`, `int`, `timestamp`, `long`, `decimal`, `minKey`, `maxKey`.
- `function type_code_of(v: Value) -> i64`, called `bson.type_code_of(v)`: The type byte of `v`, 1 to 19, 127 for `max_key` and 255 for `min_key`.
- `function text_of(v: Value) -> str?`, called `bson.text_of(v)`: The text of a string `v`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function int_of(v: Value) -> i64?`, called `bson.int_of(v)`: The integer `v` holds: an int32, an int64, or a double that is a whole number, as a server answers `{"ok": 1.0}` and counts. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function number_of(v: Value) -> f64?`, called `bson.number_of(v)`: The number `v` holds as an `f64`: a double, an int32, or an int64, which rounds to the nearest `f64` past 2^53. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bool_of(v: Value) -> bool?`, called `bson.bool_of(v)`: The truth value of a boolean `v`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function document_of(v: Value) -> Document?`, called `bson.document_of(v)`: The document an embedded document `v` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function items_of(v: Value) -> [Value]?`, called `bson.items_of(v)`: The elements of an array `v`, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function object_id_of(v: Value) -> ObjectId?`, called `bson.object_id_of(v)`: The id an ObjectId `v` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bytes_of(v: Value) -> [u8]?`, called `bson.bytes_of(v)`: The bytes of a binary `v`, of any subtype. Fails `invalid`.
- `function instant_of(v: Value) -> time.Instant?`, called `bson.instant_of(v)`: The instant a datetime `v` names. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function from_int(n: i64) -> Value`, called `bson.from_int(n)`: `n` as an int32 where it fits one, else as an int64, as Go's and Python's drivers write an integer.
- `function from_instant(t: time.Instant) -> Value`, called `bson.from_instant(t)`: `t` as a datetime, cut to the millisecond toward the past.
- `function from_regex(pattern: str, options: str) -> Value`, called `bson.from_regex(pattern: pattern, options: options)`: A regex of `pattern` and `options`, the options in alphabetical order.
- `record ObjectIdMaker(random: [u8], counter: i64)`: What makes ObjectIds for one program: five random bytes of its own and a counter.
- `function object_id_maker() -> ObjectIdMaker?`, called `bson.object_id_maker()`: A maker of ObjectIds, its five bytes and its counter's start drawn from the system's generator for keys. Fails where `os.random_bytes` fails, with its code.
- `function object_id_from_parts(seconds: i64, random: [u8], counter: i64) -> ObjectId`, called `bson.object_id_from_parts(seconds: seconds, random, counter: counter)`: The twelve bytes of an id of `seconds`, `random` and `counter`.
- `function next_object_id(@maker: ObjectIdMaker) -> ObjectId?`, called `bson.next_object_id(@maker)`: A new ObjectId: the seconds the wall clock reads now, the maker's five bytes, and its counter advanced by one. Fails `does_not_fit`.
- `function object_id_at(t: time.Instant) -> ObjectId?`, called `bson.object_id_at(t)`: The least ObjectId of the second `t` stands in, its last eight bytes zero: a bound for a query over the ids made from that second on. Fails `does_not_fit`.
- `function parse_object_id(s: str) -> ObjectId?`, called `bson.parse_object_id(s)`: The ObjectId whose 24 hexadecimal digits `s` holds, in either case. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_object_id(id: ObjectId) -> str`, called `bson.format_object_id(id)`: `id` as 24 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
- `function object_id_from_bytes(b: [u8]) -> ObjectId?`, called `bson.object_id_from_bytes(b)`: The ObjectId of the twelve bytes `b`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function time_of(id: ObjectId) -> time.Instant`, called `bson.time_of(id)`: The second `id` was made in, its first four bytes.
- `function is_object_id(s: str) -> bool`, called `bson.is_object_id(s)`: Whether `s` is 24 hexadecimal digits, in either case.
- `function parse_decimal128(s: str) -> Decimal128?`, called `bson.parse_decimal128(s)`: The Decimal128 `s` spells: an optional sign, then `Infinity`, `Inf` or `NaN` in any case, or digits with at most one point and an optional exponent after `e` or `E`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function format_decimal128(d: Decimal128) -> str`, called `bson.format_decimal128(d)`: `d` as text, as the General Decimal Arithmetic and Python's `Decimal` write it: `1.23E+3`, `0.000001`, `1E-7`, `-0`, `NaN`, `Infinity`.
- `function from_decimal(d: big.Decimal) -> Value?`, called `bson.from_decimal(d)`: `d` as a Decimal128 value, exactly. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function decimal_of(v: Value) -> big.Decimal?`, called `bson.decimal_of(v)`: The number a Decimal128 `v` holds, as a `big.Decimal`; a negative zero is zero. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function compare_timestamps(a: Timestamp, b: Timestamp) -> i64`, called `bson.compare_timestamps(a: a, b: b)`: Whether `a` comes before `b` (-1), is `b` (0), or comes after it (1): by their seconds, then their increments.
- `variant UuidRepresentation = .standard | .python_legacy | .java_legacy | .csharp_legacy`: The byte order a UUID is held in: the standard one of subtype 4, or one of the three legacy orders of subtype 3 that older drivers wrote.
- `function reordered(b: [u8], representation: UuidRepresentation) -> [u8]`, called `bson.reordered(b, representation)`: The bytes of `b` in or out of `representation`'s order, which is its own inverse.
- `function from_uuid(b: [u8], representation: UuidRepresentation) -> Value?`, called `bson.from_uuid(b, representation)`: The binary value of the UUID `b` in `representation`'s subtype and order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function uuid_of(v: Value, representation: UuidRepresentation) -> [u8]?`, called `bson.uuid_of(v, representation)`: The UUID a binary `v` holds in `representation`'s subtype and order, in its standard order. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Vector = .int8(values: [i8]) | .float32(values: [f32]) | .packed_bit(bits: [u8], padding: u8)`: A dense vector held in a binary of subtype 9, as MongoDB's vector search reads one: its type of element, and its elements.
- `function from_vector(v: Vector) -> Value?`, called `bson.from_vector(v)`: The binary value of subtype 9 holding `v`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function vector_of(v: Value) -> Vector?`, called `bson.vector_of(v)`: The vector a binary `v` of subtype 9 holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `record DBRef(collection: str, id: Value, database: str)`: A DBRef, MongoDB's convention for a reference to a document of another collection: a document of `$ref`, `$id` and an optional `$db`.
- `function from_dbref(r: DBRef) -> Document`, called `bson.from_dbref(r)`: The document of `r`: `$ref`, `$id`, then `$db` where `r` names a database.
- `function dbref_of(doc: Document) -> DBRef?`, called `bson.dbref_of(doc)`: The DBRef `doc` is: a first field `$ref` holding a string, a second `$id`, and an optional `$db` holding a string; other fields after them are allowed and left out. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant JsonMode = .canonical | .relaxed`: The two modes of MongoDB's Extended JSON v2.
- `function to_json(doc: Document, mode: JsonMode) -> json.Value?`, called `bson.to_json(doc, mode)`: `doc` as Extended JSON, a `json.Value`, in `mode`. Fails as `encode` fails on a document that is no BSON.
- `function from_json(v: json.Value) -> Document?`, called `bson.from_json(v)`: The document the Extended JSON `v` writes, canonical or relaxed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_json(doc: Document, mode: JsonMode) -> str?`, called `bson.format_json(doc, mode)`: `doc` as Extended JSON text on one line. Fails as `to_json` fails.
- `function parse_json(text: str) -> Document?`, called `bson.parse_json(text)`: The document the Extended JSON text `text` writes. Fails where `json.parse` fails, with its code, and as `from_json` fails.
- `function value_to_json(v: Value, mode: JsonMode) -> json.Value?`, called `bson.value_to_json(v, mode)`: The value `v` as Extended JSON in `mode`. Fails as `to_json` fails.
- `function value_from_json(j: json.Value) -> Value?`, called `bson.value_from_json(j)`: The value the Extended JSON `j` writes: a wrapper, a document, or a plain JSON value. Fails as `from_json` fails.


### tui

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/tui`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/tui/).

Full-screen terminal programs in immediate mode, as Rust's `ratatui` draws them: the program keeps its own state; each frame it asks for a blank buffer of the screen's size, cuts it into areas by constraints, draws widgets into those areas, and hands the buffer to `flush`, which writes only the cells that changed since the frame before; then it reads the next event, a key, a click, a paste or a new size, and changes its state.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: Nothing is selected where a selected row or column was asked.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The program's standard output is no terminal, or the program has none.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument out of its range: a time below zero.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: No event came in the time allowed.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The terminal is gone.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names; the message carries its words.
- `variant Cursor = .hidden | .at(x: i64, y: i64)`: Where the cursor stands after a flush.
- `record Options(mouse: bool, mouse_motion: bool, paste: bool, focus: bool)`: What a terminal reports besides keys, asked at `start`.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `tui.default_options()`: The options most programs start with: paste as one event, no mouse, no focus reports.
- `record Terminal(output: io.Stream, screen: screen.Screen)`: The program's terminal in full-screen mode, between `start` and `stop`: the frame on the screen, its size, and the modes turned on.
- `variant Event = .key(key: term.Key) | .mouse(action: MouseAction, button: MouseButton, x: i64, y: i64, shift: bool, alt: bool, control: bool) | .pasted(text: str) | .resized(width: i64, height: i64) | .focus_gained | .focus_lost`: Something that happened at the terminal, as the event readers answer it.
- `variant MouseAction = .press | .release | .drag | .motion | .scroll_up | .scroll_down | .scroll_left | .scroll_right`: What the mouse did.
- `variant MouseButton = .none | .left | .middle | .right`: A button of the mouse.
- `function start(options: Options) -> Terminal?`, called `tui.start(options)`: Puts the program's terminal in full-screen mode: the raw mode, the alternate screen cleared, the cursor hidden, and the reports `options` asks for. Fails `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function stop(@terminal: Terminal) -> ()?`, called `tui.stop(@terminal)`: Puts the terminal back as it was before `start`: the reports off, the cursor shown, the alternate screen left, the raw mode left. Fails `failed`.
- `function area_of(terminal: Terminal) -> Rect`, called `tui.area_of(terminal)`: The screen as a rectangle at 0, 0, as the last event read or `start` found it.
- `function frame_of(terminal: Terminal) -> Buffer`, called `tui.frame_of(terminal)`: A blank buffer of the screen's size, for one frame.
- `function flush(@terminal: Terminal, frame: Buffer, cursor: Cursor) -> ()?`, called `tui.flush(@terminal, frame, cursor)`: Writes `frame` to the screen: only the cells that differ from the frame before, or every cell where the size changed or `redraw` was asked; then the cursor where `cursor` says. Fails `closed`.
- `function redraw(@terminal: Terminal)`, called `tui.redraw(@terminal)`: Makes the next `flush` clear the screen and write every cell: after another program, or a write of the program's own, changed the screen.
- `function read_event(@terminal: Terminal) -> Event?`, called `tui.read_event(@terminal)`: The next event at the terminal, waiting as long as it takes. Fails `closed`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function read_event_within(@terminal: Terminal, limit: time.Duration) -> Event?`, called `tui.read_event_within(@terminal, limit)`: The next event at the terminal, waiting at most `limit`: the reader of a program that also moves on its own, a clock or an animation. Fails `timeout`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function suspend(@terminal: Terminal) -> ()?`, called `tui.suspend(@terminal)`: Gives the terminal back to the person for a while, as `stop` does, so another program can run in it (an editor, a pager); `resume` takes it again. Fails `failed`.
- `function resume(@terminal: Terminal) -> ()?`, called `tui.resume(@terminal)`: Takes the terminal again after `suspend`, as `start` took it, and asks the next flush to write every cell. Fails as `start` does.
- `function set_title(terminal: Terminal lent, title: str) -> ()?`, called `tui.set_title(terminal, title)`: Sets the title of the terminal's window. Fails `failed`.
- `record Rect(x: i64, y: i64, width: i64, height: i64)`: A rectangle of cells on the screen.
- `function inner(area: Rect, horizontal: i64, vertical: i64) -> Rect`, called `tui.inner(area, horizontal: horizontal, vertical: vertical)`: `area` with `horizontal` columns taken off each side and `vertical` rows off the top and the bottom.
- `function outer(area: Rect, horizontal: i64, vertical: i64) -> Rect`, called `tui.outer(area, horizontal: horizontal, vertical: vertical)`: `area` with `horizontal` columns added to each side and `vertical` rows to the top and the bottom, its left and top edges stopping at 0.
- `function intersection(a: Rect, b: Rect) -> Rect`, called `tui.intersection(a: a, b: b)`: The cells `a` and `b` share.
- `function intersects(a: Rect, b: Rect) -> bool`, called `tui.intersects(a: a, b: b)`: Whether `a` and `b` share a cell.
- `function enclosing(a: Rect, b: Rect) -> Rect`, called `tui.enclosing(a: a, b: b)`: The smallest rectangle holding both `a` and `b`.
- `function contains(area: Rect, x: i64, y: i64) -> bool`, called `tui.contains(area, x: x, y: y)`: Whether the cell at column `x` and row `y` is inside `area`: where a click landed, for instance.
- `function clamp(area: Rect, within: Rect) -> Rect`, called `tui.clamp(area: area, within: within)`: `area` moved inside `within` and cut to its size: no larger than `within`, and moved the least that puts it inside.
- `function offset(area: Rect, dx: i64, dy: i64) -> Rect`, called `tui.offset(area, dx: dx, dy: dy)`: `area` moved `dx` columns right and `dy` rows down, its edges stopping at 0.
- `function rows_of(area: Rect) -> [Rect]`, called `tui.rows_of(area)`: Each row of `area`, a rectangle one row high, the top one first.
- `function columns_of(area: Rect) -> [Rect]`, called `tui.columns_of(area)`: Each column of `area`, a rectangle one column wide, the left one first.
- `function centered(area: Rect, width: Constraint, height: Constraint) -> Rect`, called `tui.centered(area, width: width, height: height)`: A rectangle in the middle of `area`, its size given by `width` and `height` as a layout of one part gives it: a dialog drawn over the screen.
- `function is_empty(area: Rect) -> bool`, called `tui.is_empty(area)`: Whether `area` holds no cell: a width or a height of 0 or below.
- `variant Constraint = .length(n: i64) | .percentage(n: i64) | .ratio(numerator: i64, denominator: i64) | .min(n: i64) | .max(n: i64) | .fill(weight: i64)`: What a part of a layout asks for.
- `variant Direction = .horizontal | .vertical`: The way a layout lays its parts.
- `variant Flex = .legacy | .start | .end | .center | .space_between | .space_around | .space_evenly`: Where the space goes that no part takes, where no part is a `min` or a `fill`.
- `record Layout(direction: Direction, constraints: [Constraint], horizontal_margin: i64, vertical_margin: i64, spacing: i64, flex: Flex)`: How an area is cut into parts.
- `function new_layout(direction: Direction, constraints: [Constraint]) -> Layout`, called `tui.new_layout(direction, constraints)`: A layout of `constraints` laid in `direction`, with no margin, no spacing, and the space no part takes left after the last part (`.start`).
- `function split(area: Rect, layout: Layout) -> [Rect]`, called `tui.split(area, layout)`: `area` cut by `layout` into one rectangle per constraint, in order.
- `function spacers_of(area: Rect, layout: Layout) -> [Rect]`, called `tui.spacers_of(area, layout)`: The gaps `split` leaves around and between the parts of `area`: one before the first part, one between each two, and one after the last, in order.
- `variant Alignment = .left | .center | .right`: Where a line stands in the width it is drawn in.
- `record Span(text: str, style: term.Style)`: A piece of text drawn in one style.
- `record Line(spans: [Span], style: term.Style, alignment: Alignment)`: One line of text: spans drawn one after another, a style under them all, and where the line stands.
- `function new_line(text: str) -> Line`, called `tui.new_line(text)`: `text` as one line of one plain span, against the left.
- `function styled_line(text: str, style: term.Style) -> Line`, called `tui.styled_line(text, style)`: `text` as one line of one span drawn in `style`, against the left.
- `function new_lines(text: str) -> [Line]`, called `tui.new_lines(text)`: The lines of `text`, each a plain line against the left: cut at each line feed, a carriage return before one taken away with it.
- `function width_of(line: Line) -> i64`, called `tui.width_of(line)`: How many cells `line` takes when drawn: each grapheme as `unicode/segment`'s `width_of` measures it, a control character none.
- `function with_alignment(lines: [Line], alignment: Alignment) -> [Line]`, called `tui.with_alignment(lines, alignment)`: `lines`, each standing where `alignment` says.
- `record Cell(symbol: str, style: term.Style)`: One cell of a buffer: what is drawn in it, and how.
- `record Buffer(area: Rect, grid: grid.Grid)`: A rectangle of cells a frame is drawn in.
- `record Change(x: i64, y: i64, cell: Cell)`: One cell that differs between two buffers, as `diff` answers it.
- `function blank(area: Rect) -> Buffer`, called `tui.blank(area)`: A buffer over `area`, every cell blank and plain.
- `function new_buffer(lines: [str]) -> Buffer`, called `tui.new_buffer(lines)`: A buffer at 0, 0 holding `lines`, as wide as the widest and as high as there are lines, every cell plain: what a test compares a drawing with.
- `function cell_at(buffer: Buffer, x: i64, y: i64) -> Cell`, called `tui.cell_at(buffer, x: x, y: y)`: The cell of `buffer` at column `x` and row `y` of the screen.
- `function to_lines(buffer: Buffer) -> [str]`, called `tui.to_lines(buffer)`: The rows of `buffer` as text, the top one first: each cell's symbol, a wide character once for its two cells.
- `function draw_text(@buffer: Buffer, x: i64, y: i64, text: str, style: term.Style, width: i64) -> i64`, called `tui.draw_text(@buffer, x: x, y: y, text, style, width: width)`: Draws `text` into `buffer` from column `x` of row `y`, in `style`, taking at most `width` cells, and answers the column after the last cell drawn.
- `function draw_line(@buffer: Buffer, x: i64, y: i64, line: Line, width: i64) -> i64`, called `tui.draw_line(@buffer, x: x, y: y, line, width: width)`: Draws `line` into `buffer` from column `x` of row `y`, taking at most `width` cells, and answers the column after the last cell drawn.
- `function set_style(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, style: term.Style)`, called `tui.set_style(@buffer, area, style)`: Lays `style` over every cell of `area` in `buffer`, the symbols kept.
- `function fill(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, symbol: str, style: term.Style)`, called `tui.fill(@buffer, area, symbol, style)`: Puts `symbol` in every cell of `area` in `buffer`, with `style` laid over each.
- `function clear(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect)`, called `tui.clear(@buffer, area)`: Puts every cell of `area` in `buffer` back to blank and plain: what a dialog drawn over other widgets clears first.
- `function paste(@buffer: Buffer, from: Buffer)`, called `tui.paste(buffer: @buffer, from: from)`: Copies every cell of `from` into `buffer` where the two areas meet, each cell as it is: a drawing made apart, laid on a frame.
- `function diff(before: Buffer, after: Buffer) -> [Change]`, called `tui.diff(before: before, after: after)`: The cells of `after` that differ from `before`, row by row: what a terminal showing `before` must be written to show `after`.
- `function format_changes(changes: [Change]) -> str`, called `tui.format_changes(changes)`: The bytes that write `changes` on a terminal: the cursor moved to each run of changed cells, each run in its style, the terminal's own rendition put back after each styled run, the cursor left where the last cell ended.
- `variant BorderType = .plain | .rounded | .double | .thick | .light_double_dashed | .heavy_double_dashed | .light_triple_dashed | .heavy_triple_dashed | .light_quadruple_dashed | .heavy_quadruple_dashed | .quadrant_inside | .quadrant_outside`: The lines a block's border is drawn with.
- `record Borders(top: bool, right: bool, bottom: bool, left: bool)`: Which sides of a block have a border.
- `variant TitlePosition = .top | .bottom`: Whether a title stands on a block's top edge or its bottom edge.
- `record Title(line: Line, position: TitlePosition)`: A title on a block's edge.
- `record Padding(left: i64, right: i64, top: i64, bottom: i64)`: The cells left empty inside a block's border, on each side.
- `record Block(borders: Borders, border_type: BorderType, border_style: term.Style, titles: [Title], title_style: term.Style, style: term.Style, padding: Padding)`: A box around an area: borders, titles on its edges, a style under it all, and padding inside.
- `function bordered() -> Block`, called `tui.bordered()`: A block with all four borders of thin lines, no title, plain.
- `function borderless() -> Block`, called `tui.borderless()`: A block with no border, no title and no padding: only a style under an area, or a title over it.
- `function with_title(block: Block, title: str) -> Block`, called `tui.with_title(block, title)`: A copy of `block` with `title` added on its top edge, against the left.
- `function inner_of(block: Block, area: Rect) -> Rect`, called `tui.inner_of(block, area)`: The area left inside `block` drawn over `area`: its borders, the rows its titles take where there is no border on their edge, and its padding taken off.
- `function draw_block(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, block: Block)`, called `tui.draw_block(@buffer, area, block)`: Draws `block` over `area` of `buffer`: its style under the area, then its borders, then its titles, each cut to the edge between its corners.
- `record Paragraph(lines: [Line], style: term.Style, wrap: bool, trim: bool, scroll_x: i64, scroll_y: i64)`: Lines of text drawn in an area, wrapped at its width or cut at it, and scrolled.
- `function new_paragraph(text: str) -> Paragraph`, called `tui.new_paragraph(text)`: A paragraph of the lines of `text`, plain, cut at the area's edge, not scrolled; `wrap` and `trim` may be set after.
- `function draw_paragraph(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, paragraph: Paragraph)`, called `tui.draw_paragraph(@buffer, area, paragraph)`: Draws `paragraph` in `area` of `buffer`.
- `function height_of(paragraph: Paragraph, width: i64) -> i64`, called `tui.height_of(paragraph, width)`: How many rows `paragraph` takes drawn `width` cells wide, its scrolling not counted: what a scrollbar or a layout asks before drawing.
- `record Selection(marks: marks.Marks)`: What a list or a table keeps between frames: the row selected, if any, the column selected, if any, and the first row shown.
- `function selection() -> Selection`, called `tui.selection()`: A selection of nothing, its first row shown the first.
- `function select(@state: Selection, index: i64)`, called `tui.select(@state, index)`: Selects the row `index`.
- `function unselect(@state: Selection)`, called `tui.unselect(@state)`: Selects no row; the column selected, if any, stays.
- `function selected_of(state: Selection) -> i64?`, called `tui.selected_of(state)`: The row selected. Fails `not_found`.
- `function select_first(@state: Selection, count: i64)`, called `tui.select_first(@state, count)`: Selects the first of `count` rows; nothing where there is none.
- `function select_last(@state: Selection, count: i64)`, called `tui.select_last(@state, count)`: Selects the last of `count` rows; nothing where there is none.
- `function move_selection(@state: Selection, count: i64, by: i64)`, called `tui.move_selection(@state, count: count, by: by)`: Moves the selected row `by` rows down among `count`, stopping at the first and the last: Down is 1, Up is -1, Page Down a page.
- `function select_column(@state: Selection, index: i64)`, called `tui.select_column(@state, index)`: Selects the column `index`, which a table highlights.
- `function unselect_column(@state: Selection)`, called `tui.unselect_column(@state)`: Selects no column.
- `function selected_column_of(state: Selection) -> i64?`, called `tui.selected_column_of(state)`: The column selected. Fails `not_found`.
- `function move_column(@state: Selection, count: i64, by: i64)`, called `tui.move_column(@state, count: count, by: by)`: Moves the selected column `by` columns right among `count`, stopping at the first and the last.
- `function offset_of(state: Selection) -> i64`, called `tui.offset_of(state)`: The first row shown, from 0, as the last draw left it.
