- `variant HighlightSpacing = .always | .when_selected | .never`: When a list or a table keeps room for its highlight symbol before its rows.
- `variant ListDirection = .top_to_bottom | .bottom_to_top`: Which way a list's items go.
- `record ListItem(lines: [Line], style: term.Style)`: One item of a list: one or more lines.
- `record List(items: [ListItem], style: term.Style, highlight_style: term.Style, highlight_symbol: str, highlight_spacing: HighlightSpacing, repeat_highlight_symbol: bool, direction: ListDirection, scroll_padding: i64)`: Items one under another, one of them selected.
- `function new_list(items: [str]) -> List`, called `tui.new_list(items)`: A list of `items`, each a plain item of the lines of its text, the selected one drawn reversed with no symbol before it.
- `function draw_list(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, list: List, @state: Selection)`, called `tui.draw_list(@buffer, area, list, @state)`: Draws `list` in `area` of `buffer` with `state`'s selected item highlighted, and moves `state`'s first row shown so that item is in view.
- `record TableCell(lines: [Line], style: term.Style)`: One cell of a table: one or more lines.
- `record Row(cells: [TableCell], height: i64, top_margin: i64, bottom_margin: i64, style: term.Style)`: One row of a table.
- `record Table(header: [Row], rows: [Row], footer: [Row], widths: [Constraint], column_spacing: i64, flex: Flex, style: term.Style, row_highlight_style: term.Style, column_highlight_style: term.Style, cell_highlight_style: term.Style, highlight_symbol: str, highlight_spacing: HighlightSpacing)`: Rows of cells in columns, under a header, one row selected.
- `function new_table(rows: [[str]], widths: [Constraint]) -> Table`, called `tui.new_table(rows, widths)`: A table of `rows`, each a list of the cells' texts, its columns as wide as `widths` asks, a column apart, the selected row drawn reversed.
- `function new_row(cells: [str]) -> Row`, called `tui.new_row(cells)`: A row of plain cells holding `cells`, as tall as its tallest cell.
- `function draw_table(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, table: Table, @state: Selection)`, called `tui.draw_table(@buffer, area, table, @state)`: Draws `table` in `area` of `buffer`: its header at the top, its footer at the bottom, and between them the rows from `state`'s first row shown, the selected row, column and cell highlighted.
- `record Tabs(titles: [Line], selected: i64, style: term.Style, highlight_style: term.Style, divider: str, padding_left: str, padding_right: str)`: A row of titles, one of them selected.
- `function new_tabs(titles: [str], selected: i64) -> Tabs`, called `tui.new_tabs(titles, selected)`: Tabs of `titles` with the title `selected` drawn reversed, a space on each side of each title and `│` between them.
- `function draw_tabs(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, tabs: Tabs)`, called `tui.draw_tabs(@buffer, area, tabs)`: Draws `tabs` on the first row of `area` of `buffer`, cut at its right edge.
- `record Gauge(ratio: f64, label: str, style: term.Style, gauge_style: term.Style, use_unicode: bool)`: How far something has gone, as a bar filling its area with a label in its middle.
- `function new_gauge(ratio: f64) -> Gauge`, called `tui.new_gauge(ratio)`: A gauge at `ratio`, labelled with its percentage rounded (`50%`), plain, filling whole cells.
- `function draw_gauge(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, gauge: Gauge)`, called `tui.draw_gauge(@buffer, area, gauge)`: Draws `gauge` in `area` of `buffer`: the bar from the left, the label on the middle row.
- `record LineGauge(ratio: f64, label: str, style: term.Style, filled_style: term.Style, unfilled_style: term.Style, filled_symbol: str, unfilled_symbol: str)`: How far something has gone, as a label and a line on one row.
- `function new_line_gauge(ratio: f64) -> LineGauge`, called `tui.new_line_gauge(ratio)`: A line gauge at `ratio`, labelled with its percentage rounded and set against the right of three cells (` 50%`), and drawn with `─`.
- `function draw_line_gauge(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, gauge: LineGauge)`, called `tui.draw_line_gauge(@buffer, area, gauge)`: Draws `gauge` on the first row of `area` of `buffer`: the label, a space, then the line to the right edge.
- `variant SparklineDirection = .left_to_right | .right_to_left`: Which way a sparkline's values go.
- `record Sparkline(data: [i64], max: i64, style: term.Style, direction: SparklineDirection, symbols: [str])`: Values drawn as bars one cell wide, their heights in eighths of a cell.
- `function new_sparkline(data: [i64]) -> Sparkline`, called `tui.new_sparkline(data)`: A sparkline of `data`, plain, left to right, scaled to its largest value.
- `function draw_sparkline(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, sparkline: Sparkline)`, called `tui.draw_sparkline(@buffer, area, sparkline)`: Draws `sparkline` in `area` of `buffer`, each value a bar from the bottom.
- `variant ScrollbarOrientation = .vertical_right | .vertical_left | .horizontal_bottom | .horizontal_top`: Where a scrollbar stands in its area.
- `record Scrollbar(orientation: ScrollbarOrientation, content_length: i64, position: i64, viewport_length: i64, thumb_symbol: str, track_symbol: str, begin_symbol: str, end_symbol: str, thumb_style: term.Style, track_style: term.Style)`: A bar telling how much of a content is shown and where: a track, a thumb in it, and an arrow at each end.
- `function new_scrollbar(orientation: ScrollbarOrientation, content_length: i64, position: i64) -> Scrollbar`, called `tui.new_scrollbar(orientation, content_length: content_length, position: position)`: A scrollbar on `orientation`'s edge for a content of `content_length` rows shown from `position`, with arrows at its ends.
- `function draw_scrollbar(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, scrollbar: Scrollbar)`, called `tui.draw_scrollbar(@buffer, area, scrollbar)`: Draws `scrollbar` on its edge of `area` of `buffer`.
- `record Input(text: str, cursor: i64, mask: str, placeholder: str, style: term.Style, placeholder_style: term.Style, view: i64)`: One line of text being typed, and where its cursor stands.
- `function new_input(text: str) -> Input`, called `tui.new_input(text)`: An input holding `text`, its cursor at the end, no mask, no placeholder.
- `function press_input(@input: Input, key: term.Key) -> bool`, called `tui.press_input(@input, key)`: Does `key` to `input` and answers whether it was taken: a character typed goes in at the cursor; Left, Right, Home, End, Ctrl-B, Ctrl-F, Ctrl-A and Ctrl-E move by a grapheme or to an end; Backspace, Delete and Ctrl-D take a grapheme out; Ctrl-K takes the text after the cursor, Ctrl-U the text before it, Ctrl-W the word before it.
- `function draw_input(@buffer: Buffer, area: Rect, @input: Input) -> Cursor`, called `tui.draw_input(@buffer, area, @input)`: Draws `input` on the first row of `area` of `buffer`, scrolled so its cursor is in view, and answers where the cursor stands, for `flush`.


### webauthn

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/webauthn`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/webauthn/).

A relying party of W3C Web Authentication Level 3: the options of a registration and of an authentication written as the JSON a browser hands `navigator.credentials`, and the responses verified: the client data's type, challenge and origin, the authenticator data's RP ID, flags and counter, the attestation, and the assertion's signature.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of a response that is not well formed or does not verify: every `verify_*` and `decode_*` function answers it, the message naming the check.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `codes.UNSUPPORTED`: The code of a key whose algorithm or curve this system's cryptography lacks: EdDSA on Windows, ES512 everywhere; `decode_public_key`, `verify_signature` and the `verify_*` functions answer it.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `codes.NOT_FOUND`: The code an `AuthenticatorData`'s `credential` and `extensions` answer where its flags say no attested credential, or no extension outputs, follow.
- `constant ES256: i64`, value `-7`: ECDSA on P-256 with SHA-256, the COSE algorithm every authenticator has.
- `constant ES384: i64`, value `-35`: ECDSA on P-384 with SHA-384.
- `constant ES512: i64`, value `-36`: ECDSA on P-521 with SHA-512, which no system here verifies.
- `constant EDDSA: i64`, value `-8`: EdDSA, Ed25519 in practice.
- `constant PS256: i64`, value `-37`: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256.
- `constant PS384: i64`, value `-38`: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-384.
- `constant PS512: i64`, value `-39`: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-512.
- `constant RS256: i64`, value `-257`: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256, Windows Hello's.
- `constant RS384: i64`, value `-258`: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-384.
- `constant RS512: i64`, value `-259`: RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-512.
- `record RelyingParty(id: str, name: str, origins: [str])`: The relying party: the site a credential belongs to.
- `record User(id: [u8], name: str, display_name: str)`: A user account, as a registration names it.
- `variant Requirement = .required | .preferred | .discouraged`: How strongly the relying party asks for a property.
- `variant Conveyance = .none | .indirect | .direct | .enterprise`: Which attestation the relying party asks for.
- `variant Attachment = .either | .platform | .cross_platform`: Which authenticators a registration may use.
- `variant Hint = .security_key | .client_device | .hybrid`: A hint to the browser of the authenticator the relying party expects.
- `record Descriptor(id: [u8], transports: [str])`: A credential named in the options: one to exclude from a registration or to allow in an authentication.
- `record RegistrationOptions(challenge: [u8], timeout: time.Duration, algorithms: [i64], exclude: [Descriptor], attestation: Conveyance, attachment: Attachment, resident_key: Requirement, user_verification: Requirement, hints: [Hint])`: The options of a registration.
- `function registration_options(challenge: [u8]) -> RegistrationOptions`, called `webauthn.registration_options(challenge)`: The options of an ordinary registration with `challenge`: a minute to answer, ES256, EdDSA where this system verifies it, and RS256, no attestation, any authenticator, a discoverable credential and user verification preferred.
- `function format_registration_options(rp: RelyingParty, user: User, options: RegistrationOptions) -> str?`, called `webauthn.format_registration_options(rp, user, options)`: The JSON of a registration's options, `PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON`: what a page hands `PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON`, every byte string in base 64 for URLs without padding. Fails `invalid`.
- `record AuthenticationOptions(challenge: [u8], timeout: time.Duration, allow: [Descriptor], user_verification: Requirement, hints: [Hint])`: The options of an authentication.
- `function authentication_options(challenge: [u8]) -> AuthenticationOptions`, called `webauthn.authentication_options(challenge)`: The options of an ordinary authentication with `challenge`: a minute, any discoverable credential, user verification preferred.
- `function format_authentication_options(rp_id: str, options: AuthenticationOptions) -> str?`, called `webauthn.format_authentication_options(rp_id, options)`: The JSON of an authentication's options, `PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON`: what a page hands `PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function new_challenge() -> [u8]?`, called `webauthn.new_challenge()`: Thirty-two bytes from the system's generator for keys: a challenge, or a user handle. Fails with `os.random_bytes`'s code where the generator refuses.
- `record Expected(challenge: [u8], rp_id: str, origins: [str], top_origins: [str], user_verification: bool, algorithms: [i64])`: What a ceremony's response must show.
- `function expect(rp: RelyingParty, challenge: [u8]) -> Expected`, called `webauthn.expect(rp, challenge)`: What `rp`'s ceremony with `challenge` must show: one of its origins, no cross-origin frame, the user present but not necessarily verified, and any algorithm of this package.
- `record Credential(id: [u8], public_key: [u8], sign_count: i64, transports: [str])`: A credential the relying party keeps, made by `verify_registration` and handed to `verify_authentication`.
- `variant Attestation = .none | .self_attested | .certified | .unverified`: How a registration's authenticator vouched for its key.
- `record Registration(credential: Credential, algorithm: i64, aaguid: [u8], format: str, attestation: Attestation, certificates: [[u8]], user_verified: bool, backup_eligible: bool, backed_up: bool)`: What a verified registration answers.
- `function verify_registration(response: str, expected: Expected) -> Registration?`, called `webauthn.verify_registration(response, expected)`: The registration `response` makes, every check of Web Authentication Level 3 § 7.1 made against `expected`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Authentication(credential_id: [u8], user_handle: [u8], sign_count: i64, user_verified: bool, backup_eligible: bool, backed_up: bool)`: What a verified authentication answers.
- `function verify_authentication(response: str, expected: Expected, credential: Credential) -> Authentication?`, called `webauthn.verify_authentication(response, expected, credential)`: The authentication `response` makes with `credential`, every check of Web Authentication Level 3 § 7.2 made against `expected`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function credential_id_of(response: str) -> [u8]?`, called `webauthn.credential_id_of(response)`: The credential ID a response names, so the program finds the credential it registered before verifying. Fails `invalid`.
- `function user_handle_of(response: str) -> [u8]?`, called `webauthn.user_handle_of(response)`: The user handle an authentication's response carries: the account of a discoverable credential, found before the credential is. Fails `invalid`.
- `record ClientData(kind: str, challenge: [u8], origin: str, cross_origin: bool, top_origin: str)`: The client data a browser signs over.
- `function decode_client_data(data: [u8]) -> ClientData?`, called `webauthn.decode_client_data(data)`: The client data `data` holds, `clientDataJSON` decoded from base 64. Fails `invalid`.
- `record AttestedCredential(aaguid: [u8], credential_id: [u8], public_key: [u8])`: The credential an authenticator data carries at registration, where its flag AT is set: the three parts that follow the counter, all of them or none.
- `record AuthenticatorData(rp_id_hash: [u8], user_present: bool, user_verified: bool, backup_eligible: bool, backed_up: bool, sign_count: i64, credential: AttestedCredential?, extensions: [u8]?)`: The authenticator data: the RP ID's hash, the flags, the counter, and at registration the new credential.
- `function decode_authenticator_data(data: [u8]) -> AuthenticatorData?`, called `webauthn.decode_authenticator_data(data)`: The authenticator data `data` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `record AttestationObject(format: str, statement: cbor.Value, auth_data: [u8])`: An attestation object: what an authenticator answers a registration.
- `function decode_attestation_object(data: [u8]) -> AttestationObject?`, called `webauthn.decode_attestation_object(data)`: The attestation object `data` holds, CBOR with the members `fmt`, `attStmt` and `authData`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record PublicKey(algorithm: i64, kind: keypairs.Kind, scheme: keypairs.Scheme, der: [u8])`: A credential's public key, read from its COSE key.
- `function decode_public_key(cose: [u8]) -> PublicKey?`, called `webauthn.decode_public_key(cose)`: The public key the COSE key `cose` holds. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function verify_signature(cose: [u8], data: [u8], signature: [u8]) -> bool?`, called `webauthn.verify_signature(cose: cose, data: data, signature: signature)`: Whether `signature` is the signature of `data` by the key `cose` holds. Fails as `decode_public_key` fails, and with `keypairs.verify_der`'s codes.


### image/png

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/image/png`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/png/).

PNG read and written, by the W3C's PNG specification (third edition): every colour type and bit depth, interlaced or not, read into an `image.Image`; an image written with the filter and compression level the caller picks; the chunks a program does not need dropped or kept, and text chunks read and made.

- `record Chunk(kind: str, data: [u8], after_image: bool)`: One chunk of a PNG file that `decode` kept or `encode` writes: an ancillary chunk, whose four letters begin in lower case (`tEXt`, `gAMA`, `pHYs`, `eXIf`).
- `variant Keep = .none | .all | .only(kinds: [str])`: Which ancillary chunks `decode` keeps.
- `record DecodeOptions(limits: image.Limits, keep: Keep)`: How `decode_with` reads a file.
- `function decoding() -> DecodeOptions`, called `png.decoding()`: Options of `image.default_limits` that keep no chunk, which `decode` takes.
- `record Png(image: image.Image, palette: [image.Color], bit_depth: i64, color_type: i64, interlaced: bool, chunks: [Chunk])`: What `decode` answers: the image and what the file says of it.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> Png?`, called `png.decode(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, and its palette, keeping no ancillary chunk. Fails as `decode_with` fails.
- `function decode_with(data: [u8], options: DecodeOptions) -> Png?`, called `png.decode_with(data, options)`: The image `data` holds, and its palette and the chunks `options` keeps. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `png.decode_image(data, limits)`: The image `data` holds, alone: what a program that reads any of the formats asks of each, by one call of one shape in `image/bmp`, `image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/netpbm` and `image/png`. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `record Info(width: i64, height: i64, format: image.Format, bit_depth: i64, color_type: i64, interlaced: bool)`: What the header of a PNG file says, read without its image data.
- `function info_of(data: [u8]) -> Info?`, called `png.info_of(data)`: The size and format of the image `data` holds, read from its chunks up to the first `IDAT`, nothing inflated: Go's `png.DecodeConfig`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `variant Filter = .none | .sub | .up | .average | .paeth | .adaptive`: How `encode` chooses each row's filter, which makes the rows compress better (PNG section 9).
- `record EncodeOptions(level: i64, filter: Filter, chunks: [Chunk])`: How `encode` writes a file.
- `function default_encode_options() -> EncodeOptions`, called `png.default_encode_options()`: Options of level 6, the adaptive filter, and no chunk.
- `function encode(img: image.Image, options: EncodeOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `png.encode(img, options)`: `img` as a PNG file: colour type 0, 2, 4 or 6 as its format has gray or colour and alpha or not, 8 or 16 bits as it holds them, not interlaced. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_indexed(ix: image.Indexed, options: EncodeOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `png.encode_indexed(ix, options)`: `ix` as a PNG file of colour type 3: its palette in `PLTE`, alpha in `tRNS` where an entry is not opaque, and the fewest bits an index needs, 1, 2, 4 or 8, for the palette's count. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Text(keyword: str, text: str)`: One text of a PNG file: a keyword and its text.
- `function texts_of(chunks: [Chunk], limit: i64) -> [Text]?`, called `png.texts_of(chunks, limit)`: The texts of the `tEXt`, `zTXt` and `iTXt` chunks among `chunks`, in their order, their Latin-1 read as UTF-8 and their compression undone. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function text_chunk(keyword: str, text: str) -> Chunk?`, called `png.text_chunk(keyword: keyword, text: text)`: A chunk holding `text` under `keyword`: `tEXt` where the text is ASCII, `iTXt` otherwise, uncompressed, before the image data. Fails `invalid`.


### retries

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/retries`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/retries/).

The waits of a retry loop and circuit breakers: how long a program waits before it tries a failed call again, spread by chance so that clients that failed together do not try again together, when it gives up, and the wait an HTTP `Retry-After` asks; and a breaker that stops calling a service that keeps failing, then lets a trial through.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a policy or an argument outside its bounds, and of a `Retry-After` value that is neither seconds nor a date; the message names the number or the text.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a retry loop whose attempts allowed are all made: `next_wait` fails with it.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a retry loop whose next wait would end past the total time allowed: `next_wait` fails with it.
- `variant Jitter = .none | .full | .equal | .decorrelated | .spread(factor: f64)`: How a wait between two attempts is spread by chance, so that clients that failed together do not try again together.
- `record Backoff(first: time.Duration, multiplier: f64, longest: time.Duration, jitter: Jitter, attempts: i64, total: time.Duration)`: How the waits of a retry loop grow, how chance spreads them, and when the loop gives up.
- `record Retry(policy: Backoff, failures: i64, last_wait: time.Duration)`: Where a retry loop stands: the policy, the failures counted, the last wait.
- `function backoff(first: time.Duration, multiplier: f64, longest: time.Duration) -> Backoff?`, called `retries.backoff(first: first, multiplier, longest: longest)`: A policy of exponential waits: `first` after the first failure, each next one `multiplier` times the one before, none longer than `longest`; no jitter, and no limit until `with_attempts` or `with_total` sets one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_jitter(policy: Backoff, jitter: Jitter) -> Backoff?`, called `retries.with_jitter(policy, jitter)`: `policy` with its waits spread by `jitter`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_attempts(policy: Backoff, attempts: i64) -> Backoff?`, called `retries.with_attempts(policy, attempts)`: `policy` giving up once `attempts` attempts in all are made. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_total(policy: Backoff, total: time.Duration) -> Backoff?`, called `retries.with_total(policy, total)`: `policy` giving up where the next wait would end more than `total` after the first attempt began, as cenkalti/backoff's `MaxElapsedTime` does. Fails `invalid`.
- `function wait_after(policy: Backoff, failures: i64, previous: time.Duration, fraction: f64) -> time.Duration?`, called `retries.wait_after(policy, failures, previous, fraction)`: The wait after `failures` failures in a row: `first` times `multiplier` to the power `failures - 1`, at most `longest`, then spread by the policy's jitter from `fraction`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function drawn_wait(policy: Backoff, failures: i64, previous: time.Duration) -> time.Duration?`, called `retries.drawn_wait(policy, failures, previous)`: The wait after `failures` failures in a row, as `wait_after` answers it, its fraction drawn by `random_fraction` where the policy's jitter reads one and nothing drawn where it does not: the wait a program that retries sleeps, with no fraction of its own to give. Fails `invalid`.
- `function random_fraction() -> f64?`, called `retries.random_fraction()`: A number from 0 up to 1, 1 left out, drawn from the system's generator for keys: the `fraction` `wait_after` and `next_wait` read, so that waits are spread unseen by any other program. Fails where `os.random_bytes` fails, with its code.
- `function new_retry(policy: Backoff) -> Retry`, called `retries.new_retry(policy)`: A retry loop about to make its first attempt under `policy`.
- `function next_wait(@retry: Retry, spent: time.Duration, fraction: f64) -> time.Duration?`, called `retries.next_wait(@retry, spent, fraction)`: The wait before the next attempt, once one more attempt has failed: the program sleeps it, then tries again. Fails `limit`, `timeout`, `invalid`.
- `function parse_retry_after(s: str, received: time.Instant, longest: time.Duration) -> time.Duration?`, called `retries.parse_retry_after(s, received, longest)`: The wait an HTTP `Retry-After` value asks for (RFC 9110, 10.2.3), from `received`, at most `longest`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record BreakerPolicy(failures: i64, open_for: time.Duration, trials: i64, successes: i64, ratio: f64, window: time.Duration, least_calls: i64)`: When a circuit breaker opens, how long it stays open, and what closes it.
- `variant BreakerState = .closed | .open(until: time.Instant) | .half_open`: Where a circuit breaker stands at an instant.
- `record Breaker(policy: BreakerPolicy, machine: circuit.Machine)`: A circuit breaker the program holds: its policy and what it has seen.
- `function breaker_policy(failures: i64, open_for: time.Duration) -> BreakerPolicy?`, called `retries.breaker_policy(failures, open_for)`: A policy that opens after `failures` failures in a row and stays open for `open_for`, then lets one trial through, whose success closes it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_trials(policy: BreakerPolicy, trials: i64, successes: i64) -> BreakerPolicy?`, called `retries.with_trials(policy, trials: trials, successes: successes)`: `policy` letting `trials` trial calls through while half-open, closing after `successes` of them succeed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_failure_ratio(policy: BreakerPolicy, ratio: f64, window: time.Duration, least_calls: i64) -> BreakerPolicy?`, called `retries.with_failure_ratio(policy, ratio, window, least_calls)`: `policy` also opening where, in the last `window`, at least `least_calls` calls were recorded and at least `ratio` of them failed, as Polly's breaker reads its failure ratio. Fails `invalid`.
- `function new_breaker(policy: BreakerPolicy) -> Breaker`, called `retries.new_breaker(policy)`: A closed breaker following `policy`, having seen nothing.
- `function allow_call(@breaker: Breaker, at: time.Instant) -> bool`, called `retries.allow_call(@breaker, at)`: Whether a call may go at the instant `at`: always while closed; never while open, until its open time has passed, when it turns half-open and lets the first trial through; while half-open, while trials are left.
- `function record_success(@breaker: Breaker, at: time.Instant)`, called `retries.record_success(@breaker, at)`: The call let through by `allow_call` succeeded, ending at the instant `at`: while closed, the failures in a row end; while half-open, enough successes close it; while open, nothing changes.
- `function record_failure(@breaker: Breaker, at: time.Instant)`, called `retries.record_failure(@breaker, at)`: The call let through by `allow_call` failed, ending at the instant `at`: while closed, it is counted, and the breaker opens where the failures in a row or the share of the window reach the policy's; while half-open, it opens again; while open, nothing changes.
- `function breaker_state(breaker: Breaker, at: time.Instant) -> BreakerState`, called `retries.breaker_state(breaker, at)`: Where `breaker` stands at the instant `at`, changing nothing: an open breaker whose open time has passed reads as half-open, though no call has asked yet.


### compress/zstd

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/compress/zstd`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/zstd/).

Zstandard (RFC 8878) compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: every frame read, its blocks stored, repeated or compressed with Huffman-coded literals and FSE-coded sequences, its checksum checked, skippable frames passed over, with or without a dictionary; and frames written at a basic level.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input that is not Zstandard (a wrong magic, a reserved bit set, a table no decoder reads, an offset before the start, a size or checksum that does not match, a frame cut short, bytes after its end, a frame made with another dictionary), the message naming the byte; and of options out of their range.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The code of an output that would pass the `limit` the caller set.
- `constant MIN_LEVEL: i64`, value `1`: The fastest level: two earlier places tried for each byte.
- `constant DEFAULT_LEVEL: i64`, value `3`: The level `default_options` sets, as the `zstd` tool's and Python's.
- `constant MAX_LEVEL: i64`, value `22`: The level that tries most: 2,048 earlier places for each byte.
- `record Options(level: i64, checksum: bool, content_size: bool)`: How `compress` and `compress_with` write a frame.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `zstd.default_options()`: Options at level 3, the size said and no checksum, as Python's usual.
- `function compress(data: [u8], options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `zstd.compress(data, options)`: `data` compressed whole into one Zstandard frame. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `zstd.decompress(data, limit)`: The bytes `data` decompresses to: every frame of it one after another, skippable frames passed over. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `record Leading(data: [u8], used: i64)`: What `decompress_leading` answers: a frame's bytes, and where it ended.
- `function decompress_leading(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> Leading?`, called `zstd.decompress_leading(data, limit)`: The frame at the start of `data` decompressed, and how many bytes of `data` it took. Fails as `decompress` does, but never for bytes after the frame.
- `variant ContentSize = .known(bytes: u64) | .unknown`: How many bytes a frame says it decompresses to.
- `record FrameInfo(content_size: ContentSize, window_size: u64, dictionary_id: u32, has_checksum: bool, is_skippable: bool)`: What a frame's header says, read without decompressing it.
- `function frame_info(data: [u8]) -> FrameInfo?`, called `zstd.frame_info(data)`: What the header of the frame at the start of `data` says. Fails `invalid`.
- `function frame_size(data: [u8]) -> i64?`, called `zstd.frame_size(data)`: How many bytes the frame at the start of `data` takes, its blocks walked and not decoded: where the next frame begins. Fails `invalid`.
- `function skippable_frame(data: [u8], magic: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `zstd.skippable_frame(data, magic)`: `data` wrapped in a skippable frame, which every reader passes over: a place for the program's own bytes beside Zstandard frames. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Dictionary(state: frame.Dict)`: A dictionary: bytes a compressor and a decompressor both hold, which the data is likely to repeat, and, for one `zstd --train` made, the tables and offsets its frames start with.
- `function new_dictionary(data: [u8]) -> Dictionary?`, called `zstd.new_dictionary(data)`: The dictionary `data` holds: one `zstd --train` wrote, which begins with 37 A4 30 EC, its id, tables and offsets read; or any other bytes, taken as the content of a dictionary of no id. Fails `invalid`.
- `function new_raw_dictionary(content: [u8]) -> Dictionary`, called `zstd.new_raw_dictionary(content)`: `content` as the content of a dictionary of no id and no table, even where it begins as a formatted one: what Python calls a raw dictionary or a prefix.
- `function id_of(d: Dictionary) -> u32`, called `zstd.id_of(d)`: The id of `d`, 0 for a raw one.
- `function content_of(d: Dictionary) -> [u8]`, called `zstd.content_of(d)`: The content of `d`: the bytes repeats may reach back into.
- `function decompress_with(data: [u8], dictionary: Dictionary, limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `zstd.decompress_with(data, dictionary, limit)`: The bytes `data` decompresses to, its frames read with `dictionary`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compress_with(data: [u8], dictionary: Dictionary, options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `zstd.compress_with(data, dictionary, options)`: `data` compressed into one frame that reaches back into `dictionary`'s content and names its id. Fails `invalid`.


### compress/brotli

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/compress/brotli`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/brotli/).

Brotli (RFC 7932) compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: every stream read whole, its meta-blocks stored or compressed, block types and their switches, context modes and maps, every prefix code, the distances and the 121 transforms of the static dictionary's 122,784 bytes (carried here, so only the programs that use this package carry them); and streams written at a basic level.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input that is not Brotli (a reserved window, a prefix code that is not complete, a distance before the start, a count past the meta-block, fill bits that are not zeros, a stream cut short, bytes after its end), the message naming the byte; and of options out of their range.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The code of an output that would pass the `limit` the caller set.
- `constant MIN_QUALITY: i64`, value `0`: The quality that stores every meta-block as it is.
- `constant MAX_QUALITY: i64`, value `11`: The highest quality: 512 earlier places tried for each byte.
- `constant DEFAULT_QUALITY: i64`, value `11`: The quality `default_options` sets, the `brotli` tool's usual and the highest.
- `constant MIN_WINDOW_BITS: i64`, value `10`: The narrowest window: 2^10 - 16 bytes.
- `constant MAX_WINDOW_BITS: i64`, value `24`: The widest window RFC 7932 allows: 2^24 - 16 bytes.
- `record Options(quality: i64, window_bits: i64)`: How `compress` writes a stream.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `brotli.default_options()`: Options of quality 11 and a window of 22 bits, as the `brotli` tool's usual.
- `function compress(data: [u8], options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `brotli.compress(data, options)`: `data` compressed whole into one Brotli stream. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `brotli.decompress(data, limit)`: The bytes the Brotli stream `data` decompresses to. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `record Leading(data: [u8], used: i64)`: What `decompress_leading` answers: a stream's bytes, and where it ended.
- `function decompress_leading(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> Leading?`, called `brotli.decompress_leading(data, limit)`: The stream at the start of `data` decompressed, and how many bytes of `data` it took: Brotli has no header that says its length, so the stream itself says where it ends. Fails as `decompress` does, but never for bytes after the stream.


### compress/bzip2

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/compress/bzip2`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/bzip2/).

bzip2 compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: the Burrows-Wheeler transform, the move to front, the runs and the Huffman codes of Julian Seward's format, each block's CRC and the stream's.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input that is not bzip2 (a wrong header, a block no decoder reads, a CRC that does not match, a stream cut short, bytes after its end), the message naming the byte; and of a level out of its range.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The code of an output that would pass the `limit` the caller set.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `decoder.UNSUPPORTED`: The code of a block written in the randomised form of bzip2 0.9.0, which no compressor has written since 0.9.5 and which this package does not read, as Go's `compress/bzip2` does not.
- `constant MIN_LEVEL: i64`, value `1`: The smallest level: blocks of 100,000 bytes, the least memory.
- `constant MAX_LEVEL: i64`, value `9`: The largest level: blocks of 900,000 bytes.
- `constant DEFAULT_LEVEL: i64`, value `9`: The level `default_options` sets, the `bzip2` tool's usual and Python's, the largest.
- `record Options(level: i64)`: How `compress` writes a stream, as its siblings' `Options` say it of theirs.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `bzip2.default_options()`: Options at level 9, as the `bzip2` tool's and Python's usual.
- `function compress(data: [u8], options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `bzip2.compress(data, options)`: `data` compressed whole into one bzip2 stream, in blocks of `options.level` times 100,000 bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `bzip2.decompress(data, limit)`: The bytes `data` decompresses to: one bzip2 stream or several, one after another, as the `bzip2` tool writes them for files joined by `cat`. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Leading(data: [u8], used: i64)`: What `decompress_leading` answers: a stream's bytes, and where it ended.
- `function decompress_leading(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> Leading?`, called `bzip2.decompress_leading(data, limit)`: The stream at the start of `data` decompressed, and how many bytes of `data` it took: for a stream followed by something else. Fails as `decompress` does, but never for bytes after the stream.


### process

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/process`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/process/).

Another program run, fed, read and waited for: a command built as a record, run to its end with what it writes captured, or started as a child whose pipes are `io.Stream`s, waited for, asked to end or ended at once; a program looked up on PATH; a text quoted for a POSIX shell.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `codes.NOT_FOUND`: A program that is not there: a name in no folder of PATH, or a path that names nothing that runs.
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `codes.FILE_NOT_FOUND`: A command's working folder names nothing.
- `constant NOT_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `codes.NOT_A_DIRECTORY`: A command's working folder names what is no folder.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `codes.PERMISSION`: The system will not run the program for this one.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The input is not what the function reads: a zero byte in a word, a variable's name that names none, a time limit not above 0, a child given up already, a file that is no program; the message says which.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `codes.CLOSED`: A stream given to a child is closed.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `codes.TIMEOUT`: A child ran past its command's time limit and was ended.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The system has no process or descriptor left, or a command holds more than 4,096 arguments or variables.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `codes.UNSUPPORTED`: This platform has no such thing: a request to end a child on Windows, a script holding `"` for Windows' shell.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `codes.NOT_TEXT`: A child's output read as text is not UTF-8.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `codes.FAILED`: A child did not end with the exit code 0, or the system refused for a reason none of the other codes names; the message says which.
- `variant Input = .parent | .nothing | .pipe | .stream(stream: io.Stream) | .bytes(data: [u8]) | .text(text: str)`: What a child's input is: this process's, nothing, a pipe, a stream the program holds, or bytes given whole.
- `variant Output = .parent | .nothing | .pipe | .stream(stream: io.Stream)`: Where a child's output or its error goes: this process's, nowhere, a pipe, or a stream the program holds.
- `variant Limit = .none | .after(limit: time.Duration)`: How long a child may run: without end, or a time from its start.
- `variant Group = .parent | .own | .joined(leader: hero_proc.Proc)`: Which process group a child starts in (POSIX): the group is what Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z at the terminal reach, what `send_group_signal` sends to and what `give_terminal` puts in front, so a shell starts each job in a group of its own and hands it the terminal.
- `record Command(program: str, arguments: [str], env_inherited: bool, env_set: {str: str}, env_removed: [str], dir: str, input: Input, output: Output, error: Output, error_to_output: bool, time_limit: Limit, group: Group)`: A program to run, with its arguments, its environment, its working folder, what each of its three standard streams is, how long it may run and the process group it starts in.
- `variant Status = .exited(code: i64) | .signaled(signal: i64) | .timed_out`: How a child ended: by itself with an exit code, by a signal on POSIX, or at its command's time limit.
- `record CpuTime(user: time.Duration, system: time.Duration)`: The CPU time a child used once it has ended: its own, and on POSIX that of the children it waited for.
- `record Finished(status: Status, output: [u8], error: [u8], cpu: CpuTime)`: What `run` answers: how the child ended, what it wrote where its command asked for a pipe, and the CPU time it used.
- `variant State = .running | .stopped(signal: i64) | .ended(status: Status, cpu: CpuTime)`: Where a started child stands: running, stopped by a signal, or seen to have ended.
- `record Child(handle: hero_proc.Proc, command: Command, id: i64, input: io.Stream, output: io.Stream, error: io.Stream, started: i64, state: State)`: A child `start` began: its process, the program's ends of its pipes, and what is known of its end.
- `function command(program: str, arguments: [str]) -> Command`, called `process.command(program, arguments)`: A command that runs `program` with `arguments`, with this process's variables, working folder, three standard streams and process group, and no time limit.
- `function shell(script: str) -> Command?`, called `process.shell(script)`: A command that runs `script` through the system's shell: `/bin/sh -c script` on POSIX, and `cmd.exe /d /s /c script` on Windows. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function with_arguments(c: Command, arguments: [str]) -> Command`, called `process.with_arguments(c, arguments)`: `c` with `arguments` in place of its own.
- `function with_env(c: Command, name: str, value: str) -> Command`, called `process.with_env(c, name: name, value: value)`: `c` with the variable `name` set to `value` for its child, over the variables the child starts from, in place of one of that name.
- `function with_env_all(c: Command, variables: {str: str}) -> Command`, called `process.with_env_all(c, variables)`: `c` with every one of `variables` set for its child as `with_env` sets one, in the map's order.
- `function with_env_removed(c: Command, name: str) -> Command`, called `process.with_env_removed(c, name)`: `c` with the variable `name` out of its child's environment, whether `with_env` set it or it would come from this process's.
- `function with_env_cleared(c: Command) -> Command`, called `process.with_env_cleared(c)`: `c` whose child starts with no variable at all but those `with_env` sets after this call.
- `function env_of(c: Command) -> {str: str}?`, called `process.env_of(c)`: The variables `c`'s child would start with, name to value: this process's as they stand now, or none, with the command's changes made. Fails `not_text`.
- `function with_dir(c: Command, dir: str) -> Command`, called `process.with_dir(c, dir)`: `c` with its child working in `dir`.
- `function with_input(c: Command, from: Input) -> Command`, called `process.with_input(c, from)`: `c` with `from` as its child's input.
- `function with_output(c: Command, to: Output) -> Command`, called `process.with_output(c, to)`: `c` with its child's output going to `to`.
- `function with_error(c: Command, to: Output) -> Command`, called `process.with_error(c, to)`: `c` with its child's error going to `to`, and no longer to its output.
- `function with_error_to_output(c: Command) -> Command`, called `process.with_error_to_output(c)`: `c` with its child's error going wherever its output goes, the two interleaved in the order the child writes them.
- `function with_time_limit(c: Command, limit: time.Duration) -> Command`, called `process.with_time_limit(c, limit)`: `c` whose child may run `limit` from its start, and is ended at once past it.
- `function with_own_group(c: Command) -> Command`, called `process.with_own_group(c)`: `c` whose child starts as the leader of a process group of its own (POSIX): Ctrl-C at the terminal no longer reaches it with this process, and `send_group_signal` and `give_terminal` name its group.
- `function with_group_of(c: Command, leader: Child) -> Command`, called `process.with_group_of(c, leader)`: `c` whose child starts in the process group `leader` stands in (POSIX), as a shell starts a pipeline's later programs in its first one's group.
- `function run(c: Command) -> Finished?`, called `process.run(c)`: How `c`'s child ended and what it wrote, once it has ended: started, fed, waited for, and what it wrote to its pipes read whole. Fails `not_found`, `file_not_found`, `not_a_directory`, `permission`, `invalid`, `closed`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `function capture(c: Command) -> str?`, called `process.capture(c)`: The text `c`'s child writes to its output, once it has ended with the exit code 0. Fails `failed`, `timeout`, `not_text`.
- `function start(c: Command) -> Child?`, called `process.start(c)`: A child running `c`, begun and not waited for: the program writes to its input and reads its output and its error through the `io.Stream`s of the answer, then ends it with `wait`, or gives it up with `release`. Fails as `run` does.
- `function wait(@child: Child) -> Status?`, called `process.wait(@child)`: How `child` ended, waiting for it. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function has_ended(@child: Child) -> bool?`, called `process.has_ended(@child)`: Whether `child` has ended, never waiting for it: `true` once it has, its status kept for `wait`. Fails as `wait` does.
- `function terminate(child: Child) -> ()?`, called `process.terminate(child)`: Asks `child` to end: SIGTERM on POSIX, which a program may catch to end cleanly, or not end at all. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function kill(child: Child) -> ()?`, called `process.kill(child)`: Ends `child` at once: SIGKILL on POSIX, and on Windows the end of its process with the exit code 1. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function release(@child: Child) -> ()?`, called `process.release(@child)`: Gives `child` up: every end of its pipes the program did not close is closed and its process given back, so nothing of it is the program's. Fails with the code of the first end that could not be closed; the rest is given up either way.
- `function cpu_of(child: Child) -> CpuTime?`, called `process.cpu_of(child)`: The CPU time `child` used, once `wait` or `has_ended` has seen it end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function usage_of(child: Child) -> os.ProcessUsage?`, called `process.usage_of(child)`: What `child` holds and has spent now, while it runs: its resident and virtual memory and the processor time it has used, as `os.process_usage` reads a process. Fails `invalid`.
- `function state_of(@child: Child) -> State?`, called `process.state_of(@child)`: Where `child` stands now, never waiting: running, stopped by a signal, or ended, a stop and a going on seen as well as an end, as a shell asks of each job before its prompt. Fails as `wait` does.
- `function wait_or_stop(@child: Child) -> State?`, called `process.wait_or_stop(@child)`: How `child` ended, or the signal that stopped it, waiting for the first of the two: what a shell waits for of the job it runs in front, which Ctrl-Z stops. Fails as `wait` does.
- `function wait_or_signal(@child: Child) -> State?`, called `process.wait_or_signal(@child)`: How `child` ended, the signal that stopped it, or `.running` where a signal the program counts came first: the first of the three, as a shell's `fg` and `wait` end on Ctrl-C as well as on Ctrl-Z, with nothing asked at intervals. Fails as `wait` does.
- `function send_signal(child: Child, signal: os.Signal) -> ()?`, called `process.send_signal(child, signal)`: Sends `signal` to `child` alone: a stop, a going on, Ctrl-C's, or any other signal `os.Signal` names (POSIX). Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function send_group_signal(child: Child, signal: os.Signal) -> ()?`, called `process.send_group_signal(child, signal)`: Sends `signal` to every process of the group `child` stands in, its own children included: what a shell sends a job to stop it, continue it or end it (POSIX). Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function give_terminal(child: Child, terminal: io.Stream) -> ()?`, called `process.give_terminal(child, terminal)`: Puts the group `child` stands in in front at the terminal `terminal`, so Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Z and the terminal's reads reach that group and not this process: what a shell does for the job it runs in front (POSIX). Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function take_terminal(terminal: io.Stream) -> ()?`, called `process.take_terminal(terminal)`: Puts this process's own group in front at `terminal` again: what a shell does once the job it ran in front ended or stopped (POSIX). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function holds_terminal(terminal: io.Stream) -> bool?`, called `process.holds_terminal(terminal)`: Whether this process's own group is in front at `terminal`: a shell takes job control only where it holds its terminal (POSIX). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function is_success(status: Status) -> bool`, called `process.is_success(status)`: Whether `status` says the child ended by itself with the exit code 0.
- `function code_of(status: Status) -> i64?`, called `process.code_of(status)`: The exit code `status` holds. Fails `not_found`.
- `function signal_of(status: Status) -> i64?`, called `process.signal_of(status)`: The number of the signal that ended the child, on POSIX. Fails `not_found`.
- `function require_success(status: Status) -> ()?`, called `process.require_success(status)`: Nothing, where `status` says the child ended by itself with the exit code 0. Fails `failed`, `timeout`.
- `function format_status(status: Status) -> str`, called `process.format_status(status)`: `status` as words to show: `exited with code 3`, `ended by signal 9`, or `ended at its time limit`.
- `function path_of(program: str) -> str?`, called `process.path_of(program)`: Where `start` finds `program`: `program` itself where it holds a separator and names a file that runs, else the first file named `program` that runs in the folders the search reads. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function quote(word: str) -> str`, called `process.quote(word)`: `word` as a POSIX shell reads it back whole: as it is where it holds only ASCII letters, digits and `@%+=:,./-_`, else between single quotes, each `'` in it written `'"'"'`.
- `function quote_all(words: [str]) -> str`, called `process.quote_all(words)`: Every one of `words` put through `quote`, joined with one space: a line a POSIX shell reads back as those words.


### compress/lz4

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/compress/lz4`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/lz4/).

LZ4 compressed and decompressed: its blocks bare, and its frames (the magic 04 22 4D 18, a header, blocks of up to 64 KiB to 4 MiB that stand alone or reach back into the blocks before them, an xxHash32 checksum of each block and of the content, the content's size, a dictionary's id), all at once over a `[u8]`, piece by piece in memory, or through an `io.Stream`; skippable frames passed over, and legacy frames read and written.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input that is not LZ4 (a wrong magic, a reserved bit set, a block size no reader takes, a repeat reaching before the start or an offset of 0, a checksum or size that does not match, a block or frame cut short, bytes after the last frame), the message naming the byte; and of options and arguments out of their range.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The code of an output that would pass the `limit` the caller set: what an input that expands without measure answers.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `codes.CLOSED`: The code of a `Writer` written, flushed or finished after `finish`.
- `constant MIN_LEVEL: i64`, value `-65536`: The fastest level: the fast compressor skipping 65,537 bytes ahead at once where it finds no repeat, as `lz4 --fast=65536`.
- `constant DEFAULT_LEVEL: i64`, value `1`: The level `default_options` sets, as the `lz4` tool's: the fast compressor, one earlier place tried for each byte.
- `constant MIN_HIGH_LEVEL: i64`, value `3`: The first level of high compression: from it on, a chain of earlier places is tried for each byte, 16 at this level.
- `constant MAX_LEVEL: i64`, value `12`: The level that compresses most and most slowly: 8,192 earlier places tried for each byte.
- `variant BlockSize = .max_64_kib | .max_256_kib | .max_1_mib | .max_4_mib`: The most bytes a block of a frame decompresses to, which a reader of the frame holds at once.
- `record Options(level: i64, block_size: BlockSize, linked: bool, block_checksum: bool, content_checksum: bool, content_size: bool, dictionary: [u8], dictionary_id: u32)`: How `compress`, `compressor`, `writer` and `compress_stream` write a frame.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `lz4.default_options()`: The `lz4` tool's options: level 1, blocks of 4 MiB that stand alone, a content checksum, no block checksum, no size, no dictionary.
- `function compress(data: [u8], options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress(data, options)`: `data` compressed whole into one frame, as `options` says. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress(data, limit)`: The bytes `data` decompresses to: every frame of it one after another, legacy frames read, skippable frames passed over. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function decompress_with(data: [u8], dictionary: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress_with(data: data, dictionary: dictionary, limit)`: The bytes `data` decompresses to, its frames read with `dictionary` before each. Fails as `decompress` does.
- `record Leading(data: [u8], used: i64)`: What `decompress_leading` answers: a frame's bytes, and where it ended.
- `function decompress_leading(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> Leading?`, called `lz4.decompress_leading(data, limit)`: The frame at the start of `data` decompressed, and how many bytes of `data` it took. Fails as `decompress` does, but never for bytes after the frame.
- `variant ContentSize = .known(bytes: u64) | .unknown`: How many bytes a frame says it decompresses to.
- `variant FrameKind = .standard | .skippable(magic: i64) | .legacy`: Which of LZ4's three kinds of frame a frame is.
- `record FrameInfo(kind: FrameKind, content_size: ContentSize, block_bytes: i64, linked: bool, block_checksum: bool, content_checksum: bool, dictionary_id: u32, header_size: i64)`: What a frame's header says, read without decompressing it.
- `function frame_info(data: [u8]) -> FrameInfo?`, called `lz4.frame_info(data)`: What the header of the frame at the start of `data` says. Fails `invalid`.
- `function frame_size(data: [u8]) -> i64?`, called `lz4.frame_size(data)`: How many bytes the frame at the start of `data` takes, its blocks walked and not decoded: where the next frame begins. Fails `invalid`.
- `function skippable_frame(data: [u8], magic: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.skippable_frame(data, magic)`: `data` wrapped in a skippable frame, which every reader passes over: a place for the program's own bytes beside LZ4 frames. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compress_legacy(data: [u8], level: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress_legacy(data, level)`: `data` compressed whole into one legacy frame, as `lz4 -l` writes it: blocks of 8 MiB that stand alone, each compressed, with no checksum and no end mark. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compress_block(data: [u8], level: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress_block(data, level)`: `data` compressed into one bare LZ4 block: no magic, no size, no checksum. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compress_block_with(data: [u8], dictionary: [u8], level: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress_block_with(data: data, dictionary: dictionary, level)`: `data` compressed into one bare block that may repeat bytes of the last 65,536 of `dictionary`, which are not written. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress_block(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress_block(data, limit)`: The bytes one bare block decompresses to. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function decompress_block_with(data: [u8], dictionary: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress_block_with(data: data, dictionary: dictionary, limit)`: The bytes one bare block decompresses to, its repeats reaching back into `dictionary`. Fails as `decompress_block` does.
- `function compress_sized(data: [u8], level: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress_sized(data, level)`: `data` compressed into one block led by its length in four bytes, little end first: Python's `lz4.block.compress` and Rust's `compress_prepend_size` write this form. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compress_sized_with(data: [u8], dictionary: [u8], level: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress_sized_with(data: data, dictionary: dictionary, level)`: `data` compressed into one block led by its length, its repeats reaching back into `dictionary`. Fails as `compress_sized` does.
- `function decompress_sized(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress_sized(data, limit)`: The bytes a block led by its length decompresses to: exactly that many. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function decompress_sized_with(data: [u8], dictionary: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress_sized_with(data: data, dictionary: dictionary, limit)`: The bytes a block led by its length decompresses to, its repeats reaching back into `dictionary`. Fails as `decompress_sized` does.
- `function block_bound(size: i64) -> i64?`, called `lz4.block_bound(size)`: The most bytes `compress_block` answers for `size` bytes: `size`, one more for every 255, and 16. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Compressor(state: framer.State)`: A compressor of one frame fed piece by piece, holding the block in progress and, for linked blocks, the 64 KiB before it: made by `compressor`, fed by `compress_part`, pushed by `compress_flush`, ended by `compress_end`.
- `function compressor(options: Options) -> Compressor?`, called `lz4.compressor(options)`: A compressor that writes a frame as `options` says, its header ready to be handed out by the first call that answers bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_size(c: Compressor, size: u64) -> Compressor?`, called `lz4.with_size(c, size)`: A copy of `c` whose frame header says it decompresses to `size` bytes, which a reader checks. Fails `invalid`.
- `function compress_part(@c: Compressor, data: [u8]) -> [u8]`, called `lz4.compress_part(@c, data)`: The compressed bytes ready after feeding `data` to `c`: the header the first time, and every block filled; often nothing else.
- `function compress_flush(@c: Compressor) -> [u8]`, called `lz4.compress_flush(@c)`: The compressed bytes that let everything fed to `c` so far be decompressed: the block in progress written, shorter than the most.
- `function compress_end(@c: Compressor) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.compress_end(@c)`: The last compressed bytes of `c`: its last block, the end mark and the content checksum. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_compressor_ended(c: Compressor) -> bool`, called `lz4.is_compressor_ended(c)`: Whether `compress_end` has ended `c`.
- `record Decompressor(state: unframer.State)`: A decompressor fed piece by piece, holding the input not yet read, the 64 KiB a block may reach back into and the output not yet handed out: made by `decompressor`, fed by `decompress_part`.
- `function decompressor(limit: i64) -> Decompressor`, called `lz4.decompressor(limit)`: A decompressor of one frame that may produce at most `limit` bytes.
- `function with_dictionary(d: Decompressor, dictionary: [u8]) -> Decompressor?`, called `lz4.with_dictionary(d, dictionary)`: A copy of `d` that reads frames made with `dictionary`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress_part(@d: Decompressor, data: [u8], most: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.decompress_part(@d, data, most)`: Up to `most` decompressed bytes, after feeding `data` to `d`: fewer where the input fed so far gives fewer, and none at the frame's end. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function is_decompressor_ended(d: Decompressor) -> bool`, called `lz4.is_decompressor_ended(d)`: Whether `d`'s frame has ended, its checksum read, and every byte of it handed out.
- `function unused(d: Decompressor) -> [u8]`, called `lz4.unused(d)`: The bytes fed to `d` after the end of its frame: the rest of the input, where another frame or other data may begin.
- `record Writer(to: io.Stream, compressor: Compressor)`: A writer of one compressed frame to a stream: what is written to it reaches `to` compressed.
- `function writer(to: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Writer?`, called `lz4.writer(to, options)`: A writer to `to` that compresses as `options` says; nothing is written until the first `write`, `flush` or `finish`. Fails as `compressor` does.
- `function write(@w: Writer, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `lz4.write(@w, data)`: Compresses `data` into `w`, writing to its stream every block filled. Fails `closed`.
- `function flush(@w: Writer) -> ()?`, called `lz4.flush(@w)`: Writes to `w`'s stream the block in progress, so that everything written so far can be decompressed; the writer goes on after it. Fails `closed`.
- `function finish(@w: Writer) -> ()?`, called `lz4.finish(@w)`: Writes `w`'s last block, end mark and checksum to its stream. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `record Reader(from: io.Stream, decompressor: Decompressor)`: A reader of the decompressed bytes of a stream: it reads the compressed stream 65,536 bytes at a time, as it needs them, every frame one after another.
- `function reader(from: io.Stream, limit: i64) -> Reader`, called `lz4.reader(from, limit)`: A reader of the frames `from` holds, which may decompress to at most `limit` bytes in all.
- `function read(@r: Reader, most: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.read(@r, most)`: Up to `most` decompressed bytes of `r`, reading its stream as needed: fewer where the stream gives fewer at once, and none at its end. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function read_rest(@r: Reader) -> [u8]?`, called `lz4.read_rest(@r)`: Every decompressed byte of `r` from where it stands to the stream's end. Fails as `read` does; the bytes read before a failure are lost.
- `function compress_stream(from: io.Stream, to: io.Stream, options: Options) -> i64?`, called `lz4.compress_stream(from: from, to: to, options)`: Compresses everything `from` holds, to its end, into one frame written to `to`, and answers how many compressed bytes it wrote. Fails as `compressor` does, and as `io.read` and `io.write` fail; the bytes written before stay written.
- `function decompress_stream(from: io.Stream, to: io.Stream, limit: i64) -> i64?`, called `lz4.decompress_stream(from: from, to: to, limit)`: Decompresses every frame `from` holds, to its end, into `to`, and answers how many bytes it wrote. Fails as `read` does, and as `io.write` fails; the bytes written before stay written.


### compress/xz

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/compress/xz`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/compress/xz/).

xz and LZMA compressed and decompressed, all at once over a `[u8]`: the xz container (its blocks, index, footer and checks, several streams one after another with their padding) holding LZMA2 data, and the older `.lzma` format of a header and LZMA data.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input that is not xz or `.lzma` (a wrong header, a block or index whose CRC-32 does not match, a check that does not match its bytes, a size that is not the one the container says, LZMA data no decoder reads, a stream cut short, bytes after its end), the message naming the byte; and of options out of their range.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The code of an output that would pass the `limit` the caller set.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `filters.UNSUPPORTED`: The code of a block filtered by a branch converter or by a filter this package does not know, and of a check this format reserves asked of by `check_of`.
- `constant MIN_LEVEL: i64`, value `0`: The fastest level: a dictionary of 256 KiB, four earlier places tried for each byte.
- `constant DEFAULT_LEVEL: i64`, value `6`: The level `default_options` sets, as the `xz` tool's and Python's: a dictionary of 8 MiB.
- `constant MAX_LEVEL: i64`, value `9`: The level that compresses most: a dictionary of 64 MiB, 512 earlier places tried for each byte.
- `variant Check = .none | .crc32 | .crc64 | .sha256`: What an xz stream checks its blocks' bytes with.
- `record Options(level: i64, check: Check)`: How `compress` writes an xz stream.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `xz.default_options()`: Options at level 6 with a CRC-64 check, as the `xz` tool's and Python's usual.
- `function compress(data: [u8], options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `xz.compress(data, options)`: `data` compressed whole into one xz stream of one LZMA2 block, or of none where `data` is empty. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `xz.decompress(data, limit)`: The bytes `data` decompresses to: one xz stream or several, one after another, with stream padding (zero bytes in fours) between and after them. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Leading(data: [u8], used: i64)`: What `decompress_leading` and `decompress_lzma_leading` answer: a stream's bytes, and where it ended.
- `function decompress_leading(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> Leading?`, called `xz.decompress_leading(data, limit)`: The xz stream at the start of `data` decompressed, and how many bytes of `data` it took. Fails as `decompress` does, but never for bytes after the stream.
- `function check_of(data: [u8]) -> Check?`, called `xz.check_of(data)`: The check the xz stream at the start of `data` writes after each block, read from its header. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function compress_lzma(data: [u8], level: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `xz.compress_lzma(data, level)`: `data` compressed whole into one `.lzma` stream: 13 bytes of header that say its size, then LZMA data. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decompress_lzma(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `xz.decompress_lzma(data, limit)`: The bytes the `.lzma` stream `data` decompresses to: its size said in its header, or ended by the end marker where the header says none. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function decompress_lzma_leading(data: [u8], limit: i64) -> Leading?`, called `xz.decompress_lzma_leading(data, limit)`: The `.lzma` stream at the start of `data` decompressed, and how many bytes of `data` it took. Fails as `decompress_lzma` does, but never for bytes after the stream.


### template/sanitized

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/template/sanitized`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/template/sanitized/).

A page of `template`'s HTML mode that places HTML from outside where its template says: each `clean` action writes the text its value names as markup, cleaned by an `html/sanitize` policy inside the element it lands in, so a note written in Markdown and made HTML, or a visitor's comment, stands in its layout as one template, inside a loop as anywhere, and runs nothing.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a value of a kind its place does not take, a `clean` action's that is not a text among them: `render` and `render_named` fail with it.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a value, a key or a template named that is not there: `render` and `render_named` fail with it.
- `function render(t: template.Template, value: json.Value, policy: sanitize.Policy) -> str?`, called `sanitized.render(t, value, policy)`: The text the main template of `t` makes of `value`, each `clean` action's text cleaned by `policy` inside the element it lands in. Fails `invalid`.
- `function render_named(t: template.Template, name: str, value: json.Value, policy: sanitize.Policy) -> str?`, called `sanitized.render_named(t, name, value, policy)`: The text the template of `t` named `name` makes of `value`, each `clean` action's text cleaned by `policy` inside the element it lands in. Fails `not_found`.


### ical

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/ical`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ical/).

iCalendar (RFC 5545), the format every calendar program imports and exports, and the content lines it shares with vCard (RFC 6350).

- `record Param(name: str, values: [str])`: A parameter of a content line: `TZID=Europe/Rome`, `PARTSTAT=ACCEPTED`.
- `record Line(group: str?, name: str, params: [Param], value: str)`: One content line: a property with its parameters and its value.
- `record Component(name: str, lines: [Line], children: [Component])`: A component: `BEGIN:VEVENT` up to its `END:VEVENT`.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a document that is not what the format says.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of bytes that are not UTF-8.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a name or a value that is not there.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a document nested deeper than `MAX_DEPTH`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a form this package does not read.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a number past its type.
- `constant MAX_DEPTH: i64`, value `16`: The deepest nesting of components a document may have, a `VCALENDAR` inside nothing and a `VALARM` inside a `VEVENT` being three.
- `function parse_lines(text: str) -> [Line]?`, called `ical.parse_lines(text)`: The content lines of a document, unfolded and parsed, with no regard for `BEGIN` and `END`: what a vCard or a line-based format needs. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_lines(lines: [Line]) -> str?`, called `ical.format_lines(lines)`: The lines written, folded at 75 octets, each ending in CRLF. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse(text: str) -> [Component]?`, called `ical.parse(text)`: The components of a document: each `BEGIN` up to its `END`, with the lines and the components between them. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function decode(data: [u8]) -> [Component]?`, called `ical.decode(data)`: The components of a document read from bytes. Fails `not_text`.
- `function format(components: [Component]) -> str?`, called `ical.format(components)`: The components written as a document, each line folded, each ending in CRLF. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode(components: [Component]) -> [u8]?`, called `ical.encode(components)`: The components written as bytes. Fails as `format` does.
- `function escape_value(s: str) -> str?`, called `ical.escape_value(s)`: `s` escaped as the value of a `TEXT` property: a backslash, a semicolon and a comma take a backslash before them, and a line break is written `\n`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function unescape_value(s: str) -> str`, called `ical.unescape_value(s)`: The text a `TEXT` value holds: `\n` and `\N` read as a line feed, and a backslash before another character read as that character.
- `record Span(negative: bool, weeks: i64, days: i64, hours: i64, minutes: i64, seconds: i64)`: A length of time as RFC 5545 writes it: weeks, or days with hours, minutes and seconds.
- `variant When = .date(year: i64, month: i64, day: i64) | .floating(local: time.DateTime) | .utc(at: time.Instant) | .zoned(local: time.DateTime, zone: time.Zone)`: A date or a moment, as RFC 5545 says a property holds one.
- `function whens_of(line: Line, zones: [time.Zone]) -> [When]?`, called `ical.whens_of(line, zones)`: The moments a line holds, `DTSTART`, `DUE`, `EXDATE`, `RDATE` or any other of dates or date-times, one for each comma-separated value. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `does_not_fit`, `unsupported`.
- `function when_of(line: Line, zones: [time.Zone]) -> When?`, called `ical.when_of(line, zones)`: The moment a line holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function when_line(name: str, when: When) -> Line?`, called `ical.when_line(name, when)`: The line a moment is written as. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_span(s: str) -> Span?`, called `ical.parse_span(s)`: The span `P15DT5H0M20S` or `-PT15M` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_span(span: Span) -> str`, called `ical.format_span(span)`: The text of a span.
- `function add_span(when: When, span: Span) -> When?`, called `ical.add_span(when, span)`: A moment moved by a span. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function instant_of(when: When, floating: time.Zone) -> time.Instant?`, called `ical.instant_of(when, floating)`: The instant a moment is. Fails `does_not_fit`.
- `variant Freq = .secondly | .minutely | .hourly | .daily | .weekly | .monthly | .yearly`: How often a rule repeats: the unit of its periods.
- `variant DayRule = .every(day: time.Weekday) | .nth(day: time.Weekday, n: i64)`: One entry of a rule's `by_day`.
- `variant End = .forever | .count(n: i64) | .until(when: When)`: Where a rule ends.
- `record Recur(freq: Freq, interval: i64, end: End, by_second: [i64], by_minute: [i64], by_hour: [i64], by_day: [DayRule], by_month_day: [i64], by_year_day: [i64], by_week_no: [i64], by_month: [i64], by_set_pos: [i64], week_start: time.Weekday)`: A recurrence rule, the value of `RRULE` (RFC 5545 section 3.3.10).
- `function recur(freq: Freq) -> Recur`, called `ical.recur(freq)`: A rule that repeats at `freq` and names nothing else: every period, forever, the weeks beginning on Monday.
- `function parse_recur(s: str) -> Recur?`, called `ical.parse_recur(s)`: The rule `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE` writes. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_recur(rule: Recur) -> str?`, called `ical.format_recur(rule)`: The text of a rule. Fails `invalid`.
- `function expand(rule: Recur, start: When, after: time.Instant, before: time.Instant, floating: time.Zone, max: i64) -> [When]?`, called `ical.expand(rule, start, after: after, before: before, floating, max)`: The occurrences of a rule that fall in a window. Fails `limit`, `does_not_fit`.
- `record Person(address: str, name: str?, params: [Param])`: A person or a place named by a calendar address: an `ORGANIZER`, an `ATTENDEE`, a `CONTACT`.
- `variant Status = .tentative | .confirmed | .cancelled | .needs_action | .completed | .in_process | .draft | .final`: The status of an event, a to-do or a journal entry; each component allows some of the cases, and a component read or written with another is `invalid`.
- `variant Trigger = .relative(span: Span, from_end: bool) | .absolute(at: time.Instant)`: When an alarm sounds.
- `record Alarm(action: str, trigger: Trigger, description: str?, summary: str?, repeat: i64?, duration: Span?, attendees: [Person], extra: [Line])`: A reminder, `VALARM`, inside an event or a to-do.
- `record Event(uid: str?, stamp: time.Instant?, created: time.Instant?, modified: time.Instant?, sequence: i64?, start: When?, end: When?, duration: Span?, summary: str?, description: str?, location: str?, url: str?, status: Status?, access: str?, transparency: str?, priority: i64?, categories: [str], organizer: Person?, attendees: [Person], rules: [Recur], rdates: [When], exdates: [When], recurrence_id: When?, alarms: [Alarm], extra: [Line], children: [Component])`: An event, `VEVENT`.
- `record Todo(uid: str?, stamp: time.Instant?, created: time.Instant?, modified: time.Instant?, sequence: i64?, start: When?, due: When?, duration: Span?, completed: time.Instant?, percent: i64?, summary: str?, description: str?, location: str?, url: str?, status: Status?, access: str?, priority: i64?, categories: [str], organizer: Person?, attendees: [Person], rules: [Recur], rdates: [When], exdates: [When], recurrence_id: When?, alarms: [Alarm], extra: [Line], children: [Component])`: A to-do, `VTODO`.
- `record Journal(uid: str?, stamp: time.Instant?, created: time.Instant?, modified: time.Instant?, sequence: i64?, start: When?, summary: str?, description: str?, status: Status?, access: str?, categories: [str], organizer: Person?, attendees: [Person], rules: [Recur], rdates: [When], exdates: [When], recurrence_id: When?, extra: [Line], children: [Component])`: A journal entry, `VJOURNAL`.
- `record Calendar(product_id: str, version: str, scale: str?, method: str?, events: [Event], todos: [Todo], journals: [Journal], zones: [time.Zone], extra: [Line], others: [Component])`: A calendar, `VCALENDAR`, with the events, to-dos and journal entries it holds.
- `function calendar_from(c: Component) -> Calendar?`, called `ical.calendar_from(c)`: The calendar a `VCALENDAR` component holds. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function parse_calendar(text: str) -> Calendar?`, called `ical.parse_calendar(text)`: The calendar a document holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_calendar(data: [u8]) -> Calendar?`, called `ical.decode_calendar(data)`: The calendar a document holds, read from bytes. Fails `not_text`.
- `function zone_from(c: Component) -> time.Zone?`, called `ical.zone_from(c)`: The zone a `VTIMEZONE` component defines. Fails `invalid`.
- `function timezone_component(zone: time.Zone, from_year: i64, to_year: i64) -> Component?`, called `ical.timezone_component(zone, from_year: from_year, to_year: to_year)`: A `VTIMEZONE` that defines `zone`, one observance for each change of offset between two years. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Occurrence(event: Event, start: When, start_at: time.Instant, end_at: time.Instant)`: One occurrence of an event: a moment it takes place.
- `function occurrences(cal: Calendar, after: time.Instant, before: time.Instant, floating: time.Zone, max: i64) -> [Occurrence]?`, called `ical.occurrences(cal, after: after, before: before, floating, max)`: The occurrences of a calendar's events that overlap a window, in order of start. Fails `limit`.
- `function calendar_to(cal: Calendar) -> Component?`, called `ical.calendar_to(cal)`: The component of a calendar. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_calendar(cal: Calendar) -> str?`, called `ical.format_calendar(cal)`: The calendar written as a document. Fails as `calendar_to` and `format` do.
- `function encode_calendar(cal: Calendar) -> [u8]?`, called `ical.encode_calendar(cal)`: The calendar written as bytes. Fails as `format_calendar` does.
- `function person(address: str) -> Person`, called `ical.person(address)`: A person with an address and nothing else.
- `function event(uid: str, stamp: time.Instant, start: When) -> Event`, called `ical.event(uid, stamp, start)`: An event with a `UID`, a stamp and a start, and nothing else; a program sets the fields it needs on it, `e.summary @ ok("Lunch")`.
- `function todo(uid: str, stamp: time.Instant) -> Todo`, called `ical.todo(uid, stamp)`: A to-do with a `UID` and a stamp and nothing else.
- `function journal(uid: str, stamp: time.Instant, start: When) -> Journal`, called `ical.journal(uid, stamp, start)`: A journal entry with a `UID`, a stamp and a start.
- `function alarm(action: str, trigger: Trigger) -> Alarm`, called `ical.alarm(action, trigger)`: An alarm that does `action` at `trigger`, with nothing else.
- `function calendar(product_id: str) -> Calendar`, called `ical.calendar(product_id)`: A calendar of version 2.0 holding nothing.


### barcode

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/barcode`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/barcode/).

Barcodes made: EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A and UPC-E with their two- and five-digit add-ons (ISO/IEC 15420 and the GS1 General Specifications), Code 128 and GS1-128 (ISO/IEC 15417), Data Matrix ECC 200 and GS1 Data Matrix (ISO/IEC 16022), and PDF417 and compact PDF417 (ISO/IEC 15438), each with its check characters or error correction and its quiet zones, and written as SVG text or drawn into an `image`, the digits a person reads set under a linear symbol's bars.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input the function does not read: a byte the symbology cannot write, a wrong check digit, a count of digits the symbology does not take, a scale below 1, a colour SVG cannot hold.
