- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `codes.UNSUPPORTED`: The code of data longer than the symbology holds: `gs1_128` past 48 characters; `data_matrix`, `data_matrix_bytes` and `gs1_data_matrix` past the size asked or the largest; `pdf417` and `pdf417_bytes` past 928 codewords or 90 rows.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of an image that would pass 16,384 pixels a side, which `to_image` and `to_image_with_text` answer.
- `variant Symbology = .ean13 | .ean8 | .upca | .upce | .code128 | .gs1_128 | .data_matrix | .gs1_data_matrix | .pdf417`: Which symbology a symbol is written in.
- `record Caption(text: str, center: f64, above: bool, small: bool)`: Text written with a symbol: the digits a person reads.
- `record Quiet(left: i64, right: i64, top: i64, bottom: i64)`: The light margin a reader needs around a symbol, in modules.
- `record Symbol(symbology: Symbology, rows: [[bool]], row_height: i64, guards: [bool], add_on: [bool], quiet: Quiet, captions: [Caption], text: str)`: A barcode made.
- `constant EAN13_HEIGHT: i64`, value `69`: How many modules tall the bars of an EAN-13, a UPC-A and a UPC-E are: 22.85 mm at a module of 0.33 mm, GS1's nominal size.
- `constant EAN8_HEIGHT: i64`, value `55`: How many modules tall the bars of an EAN-8 are: 18.23 mm at 0.33 mm.
- `function check_digit(digits: str) -> i64?`, called `barcode.check_digit(digits)`: The GS1 check digit of `digits`: from the right, every other digit counted three times beginning with the last, and the distance from the sum up to a multiple of ten. Fails `invalid`.
- `function ean13(digits: str) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.ean13(digits)`: The EAN-13 of `digits`: a GTIN-13, an ISBN or an ISSN's EAN form. Fails `invalid`.
- `function ean8(digits: str) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.ean8(digits)`: The EAN-8 of `digits`, a GTIN-8. Fails `invalid`.
- `function upca(digits: str) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.upca(digits)`: The UPC-A of `digits`, a GTIN-12. Fails `invalid`.
- `function upce(digits: str) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.upce(digits)`: The UPC-E of `digits`: a GTIN-12 whose zeros its six digits leave out. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_add_on(symbol: Symbol, digits: str) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.with_add_on(symbol, digits)`: `symbol` with a two- or five-digit add-on after it: a periodical's issue, a book's price. Fails `invalid`.
- `function code128(text: str) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.code128(text)`: The Code 128 of `text`, its code sets changed where that makes the symbol shortest. Fails `invalid`.
- `function code128_bytes(data: [u8]) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.code128_bytes(data)`: The Code 128 of `data`, read back as its bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Element(ai: str, data: str)`: A GS1 element string: an application identifier and its data.
- `function gs1_128(elements: [Element]) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.gs1_128(elements)`: The GS1-128 of `elements`: FNC1 first, then each identifier and its data, FNC1 after each element whose length GS1 does not fix, but the last. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function parse_elements(text: str) -> [Element]?`, called `barcode.parse_elements(text)`: The element strings of `text`, written as a person reads them under a symbol: `(01)09501101530003(10)AB-123`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_elements(elements: [Element]) -> str`, called `barcode.format_elements(elements)`: `elements` as a person reads them: each identifier in brackets, then its data.
- `variant Shape = .square | .rectangle | .either`: The shapes a Data Matrix may take.
- `variant Size = .smallest(shape: Shape) | .fixed(rows: i64, columns: i64)`: How big a Data Matrix is made.
- `function data_matrix(text: str, size: Size) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.data_matrix(text, size)`: The Data Matrix of `text`, its encodations chosen so that its codewords are fewest. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function data_matrix_bytes(data: [u8], size: Size) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.data_matrix_bytes(data, size)`: The Data Matrix of `data`, read back as its bytes. Fails as `data_matrix` fails.
- `function gs1_data_matrix(elements: [Element], size: Size) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.gs1_data_matrix(elements, size)`: The GS1 Data Matrix of `elements`: FNC1 first, then each identifier and its data, FNC1 after each element whose length GS1 does not fix, but the last. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Count = .automatic | .exactly(value: i64)`: A count the program gives, or one the package chooses.
- `record Pdf417Options(columns: Count, level: Count, row_height: i64, compact: bool)`: How `pdf417` makes a symbol.
- `function default_pdf417_options() -> Pdf417Options`, called `barcode.default_pdf417_options()`: The options of an ordinary PDF417: the columns and the level chosen, rows three modules tall, not compact.
- `function pdf417(text: str, options: Pdf417Options) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.pdf417(text, options)`: The PDF417 of `text`: runs of thirteen digits or more in numeric compaction, runs of text in text compaction, and the rest in byte. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function pdf417_bytes(data: [u8], options: Pdf417Options) -> Symbol?`, called `barcode.pdf417_bytes(data, options)`: The PDF417 of `data`, read back as its bytes. Fails as `pdf417` fails.
- `record SvgOptions(scale: i64, dark: str, light: str, captions: bool, font_family: str)`: How `to_svg` writes a symbol.
- `function default_svg_options() -> SvgOptions`, called `barcode.default_svg_options()`: The SVG options of an ordinary symbol: one unit a module, black on white, the captions in a monospaced font, OCR-B where the reader has it.
- `function to_svg(symbol: Symbol, options: SvgOptions) -> str?`, called `barcode.to_svg(symbol, options)`: `symbol` as an SVG document: the ground, one path of its bars or modules crisp at every scale, and its captions as text centred on their columns. Fails `invalid`.
- `record ImageOptions(scale: i64, dark: image.Color, light: image.Color)`: How `to_image` draws a symbol.
- `function default_image_options() -> ImageOptions`, called `barcode.default_image_options()`: The image options of an ordinary symbol: three pixels a module, opaque black on opaque white.
- `function to_image(symbol: Symbol, options: ImageOptions) -> image.Image?`, called `barcode.to_image(symbol, options)`: `symbol` drawn into an RGBA image without its captions, every module `options.scale` pixels a side, its quiet zone in the light colour. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function to_image_with_text(symbol: Symbol, options: ImageOptions, f: font.Font) -> image.Image?`, called `barcode.to_image_with_text(symbol, options, f)`: `symbol` drawn into an RGBA image with its captions set in `f`, as a label is printed. Fails `not_found`.


### chart

Layer 4, named `use <rebel>/chart`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/chart/).

Plots and charts made: lines, points and areas over two axes, bars side by side or stacked, upright or lying, histograms, pies and donuts, each with its axes' ticks computed (nice numbers, logarithmic scales, the calendar's steps for dates), a grid, a legend, a title and the axes' labels, its text set in a `font.Font` and its colours from a palette made in `image/colorspace`; written as SVG text or drawn into an `image` through `image/vector`, the same drawing either way.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `codes.INVALID`: The code of an input the function does not read: a value that is infinite, or not a number where a gap is not taken; a range that does not rise; a count of ticks or bins out of its range; a logarithmic base not above 1 or a value at or below zero on such an axis; a date outside the years 1 to 9999; a size, a text size or a palette out of range; a chart too small for its text.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `codes.LIMIT`: The code of an image past 16,384 pixels a side, which `lay_out` answers.
- `variant Scale = .linear | .log(base: f64) | .time`: How an axis places its values.
- `record Range(low: f64, high: f64)`: Two ends of a range of values.
- `record Tick(value: f64, label: str)`: A tick of an axis.
- `function ticks(span: Range, scale: Scale, count: i64) -> [Tick]?`, called `chart.ticks(span, scale, count)`: The ticks of an axis over `span`, about `count` of them where the scale can choose. Fails `invalid`.
- `function nice(span: Range, scale: Scale, count: i64) -> Range?`, called `chart.nice(span, scale, count)`: `span` moved out to the ticks of about `count`, so that the axis begins and ends on a tick. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Bins = .auto | .count(count: i64) | .edges(edges: [f64])`: How a histogram's values are cut into bins.
- `record Bin(low: f64, high: f64, count: i64)`: A bin of a histogram: the values from `low` up to `high`; the last bin also takes a value equal to its `high`.
- `function bin(values: [f64], bins: Bins) -> [Bin]?`, called `chart.bin(values, bins)`: `values` counted into bins. Fails `invalid`.
- `function palette(count: i64) -> [image.Color]?`, called `chart.palette(count)`: `count` colours for the series of a chart, of hues evenly spaced around the circle from a blue, as light and as saturated as one another in HLS, taken in an order that sets each far from the one before it. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Look(width: i64, height: i64, title: str, text_size: f64, background: image.Color, ink: image.Color, grid: image.Color, palette: [image.Color], legend: bool)`: The frame of a chart: its size, its title and how its text and colours look.
- `function look(title: str, width: i64, height: i64) -> Look`, called `chart.look(title, width: width, height: height)`: The look of an ordinary chart: text 12 pixels to the em in a near black on white, a light gray grid, ten colours of `palette` and a legend.
- `variant Extent = .data | .fixed(low: f64, high: f64)`: What range an axis spans.
- `variant TickCount = .auto | .about(count: i64)`: How many ticks an axis takes.
- `record Axis(label: str, scale: Scale, extent: Extent, ticks: TickCount, grid: bool)`: An axis of a chart.
- `function axis(label: str) -> Axis`, called `chart.axis(label)`: A linear axis over the data's range, its ticks as many as its length holds and its grid drawn.
- `variant Mark = .line | .points | .line_and_points | .area`: How a series is drawn.
- `record Series(name: str, xs: [f64], ys: [f64], mark: Mark)`: A series of points.
- `record Plot(look: Look, x: Axis, y: Axis, series: [Series], stacked: bool)`: Series over two axes.
- `variant Grouping = .grouped | .stacked`: How bars of several series share a category.
- `variant Direction = .vertical | .horizontal`: Which way bars run.
- `record BarSeries(name: str, values: [f64])`: The values of one series of bars.
- `record Bars(look: Look, categories: [str], category_label: str, value: Axis, series: [BarSeries], grouping: Grouping, direction: Direction)`: Bars of categories.
- `record Histogram(look: Look, values: [f64], bins: Bins, x: Axis, y: Axis)`: The counts of values in bins.
- `record Slice(name: str, value: f64)`: A slice of a pie.
- `record Pie(look: Look, slices: [Slice], hole: f64, percentages: bool)`: Shares of a whole.
- `variant Chart = .plot(plot: Plot) | .bars(bars: Bars) | .histogram(histogram: Histogram) | .pie(pie: Pie)`: A chart.
- `record Layout(scene: scene.Scene, font: font.Font)`: A chart laid out, ready to be written as SVG and drawn as an image, the same drawing either way.
- `variant SvgText = .elements | .outlines`: How an SVG holds a chart's text.
- `function lay_out(c: Chart, f: font.Font) -> Layout?`, called `chart.lay_out(c, f)`: `c` laid out in `f`: its ranges and ticks found, its margins measured from its text, its shapes mapped to pixels and cut to the plot. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `not_found`.
- `function to_svg(l: Layout, text: SvgText) -> str?`, called `chart.to_svg(l, text)`: The SVG document of a laid out chart: one line ending with a line feed, no XML declaration, as wide and as high as its look in pixels. Fails `not_found`.
- `function to_image(l: Layout) -> image.Image?`, called `chart.to_image(l)`: A laid out chart drawn into an RGBA image as wide and as high as its look, anti-aliased, the text filled from the font's outlines. Fails `limit`, `not_found`.


### jobs

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/jobs`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jobs/).

Background work kept in a store and run by workers, as Celery, Sidekiq and river do it: a job is a value (a kind, a JSON payload, a queue, a priority, a time to start, its attempts), a worker claims the next one ready, runs the program's own function for its kind, and marks it completed or failed; a failed attempt runs again after a wait that grows, until its attempts are spent and it is kept, failed, with every error.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a job, a worker or a schedule outside its bounds, and of a change a job's state refuses: every check and every store.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of an id that names no job, of a claim that found no job ready, and of an attempt that is no longer running: the stores.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a unique key held by a job not yet finished: the stores' `enqueue` and `enqueue_many`.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The code of a job whose cancellation was asked while it ran: the stores' `extend`.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a wait for tokens longer than the caller accepts: `reserve_within`.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a time too near the ends of an `Instant` for a bucket's sums: `bucket`, `allow`, `reserve`, `reserve_within`, `cancel` and `with_rate`.
- `constant DEFAULT_QUEUE: str`, value `"default"`: The queue a job goes to unless it names another.
- `constant FIRST_PRIORITY: i64`, value `1`: The first priority: a job of priority 1 is claimed before any other ready in its worker's queues.
- `constant LAST_PRIORITY: i64`, value `9`: The last priority: a job of priority 9 is claimed after every other.
- `constant DEFAULT_PRIORITY: i64`, value `5`: The priority of a job unless it names another, in the middle, so that a program can put a job before the rest or after them.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS: i64`, value `25`: The attempts a job has in all unless it names another, the first included: Sidekiq's, river's and asynq's 25, which the default backoff spreads over about two weeks.
- `constant MAX_NAME_BYTES: i64`, value `limits.MAX_NAME_BYTES`: The longest kind, queue, unique key and worker's name, in bytes.
- `variant Start = .now | .after(wait: time.Duration) | .at(instant: time.Instant)`: When a job may first run.
- `record Job(kind: str, payload: json.Value, queue: str, priority: i64, start: Start, max_attempts: i64, unique_key: str)`: A job as a program enqueues it: what to run, with what, where and when.
- `function new_job(kind: str, payload: json.Value) -> Job`, called `jobs.new_job(kind, payload)`: A job of `kind` with `payload`, in `DEFAULT_QUEUE` at `DEFAULT_PRIORITY`, to run now, with `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts and no unique key.
- `function check_job(job: Job) -> ()?`, called `jobs.check_job(job)`: Checks that a store can keep `job`: each field within its bounds and its payload written as JSON. Fails `invalid`.
- `function payload_text(job: Job) -> str?`, called `jobs.payload_text(job)`: The JSON a store keeps of `job`'s payload, compact. Fails `unsupported`.
- `variant State = .available | .running | .completed | .failed | .cancelled`: Where a job stands in its store.
- `function state_name(state: State) -> str`, called `jobs.state_name(state)`: The name a store keeps for `state`: `available`, `running`, `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`.
- `function parse_state(name: str) -> State?`, called `jobs.parse_state(name)`: The state `name` names, as `state_name` writes it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_finished(state: State) -> bool`, called `jobs.is_finished(state)`: Whether `state` is one a job never leaves by itself: completed, failed or cancelled.
- `record AttemptError(attempt: i64, at: time.Instant, error: str)`: The error of one failed attempt, kept with the job.
- `record Info(id: i64, kind: str, payload: json.Value, queue: str, priority: i64, state: State, attempt: i64, max_attempts: i64, unique_key: str, created_at: time.Instant, run_at: time.Instant, attempted_at: time.Instant?, finished_at: time.Instant?, lease_until: time.Instant?, worker: str, cancel_requested: bool, errors: [AttemptError], output: json.Value)`: A job as its store holds it, which `claim`, `get` and the other reads of a store answer.
- `record Count(queue: str, state: State, jobs: i64)`: How many jobs of one queue stand in one state, as a store's `counts` answers it.
- `function info_of(fields: {str: str}) -> Info?`, called `jobs.info_of(fields)`: The job a store's fields describe: each field of `Info` by its name, as text, which is how both stores read a job back. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `record Worker(name: str, queues: [str], lease: time.Duration, backoff: retries.Backoff, poll: time.Duration)`: How a worker claims: its name, its queues, how long a claim holds, how its failed attempts wait, and how long it sleeps where none is ready.
- `function new_worker(queues: [str]) -> Worker`, called `jobs.new_worker(queues)`: A worker of `queues`, named by the host and the process, with a lease of 30 minutes, `default_backoff()`, and a poll of a second.
- `function check_worker(worker: Worker) -> ()?`, called `jobs.check_worker(worker)`: Checks that a store can claim for `worker`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function default_backoff() -> retries.Backoff`, called `jobs.default_backoff()`: The waits a worker's failed attempts follow unless it names others: 15 seconds after the first failure, doubling, at most a day, each spread by a fifth either way so that jobs that failed together do not run again together.
- `function retry_wait(policy: retries.Backoff, attempt: i64) -> time.Duration?`, called `jobs.retry_wait(policy, attempt)`: The wait before a job runs again after its attempt number `attempt` failed, by `policy`, its jitter drawn from the system's random bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function retry_wait_with(policy: retries.Backoff, attempt: i64, fraction: f64) -> time.Duration?`, called `jobs.retry_wait_with(policy, attempt, fraction)`: The wait before a job runs again after its attempt number `attempt` failed, by `policy`, its jitter spread by the caller's `fraction`: the same fraction gives the same wait, so a program whose waits must repeat (a generator it seeds, a test, a demonstration on a fixed clock) computes the wait itself and hands it to its store's `fail_attempt_with`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Periodic(name: str, schedule: time.Cron, zone: time.Zone, job: Job)`: A job enqueued at every run of a cron schedule, once whatever the number of programs that ask: a store keeps the next run of each schedule by its name, and the program that finds it due first moves it on and enqueues.
- `function new_periodic(name: str, cron: str, job: Job) -> Periodic?`, called `jobs.new_periodic(name: name, cron: cron, job)`: The schedule `name` that enqueues `job` at every run of the cron expression `cron`, read on UTC's clocks. Fails `invalid`.
- `function next_due(periodic: Periodic, after: time.Instant) -> time.Instant?`, called `jobs.next_due(periodic, after)`: The first run of `periodic` strictly after `after`. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Bucket(every: time.Duration, burst: i64, empty_at: time.Instant, seen: time.Instant)`: A token bucket, which holds a rate: it earns one token every `every`, holds at most `burst`, and an attempt takes tokens from it.
- `record Reservation(bucket: Bucket, tokens: i64, delay: time.Duration, ready: time.Instant, finish: time.Instant)`: What `reserve` answers: the bucket with the tokens taken, and the wait.
- `record Allowed(granted: bool, bucket: Bucket)`: What `allow` answers.
- `function bucket(every: time.Duration, burst: i64, at: time.Instant) -> Bucket?`, called `jobs.bucket(every, burst, at)`: A bucket full at `at`: a rate of one token every `every` with a burst of `burst`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function allow(limit: Bucket, at: time.Instant, n: i64) -> Allowed?`, called `jobs.allow(limit, at, n)`: Whether `n` tokens are there at `at`, taking them where they are. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function reserve(limit: Bucket, at: time.Instant, n: i64) -> Reservation?`, called `jobs.reserve(limit, at, n)`: Takes `n` tokens at `at` even if they are not there, and tells how long to wait for them: reservations queue, each behind the ones before. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function reserve_within(limit: Bucket, at: time.Instant, n: i64, within: time.Duration) -> Reservation?`, called `jobs.reserve_within(limit, at, n, within)`: `reserve`, kept only where the wait is no longer than `within`. Fails `timeout`.
- `function cancel(limit: Bucket, taken: Reservation, at: time.Instant) -> Bucket?`, called `jobs.cancel(limit, taken, at)`: Gives a reservation back, as far as no later reservation has used what it took. Fails `does_not_fit`.
- `function tokens(limit: Bucket, at: time.Instant) -> f64`, called `jobs.tokens(limit, at)`: The tokens the bucket holds at `at`, a fraction of one and the debt of reservations that wait included, as a negative number.
- `function available(limit: Bucket, at: time.Instant) -> i64`, called `jobs.available(limit, at)`: The whole tokens the bucket holds at `at`, never below none: the most `allow` grants at that time, counted on whole numbers.
- `function with_rate(limit: Bucket, at: time.Instant, every: time.Duration, burst: i64) -> Bucket?`, called `jobs.with_rate(limit, at, every, burst)`: The bucket with another rate and another burst, holding at `at` the tokens it held, as many as the new burst allows. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `does_not_fit`.
- `record Sometimes(first: i64, every: i64, interval: time.Duration, count: i64, last: time.Instant?)`: Something done now and then: the first calls, every so many, and at most once in a span, as Go's `rate.Sometimes` decides it, kept as a value with the clock the caller's.
- `record Sampled(due: bool, state: Sometimes)`: What `sometimes_due` answers.
- `function sometimes(first: i64, every: i64, interval: time.Duration) -> Sometimes?`, called `jobs.sometimes(first: first, every: every, interval)`: A `Sometimes` of no calls yet. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sometimes_due(state: Sometimes, at: time.Instant) -> Sampled?`, called `jobs.sometimes_due(state, at)`: Whether the next call is due, and the state after it. Fails `does_not_fit`.


### jose

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/jose`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jose/).

JSON Web Signatures, Keys, Tokens and Encryption (RFC 7515, 7517, 7519 and 7516, the algorithms of RFC 7518 and RFC 8037): a payload signed and verified in the compact and the JSON serializations, a key read from and written as its JSON or as DER and PEM, a JWT's claims checked, and a plaintext encrypted where the system's cryptography allows it.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A token, a key or a text not of its form, a signature that does not hold, a claim the rules refuse, a key that serves none of the algorithms asked: every function that reads or checks.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No key given has the header's `kid` (`verify_compact`, `verify_json`, `verify_token`, `decrypt_compact`), no key has the id asked (`key_by_id`), a claim is absent (`claim_text`, `claim_texts`, `claim_time`).
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: A time past what a `time.Instant` holds: `claim_time`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: An algorithm, a curve or a key type that this platform's cryptography, or Rebel's, lacks: Ed25519 and X25519 on Windows; `ES512`, Ed448, AES key wrap and AES-CBC everywhere.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system has no memory or key left, from `crypto/keypairs` and `crypto/seal`.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system's cryptography failed for another reason, its words in the message.
- `variant Algorithm = .hs256 | .hs384 | .hs512 | .rs256 | .rs384 | .rs512 | .ps256 | .ps384 | .ps512 | .es256 | .es384 | .eddsa | .ed25519`: A signature's algorithm (RFC 7518 § 3, RFC 8037, RFC 9864): what a JWS header's `alg` names.
- `variant KeyAlgorithm = .direct | .rsa_oaep_256 | .ecdh_es | .a128gcmkw | .a256gcmkw`: How a JWE's content key reaches its recipient: what its header's `alg` names (RFC 7518 § 4).
- `variant ContentAlgorithm = .a128gcm | .a256gcm`: How a JWE's content is sealed: what its header's `enc` names (RFC 7518 § 5.3).
- `function format_algorithm(algorithm: Algorithm) -> str`, called `jose.format_algorithm(algorithm)`: The JOSE name of `algorithm`: `HS256`, `RS256`, `ES256`, `EdDSA`, `Ed25519` and the others.
- `function parse_algorithm(name: str) -> Algorithm?`, called `jose.parse_algorithm(name)`: The algorithm a JWS header's `alg` names. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function is_available(algorithm: Algorithm) -> bool`, called `jose.is_available(algorithm)`: Whether this machine's cryptography signs and verifies by `algorithm`: false for `EdDSA` and `Ed25519` on Windows.
- `function format_key_algorithm(algorithm: KeyAlgorithm) -> str`, called `jose.format_key_algorithm(algorithm)`: The JOSE name of `algorithm`: `dir`, `RSA-OAEP-256`, `ECDH-ES`, `A128GCMKW` or `A256GCMKW`.
- `function parse_key_algorithm(name: str) -> KeyAlgorithm?`, called `jose.parse_key_algorithm(name)`: The key algorithm a JWE header's `alg` names. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_content_algorithm(algorithm: ContentAlgorithm) -> str`, called `jose.format_content_algorithm(algorithm)`: The JOSE name of `algorithm`: `A128GCM` or `A256GCM`.
- `function parse_content_algorithm(name: str) -> ContentAlgorithm?`, called `jose.parse_content_algorithm(name)`: The content algorithm a JWE header's `enc` names. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `record Key(key_type: str, curve: str, id: str, usage: str, operations: [str], algorithm: str, material: {str: [u8]}, chain: [[u8]], extra: {str: json.Value})`: A JSON Web Key (RFC 7517): a key as its JSON holds it, its members read and their base 64 undone.
- `function key_of(v: json.Value) -> Key?`, called `jose.key_of(v)`: The key the JSON object `v` writes. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function key_json(key: Key) -> json.Value`, called `jose.key_json(key)`: `key` as a JSON object: `kty`, `crv`, `kid`, `use`, `key_ops`, `alg`, the key's members in RFC 7517's order, `x5c`, then `extra`, each only where it is set.
- `function parse_key(text: str) -> Key?`, called `jose.parse_key(text)`: The key the JSON text `text` writes. Fails as `json.parse` and `key_of` do.
- `function format_key(key: Key) -> str?`, called `jose.format_key(key)`: `key` as JSON text on one line, as `key_json` orders it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_key_set(text: str) -> [Key]?`, called `jose.parse_key_set(text)`: The keys of a JWK set's JSON text, `{"keys": [...]}`, in their order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_key_set(key_set: [Key]) -> str?`, called `jose.format_key_set(key_set)`: `key_set` as a JWK set's JSON text on one line. Fails as `format_key` does.
- `function key_by_id(key_set: [Key], id: str) -> Key?`, called `jose.key_by_id(key_set, id)`: The first key of `key_set` whose `kid` is `id`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function key_from_secret(secret: [u8]) -> Key`, called `jose.key_from_secret(secret)`: A symmetric key, `kty` `oct`, made of `secret`'s bytes: an HMAC's, or a content key for `dir`.
- `function decode_public_der(der: [u8]) -> Key?`, called `jose.decode_public_der(der)`: The public key a SubjectPublicKeyInfo holds (RFC 5280), as a JWK. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_private_der(der: [u8]) -> Key?`, called `jose.decode_private_der(der)`: The private key a PKCS #8 holds (RFC 5208), unencrypted, as a JWK with its public members. Fails `invalid`.
- `function key_from_pem(text: str) -> Key?`, called `jose.key_from_pem(text)`: The key of the first `PUBLIC KEY` or `PRIVATE KEY` block of PEM in `text`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function encode_public_der(key: Key) -> [u8]?`, called `jose.encode_public_der(key)`: `key`'s public half as SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER, which `crypto/keypairs.decode_public_der` reads. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_private_der(key: Key) -> [u8]?`, called `jose.encode_private_der(key)`: `key` as PKCS #8 DER, unencrypted: the secret, handed to the caller. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_public_pem(key: Key) -> str?`, called `jose.format_public_pem(key)`: `key`'s public half as PEM's `PUBLIC KEY`, lines of 64 characters each ending in `\n`. Fails as `encode_public_der` does.
- `function format_private_pem(key: Key) -> str?`, called `jose.format_private_pem(key)`: `key` as PEM's `PRIVATE KEY`: the secret, handed to the caller. Fails as `encode_private_der` does.
- `function generate_key(kind: keypairs.Kind) -> Key?`, called `jose.generate_key(kind)`: A new private key of `kind`, drawn by the system's generator, as a JWK. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function public_of(key: Key) -> Key?`, called `jose.public_of(key)`: `key` with its private members taken out: what may be published. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_private(key: Key) -> bool`, called `jose.is_private(key)`: Whether `key` holds a secret: a `d` member, or any `oct` key.
- `function thumbprint(key: Key, algorithm: crypto.Algorithm) -> [u8]?`, called `jose.thumbprint(key, algorithm)`: `key`'s thumbprint (RFC 7638): the digest by `algorithm` of the JSON of its required public members, in the order of their names, with no space. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Message(protected: {str: json.Value}, unprotected: {str: json.Value}, payload: [u8])`: A JWS verified: its headers and its payload.
- `record Signer(key: Key, algorithm: Algorithm, protected: {str: json.Value}, unprotected: {str: json.Value})`: One signature of a JWS in the JSON serialization: the key, the algorithm and the two headers it is made with.
- `function sign_compact(payload: [u8], key: Key, algorithm: Algorithm, header: {str: json.Value}) -> str?`, called `jose.sign_compact(payload, key, algorithm, header)`: `payload` signed by `key` with `algorithm`, in the compact serialization: three parts of base64url between two dots. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function verify_compact(token: str, trusted: [Key], algorithms: [Algorithm]) -> Message?`, called `jose.verify_compact(token, trusted, algorithms)`: The JWS `token`, compact, verified by one of `trusted` with one of `algorithms`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function verify_detached(token: str, payload: [u8], trusted: [Key], algorithms: [Algorithm]) -> Message?`, called `jose.verify_detached(token, payload, trusted, algorithms)`: The JWS `token`, compact with its payload carried apart (RFC 7515 Appendix F), verified over `payload`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function header_of(token: str) -> {str: json.Value}?`, called `jose.header_of(token)`: The protected header of the compact JWS or JWE `token`, read and NOT verified: what names the key (`kid`) before one is chosen. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sign_json(payload: [u8], signers: [Signer]) -> str?`, called `jose.sign_json(payload, signers)`: `payload` signed by each of `signers`, in the general JSON serialization: `{"payload": ..., "signatures": [...]}`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sign_flattened(payload: [u8], signer: Signer) -> str?`, called `jose.sign_flattened(payload, signer)`: `payload` signed by `signer`, in the flattened JSON serialization: `{"payload": ..., "protected": ..., "header": ..., "signature": ...}`. Fails as `sign_json` does.
- `function verify_json(text: str, trusted: [Key], algorithms: [Algorithm]) -> Message?`, called `jose.verify_json(text, trusted, algorithms)`: The JWS `text`, in the general or the flattened JSON serialization, verified: the first of its signatures that one of `trusted` verifies with one of `algorithms`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `record Rules(algorithms: [Algorithm], issuer: str, audience: str, subject: str, token_type: str, required: [str], leeway: time.Duration, now: time.Instant)`: What a JWT must answer to be accepted: the algorithms, the claims expected and the time it is judged at.
- `record Token(header: {str: json.Value}, claims: {str: json.Value})`: A JWT read: its header and its claims.
- `function default_rules(algorithms: [Algorithm]) -> Rules?`, called `jose.default_rules(algorithms)`: Rules that accept `algorithms` and nothing else, judge at the wall clock's time, with no leeway, and check no issuer, audience, subject, type or required claim. Fails `failed`.
- `function sign_token(claims: {str: json.Value}, key: Key, algorithm: Algorithm) -> str?`, called `jose.sign_token(claims, key, algorithm)`: The JWT of `claims` signed by `key` with `algorithm`: a header `{"alg":...,"typ":"JWT"}` and the key's `kid` where it has one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function verify_token(token: str, trusted: [Key], rules: Rules) -> Token?`, called `jose.verify_token(token, trusted, rules)`: The JWT `token` verified by one of `trusted` and its claims checked by `rules`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function check_claims(claims: {str: json.Value}, rules: Rules) -> ()?`, called `jose.check_claims(claims, rules)`: Whether `claims` answer `rules`, the algorithms aside: `exp` after `now`, `nbf` and `iat` not after it, each with the leeway, and `iss`, `aud`, `sub` and the required claims as the rules ask. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_unverified(token: str) -> Token?`, called `jose.read_unverified(token)`: The header and claims of the JWT `token`, read and NOT verified: for a program that must look inside before it can choose a key, or one that trusts the channel the token came by. Fails `invalid`.
- `function claim_text(claims: {str: json.Value}, name: str) -> str?`, called `jose.claim_text(claims, name)`: The text of the claim `name` in `claims`: `iss`, `sub`, `jti`, `nonce`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function claim_texts(claims: {str: json.Value}, name: str) -> [str]?`, called `jose.claim_texts(claims, name)`: The texts of the claim `name`, which is one text or a list of texts, as `aud` is (RFC 7519 § 4.1.3). Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function claim_time(claims: {str: json.Value}, name: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `jose.claim_time(claims, name)`: The instant the claim `name` gives as a NumericDate, seconds since 1970 in UTC: `exp`, `nbf`, `iat`, `auth_time`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function numeric_date(t: time.Instant) -> json.Value`, called `jose.numeric_date(t)`: `t` as a NumericDate: its whole seconds since 1970, the fraction dropped toward the past, as golang-jwt writes them.
- `record Decrypted(protected: {str: json.Value}, plaintext: [u8])`: A JWE decrypted: its protected header and its plaintext.
- `function encrypt_compact(plaintext: [u8], key: Key, algorithm: KeyAlgorithm, encryption: ContentAlgorithm, header: {str: json.Value}) -> str?`, called `jose.encrypt_compact(plaintext, key, algorithm, encryption, header)`: `plaintext` encrypted to `key` in the compact serialization: five parts of base64url between four dots. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decrypt_compact(token: str, trusted: [Key], algorithms: [KeyAlgorithm], encryptions: [ContentAlgorithm]) -> Decrypted?`, called `jose.decrypt_compact(token, trusted, algorithms, encryptions)`: The JWE `token`, compact, decrypted by one of `trusted`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.


### archive

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/archive`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/archive/).

Archives of many files in one: tar (ustar, with PAX records and GNU's long names read) plain or gzip, and zip (stored and deflated members, ZIP64 for large ones), read entry by entry, listed, extracted into a folder, written entry by entry or from files on the disk; and read from, or written as, bytes held in memory (`decode_tar`, `encode_tar`, `decode_zip`, `encode_zip`), with no file on the way.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an archive that is not what its format says, the message naming the byte; and of an entry refused by extraction, the message naming the entry and why.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of an archive, or an entry's data, that would pass the `limit` the caller set.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a zip entry asked for by a name the archive does not hold: `entry_of`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of what this package does not read: an encrypted zip member, a zip method other than stored and deflated, a sparse tar member, an archive split over disks.
- `variant Kind = .file | .directory | .symlink | .hard_link | .other(flag: u8)`: What an entry is.
- `variant Compression = .none | .gzip`: How a tar archive is compressed.
- `variant Method = .stored | .deflated`: How a zip member's data is held.
- `variant Format = .tar | .zip`: Which archive a file is, as `format_of` tells.
- `function format_of(start: [u8]) -> Format?`, called `archive.format_of(start)`: Which archive `start` begins, told by its first bytes: zip's local header or end record signature, or a tar header whose checksum holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `record TarEntry(name: str, kind: Kind, size: i64, mode: i64, modified: time.Instant, link: str, user_id: i64, group_id: i64, user_name: str, group_name: str, device_major: i64, device_minor: i64, records: {str: str})`: What a tar header says of an entry.
- `function tar_entry(name: str, kind: Kind) -> TarEntry`, called `archive.tar_entry(name, kind)`: A tar entry named `name` of kind `kind` with every other field at its usual value: mode 0o644 (0o755 for a folder), no data, the time 1970-01-01 UTC, no link, no owner.
- `variant Next = .entry(value: TarEntry) | .end`: What `next_tar_entry` answers: the next entry, or the archive's end.
- `record TarReader(state: tar_read.State)`: A reader of a tar archive from a stream: made by `tar_reader`, it reads entry by entry.
- `function tar_reader(from: io.Stream, compression: Compression, limit: i64) -> TarReader`, called `archive.tar_reader(from, compression, limit)`: A reader of the tar archive in `from`, compressed as `compression` says, of at most `limit` bytes once decompressed.
- `function next_tar_entry(@r: TarReader) -> Next?`, called `archive.next_tar_entry(@r)`: The next entry of `r`, or the archive's end; the data of the entry before it that was not read is skipped. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function read_tar_data(@r: TarReader, most: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `archive.read_tar_data(@r, most)`: Up to `most` bytes of the data of `r`'s entry in hand, fewer where fewer come at once, none at its end. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function read_tar_rest(@r: TarReader) -> [u8]?`, called `archive.read_tar_rest(@r)`: The rest of the data of `r`'s entry in hand, whole. Fails as `read_tar_data` does.
- `function list_tar(from: io.Stream, compression: Compression, limit: i64) -> [TarEntry]?`, called `archive.list_tar(from, compression, limit)`: Every entry of the tar archive in `from`, in order, their data skipped. Fails as `next_tar_entry` does.
- `function extract_tar(from: io.Stream, compression: Compression, to: str, limit: i64) -> [str]?`, called `archive.extract_tar(from, compression, to, limit)`: Extracts every entry of the tar archive in `from` into the folder `to`, and answers their names in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `record TarWriter(sink: tar_write.Sink, owed: i64, size: i64, name: str)`: A writer of a tar archive to a stream: made by `tar_writer`, it writes entry by entry, and `finish_tar` writes the archive's end.
- `function tar_writer(to: io.Stream, compression: Compression) -> TarWriter`, called `archive.tar_writer(to, compression)`: A writer of a tar archive to `to`, compressed as `compression` says (gzip at level 6).
- `function write_tar_header(@w: TarWriter, entry: TarEntry) -> ()?`, called `archive.write_tar_header(@w, entry)`: Writes `entry`'s header; its data, `entry.size` bytes for a file, follows by `write_tar_data`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_tar_data(@w: TarWriter, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `archive.write_tar_data(@w, data)`: Writes `data` as the next bytes of the entry in hand's data. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_tar_entry(@w: TarWriter, entry: TarEntry, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `archive.write_tar_entry(@w, entry, data)`: Writes an entry and its data whole: `entry`'s size is `data`'s length. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_tar_file(@w: TarWriter, file: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `archive.add_tar_file(@w, file: file, name: name)`: Writes the file, folder or symbolic link at `file` on the disk as the entry `name`, with its mode and time; a file's data is read 65,536 bytes at a time. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_tar_tree(@w: TarWriter, dir: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `archive.add_tar_tree(@w, dir: dir, name: name)`: Writes the folder `dir` and everything under it as entries below `name`, folders before what they hold, links as links. Fails as `add_tar_file` and `fs.walk` fail.
- `function finish_tar(@w: TarWriter) -> ()?`, called `archive.finish_tar(@w)`: Writes the archive's end, and gzip's end where it is compressed. Fails `invalid`.
- `record TarMember(entry: TarEntry, data: [u8])`: An entry of a tar archive with its data, whole: what `decode_tar` answers and `encode_tar` takes.
- `function decode_tar(data: [u8], compression: Compression, limit: i64) -> [TarMember]?`, called `archive.decode_tar(data, compression, limit)`: The tar archive whose bytes are `data`, compressed as `compression` says: every entry in order, each with its data whole. Fails `limit`.
- `function encode_tar(members: [TarMember], compression: Compression) -> [u8]?`, called `archive.encode_tar(members, compression)`: `members` as the bytes of a tar archive, compressed as `compression` says (gzip at level 6): each entry's header and data, in order, then the archive's end. Fails as `write_tar_entry` fails.
- `record ZipEntry(name: str, kind: Kind, method: Method, size: i64, compressed_size: i64, crc: u32, modified: time.Instant, mode: i64, comment: str, offset: i64)`: What a zip archive's central directory says of a member.
- `function zip_entry(name: str, kind: Kind) -> ZipEntry`, called `archive.zip_entry(name, kind)`: A zip member named `name` of kind `kind`, deflated, with every other field at its usual value: mode 0o644 (0o755 for a folder), the time 1980-01-01 UTC, no comment.
- `record ZipReader(source: zip_read.Source, size: i64, entries: [ZipEntry], comment: str, members: [zip_read.Member])`: A zip archive open to read: its central directory read, its members' data read on demand.
- `function zip_reader(from: io.Stream) -> ZipReader?`, called `archive.zip_reader(from)`: A reader of the zip archive in `from`, its central directory read. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_zip(data: [u8]) -> ZipReader?`, called `archive.decode_zip(data)`: The zip archive whose bytes are `data`, its central directory read, as `zip_reader` reads one from a file; its members' data is read by `read_zip_entry`, from the bytes it holds. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function entry_of(r: ZipReader, name: str) -> ZipEntry?`, called `archive.entry_of(r, name)`: The member of `r` named `name`, the first where several are. Fails `not_found`.
- `function read_zip_entry(r: ZipReader, entry: ZipEntry, limit: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `archive.read_zip_entry(r, entry, limit)`: The data of `entry`, a member of `r`, whole: its CRC-32 and size checked. Fails `not_found`, `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function extract_zip(from: io.Stream, to: str, limit: i64) -> [str]?`, called `archive.extract_zip(from, to, limit)`: Extracts every member of the zip archive in `from` into the folder `to`, and answers their names in order. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `record ZipWriter(sink: zip_write.Sink)`: A writer of a zip archive to a stream: made by `zip_writer`, it writes member by member, and `finish_zip` writes the central directory.
- `function zip_writer(to: io.Stream) -> ZipWriter`, called `archive.zip_writer(to)`: A writer of a zip archive to `to`.
- `function write_zip_entry(@w: ZipWriter, entry: ZipEntry, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `archive.write_zip_entry(@w, entry, data)`: Writes a member and its data whole, compressed by `entry.method` at level 6: its size, compressed size and CRC-32 are `data`'s, whatever `entry` says. Fails `invalid`.
- `function begin_zip_member(@w: ZipWriter, entry: ZipEntry) -> ()?`, called `archive.begin_zip_member(@w, entry)`: Begins the member `entry`, whose data follows in pieces by `write_zip_data` and ends with `end_zip_member`: what `write_zip_entry` writes whole, written a piece at a time, so a program that runs a long job in steps writes a large member between two of them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_zip_data(@w: ZipWriter, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `archive.write_zip_data(@w, data)`: Writes `data` as the next bytes of the member `begin_zip_member` began, compressed by its method as they come, its CRC-32 counted. Fails `invalid`.
- `function end_zip_member(@w: ZipWriter) -> ()?`, called `archive.end_zip_member(@w)`: Ends the member `begin_zip_member` began: the compressor's last bytes, then the data descriptor with the CRC-32 and the sizes of the data written, and the member kept for the central directory `finish_zip` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_zip_file(@w: ZipWriter, file: str, name: str, method: Method) -> ()?`, called `archive.add_zip_file(@w, file: file, name: name, method)`: Writes the file, folder or symbolic link at `file` on the disk as the member `name`, with its mode and time; a file's data is read and compressed 65,536 bytes at a time, a data descriptor after it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_zip_tree(@w: ZipWriter, dir: str, name: str, method: Method) -> ()?`, called `archive.add_zip_tree(@w, dir: dir, name: name, method)`: Writes the folder `dir` and everything under it as members below `name`, folders before what they hold, links as links. Fails as `add_zip_file` and `fs.walk` fail.
- `function finish_zip(@w: ZipWriter, comment: str) -> ()?`, called `archive.finish_zip(@w, comment)`: Writes the central directory and the end records, with the archive's `comment`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record ZipMember(entry: ZipEntry, data: [u8])`: A member of a zip archive with its data, whole: what `encode_zip` takes.
- `function encode_zip(members: [ZipMember], comment: str) -> [u8]?`, called `archive.encode_zip(members, comment)`: `members` as the bytes of a zip archive: each member written whole, compressed by its entry's method at level 6, then the central directory with `comment`. Fails as `write_zip_entry` and `finish_zip` fail.


### sql/postgres

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/sql/postgres`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/postgres/).

A PostgreSQL client written in Heroes: it speaks the database's own frontend/backend protocol, version 3.0, over a TCP connection of `net`, and links no library of PostgreSQL.

- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `5432`: The port PostgreSQL listens on unless it is told another.
- `variant Security = .plain | .checked(roots: str) | .direct(roots: str)`: How the connection to the server is secured.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, user: str, password: str, database: str, application_name: str, deadline: time.Duration, security: Security)`: Where a database is and who logs into it.
- `function options(host: str, user: str, database: str) -> Options`, called `postgres.options(host: host, user: user, database: database)`: The options of a connection to `database` on `host` at `DEFAULT_PORT` as `user`, with no password, no application name and no deadline, over TLS checked against the system's own store.
- `function parse_url(url: str) -> Options?`, called `postgres.parse_url(url)`: The options a `postgres://` or `postgresql://` URL names, as libpq reads one: `postgres://user:password@host:port/database?application_name=app`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function open(opts: Options) -> Db?`, called `postgres.open(opts)`: A connection to the database `opts` names, logged in and ready for a statement. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `not_found`, `closed`, `limit`.
- `function close(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `postgres.close(@db)`: Ends the connection: tells the server it is leaving, then closes the socket, and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(db: Db) -> bool`, called `postgres.is_closed(db)`: Whether `close` has emptied `db`, or a failure the server called `FATAL` or a lost connection has ended it.
- `function ping(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `postgres.ping(@db)`: Asks the server whether the connection still works, with a statement that does nothing. Fails `closed`, `timeout`.
- `record Db(session: session.Session)`: A connection to a PostgreSQL server, which `open` makes and `close` ends.
- `variant Transaction = .idle | .open | .failed`: The transaction a connection stands in.
- `record Notice(severity: str, code: str, message: str)`: A warning or a notice the server sent beside an answer, as a `RAISE NOTICE` or a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` of a table that was not there does.
- `function in_transaction(db: Db) -> bool`, called `postgres.in_transaction(db)`: Whether a transaction is open on `db`, as the server said after its last answer: after `begin` until `commit` or `rollback` ends it, a failed one included; the contract's question, which `transaction_of` answers in full.
- `function transaction_of(db: Db) -> Transaction`, called `postgres.transaction_of(db)`: The transaction `db` stands in, as the server said after its last answer.
- `function parameter_of(db: Db, name: str) -> str?`, called `postgres.parameter_of(db, name)`: The value of the run-time parameter `name` as the server reported it: `server_version`, `server_encoding`, `TimeZone`, `DateStyle`, `integer_datetimes`, `standard_conforming_strings`, `application_name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function take_notices(@db: Db) -> [Notice]`, called `postgres.take_notices(@db)`: The warnings and notices the server sent since the last call, oldest first, and empties the connection's list.
- `function exec(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `postgres.exec(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement`, one statement that answers no rows, with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers how many rows it changed. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `postgres.query(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its columns and every row it answered. Fails `invalid`.
- `function query_one(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Row?`, called `postgres.query_one(@db, statement, params)`: The first row `statement` answers, with `params` bound to its placeholders. Fails `not_found`.
- `function exec_script(@db: Db, script: str) -> ()?`, called `postgres.exec_script(@db, script)`: Runs every statement of `script`, separated by semicolons, in order and with no parameters, as a migration does. Fails with the first failure, as `exec` does.
- `record Statement(name: str, text: str, parameter_types: [i64], columns: [sql.Column], column_types: [i64])`: A statement the server has read and planned, which `prepare` makes and `close_statement` ends.
- `function prepare(@db: Db, statement: str) -> Statement?`, called `postgres.prepare(@db, statement)`: `statement` read and planned by the server once, to be run many times with `exec_prepared` and `query_prepared`. Fails with the database's failure where the statement is not one it can plan, as `exec` does.
- `function exec_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `postgres.exec_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, as `exec` runs a statement. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `postgres.query_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its rows, as `query` does. Fails as `exec_prepared` does.
- `function close_statement(@db: Db, @prepared: Statement) -> ()?`, called `postgres.close_statement(@db, @prepared)`: Ends `prepared` on the server and empties its name, so every later run of it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function begin(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `postgres.begin(@db)`: Opens a transaction: the statements after it commit together at `commit`, or none of them does, at `rollback`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function commit(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `postgres.commit(@db)`: Commits the open transaction: every statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function rollback(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `postgres.rollback(@db)`: Rolls the open transaction back: no statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`.


### sql/sqlite

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/sql/sqlite`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/sqlite/).

SQLite from Heroes: a database in a file or in memory, run inside the program through SQLite's own C library, with the API every driver of Rebel keeps over `sql`'s types, name for name, as `sql`'s opening comment writes it: `open`, `close`, `is_closed`, `ping`, `exec`, `query`, `query_one`, `exec_script`, `prepare`, `exec_prepared`, `query_prepared`, `close_statement`, `begin`, `commit`, `rollback` and `in_transaction`.

- `function open(path: str) -> Db?`, called `sqlite.open(path)`: A connection to the database in the file at `path`, made where it is not there yet, ready for a statement. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `permission`, `failed`.
- `function open_read_only(path: str) -> Db?`, called `sqlite.open_read_only(path)`: A connection to the database in the file at `path` that reads and never writes: a statement that would change it fails `permission`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function open_memory() -> Db?`, called `sqlite.open_memory()`: A connection to a new database in memory, empty, which no other connection reaches and which ends with `close`. Fails `limit`.
- `function close(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.close(@db)`: Ends the connection: SQLite rolls back a transaction still open, gives back the statements `exec` and `query` kept, and closes the file; the place is emptied, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function is_closed(db: Db) -> bool`, called `sqlite.is_closed(db)`: Whether `close` has ended `db`.
- `function set_busy_timeout(@db: Db, timeout: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.set_busy_timeout(@db, timeout)`: Sets how long a statement on `db` waits for a lock another connection holds before it fails `timeout`. Fails `invalid`, `timeout`, `closed`.
- `record Db(connection: hero_sqlite3.Connection, path: str, transaction_open: bool, busy_timeout: time.Duration, cached: [statements.Cached], prepared: i64)`: A connection to a SQLite database, which `open`, `open_read_only` or `open_memory` makes and `close` ends.
- `function ping(db: Db) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.ping(db)`: Answers whether the connection still works: SQLite runs in this process, so a connection that is open works, and nothing is asked of the database. Fails `closed`.
- `function in_transaction(db: Db) -> bool`, called `sqlite.in_transaction(db)`: Whether a transaction is open on `db`: after `begin`, or a `BEGIN` run as a statement, until `commit` or `rollback` ends it, or SQLite rolls it back on a failure of the disk or of memory.
- `function total_changes(db: Db) -> i64?`, called `sqlite.total_changes(db)`: How many rows every statement on `db` has inserted, changed or deleted since it opened, those a trigger changed included. Fails `closed`.
- `function exec(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `sqlite.exec(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement`, one statement that answers no rows, with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers how many rows it changed. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `sqlite.query(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its columns and every row it answered. Fails `invalid`.
- `function query_one(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Row?`, called `sqlite.query_one(@db, statement, params)`: The first row `statement` answers, with `params` bound to its placeholders. Fails `not_found`.
- `function exec_script(@db: Db, script: str) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.exec_script(@db, script)`: Runs every statement of `script`, separated by semicolons, in order and with no parameters, as a migration does. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Statement(compiled: hero_sqlite3.Compiled, text: str, parameter_count: i64, columns: [sql.Column])`: A statement SQLite has compiled, which `prepare` makes and `close_statement` ends.
- `function prepare(@db: Db, statement: str) -> Statement?`, called `sqlite.prepare(@db, statement)`: `statement` compiled by SQLite once, to be run many times with `exec_prepared` and `query_prepared`. Fails as `exec` does where the statement is not one SQLite can compile.
- `function exec_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `sqlite.exec_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, as `exec` runs a statement. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `sqlite.query_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its rows, as `query` does. Fails as `exec_prepared` does.
- `function close_statement(@db: Db, @prepared: Statement) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.close_statement(@db, @prepared)`: Gives `prepared` back to SQLite and empties it, so every later run of it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function begin(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.begin(@db)`: Opens a transaction: the statements after it commit together at `commit`, or none of them does, at `rollback`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function commit(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.commit(@db)`: Commits the open transaction: every statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `function rollback(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.rollback(@db)`: Rolls the open transaction back: no statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`.
- `function backup(db: Db, into: Db) -> ()?`, called `sqlite.backup(db: db, into: into)`: Copies the whole database of `db` into the database of `into`, replacing what `into` held: a database in memory saved to a file, or a file read into memory. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `function is_complete(text: str) -> bool`, called `sqlite.is_complete(text)`: Whether `text` ends a whole statement: its last statement ends with a semicolon outside every quote, comment and trigger body.
- `function version() -> str`, called `sqlite.version()`: The version of the SQLite library the program runs with, `3.54.0` and on.


### sql/mysql

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/sql/mysql`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/mysql/).

A MySQL and MariaDB client written in Heroes: it speaks the servers' own client/server protocol, 4.1, over a TCP connection of `net`, and links no library of either.

- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `3306`: The port MySQL and MariaDB listen on unless told another.
- `variant Security = .plain | .checked(roots: str)`: How the connection to the server is secured.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, user: str, password: str, database: str, application_name: str, deadline: time.Duration, security: Security)`: Where a database is and who logs into it.
- `function options(host: str, user: str, database: str) -> Options`, called `mysql.options(host: host, user: user, database: database)`: The options of a connection to `database` on `host` at `DEFAULT_PORT` as `user`, with no password, no application name and no deadline, over TLS checked against the system's own store.
- `function parse_url(url: str) -> Options?`, called `mysql.parse_url(url)`: The options a `mysql://` or `mariadb://` URL names, as MySQL Shell reads one: `mysql://user:password@host:port/database?ssl-mode=DISABLED`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function open(opts: Options) -> Db?`, called `mysql.open(opts)`: A connection to the database `opts` names, logged in and ready for a statement. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`, `not_found`, `limit`, `closed`.
- `function close(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `mysql.close(@db)`: Ends the connection: tells the server it is leaving, then closes the socket, and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(db: Db) -> bool`, called `mysql.is_closed(db)`: Whether `close` has emptied `db`, or a failure that ends a connection or a lost connection has ended it.
- `function ping(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `mysql.ping(@db)`: Asks the server whether the connection still works (`COM_PING`). Fails `closed`, `timeout`.
- `record Db(session: session.Session)`: A connection to a MySQL or MariaDB server, which `open` makes and `close` ends.
- `function in_transaction(db: Db) -> bool`, called `mysql.in_transaction(db)`: Whether a transaction is open on `db`, as the server's status said after its last answer: after `begin`, or a `BEGIN` run as a statement, until `commit` or `rollback` ends it.
- `function server_version_of(db: Db) -> str`, called `mysql.server_version_of(db)`: The server's version as its greeting wrote it: `8.4.3` for MySQL, `5.5.5-10.11.6-MariaDB` or `11.4.2-MariaDB` for MariaDB.
- `function is_mariadb(db: Db) -> bool`, called `mysql.is_mariadb(db)`: Whether the server is MariaDB, as its version says.
- `function connection_id_of(db: Db) -> i64`, called `mysql.connection_id_of(db)`: The server's number for this connection, as its greeting said it: what `KILL QUERY` names from another connection to stop a statement running here, and `CONNECTION_ID()` answers.
- `function warning_count_of(db: Db) -> i64`, called `mysql.warning_count_of(db)`: How many warnings the last statement raised, as its answer counted them; `SHOW WARNINGS` reads them.
- `function quote_identifier(name: str) -> str?`, called `mysql.quote_identifier(name)`: `name` as MySQL quotes an identifier: inside backquotes, each backquote in it doubled. Fails `invalid`.
- `function exec(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `mysql.exec(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement`, one statement that answers no rows, with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers how many rows it changed and the id it made. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `mysql.query(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its columns and every row it answered. Fails `invalid`.
- `function query_one(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Row?`, called `mysql.query_one(@db, statement, params)`: The first row `statement` answers, with `params` bound to its placeholders. Fails `not_found`.
- `function exec_script(@db: Db, script: str) -> ()?`, called `mysql.exec_script(@db, script)`: Runs every statement of `script`, separated by semicolons, in order and with no parameters, as a migration does. Fails with the first failure, as `exec` does; the statements after it do not run.
- `record Statement(id: i64, text: str, parameter_count: i64, columns: [sql.Column])`: A statement the server has read and planned, which `prepare` makes and `close_statement` ends.
- `function prepare(@db: Db, statement: str) -> Statement?`, called `mysql.prepare(@db, statement)`: `statement` read and planned by the server once, to be run many times with `exec_prepared` and `query_prepared`. Fails with the server's failure where the statement is not one it can prepare, as `exec` does.
- `function exec_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `mysql.exec_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, as `exec` runs a statement. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `mysql.query_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its rows, as `query` does. Fails as `exec_prepared` does.
- `function close_statement(@db: Db, @prepared: Statement) -> ()?`, called `mysql.close_statement(@db, @prepared)`: Ends `prepared` on the server and empties its number, so every later run of it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function begin(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `mysql.begin(@db)`: Opens a transaction (`START TRANSACTION`): the statements after it commit together at `commit`, or none of them does, at `rollback`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function commit(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `mysql.commit(@db)`: Commits the open transaction: every statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rollback(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `mysql.rollback(@db)`: Rolls the open transaction back: no statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`.


### redis

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/redis`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/redis/).

A Redis client written in Heroes: it speaks RESP, the Redis serialization protocol, versions 2 and 3, over a TCP connection of `net` or a TLS connection of `tls`, and links no library.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an argument refused, a reply that is not of the kind asked for, bytes that are no RESP, and an error the server replies for a command it could not run as written: `call`, the readers, `decode`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a key or a reply that holds nothing (`get`, the readers on a null), of a script or a group the server does not know, and of a lock that is no longer this holder's (`unlock`, `renew`).
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a lock another holds (`try_lock`) and of a consumer group that exists already.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a login refused and of a command the user may not run.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a client that is closed, or whose connection the server or the network closed while the call waited.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a call whose deadline passed, and of `lock` waiting past its time.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The code of a call that ended because the program was asked to stop.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a server that has no more memory or connections, and of a reply past what the client reads.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a command the server does not know, a cluster's redirection, and a protocol the server does not speak.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of every other error the server replies; the message carries its word and its words.
- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `6379`: The port Redis listens on unless told another.
- `variant Security = .plain | .checked(roots: str)`: How the connection to the server is secured.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, username: str, password: str, database: i64, protocol: i64, client_name: str, deadline: time.Duration, security: Security)`: Where a server is and how to log in.
- `function options(host: str) -> Options`, called `redis.options(host)`: The options of a connection to `host` at `DEFAULT_PORT`, as the `default` user with no password, database 0, RESP3, no name and no deadline, over TLS checked against the system's own store.
- `function parse_url(text: str) -> Options?`, called `redis.parse_url(text)`: The options a `redis://` or `rediss://` URL names, as redis-py and go-redis read one: `redis://user:password@host:port/database`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Client?`, called `redis.connect(opts)`: A connection to the server `opts` names, logged in, its protocol agreed and its database selected. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `closed`.
- `function close(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `redis.close(@c)`: Closes the connection and empties the client, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(c: Client) -> bool`, called `redis.is_closed(c)`: Whether `close` has emptied `c`, or a lost connection or bytes that are no RESP have ended it.
- `function protocol_of(c: Client) -> i64`, called `redis.protocol_of(c)`: The protocol the server speaks with `c`: 3 for RESP3, 2 for RESP2.
- `function set_deadline(c: Client, deadline: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `redis.set_deadline(c, deadline)`: Moves the deadline of `c`'s connection: every later wait on it, a `receive` among them, ends by `deadline` from now, failing `timeout`. Fails `closed`.
- `record Client(session: session.Session)`: A connection to a Redis server, which `connect` makes and `close` ends.
- `variant Reply = .simple(v: str) | .error(code: str, message: str) | .integer(v: i64) | .bulk(v: [u8]) | .null_value | .array(items: [Reply]) | .mapping(entries: [Entry]) | .set(items: [Reply]) | .double(v: f64) | .boolean(v: bool) | .big_number(v: str) | .verbatim(format: str, v: str) | .pushed(items: [Reply])`: A reply, as RESP writes one: each case one of its types.
- `record Entry(key: Reply, value: Reply)`: One entry of a map.
- `variant Decoded = .whole(reply: Reply, next: i64) | .partial`: What `decode_next` found at a place in bytes read so far: a whole reply, or bytes that end inside one that more bytes may complete.
- `function decode(data: [u8]) -> Reply?`, called `redis.decode(data)`: The one reply `data` holds, with nothing after it. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_next(data: [u8], from: i64) -> Decoded?`, called `redis.decode_next(data, from)`: The reply that begins at byte `from` of `data` and where the next begins, or that the bytes end inside it: what a reader holding the bytes a connection has sent so far asks, to read more or to refuse. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_command(words: [[u8]]) -> [u8]`, called `redis.encode_command(words)`: The bytes of the command `words` as RESP writes one: an array of bulk strings, which every version of Redis reads.
- `function checked(r: Reply) -> Reply?`, called `redis.checked(r)`: `r` itself where it is no error, else the failure the error tells: its code chosen by its word, its message its word in brackets and its words. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `not_found`, `exists`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function error_code_of(msg: str) -> str?`, called `redis.error_code_of(msg)`: The word an error reply's failure was told with: `WRONGTYPE` in `[WRONGTYPE] Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function kind_of(r: Reply) -> str`, called `redis.kind_of(r)`: The name of the case `r` is, as a failure's message names it: `a simple string`, `an integer`, `a map`.
- `function is_null(r: Reply) -> bool`, called `redis.is_null(r)`: Whether `r` is null: RESP3's null, or RESP2's null bulk string or null array, as `GET` of a key that is not there answers.
- `function text_of(r: Reply) -> str?`, called `redis.text_of(r)`: The text `r` holds: a simple string, a bulk string's bytes, a verbatim string's text, a big number's digits. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function bytes_of(r: Reply) -> [u8]?`, called `redis.bytes_of(r)`: The bytes `r` holds: a bulk string's, or the text of a simple string, a verbatim string or a big number. Fails as `text_of` does, but never for bytes that are not UTF-8.
- `function int_of(r: Reply) -> i64?`, called `redis.int_of(r)`: The integer `r` holds: an integer, or a string of decimal digits, as RESP2 answers `HGET` of a counter. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function float_of(r: Reply) -> f64?`, called `redis.float_of(r)`: The number `r` holds: a double, an integer, or a string that writes one, as RESP2 answers `ZSCORE` and `INCRBYFLOAT`, `inf` and `-inf` included. Fails as `int_of` does.
- `function bool_of(r: Reply) -> bool?`, called `redis.bool_of(r)`: The truth `r` holds: a boolean, or the integer 0 or 1, as RESP2 answers `EXPIRE` and `SISMEMBER`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function list_of(r: Reply) -> [Reply]?`, called `redis.list_of(r)`: The elements `r` holds: an array's, a set's or a push's, in order. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function texts_of(r: Reply) -> [str]?`, called `redis.texts_of(r)`: The text of each element `r` holds, as `list_of` and `text_of` read them: what `KEYS`, `SMEMBERS` and `LRANGE` answer. Fails `not_found`.
- `function entries_of(r: Reply) -> [Entry]?`, called `redis.entries_of(r)`: The entries `r` holds: a map's, or the keys and values in turn of an array or a set of even length, as RESP2 answers `HGETALL` and `CONFIG GET`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function send(@c: Client, words: [[u8]]) -> ()?`, called `redis.send(@c, words)`: Writes the command `words` to the server without reading its reply, which `read_reply` reads: a pipeline written by hand. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function read_reply(@c: Client) -> Reply?`, called `redis.read_reply(@c)`: The next reply the server sends, waiting until it comes; an error reply is answered as `.error`, not a failure. Fails `closed`, `timeout`, `invalid`.
- `function call(@c: Client, words: [str]) -> Reply?`, called `redis.call(@c, words)`: Runs the command `words` and answers its reply. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function call_bytes(@c: Client, words: [[u8]]) -> Reply?`, called `redis.call_bytes(@c, words)`: Runs the command `words`, arguments of any bytes, and answers its reply. Fails as `call` does.
- `function get(@c: Client, key: str) -> str?`, called `redis.get(@c, key)`: The text `key` holds (`GET`). Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function set(@c: Client, key: str, value: str) -> ()?`, called `redis.set(@c, key: key, value: value)`: Sets `key` to `value`, with no time to live (`SET`). Fails as `call` does.
- `function set_for(@c: Client, key: str, value: str, ttl: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `redis.set_for(@c, key: key, value: value, ttl)`: Sets `key` to `value` for `ttl`, after which it is gone (`SET key value PX ttl`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function delete(@c: Client, names: [str]) -> i64?`, called `redis.delete(@c, names)`: Deletes each of `names`, and answers how many were there (`DEL`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function increment(@c: Client, key: str, by: i64) -> i64?`, called `redis.increment(@c, key, by)`: Adds `by` to the integer `key` holds, 0 where it is not there, and answers the sum (`INCRBY`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function pipeline(@c: Client, commands: [[str]]) -> [Reply]?`, called `redis.pipeline(@c, commands)`: Runs every command of `commands` in one round trip, all written before any reply is read, and answers their replies in order. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `record Transaction(committed: bool, replies: [Reply])`: What a transaction answered.
- `function transaction(@c: Client, commands: [[str]]) -> Transaction?`, called `redis.transaction(@c, commands)`: Runs every command of `commands` as one transaction (`MULTI`, the commands, `EXEC`): no other client's command runs between them, and none of them runs where a key `watch` named has changed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function watch(@c: Client, names: [str]) -> ()?`, called `redis.watch(@c, names)`: Watches `names`: the next `transaction` on this client runs none of its commands where another client has changed one of them since (`WATCH`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function unwatch(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `redis.unwatch(@c)`: Forgets the keys `watch` named (`UNWATCH`); a transaction does the same when it ends. Fails as `call` does.
- `record Message(kind: str, pattern: str, channel: str, payload: [u8])`: A message published to a channel the client is subscribed to.
- `function publish(@c: Client, channel: str, message: str) -> i64?`, called `redis.publish(@c, channel: channel, message: message)`: Posts `message` to `channel`, and answers how many clients received it (`PUBLISH`). Fails as `call` does.
- `function subscribe(@c: Client, channels: [str]) -> ()?`, called `redis.subscribe(@c, channels)`: Subscribes to `channels`, waiting until the server confirms each (`SUBSCRIBE`); `receive` then reads their messages. Fails `invalid`.
- `function psubscribe(@c: Client, patterns: [str]) -> ()?`, called `redis.psubscribe(@c, patterns)`: Subscribes to every channel whose name matches one of `patterns`, as `subscribe` does by name (`PSUBSCRIBE`). Fails as `subscribe` does.
- `function unsubscribe(@c: Client, channels: [str]) -> ()?`, called `redis.unsubscribe(@c, channels)`: Ends the subscriptions to `channels`, or to every channel where it is empty, waiting until the server confirms each (`UNSUBSCRIBE`). Fails as `call` does.
- `function punsubscribe(@c: Client, patterns: [str]) -> ()?`, called `redis.punsubscribe(@c, patterns)`: Ends the subscriptions to `patterns`, or to every pattern where it is empty (`PUNSUBSCRIBE`). Fails as `call` does.
- `function message_of(r: Reply) -> Message?`, called `redis.message_of(r)`: The message a reply carries: a push of RESP3, or an array of RESP2 read while subscribed, whose first element names it `message`, `pmessage` or `smessage`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function receive(@c: Client) -> Message?`, called `redis.receive(@c)`: The next message of a channel the client is subscribed to, waiting until one comes; one kept while a reply was awaited comes first. Fails `invalid`, `timeout`, `closed`.
- `record Lock(key: str, token: str, ttl: time.Duration, fence: i64)`: A lock `try_lock` or `lock` took, which `unlock` gives back.
- `function try_lock(@c: Client, key: str, ttl: time.Duration) -> Lock?`, called `redis.try_lock(@c, key, ttl)`: Takes the lock `key` where nobody holds it, for `ttl`, trying once. Fails `exists`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function lock(@c: Client, key: str, ttl: time.Duration, wait: time.Duration) -> Lock?`, called `redis.lock(@c, key, ttl: ttl, wait: wait)`: Takes the lock `key`, trying again until `wait` has passed, each wait after a refusal longer than the one before, from 10 to 250 milliseconds, with a random part so two waiters do not try together. Fails `timeout`, `invalid`.
- `function unlock(@c: Client, held: Lock) -> ()?`, called `redis.unlock(@c, held)`: Gives `held` back: deletes its key, only where it still holds this holder's token, by a script the server runs whole. Fails `not_found`.
- `function renew(@c: Client, held: Lock) -> ()?`, called `redis.renew(@c, held)`: Extends `held` by its time to live, from now, only where it still holds this holder's token. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_held(@c: Client, held: Lock) -> bool?`, called `redis.is_held(@c, held)`: Whether `held`'s key still holds this holder's token: true until it expires or is given back. Fails as `call` does.


### sql/build

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/sql/build`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/build/).
