Queries as values: a SELECT, an INSERT, an UPDATE or a DELETE built by functions and composed as any value is, then written by `to_sql` as the text and the parameters a driver of Rebel runs, with each database's own placeholders: `$1` for PostgreSQL, `?1` for SQLite.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a query `to_sql` refuses: a name that is empty or holds a zero byte, a row of the wrong length, an UPDATE or a DELETE with no condition, a `NULL` where no comparison can match it, a fragment, an operator or a type that could carry a value.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of what one dialect writes and the one asked does not: `to_sql`.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a statement with more parameters than PostgreSQL's protocol carries, 65,535: `to_sql`.
- `variant Dialect = .postgres | .sqlite`: The database a statement is written for: the placeholders it reads and what it supports.
- `record Statement(text: str, params: [sql.Value])`: A statement as a driver takes it: `postgres.query(@db, s.text, s.params)`.
- `record Expr(part: clauses.Part)`: A value a statement computes: a column, a parameter, a function's call, an operation.
- `function column(name: str) -> Expr`, called `build.column(name)`: The column `name`: `"name"`, or `"users"."id"` for `users.id`.
- `function columns_named(names: [str]) -> [Expr]`, called `build.columns_named(names)`: The columns `names`, in order, as `column` makes each one.
- `function every_column() -> Expr`, called `build.every_column()`: Every column of every table a SELECT reads: `*`.
- `function every_column_of(name: str) -> Expr`, called `build.every_column_of(name)`: Every column of the table `name`: `"users".*`.
- `function parameter(v: sql.Value) -> Expr`, called `build.parameter(v)`: The value `v`, as a parameter: `$1` or `?1`, with `v` in the statement's `params`.
- `function call(name: str, arguments: [Expr]) -> Expr`, called `build.call(name, arguments)`: A call of the function of SQL `name` on `arguments`: `lower("name")`, `coalesce("nick", $1)`.
- `function call_distinct(name: str, arguments: [Expr]) -> Expr`, called `build.call_distinct(name, arguments)`: A call of the aggregate `name` on the distinct values of `arguments` alone: `count(DISTINCT "city")`.
- `function count_all() -> Expr`, called `build.count_all()`: The count of the rows: `count(*)`.
- `function cast(e: Expr, type_name: str) -> Expr`, called `build.cast(e, type_name)`: `e` read as the type `type_name`: `CAST($1 AS uuid)`.
- `function operation(left: Expr, operator: str, right: Expr) -> Expr`, called `build.operation(left: left, operator, right: right)`: `left` and `right` joined by `operator`: `"price" * "quantity"`, `"first" || $1`.
- `function aliased(e: Expr, alias: str) -> Expr`, called `build.aliased(e, alias)`: `e` under the other name `alias`: `count(*) AS "total"`.
- `function excluded(name: str) -> Expr`, called `build.excluded(name)`: The value an INSERT proposed for the column `name` and could not insert, inside its `do_update`: `excluded."count"`.
- `function subquery(query: Select) -> Expr`, called `build.subquery(query)`: `query` as a value inside another statement, in parentheses: a column computed by a SELECT, or the operand of `in_query`.
- `record When(condition: Condition, result: Expr)`: What a `choose` answers where `condition` holds.
- `function choose(whens: [When], otherwise: Expr) -> Expr`, called `build.choose(whens, otherwise)`: The `result` of the first of `whens` whose condition holds, `otherwise` where none does: `CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END`.
- `function raw_without_values(text: str) -> Expr`, called `build.raw_without_values(text)`: A fragment of SQL written as it is, for what this package does not offer: `raw_without_values("CURRENT_DATE")`.
- `record Condition(clause: clauses.Clause)`: A condition a row holds or not: built by the functions under this heading and combined by `all_of`, `any_of` and `negate`.
- `variant Op = .equal | .not_equal | .less | .less_or_equal | .greater | .greater_or_equal | .like | .other(operator: str)`: How `compare` compares.
- `function equal(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.equal(name, value)`: Whether the column `name` holds `value`: `"name" = $1`, or `"left_at" IS NULL` where `value` is `NULL`, since `= NULL` holds for no row.
- `function not_equal(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.not_equal(name, value)`: Whether the column `name` holds another value than `value`: `"name" <> $1`, or `"left_at" IS NOT NULL` where `value` is `NULL`.
- `function less(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.less(name, value)`: Whether the column `name` holds less than `value`: `"age" < $1`.
- `function less_or_equal(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.less_or_equal(name, value)`: Whether the column `name` holds at most `value`: `"age" <= $1`.
- `function greater(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.greater(name, value)`: Whether the column `name` holds more than `value`: `"age" > $1`.
- `function greater_or_equal(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.greater_or_equal(name, value)`: Whether the column `name` holds at least `value`: `"age" >= $1`.
- `function like(name: str, pattern: str) -> Condition`, called `build.like(name: name, pattern: pattern)`: Whether the text in the column `name` matches `pattern`: `"name" LIKE $1 ESCAPE $2`, where `%` matches any text and `_` any one character.
- `function escape_like(text: str) -> str`, called `build.escape_like(text)`: `text` with a backslash before each `%`, `_` and backslash, so that `like` matches it as itself: `escape_like(s) + "%"` matches what begins with `s`.
- `function in_values(name: str, values: [sql.Value]) -> Condition`, called `build.in_values(name, values)`: Whether the column `name` holds one of `values`: `"id" IN ($1, $2, $3)`.
- `function between(name: str, low: sql.Value, high: sql.Value) -> Condition`, called `build.between(name, low: low, high: high)`: Whether the column `name` holds a value from `low` to `high`, both included: `"age" BETWEEN $1 AND $2`.
- `function columns_equal(left: str, right: str) -> Condition`, called `build.columns_equal(left: left, right: right)`: Whether two columns hold the same value: `"users"."id" = "posts"."user_id"`, as a join's condition is.
- `function compare(left: Expr, op: Op, right: Expr) -> Condition`, called `build.compare(left: left, op, right: right)`: Whether `left` and `right` compare by `op`: the general form of `equal` and the rest, for any two expressions.
- `function in_query(name: str, query: Select) -> Condition`, called `build.in_query(name, query)`: Whether the column `name` holds a value among the rows `query` answers: `"id" IN (SELECT ...)`.
- `function exists(query: Select) -> Condition`, called `build.exists(query)`: Whether `query` answers at least one row: `EXISTS (SELECT ...)`.
- `function all_of(conditions: [Condition]) -> Condition`, called `build.all_of(conditions)`: Whether every one of `conditions` holds: each in parentheses where it is an `any_of`, joined by `AND`.
- `function any_of(conditions: [Condition]) -> Condition`, called `build.any_of(conditions)`: Whether at least one of `conditions` holds: each in parentheses where it is an `all_of`, joined by `OR`.
- `function negate(condition: Condition) -> Condition`, called `build.negate(condition)`: Whether `condition` does not hold: `NOT (...)`.
- `function holds(e: Expr) -> Condition`, called `build.holds(e)`: The condition that `e` is true: a column of booleans, or a fragment `raw_without_values` writes.
- `function every_row() -> Condition`, called `build.every_row()`: The condition every row holds, `1 = 1`, which an UPDATE or a DELETE meant for every row of its table names in its `where`: one with an empty `where` fails `to_sql` `invalid`.
- `record Table(pieces: [tokens.Token])`: A table a statement reads, under its own name or another, or a subquery read as one.
- `function table(name: str) -> Table`, called `build.table(name)`: The table `name`: `"users"`, `"app"."users"`.
- `function table_as(name: str, alias: str) -> Table`, called `build.table_as(name: name, alias: alias)`: The table `name` under the other name `alias`, which the query's columns name it by: `"users" AS "u"`.
- `function from_subquery(query: Select, alias: str) -> Table`, called `build.from_subquery(query, alias)`: The rows of `query` read as a table named `alias`: `(SELECT ...) AS "recent"`.
- `variant JoinKind = .inner | .left | .right | .full | .cross`: How a join keeps rows that find no match.
- `record Join(kind: JoinKind, table: Table, on: [Condition])`: A table joined to the ones a SELECT reads before it.
- `function inner_join(name: str, on: Condition) -> Join`, called `build.inner_join(name, on)`: The table `name` names, joined where `on` holds, keeping only the rows that match.
- `function left_join(name: str, on: Condition) -> Join`, called `build.left_join(name, on)`: The table `name` names, joined where `on` holds, keeping every row before it.
- `function right_join(name: str, on: Condition) -> Join`, called `build.right_join(name, on)`: The table `name` names, joined where `on` holds, keeping every row of that table.
- `function full_join(name: str, on: Condition) -> Join`, called `build.full_join(name, on)`: The table `name` names, joined where `on` holds, keeping every row of both sides.
- `function cross_join(name: str) -> Join`, called `build.cross_join(name)`: The table `name` names, joined with no condition: each row with each of its rows.
- `variant NullsAt = .database_default | .first | .last`: Where `NULL` goes in an order.
- `record Order(by: Expr, descending: bool, nulls: NullsAt)`: One key of a SELECT's order.
- `function ascending(name: str) -> Order`, called `build.ascending(name)`: The order by the column `name` from the smallest up, `NULL` where the database puts it.
- `function descending(name: str) -> Order`, called `build.descending(name)`: The order by the column `name` from the largest down, `NULL` where the database puts it.
- `variant SetOperation = .union_distinct | .union_all | .intersect_distinct | .intersect_all | .except_distinct | .except_all`: How a SELECT's rows are combined with another's.
- `record Combined(operation: SetOperation, query: Select)`: A SELECT whose rows are combined with the rows before it.
- `record Select(distinct: bool, columns: [Expr], from: [Table], joins: [Join], where: [Condition], group_by: [Expr], having: [Condition], order_by: [Order], limit: i64?, offset: i64?, combined: [Combined])`: A SELECT.
- `function select(from: str, columns: [Expr]) -> Select`, called `build.select(from, columns)`: The SELECT of `columns` from the table `from`, every other part empty.
- `variant Source = .rows(values: [[sql.Value]]) | .query(select: Select) | .defaults`: What an INSERT inserts.
- `record Assignment(column: str, value: Expr)`: A column and the value an UPDATE, or an INSERT's `do_update`, gives it.
- `function assign(name: str, value: sql.Value) -> Assignment`, called `build.assign(name, value)`: The column `name` given `value`, a parameter: `"name" = $1`.
- `variant Conflict = .unhandled | .do_nothing(target: [str]) | .do_update(target: [str], set: [Assignment])`: What an INSERT does with a row a unique key already holds.
- `record Insert(into: str, columns: [str], source: Source, conflict: Conflict, returning: [Expr])`: An INSERT.
- `function insert(into: str, columns: [str], rows: [[sql.Value]]) -> Insert`, called `build.insert(into, columns, rows)`: The INSERT of `rows` into `columns` of `into`.
- `function insert_select(into: str, columns: [str], query: Select) -> Insert`, called `build.insert_select(into, columns, query)`: The INSERT of the rows `query` answers into `columns` of `into`.
- `record Update(table: str, set: [Assignment], where: [Condition], returning: [Expr])`: An UPDATE.
- `function update(name: str, set: [Assignment]) -> Update`, called `build.update(name, set)`: The UPDATE of the table `name` that makes `set`'s changes, with no condition yet: a program sets `where` before `to_sql`, which refuses it empty.
- `record Delete(from: str, where: [Condition], returning: [Expr])`: A DELETE.
- `function delete(from: str) -> Delete`, called `build.delete(from)`: The DELETE from `from`, with no condition yet: a program sets `where` before `to_sql`, which refuses it empty.
- `variant Query = .select(query: Select) | .insert(query: Insert) | .update(query: Update) | .delete(query: Delete)`: A statement `to_sql` writes.
- `function to_sql(query: Query, dialect: Dialect) -> Statement?`, called `build.to_sql(query, dialect)`: `query` written for `dialect`: its text, every name quoted and every value a placeholder, and the values in order. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.


### http2

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/http2`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/http2/).

HTTP/2 (RFC 9113) and its header compression HPACK (RFC 7541), client and server, over a `tls` stream whose ALPN chose `h2` or over a plain stream by prior knowledge (h2c): many requests at once on one connection, each on a stream of its own.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A frame, a header block or an argument that RFC 9113 or RFC 7541 refuses; the message names the RFC's error and says what was found.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A bound of `Limits` or of the settings passed by the peer, or a body past `Limits.body_bytes`.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: A header field that is not UTF-8: `decode_fields`, and a session's peer.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection or the stream is closed, reset, or past the peer's GOAWAY.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A name with no address, or an error code with no name: `connect`, `connect_plain`, `error_name`, `frame_name`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A server whose TLS chose another protocol than `h2`: `connect`.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The time a connection allows ran out: the connection's functions.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while a connection waited.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason no other code names.
- `record Priority(exclusive: bool, depends_on: i64, weight: i64)`: A stream's priority as RFC 7540 § 5.3 wrote it, which RFC 9113 deprecates: read from HEADERS and PRIORITY frames and ignored by a session, written by a program that sends frames itself.
- `record Setting(id: i64, value: i64)`: One setting of a SETTINGS frame.
- `variant Frame = .data(stream: i64, data: [u8], end_stream: bool, padding: i64) | .headers(stream: i64, block: [u8], end_stream: bool, end_headers: bool, padding: i64, priority: Priority?) | .priority(stream: i64, priority: Priority) | .rst_stream(stream: i64, error: i64) | .settings(ack: bool, settings: [Setting]) | .push_promise(stream: i64, promised: i64, block: [u8], end_headers: bool, padding: i64) | .ping(ack: bool, data: [u8]) | .goaway(last_stream: i64, error: i64, debug: [u8]) | .window_update(stream: i64, increment: i64) | .continuation(stream: i64, block: [u8], end_headers: bool) | .unknown(kind: i64, flags: i64, stream: i64, payload: [u8])`: One frame (RFC 9113 § 6): what `decode_frame` and `read_frame` answer and `encode_frame` and `write_frame` take.
- `function encode_frame(f: Frame) -> [u8]?`, called `http2.encode_frame(f)`: The bytes of `f` on the wire: its head of nine bytes, then its payload. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_frame(data: [u8], max_size: i64) -> Frame?`, called `http2.decode_frame(data, max_size)`: The frame `data` holds: exactly one frame, its head and its payload. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_frame(@r: io.Reader, max_size: i64) -> Frame?`, called `http2.read_frame(@r, max_size)`: The next frame `r` reads, its head then its payload, checked as `decode_frame` checks it. Fails `closed`.
- `function write_frame(s: io.Stream, f: Frame) -> ()?`, called `http2.write_frame(s, f)`: Writes `f` to `s`, its bytes as `encode_frame` makes them, in one write. Fails as `encode_frame` does, and as `io.write` does.
- `function frame_name(kind: i64) -> str?`, called `http2.frame_name(kind)`: The name RFC 9113 gives a frame's type: `"HEADERS"` for 1. Fails `not_found`.
- `function stream_of(f: Frame) -> i64`, called `http2.stream_of(f)`: The stream a frame is sent on: 0 for SETTINGS, PING and GOAWAY, and for a WINDOW_UPDATE of the connection.
- `record Field(name: str, value: str, sensitive: bool)`: One field of a header list: a name and its value, as HTTP/2 carries them.
- `function field_size(f: Field) -> i64`, called `http2.field_size(f)`: The size RFC 7541 § 4.1 counts a field as: its name's bytes, its value's, and 32.
- `record Encoder(state: encoding.State)`: An HPACK encoder: the dynamic table of the blocks it wrote.
- `record Decoder(state: decoding.State)`: An HPACK decoder: the dynamic table of the blocks it read, kept in step with the peer's encoder.
- `function encoder(table_size: i64) -> Encoder`, called `http2.encoder(table_size)`: A new encoder whose dynamic table holds `table_size` bytes.
- `function encode_fields(@e: Encoder, fields: [Field]) -> [u8]`, called `http2.encode_fields(@e, fields)`: The header block of `fields`, in their order, written against the static table and `e`'s dynamic table, which it changes as the peer's decoder will.
- `function resize_encoder(@e: Encoder, size: i64) -> ()?`, called `http2.resize_encoder(@e, size)`: Makes `e`'s table hold `size` bytes from the next block, which opens with the size update RFC 7541 § 6.3 writes; a size smaller and then larger before one block writes both. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decoder(table_size: i64, list_size: i64) -> Decoder`, called `http2.decoder(table_size: table_size, list_size: list_size)`: A new decoder whose peer's table may hold `table_size` bytes and whose lists may hold `list_size`.
- `function decode_fields(@d: Decoder, block: [u8]) -> [Field]?`, called `http2.decode_fields(@d, block)`: The header list a block holds, in its order, `d`'s table changed as the peer's encoder changed its own. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `not_text`.
- `function resize_decoder(@d: Decoder, size: i64) -> ()?`, called `http2.resize_decoder(@d, size)`: Makes the most the peer may make its table `size` bytes: this end's new SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE once the peer has acknowledged it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_huffman(data: [u8]) -> [u8]`, called `http2.encode_huffman(data)`: `data` in HPACK's Huffman code (RFC 7541 Appendix B), its last byte padded with the first bits of EOS.
- `function decode_huffman(data: [u8]) -> [u8]?`, called `http2.decode_huffman(data)`: The bytes `data` codes in HPACK's Huffman code. Fails `invalid`.
- `function huffman_length(data: [u8]) -> i64`, called `http2.huffman_length(data)`: How many bytes `encode_huffman` makes of `data`.
- `constant SETTING_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE: i64`, value `0x1`: The identifier of SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE: the most bytes the sender's decoder lets the peer's encoder put in its table; 4,096 at first.
- `constant SETTING_ENABLE_PUSH: i64`, value `0x2`: The identifier of SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH: 0 refuses PUSH_PROMISE, 1 allows it; 1 at first, and a server may send only 0.
- `constant SETTING_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS: i64`, value `0x3`: The identifier of SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS: the most streams the peer may open at once toward the sender; no limit at first.
- `constant SETTING_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE: i64`, value `0x4`: The identifier of SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE: each stream's first window toward the sender, at most 2^31 - 1; 65,535 at first.
- `constant SETTING_MAX_FRAME_SIZE: i64`, value `0x5`: The identifier of SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE: the largest payload the sender reads, 16,384 to 16,777,215; 16,384 at first.
- `constant SETTING_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE: i64`, value `0x6`: The identifier of SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE: the largest header list the sender accepts, counted as `field_size` counts it; no limit at first.
- `constant SETTING_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL: i64`, value `0x8`: The identifier of SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL (RFC 8441): 1 lets a client send an extended CONNECT with `:protocol`; 0 at first.
- `constant SETTING_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES: i64`, value `0x9`: The identifier of SETTINGS_NO_RFC7540_PRIORITIES (RFC 9218): 1 says the sender ignores RFC 7540's priorities, which a session sends as it does.
- `record Settings(header_table_size: i64, enable_push: bool, max_concurrent_streams: i64, initial_window_size: i64, max_frame_size: i64, max_header_list_size: i64, enable_connect_protocol: bool)`: The settings of one end, each as RFC 9113 § 6.5.2 defines it.
- `function initial_settings() -> Settings`, called `http2.initial_settings()`: The settings RFC 9113 gives an end before its SETTINGS frame: a table of 4,096 bytes, push allowed, no limit on streams or on a header list, windows of 65,535 bytes, frames of 16,384, no extended CONNECT.
- `function apply_settings(before: Settings, list: [Setting]) -> Settings?`, called `http2.apply_settings(before, list)`: `before` with the settings of one SETTINGS frame applied, in their order, each checked as RFC 9113 § 6.5.2 checks it; an identifier it does not define is ignored. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_setting_list(s: Settings) -> [Setting]`, called `http2.to_setting_list(s)`: The settings a SETTINGS frame sends to make `initial_settings()` into `s`: those that differ, in the order of their identifiers.
- `record Limits(header_block_bytes: i64, header_frames: i64, resets_per_second: i64, control_per_second: i64, body_bytes: i64)`: The bounds a session holds its peer to, past what the settings say.
- `record Options(settings: Settings, connection_window: i64, limits: Limits)`: How one end runs a connection.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `http2.default_options()`: The usual options: a table of 4,096 bytes, push refused, 100 streams at once, windows of 1 MiB per stream and 16 MiB per connection, frames of 16,384 bytes, header lists of 64 KiB; header blocks of 128 KiB in at most 64 frames, 100 resets and 1,000 frames carrying nothing a second, and bodies of 10 MiB.
- `variant Role = .client | .server`: Which end of a connection a session is.
- `variant StreamState = .idle | .reserved_local | .reserved_remote | .open | .half_closed_local | .half_closed_remote | .closed`: The state of one stream (RFC 9113 § 5.1).
- `variant Event = .request(stream: i64, method: str, scheme: str, authority: str, path: str, protocol: str, headers: [Field], end_stream: bool) | .response(stream: i64, status: i64, headers: [Field], end_stream: bool) | .informational(stream: i64, status: i64, headers: [Field]) | .trailers(stream: i64, headers: [Field]) | .data(stream: i64, data: [u8], end_stream: bool) | .reset(stream: i64, error: i64, remote: bool) | .settings(settings: Settings) | .settings_acked | .ping(data: [u8]) | .pong(data: [u8]) | .goaway(last_stream: i64, error: i64, debug: [u8]) | .window(stream: i64)`: What a session tells the program, `receive` answering them in the order the frames came.
- `record Session(state: engine.State)`: One HTTP/2 connection's protocol, with no stream under it, as Python's `h2` keeps one: bytes read are handed to `receive`, and the bytes to write are taken by `take_output`.
- `function client_session(options: Options) -> Session`, called `http2.client_session(options)`: A client's session: the preface, the first SETTINGS and the connection's WINDOW_UPDATE waiting in its output.
- `function server_session(options: Options) -> Session`, called `http2.server_session(options)`: A server's session: its first SETTINGS and the connection's WINDOW_UPDATE waiting in its output; the client's preface is the first thing `receive` reads.
- `function receive(@s: Session, data: [u8], now: time.Mark) -> [Event]?`, called `http2.receive(@s, data, now)`: The events `data` makes, reading it after the bytes held from before: every whole frame is read, a frame cut short held for the next call. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `closed`.
- `function take_output(@s: Session) -> [u8]`, called `http2.take_output(@s)`: The bytes the session has to write, in order, emptied from it.
- `function open_stream(@s: Session, headers: [Field], end_stream: bool) -> i64?`, called `http2.open_stream(@s, headers, end_stream)`: A client's: opens the next stream with a request's header list, and answers its identifier. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `closed`.
- `function send_headers(@s: Session, stream: i64, headers: [Field], end_stream: bool) -> ()?`, called `http2.send_headers(@s, stream, headers, end_stream)`: Sends a header list on an open stream: a server's response or an informational answer, or either end's trailers. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function send_data(@s: Session, stream: i64, data: [u8], end_stream: bool) -> i64?`, called `http2.send_data(@s, stream, data, end_stream)`: Sends as much of `data` on a stream as the peer's windows allow, in DATA frames of the peer's largest size, and answers how many bytes it took: the rest is the program's to send again once a `window` event comes. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function acknowledge(@s: Session, stream: i64, count: i64) -> ()?`, called `http2.acknowledge(@s, stream: stream, count: count)`: Tells the session the program has taken `count` bytes of a stream's data, so the peer may send as many again: the WINDOW_UPDATEs wait in the output once half a window is taken. Fails `invalid`.
- `function reset_stream(@s: Session, stream: i64, error: i64) -> ()?`, called `http2.reset_stream(@s, stream: stream, error: error)`: Ends a stream at once with a RST_STREAM, its queued data dropped. Fails `invalid`.
- `function send_ping(@s: Session, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `http2.send_ping(@s, data)`: Sends a PING whose answer comes back as a `pong` event. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function change_settings(@s: Session, settings: Settings) -> ()?`, called `http2.change_settings(@s, settings)`: Sends new settings, applied to what this end holds the peer to once the peer acknowledges them (`settings_acked`). Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function send_goaway(@s: Session, error: i64, debug: str) -> ()?`, called `http2.send_goaway(@s, error, debug)`: Sends GOAWAY: no stream the peer opens after those it opened already will be processed; with an error other than `NO_ERROR` the session is closed. Fails `closed`.
- `function state_of(s: Session, stream: i64) -> StreamState`, called `http2.state_of(s, stream)`: The state of a stream as the session knows it.
- `function window_of(s: Session, stream: i64) -> i64`, called `http2.window_of(s, stream)`: How many bytes this end may send on a stream now: the stream's window, bounded by the connection's.
- `function peer_settings_of(s: Session) -> Settings`, called `http2.peer_settings_of(s)`: The settings the peer holds this end to: `initial_settings()` until its first SETTINGS frame.
- `function is_open(s: Session) -> bool`, called `http2.is_open(s)`: Whether the session still runs: no connection error, no GOAWAY with an error either way.
- `function has_room(s: Session) -> bool`, called `http2.has_room(s)`: Whether a client's session may open a stream now: open, before any GOAWAY, below the server's SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS.
- `record Request(method: str, scheme: str, authority: str, path: str, protocol: str, headers: [Field], body: [u8], trailers: [Field], stream: i64)`: A request as one HTTP/2 stream carries it: its pseudo-headers by name, its fields, its body and its trailers.
- `record Response(status: i64, headers: [Field], body: [u8], trailers: [Field])`: A response as one HTTP/2 stream carries it.
- `record Conn(stream: io.Stream, state: wire.State)`: An HTTP/2 connection over a stream: a session, the stream it reads and writes, and the events read for streams nobody has asked for yet.
- `function connect(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, roots: str, options: Options) -> Conn?`, called `http2.connect(host: host, port, deadline, roots: roots, options)`: A client's connection to `host` at `port` over TLS, offering `h2` alone by ALPN, its preface and settings sent. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function connect_plain(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, options: Options) -> Conn?`, called `http2.connect_plain(host, port, deadline, options)`: A client's connection to `host` at `port` in plain text, HTTP/2 by prior knowledge (h2c, RFC 9113 § 3.3), its preface and settings sent. Fails `invalid`.
- `function client(@stream: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Conn?`, called `http2.client(@stream, options)`: A client's connection over `stream`, a stream the program holds already: one `tls.connect` answered with `h2` chosen, or a plain one. Fails as `io.write` does, `stream` then given back to the caller's place, open, to close.
- `function server(@stream: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Conn?`, called `http2.server(@stream, options)`: A server's connection over `stream`, a client's connection accepted: by `tls.accept` with `h2` chosen, or plain with prior knowledge. Fails as `io.write` does, `stream` then given back to the caller's place, open, to close.
- `function close(@c: Conn) -> ()?`, called `http2.close(@c)`: Ends the connection: GOAWAY with `NO_ERROR` and the last stream the peer opened, then the stream closed; this place emptied either way. Fails `closed`.
- `function read_event(@c: Conn) -> Event?`, called `http2.read_event(@c)`: The next event of the connection, held ones first, reading the stream until one comes; what the session must answer is written on the way. Fails `closed`.
- `function read_event_of(@c: Conn, stream: i64) -> Event?`, called `http2.read_event_of(@c, stream)`: The next event of one stream, reading the connection until one comes and holding the events of other streams, and those of no stream, for later. Fails `closed`.
- `function accept_stream(@c: Conn) -> Event?`, called `http2.accept_stream(@c)`: A server's: the head of the next stream a client opens, the events of every other stream held: what a server waits for while it answers other streams of the connection one by one, as gRPC's does. Fails `closed`.
- `function start_stream(@c: Conn, headers: [Field], end_stream: bool) -> i64?`, called `http2.start_stream(@c, headers, end_stream)`: A client's: opens a stream with a header list, written at once, and answers its identifier; waits, reading and holding events, while the server's SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS are open. Fails as `open_stream` does, and as `read_event` does while it waits.
- `function write_headers(@c: Conn, stream: i64, headers: [Field], end_stream: bool) -> ()?`, called `http2.write_headers(@c, stream, headers, end_stream)`: Writes a header list on a stream: a response, an informational answer or trailers, as `send_headers` takes them. Fails as `send_headers` and `io.write` do.
- `function write_data(@c: Conn, stream: i64, data: [u8], end_stream: bool) -> ()?`, called `http2.write_data(@c, stream, data, end_stream)`: Writes `data` on a stream, waiting, reading and holding events, until the peer's windows have let every byte go. Fails `closed`.
- `function write_reset(@c: Conn, stream: i64, error: i64) -> ()?`, called `http2.write_reset(@c, stream: stream, error: error)`: Resets a stream with `error`, written at once. Fails as `reset_stream` and `io.write` do.
- `function ping(@c: Conn, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `http2.ping(@c, data)`: Sends a PING and waits for its answer, holding the events that come before it. Fails as `send_ping` and `read_event` do.
- `function start(@c: Conn, r: Request) -> i64?`, called `http2.start(@c, r)`: A client's: sends `r` on a new stream, its head, its body and its trailers, and answers the stream; its response is read by `finish`, so several requests may be started before any is finished. Fails as `start_stream` and `write_data` do.
- `function finish(@c: Conn, stream: i64) -> Response?`, called `http2.finish(@c, stream)`: A client's: the response on `stream`, read whole, informational answers skipped, events of other streams held. Fails `closed`, `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function round_trip(@c: Conn, r: Request) -> Response?`, called `http2.round_trip(@c, r)`: A client's: the response to `r`, sent on a new stream and read whole, as `start` and `finish` together. Fails as `start` and `finish` do.
- `function next_request(@c: Conn) -> Request?`, called `http2.next_request(@c)`: A server's: the next request whose body has ended, read whole, events of other streams held. Fails `closed`.
- `function answer(@c: Conn, stream: i64, response: Response) -> ()?`, called `http2.answer(@c, stream, response)`: A server's: writes `response` on `stream`, its head, its body and its trailers, waiting while the client's windows hold the body back. Fails as `write_headers` and `write_data` do.
- `function serve(@c: Conn, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http2.serve(@c, handler)`: A server's: answers every request of the connection with `handler`, one after another, until the client closes it or sends GOAWAY, and answers how many were answered.
- `function serve_with<S>(@c: Conn, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http2.serve_with(@c, state, handler)`: `serve` with `state` handed to `handler` beside each request: how a handler reads the program's own values, since a function takes no closure.
- `constant NO_ERROR: i64`, value `0x0`: NO_ERROR (RFC 9113 § 7): a graceful end, no error at all.
- `constant PROTOCOL_ERROR: i64`, value `0x1`: PROTOCOL_ERROR: the peer broke the protocol where no other code is more specific.
- `constant INTERNAL_ERROR: i64`, value `0x2`: INTERNAL_ERROR: the end that sends it failed on its own.
- `constant FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR: i64`, value `0x3`: FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR: a window was overrun or overflowed.
- `constant SETTINGS_TIMEOUT: i64`, value `0x4`: SETTINGS_TIMEOUT: settings sent were not acknowledged in time.
- `constant STREAM_CLOSED: i64`, value `0x5`: STREAM_CLOSED: a frame came on a stream half closed already.
- `constant FRAME_SIZE_ERROR: i64`, value `0x6`: FRAME_SIZE_ERROR: a frame of a size its type or the settings refuse.
- `constant REFUSED_STREAM: i64`, value `0x7`: REFUSED_STREAM: the stream was refused before any of it was processed, so a client may send it again.
- `constant CANCEL: i64`, value `0x8`: CANCEL: the stream is no longer wanted.
- `constant COMPRESSION_ERROR: i64`, value `0x9`: COMPRESSION_ERROR: a header block HPACK cannot read; the connection ends.
- `constant CONNECT_ERROR: i64`, value `0xa`: CONNECT_ERROR: the connection a CONNECT request opened was reset or closed.
- `constant ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM: i64`, value `0xb`: ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM: the peer is sending more than this end allows.
- `constant INADEQUATE_SECURITY: i64`, value `0xc`: INADEQUATE_SECURITY: the TLS under the connection is too weak.
- `constant HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED: i64`, value `0xd`: HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED: the request must be sent over HTTP/1.1.
- `function error_name(code: i64) -> str?`, called `http2.error_name(code)`: The name RFC 9113 § 7 gives an error code: `"PROTOCOL_ERROR"` for 1. Fails `not_found`.
- `constant FRAME_DATA: i64`, value `0x0`: The type of a DATA frame.
- `constant FRAME_HEADERS: i64`, value `0x1`: The type of a HEADERS frame.
- `constant FRAME_PRIORITY: i64`, value `0x2`: The type of a PRIORITY frame.
- `constant FRAME_RST_STREAM: i64`, value `0x3`: The type of a RST_STREAM frame.
- `constant FRAME_SETTINGS: i64`, value `0x4`: The type of a SETTINGS frame.
- `constant FRAME_PUSH_PROMISE: i64`, value `0x5`: The type of a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
- `constant FRAME_PING: i64`, value `0x6`: The type of a PING frame.
- `constant FRAME_GOAWAY: i64`, value `0x7`: The type of a GOAWAY frame.
- `constant FRAME_WINDOW_UPDATE: i64`, value `0x8`: The type of a WINDOW_UPDATE frame.
- `constant FRAME_CONTINUATION: i64`, value `0x9`: The type of a CONTINUATION frame.
- `constant FLAG_END_STREAM: i64`, value `0x1`: The flag END_STREAM of DATA and HEADERS: the sender's last frame on the stream.
- `constant FLAG_ACK: i64`, value `0x1`: The flag ACK of SETTINGS and PING: an acknowledgement.
- `constant FLAG_END_HEADERS: i64`, value `0x4`: The flag END_HEADERS of HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE and CONTINUATION: the header block ends in this frame.
- `constant FLAG_PADDED: i64`, value `0x8`: The flag PADDED of DATA, HEADERS and PUSH_PROMISE: a byte of padding's length opens the payload.
- `constant FLAG_PRIORITY: i64`, value `0x20`: The flag PRIORITY of HEADERS: five bytes of priority follow the padding's length.
- `constant FRAME_HEAD_BYTES: i64`, value `9`: The bytes of a frame's head: a length of 24 bits, a type, flags and a stream identifier of 31 bits.
- `constant MIN_FRAME_SIZE: i64`, value `16384`: The smallest SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE, and its initial value: 16,384 bytes.
- `constant MAX_FRAME_SIZE: i64`, value `16777215`: The largest SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE: 16,777,215 bytes.
- `constant MAX_WINDOW: i64`, value `2147483647`: The largest window and the largest stream identifier: 2^31 - 1.
- `constant NO_LIMIT: i64`, value `4294967295`: What a setting with no limit holds: 2^32 - 1, its largest value, which is what SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS and SETTINGS_MAX_HEADER_LIST_SIZE hold before a peer says otherwise.
- `constant PREFACE: str`, value `"PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n"`: The bytes a client sends before its first frame (RFC 9113 § 3.4).
- `constant ALPN: str`, value `"h2"`: The name TLS's ALPN gives HTTP/2.


### mail/imap

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/mail/imap`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mail/imap/).

Mail read from a server by IMAP (RFC 9051, IMAP4rev2, and RFC 3501, IMAP4rev1): a client that connects in plain text, by STARTTLS or by TLS from the first byte (RFC 8314, port 993), logs in by LOGIN or by AUTHENTICATE with PLAIN, XOAUTH2 or OAUTHBEARER, enables IMAP4rev2 where the server offers it, lists, makes, renames and selects mailboxes, fetches messages whole or in parts (envelopes, body structures, sections, partial fetches, BINARY), searches, changes flags, copies, moves, appends and expunges, by message number or by UID, and waits for news with IDLE.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument refused, an answer that is not IMAP, a BAD, or a certificate `tls` refused: every function.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection closed, or the server said BYE: every function.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The host's name has no address, or a mailbox does not exist (NONEXISTENT, TRYCREATE).
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: A mailbox made or renamed exists already (ALREADYEXISTS).
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: A step took longer than its deadline: every function that talks.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while a step waited (`os.ask_stop`).
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The server refused a login or a right: AUTHENTICATIONFAILED, NOPERM, and a NO to LOGIN or AUTHENTICATE.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A quota or a size passed (OVERQUOTA, LIMIT, TOOBIG), or an answer larger than `Options.max_bytes`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The server lacks a capability a step needs: MOVE, UIDPLUS, IDLE, a SASL mechanism, BINARY.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: Any other refusal of the server, or a failure of the connection the other codes do not name; the message carries the status or the system's words.
- `constant PORT_IMAP: i64`, value `143`: IMAP's port, in plain text and for STARTTLS (RFC 9051).
- `constant PORT_IMAPS: i64`, value `993`: IMAP over TLS from the first byte (RFC 8314).
- `variant Security = .starttls | .implicit | .plain`: How a connection is protected.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, security: Security, roots: str, deadline: time.Duration, max_bytes: i64)`: How a client connects.
- `function options(host: str, security: Security) -> Options`, called `imap.options(host, security)`: The options of a connection to `host` protected by `security`, on the port it is used on: 143 for `.starttls` and `.plain`, 993 for `.implicit`; the system's authorities, 60 seconds a step, 64 MiB an answer.
- `record Client(conn: flow.Conn)`: An IMAP session with a server, made by `connect`.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Client?`, called `imap.connect(opts)`: A session with the server `opts` names: connected, protected as `opts` says, its greeting read and its capabilities known. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function logout(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.logout(@c)`: Says LOGOUT, reads the server's BYE and status, and closes the connection, whatever they are. Fails where the connection fails; it is closed either way.
- `function close(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.close(@c)`: Closes the connection without a word to the server. Fails `closed`.
- `function noop(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.noop(@c)`: Says NOOP: the server's news since the last command are kept for `take_updates`. Fails as a command fails.
- `function check(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.check(@c)`: Says CHECK on IMAP4rev1, a checkpoint of the mailbox selected; NOOP on IMAP4rev2, which has no CHECK and does its work at every command. Fails as a command fails.
- `record Status(condition: str, code: str, args: str, text: str)`: A status the server said: OK, NO, BAD, BYE or PREAUTH, with its response code.
- `function greeting_of(c: Client) -> Status`, called `imap.greeting_of(c)`: The server's greeting; with STARTTLS `tls` read it, and this holds its condition alone.
- `function last_status_of(c: Client) -> Status`, called `imap.last_status_of(c)`: The tagged status that ended the last command, a refusal's included.
- `function format_status(s: Status) -> str`, called `imap.format_status(s)`: `s` as one line for a person: its condition, its code in brackets, its text; any byte outside printable ASCII escaped.
- `function capabilities_of(c: Client) -> [str]`, called `imap.capabilities_of(c)`: The capabilities the server names, upper case: `IMAP4REV2`, `IDLE`, `AUTH=PLAIN`.
- `function has_capability(c: Client, name: str) -> bool`, called `imap.has_capability(c, name)`: Whether the server names `name` among its capabilities, in any case.
- `function capability(@c: Client) -> [str]?`, called `imap.capability(@c)`: Asks the server for its capabilities anew, and answers them. Fails as a command fails.
- `function is_rev2(c: Client) -> bool`, called `imap.is_rev2(c)`: Whether IMAP4rev2 is in force: the server offered it and this client enabled it after the login.
- `function is_tls(c: Client) -> bool`, called `imap.is_tls(c)`: Whether TLS protects the connection.
- `function login(@c: Client, user: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.login(@c, user: user, password: password)`: Logs in with LOGIN, `user` and `password` sent as the server's strings. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`.
- `function auth_plain(@c: Client, identity: str, user: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.auth_plain(@c, identity: identity, user: user, password: password)`: Logs in by AUTHENTICATE PLAIN (RFC 4616), the first answer sent with the command where the server offers SASL-IR. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`.
- `function auth_xoauth2(@c: Client, user: str, token: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.auth_xoauth2(@c, user: user, token: token)`: Logs in by AUTHENTICATE XOAUTH2, as Google's and Microsoft's servers take an OAuth 2.0 access token; where the server refuses, it says why in a challenge, shown in the failure. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`.
- `function auth_oauthbearer(@c: Client, user: str, token: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.auth_oauthbearer(@c, user: user, token: token)`: Logs in by AUTHENTICATE OAUTHBEARER (RFC 7628) with an OAuth 2.0 bearer token; where the server refuses, it says why in a challenge, shown in the failure. Fails as `auth_xoauth2` does, AUTH=OAUTHBEARER being the one asked.
- `function enable(@c: Client, names: [str]) -> [str]?`, called `imap.enable(@c, names)`: Enables the extensions `names` with ENABLE (RFC 5161), and answers those the server enabled. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Mailbox(name: str, delimiter: str, attributes: [str])`: A mailbox a LIST names.
- `function list(@c: Client, reference: str, pattern: str) -> [Mailbox]?`, called `imap.list(@c, reference: reference, pattern: pattern)`: The mailboxes whose names `pattern` matches below `reference` (LIST). Fails `invalid`.
- `function list_subscribed(@c: Client, reference: str, pattern: str) -> [Mailbox]?`, called `imap.list_subscribed(@c, reference: reference, pattern: pattern)`: The subscribed mailboxes whose names `pattern` matches below `reference`: LSUB on IMAP4rev1, LIST (SUBSCRIBED) on IMAP4rev2, which has no LSUB. Fails as `list` fails.
- `function create(@c: Client, name: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.create(@c, name)`: Makes the mailbox `name` (CREATE). Fails `exists`.
- `function delete(@c: Client, name: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.delete(@c, name)`: Removes the mailbox `name` (DELETE). Fails `not_found`.
- `function rename(@c: Client, from: str, to: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.rename(@c, from: from, to: to)`: Renames the mailbox `from` to `to` (RENAME); INBOX renamed moves its messages into a new mailbox and stays. Fails `not_found`, `exists`.
- `function subscribe(@c: Client, name: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.subscribe(@c, name)`: Subscribes to the mailbox `name` (SUBSCRIBE). Fails as a command fails.
- `function unsubscribe(@c: Client, name: str) -> ()?`, called `imap.unsubscribe(@c, name)`: Unsubscribes from the mailbox `name` (UNSUBSCRIBE). Fails as a command fails.
- `record MailboxStatus(name: str, messages: i64, recent: i64, uid_next: i64, uid_validity: i64, unseen: i64, deleted: i64, size: i64)`: What STATUS says of a mailbox: -1 for a number the server did not give.
- `function status(@c: Client, name: str) -> MailboxStatus?`, called `imap.status(@c, name)`: What the mailbox `name` holds, without selecting it (STATUS): MESSAGES, UIDNEXT, UIDVALIDITY and UNSEEN, with RECENT on IMAP4rev1 and DELETED and SIZE on IMAP4rev2. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Selected(name: str, read_only: bool, exists: i64, recent: i64, flags: [str], permanent_flags: [str], uid_validity: i64, uid_next: i64, unseen: i64, highest_modseq: i64)`: A mailbox selected or examined, as the server described it.
- `function select(@c: Client, name: str) -> Selected?`, called `imap.select(@c, name)`: Selects the mailbox `name` to read and change it (SELECT). Fails `not_found`.
- `function examine(@c: Client, name: str) -> Selected?`, called `imap.examine(@c, name)`: Selects the mailbox `name` to read it alone (EXAMINE): nothing changes it, `\Seen` included. Fails as `select` fails.
- `function close_mailbox(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.close_mailbox(@c)`: Leaves the mailbox selected, removing its messages marked `\Deleted` where it is not read-only (CLOSE). Fails as a command fails.
- `function unselect(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.unselect(@c)`: Leaves the mailbox selected and removes nothing (UNSELECT, RFC 3691 and IMAP4rev2). Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Set(uid: bool, text: str)`: Messages named by number or by UID, as IMAP writes a set: `1:4,9`, `100:*`.
- `constant LAST: i64`, value `0`: The number that stands for the last message in a range, `*`.
- `function seqs(numbers: [i64]) -> Set`, called `imap.seqs(numbers)`: The messages numbered `numbers`, in order; 0 is the last.
- `function uids(numbers: [i64]) -> Set`, called `imap.uids(numbers)`: The messages whose UIDs are `numbers`; 0 is the last.
- `function seq_range(first: i64, last: i64) -> Set`, called `imap.seq_range(first: first, last: last)`: The messages numbered `first` to `last`.
- `function uid_range(first: i64, last: i64) -> Set`, called `imap.uid_range(first: first, last: last)`: The messages whose UIDs run from `first` to `last`.
- `function numbers_of(s: Set, most: i64) -> [i64]?`, called `imap.numbers_of(s, most)`: Each number `s` names, ranges written out, in the order written. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `variant Item = .flags | .envelope | .structure | .internal_date | .size | .uid | .modseq | .body(section: str, start: i64, count: i64) | .binary(section: str, start: i64, count: i64) | .binary_size(section: str)`: What a fetch asks of each message.
- `record Envelope(date: str, subject: str, from: [mail.Address], sender: [mail.Address], reply_to: [mail.Address], to: [mail.Address], cc: [mail.Address], bcc: [mail.Address], in_reply_to: str, message_id: str)`: A message's envelope, its fields as the message's own header writes them.
- `record Part(type: str, subtype: str, params: {str: str}, id: str, description: str, encoding: str, size: i64, lines: i64, md5: str, disposition: str, disposition_params: {str: str}, language: [str], location: str, parts: [Part], envelope: [Envelope])`: One part of a message's MIME structure.
- `record Body(section: str, origin: i64, data: [u8], binary: bool)`: A body section a fetch answered.
- `record Message(seq: i64, items: [str], uid: i64, flags: [str], envelope: Envelope, structure: Part, internal_date: mail.Date, size: i64, modseq: i64, bodies: [Body], binary_sizes: {str: i64})`: One message as a fetch, a store or the server's news answered it.
- `function fetch(@c: Client, which: Set, items: [Item]) -> [Message]?`, called `imap.fetch(@c, which, items)`: The messages `which` names, each with the items `items` asks (FETCH, or UID FETCH where `which.uid`); UID is always asked with a UID FETCH. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function body_of(m: Message, section: str) -> [u8]?`, called `imap.body_of(m, section)`: The bytes of the section `section` that `m` answered. Fails `not_found`.
- `variant Key = .all | .answered | .deleted | .draft | .flagged | .seen | .unanswered | .undeleted | .undraft | .unflagged | .unseen | .keyword(flag: str) | .unkeyword(flag: str) | .from(text: str) | .to(text: str) | .cc(text: str) | .bcc(text: str) | .subject(text: str) | .body(text: str) | .text(text: str) | .header(name: str, text: str) | .before(day: time.Instant) | .on(day: time.Instant) | .since(day: time.Instant) | .sent_before(day: time.Instant) | .sent_on(day: time.Instant) | .sent_since(day: time.Instant) | .larger(size: i64) | .smaller(size: i64) | .within(set: Set) | .not(keys: [Key]) | .either(left: [Key], right: [Key])`: One key of a search; the keys of a list must all hold.
- `function search(@c: Client, criteria: [Key], by_uid: bool) -> [i64]?`, called `imap.search(@c, criteria, by_uid)`: The messages where every key of `criteria` holds (SEARCH, or UID SEARCH where `by_uid`), in increasing order; texts are sent as UTF-8. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `variant Change = .add | .remove | .replace`: How `store` changes flags.
- `function store(@c: Client, which: Set, change: Change, flags: [str]) -> [Message]?`, called `imap.store(@c, which, change, flags)`: Changes the flags of the messages `which` names (STORE, or UID STORE), and answers each message with its flags after the change. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Copied(uid_validity: i64, from: Set, to: Set)`: What COPYUID and APPENDUID say of messages copied, moved or appended (UIDPLUS, RFC 4315): empty sets where the server says nothing.
- `function copy(@c: Client, which: Set, to: str) -> Copied?`, called `imap.copy(@c, which, to)`: Copies the messages `which` names into the mailbox `to` (COPY, or UID COPY). Fails `not_found`.
- `function move(@c: Client, which: Set, to: str) -> Copied?`, called `imap.move(@c, which, to)`: Moves the messages `which` names into the mailbox `to` (MOVE, RFC 6851 and IMAP4rev2, or UID MOVE): one step, which no copy and expunge make. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function expunge(@c: Client) -> [i64]?`, called `imap.expunge(@c)`: Removes the messages marked `\Deleted` from the mailbox selected (EXPUNGE), and answers the number each had as it went, in the server's order: each later number counts the ones removed before it. Fails as a command fails.
- `function expunge_uids(@c: Client, which: Set) -> [i64]?`, called `imap.expunge_uids(@c, which)`: Removes the messages marked `\Deleted` among the UIDs `which` names, and no other (UID EXPUNGE, UIDPLUS and IMAP4rev2). Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Appended(uid_validity: i64, uid: i64)`: What APPENDUID says of a message appended: 0 where the server says nothing.
- `function append(@c: Client, to: str, message: [u8], flags: [str]) -> Appended?`, called `imap.append(@c, to, message, flags)`: Adds `message` to the mailbox `to` with the flags `flags` (APPEND), the server's clock naming when it was received. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `not_found`.
- `function append_dated(@c: Client, to: str, message: [u8], flags: [str], date: mail.Date) -> Appended?`, called `imap.append_dated(@c, to, message, flags, date)`: Adds `message` to the mailbox `to` as `append` does, received at `date`. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Update = .exists(count: i64) | .recent(count: i64) | .expunge(seq: i64) | .fetch(message: Message) | .flags(flags: [str]) | .said(status: Status) | .other(name: str)`: Something the server told without being asked: a message arrived or went, flags changed, an alert.
- `function take_updates(@c: Client) -> [Update]`, called `imap.take_updates(@c)`: The news the server told since the last call, oldest first, and empties them.
- `function lost_updates_of(c: Client) -> i64`, called `imap.lost_updates_of(c)`: How many news `take_updates` lost to its bound since the session began.
- `function idle(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `imap.idle(@c)`: Begins IDLE (RFC 2177, IMAP4rev2): the server tells its news as they come until `idle_done`. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function idle_wait(@c: Client, within: time.Duration) -> [Update]?`, called `imap.idle_wait(@c, within)`: The news that come while idling: it waits up to `within` for the first and answers it with every other already arrived; [] where none came. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function idle_done(@c: Client) -> [Update]?`, called `imap.idle_done(@c)`: Ends the IDLE (DONE), and answers the news that came before its end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_utf7(name: str) -> str`, called `imap.format_utf7(name)`: `name` in IMAP4rev1's modified UTF-7 (RFC 3501 § 5.1.3), as this client writes a name where UTF-8 is not in force: `Entwürfe` is `Entw&APw-rfe`.
- `function parse_utf7(wire: str) -> str?`, called `imap.parse_utf7(wire)`: The name modified UTF-7 `wire` writes. Fails `invalid`.


### mail/smtp

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/mail/smtp`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mail/smtp/).

Mail sent by SMTP (RFC 5321): a client that connects in plain text, by STARTTLS (RFC 3207) or by TLS from the first byte (RFC 8314, port 465), reads the extensions EHLO names, logs in by AUTH PLAIN, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5 or XOAUTH2, and sends a message to its recipients with SIZE, 8BITMIME, SMTPUTF8 and PIPELINING where the server offers them; each step bounded by a deadline, every reply a value with its code.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument refused, a reply that is not SMTP, or a certificate `tls` refused: every function.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection closed, or the server answered 421: every function.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The host's name has no address: `connect`, `send_mail`.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: A step took longer than its deadline: every function that talks.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while a step waited (`os.ask_stop`).
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The server refused a login or a sender: 530, 534, 535, 538.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The message is larger than the server takes, or the server has no room: 452, 552, and `SIZE` exceeded before sending.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The server lacks a command, a mechanism or an extension the message needs: 502, 504, no AUTH mechanism in common, 8-bit bytes without 8BITMIME, UTF-8 without SMTPUTF8.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: Any other refusal of the server, or a failure of the connection the other codes do not name; the message carries the reply or the system's words.
- `record Reply(code: i64, enhanced: str, lines: [str])`: A reply of the server: its code, and the text of its lines.
- `function is_positive(r: Reply) -> bool`, called `smtp.is_positive(r)`: Whether `r` says the command was done or is going on: a code of 2xx or 3xx.
- `function is_transient(r: Reply) -> bool`, called `smtp.is_transient(r)`: Whether `r` refuses for now, so the same command may succeed later: a code of 4xx.
- `function is_permanent(r: Reply) -> bool`, called `smtp.is_permanent(r)`: Whether `r` refuses for good: a code of 5xx.
- `function format_reply(r: Reply) -> str`, called `smtp.format_reply(r)`: `r` as one line for a person: its code, its enhanced code, and its lines joined by a space; any byte outside printable ASCII escaped.
- `variant Security = .starttls | .implicit | .plain`: How a connection is protected.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, security: Security, roots: str, local_name: str, deadline: time.Duration)`: How a client connects.
- `function options(host: str, security: Security) -> Options`, called `smtp.options(host, security)`: The options of a connection to `host` protected by `security`, on the port it is used on: 587 for `.starttls`, 465 for `.implicit`, 25 for `.plain`; the system's authorities, `localhost` as the client's name, 60 seconds a step.
- `record Client(session: wire.Session, host: str, is_tls: bool)`: An SMTP session with a server, made by `connect`.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Client?`, called `smtp.connect(opts)`: A session with the server `opts` names: connected, protected as `opts` says, its greeting read and its EHLO answered. Fails `invalid`.
- `function hello(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `smtp.hello(@c)`: Says EHLO again and reads the extensions anew, as after a change of the server's state. Fails as a command fails.
- `function quit(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `smtp.quit(@c)`: Says QUIT, reads the reply, and closes the connection, whatever the reply. Fails where the connection fails; it is closed either way.
- `function close(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `smtp.close(@c)`: Closes the connection without a word to the server. Fails `closed`.
- `function greeting_of(c: Client) -> Reply`, called `smtp.greeting_of(c)`: The server's greeting, 220; with STARTTLS `tls` read it, and this holds its code alone.
- `function last_reply_of(c: Client) -> Reply`, called `smtp.last_reply_of(c)`: The last reply the server gave: the one a failure of the last call names, whole.
- `function extensions_of(c: Client) -> {str: str}`, called `smtp.extensions_of(c)`: The extensions the server named in its last EHLO reply: each keyword in upper case, and its parameters as one text, "" for none: `SIZE` holding `35882577`, `AUTH` holding `PLAIN LOGIN`; empty after HELO.
- `function has_extension(c: Client, keyword: str) -> bool`, called `smtp.has_extension(c, keyword)`: Whether the server named the extension `keyword` in its EHLO reply.
- `function extension_of(c: Client, keyword: str) -> str?`, called `smtp.extension_of(c, keyword)`: The parameters the server gave the extension `keyword`, as one text: `SIZE` answers `35882577`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function max_size_of(c: Client) -> i64?`, called `smtp.max_size_of(c)`: The largest message the server takes, in bytes, as its SIZE names it. Fails `not_found`.
- `function auth_mechanisms_of(c: Client) -> [str]`, called `smtp.auth_mechanisms_of(c)`: The login mechanisms the server offers, in upper case, in its order: `["PLAIN", "LOGIN"]`; [] where it offers none.
- `function login(@c: Client, user: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `smtp.login(@c, user: user, password: password)`: Logs in with `user` and `password` by the best mechanism the server offers: PLAIN, then LOGIN, then CRAM-MD5. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `permission`.
- `function auth_plain(@c: Client, identity: str, user: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `smtp.auth_plain(@c, identity: identity, user: user, password: password)`: Logs in by AUTH PLAIN (RFC 4616), the credentials sent with the command. Fails `invalid`.
- `function auth_login(@c: Client, user: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `smtp.auth_login(@c, user: user, password: password)`: Logs in by AUTH LOGIN, the name and the password each sent when the server asks for it. Fails as `login` does.
- `function auth_cram_md5(@c: Client, user: str, secret: str) -> ()?`, called `smtp.auth_cram_md5(@c, user: user, secret: secret)`: Logs in by AUTH CRAM-MD5 (RFC 2195): the password never sent, an HMAC of the server's challenge sent instead. Fails `invalid`.
- `function auth_xoauth2(@c: Client, user: str, token: str) -> ()?`, called `smtp.auth_xoauth2(@c, user: user, token: token)`: Logs in by AUTH XOAUTH2 with an OAuth 2.0 access token, as Gmail and Outlook ask. Fails as `login` does.
- `function mail_from(@c: Client, from: str, params: [str]) -> ()?`, called `smtp.mail_from(@c, from, params)`: Says MAIL FROM, beginning a transaction. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rcpt_to(@c: Client, to: str, params: [str]) -> ()?`, called `smtp.rcpt_to(@c, to, params)`: Says RCPT TO, adding a recipient to the transaction. Fails as `mail_from` does.
- `function data(@c: Client, message: [u8]) -> Reply?`, called `smtp.data(@c, message)`: Says DATA and sends `message`, its lines ended by `\r\n` and its dots doubled where a line begins with one, then the line holding `.`. Fails with the code a refusal means.
- `function reset(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `smtp.reset(@c)`: Says RSET, ending the transaction under way without sending. Fails with the code a refusal means.
- `function noop(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `smtp.noop(@c)`: Says NOOP, which keeps the connection alive and asks that the server answers. Fails with the code a refusal means.
- `function verify(@c: Client, address: str) -> Reply?`, called `smtp.verify(@c, address)`: Says VRFY, asking whether the server knows the mailbox `address`. Fails with the code a refusal means.
- `function expand(@c: Client, list: str) -> Reply?`, called `smtp.expand(@c, list)`: Says EXPN, asking the server for the members of the mailing list `list`. Fails with the code a refusal means.
- `function help(@c: Client, topic: str) -> Reply?`, called `smtp.help(@c, topic)`: Says HELP, about `topic` or about the server. Fails with the code a refusal means.
- `function command(@c: Client, line: str) -> Reply?`, called `smtp.command(@c, line)`: Sends `line` and answers the server's reply, whatever its code. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Refusal(address: str, reply: Reply)`: One recipient the server refused, and its reply.
- `record Sent(reply: Reply, refused: [Refusal])`: What `send` answers: the server's reply to the message, and the recipients it refused while taking the message for the others.
- `function send(@c: Client, from: str, to: [str], message: [u8]) -> Sent?`, called `smtp.send(@c, from, to, message)`: Sends `message` from `from` to `to`: MAIL FROM, RCPT TO for each, DATA, in one round trip where the server offers PIPELINING. Fails `invalid`.
- `function send_message(@c: Client, m: mail.Message) -> Sent?`, called `smtp.send_message(@c, m)`: Sends `m` to every address of its `To`, `Cc` and `Bcc`, from the address of its `Sender`, else of its first `From`, without its `Bcc`. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Auth = .none | .password(user: str, password: str) | .oauth2(user: str, token: str)`: How `send_mail` logs in.
- `function send_mail(opts: Options, auth: Auth, from: str, to: [str], message: [u8]) -> Sent?`, called `smtp.send_mail(opts, auth, from, to, message)`: Sends `message` in one call: connects as `opts` says, logs in as `auth` says, sends, and says QUIT. Fails as `connect`, `login`, `auth_xoauth2` and `send` fail.
- `function dot_stuff(message: [u8]) -> [u8]`, called `smtp.dot_stuff(message)`: `message` as DATA sends it: every line break made `\r\n`, a dot doubled where a line begins with one, and a last line break added where it lacks one; the line holding `.` is not added.
- `constant PORT_SMTP: i64`, value `25`: SMTP between servers, in plain text or with STARTTLS: 25.
- `constant PORT_SUBMISSION: i64`, value `587`: Message submission with STARTTLS (RFC 6409): 587.
- `constant PORT_SUBMISSIONS: i64`, value `465`: Message submission over TLS from the first byte (RFC 8314): 465.
- `constant REPLY_SYSTEM_STATUS: i64`, value `211`: 211: a system status or a help reply.
- `constant REPLY_HELP_MESSAGE: i64`, value `214`: 214: a help message.
- `constant REPLY_SERVICE_READY: i64`, value `220`: 220: the service is ready; the greeting, and the answer to STARTTLS.
- `constant REPLY_SERVICE_CLOSING: i64`, value `221`: 221: the service closes the connection, the answer to QUIT.
- `constant REPLY_AUTH_SUCCEEDED: i64`, value `235`: 235: the login succeeded (RFC 4954).
- `constant REPLY_OK: i64`, value `250`: 250: the command was done.
- `constant REPLY_WILL_FORWARD: i64`, value `251`: 251: the recipient is not local and will be forwarded.
- `constant REPLY_CANNOT_VERIFY: i64`, value `252`: 252: the server cannot verify the user but will take the message.
- `constant REPLY_AUTH_CONTINUE: i64`, value `334`: 334: a login's challenge, the server waiting for the next line (RFC 4954).
- `constant REPLY_START_MAIL_INPUT: i64`, value `354`: 354: the server waits for the message, ended by a line holding `.`.
- `constant REPLY_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: i64`, value `421`: 421: the service is not available and closes the connection.
- `constant REPLY_MAILBOX_BUSY: i64`, value `450`: 450: the mailbox is busy or unavailable for now.
- `constant REPLY_LOCAL_ERROR: i64`, value `451`: 451: a local error in processing; try later.
- `constant REPLY_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE: i64`, value `452`: 452: the server has no room now.
- `constant REPLY_TEMPORARY_FAILURE: i64`, value `454`: 454: TLS or a login is not available for now.
- `constant REPLY_SYNTAX_ERROR: i64`, value `500`: 500: a command the server cannot read.
- `constant REPLY_PARAMETER_ERROR: i64`, value `501`: 501: a parameter the server cannot read.
- `constant REPLY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: i64`, value `502`: 502: a command the server does not have.
- `constant REPLY_BAD_SEQUENCE: i64`, value `503`: 503: a command out of its order.
- `constant REPLY_PARAMETER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: i64`, value `504`: 504: a parameter, or a login mechanism, the server does not have.
- `constant REPLY_AUTH_REQUIRED: i64`, value `530`: 530: a login is required first (RFC 4954).
- `constant REPLY_AUTH_FAILED: i64`, value `535`: 535: the credentials were refused (RFC 4954).
- `constant REPLY_MAILBOX_UNAVAILABLE: i64`, value `550`: 550: the mailbox is unavailable, or the server will not take the message for it.
- `constant REPLY_USER_NOT_LOCAL: i64`, value `551`: 551: the user is not local.
- `constant REPLY_EXCEEDED_STORAGE: i64`, value `552`: 552: the message is larger than the server takes.
- `constant REPLY_MAILBOX_NAME_NOT_ALLOWED: i64`, value `553`: 553: the mailbox's name is not allowed.
- `constant REPLY_TRANSACTION_FAILED: i64`, value `554`: 554: the transaction failed, or the server will not serve this client.
- `constant REPLY_PARAMETERS_NOT_RECOGNIZED: i64`, value `555`: 555: a parameter of MAIL or RCPT the server does not know.


### x509

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/x509`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/x509/).

Certificates of X.509 read as RFC 5280 writes them: the subject and the issuer with their attributes, the validity, the serial, the public key, the signature's algorithm and bytes, and every common extension decoded, an unknown one kept with its criticality; certificate requests (PKCS #10, RFC 2986) and revocation lists (RFC 5280 § 5) read; a signature checked by the system's own cryptography through `crypto/keypairs`; a chain put in order from a leaf and a pool, and checked; a host name and an address matched against a certificate as RFC 6125 says; and certificates, requests and revocation lists made and signed through `crypto/keypairs`.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A structure that is not what RFC 5280 says, a chain that does not hold, or a signature's parameters its RFC forbids: the message says which part.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No such thing where one was asked for: `text_of`, `extension_of`, `revoked_of`, `parse_certificate`, `parse_request`, `parse_crl`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A signature or a key of an algorithm `crypto/keypairs` does not check on this platform: `scheme_of`, `kind_of`, `verify_signature`, `is_signed_by`, `is_request_signed`, `is_crl_signed_by`, `verify_chain`.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: A string in a name or an extension whose characters are not its type's: every reader, as `asn1` says it.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: A number outside its type where a structure is read, as `asn1` says it: a REAL, an ENUMERATED or a time's offset; every reader.
- `record Attribute(oid: asn1.Oid, value: asn1.Value)`: One attribute of a name, `CN=example.com`: its type and its value.
- `record Name(rdns: [[Attribute]], der: [u8])`: A distinguished name: relative names in the order the certificate writes them, the least specific first, each one attribute or more.
- `function to_name(v: asn1.Value) -> Name?`, called `x509.to_name(v)`: The name `v` holds, an RDNSequence. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_name(n: Name) -> str`, called `x509.format_name(n)`: `n` as RFC 4514's text, the most specific relative name first, as Python's `rfc4514_string` writes it: `CN=example.com,O=Heroes Test,C=IT`.
- `function text_of(n: Name, oid: str) -> str?`, called `x509.text_of(n, oid)`: The characters of the first attribute of `n` whose type is `oid`: the common name of a subject, its organization. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `variant GeneralName = .other_name(type_id: asn1.Oid, value: asn1.Value) | .email(address: str) | .dns(name: str) | .x400_address(der: [u8]) | .directory(name: Name) | .edi_party(der: [u8]) | .uri(uri: str) | .ip(address: net.Host) | .ip_network(network: net.Network) | .registered_id(oid: asn1.Oid)`: A name of another kind than a distinguished one, as RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.6 lists them: what an alternative name, an access location and a name constraint hold.
- `function to_general_name(v: asn1.Value) -> GeneralName?`, called `x509.to_general_name(v)`: The general name `v` holds, its IMPLICIT tag read. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `record Algorithm(oid: asn1.Oid, parameters: asn1.Value?)`: An AlgorithmIdentifier: the algorithm and its parameters, which some algorithms leave out and others write as NULL.
- `record PublicKey(algorithm: Algorithm, key: [u8], der: [u8])`: A subject's public key as a certificate holds it: SubjectPublicKeyInfo.
- `function to_algorithm(v: asn1.Value) -> Algorithm?`, called `x509.to_algorithm(v)`: The algorithm `v` holds, an AlgorithmIdentifier. Fails `invalid`.
- `function scheme_of(algorithm: Algorithm) -> keypairs.Scheme?`, called `x509.scheme_of(algorithm)`: The scheme of `crypto/keypairs` that checks a signature of `algorithm`. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function algorithm_of(scheme: keypairs.Scheme) -> Algorithm`, called `x509.algorithm_of(scheme)`: The algorithm `scheme`'s signatures are named by, as this package writes it into a certificate, a request and a list: the inverse of `scheme_of`, for a document of another standard signed by the same schemes (an OCSP response, a timestamp).
- `function decode_public_key(der: [u8]) -> PublicKey?`, called `x509.decode_public_key(der)`: The public key DER `der` holds, a SubjectPublicKeyInfo. Fails `invalid`.
- `function kind_of(key: PublicKey) -> keypairs.Kind?`, called `x509.kind_of(key)`: The kind of `key` as `crypto/keypairs` names it, an RSA key's modulus measured. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function verify_signature(key: PublicKey, algorithm: Algorithm, message: [u8], signature: [u8]) -> bool?`, called `x509.verify_signature(key, algorithm, message: message, signature: signature)`: Whether `signature` is the signature of `message` by `algorithm` of the key `key`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Extension(oid: asn1.Oid, critical: bool, value: [u8])`: One extension as written: its identifier, whether it is critical, and its value's DER, decoded or not.
- `record KeyUsage(digital_signature: bool, content_commitment: bool, key_encipherment: bool, data_encipherment: bool, key_agreement: bool, key_cert_sign: bool, crl_sign: bool, encipher_only: bool, decipher_only: bool)`: The key usages of `keyUsage` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.3), one for each bit.
- `record BasicConstraints(is_ca: bool, path_len: i64?)`: `basicConstraints` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.9).
- `record AuthorityKeyId(key_id: [u8]?, issuer: [GeneralName], serial: big.Integer?)`: `authorityKeyIdentifier` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.1).
- `variant Reason = .unspecified | .key_compromise | .ca_compromise | .affiliation_changed | .superseded | .cessation_of_operation | .certificate_hold | .remove_from_crl | .privilege_withdrawn | .aa_compromise`: Why a certificate was revoked (RFC 5280 § 5.3.1), and the reasons a list covers.
- `record DistributionPoint(full_name: [GeneralName], relative_name: [Attribute], reasons: [Reason]?, crl_issuer: [GeneralName])`: Where a revocation list is: a point of `cRLDistributionPoints` or `freshestCRL` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.13).
- `record AccessDescription(method: asn1.Oid, location: GeneralName)`: One access of `authorityInfoAccess` or `subjectInfoAccess` (RFC 5280 §§ 4.2.2.1, 4.2.2.2).
- `record PolicyQualifier(oid: asn1.Oid, cps_uri: str, organization: str, notice_numbers: [i64], explicit_text: str, value: asn1.Value)`: One qualifier of a policy (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.4).
- `record Policy(oid: asn1.Oid, qualifiers: [PolicyQualifier])`: One policy of `certificatePolicies` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.4).
- `record PolicyMapping(issuer_domain: asn1.Oid, subject_domain: asn1.Oid)`: One mapping of `policyMappings` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.5).
- `record PolicyConstraints(require_explicit: i64?, inhibit_mapping: i64?)`: `policyConstraints` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.11).
- `record Subtree(base: GeneralName, minimum: i64, maximum: i64?)`: A subtree of a name constraint: a base name and the distances it covers.
- `record NameConstraints(permitted: [Subtree], excluded: [Subtree])`: `nameConstraints` (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.10).
- `record IssuingDistributionPoint(full_name: [GeneralName], relative_name: [Attribute], only_user_certs: bool, only_ca_certs: bool, only_some_reasons: [Reason]?, indirect_crl: bool, only_attribute_certs: bool)`: `issuingDistributionPoint` of a revocation list (RFC 5280 § 5.2.5).
- `record Extensions(list: [Extension], unknown: [Extension], alt_names: [GeneralName]?, issuer_alt_names: [GeneralName]?, key_usage: KeyUsage?, extended_key_usage: [asn1.Oid]?, basic_constraints: BasicConstraints?, subject_key_id: [u8]?, authority_key_id: AuthorityKeyId?, crl_distribution_points: [DistributionPoint]?, freshest_crl: [DistributionPoint]?, authority_info_access: [AccessDescription]?, subject_info_access: [AccessDescription]?, policies: [Policy]?, policy_mappings: [PolicyMapping]?, policy_constraints: PolicyConstraints?, inhibit_any_policy: i64?, name_constraints: NameConstraints?, crl_number: big.Integer?, delta_crl_indicator: big.Integer?, issuing_distribution_point: IssuingDistributionPoint?, reason: Reason?, invalidity_date: time.DateTime?, certificate_issuer: [GeneralName]?)`: The extensions of a certificate, a request, a list or a revoked entry: every one as written, and the ones this package knows decoded, each failing `not_found` where it is not there.
- `function to_extension(v: asn1.Value) -> Extension?`, called `x509.to_extension(v)`: The extension `v` holds, as written, undecoded. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_extensions(list: [Extension]) -> Extensions?`, called `x509.to_extensions(list)`: The extensions `list`, the ones this package knows decoded. Fails `invalid`.
- `function extension_of(extensions: Extensions, oid: str) -> Extension?`, called `x509.extension_of(extensions, oid)`: The extension of `extensions` whose identifier is `oid`, known or not. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Certificate(der: [u8], tbs: [u8], version: i64, serial: big.Integer, signature_algorithm: Algorithm, issuer: Name, not_before: time.DateTime, not_after: time.DateTime, subject: Name, public_key: PublicKey, issuer_unique_id: asn1.BitString?, subject_unique_id: asn1.BitString?, extensions: Extensions, signature: [u8])`: A certificate read (RFC 5280 § 4.1).
- `function decode_certificate(der: [u8]) -> Certificate?`, called `x509.decode_certificate(der)`: The certificate DER `der` holds. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function decode_certificates(der: [u8]) -> [Certificate]?`, called `x509.decode_certificates(der)`: Every certificate of `der`, certificates' DER written one after another, as a TLS server sends its chain. Fails as `decode_certificate` does for the first it refuses.
- `function parse_certificate(text: str) -> Certificate?`, called `x509.parse_certificate(text)`: The certificate of the first `CERTIFICATE` block of PEM in `text`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function parse_certificates(text: str) -> [Certificate]?`, called `x509.parse_certificates(text)`: The certificates of every `CERTIFICATE` block of PEM in `text`, in order: a bundle of roots, a chain. Fails as `parse_certificate` does for a block it refuses.
- `function format_certificate(certificate: Certificate) -> str`, called `x509.format_certificate(certificate)`: `certificate` as a `CERTIFICATE` block of PEM, lines of 64 characters each ending in `\n`.
- `function is_valid_at(certificate: Certificate, at: time.Instant) -> bool`, called `x509.is_valid_at(certificate, at)`: Whether `at` falls inside `certificate`'s validity, both ends included.
- `function is_self_issued(certificate: Certificate) -> bool`, called `x509.is_self_issued(certificate)`: Whether `certificate` names itself as its issuer: a root, or a certificate an authority issued to itself.
- `function is_signed_by(certificate: Certificate, issuer: Certificate) -> bool?`, called `x509.is_signed_by(certificate: certificate, issuer: issuer)`: Whether `issuer`'s key signed `certificate`. Fails as `verify_signature` does.
- `record RequestAttribute(oid: asn1.Oid, values: [asn1.Value])`: One attribute of a certificate request: its type and its values.
- `record Request(der: [u8], info: [u8], version: i64, subject: Name, public_key: PublicKey, attributes: [RequestAttribute], extensions: Extensions, signature_algorithm: Algorithm, signature: [u8])`: A certificate request of PKCS #10 (RFC 2986), read by `decode_request` or `parse_request`.
- `function decode_request(der: [u8]) -> Request?`, called `x509.decode_request(der)`: The certificate request DER `der` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_request(text: str) -> Request?`, called `x509.parse_request(text)`: The request of the first `CERTIFICATE REQUEST` block of PEM in `text`, or of OpenSSL's older `NEW CERTIFICATE REQUEST`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_request_signed(request: Request) -> bool?`, called `x509.is_request_signed(request)`: Whether `request` is signed by its own subject's key, as a request must be. Fails as `verify_signature` does.
- `record Revoked(serial: big.Integer, date: time.DateTime, extensions: Extensions)`: One certificate a list revokes.
