- `record RevocationList(der: [u8], tbs: [u8], version: i64, signature_algorithm: Algorithm, issuer: Name, this_update: time.DateTime, next_update: time.DateTime?, revoked: [Revoked], extensions: Extensions, signature: [u8])`: A certificate revocation list (RFC 5280 § 5), read by `decode_crl` or `parse_crl`.
- `function decode_crl(der: [u8]) -> RevocationList?`, called `x509.decode_crl(der)`: The revocation list DER `der` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_crl(text: str) -> RevocationList?`, called `x509.parse_crl(text)`: The list of the first `X509 CRL` block of PEM in `text`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_crl_signed_by(crl: RevocationList, issuer: Certificate) -> bool?`, called `x509.is_crl_signed_by(crl, issuer)`: Whether `issuer`'s key signed `crl`. Fails as `verify_signature` does.
- `function revoked_of(crl: RevocationList, serial: big.Integer) -> Revoked?`, called `x509.revoked_of(crl, serial)`: The entry of `crl` that revokes the serial `serial`. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Verification(roots: [Certificate], at: time.Instant, purpose: str, host: str)`: What `verify_chain` holds a chain to.
- `function chain_of(leaf: Certificate, pool: [Certificate]) -> [Certificate]`, called `x509.chain_of(leaf, pool)`: `leaf` and its issuers from `pool`, in order: the leaf, the certificate that issued it, the one that issued that, up to a self-issued certificate or one whose issuer `pool` does not hold.
- `function verify_chain(chain: [Certificate], options: Verification) -> ()?`, called `x509.verify_chain(chain, options)`: Whether `chain` holds under `options`: each certificate issued by the next and signed by its key, the last a root of `options.roots` or issued by one, every one valid at `options.at`, every issuer a certificate authority whose key may sign certificates and whose path length allows what follows it, no critical extension this package does not read, every name below an issuer within its name constraints, and the leaf for `options.purpose` and `options.host` where they are not empty. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_for_host(certificate: Certificate, host: str) -> bool`, called `x509.is_for_host(certificate, host)`: Whether `certificate` is for the host `host`, as RFC 6125 § 6.4 says: one of its DNS names matches it, ASCII case ignored, a wildcard standing for the whole first label alone; an IP literal is matched as `is_for_address` matches an address.
- `function is_for_address(certificate: Certificate, address: net.Host) -> bool`, called `x509.is_for_address(certificate, address)`: Whether `certificate` is for the address `address`: one of its IP addresses is it, an IPv4 address and the IPv6 address that maps it being one.
- `variant Role = .unstated | .end_entity | .authority | .limited_authority(path_len: i64)`: What a certificate or a request says about its key's role: the `basicConstraints` extension (RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.9), written critical where it is written at all.
- `record Profile(alt_names: [GeneralName], key_usage: KeyUsage, extended_key_usage: [asn1.Oid], role: Role, extra: [Extension])`: What a certificate or a request says beyond its names and its key: the role of the key, what it may be used for, and the names the subject also goes by.
- `function default_profile() -> Profile`, called `x509.default_profile()`: The profile that says nothing: no name, no usage, no purpose, no `basicConstraints`, no other extension.
- `record CertificateTemplate(serial: big.Integer, subject: Name, not_before: time.DateTime, not_after: time.DateTime, profile: Profile, ocsp_urls: [str], issuer_urls: [str], crl_urls: [str])`: What `create_certificate` and `create_self_signed` write into a certificate besides its key and its issuer.
- `record RequestTemplate(subject: Name, profile: Profile, attributes: [RequestAttribute])`: What `create_request` writes into a certificate request.
- `record Revocation(serial: big.Integer, date: time.DateTime, reason: Reason, invalidity: Invalidity)`: One certificate a revocation list lists, and why.
- `variant Invalidity = .unstated | .since(at: time.DateTime)`: The `invalidityDate` of a revoked certificate (RFC 5280 § 5.3.2).
- `record RevocationListTemplate(number: big.Integer, this_update: time.DateTime, next_update: time.DateTime, revoked: [Revocation])`: What `create_crl` writes into a revocation list besides its issuer.
- `function new_attribute(oid: str, text: str) -> Attribute?`, called `x509.new_attribute(oid: oid, text: text)`: One attribute of a name made from text, written in the string type RFC 5280 gives its type: PrintableString for a country and a serial number, IA5String for an email address and a domain component, UTF8String for any other. Fails `invalid`.
- `function new_name(rdns: [[Attribute]]) -> Name?`, called `x509.new_name(rdns)`: A name made from its relative names, which `to_name` reads back and DER writes in a canonical order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function public_key_of(key: keypairs.PrivateKey) -> PublicKey?`, called `x509.public_key_of(key)`: The public key of `key`, as a certificate's subject key and a request's. Fails as `keypairs.public_of` and `keypairs.encode_public_der` fail, and as `decode_public_key` does.
- `function random_serial() -> big.Integer?`, called `x509.random_serial()`: A serial number of 159 random bits from the system's generator for keys, positive and 20 octets at most in DER, as Python's `random_serial_number` draws one. Fails with the code of `os.random_bytes` where the system's generator refuses.
- `function from_general_name(general: GeneralName) -> asn1.Value?`, called `x509.from_general_name(general)`: The ASN.1 of `general`, a name of the kinds a subject alternative name, an access and a distribution point hold: the inverse of `to_general_name`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_extension(extension: Extension) -> asn1.Value?`, called `x509.from_extension(extension)`: The SEQUENCE of `extension`, as a certificate holds it: the inverse of `to_extension`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function profile_extensions(profile: Profile, subject_empty: bool) -> [Extension]?`, called `x509.profile_extensions(profile, subject_empty)`: The extensions `profile` writes, as `Extension`s whose values are DER: `basicConstraints`, `keyUsage`, `extKeyUsage` and `subjectAltName` from its own fields, in that order, then `extra` as given. Fails `invalid`.
- `function create_self_signed(template: CertificateTemplate, signer: keypairs.PrivateKey, scheme: keypairs.Scheme) -> Certificate?`, called `x509.create_self_signed(template, signer, scheme)`: A certificate that `signer` gives itself: its own key is the subject's, its subject is its issuer, and no `authorityKeyIdentifier` is written, as RFC 5280 § 4.2.1.1 allows of a self-signed one. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function create_certificate(template: CertificateTemplate, subject_key: PublicKey, issuer: Certificate, signer: keypairs.PrivateKey, scheme: keypairs.Scheme) -> Certificate?`, called `x509.create_certificate(template, subject_key, issuer, signer, scheme)`: A certificate that `issuer`'s key signs for `subject_key`: its issuer is `issuer`'s subject, written with `issuer`'s own bytes, and its `authorityKeyIdentifier` is `issuer`'s key identifier (or RFC 5280's first method over `issuer`'s key where `issuer` writes none). Fails `invalid`.
- `function create_request(template: RequestTemplate, signer: keypairs.PrivateKey, scheme: keypairs.Scheme) -> Request?`, called `x509.create_request(template, signer, scheme)`: A certificate request (PKCS #10, RFC 2986) for `signer`'s key, signed by `signer` to show that its holder has it. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_request(request: Request) -> str`, called `x509.format_request(request)`: `request` as a `CERTIFICATE REQUEST` block of PEM, lines of 64 characters each ending in `\n`.
- `function create_crl(template: RevocationListTemplate, issuer: Certificate, signer: keypairs.PrivateKey, scheme: keypairs.Scheme) -> RevocationList?`, called `x509.create_crl(template, issuer, signer, scheme)`: A revocation list (RFC 5280 § 5) of `template`, issued by `issuer` and signed with its key: version 2, with `authorityKeyIdentifier` and `cRLNumber`, each entry's reason and invalidity date where it has them. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_crl(crl: RevocationList) -> str`, called `x509.format_crl(crl)`: `crl` as an `X509 CRL` block of PEM, lines of 64 characters each ending in `\n`.
- `constant COMMON_NAME: str`, value `"2.5.4.3"`: The attribute `commonName`, `2.5.4.3`.

### fs/acl

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/fs/acl`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/acl/).

Who may do what to a file or a folder beyond its permission bits: its access control list read, written whole, copied to another path, and the id of a user or a group found by name, so a backup restores a folder with who may read it and a program grants one user or group a right.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `lists.INVALID`: An id holding a zero byte, a path holding one, an entry's rights or flags below 0, an id the system cannot read as one, a Linux list missing its owner, owning group or everyone-else entry or naming one twice.
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `lists.FILE_NOT_FOUND`: The path names nothing.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `lists.NOT_FOUND`: The system knows no user or group of that name.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `lists.PERMISSION`: The system refuses the call to this program: only a file's owner, or a user its list lets, changes a list.
- `constant NOT_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `lists.NOT_A_DIRECTORY`: A part of the path on its way is not a folder.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `lists.NOT_TEXT`: On Windows, a path or a name that is not UTF-8.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `lists.LIMIT`: The system has no room for the list, or one read is past 16 MiB.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `lists.UNSUPPORTED`: The volume keeps no list, an entry is one this system's lists cannot hold, or the system keeps none that is read here.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `lists.FAILED`: The system refused for a reason none of the codes above names; the message carries its number.
- `constant READ_DATA: i64`, value `0x1`: To read a file's bytes, or list a folder.
- `constant WRITE_DATA: i64`, value `0x2`: To write a file's bytes, or make a file in a folder.
- `constant APPEND_DATA: i64`, value `0x4`: To write at a file's end, or make a folder in a folder.
- `constant READ_EXTENDED: i64`, value `0x8`: To read the extended attributes.
- `constant WRITE_EXTENDED: i64`, value `0x10`: To write the extended attributes.
- `constant EXECUTE: i64`, value `0x20`: To run a file, or pass through a folder.
- `constant DELETE_CHILD: i64`, value `0x40`: To remove what a folder holds, whatever the list of what it holds says.
- `constant READ_ATTRIBUTES: i64`, value `0x80`: To read the attributes: times, size, kind.
- `constant WRITE_ATTRIBUTES: i64`, value `0x100`: To write the attributes.
- `constant DELETE: i64`, value `0x10000`: To remove it.
- `constant READ_SECURITY: i64`, value `0x20000`: To read its list.
- `constant WRITE_SECURITY: i64`, value `0x40000`: To write its list.
- `constant CHANGE_OWNER: i64`, value `0x80000`: To make oneself its owner.
- `constant SYNCHRONIZE: i64`, value `0x100000`: To wait on it, which Windows asks of every reading and writing.
- `constant GENERIC_ALL: i64`, value `0x10000000`: Windows' generic right to everything, which an entry a folder hands down may carry and Darwin has no place for.
- `constant GENERIC_EXECUTE: i64`, value `0x20000000`: Windows' generic right to run a file or pass through a folder, which an entry a folder hands down may carry and Darwin has no place for.
- `constant GENERIC_WRITE: i64`, value `0x40000000`: Windows' generic right to write, which an entry a folder hands down may carry and Darwin has no place for.
- `constant GENERIC_READ: i64`, value `0x80000000`: Windows' generic right to read, which an entry a folder hands down may carry and Darwin has no place for.
- `constant READ: i64`, value `0x120089`: What Windows' Explorer calls Read: the data, the attributes, the extended attributes and the list read, and the wait (`FILE_GENERIC_READ`).
- `constant WRITE: i64`, value `0x120116`: What Explorer calls Write (`FILE_GENERIC_WRITE`).
- `constant READ_AND_EXECUTE: i64`, value `0x1200a9`: What Explorer calls Read and execute.
- `constant MODIFY: i64`, value `0x1301bf`: What Explorer calls Modify: read, execute, write and remove.
- `constant FULL_CONTROL: i64`, value `0x1f01ff`: What Explorer calls Full control (`FILE_ALL_ACCESS`).
- `constant FILE_INHERIT: i64`, value `0x1`: The entry is handed down to the files made in a folder.
- `constant FOLDER_INHERIT: i64`, value `0x2`: The entry is handed down to the folders made in a folder.
- `constant LIMIT_INHERIT: i64`, value `0x4`: The entry handed down goes one level only, and no further.
- `constant ONLY_INHERIT: i64`, value `0x8`: The entry is only handed down, and does not govern the folder itself.
- `constant INHERITED: i64`, value `0x10`: The entry came down from a parent; on Windows a list not protected takes its parent's again when written, so such an entry is left to the system.
- `constant LINUX_DEFAULT: i64`, value `0xb`: A Linux folder's default entries: handed down to the files and folders made in it, and not governing the folder itself.
- `variant Who = .user | .group | .owner | .owning_group | .others | .mask`: Whom an entry names.
- `record Entry(who: Who, deny: bool, rights: i64, flags: i64, id: str, name: str)`: One entry of a list.
- `record Acl(protected: bool, entries: [Entry])`: A file's or a folder's list.
- `function read(path: str) -> Acl?`, called `acl.read(path)`: `path`'s access list. Fails `file_not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function link_read(path: str) -> Acl?`, called `acl.link_read(path)`: The access list of the link at `path` itself, not of what it names. Fails as `read` does.
- `function write(path: str, acl: Acl) -> ()?`, called `acl.write(path, acl)`: Replaces `path`'s access list with `acl`. Fails `unsupported`, `permission`, `invalid`.
- `function link_write(path: str, acl: Acl) -> ()?`, called `acl.link_write(path, acl)`: Replaces the access list of the link at `path` itself with `acl`. Fails as `write` does.
- `function copy(from: str, to: str) -> ()?`, called `acl.copy(from: from, to: to)`: Writes `from`'s access list on `to`. Fails as `read` and `write` do.
- `function user_id_of(name: str) -> str?`, called `acl.user_id_of(name)`: The id of the user the system knows by `name`, as an entry's `id` holds it. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function group_id_of(name: str) -> str?`, called `acl.group_id_of(name)`: The id of the group the system knows by `name`, as an entry's `id` holds it. Fails `not_found`.


### fs/watch

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/fs/watch`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/watch/).

A folder, a folder's whole tree or one file watched, and every change the system tells of it handed to the program as an `Event`, in order: an entry created, removed, written, its facts changed, or renamed with both its names; events lost told as one `overflow`; the watched folder itself gone.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument out of its range: an empty path or one holding a zero byte, a room outside 1 to `MOST`, a limit below zero.
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"file_not_found"`: The path names nothing, or a folder on its way is not there; and a watch whose watched folder is gone, once its `gone` event was taken.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The system refuses this program the path.
- `constant NOT_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `"not_a_directory"`: A tree was asked of a path that names a file, or a file stands on the path's way.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system or the process has no watch, descriptor, thread or memory left; on Linux, `/proc/sys/fs/inotify/max_user_watches` counts one watch per folder of a tree.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The watch is closed.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop (`os.catch_stop`, `os.ask_stop`), before the call or while it waited.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This system cannot watch the volume the path stands on.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names; the message carries its number.
- `constant ROOM: i64`, value `65536`: The room a watch is opened with by `open` and `open_tree`: the events it holds before it overflows.
- `constant MOST: i64`, value `1048576`: The most room a watch may be opened with, by `open_with`.
- `record Watch(handle: hero_watch.Watch, path: str, tree: bool)`: A watch of one path.
- `variant Change = .created | .removed | .changed | .attributes | .renamed(from: str) | .overflow | .gone`: What happened to an entry.
- `record Event(path: str, change: Change, directory: bool)`: One change the system told.
- `function open(path: str) -> Watch?`, called `watch.open(path)`: A watch of `path`: a folder's own entries, the folder's entries and not theirs, or one file, with room for `ROOM` events. Fails `invalid`, `file_not_found`, `permission`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function open_tree(path: str) -> Watch?`, called `watch.open_tree(path)`: A watch of the folder `path` and of every folder below it, with room for `ROOM` events. Fails `not_a_directory`.
- `function open_with(path: str, tree: bool, room: i64) -> Watch?`, called `watch.open_with(path, tree, room)`: A watch of `path`, its whole tree or not, holding at most `room` events before it overflows. Fails `invalid`.
- `function close(@w: Watch) -> ()?`, called `watch.close(@w)`: Closes the watch and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`: the system's watch ends, and the events not taken are let go. Fails `closed`.
- `function wait(w: Watch, limit: time.Duration) -> [Event]?`, called `watch.wait(w, limit)`: The events the watch holds, in the order the system told them, waiting until one is told, `limit` passes, or the stop is asked. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `stopped`, `closed`, `file_not_found`.
- `function wait_forever(w: Watch) -> [Event]?`, called `watch.wait_forever(w)`: The events the watch holds, waiting as long as it takes: until one is told or the stop is asked. Fails `stopped`, `closed`, `file_not_found`.
- `function count(w: Watch) -> i64?`, called `watch.count(w)`: How many events wait in the watch, an `overflow` among them, without waiting. Fails `closed`.
- `function add_to(set: poll.Set, w: Watch) -> i64?`, called `watch.add_to(set, w)`: Adds the watch to the set `set` and answers the entry's key: a wait on the set tells the key readable while an event waits in the watch, and the program then takes them with `wait` and a limit of zero. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function format_event(e: Event) -> str`, called `watch.format_event(e)`: An event as one line a person reads: what happened, whether to a folder, and its path in double quotes as it stands; a rename names both paths.


### fs/xattr

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/fs/xattr`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/fs/xattr/).

The extended attributes of a file or a folder: named values it carries beside its bytes, listed, read, written, removed and copied to another path, so a backup keeps a macOS file's tags (`com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags`) and quarantine (`com.apple.quarantine`), a Linux file's SELinux label (`security.selinux`), and what a program stored beside a file of its own.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `calls.INVALID`: A name that is empty, holds a zero byte, is longer than the system takes, or on Windows holds `:`, `\` or `/`; a path that holds a zero byte; a value of a form the name keeps for itself (Darwin's `com.apple.FinderInfo` is 32 bytes).
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `calls.FILE_NOT_FOUND`: The path names nothing.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `calls.NOT_FOUND`: The path has no attribute of that name.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `calls.EXISTS`: The path has an attribute of that name, and `write_with` was told `.only_new`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `calls.PERMISSION`: The system refuses the call to this program: the file's permission, a namespace this user may not write, a name the system keeps for itself, a `user.` attribute on a Linux link.
- `constant NOT_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `calls.NOT_A_DIRECTORY`: A part of the path on its way is not a folder.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `calls.NOT_TEXT`: A name the system lists is not UTF-8, or on Windows the path or the name handed is not.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `calls.LIMIT`: The system has no room for the attribute, the value is larger than the volume keeps for one, or one read is past a GiB.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `calls.UNSUPPORTED`: The volume keeps no extended attribute of that kind, or the system keeps none that is read here.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `calls.FAILED`: The system refused for a reason none of the codes above names; the message carries its number.
- `variant When = .always | .only_new | .only_existing`: What `write_with` does where the attribute is there, or is not.
- `function names(path: str) -> [str]?`, called `xattr.names(path)`: The names of `path`'s extended attributes, in the order the system lists them. Fails `file_not_found`, `not_text`.
- `function link_names(path: str) -> [str]?`, called `xattr.link_names(path)`: The names of the extended attributes of the link at `path` itself, as `names` lists them. Fails as `names` does.
- `function read(path: str, name: str) -> [u8]?`, called `xattr.read(path: path, name: name)`: The value of `path`'s extended attribute `name`, its bytes, which may be none. Fails `not_found`, `file_not_found`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function link_read(path: str, name: str) -> [u8]?`, called `xattr.link_read(path: path, name: name)`: The value of the extended attribute `name` of the link at `path` itself. Fails as `read` does.
- `function write(path: str, name: str, value: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `xattr.write(path: path, name: name, value)`: Writes `value` as `path`'s extended attribute `name`, made where it is not there and replaced where it is. Fails `limit`, `permission`.
- `function write_with(path: str, name: str, value: [u8], when: When, follow: bool) -> ()?`, called `xattr.write_with(path: path, name: name, value, when, follow)`: Writes `value` as `path`'s extended attribute `name` where `when` says, on the link itself where `follow` is false. Fails `exists`, `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function remove(path: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `xattr.remove(path: path, name: name)`: Removes `path`'s extended attribute `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function link_remove(path: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `xattr.link_remove(path: path, name: name)`: Removes the extended attribute `name` of the link at `path` itself. Fails as `remove` does.
- `function copy(from: str, to: str) -> ()?`, called `xattr.copy(from: from, to: to)`: Writes every extended attribute of `from` on `to`, each made or replaced; an attribute `to` has and `from` has not stays. Fails `permission`.


### sql/odbc

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/sql/odbc`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/odbc/).

Any database the system's ODBC driver manager reaches, through the API every driver of Rebel keeps over `sql`'s types, name for name, as `sql`'s opening comment writes it: `open`, `close`, `is_closed`, `ping`, `exec`, `query`, `query_one`, `exec_script`, `prepare`, `exec_prepared`, `query_prepared`, `close_statement`, `begin`, `commit`, `rollback` and `in_transaction`.

- `variant Target = .connection_string(text: str) | .data_source(name: str, user: str, password: str)`: What names the database a connection is made to.
- `record Options(target: Target, login_timeout: time.Duration, query_timeout: time.Duration)`: Where a database is and how long to wait for it.
- `function options(connection: str) -> Options`, called `odbc.options(connection)`: The options of a connection made from the connection string `connection`, waiting fifteen seconds to log in, .NET's `OdbcConnection`'s default, and with no limit on a statement.
- `function dsn_options(dsn: str, user: str, password: str) -> Options`, called `odbc.dsn_options(dsn: dsn, user: user, password: password)`: The options of a connection to the data source `dsn`, as `options` sets the rest.
- `function open(opts: Options) -> Db?`, called `odbc.open(opts)`: A connection to the database `opts` names, ready for a statement, each statement committed on its own until `begin`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `not_found`, `timeout`, `permission`.
- `function close(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `odbc.close(@db)`: Ends the connection: a transaction still open is rolled back and the connection is given back; the place is emptied, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function is_closed(db: Db) -> bool`, called `odbc.is_closed(db)`: Whether `close` has ended `db`.
- `function ping(db: Db) -> ()?`, called `odbc.ping(db)`: Answers whether the connection still works, as its driver knows without a statement (`SQL_ATTR_CONNECTION_DEAD`). Fails `closed`.
- `record Db(connection: hero_odbc.Connection, name: str, transaction_open: bool, query_timeout: time.Duration, prepared: i64)`: A connection to a data source, which `open` makes and `close` ends.
- `function in_transaction(db: Db) -> bool`, called `odbc.in_transaction(db)`: Whether a transaction `begin` opened is open on `db`.
- `function set_query_timeout(@db: Db, timeout: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `odbc.set_query_timeout(@db, timeout)`: Sets how long each later statement on `db` runs before its driver stops it, failing `timeout`. Fails `invalid`, `timeout`, `closed`.
- `variant Isolation = .read_uncommitted | .read_committed | .repeatable_read | .serializable`: How far the transactions of a connection are kept from each other's changes, SQL's four levels.
- `function set_isolation(db: Db, level: Isolation) -> ()?`, called `odbc.set_isolation(db, level)`: Sets the isolation of `db`'s later transactions. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function isolation_of(db: Db) -> Isolation?`, called `odbc.isolation_of(db)`: The isolation of `db`'s transactions, as its driver reports it. Fails `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_read_only(db: Db, read_only: bool) -> ()?`, called `odbc.set_read_only(db, read_only)`: Tells `db`'s driver whether the program only reads through it, so that it may read faster or refuse a change (`SQL_ATTR_ACCESS_MODE`). Fails `closed`.
- `record Info(dbms_name: str, dbms_version: str, driver_name: str, driver_version: str, odbc_version: str, manager_version: str, data_source: str, database: str, server: str, user: str, identifier_quote: str, search_escape: str, keywords: [str], multiple_results: bool, read_only: bool)`: What a connection's driver says of its database and itself, as `SQLGetInfo` answers; each text is "" where the driver says nothing.
- `function info_of(db: Db) -> Info?`, called `odbc.info_of(db)`: What `db`'s driver says of its database and itself. Fails `closed`.
- `function exec(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `odbc.exec(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement`, one statement that answers no rows, with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers how many rows it changed. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.query(@db, statement, params)`: Runs `statement` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its columns and every row it answered. Fails `invalid`.
- `function query_one(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Row?`, called `odbc.query_one(@db, statement, params)`: The first row `statement` answers, with `params` bound to its placeholders. Fails `not_found`.
- `function query_sets(@db: Db, statement: str, params: [sql.Value]) -> [sql.Rows]?`, called `odbc.query_sets(@db, statement, params)`: Every result `statement` answers, in order: a procedure or a batch the driver runs whole may answer several. Fails as `query` does, with the failure of the first result that fails.
- `function exec_script(@db: Db, script: str) -> ()?`, called `odbc.exec_script(@db, script)`: Runs every statement of `script`, in order and with no parameters, as a migration does; their rows are dropped. Fails `invalid`.
- `function split_script(script: str) -> [str]`, called `odbc.split_script(script)`: The statements of `script`, cut as `exec_script` cuts it, each without its `;` and the blanks around it, a comment before it kept as part of it; a piece holding nothing but blanks and comments is left out.
- `record Statement(handle: hero_odbc.Statement, text: str, parameter_count: i64, columns: [sql.Column])`: A statement its driver has read once, which `prepare` makes and `close_statement` ends.
- `function prepare(@db: Db, statement: str) -> Statement?`, called `odbc.prepare(@db, statement)`: `statement` read by its driver once, to be run many times with `exec_prepared` and `query_prepared`. Fails as `exec` does where the driver refuses the statement.
- `function exec_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Result?`, called `odbc.exec_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, as `exec` runs a statement. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function query_prepared(@db: Db, prepared: Statement, params: [sql.Value]) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.query_prepared(@db, prepared, params)`: Runs `prepared` with `params` bound to its placeholders, and answers its rows, as `query` does. Fails as `exec_prepared` does.
- `function close_statement(@db: Db, @prepared: Statement) -> ()?`, called `odbc.close_statement(@db, @prepared)`: Gives `prepared` back and empties it, so every later run of it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function begin(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `odbc.begin(@db)`: Opens a transaction: the statements after it commit together at `commit`, or none of them does, at `rollback`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function commit(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `odbc.commit(@db)`: Commits the open transaction: every statement since `begin` takes effect, and each statement after it commits on its own again. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rollback(@db: Db) -> ()?`, called `odbc.rollback(@db)`: Rolls the open transaction back: no statement since `begin` takes effect. Fails `invalid`.
- `function tables(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str, kinds: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.tables(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table, kinds: kinds)`: The tables the database holds, as ODBC's catalog answers them (`SQLTables`): the columns `TABLE_CAT`, `TABLE_SCHEM`, `TABLE_NAME`, `TABLE_TYPE` and `REMARKS`, in the driver's order. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function table_columns(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str, column: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.table_columns(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table, column: column)`: The columns of the tables asked, as ODBC's catalog answers them (`SQLColumns`): `TABLE_NAME`, `COLUMN_NAME`, `DATA_TYPE`, `TYPE_NAME`, `COLUMN_SIZE`, `NULLABLE` and the rest of ODBC's eighteen. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function primary_keys(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.primary_keys(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table)`: The columns of `table`'s primary key, in the key's order (`SQLPrimaryKeys`): `COLUMN_NAME`, `KEY_SEQ` and `PK_NAME` among them. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function foreign_keys(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str, foreign_catalog: str, foreign_schema: str, foreign_table: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.foreign_keys(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table, foreign_catalog: foreign_catalog, foreign_schema: foreign_schema, foreign_table: foreign_table)`: The foreign keys between tables (`SQLForeignKeys`): those of `foreign_table` where it is given, those that point at `table` where it is given, the one between them where both are. Fails `invalid`.
- `function indexes(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str, unique_only: bool) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.indexes(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table, unique_only)`: The indexes of `table` and the counts the driver keeps of it (`SQLStatistics`): `INDEX_NAME`, `NON_UNIQUE`, `COLUMN_NAME` and `ORDINAL_POSITION` among them. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function procedures(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, procedure: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.procedures(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, procedure: procedure)`: The procedures the database holds (`SQLProcedures`): `PROCEDURE_NAME` and `PROCEDURE_TYPE` among them. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function procedure_columns(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, procedure: str, column: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.procedure_columns(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, procedure: procedure, column: column)`: The parameters and result columns of the procedures asked (`SQLProcedureColumns`). Fails as `tables` does.
- `function data_types(db: Db) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.data_types(db)`: The data types the database offers (`SQLGetTypeInfo`): `TYPE_NAME`, `DATA_TYPE`, `COLUMN_SIZE` and the rest, one row a type. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function row_id_columns(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.row_id_columns(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table)`: The columns that best tell a row of `table` apart (`SQLSpecialColumns`, `SQL_BEST_ROWID`), a row id where the database has one. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function row_version_columns(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.row_version_columns(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table)`: The columns of `table` the database changes itself whenever a row changes (`SQLSpecialColumns`, `SQL_ROWVER`), a row's version. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function table_privileges(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.table_privileges(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table)`: Who may do what to the tables asked (`SQLTablePrivileges`): `GRANTEE` and `PRIVILEGE` among the columns. Fails as `tables` does.
- `function column_privileges(db: Db, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str, column: str) -> sql.Rows?`, called `odbc.column_privileges(db, catalog: catalog, schema: schema, table: table, column: column)`: Who may do what to the columns of `table` (`SQLColumnPrivileges`). Fails as `tables` does.
- `function manager() -> str?`, called `odbc.manager()`: The library of the driver manager this program loaded: `odbc32.dll`, `libodbc.so.2`, `libiodbc.2.dylib`. Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Driver(name: str, attributes: [Attribute])`: A driver the manager knows, and what its configuration says of it.
- `function drivers() -> [Driver]?`, called `odbc.drivers()`: The drivers the manager knows, in its order (`SQLDrivers`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `record DataSource(name: str, driver: str, system: bool)`: A data source the manager knows by its name.
- `function data_sources() -> [DataSource]?`, called `odbc.data_sources()`: The data sources the manager knows (`SQLDataSources`): the user's own first, then the system's. Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Attribute(key: str, value: str)`: One `key=value` pair of a connection string.
- `function parse_connection(text: str) -> [Attribute]?`, called `odbc.parse_connection(text)`: The pairs of the connection string `text`, in its order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_connection(attributes: [Attribute]) -> str?`, called `odbc.format_connection(attributes)`: The connection string of `attributes`, each `key=value` and `;` between them, a value inside braces where it holds `;`, `{`, `}`, `=` or a blank at either end, or is empty. Fails `invalid`.


### ldap

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/ldap`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ldap/).

An LDAP client written in Heroes: it speaks LDAPv3 (RFC 4511) to a directory server over a TCP connection of `net` or a TLS connection of `tls`, every message BER of `asn1`, and links no library.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: Bytes that are no LDAP, an argument the client refuses, or a result the server gives for a request it cannot read (protocolError, invalidDNSyntax, invalidAttributeSyntax, undefinedAttributeType, constraintViolation, namingViolation, objectClassViolation and the others about what was asked): every function.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: A value that is not UTF-8 where text was asked: `texts_of`, `text_of`, `parse_dn`, `unescape_dn_value`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The entry named does not exist (noSuchObject), an attribute or a value does not (noSuchAttribute), or the server refers the request elsewhere (referral): every operation; and `text_of`, `paged_of`, `parent_of` where what they read is not there.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The entry or the value is there already (entryAlreadyExists, attributeOrValueExists): `add`, `modify`, `rename`.
- `constant NOT_EMPTY: str`, value `"not_empty"`: The entry has entries below it (notAllowedOnNonLeaf): `delete`, `rename`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The server refuses the identity or its rights (invalidCredentials, insufficientAccessRights, inappropriateAuthentication, strongerAuthRequired, confidentialityRequired): every operation; and `connect` and `start_tls` where `tls` refuses.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection is closed, ended by an earlier failure, or the server closed it or sent a notice of disconnection: every operation.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The operation's deadline passed, or the server's own time limit did (timeLimitExceeded where the query asked none): every operation.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while a call waited: every operation.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The server's own limits cut the answer (sizeLimitExceeded where the query asked none, adminLimitExceeded), or it is busy or unavailable: `search` and every operation.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The server knows no such operation, control or mechanism (unavailableCriticalExtension, authMethodNotSupported, unwillingToPerform, affectsMultipleDSAs), or this platform cannot do what was asked: every operation, and `start_tls` on macOS.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: A result none of the codes above names (operationsError, other, a loop detected), the message carrying the server's own words; and `connect` where the network fails as `net` says.
- `record Result(code: i64, matched_dn: str, message: str, referrals: [str], controls: [Control])`: What the server answered an operation (RFC 4511 § 4.1.9): the last one, which `result_of` tells, and the end of a search.
- `function result_of(c: Conn) -> Result`, called `ldap.result_of(c)`: The result the server answered `c`'s last operation, whether it succeeded or failed.
- `record Control(oid: str, critical: bool, value: [u8])`: A control sent with a request or read from an answer (RFC 4511 § 4.1.11).
- `constant PAGED_RESULTS: str`, value `"1.2.840.113556.1.4.319"`: The simple paged results control (RFC 2696).
- `constant SORT_REQUEST: str`, value `"1.2.840.113556.1.4.473"`: The server-side sort request control (RFC 2891).
- `constant SORT_RESPONSE: str`, value `"1.2.840.113556.1.4.474"`: The server-side sort response control (RFC 2891).
- `constant MANAGE_DSA_IT: str`, value `"2.16.840.1.113730.3.4.2"`: The ManageDsaIT control: referrals and aliases read as entries (RFC 3296).
- `constant TREE_DELETE: str`, value `"1.2.840.113556.1.4.805"`: The subtree delete control, read by Active Directory and OpenLDAP.
- `constant PROXIED_AUTHORIZATION: str`, value `"2.16.840.1.113730.3.4.18"`: The proxied authorization control, version 2 (RFC 4370).
- `constant ASSERTION: str`, value `"1.3.6.1.1.12"`: The assertion control (RFC 4528).
- `constant WHO_AM_I: str`, value `"1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.11.3"`: The Who am I? extended operation (RFC 4532).
- `constant PASSWORD_MODIFY: str`, value `"1.3.6.1.4.1.4203.1.11.1"`: The Password Modify extended operation (RFC 3062).
- `constant START_TLS: str`, value `"1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.20037"`: The StartTLS extended operation (RFC 4511 § 4.14).
- `constant NOTICE_OF_DISCONNECTION: str`, value `"1.3.6.1.4.1.1466.20036"`: The notice of disconnection a server sends before it closes (RFC 4511 § 4.4.1).
- `function set_controls(@c: Conn, controls: [Control])`, called `ldap.set_controls(@c, controls)`: Sets the controls sent with every later request on `c`, bind and search included, until set again.
- `function paged_control(size: i64, cookie: [u8]) -> Control`, called `ldap.paged_control(size, cookie)`: The paged results control asking for a page of `size` entries after the page `cookie` ended (RFC 2696).
- `record Paged(size: i64, cookie: [u8])`: What a paged results control says (RFC 2696).
- `function paged_of(controls: [Control]) -> Paged?`, called `ldap.paged_of(controls)`: The paged results control among `controls`, read. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `record SortKey(attribute: str, ordering_rule: str, reverse: bool)`: One key of a server-side sort (RFC 2891).
- `function sort_control(sort_keys: [SortKey], critical: bool) -> Control?`, called `ldap.sort_control(sort_keys, critical)`: The server-side sort control asking for the entries in the order of `sort_keys` (RFC 2891). Fails `invalid`.
- `function sort_result_of(controls: [Control]) -> i64?`, called `ldap.sort_result_of(controls)`: The result code of the server-side sort response control among `controls`: `SUCCESS` where the entries are sorted. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function manage_dsa_it_control() -> Control`, called `ldap.manage_dsa_it_control()`: The ManageDsaIT control (RFC 3296): referral and alias entries read and changed as ordinary entries, critical.
- `function tree_delete_control() -> Control`, called `ldap.tree_delete_control()`: The subtree delete control: `delete` removes the entry and every entry below it, critical.
- `function proxied_authorization_control(authz_id: str) -> Control`, called `ldap.proxied_authorization_control(authz_id)`: The proxied authorization control (RFC 4370): the request runs as `authz_id`, critical.
- `function assertion_control(f: Filter) -> Control?`, called `ldap.assertion_control(f)`: The assertion control (RFC 4528): the request is done only where `f` holds of the entry, and fails `ASSERTION_FAILED` otherwise, critical. Fails `invalid`.
- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `389`: The port LDAP listens on, in plain text or for StartTLS.
- `constant DEFAULT_TLS_PORT: i64`, value `636`: The port LDAP listens on over TLS from the first byte (`ldaps://`).
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE: i64`, value `16777216`: The bytes a message may hold unless told otherwise: 16 MiB.
- `variant Security = .plain | .direct(roots: str) | .start_tls(roots: str)`: How a connection is secured.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, security: Security, deadline: time.Duration, max_message: i64)`: Where a server is and how a connection to it is made.
- `function options(host: str) -> Options`, called `ldap.options(host)`: The options of a connection to `host` on `DEFAULT_PORT` with StartTLS, the system's authorities trusted, a minute for each operation and `DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE`.
- `record Conn(session: session.Session)`: A connection to a directory server, anonymous until a bind.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Conn?`, called `ldap.connect(opts)`: A connection to the server `opts` names, secured as it says, anonymous. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function close(@c: Conn) -> ()?`, called `ldap.close(@c)`: Ends the session with an UnbindRequest and closes the connection. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(c: Conn) -> bool`, called `ldap.is_closed(c)`: Whether `c` is closed, by `close` or by a failure that ended it.
- `function is_secured(c: Conn) -> bool`, called `ldap.is_secured(c)`: Whether `c` runs over TLS.
- `function start_tls(@c: Conn, roots: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.start_tls(@c, roots)`: Begins TLS on `c`, open in plain text, with the StartTLS operation, the server's certificate checked for its authority and `c`'s host. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_deadline(@c: Conn, deadline: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `ldap.set_deadline(@c, deadline)`: Sets how long each later operation on `c` may take. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bind(@c: Conn, dn: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.bind(@c, dn: dn, password: password)`: Binds `c` as `dn` with `password`: a simple bind (RFC 4513 § 5.1.3). Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function bind_anonymous(@c: Conn) -> ()?`, called `ldap.bind_anonymous(@c)`: Binds `c` anonymously, dropping the identity an earlier bind gave it. Fails with the code of the server's result where it refuses.
- `function bind_unauthenticated(@c: Conn, dn: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.bind_unauthenticated(@c, dn)`: Binds `c` as `dn` with no password: RFC 4513 § 5.1.2's unauthenticated bind, which a server accepts, where it accepts it, as anonymous. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Challenge(finished: bool, credentials: [u8])`: What one step of a SASL bind answered.
- `function bind_sasl(@c: Conn, mechanism: str, credentials: [u8]) -> Challenge?`, called `ldap.bind_sasl(@c, mechanism, credentials)`: One step of a SASL bind of `mechanism`, sending `credentials`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bind_external(@c: Conn, authz_id: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.bind_external(@c, authz_id)`: Binds `c` with SASL EXTERNAL (RFC 4422 Appendix A): the identity the connection already proves to the server. Fails `permission`.
- `function bind_plain(@c: Conn, authz_id: str, user: str, password: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.bind_plain(@c, authz_id: authz_id, user: user, password: password)`: Binds `c` with SASL PLAIN (RFC 4616): a user and a password, optionally acting as another identity. Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function who_am_i(@c: Conn) -> str?`, called `ldap.who_am_i(@c)`: The identity the server sees on `c` (RFC 4532): `dn:` and a name, `u:` and a user name, or "" for anonymous. Fails `not_text`.
- `variant Scope = .base_object | .one_level | .subtree | .children`: How far below its base a search reaches.
- `variant Deref = .never | .in_searching | .finding_base | .always`: When a search follows an alias to the entry it names.
- `record Query(base: str, scope: Scope, filter: Filter, attributes: [str], size_limit: i64, time_limit: time.Duration, types_only: bool, deref: Deref, controls: [Control])`: A search, built by `query` and changed with `@`.
- `function query(base: str, f: Filter) -> Query`, called `ldap.query(base, f)`: A search of the subtree at `base` for the entries `f` matches, every user attribute answered, no limit but the server's, aliases never followed.
- `record Attribute(name: str, values: [[u8]])`: One attribute of an entry: its name and its values.
- `record Entry(dn: str, attributes: [Attribute], controls: [Control])`: An entry a search answered.
- `record Reference(urls: [str])`: A continuation reference: other servers to ask for the rest of a search.
- `record Found(entries: [Entry], references: [Reference], result: Result)`: What a search answered.
- `function search(@c: Conn, q: Query) -> Found?`, called `ldap.search(@c, q)`: The entries `q` finds on `c`, with its references and its result. Fails `limit`, `timeout`, `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function lookup(@c: Conn, dn: str, attributes: [str]) -> Entry?`, called `ldap.lookup(@c, dn, attributes)`: The entry named `dn`, with `attributes`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function root_dse(@c: Conn) -> Entry?`, called `ldap.root_dse(@c)`: The server's root DSE: its naming contexts, versions, controls, extensions and SASL mechanisms, its user and operational attributes. Fails as `lookup` does.
- `variant Item = .entry(v: Entry) | .reference(v: Reference) | .done(v: Result)`: One message of a search read by `next_item`.
- `function start_search(@c: Conn, q: Query) -> ()?`, called `ldap.start_search(@c, q)`: Sends the search `q` on `c` and returns at once: `next_item` reads its answer one message at a time, so a large answer is never held whole. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function next_item(@c: Conn) -> Item?`, called `ldap.next_item(@c)`: The next message of the search running on `c`: an entry, a reference, or its end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function abandon_search(@c: Conn) -> ()?`, called `ldap.abandon_search(@c)`: Gives up the search running on `c` (an AbandonRequest), which the server answers with nothing: entries it had sent already are read past. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `record Page(found: Found, cookie: [u8])`: One page of a paged search.
- `function search_page(@c: Conn, q: Query, size: i64, cookie: [u8]) -> Page?`, called `ldap.search_page(@c, q, size, cookie)`: One page of `q` on `c`: at most `size` entries after the page `cookie` ended (RFC 2696). Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function search_paged(@c: Conn, q: Query, size: i64) -> Found?`, called `ldap.search_paged(@c, q, size)`: Every entry `q` finds on `c`, asked for in pages of `size`, so a server's own size limit does not cut the answer. Fails as `search_page` does.
- `function text_attribute(name: str, values: [str]) -> Attribute`, called `ldap.text_attribute(name, values)`: The attribute `name` with `values`, each written as its UTF-8 bytes.
- `function values_of(e: Entry, name: str) -> [[u8]]`, called `ldap.values_of(e, name)`: The values of the attribute `name` of `e`, as the server sent them.
- `function texts_of(e: Entry, name: str) -> [str]?`, called `ldap.texts_of(e, name)`: The values of the attribute `name` of `e`, as text. Fails `not_text`.
- `function text_of(e: Entry, name: str) -> str?`, called `ldap.text_of(e, name)`: The first value of the attribute `name` of `e`, as text. Fails `not_found`, `not_text`.
- `function has_attribute(e: Entry, name: str) -> bool`, called `ldap.has_attribute(e, name)`: Whether `e` has the attribute `name`.
- `function add(@c: Conn, dn: str, attributes: [Attribute]) -> ()?`, called `ldap.add(@c, dn, attributes)`: Adds the entry `dn` with `attributes`. Fails `invalid`, `exists`, `not_found`, `permission`.
- `variant ChangeKind = .add | .delete | .replace | .increment`: What a change does to an attribute (RFC 4511 § 4.6, RFC 4525).
- `record Change(kind: ChangeKind, attribute: Attribute)`: One change of a `modify`.
- `function modify(@c: Conn, dn: str, changes: [Change]) -> ()?`, called `ldap.modify(@c, dn, changes)`: Changes the attributes of the entry `dn`, every change or none. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `exists`, `permission`.
- `function delete(@c: Conn, dn: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.delete(@c, dn)`: Deletes the entry `dn`, which has no entry below it. Fails `not_found`, `not_empty`, `permission`.
- `function rename(@c: Conn, dn: str, new_rdn: str, delete_old: bool, new_parent: str) -> ()?`, called `ldap.rename(@c, dn: dn, new_rdn: new_rdn, delete_old, new_parent: new_parent)`: Renames the entry `dn` to `new_rdn`, and moves it below `new_parent` (ModifyDN). Fails `not_found`, `exists`, `not_empty`, `permission`.
- `function compare(@c: Conn, dn: str, attribute: str, value: [u8]) -> bool?`, called `ldap.compare(@c, dn: dn, attribute: attribute, value)`: Whether the entry `dn`'s attribute `attribute` holds `value`, as the attribute's equality rule compares it on the server. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function change_password(@c: Conn, user: str, old: str, new: str) -> str?`, called `ldap.change_password(@c, user: user, old: old, new: new)`: Changes the password of `user` from `old` to `new` (RFC 3062), and answers the password the server made where `new` is "". Fails `permission`, `not_text`.
- `record Extended(name: str, value: [u8])`: What an extended operation answered.
- `function extended(@c: Conn, name: str, value: [u8]) -> Extended?`, called `ldap.extended(@c, name, value)`: Runs the extended operation `name` with `value` (RFC 4511 § 4.12). Fails `invalid`.
- `record Ava(attribute: str, value: str)`: One attribute and value of a relative distinguished name: `cn=Ana`.
- `record Rdn(parts: [Ava])`: A relative distinguished name: one attribute and value, or several joined by `+`.
- `record Dn(rdns: [Rdn])`: A distinguished name (RFC 4514): relative names from the entry up to the root, as written left to right.
- `function parse_dn(s: str) -> Dn?`, called `ldap.parse_dn(s)`: The distinguished name `s` writes (RFC 4514). Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function format_dn(dn: Dn) -> str`, called `ldap.format_dn(dn)`: `dn` written in RFC 4514's form: `cn=Ana Rossi,ou=people,dc=example,dc=org`.
- `function parse_rdn(s: str) -> Rdn?`, called `ldap.parse_rdn(s)`: The relative distinguished name `s` writes: `cn=Ana+sn=Rossi`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_rdn(rdn: Rdn) -> str`, called `ldap.format_rdn(rdn)`: `rdn` written in RFC 4514's form.
- `function escape_dn_value(s: str) -> str`, called `ldap.escape_dn_value(s)`: `s` escaped to stand as a value of a distinguished name (RFC 4514 § 2.4).
- `function unescape_dn_value(s: str) -> str?`, called `ldap.unescape_dn_value(s)`: The value an escaped value of a distinguished name holds. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function is_same_dn(a: Dn, b: Dn) -> bool`, called `ldap.is_same_dn(a: a, b: b)`: Whether `a` and `b` name the same entry: attribute names compared with ASCII case ignored, values byte for byte, the parts of a relative name in any order.
- `function is_same_dn_ignoring_case(a: Dn, b: Dn) -> bool`, called `ldap.is_same_dn_ignoring_case(a: a, b: b)`: Whether `a` and `b` name the same entry, the values compared with case ignored as `strings.equals_ignoring_case` compares them, as most directory attributes compare.
- `function is_under(dn: Dn, ancestor: Dn) -> bool`, called `ldap.is_under(dn: dn, ancestor: ancestor)`: Whether `dn` stands below `ancestor`, at any depth, as `is_same_dn` compares names.
- `function parent_of(dn: Dn) -> Dn?`, called `ldap.parent_of(dn)`: The name of the entry right above `dn`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function child_of(parent: Dn, rdn: Rdn) -> Dn`, called `ldap.child_of(parent, rdn)`: The name of the entry `rdn` right below `parent`.
- `variant Filter = .and_of(items: [Filter]) | .or_of(items: [Filter]) | .not_of(items: [Filter]) | .equal(attribute: str, value: [u8]) | .substrings(attribute: str, initial: [u8], middle: [[u8]], final: [u8]) | .greater_or_equal(attribute: str, value: [u8]) | .less_or_equal(attribute: str, value: [u8]) | .present(attribute: str) | .approx(attribute: str, value: [u8]) | .extensible(rule: str, attribute: str, value: [u8], dn_attributes: bool)`: A search filter (RFC 4511 § 4.5.1, RFC 4515).
- `constant MAX_FILTER_DEPTH: i64`, value `100`: The deepest a filter nests: `and_of`, `or_of` and `not_of` inside each other 100 deep, read and written with a stack of their own.
- `function parse_filter(s: str) -> Filter?`, called `ldap.parse_filter(s)`: The filter `s` writes (RFC 4515). Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_filter(f: Filter) -> str?`, called `ldap.format_filter(f)`: `f` written as RFC 4515's text: a value that is UTF-8 kept as text, its `*`, `(`, `)`, `\` and control bytes escaped as `escape_filter` does, and a value that is not UTF-8 escaped byte by byte as `escape_filter_bytes` does. Fails `invalid`.
- `function escape_filter(s: str) -> str`, called `ldap.escape_filter(s)`: `s` escaped to stand as a value in a filter's text: `\2a` for `*`, `\28` and `\29` for the parentheses, `\5c` for `\`, `\00` for a zero byte and the same form for every control byte; characters past ASCII stay as they are, as Python's `escape_filter_chars` leaves them.
- `function escape_filter_bytes(b: [u8]) -> str`, called `ldap.escape_filter_bytes(b)`: `b` escaped to stand as a value in a filter's text, every byte that is not printable ASCII written as `\` and two hexadecimal digits: the form of a binary value, an `objectGUID`.
- `function unescape_filter(s: str) -> [u8]?`, called `ldap.unescape_filter(s)`: The bytes an escaped value of a filter's text holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_filter(f: Filter) -> [u8]?`, called `ldap.encode_filter(f)`: `f` encoded as BER, as a SearchRequest carries it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_filter(data: [u8]) -> Filter?`, called `ldap.decode_filter(data)`: The filter whose BER is `data`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Url(scheme: str, host: str, port: i64, dn: str, attributes: [str], scope: Scope, filter: Filter, extensions: [str])`: An LDAP URL (RFC 4516): a server, and a search on it.
- `function parse_url(s: str) -> Url?`, called `ldap.parse_url(s)`: The LDAP URL `s` (RFC 4516). Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_url(u: Url) -> str?`, called `ldap.format_url(u)`: `u` written as an LDAP URL, every part escaped as RFC 4516 asks. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_options(u: Url) -> Options`, called `ldap.to_options(u)`: The options of a connection to the server `u` names: `.start_tls` for `ldap`, `.direct` for `ldaps`, the system's authorities trusted, the default deadline and bound of a message.
- `function to_query(u: Url) -> Query`, called `ldap.to_query(u)`: The search `u` names: its base, attributes, scope and filter.
- `constant SUCCESS: i64`, value `0`: The operation succeeded.
- `constant OPERATIONS_ERROR: i64`, value `1`: The operation could not be done in the right order (operationsError).
- `constant PROTOCOL_ERROR: i64`, value `2`: The server could not read the request (protocolError).
- `constant TIME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: i64`, value `3`: The search's time limit passed (timeLimitExceeded).
- `constant SIZE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: i64`, value `4`: The search's size limit was reached (sizeLimitExceeded).
- `constant COMPARE_FALSE: i64`, value `5`: A compare found the value absent (compareFalse).
- `constant COMPARE_TRUE: i64`, value `6`: A compare found the value present (compareTrue).
- `constant AUTH_METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED: i64`, value `7`: The server knows no such authentication method (authMethodNotSupported).
- `constant STRONGER_AUTH_REQUIRED: i64`, value `8`: The server asks for a stronger authentication (strongerAuthRequired).
- `constant REFERRAL: i64`, value `10`: Another server holds the entry, which the result's referrals name (referral).
- `constant ADMIN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: i64`, value `11`: A limit the administrator set was passed (adminLimitExceeded).
- `constant UNAVAILABLE_CRITICAL_EXTENSION: i64`, value `12`: A control marked critical is unknown to the server (unavailableCriticalExtension).
- `constant CONFIDENTIALITY_REQUIRED: i64`, value `13`: The server asks for TLS first (confidentialityRequired).
- `constant SASL_BIND_IN_PROGRESS: i64`, value `14`: A SASL bind goes on: the server sent a challenge (saslBindInProgress).
- `constant NO_SUCH_ATTRIBUTE: i64`, value `16`: The entry has no such attribute or value (noSuchAttribute).
- `constant UNDEFINED_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE: i64`, value `17`: The attribute type is not in the schema (undefinedAttributeType).
- `constant INAPPROPRIATE_MATCHING: i64`, value `18`: The attribute has no such matching rule (inappropriateMatching).
- `constant CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION: i64`, value `19`: A value breaks a constraint of the schema (constraintViolation).
- `constant ATTRIBUTE_OR_VALUE_EXISTS: i64`, value `20`: The value is there already (attributeOrValueExists).
- `constant INVALID_ATTRIBUTE_SYNTAX: i64`, value `21`: A value is not of its attribute's syntax (invalidAttributeSyntax).
- `constant NO_SUCH_OBJECT: i64`, value `32`: No entry has the name (noSuchObject).
- `constant ALIAS_PROBLEM: i64`, value `33`: An alias names no entry (aliasProblem).
- `constant INVALID_DN_SYNTAX: i64`, value `34`: A name is not a distinguished name (invalidDNSyntax).
- `constant ALIAS_DEREFERENCING_PROBLEM: i64`, value `36`: An alias could not be followed (aliasDereferencingProblem).
- `constant INAPPROPRIATE_AUTHENTICATION: i64`, value `48`: The authentication fits nothing the entry holds (inappropriateAuthentication).
- `constant INVALID_CREDENTIALS: i64`, value `49`: The name or the password is wrong (invalidCredentials).
- `constant INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS_RIGHTS: i64`, value `50`: The identity has no right to do this (insufficientAccessRights).
- `constant BUSY: i64`, value `51`: The server is too busy (busy).
- `constant UNAVAILABLE: i64`, value `52`: The server is shutting down or cannot serve (unavailable).
- `constant UNWILLING_TO_PERFORM: i64`, value `53`: The server will not do this (unwillingToPerform).
- `constant LOOP_DETECT: i64`, value `54`: A loop was found following aliases or referrals (loopDetect).
- `constant NAMING_VIOLATION: i64`, value `64`: The name breaks the directory's naming rules (namingViolation).
- `constant OBJECT_CLASS_VIOLATION: i64`, value `65`: The entry breaks its object classes' rules (objectClassViolation).
- `constant NOT_ALLOWED_ON_NON_LEAF: i64`, value `66`: The entry has entries below it (notAllowedOnNonLeaf).
- `constant NOT_ALLOWED_ON_RDN: i64`, value `67`: The change would remove a value of the entry's name (notAllowedOnRDN).
- `constant ENTRY_ALREADY_EXISTS: i64`, value `68`: An entry has the name already (entryAlreadyExists).
- `constant OBJECT_CLASS_MODS_PROHIBITED: i64`, value `69`: The entry's structural object class may not change (objectClassModsProhibited).
- `constant AFFECTS_MULTIPLE_DSAS: i64`, value `71`: The change would reach more than one server (affectsMultipleDSAs).
- `constant OTHER: i64`, value `80`: A failure no other code names (other).
- `constant CANCELED: i64`, value `118`: The operation was cancelled (canceled, RFC 3909).
- `constant NO_SUCH_OPERATION: i64`, value `119`: The operation to cancel is unknown (noSuchOperation, RFC 3909).
- `constant TOO_LATE: i64`, value `120`: The operation to cancel is too far along (tooLate, RFC 3909).
- `constant CANNOT_CANCEL: i64`, value `121`: The operation cannot be cancelled (cannotCancel, RFC 3909).
- `constant ASSERTION_FAILED: i64`, value `122`: The assertion control's filter does not hold (assertionFailed, RFC 4528).
- `constant AUTHORIZATION_DENIED: i64`, value `123`: The proxied identity is refused (authorizationDenied, RFC 4370).
- `function result_name(code: i64) -> str`, called `ldap.result_name(code)`: The name RFC 4511 and its extensions give `code`: `noSuchObject` for 32, `success` for 0.


### config

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/config`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/config/).

Settings read in layers: defaults, files in TOML, YAML, JSON, INI or Java's properties, `.env` files, the environment and the command line, each a `Layer` holding an object of `json.Value`, merged by `merge` in the order the program lists them, each over the ones before it, into `Settings` read by dotted path with typed getters.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text that is not of its format, of a path that is not one, of a setting that is not of the kind a getter reads, and of settings a program does not know: every function that reads a text or a setting.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a path that names no setting, `value_of` and every getter, and of a file in none of the folders searched, `find_file` and `find_upward`.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: The code of a number past what its type holds: an integer past an `i64`, or past `json.MAX_EXACT_INT` where it must be a `json.Value`.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of a variable of the process's environment whose name or value is not UTF-8: `read_env`.
- `record Layer(name: str, value: json.Value, origins: {str: str}, file: str)`: One source of settings: the name messages give it, its settings as an object, and the name each value had inside the source.
- `function from_value(name: str, value: json.Value) -> Layer?`, called `config.from_value(name, value)`: A layer named `name` holding `value`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_value(@layer: Layer, path: str, value: json.Value) -> ()?`, called `config.set_value(@layer, path, value)`: Sets the setting `path` of `layer` to `value`, the objects on the way made where they are not there. Fails `invalid`.
- `function layer_at(layer: Layer, path: str) -> Layer?`, called `config.layer_at(layer, path)`: The object at `path` in `layer`, as a layer of its own: one table of a file, or one profile among several. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `variant Format = .json | .toml | .yaml | .ini | .properties`: A format a settings file is written in.
- `function format_of(path: str) -> Format?`, called `config.format_of(path)`: The format the extension of `path` names: `.json`, `.toml`, `.yaml` or `.yml`, `.ini`, and `.properties`, in any case. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_layer(name: str, text: str, format: Format) -> Layer?`, called `config.parse_layer(name: name, text: text, format)`: The settings `text` holds in `format`, as a layer named `name`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function read_layer(path: str) -> Layer?`, called `config.read_layer(path)`: The settings of the file at `path`, its format read from its extension, as a layer named `path` and read from it. Fails `file_not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function read_layer_if_present(path: str) -> Layer?`, called `config.read_layer_if_present(path)`: The settings of the file at `path` as `read_layer` reads them, or no settings where the file is not there. Fails `file_not_found`.
- `function find_file(base: str, dirs: [str]) -> str?`, called `config.find_file(base, dirs)`: The path of the first settings file named `base` in the first of `dirs` that holds one, whatever its format. Fails `not_found`.
- `function find_upward(name: str, dir: str) -> str?`, called `config.find_upward(name: name, dir: dir)`: The path of the file `name` in the folder `dir` or in the nearest folder above it that holds one, as `.env` and `pyproject.toml` are looked for. Fails `not_found`.
- `function bind_files(name: str, dir: str, names: {str: str}) -> Layer?`, called `config.bind_files(name: name, dir: dir, names)`: The settings named in `names` read from the files of the folder `dir`, a file a setting, as Docker and Kubernetes give secrets, as a layer named `name`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record EnvOptions(prefix: str, separator: str, lower_keys: bool, ignore_empty: bool, json_values: bool)`: How the variables of an environment are read into a layer.
- `function env_options(prefix: str) -> EnvOptions`, called `config.env_options(prefix)`: The options that read the variables beginning with `prefix`, nested at `__` and keyed in lower case, an empty value and a value of JSON read as text.
- `function from_env(name: str, env: {str: str}, options: EnvOptions) -> Layer?`, called `config.from_env(name, env, options)`: The variables of `env` read as `options` say, as a layer named `name`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function read_env(options: EnvOptions) -> Layer?`, called `config.read_env(options)`: The process's own environment read as `options` say, as a layer named `environment`. Fails `not_text`.
- `function bind_env(name: str, env: {str: str}, names: {str: str}) -> Layer?`, called `config.bind_env(name, env: env, names: names)`: The settings named in `names` read from the variables they name, as a layer named `name`. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant FlagKind = .flag | .count | .text | .integer | .float | .texts`: How an argument's value is read into a setting.
- `record FlagBinding(path: str, name: str, kind: FlagKind)`: One setting read from one argument of the command line.
- `function from_flags(name: str, found: flags.Found, bindings: [FlagBinding]) -> Layer?`, called `config.from_flags(name, found, bindings)`: The settings `bindings` read from the arguments a parse found given, on the command line or in their environment variable, as a layer named `name`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function from_flag_defaults(name: str, found: flags.Found, bindings: [FlagBinding]) -> Layer?`, called `config.from_flag_defaults(name, found, bindings)`: The settings `bindings` read from the defaults of the arguments a parse found not given, as a layer named `name`, which a program lists below the others. Fails and aborts as `from_flags` does.
- `record Settings(held: held.Held)`: Settings merged from layers, read by the functions below.
- `function merge(layers: [Layer]) -> Settings`, called `config.merge(layers)`: The settings of `layers`, each over the ones before it.
- `function value_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> json.Value?`, called `config.value_of(s, path)`: The value `path` names in `s`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function has_path(s: Settings, path: str) -> bool`, called `config.has_path(s, path)`: Whether `path` names a value in `s`.
- `function text_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> str?`, called `config.text_of(s, path)`: The text at `path`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function int_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> i64?`, called `config.int_of(s, path)`: The integer at `path`, from a number with no fraction or from a text that spells one in decimal. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function float_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> f64?`, called `config.float_of(s, path)`: The number at `path`, from a number or from a text that spells one in decimal, `nan` and `inf` included. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bool_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> bool?`, called `config.bool_of(s, path)`: The boolean at `path`, from a boolean, from the number 0 or 1, or from a word: `true`, `yes`, `on`, `y`, `t` and `1` are true, `false`, `no`, `off`, `n`, `f` and `0` false, in any case. Fails `invalid`.
- `function duration_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> time.Duration?`, called `config.duration_of(s, path)`: The duration at `path`, from a text `time.parse_duration` reads: `30s`, `1h30m`, `250ms`. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function instant_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `config.instant_of(s, path)`: The instant at `path`, from an RFC 3339 text with an offset: `1979-05-27T07:32:00-07:00`, as TOML's dates are given. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function path_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> str?`, called `config.path_of(s, path)`: The path at `path`: a text, read from the folder of the file whose layer set it where it is relative. Fails as `text_of` does.
- `function items_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> [json.Value]?`, called `config.items_of(s, path)`: The elements of the list at `path`, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function texts_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> [str]?`, called `config.texts_of(s, path)`: The texts of the list at `path`, in order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function keys_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> [str]?`, called `config.keys_of(s, path)`: The keys of the object at `path`, in the order they were first given. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sub(s: Settings, path: str) -> Settings?`, called `config.sub(s, path)`: The settings under `path`, read from their own top: `sub(s, "db")` reads `db.host` as `host`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function settings_json(s: Settings) -> json.Value`, called `config.settings_json(s)`: Every setting of `s` as one object.
- `function paths_of(s: Settings) -> [str]`, called `config.paths_of(s)`: The path of every setting of `s` that holds no other: each value that is not an object, and each empty object, in the order of the tree.
- `record Source(layer: str, origin: str, file: str)`: Where a setting came from.
- `function source_of(s: Settings, path: str) -> Source?`, called `config.source_of(s, path)`: Where the value at `path` came from: the last layer that set it, or, for an object several layers gave keys to, the last that gave one. Fails as `value_of` does.
- `function format_sources(s: Settings) -> str`, called `config.format_sources(s)`: Every setting of `s`, a line each in the order of `paths_of`: its path, `=`, its value as JSON, and the layer and the origin that gave it.
- `function require(s: Settings, paths: [str]) -> ()?`, called `config.require(s, paths)`: Checks that every path of `paths` names a value in `s`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function check_known(s: Settings, paths: [str]) -> ()?`, called `config.check_known(s, paths)`: Checks that every setting of `s` stands at one of `paths` or under one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_settings(s: Settings, format: Format) -> str?`, called `config.format_settings(s, format)`: Every setting of `s` written in `format`, ending with a line break. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record DotenvOptions(expand: bool, env: {str: str})`: How a `.env` text is read.
- `function parse_dotenv(text: str) -> {str: str}?`, called `config.parse_dotenv(text)`: The names and values of the `.env` text `text`, nothing replaced. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_dotenv_with(text: str, options: DotenvOptions) -> {str: str}?`, called `config.parse_dotenv_with(text, options)`: The names and values of the `.env` text `text`, read as `options` say. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_dotenv(path: str) -> {str: str}?`, called `config.read_dotenv(path)`: The names and values of the `.env` file at `path`, as `parse_dotenv` reads them: no `${NAME}` replaced. Fails where `read_file` fails, with its code, and as `parse_dotenv` does, the message opening with `path`.
- `function read_dotenv_with(path: str, options: DotenvOptions) -> {str: str}?`, called `config.read_dotenv_with(path, options)`: The names and values of the `.env` file at `path`, read as `options` say. Fails where `read_file` fails, with its code, and as `parse_dotenv_with` does, the message opening with `path`.
- `function format_dotenv(values: {str: str}) -> str?`, called `config.format_dotenv(values)`: `values` written as a `.env` text, a line `NAME="value"` each, in the map's order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_dotenv_value(text: str, name: str, value: str) -> str?`, called `config.set_dotenv_value(text: text, name: name, value: value)`: `text` with `name` set to `value`: its line rewritten in place where it stands, else a line added at the end; every other line and comment kept. Fails as `parse_dotenv` does on `text`, and as `format_dotenv` does on `name`.
- `function remove_dotenv_value(text: str, name: str) -> str?`, called `config.remove_dotenv_value(text: text, name: name)`: `text` without the lines that set `name`, every other line and comment kept. Fails `not_found`.


### amqp

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/amqp`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/amqp/).

An AMQP 0-9-1 client written in Heroes, as RabbitMQ speaks it, over a TCP connection of `net` or TLS of `tls`, linking no library.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument refused, bytes from the server that are no AMQP, or a precondition the server refused (its 406, 402 and 5xx codes): every function.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A queue, an exchange or a consumer the server does not know (its 404), a mandatory message no queue took (`next_return`), a queue empty (`get`), or nothing held (`next_return`, `next_confirmation`).
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: A login, a virtual host or a resource refused (its 403 and 530): `connect` and every function that touches a resource.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection or the channel is closed, by the program or the server: every function that talks to the server.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The time a call allowed ran out: every function that waits.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while the call waited (`os.ask_stop`).
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A frame, a body or the values held past a bound, or a body the server finds too large (its 311).
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: What the server or the platform does not offer: another protocol's version, a login mechanism the server does not take.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: A failure none of the above names, the server's reply code and text in the message: a resource locked (405), a publish the server refused (`wait_confirms`).
- `record Message(content_type: str, content_encoding: str, headers: [Field], delivery_mode: i64, priority: i64, correlation_id: str, reply_to: str, expiration: str, message_id: str, timestamp: i64, message_type: str, user_id: str, app_id: str, body: [u8])`: A message as it is published and delivered: its properties and its body.
- `record Delivery(channel: Channel, consumer_tag: str, tag: i64, redelivered: bool, exchange: str, routing_key: str, remaining: i64, message: Message)`: A message the server delivered to a consumer or answered to `get`.
- `record Return(channel: Channel, code: i64, text: str, exchange: str, routing_key: str, message: Message)`: A mandatory message no queue took, which the server handed back.
- `record Confirmation(channel: Channel, tag: i64, ack: bool)`: The server's answer to a publish on a channel in confirm mode.
- `record Cancellation(channel: Channel, consumer_tag: str)`: A consumer the server cancelled, as where its queue was deleted.
- `variant Mechanism = .plain | .amqplain`: How the login is sent.
- `variant Security = .plain | .checked(roots: str)`: How a connection is protected.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, security: Security, vhost: str, username: str, password: str, mechanism: Mechanism, heartbeat: time.Duration, frame_max: i64, channel_max: i64, connection_name: str, properties: [Field], locale: str, connect_timeout: time.Duration, wait: time.Duration, most_body_bytes: i64, most_held: i64)`: Where the server is and how to talk to it.
- `record Server(properties: [Field], mechanisms: [str], locales: [str], version_major: i64, version_minor: i64, channel_max: i64, frame_max: i64, heartbeat: time.Duration)`: What the server said of itself and agreed when the connection was made.
- `record Closing(code: i64, text: str, class_id: i64, method_id: i64)`: Why the server closed a connection or a channel.
- `record Blocked(active: bool, reason: str)`: Whether the server holds the connection's publishes back, as RabbitMQ does when its memory or disk runs short.
- `record Connection(session: state.Session)`: A connection to an AMQP server, which `connect` makes and `close` ends.
- `record Channel(id: i64)`: A channel of a connection, which `open_channel` makes and `close_channel` ends; a channel the server closes stays closed.
- `function options(host: str) -> Options`, called `amqp.options(host)`: The options of a connection to `host` at `DEFAULT_PORT`: the virtual host `/`, the user `guest` with the password `guest` over PLAIN, a heartbeat of 60 seconds, frames of 131,072 bytes, 2,047 channels, the locale `en_US`, 10 seconds to connect and for each answer, bodies of 128 MiB at most, and 65,536 values held unread.
- `function parse_url(text: str) -> Options?`, called `amqp.parse_url(text)`: The options a URL names, as RabbitMQ writes one: `amqp://user:password@host:5672/vhost?heartbeat=10`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Connection?`, called `amqp.connect(opts)`: A connection to the server `opts` names, its handshake done: the protocol's header sent, the login taken, the heartbeat, frame size and channels agreed, the virtual host opened. Fails `permission`, `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function close(@c: Connection) -> ()?`, called `amqp.close(@c)`: Closes the connection with `connection.close` and its answer, which ends every channel; every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
