- `function is_closed(c: Connection) -> bool`, called `amqp.is_closed(c)`: Whether the connection is closed, by the program, the server or a loss.
- `function closing_of(c: Connection) -> Closing?`, called `amqp.closing_of(c)`: Why the server closed the connection. Fails `not_found`.
- `function server_of(c: Connection) -> Server`, called `amqp.server_of(c)`: What the server said of itself and agreed.
- `function blocked_of(c: Connection) -> Blocked`, called `amqp.blocked_of(c)`: Whether the server holds the connection's publishes back now, and why.
- `function update_secret(@c: Connection, secret: str, reason: str) -> ()?`, called `amqp.update_secret(@c, secret: secret, reason: reason)`: Replaces the secret the connection logged in with, as an OAuth 2 token that expires asks (`connection.update-secret`). Fails `permission`.
- `function idle(@c: Connection, wait: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `amqp.idle(@c, wait)`: Waits `wait` doing nothing but what the connection needs: the heartbeat sent and read, and what the server sends held. Fails `closed`, `stopped`, `invalid`.
- `function stream_of(c: Connection) -> io.Stream?`, called `amqp.stream_of(c)`: The stream under the connection, for a program that waits on it with `poll`; only this package reads and writes it. Fails `closed`.
- `function read_ready(@c: Connection) -> ()?`, called `amqp.read_ready(@c)`: Reads what the stream holds now, without waiting longer, and holds what it brings; for a program `poll` has told the stream is readable. Fails `closed`.
- `function held_of(c: Connection) -> i64`, called `amqp.held_of(c)`: The values held unread: deliveries, returned messages and confirmations; every whole frame a call read, while it waited for something else or in the read that brought its own answer, is acted on before the call returns, so what it holds is counted here.
- `function open_channel(@c: Connection) -> Channel?`, called `amqp.open_channel(@c)`: A new channel of the connection, the lowest number free. Fails `limit`.
- `function close_channel(@c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `amqp.close_channel(@c, channel)`: Closes `channel` with `channel.close` and its answer; its consumers end and the messages it was delivered and did not acknowledge go back to their queues. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_channel_open(c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> bool`, called `amqp.is_channel_open(c, channel)`: Whether `channel` is open.
- `function channel_closing_of(c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> Closing?`, called `amqp.channel_closing_of(c, channel)`: Why the server closed `channel`, as it does where a call on it fails: a queue not found, a declaration that disagrees, an acknowledgement unknown. Fails `not_found`.
- `function qos(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, prefetch_count: i64, prefetch_size: i64, global: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.qos(@c, channel, prefetch_count: prefetch_count, prefetch_size: prefetch_size, global)`: Sets how much the server sends `channel`'s consumers before they acknowledge (`basic.qos`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function flow(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, active: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.flow(@c, channel, active)`: Asks the server to stop or go on sending to `channel` (`channel.flow`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Exchange(name: str, kind: str, durable: bool, auto_delete: bool, internal: bool, passive: bool, arguments: [Field])`: An exchange to declare.
- `record Queue(name: str, durable: bool, exclusive: bool, auto_delete: bool, passive: bool, arguments: [Field])`: A queue to declare.
- `record Declared(name: str, messages: i64, consumers: i64)`: What the server answered a queue's declaration.
- `record Consumer(queue_name: str, tag: str, auto_ack: bool, exclusive: bool, no_local: bool, arguments: [Field])`: A consumer to start.
- `function exchange(name: str, kind: str) -> Exchange`, called `amqp.exchange(name: name, kind: kind)`: An exchange named `name` of the kind `kind`, not durable, not deleted with its last binding, not internal, declared and not only asked about, with no argument.
- `function declare_exchange(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, e: Exchange) -> ()?`, called `amqp.declare_exchange(@c, channel, e)`: Declares the exchange `e`, made where it does not exist. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function delete_exchange(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, name: str, if_unused: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.delete_exchange(@c, channel, name, if_unused)`: Deletes the exchange `name`. Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function bind_exchange(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, destination: str, source: str, routing_key: str, arguments: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `amqp.bind_exchange(@c, channel, destination: destination, source: source, routing_key: routing_key, arguments)`: Binds the exchange `destination` to the exchange `source`, so `source` routes to it what the key matches, as a queue's binding does (RabbitMQ's extension). Fails `not_found`.
- `function unbind_exchange(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, destination: str, source: str, routing_key: str, arguments: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `amqp.unbind_exchange(@c, channel, destination: destination, source: source, routing_key: routing_key, arguments)`: Takes back a binding `bind_exchange` made. Fails as `bind_exchange` does.
- `function queue(name: str) -> Queue`, called `amqp.queue(name)`: A queue named `name`, "" for one the server names, not durable, not exclusive, not deleted with its last consumer, declared and not only asked about, with no argument.
- `function declare_queue(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, q: Queue) -> Declared?`, called `amqp.declare_queue(@c, channel, q)`: Declares the queue `q`, made where it does not exist, and answers its name and counts. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `failed`, `permission`.
- `function bind_queue(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, queue_name: str, exchange_name: str, routing_key: str, arguments: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `amqp.bind_queue(@c, channel, queue_name: queue_name, exchange_name: exchange_name, routing_key: routing_key, arguments)`: Binds the queue `queue_name` to the exchange `exchange_name`, so the exchange routes to it what the key matches. Fails `not_found`.
- `function unbind_queue(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, queue_name: str, exchange_name: str, routing_key: str, arguments: [Field]) -> ()?`, called `amqp.unbind_queue(@c, channel, queue_name: queue_name, exchange_name: exchange_name, routing_key: routing_key, arguments)`: Takes back a binding `bind_queue` made. Fails as `bind_queue` does.
- `function purge_queue(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, name: str) -> i64?`, called `amqp.purge_queue(@c, channel, name)`: Removes every message ready in the queue `name`, and answers how many. Fails `not_found`.
- `function delete_queue(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, name: str, if_unused: bool, if_empty: bool) -> i64?`, called `amqp.delete_queue(@c, channel, name, if_unused: if_unused, if_empty: if_empty)`: Deletes the queue `name`, and answers how many messages it held. Fails `invalid`.
- `function message(body: [u8]) -> Message`, called `amqp.message(body)`: A message holding `body` and no property.
- `function publish(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, exchange_name: str, routing_key: str, m: Message, mandatory: bool) -> i64?`, called `amqp.publish(@c, channel, exchange_name: exchange_name, routing_key: routing_key, m, mandatory)`: Publishes `m` to the exchange `exchange_name` with the routing key `routing_key`, and answers its sequence number where `channel` is in confirm mode, 0 elsewhere. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function select_confirms(@c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `amqp.select_confirms(@c, channel)`: Puts `channel` in confirm mode (`confirm.select`): the server then confirms or refuses every publish, numbered from 1. Fails `invalid`.
- `function next_confirmation(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, wait: time.Duration) -> Confirmation?`, called `amqp.next_confirmation(@c, channel, wait)`: The next confirmation of a publish on `channel`, waiting for one; a confirmation of several publishes at once is answered one publish at a time, in order. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function wait_confirms(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, wait: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `amqp.wait_confirms(@c, channel, wait)`: Waits until the server has confirmed or refused every publish of `channel` so far, and forgets the confirmations held. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function next_return(@c: Connection, wait: time.Duration) -> Return?`, called `amqp.next_return(@c, wait)`: The next mandatory message the server handed back, waiting for one. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function consumer(queue_name: str) -> Consumer`, called `amqp.consumer(queue_name)`: A consumer of the queue `queue_name`, named by the server, acknowledging by the program's own `ack`, not exclusive, with no argument.
- `function consume(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, k: Consumer) -> str?`, called `amqp.consume(@c, channel, k)`: Starts the consumer `k` on `channel`, and answers its tag; its messages come by `next_delivery`. Fails `not_found`, `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function cancel(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, tag: str) -> ()?`, called `amqp.cancel(@c, channel, tag)`: Ends the consumer `tag` of `channel`; the messages delivered before stay to be acknowledged. Fails as every call that waits fails; a tag unknown is ended without failing.
- `function next_delivery(@c: Connection, wait: time.Duration) -> Delivery?`, called `amqp.next_delivery(@c, wait)`: The next message delivered to any consumer of the connection, waiting for one; those held come first, in the order they came. Fails `timeout`, `closed`, `stopped`, `invalid`.
- `function get(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, queue_name: str, auto_ack: bool) -> Delivery?`, called `amqp.get(@c, channel, queue_name, auto_ack)`: Takes one message from the queue `queue_name` (`basic.get`). Fails `not_found`.
- `function ack(@c: Connection, d: Delivery lent, multiple: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.ack(@c, d, multiple)`: Acknowledges `d`: the server forgets it. Fails `closed`.
- `function nack(@c: Connection, d: Delivery lent, multiple: bool, requeue: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.nack(@c, d, multiple: multiple, requeue: requeue)`: Refuses `d` (`basic.nack`, RabbitMQ's extension). Fails as `ack` does.
- `function reject(@c: Connection, d: Delivery lent, requeue: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.reject(@c, d, requeue)`: Refuses `d` alone (`basic.reject`). Fails as `ack` does.
- `function recover(@c: Connection, channel: Channel, requeue: bool) -> ()?`, called `amqp.recover(@c, channel, requeue)`: Asks the server to send `channel` again every message delivered and not acknowledged (`basic.recover`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function cancellations_of(c: Connection) -> [Cancellation]`, called `amqp.cancellations_of(c)`: The consumers the server cancelled since the connection was made, in the order it cancelled them: a queue deleted ends its consumers.
- `function select_transactions(@c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `amqp.select_transactions(@c, channel)`: Makes `channel` transactional (`tx.select`): its publishes and acknowledgements take effect at `commit`, or never at `rollback`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function commit(@c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `amqp.commit(@c, channel)`: Commits the transaction of `channel`; the next begins at once. Fails `invalid`.
- `function rollback(@c: Connection, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `amqp.rollback(@c, channel)`: Takes back the transaction of `channel`; the next begins at once. Fails as `commit` does.
- `variant Value = .boolean(v: bool) | .int8(v: i8) | .uint8(v: u8) | .int16(v: i16) | .uint16(v: u16) | .int32(v: i32) | .uint32(v: u32) | .int64(v: i64) | .float32(v: f32) | .float64(v: f64) | .decimal(scale: u8, digits: i32) | .text(v: str) | .binary(v: [u8]) | .timestamp(seconds: i64) | .array(items: [Value]) | .table(fields: [Field]) | .void`: One value of a field table, by the types RabbitMQ reads and writes: AMQP carries arguments, headers and properties in such tables.
- `record Field(name: str, value: Value)`: One named value of a field table.
- `function value_of(fields: [Field], name: str) -> Value?`, called `amqp.value_of(fields, name)`: The value of the field `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function encode_table(fields: [Field]) -> [u8]?`, called `amqp.encode_table(fields)`: The bytes AMQP writes for the table `fields`: its length in four bytes, then each field's name and typed value. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_table(data: [u8]) -> [Field]?`, called `amqp.decode_table(data)`: The table `data` holds, as `encode_table` writes it; `U` and `L`, the standard's own letters for 16-bit and 64-bit integers, are read too. Fails `invalid`.
- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `5672`: The port an AMQP server listens on unless told another.
- `constant DEFAULT_TLS_PORT: i64`, value `5671`: The port an AMQP server listens on for TLS unless told another.
- `constant DIRECT: str`, value `"direct"`: An exchange that routes a message to the queues bound with its routing key exactly.
- `constant FANOUT: str`, value `"fanout"`: An exchange that routes a message to every queue bound to it.
- `constant TOPIC: str`, value `"topic"`: An exchange that routes a message to the queues whose binding's pattern its routing key matches: words separated by `.`, `*` one word, `#` any.
- `constant HEADERS: str`, value `"headers"`: An exchange that routes a message by its headers, the binding's `x-match` saying `all` or `any`.
- `constant TRANSIENT: i64`, value `1`: A message the server keeps in memory only.
- `constant PERSISTENT: i64`, value `2`: A message the server writes to disk where its queue is durable.
- `constant REPLY_SUCCESS: i64`, value `200`: A connection or a channel closed at the program's own asking.
- `constant REPLY_CONTENT_TOO_LARGE: i64`, value `311`: A body too large for the server.
- `constant REPLY_NO_ROUTE: i64`, value `312`: A mandatory message no queue took.
- `constant REPLY_NO_CONSUMERS: i64`, value `313`: An immediate message no consumer took.
- `constant REPLY_CONNECTION_FORCED: i64`, value `320`: A connection the server's operator closed.
- `constant REPLY_INVALID_PATH: i64`, value `402`: A virtual host that does not exist.
- `constant REPLY_ACCESS_REFUSED: i64`, value `403`: A login or a resource refused.
- `constant REPLY_NOT_FOUND: i64`, value `404`: A queue, an exchange or a consumer the server does not know.
- `constant REPLY_RESOURCE_LOCKED: i64`, value `405`: A resource another connection holds exclusively.
- `constant REPLY_PRECONDITION_FAILED: i64`, value `406`: A request whose precondition is false: a declaration that disagrees with what exists, a delivery tag unknown.
- `constant REPLY_FRAME_ERROR: i64`, value `501`: A frame the server could not read.
- `constant REPLY_SYNTAX_ERROR: i64`, value `502`: A method whose fields the server could not read.
- `constant REPLY_COMMAND_INVALID: i64`, value `503`: A method sent where it is not allowed.
- `constant REPLY_CHANNEL_ERROR: i64`, value `504`: A channel used before it is opened, or after.
- `constant REPLY_UNEXPECTED_FRAME: i64`, value `505`: A frame the server did not expect.
- `constant REPLY_RESOURCE_ERROR: i64`, value `506`: A resource the server has run out of.
- `constant REPLY_NOT_ALLOWED: i64`, value `530`: A method the server does not allow here, a virtual host refused.
- `constant REPLY_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: i64`, value `540`: A method the server does not implement.
- `constant REPLY_INTERNAL_ERROR: i64`, value `541`: A fault of the server itself.


### kafka

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/kafka`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/kafka/).

A Kafka client written in Heroes, speaking the wire protocol over TCP connections of `net` or TLS of `tls`, linking no library.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument refused, bytes from a broker that are no Kafka, or an offset outside a partition's log: every function.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A topic, a partition, a group or a coordinator the cluster does not know.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: A topic made already: `create_topics`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: A login or an authorization refused: every function that talks to a broker.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The client or a broker's connection is closed: every function that talks to a broker.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The time a call allowed ran out, the broker's last error, where a retry met one, in the message: every function that waits.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while the call waited (`os.ask_stop`).
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: An answer or a batch past a bound, the broker's or this client's.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A version, a login mechanism or a compression the broker or this client does not speak.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: A failure none of the above names, the broker's error named in the message: a group rebalanced under a commit.
- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `9092`: The port a Kafka broker listens on unless told another.
- `constant EARLIEST: i64`, value `-2`: The offset `list_offset` answers for the start of a partition's log.
- `constant LATEST: i64`, value `-1`: The offset `list_offset` answers for the end of a partition's log: the offset the next record will take.
- `record Header(key: str, value: [u8])`: One header of a message: a key and bytes.
- `record Message(topic: str, partition: i64, offset: i64, timestamp: time.Instant?, key: [u8]?, value: [u8]?, headers: [Header])`: A message as it is produced and fetched.
- `record Produced(base_offset: i64, log_append_time: time.Instant?, log_start_offset: i64)`: What a broker answered a batch written to one partition.
- `record Fetched(messages: [Message], high_watermark: i64, last_stable_offset: i64, log_start_offset: i64, next_offset: i64)`: What a fetch of one partition answered.
- `record TopicPartition(topic: str, partition: i64)`: A partition of a topic.
- `record Offset(topic: str, partition: i64, offset: i64, metadata: str)`: An offset a group keeps for a partition: where its next read begins.
- `record GroupListing(group_id: str, protocol_type: str)`: A group the cluster knows.
- `record GroupMember(member_id: str, group_instance_id: str, client_id: str, client_host: str, topics: [str], assignment: [TopicPartition])`: A member of a group, as `describe_group` describes it.
- `record GroupDescription(group_id: str, state: str, protocol_type: str, protocol: str, members: [GroupMember])`: A group, as `describe_group` describes it.
- `record Subscription(member_id: str, topics: [str])`: A member's subscription, as the range assignor reads it.
- `record Assignment(member_id: str, partitions: [TopicPartition])`: The partitions the assignor gave one member.
- `record Member(group_id: str, member_id: str, generation_id: i64, leader: bool)`: A consumer's place in its group.
- `variant Sasl = .none | .plain(username: str, password: str) | .scram_sha256(username: str, password: str) | .scram_sha512(username: str, password: str)`: How a client logs in.
- `variant Compression = .none | .gzip`: How a batch is compressed.
- `variant Acks = .none | .leader | .all`: The acknowledgement a produce waits for.
- `variant Isolation = .read_uncommitted | .read_committed`: What a fetch reads.
- `variant Start = .earliest | .latest | .none`: Where a consumer begins a partition its group kept no offset for.
- `variant Security = .plain | .checked(roots: str)`: How every connection to the cluster is protected.
- `record Options(brokers: [str], client_id: str, security: Security, sasl: Sasl, connect_timeout: time.Duration, wait: time.Duration, most_response_bytes: i64, acks: Acks, compression: Compression, isolation: Isolation, most_fetch_bytes: i64, auto_create_topics: bool)`: Where the cluster is and how to talk to it.
- `record GroupOptions(group_id: str, topics: [str], session_timeout: time.Duration, rebalance_timeout: time.Duration, heartbeat_interval: time.Duration, start: Start, auto_commit_interval: time.Duration, instance_id: str)`: How a consumer takes part in its group.
- `record Client(session: state.Session)`: A client of a cluster, which `connect` makes and `close` ends.
- `record Consumer(group: state.Group)`: A consumer, a member of a group, which `subscribe` makes and `close_consumer` ends.
- `function options(brokers: [str]) -> Options`, called `kafka.options(brokers)`: The options of a client of the brokers `brokers`: the client `rebel`, no TLS, no login, 10 seconds to connect and for each request, answers of 100 MiB at most, the leader's acknowledgement, no compression, every message read, 1 MiB fetched of a partition at most, and no topic made by asking.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Client?`, called `kafka.connect(opts)`: A client of the cluster `opts` names: the first broker that answers asked its versions, logged in where `opts.sasl` asks, and asked the cluster's brokers. Fails `permission`, `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function close(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `kafka.close(@c)`: Closes every connection of the client; every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(c: Client) -> bool`, called `kafka.is_closed(c)`: Whether the client is closed.
- `function api_versions_of(c: Client) -> [ApiVersion]`, called `kafka.api_versions_of(c)`: The versions of each request the broker first reached reads, in the order of their keys.
- `record Broker(id: i64, host: str, port: i64, rack: str)`: A broker of the cluster.
- `record Partition(id: i64, leader: i64, leader_epoch: i64, replicas: [i64], isr: [i64], offline: [i64])`: A partition of a topic, as the metadata describes it.
- `record Topic(name: str, internal: bool, partitions: [Partition])`: A topic of the cluster, as the metadata describes it.
- `record Metadata(cluster_id: str, controller_id: i64, brokers: [Broker], topics: [Topic])`: What the cluster says of itself.
- `record ApiVersion(key: i64, min: i64, max: i64)`: The versions a broker reads of one request.
- `record NewTopic(name: str, partitions: i64, replication: i64, configs: [Config])`: A topic to make.
- `record Config(name: str, value: str)`: One entry of a topic's configuration.
- `function metadata(@c: Client, topics: [str]) -> Metadata?`, called `kafka.metadata(@c, topics)`: What the cluster says of itself and of the topics `topics`. Fails `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function partitions_of(@c: Client, topic: str) -> [i64]?`, called `kafka.partitions_of(@c, topic)`: The numbers of the partitions of `topic`, ascending. Fails as `metadata` does.
- `function new_topic(name: str, partitions: i64) -> NewTopic`, called `kafka.new_topic(name, partitions)`: A topic named `name` of `partitions` partitions, each copied as the broker's default asks, with no configuration.
- `function create_topics(@c: Client, topics: [NewTopic]) -> ()?`, called `kafka.create_topics(@c, topics)`: Makes the topics `topics`, waiting until the controller has made them. Fails `exists`, `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function delete_topics(@c: Client, names: [str]) -> ()?`, called `kafka.delete_topics(@c, names)`: Deletes the topics `names`, every message in them. Fails `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function create_partitions(@c: Client, topic: str, count: i64) -> ()?`, called `kafka.create_partitions(@c, topic, count)`: Gives `topic` more partitions, `count` in all. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function delete_records(@c: Client, topic: str, partition: i64, before: i64) -> i64?`, called `kafka.delete_records(@c, topic, partition: partition, before: before)`: Deletes the messages of a partition before the offset `before`, and answers the partition's first offset after. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function message(value: [u8]) -> Message`, called `kafka.message(value)`: A message holding `value`, with no key and no header, for the partition its producer chooses, its time the moment it is sent.
- `function tombstone(key: [u8]) -> Message`, called `kafka.tombstone(key)`: A tombstone: a message with the key `key` and a null value, which a compacted topic keeps in place of the key's last value until it removes both.
- `function with_key(m: Message, key: [u8]) -> Message`, called `kafka.with_key(m, key)`: `m` with the key `key`, so the partition is chosen by it.
- `function with_header(m: Message, key: str, value: [u8]) -> Message`, called `kafka.with_header(m, key, value)`: `m` with the header `key` and `value` added after the others.
- `function partition_of(key: [u8], partitions: i64) -> i64`, called `kafka.partition_of(key, partitions)`: The partition Java's client chooses for a message keyed `key` among `partitions`: the key's 32-bit MurmurHash2, its sign bit cleared, modulo their number.
- `function produce(@c: Client, topic: str, partition: i64, messages: [Message]) -> Produced?`, called `kafka.produce(@c, topic, partition, messages)`: Writes `messages` to `partition` of `topic` in one batch, and answers what the leader said. Fails `limit`, `not_found`, `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function send(@c: Client, messages: [Message]) -> [Message]?`, called `kafka.send(@c, messages)`: Writes each message of `messages` to its topic and partition, a batch for each partition and a request for each leader, and answers them in the same order, their partition and offset set. Fails as `produce` does, after every partition that could be written was.
- `function fetch(@c: Client, topic: str, partition: i64, offset: i64, wait: time.Duration) -> Fetched?`, called `kafka.fetch(@c, topic, partition: partition, offset: offset, wait)`: The messages of `partition` of `topic` from the offset `offset`, the broker waiting up to `wait` for one to come. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function list_offset(@c: Client, topic: str, partition: i64, at: i64) -> i64?`, called `kafka.list_offset(@c, topic, partition: partition, at: at)`: The offset of the first message of `partition` of `topic` written at `at` or after. Fails `not_found`.
- `function find_coordinator(@c: Client, group_id: str) -> Broker?`, called `kafka.find_coordinator(@c, group_id)`: The broker that coordinates the group `group_id`: its offsets and its members. Fails `permission`.
- `function commit_offsets(@c: Client, group_id: str, offsets: [Offset]) -> ()?`, called `kafka.commit_offsets(@c, group_id, offsets)`: Keeps `offsets` as the group `group_id`'s, outside any membership, as a program that assigns its own partitions does. Fails `failed`, `permission`.
- `function fetch_offsets(@c: Client, group_id: str) -> [Offset]?`, called `kafka.fetch_offsets(@c, group_id)`: The offsets the group `group_id` keeps, for every partition it kept one for, by topic and partition. Fails `permission`.
- `function list_groups(@c: Client) -> [GroupListing]?`, called `kafka.list_groups(@c)`: The groups the cluster knows, by group and broker in the order they answered. Fails as every call that talks to a broker fails.
- `function describe_group(@c: Client, group_id: str) -> GroupDescription?`, called `kafka.describe_group(@c, group_id)`: What the coordinator of the group `group_id` says of it: its state, its assignor, its members and their partitions. Fails `permission`.
- `function delete_groups(@c: Client, group_ids: [str]) -> ()?`, called `kafka.delete_groups(@c, group_ids)`: Deletes the groups `group_ids` and the offsets they keep. Fails `not_found`, `failed`.
- `function group_options(group_id: str, topics: [str]) -> GroupOptions`, called `kafka.group_options(group_id, topics)`: The options of a consumer of `topics` in the group `group_id`: a session of 45 seconds, five minutes to join again, a heartbeat every three seconds, the earliest offset where the group kept none, offsets committed every five seconds, and no static identifier.
- `function subscribe(opts: Options, group: GroupOptions) -> Consumer?`, called `kafka.subscribe(opts, group)`: A consumer in the group `group.group_id`: connected as `opts` says, joined, its partitions assigned by the range assignor (by this consumer where it leads the group), its positions read from the group's offsets. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function poll(@k: Consumer, wait: time.Duration) -> [Message]?`, called `kafka.poll(@k, wait)`: The messages of the consumer's partitions from its positions, waiting up to `wait` for one, its positions moved past them; the heartbeat and the commit sent where they fall due, the group joined again where it changed. Fails `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function commit(@k: Consumer) -> ()?`, called `kafka.commit(@k)`: Commits the consumer's positions as its group's offsets, so a consumer that takes its partitions over begins after the messages `poll` answered. Fails `failed`.
- `function seek(@k: Consumer, topic: str, partition: i64, offset: i64) -> ()?`, called `kafka.seek(@k, topic, partition: partition, offset: offset)`: Moves the consumer's position in a partition it was assigned. Fails `not_found`.
- `function position_of(k: Consumer, topic: str, partition: i64) -> i64?`, called `kafka.position_of(k, topic, partition)`: The consumer's position in a partition it was assigned: the offset of the next message `poll` answers. Fails `not_found`.
- `function assignment_of(k: Consumer) -> [TopicPartition]`, called `kafka.assignment_of(k)`: The partitions the consumer was assigned, by topic then number.
- `function member_of(k: Consumer) -> Member`, called `kafka.member_of(k)`: The consumer's place in its group.
- `function pause(@k: Consumer, topic: str, partition: i64) -> ()?`, called `kafka.pause(@k, topic, partition)`: Stops `poll` reading a partition the consumer was assigned, its position kept. Fails `not_found`.
- `function resume(@k: Consumer, topic: str, partition: i64) -> ()?`, called `kafka.resume(@k, topic, partition)`: Lets `poll` read a partition `pause` stopped. Fails `not_found`.
- `function close_consumer(@k: Consumer) -> ()?`, called `kafka.close_consumer(@k)`: Commits where `GroupOptions.auto_commit_interval` asks it, leaves the group so its partitions go to others at once, and closes the consumer's connections. Fails `closed`.
- `function assign_range(subscriptions: [Subscription], partition_counts: {str: i64}) -> [Assignment]`, called `kafka.assign_range(subscriptions, partition_counts)`: The range assignor's answer: each topic's partitions cut into runs, one for each member that subscribes to it in the order of their identifiers, the first members one partition longer where they do not divide evenly.
- `function encode_batch(messages: [Message], compression: Compression) -> [u8]?`, called `kafka.encode_batch(messages, compression)`: The record batch, format 2, that `messages` make: their offsets counted from 0, their times from the first, its CRC-32C computed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_batches(data: [u8]) -> [Message]?`, called `kafka.decode_batches(data)`: The messages the record batches `data` hold, as a fetch answers them; the control records of transactions left out, a batch cut short at the end left out too. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function error_name(code: i64) -> str?`, called `kafka.error_name(code)`: The name Kafka gives the error `code`: `UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PARTITION` for 3. Fails `not_found`.


### mongodb

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/mongodb`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mongodb/).

A MongoDB client written in Heroes: it speaks MongoDB's wire protocol (OP_MSG) over a TCP connection of `net` or a TLS connection of `tls`, and links no library.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an argument refused, a connection string that is none, a reply that is not of the kind asked, and what the server refuses as written.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a document `find_one` and its kin found none of, a cursor with no more documents, no server that suits the read preference, and what the server says is not there.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a duplicate key, and of a collection or an index that exists.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a login refused and of a command the user may not run.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a client that is closed, or whose connection the server or the network closed while the call waited.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a call whose time ran out: a socket's timeout, a `maxTimeMS`, a write concern's `wtimeout`, a change stream's wait.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The code of a call that ended because the program was asked to stop.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a document or a message past what the server takes, and of a stage past its memory.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of what this client or the server does not do: an option, a mechanism, a command, a transaction on a standalone server.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of every other failure the server reports.
- `constant DEFAULT_PORT: i64`, value `27017`: The port MongoDB listens on unless told another.
- `constant LABEL_TRANSIENT_TRANSACTION_ERROR: str`, value `"TransientTransactionError"`: The label of a failure after which the whole transaction may be run again.
- `constant LABEL_UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION_COMMIT_RESULT: str`, value `"UnknownTransactionCommitResult"`: The label of a commit whose outcome is unknown, which may be committed again.
- `constant LABEL_RETRYABLE_WRITE_ERROR: str`, value `"RetryableWriteError"`: The label of a write the server says may be sent again.
- `variant Security = .plain | .checked(roots: str)`: How the connection is secured.
- `variant Mechanism = .negotiated | .scram_sha_1 | .scram_sha_256 | .sasl_plain`: How the user logs in.
- `variant ReadPreference = .primary | .primary_preferred | .secondary | .secondary_preferred | .nearest`: Which server of a replica set the client connects to and reads from.
- `variant Journal = .server_default | .required | .not_required`: Whether a write waits for the server's journal.
- `record WriteConcern(w: str, journal: Journal, timeout: time.Duration)`: How a write is acknowledged.
- `record Host(name: str, port: i64)`: One server's name and port.
- `record Options(hosts: [Host], srv_name: str, srv_service_name: str, srv_max_hosts: i64, username: str, password: str, auth_source: str, mechanism: Mechanism, database: str, replica_set: str, direct: bool, security: Security, app_name: str, connect_timeout: time.Duration, socket_timeout: time.Duration, read_preference: ReadPreference, read_concern: str, write_concern: WriteConcern, retry_writes: bool, retry_reads: bool, server_api: str)`: Where the servers are, how to log in, and how commands are sent.
- `function options(host: str) -> Options`, called `mongodb.options(host)`: The options of a connection to `host` at `DEFAULT_PORT`, as the drivers default them: no user, plain TCP, the primary, the server's concerns, reads and writes retried, a TCP connection given 10 seconds and no time limit on a reply.
- `function parse_url(text: str) -> Options?`, called `mongodb.parse_url(text)`: The options a connection string names, as the drivers' URI specification reads one: `mongodb://user:password@host1:port1,host2/database?options` or `mongodb+srv://user:password@cluster.example.com/database?options`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record Client(state: session.State)`: A connection to a MongoDB server, which `connect` makes and `close` ends.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Client?`, called `mongodb.connect(opts)`: A client of the server `opts` choose: the SRV name resolved by the system's resolver where one is named, then each host tried in order and greeted with `hello`, the first that suits the read preference kept (a server that is not names the one that is, which is tried next), and the user logged in. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `permission`, `closed`, `timeout`.
- `function close(@client: Client) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.close(@client)`: Ends `client`: its logical session is ended on the server, whatever it answers, and its connection closed. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_closed(client: Client) -> bool`, called `mongodb.is_closed(client)`: Whether `client` is closed, by `close` or by a connection lost.
- `function set_timeout(@client: Client, timeout: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.set_timeout(@client, timeout)`: Makes every later command of `client` wait at most `timeout` for its reply, failing `timeout`; `time.max_duration()` takes the limit away. Fails `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `record ServerInfo(address: str, replica_set: str, is_writable: bool, is_mongos: bool, has_sessions: bool, max_wire_version: i64, max_document_size: i64, max_message_size: i64, max_write_batch_size: i64, hello: bson.Document)`: What `server_of` answers: what the server the client stands on said of itself.
- `function server_of(client: Client) -> ServerInfo`, called `mongodb.server_of(client)`: What the server `client` stands on said of itself when it connected.
- `function ping(@client: Client) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.ping(@client)`: Asks the server whether it answers: the command `ping`. Fails as every command fails.
- `function run_command(@client: Client, database: str, command: bson.Document) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.run_command(@client, database, command)`: The reply to `command`, run on `database` as it is, with what the protocol adds: the session, the transaction, the read preference, the cluster time. Fails with the code of the server's failure, and as every command fails.
- `function run_cursor_command(@client: Client, database: str, command: bson.Document) -> Cursor?`, called `mongodb.run_cursor_command(@client, database, command)`: The cursor a command answers with, `listCollections` or a command of a server's own: run on `database`, its first batch read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function explain(@client: Client, database: str, command: bson.Document, verbosity: str) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.explain(@client, database: database, command, verbosity: verbosity)`: The server's plan for `command`, as `explain` answers it. Fails as `run_command` fails.
- `function list_database_names(@client: Client) -> [str]?`, called `mongodb.list_database_names(@client)`: The names of the databases on the server, in its order. Fails `permission`.
- `function list_databases(@client: Client, query: bson.Document) -> [bson.Document]?`, called `mongodb.list_databases(@client, query)`: The databases on the server, each a document of its `name`, `sizeOnDisk` and `empty`. Fails as `list_database_names` fails.
- `function drop_database(@client: Client, database: str) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.drop_database(@client, database)`: Removes the database `database` and all it holds. Fails as every write fails.
- `function list_collection_names(@client: Client, database: str) -> [str]?`, called `mongodb.list_collection_names(@client, database)`: The names of the collections and views of `database`. Fails as `list_collections` fails.
- `function list_collections(@client: Client, database: str, query: bson.Document) -> [bson.Document]?`, called `mongodb.list_collections(@client, database, query)`: The collections and views of `database`, each the server's document of its `name`, `type`, `options` and `info`. Fails as every read fails.
- `function create_collection(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, opts: bson.Document) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.create_collection(@client, database: database, collection: collection, opts)`: Creates the collection `collection`, with the server's options. Fails `exists`.
- `function create_view(@client: Client, database: str, view: str, source: str, pipeline: [bson.Document]) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.create_view(@client, database: database, view: view, source: source, pipeline)`: Creates the view `view` of the collection `source` through `pipeline`. Fails `exists`.
- `function drop_collection(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.drop_collection(@client, database: database, collection: collection)`: Removes the collection `collection`, its documents and its indexes. Fails as every write fails.
- `function rename_collection(@client: Client, database: str, from: str, to: str, drop_target: bool) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.rename_collection(@client, database: database, from: from, to: to, drop_target)`: Gives the collection `from` the name `to`, in one database. Fails `not_found`, `exists`.
- `function insert_one(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, doc: bson.Document) -> bson.Value?`, called `mongodb.insert_one(@client, database: database, collection: collection, doc)`: Inserts `doc` into `collection`, with a new ObjectId as its `_id` where it has none, and answers its `_id`. Fails `exists`, `limit`.
- `function insert_many(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, docs: [bson.Document], ordered: bool) -> [bson.Value]?`, called `mongodb.insert_many(@client, database: database, collection: collection, docs, ordered)`: Inserts `docs` into `collection`, in batches the server takes, each with a new ObjectId where it has no `_id`, and answers their `_id`s in order. Fails with the first write's failure, its index in `docs` and how many others failed in its message, and as `insert_one` fails.
- `record WriteOptions(upsert: bool, array_filters: [bson.Document], statement: bson.Document, command: bson.Document)`: How an update, a replacement or a delete is done.
- `function default_write_options() -> WriteOptions`, called `mongodb.default_write_options()`: The options of a plain write: no upsert, no array filter, no field more.
- `record UpdateResult(matched: i64, modified: i64, upserted_ids: [bson.Value])`: What an update or a replacement answers.
- `function update_one(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, update: bson.Value, opts: WriteOptions) -> UpdateResult?`, called `mongodb.update_one(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, update, opts)`: Updates the first document of `collection` that `query` matches. Fails `invalid`.
- `function update_many(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, update: bson.Value, opts: WriteOptions) -> UpdateResult?`, called `mongodb.update_many(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, update, opts)`: Updates every document of `collection` that `query` matches. Fails as `update_one` fails.
- `function replace_one(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, replacement: bson.Document, opts: WriteOptions) -> UpdateResult?`, called `mongodb.replace_one(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query: query, replacement: replacement, opts)`: Replaces the first document of `collection` that `query` matches by `replacement`, its `_id` kept. Fails `invalid`.
- `function delete_one(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, opts: WriteOptions) -> i64?`, called `mongodb.delete_one(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, opts)`: Deletes the first document of `collection` that `query` matches, and answers how many were deleted, 0 or 1. Fails as every write fails.
- `function delete_many(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, opts: WriteOptions) -> i64?`, called `mongodb.delete_many(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, opts)`: Deletes every document of `collection` that `query` matches, and answers how many. Fails as every write fails.
- `variant WriteModel = .insert_one(doc: bson.Document) | .update_one(query: bson.Document, update: bson.Value, upsert: bool) | .update_many(query: bson.Document, update: bson.Value, upsert: bool) | .replace_one(query: bson.Document, replacement: bson.Document, upsert: bool) | .delete_one(query: bson.Document) | .delete_many(query: bson.Document)`: One write of a bulk write.
- `record BulkWriteResult(inserted: i64, matched: i64, modified: i64, deleted: i64, inserted_ids: [bson.Value], upserted_ids: [bson.Value])`: What `bulk_write` answers: the counts of its writes.
- `function bulk_write(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, models: [WriteModel], ordered: bool) -> BulkWriteResult?`, called `mongodb.bulk_write(@client, database: database, collection: collection, models, ordered)`: Runs `models` on `collection`, each run of writes of one kind sent as one command, and sums their counts. Fails `invalid`.
- `record FindOptions(projection: bson.Document, sort: bson.Document, skip: i64, limit: i64, batch_size: i64, command: bson.Document)`: How a query is run.
- `function default_find_options() -> FindOptions`, called `mongodb.default_find_options()`: The options of a plain query: every field, the server's order, no skip, no limit, its batches.
- `record Cursor(state: cursors.Cursor)`: A cursor of the server, read batch by batch by `next_document`.
- `function find_many(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, opts: FindOptions) -> Cursor?`, called `mongodb.find_many(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, opts)`: The documents of `collection` that `query` matches, as a cursor: MongoDB's `find`, which a built-in's name keeps from being this function's. Fails `invalid`.
- `function find_one(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, opts: FindOptions) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.find_one(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, opts)`: The first document of `collection` that `query` matches, in `opts`' order. Fails `not_found`.
- `function next_document(@client: Client, @cursor: Cursor) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.next_document(@client, @cursor)`: The next document of `cursor`, the server asked for its next batch where the last is read. Fails `not_found`, `timeout`.
- `function read_all(@client: Client, @cursor: Cursor) -> [bson.Document]?`, called `mongodb.read_all(@client, @cursor)`: Every document `cursor` still holds, in order: the cursor read to its end. Fails `timeout`.
- `function close_cursor(@client: Client, @cursor: Cursor) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.close_cursor(@client, @cursor)`: Tells the server to forget `cursor` where it still holds documents. Fails as every command fails.
- `function is_exhausted(cursor: Cursor) -> bool`, called `mongodb.is_exhausted(cursor)`: Whether `cursor` has given out every document: its batch read and the server holding none.
- `function count_documents(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document) -> i64?`, called `mongodb.count_documents(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query)`: How many documents of `collection` `query` matches, counted by the server's aggregation as the drivers count them. Fails as every read fails.
- `function estimated_document_count(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str) -> i64?`, called `mongodb.estimated_document_count(@client, database: database, collection: collection)`: How many documents `collection` holds, as its metadata says: fast, and approximate after an unclean shutdown. Fails as every read fails.
- `function distinct(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, field: str, query: bson.Document) -> [bson.Value]?`, called `mongodb.distinct(@client, database: database, collection: collection, field: field, query)`: The distinct values of `field` among the documents of `collection` that `query` matches. Fails `limit`.
- `record AggregateOptions(batch_size: i64, command: bson.Document)`: How a pipeline is run.
- `function default_aggregate_options() -> AggregateOptions`, called `mongodb.default_aggregate_options()`: The options of a plain pipeline.
- `function aggregate(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, pipeline: [bson.Document], opts: AggregateOptions) -> Cursor?`, called `mongodb.aggregate(@client, database: database, collection: collection, pipeline, opts)`: The documents `pipeline` makes of `collection`, as a cursor. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `variant ReturnDocument = .before | .after`: Which version of the document a find-and-modify answers.
- `record FindAndModifyOptions(sort: bson.Document, projection: bson.Document, upsert: bool, returned: ReturnDocument, array_filters: [bson.Document], command: bson.Document)`: How a find-and-modify is done.
- `function default_find_and_modify_options() -> FindAndModifyOptions`, called `mongodb.default_find_and_modify_options()`: The options of a plain find-and-modify: the document before the change.
- `function find_one_and_update(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, update: bson.Value, opts: FindAndModifyOptions) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.find_one_and_update(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, update, opts)`: Updates the first document of `collection` that `query` matches in `opts`' order, and answers it before or after. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function find_one_and_replace(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, replacement: bson.Document, opts: FindAndModifyOptions) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.find_one_and_replace(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query: query, replacement: replacement, opts)`: Replaces the first document of `collection` that `query` matches, and answers it before or after. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function find_one_and_delete(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, query: bson.Document, opts: FindAndModifyOptions) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.find_one_and_delete(@client, database: database, collection: collection, query, opts)`: Deletes the first document of `collection` that `query` matches, and answers it. Fails `not_found`.
- `record IndexModel(keys: bson.Document, options: bson.Document)`: An index to create: its keys and the server's options.
- `function index_name_of(key_pattern: bson.Document) -> str`, called `mongodb.index_name_of(key_pattern)`: The name the server gives an index of `key_pattern` when none is asked: each key and its direction or kind joined by `_`, `a_1_b_-1`.
- `function create_index(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, model: IndexModel) -> str?`, called `mongodb.create_index(@client, database: database, collection: collection, model)`: Creates the index `model` describes on `collection`, and answers its name. Fails `exists`.
- `function create_indexes(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, models: [IndexModel]) -> [str]?`, called `mongodb.create_indexes(@client, database: database, collection: collection, models)`: Creates every index `models` describe on `collection`, in one command, and answers their names in order. Fails `invalid`, `exists`.
- `function list_indexes(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str) -> [bson.Document]?`, called `mongodb.list_indexes(@client, database: database, collection: collection)`: The indexes of `collection`, each the server's document of its `key`, `name` and options. Fails `not_found`.
- `function drop_index(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.drop_index(@client, database: database, collection: collection, name: name)`: Removes the index named `name` from `collection`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function drop_indexes(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.drop_indexes(@client, database: database, collection: collection)`: Removes every index of `collection` but `_id_`. Fails as `drop_index` fails.
- `record WatchOptions(full_document: str, resume_after: bson.Document, start_after: bson.Document, max_await: time.Duration, batch_size: i64)`: How a change stream is opened.
- `function default_watch_options() -> WatchOptions`, called `mongodb.default_watch_options()`: The options of a stream that begins now.
- `function watch(@client: Client, database: str, collection: str, pipeline: [bson.Document], opts: WatchOptions) -> Cursor?`, called `mongodb.watch(@client, database: database, collection: collection, pipeline, opts)`: A change stream of `collection`, of `database`, or of the whole server: a cursor whose `next_document` answers each change as it comes, a document of its `operationType`, `documentKey`, `fullDocument`, `updateDescription`. Fails `unsupported`, `timeout`.
- `function resume_token_of(cursor: Cursor) -> bson.Document?`, called `mongodb.resume_token_of(cursor)`: The token after the last change a stream gave out, to open another stream that resumes after it. Fails `not_found`.
- `record TransactionOptions(read_concern: str, write_concern: WriteConcern, max_commit_time: time.Duration)`: How a transaction is run.
- `function default_transaction_options() -> TransactionOptions`, called `mongodb.default_transaction_options()`: The options of a transaction run with the client's concerns.
- `function start_transaction(@client: Client, opts: TransactionOptions) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.start_transaction(@client, opts)`: Starts a transaction on `client`'s session: every later command of the client runs in it until `commit_transaction` or `abort_transaction`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function commit_transaction(@client: Client) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.commit_transaction(@client)`: Commits the transaction in progress: its writes become visible together. Fails `invalid`.
- `function abort_transaction(@client: Client) -> ()?`, called `mongodb.abort_transaction(@client)`: Aborts the transaction in progress: none of its writes stands. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_in_transaction(client: Client) -> bool`, called `mongodb.is_in_transaction(client)`: Whether a transaction is in progress on `client`.
- `function session_id_of(client: Client) -> bson.Document`, called `mongodb.session_id_of(client)`: The id of `client`'s logical session, `{"id": <UUID>}`, which every command carries where the server keeps sessions.
- `function server_code_of(message: str) -> i64?`, called `mongodb.server_code_of(message)`: The server's own code a failure's message names, `11000` of `[11000 DuplicateKey] ...`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function labels_of(message: str) -> [str]`, called `mongodb.labels_of(message)`: The labels a failure's message names, `TransientTransactionError` among them, in the server's order.
- `function has_label(message: str, label: str) -> bool`, called `mongodb.has_label(message: message, label: label)`: Whether a failure's message names `label`.


### log/files

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/log/files`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/log/files/).

A logger's lines written to a file that is rotated: when the next line would take the file past a size, or is of a later day, the file is set aside under an old file's name and a new one begun at the same path; the oldest old files are removed past a count or an age, and the others gzipped where asked.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a `Rotation` out of its range, and of a path that ends in no name, from `open`.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a rotation that finds a thousand old files of one millisecond, from `write_line`, `write` and `rotate`.
- `record Rotation(max_bytes: i64, daily: bool, keep: i64, keep_days: i64, compress: bool)`: When a file is set aside, and what is kept of the old ones.
- `record Rotating(path: str, rotation: Rotation, stream: io.Stream, is_open: bool, size: i64, last: time.Instant)`: A log's file open to append, with what decides its next rotation.
- `function open(path: str, rotation: Rotation) -> Rotating?`, called `files.open(path, rotation)`: Opens the log at `path` to append, made with the folders on its way where it is not there, for lines rotated by `rotation`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write(@file: Rotating, logger: log.Logger, level: log.Level, msg: str, fields: [log.Field]) -> ()?`, called `files.write(@file, logger, level, msg, fields)`: Writes one line at `level` to the file, rotating it first where the line asks, at the time `logger`'s clock reads; where the logger does not write that level, does nothing. Fails as `write_line` fails, and as the clock fails.
- `function write_line(@file: Rotating, line: str, at: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `files.write_line(@file, line, at)`: Writes `line` and a line feed to the file in one write, setting the file aside first where the line would take it past `max_bytes`, or where `at` is of a later day and `daily` is asked; a file holding nothing is never set aside. Fails where the line could not be written, its code `io.write`'s or `fs.open_with`'s; and, the line written, where the rotation could not set the file aside (the line then in the file that stays), compress or remove an old file, with that call's code and a message that says the line is written.
- `function rotate(@file: Rotating, at: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `files.rotate(@file, at)`: Sets the file aside under an old file's name and opens a new one at its path, then compresses and removes old files as its rotation asks: what a line past a bound does, and what a program asks on a signal or a schedule of its own. Fails `limit`.
- `function close(@file: Rotating) -> ()?`, called `files.close(@file)`: Closes the file. Fails as `io.close` fails, the file closed either way.
- `function old_files(path: str) -> [str]?`, called `files.old_files(path)`: The old files of the log at `path`, in its folder, the newest first: the names `write_line` and `rotate` gave the files they set aside, compressed or not. Fails `invalid`.
- `function old_name(path: str, last: time.Instant) -> str?`, called `files.old_name(path, last)`: The name the log at `path` sets a file aside under when its last line was at `last`, where no file holds that name: its stem, a `-`, the stamp of `last`, its extension. Fails `invalid`.


### image/ico

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/image/ico`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/ico/).

ICO and CUR read and written: the directory of images that Windows keeps an icon or a cursor in, each stored as a PNG or as a bitmap with a mask, every one an RGBA image here, with a cursor's hot spot.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a value an entry does not hold.
- `variant Kind = .icon | .cursor`: What a file holds.
- `variant Storage = .png | .bmp`: How an entry's image is stored.
- `record Hotspot(x: i64, y: i64)`: The pixel of a cursor's image that points.
- `record Entry(image: image.Image, storage: Storage, bits: i64, hotspot: Hotspot?)`: One image of an icon or cursor.
- `record Ico(kind: Kind, entries: [Entry])`: An icon or cursor file read.
- `constant MAX_ENTRIES: i64`, value `65535`: The most images one file holds: the directory's count is 16 bits.
- `constant PNG_SIGNATURE: [u8]`, value `[0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a]`: The signature a PNG file begins with.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> Ico?`, called `ico.decode(data, limits)`: The icon or cursor `data` holds. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `ico.decode_image(data, limits)`: The largest image of the icon or cursor `data` holds, alone. Fails as `decode` fails.
- `function encode(ico: Ico) -> [u8]?`, called `ico.encode(ico)`: The file holding `ico`: a directory, then each image as its entry says. Fails `invalid`.


### image/tiff

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/image/tiff`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/image/tiff/).

TIFF read and written: every page of a file, classic or BigTIFF in either byte order, in strips or tiles, coded by PackBits, LZW, Deflate (with the horizontal predictor), Zstandard, JPEG or CCITT's fax codings, with 1 to 16 bits a sample as gray, RGB, a palette, CMYK or YCbCr (its chroma shared by blocks of pixels), with an alpha channel, in one plane or several, and the bits of a byte in either fill order; and written in every one of those codings but JPEG, as strips or tiles, at 8 or 16 bits or at one bit a pixel.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `ifd.NOT_FOUND`: The code of a value a page does not hold.
- `variant Compression = .none | .packbits | .lzw | .deflate | .zstd | .jpeg | .ccitt_rle | .ccitt_g3 | .ccitt_g4 | .other(code: i64)`: How the strips or tiles of a page are coded.
- `variant Unit = .none | .inch | .centimetre`: The unit a resolution is given in.
- `record Resolution(x: f64, y: f64, unit: Unit)`: How many pixels fit in a unit of length, across and down.
- `record Page(image: image.Image, orientation: i64, compression: Compression, reduced: bool, resolution: Resolution?, description: str?, software: str?, date_time: str?, icc: [u8])`: One page of a file: its pixels and what its directory says about it.
- `record Tiff(pages: [Page], big: bool, big_endian: bool)`: A file read: its pages in order.
- `constant MAX_PAGES: i64`, value `reader.MAX_PAGES`: The most directories `decode` follows in one file.
- `function decode(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> Tiff?`, called `tiff.decode(data, limits)`: The pages of the TIFF file `data`. Fails `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_image(data: [u8], limits: image.Limits) -> image.Image?`, called `tiff.decode_image(data, limits)`: The first page of `data`, its pixels alone. Fails as `decode` fails, for the first page alone.
- `function compression_of(code: i64) -> Compression`, called `tiff.compression_of(code)`: The `Compression` that the Compression tag's number `code` names.
- `record Info(width: i64, height: i64, bits: i64, samples: i64, compression: Compression, pages: i64, big: bool)`: What the first page of a file says about itself, read from its directory without decoding a pixel.
- `function info_of(data: [u8]) -> Info?`, called `tiff.info_of(data)`: The first page's size and layout and the number of pages of `data`, read from the directories alone. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `variant Depth = .natural | .bilevel(threshold: i64)`: How many bits a pixel is written in.
- `record EncodeOptions(compression: Compression, predictor: bool, rows_per_strip: i64, tile_width: i64, tile_height: i64, big_endian: bool, big: bool, depth: Depth, two_dimensional: bool, byte_aligned_eol: bool)`: How `encode` writes a file.
- `function default_encode_options() -> EncodeOptions`, called `tiff.default_encode_options()`: The options that `encode` takes unless the caller changes them: strips of about 8 KiB, uncompressed, in little-endian order, one file of classic TIFF.
- `function encode(pages: [Page], options: EncodeOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `tiff.encode(pages, options)`: The pages `pages` as a TIFF file. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function encode_image(img: image.Image, options: EncodeOptions) -> [u8]?`, called `tiff.encode_image(img, options)`: `img` as a one-page TIFF file, no other tag written but its size, samples and coding. Fails as `encode` fails.


### pdf

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/pdf`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/pdf/).

PDF documents written and read.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a file that is not what PDF says, the message naming the byte; of a value a writer is given that PDF has no form for; and of an object asked for as a kind it is not.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a file that would pass the caller's `Limits`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a key a dictionary does not hold (`entry_of`) and of a font name that is none of the 14 (`parse_font`).
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of what this package does not do: a character a font has no glyph for (`width_of`, `draw_text`), a font it does not embed (`load_font`: CFF outlines, a licence that bars embedding), an image it does not embed (`add_png`), a file encrypted with AES (`decode`), a stream of an image filter (`stream_data_of`).
- `record Size(width: f64, height: f64)`: A width and a height, in points: 72 to the inch, as PDF measures.
- `variant Paper = .a0 | .a1 | .a2 | .a3 | .a4 | .a5 | .a6 | .b4 | .b5 | .letter | .legal | .tabloid | .executive`: The usual sizes of paper.
- `variant Unit = .point | .inch | .mm | .cm | .pica`: What `to_points` converts from.
- `function size_of(paper: Paper) -> Size`, called `pdf.size_of(paper)`: The size of `paper`, upright, in points: the millimetres converted exactly, so A4 is 595.2756 by 841.8898.
- `function to_landscape(size: Size) -> Size`, called `pdf.to_landscape(size)`: `size` turned to lie on its long side: the wider of its two lengths as the width.
- `function to_portrait(size: Size) -> Size`, called `pdf.to_portrait(size)`: `size` turned to stand on its short side: the taller of its two lengths as the height.
- `function to_points(n: f64, unit: Unit) -> f64`, called `pdf.to_points(n, unit)`: `n` of `unit` in points.
- `variant Color = .gray(level: f64) | .rgb(red: f64, green: f64, blue: f64) | .cmyk(cyan: f64, magenta: f64, yellow: f64, black: f64)`: A colour, each component from 0 to 1; one outside is written as the nearest end.
- `function parse_color(s: str) -> Color?`, called `pdf.parse_color(s)`: The colour `s` writes in CSS's hexadecimal form: `#rrggbb` or `#rgb`, in either case. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Font = .helvetica | .helvetica_bold | .helvetica_oblique | .helvetica_bold_oblique | .times_roman | .times_bold | .times_italic | .times_bold_italic | .courier | .courier_bold | .courier_oblique | .courier_bold_oblique | .symbol | .zapf_dingbats | .embedded(face: embedded.Face)`: A font text is drawn in: one of the 14 standard fonts, which every reader of PDF has and no file embeds, or a TrueType font of the program's own, which the file carries, cut down to the glyphs drawn.
- `record FontMetrics(ascent: i64, descent: i64, cap_height: i64, x_height: i64, italic_angle: f64, underline_position: i64, underline_thickness: i64, box_left: i64, box_bottom: i64, box_right: i64, box_top: i64)`: What an AFM file says of a font as a whole, in thousandths of the font's size: multiply by the size and divide by 1000 for points.
- `function base_font_of(font: Font) -> str`, called `pdf.base_font_of(font)`: The name PDF gives `font`, as its `/BaseFont` writes it: `Helvetica-Bold`.
- `function parse_font(name: str) -> Font?`, called `pdf.parse_font(name)`: The standard font PDF names `name`: `Times-Roman` is `times_roman`. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Measured(number: i64, slots: [embedded.Slot])`: What the writer holds of `font` to measure with: its number, 0 to 13 for a standard font and 14 for an embedded one, and the slots that number is read against.
- `function measured(font: Font) -> Measured`, called `pdf.measured(font)`: `font` as the writer measures it: the number it has and the slots that number is read against, so that a font that is not a document's yet can be measured.
- `function font_number(@doc: Document, font: Font) -> i64`, called `pdf.font_number(@doc, font)`: The number the pen gives `font` in `doc`: an embedded font is added to the document where it is not there already.
- `function load_font(data: [u8], index: i64) -> Font?`, called `pdf.load_font(data, index)`: A TrueType font made ready to draw with: read from the bytes of its file, and carried by every document that draws with it, cut down to the glyphs drawn, with a `ToUnicode` map so that a reader copies the text out. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function metrics_of(font: Font) -> FontMetrics`, called `pdf.metrics_of(font)`: The metrics of `font`, from Adobe's AFM file of it, or from the font itself where it is embedded: its `hhea`, `OS/2`, `post` and `head` tables scaled to thousandths of the size.
- `function width_of(text: str, font: Font, size: f64) -> f64?`, called `pdf.width_of(text, font, size)`: How wide `text` is in `font` at `size`, in points: the sum of its characters' widths in Adobe's AFM file, or in the embedded font's own `hmtx` table, rounded as the file's width array writes them, with no kerning, as PDF shows it. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function has_glyphs(font: Font, text: str) -> bool`, called `pdf.has_glyphs(font, text)`: Whether `font` has a glyph for every character of `text`, so that `draw_text` can show it.
- `record Document(state: compose.Doc)`: A document being written: its pages and what is drawn on them, the pen that draws, its images, links, bookmarks and information.
- `function document() -> Document`, called `pdf.document()`: A document of no page, its content compressed, its pen Helvetica at 12 points in black, lines 1 point wide.
- `function set_info(@doc: Document, key: str, value: str)`, called `pdf.set_info(@doc, key: key, value: value)`: Sets an entry of the document's information: `Title`, `Author`, `Subject`, `Keywords`, `Creator`, `Producer`, `CreationDate`, `ModDate`, or a key of the program's own.
- `function format_date(t: time.Instant) -> str`, called `pdf.format_date(t)`: `t` as PDF writes a date, in UTC: `D:20261118103000Z`.
- `function set_compression(@doc: Document, on: bool)`, called `pdf.set_compression(@doc, on)`: Sets whether the document's page content is compressed, which it is unless asked otherwise.
- `function add_page(@doc: Document, size: Size)`, called `pdf.add_page(@doc, size)`: Adds a page of `size` after the last one and draws on it from now on, with the pen as it stands.
- `function page_count(doc: Document) -> i64`, called `pdf.page_count(doc)`: How many pages `doc` has.
- `function set_page(@doc: Document, index: i64)`, called `pdf.set_page(@doc, index)`: Draws on the page at `index` from now on, as on a page just added: what is drawn goes on top of what it holds.
- `variant LineCap = .butt | .round | .square`: How the ends of a stroked line are drawn.
- `variant LineJoin = .miter | .round | .bevel`: How two strokes meet at a corner.
- `variant TextMode = .fill | .stroke | .fill_and_stroke | .invisible`: How the characters of text are painted.
- `record TextStyle(character_spacing: f64, word_spacing: f64, horizontal_scale: f64, rise: f64, mode: TextMode)`: The text state beside the font.
- `record Matrix(a: f64, b: f64, c: f64, d: f64, e: f64, f: f64)`: A transformation of the plane, as PDF's six numbers: a point (x, y) goes to (a x + c y + e, b x + d y + f).
- `function set_font(@doc: Document, font: Font, size: f64)`, called `pdf.set_font(@doc, font, size)`: Sets the font text is drawn and measured in from now on.
- `function set_fill_color(@doc: Document, color: Color)`, called `pdf.set_fill_color(@doc, color)`: Sets the colour shapes are filled with and text is drawn in.
- `function set_stroke_color(@doc: Document, color: Color)`, called `pdf.set_stroke_color(@doc, color)`: Sets the colour lines and outlines are drawn in.
- `function set_line_width(@doc: Document, width: f64)`, called `pdf.set_line_width(@doc, width)`: Sets how wide lines are drawn.
- `function set_line_cap(@doc: Document, style: LineCap)`, called `pdf.set_line_cap(@doc, style)`: Sets how the ends of lines are drawn.
- `function set_line_join(@doc: Document, style: LineJoin)`, called `pdf.set_line_join(@doc, style)`: Sets how lines meet at a corner.
- `function set_miter_limit(@doc: Document, limit: f64)`, called `pdf.set_miter_limit(@doc, limit)`: Sets how far a mitered corner may reach before it is cut, as a ratio of its length to the line's width.
- `function set_dash(@doc: Document, lengths: [f64], phase: f64)`, called `pdf.set_dash(@doc, lengths, phase)`: Sets the dashes lines are drawn with.
- `function set_opacity(@doc: Document, fill: f64, stroke: f64)`, called `pdf.set_opacity(@doc, fill: fill, stroke: stroke)`: Sets how opaque fills, text and strokes are drawn.
- `function text_style() -> TextStyle`, called `pdf.text_style()`: The usual text state: no spacing added, a scale of 100, no rise, the characters filled.
- `function set_text_style(@doc: Document, style: TextStyle)`, called `pdf.set_text_style(@doc, style)`: Sets the text state text is drawn and measured with from now on.
- `function save_state(@doc: Document)`, called `pdf.save_state(@doc)`: Saves the pen, the transform and the clipping on a stack, for `restore_state` to bring back.
- `function restore_state(@doc: Document)`, called `pdf.restore_state(@doc)`: Brings back the pen, the transform and the clipping the last `save_state` on this page saved.
- `function identity() -> Matrix`, called `pdf.identity()`: The transform that changes nothing.
- `function translation(x: f64, y: f64) -> Matrix`, called `pdf.translation(x: x, y: y)`: The transform that moves the plane `x` right and `y` up.
- `function rotation(degrees: f64) -> Matrix`, called `pdf.rotation(degrees)`: The transform that turns the plane about its origin.
- `function scaling(x: f64, y: f64) -> Matrix`, called `pdf.scaling(x: x, y: y)`: The transform that stretches the plane from its origin.
- `function multiply(first: Matrix, then: Matrix) -> Matrix`, called `pdf.multiply(first: first, then: then)`: The transform that does `first`, then `then`.
- `function transform(@doc: Document, matrix: Matrix)`, called `pdf.transform(@doc, matrix)`: Transforms the coordinates of everything drawn from now on by `matrix`, before the transform in force takes them to the page; `save_state` and `restore_state` bound it.
- `variant Paint = .stroke | .fill | .fill_and_stroke`: How a shape is painted.
- `record Point(x: f64, y: f64)`: A point of the page, in points from its bottom left corner.
- `record Path(steps: [str])`: A path: lines and curves drawn by `draw_path` or clipped to by `clip`.
- `function draw_line(@doc: Document, from_x: f64, from_y: f64, to_x: f64, to_y: f64)`, called `pdf.draw_line(@doc, from_x: from_x, from_y: from_y, to_x: to_x, to_y: to_y)`: Draws a straight line from one point to another, with the stroke colour.
- `function draw_rect(@doc: Document, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64, paint: Paint)`, called `pdf.draw_rect(@doc, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height, paint)`: Draws a rectangle whose bottom left corner is at (`x`, `y`).
- `function draw_rounded_rect(@doc: Document, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64, radius: f64, paint: Paint)`, called `pdf.draw_rounded_rect(@doc, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height, radius: radius, paint)`: Draws a rectangle with corners rounded to `radius`.
- `function draw_circle(@doc: Document, center_x: f64, center_y: f64, radius: f64, paint: Paint)`, called `pdf.draw_circle(@doc, center_x: center_x, center_y: center_y, radius: radius, paint)`: Draws a circle, as four Bézier curves.
- `function draw_ellipse(@doc: Document, center_x: f64, center_y: f64, radius_x: f64, radius_y: f64, paint: Paint)`, called `pdf.draw_ellipse(@doc, center_x: center_x, center_y: center_y, radius_x: radius_x, radius_y: radius_y, paint)`: Draws an ellipse whose axes are level and upright, as four Bézier curves.
- `function draw_polygon(@doc: Document, points: [Point], paint: Paint)`, called `pdf.draw_polygon(@doc, points, paint)`: Draws the closed shape whose corners are `points`, in order.
- `function draw_polyline(@doc: Document, points: [Point])`, called `pdf.draw_polyline(@doc, points)`: Draws the line through `points`, in order, not closed, with the stroke colour.
- `function empty_path() -> Path`, called `pdf.empty_path()`: A path with nothing in it.
- `function move_to(@p: Path, x: f64, y: f64)`, called `pdf.move_to(@p, x: x, y: y)`: Begins a new part of `p` at (`x`, `y`).
- `function line_to(@p: Path, x: f64, y: f64)`, called `pdf.line_to(@p, x: x, y: y)`: Adds to `p` a straight line from where it stands to (`x`, `y`).
- `function curve_to(@p: Path, control1_x: f64, control1_y: f64, control2_x: f64, control2_y: f64, x: f64, y: f64)`, called `pdf.curve_to(@p, control1_x: control1_x, control1_y: control1_y, control2_x: control2_x, control2_y: control2_y, x: x, y: y)`: Adds to `p` a cubic Bézier curve from where it stands to (`x`, `y`), pulled towards two control points.
- `function close_path(@p: Path)`, called `pdf.close_path(@p)`: Closes the part of `p` being drawn with a line back to where it began.
- `function draw_path(@doc: Document, p: Path, paint: Paint)`, called `pdf.draw_path(@doc, p, paint)`: Draws `p`.
- `function clip(@doc: Document, p: Path)`, called `pdf.clip(@doc, p)`: Limits what is drawn from now on to the inside of `p`, within the limit in force; `save_state` and `restore_state` bound it.
- `variant Align = .left | .center | .right | .justify`: Where a line of text stands against the point or the box it is given.
- `function draw_text(@doc: Document, x: f64, y: f64, text: str, align: Align) -> ()?`, called `pdf.draw_text(@doc, x: x, y: y, text, align)`: Draws one line of `text` with the font, size, colour and text style of the pen, its baseline at `y`. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function wrap_text(text: str, font: Font, size: f64, width: f64) -> [str]?`, called `pdf.wrap_text(text, font, size: size, width: width)`: The lines `text` breaks into so that none is wider than `width` in `font` at `size`: at spaces where it can, inside a word too long for a line where it must, and at every line break of `text`. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function draw_text_box(@doc: Document, x: f64, top: f64, width: f64, text: str, align: Align, line_height: f64) -> f64?`, called `pdf.draw_text_box(@doc, x: x, top: top, width: width, text, align, line_height: line_height)`: Draws `text` wrapped into a box `width` wide whose top is `top`, line under line, and answers the height where the last line's descenders end: `top` where `text` is empty. Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Column(width: f64, align: Align)`: A column of a table.
- `record Table(columns: [Column], rows: [[str]], header_rows: i64, font: Font, header_font: Font, size: f64, line_height: f64, padding: f64, border: f64, header_fill: Color)`: A table of text: its columns, its rows of cells, and how it is drawn.
- `function table(widths: [f64], rows: [[str]]) -> Table`, called `pdf.table(widths, rows)`: A table of `widths` columns holding `rows`, the first row its header: in Helvetica at 10 points, the header bold on light gray, lines 12 points apart, cells padded 4 points, borders half a point wide, every column left.
- `function draw_table(@doc: Document, x: f64, top: f64, bottom: f64, t: Table) -> f64?`, called `pdf.draw_table(@doc, x: x, top: top, bottom: bottom, t)`: Draws `t` from `top` down, its left at `x`, and answers the height where its last row ends. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `record ImageId(index: i64, width: i64, height: i64)`: An image added to a document, which `draw_image` draws as often as asked while its bytes are written once.
- `function add_jpeg(@doc: Document, data: [u8]) -> ImageId?`, called `pdf.add_jpeg(@doc, data)`: Adds the JPEG image `data` to `doc`, its bytes passed through as they are, for `draw_image` to draw. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function add_png(@doc: Document, data: [u8]) -> ImageId?`, called `pdf.add_png(@doc, data)`: Adds the PNG image `data` to `doc` for `draw_image` to draw, decoded by `image/png` and embedded as `add_image` embeds it: any colour type and depth, interlaced or not, its transparency kept as a soft mask. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function add_image(@doc: Document, img: image.Image) -> ImageId?`, called `pdf.add_image(@doc, img)`: Adds the image `img` to `doc` for `draw_image` to draw: its colour samples compressed with DEFLATE, 8 or 16 bits as it holds them, and its alpha, where it has one, kept as a soft mask. Fails `invalid`.
