- `function draw_image(@doc: Document, id: ImageId, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64)`, called `pdf.draw_image(@doc, id, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height)`: Draws the image `id` stretched to the rectangle whose bottom left corner is at (`x`, `y`).
- `function add_link(@doc: Document, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64, url: str)`, called `pdf.add_link(@doc, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height, url)`: Makes the rectangle whose bottom left corner is at (`x`, `y`) open `url` when clicked.
- `function add_page_link(@doc: Document, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, height: f64, page: i64, top: f64)`, called `pdf.add_page_link(@doc, x: x, y: y, width: width, height: height, page, top: top)`: Makes the rectangle whose bottom left corner is at (`x`, `y`) go to a page of the document when clicked.
- `function add_bookmark(@doc: Document, title: str, level: i64, top: f64)`, called `pdf.add_bookmark(@doc, title, level, top)`: Adds a bookmark to the document's outline that goes to the page drawn on.
- `function encode(doc: Document lent) -> [u8]?`, called `pdf.encode(doc)`: The bytes of `doc` as a PDF 1.7 file: its pages, their content, fonts, images, links and bookmarks, its information, and a cross-reference table. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Limits(objects: i64, stream_bytes: i64, total_bytes: i64, depth: i64, pages: i64, revisions: i64)`: The limits a file is read under, so that a small file cannot cost a program more than its caller allows.
- `function default_limits() -> Limits`, called `pdf.default_limits()`: The usual limits: a million objects, streams of 256 MiB, 1 GiB decoded by one call, values nested 256 deep, 100,000 pages and 1,000 revisions.
- `record File(state: store.Store)`: A PDF file read: its objects, its trailer and its pages.
- `record Object(state: model.Obj)`: A value of a PDF file: a null, a boolean, a number, a string, a name, an array, a dictionary, a stream or a reference to another object.
- `variant Kind = .null_value | .boolean | .integer | .real | .text | .name | .array | .dictionary | .stream | .reference`: The kinds of an `Object`.
- `record Reference(number: i64, generation: i64)`: A reference to an object of a file, `12 0 R`.
- `record Box(left: f64, bottom: f64, right: f64, top: f64)`: A rectangle of a page, in points.
- `record Page(index: i64, media_box: Box, crop_box: Box, bleed_box: Box, trim_box: Box, art_box: Box, rotation: i64, object: Object)`: A page of a file read.
- `record TextPiece(text: str, x: f64, y: f64, width: f64, size: f64, font: str)`: A run of text drawn on a page, where it stands and how large.
- `variant Target = .page(index: i64, top: f64) | .url(address: str) | .other`: Where a bookmark or a link goes.
- `record Bookmark(title: str, level: i64, target: Target)`: A bookmark of a file's outline.
- `record Link(area: Box, target: Target)`: A link of a page.
- `function decode(data: [u8], password: str, limits: Limits) -> File?`, called `pdf.decode(data, password, limits)`: The file `data` holds, read whole: its cross-reference sections, each revision's, followed back from the newest, its object streams opened, its page tree walked; a cross-reference that does not match its file rebuilt from the objects themselves, as readers of PDF do. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function version_of(f: File) -> str`, called `pdf.version_of(f)`: The version of PDF `f` says it follows: `1.7`, or the catalogue's where it names a later one.
- `function is_encrypted(f: File) -> bool`, called `pdf.is_encrypted(f)`: Whether `f` was encrypted; `decode` has decrypted it.
- `function pages_of(f: File) -> [Page]`, called `pdf.pages_of(f)`: The pages of `f`, in order.
- `function text_of(f: File, page: Page) -> str?`, called `pdf.text_of(f, page)`: The text of `page`: its pieces in the order the page draws them, a space between two pieces apart on one line, a line break where the baseline moves, as `pdftotext` reads it with its `-raw` option. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function pieces_of(f: File, page: Page) -> [TextPiece]?`, called `pdf.pieces_of(f, page)`: The runs of text `page` draws, where each stands, in the order the page draws them. Fails as `text_of` fails.
- `function info_of(f: File) -> {str: str}`, called `pdf.info_of(f)`: The entries of `f`'s information dictionary that hold text, decoded: `Title`, `Author`, `Subject`, `Keywords`, `Creator`, `Producer`, `CreationDate`, `ModDate` and any other.
- `function parse_date(s: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `pdf.parse_date(s)`: The instant a PDF date names: `D:YYYYMMDDHHmmSSOHH'mm'`, every part after the year optional, `Z`, `+` or `-` its offset. Fails `invalid`.
- `function outline_of(f: File) -> [Bookmark]?`, called `pdf.outline_of(f)`: The outline of `f`, its bookmarks depth first: each bookmark, then the ones under it. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function links_of(f: File, page: Page) -> [Link]?`, called `pdf.links_of(f, page)`: The links of `page`, in the order its annotations list them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_text(s: [u8]) -> str`, called `pdf.decode_text(s)`: The text a PDF text string holds: UTF-16BE after its byte order mark, UTF-8 after its mark, PDFDocEncoding otherwise.
- `function encode_text(s: str) -> [u8]`, called `pdf.encode_text(s)`: `s` as a PDF text string: PDFDocEncoding where it holds every character, else UTF-16BE after its byte order mark.
- `function object_of(f: File, number: i64) -> Object`, called `pdf.object_of(f, number)`: The object numbered `number`; the null object where `f` holds none, as PDF reads a reference to nothing.
- `function resolve(f: File, o: Object) -> Object`, called `pdf.resolve(f, o)`: `o` itself, or the object it refers to where it is a reference, the reference after it followed too.
- `function trailer_of(f: File) -> Object`, called `pdf.trailer_of(f)`: The trailer of `f`, the newest revision's: `Root`, `Info`, `ID`, `Size`.
- `function catalog_of(f: File) -> Object`, called `pdf.catalog_of(f)`: The catalogue of `f`, its root: `Pages`, `Outlines`, `Names`.
- `function kind_of(o: Object) -> Kind`, called `pdf.kind_of(o)`: The kind of `o`.
- `function bool_of(o: Object) -> bool?`, called `pdf.bool_of(o)`: The value of the boolean `o`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function int_of(o: Object) -> i64?`, called `pdf.int_of(o)`: The value of the integer `o`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function number_of(o: Object) -> f64?`, called `pdf.number_of(o)`: The value of the number `o`, integer or real. Fails `invalid`.
- `function bytes_of(o: Object) -> [u8]?`, called `pdf.bytes_of(o)`: The bytes of the string `o`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function name_of(o: Object) -> str?`, called `pdf.name_of(o)`: The name `o` holds, without its slash: its bytes as text where they are UTF-8, else each byte past 0x7e or below 0x21 written `#XX`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function items_of(o: Object) -> [Object]?`, called `pdf.items_of(o)`: The items of the array `o`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function entry_of(o: Object, key: str) -> Object?`, called `pdf.entry_of(o, key)`: The entry `key` of the dictionary or stream `o`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function keys_of(o: Object) -> [str]?`, called `pdf.keys_of(o)`: The keys of the dictionary or stream `o`, in the order the file writes them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function reference_of(o: Object) -> Reference?`, called `pdf.reference_of(o)`: The reference `o` is. Fails `invalid`.
- `function stream_data_of(f: File, o: Object) -> [u8]?`, called `pdf.stream_data_of(f, o)`: The bytes of the stream `o`, its filters undone: FlateDecode, LZWDecode (with their predictors), ASCIIHexDecode, ASCII85Decode and RunLengthDecode. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function raw_stream_of(o: Object) -> [u8]?`, called `pdf.raw_stream_of(o)`: The bytes of the stream `o` as the file holds them, decrypted but not decoded: a JPEG image's bytes are a JPEG file. Fails `invalid`.
- `function noto() -> Font`, called `pdf.noto()`: The sample font as a face made by `load_font`.


### ipc

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/ipc`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ipc/).

Communication between the processes of one machine: a local channel by name, read and written as an `io.Stream`, and messages whole over one; memory shared by name, read and written by copies; a semaphore and a lock between processes, named, every wait with a bound.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A name that names nothing: no memory, semaphore or lock of that name, a Windows pipe no listener has, or memory its maker has not sized yet.
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"file_not_found"`: A path that names nothing: no file at the path a connect is given, or no folder where a listener's socket file would be made; the language's own code for it.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: A name taken already: a file at a listener's path, a listener on a name, memory or a semaphore of that name, on Windows an object of any kind.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The system refuses this to the program: the name's permission is another's, or a lock's file is no regular file of one name.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument outside what the function reads: a name outside the rule, a path longer than a socket's address holds, a path a connect is given where something stands that is no socket and no folder (a file, a FIFO, a device), a size or an offset outside the memory, a time below zero, a message past its most, a lock asked again or released by a thread that does not hold it.
- `constant IS_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `"is_a_directory"`: A folder is at the path a connect is given, where a listener's socket file would be.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The listener, memory, semaphore or lock is closed, or the channel's other end is gone, or it ended before a whole message, or nothing listens where a connect asks: a socket file a process that died left, an abstract name no listener has.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The bound a wait was given passed first.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while a call waited.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The process or the machine has no descriptor, handle, memory or room left.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This platform has no such thing: an abstract name off Linux, a named pipe off Windows.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the other codes names; the message carries the system's own number.
- `function is_name(name: str) -> bool`, called `ipc.is_name(name)`: Whether `name` is a name of memory, a semaphore, a lock, an abstract channel or a pipe: 1 to 29 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, the first no `.`.
- `record Listener(handle: hero_ipc.Listener, name: str, space: Space)`: A channel's listener, which `listen`, `listen_abstract` and `listen_pipe` make and `close_listener` closes.
- `variant Space = .path | .abstract | .pipe`: Where a channel's name lives.
- `function listen(path: str, permission: i64) -> Listener?`, called `ipc.listen(path, permission)`: A listener on the socket file it makes at `path`, which `close_listener` removes again. Fails `exists`, `invalid`, `file_not_found`, `permission`.
- `function listen_abstract(name: str) -> Listener?`, called `ipc.listen_abstract(name)`: A listener on `name` in Linux's abstract space, which no file holds and which ends with the listener. Fails `unsupported`, `exists`, `invalid`.
- `function listen_pipe(name: str) -> Listener?`, called `ipc.listen_pipe(name)`: A listener on the Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\` and `name`, which takes clients of this machine alone and one `accept` at a time. Fails `unsupported`, `exists`, `invalid`.
- `function accept(l: Listener, within: time.Duration) -> io.Stream?`, called `ipc.accept(l, within)`: The next connection on `l`, as a stream the caller closes with `io.close`. Fails `timeout`, `closed`, `stopped`, `invalid`.
- `function connect(path: str, within: time.Duration) -> io.Stream?`, called `ipc.connect(path, within)`: A connection to the listener at `path`, as a stream the caller closes with `io.close`. Fails `file_not_found`, `closed`, `is_a_directory`, `invalid`, `timeout`, `permission`.
- `function connect_abstract(name: str, within: time.Duration) -> io.Stream?`, called `ipc.connect_abstract(name, within)`: A connection to the listener on `name` in Linux's abstract space, as `connect` answers one. Fails `unsupported`, `closed`.
- `function connect_pipe(name: str, within: time.Duration) -> io.Stream?`, called `ipc.connect_pipe(name, within)`: A connection to the Windows named pipe `\\.\pipe\` and `name`, as `connect` answers one. Fails `unsupported`, `not_found`.
- `function close_listener(@l: Listener) -> ()?`, called `ipc.close_listener(@l)`: Closes `l` and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`; an `accept` another thread waits in ends within about 50 ms, failing `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function set_deadline(s: io.Stream, deadline: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `ipc.set_deadline(s, deadline)`: Makes every later and waiting read and write of the channel `s` end by `deadline` from now, failing `timeout`: a time, not a span. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function close_write(s: io.Stream) -> ()?`, called `ipc.close_write(s)`: Closes the writing side of the channel `s`, so its peer reads its end once the bytes written are read, while `s` still reads what the peer writes. Fails `unsupported`, `closed`, `invalid`.
- `record Peer(pid: i64, uid: i64)`: Who is at the other end of a channel, as the system told it when the connection was made.
- `function peer_of(s: io.Stream) -> Peer?`, called `ipc.peer_of(s)`: Who is at the other end of the channel `s`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function write_message(s: io.Stream, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `ipc.write_message(s, data)`: Writes `data` to `s` as one message, its length before it, so the reader reads it whole with `read_message`: the length in 4 bytes, big-endian, or for one past 2,147,483,647 bytes the 4 bytes 0xff and the length in 8, as Python's `multiprocessing.connection` writes `send_bytes`, so either reads the other's. Fails as `io.write` fails, with its code.
- `function read_message(s: io.Stream, most: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `ipc.read_message(s, most)`: The next message `write_message` wrote to the other end of `s`, whole. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `record Memory(handle: hero_ipc.Memory, name: str, size: i64)`: Memory shared by name, mapped into this process, which `create_memory` and `open_memory` answer and `close_memory` closes.
- `function create_memory(name: str, size: i64, permission: i64) -> Memory?`, called `ipc.create_memory(name, size: size, permission: permission)`: New memory named `name`, every byte zero, mapped into this process. Fails `exists`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function open_memory(name: str) -> Memory?`, called `ipc.open_memory(name)`: The memory named `name`, made by this or any process, mapped into this one. Fails `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function read_at(m: Memory, offset: i64, count: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `ipc.read_at(m, offset: offset, count: count)`: A copy of `count` bytes of `m` from `offset`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function write_at(m: Memory, offset: i64, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `ipc.write_at(m, offset, data)`: Copies `data` into `m` at `offset`. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function load_at(m: Memory, offset: i64) -> i64?`, called `ipc.load_at(m, offset)`: The `i64` at `offset` of `m`, read whole by one instruction every process sees whole, with no lock. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function store_at(m: Memory, offset: i64, value: i64) -> ()?`, called `ipc.store_at(m, offset: offset, value: value)`: Makes the `i64` at `offset` of `m` `value`, written whole as `load_at` reads one. Fails as `load_at` does.
- `function add_at(m: Memory, offset: i64, delta: i64) -> i64?`, called `ipc.add_at(m, offset: offset, delta: delta)`: Adds `delta` to the `i64` at `offset` of `m` in one step no other process divides, and answers the sum. Fails as `load_at` does.
- `function swap_at(m: Memory, offset: i64, expected: i64, desired: i64) -> i64?`, called `ipc.swap_at(m, offset: offset, expected: expected, desired: desired)`: Makes the `i64` at `offset` of `m` `desired` where it is `expected`, in one step no other process divides, and answers the word it found: the swap was made where that is `expected`. Fails as `load_at` does.
- `function close_memory(@m: Memory) -> ()?`, called `ipc.close_memory(@m)`: Unmaps `m` from this process and empties the place, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function remove_memory(name: str) -> ()?`, called `ipc.remove_memory(name)`: Takes the name `name` from its memory, so no later `open_memory` finds it and `create_memory` may take it again; who has it open keeps it until they close it. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `record Semaphore(handle: hero_ipc.Semaphore, name: str)`: A semaphore shared by name: a count that `release_semaphore` raises and `acquire_semaphore` lowers, waiting while it is 0.
- `function create_semaphore(name: str, count: i64, permission: i64) -> Semaphore?`, called `ipc.create_semaphore(name, count: count, permission: permission)`: A new semaphore named `name`, counting `count`. Fails `exists`, `invalid`.
- `function open_semaphore(name: str) -> Semaphore?`, called `ipc.open_semaphore(name)`: The semaphore named `name`, made by this or any process. Fails `not_found`, `permission`.
- `function acquire_semaphore(s: Semaphore, within: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `ipc.acquire_semaphore(s, within)`: Takes one from the count of `s`, waiting while it is 0. Fails `timeout`, `stopped`, `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function release_semaphore(s: Semaphore) -> ()?`, called `ipc.release_semaphore(s)`: Adds one to the count of `s`, letting one waiter through. Fails `limit`, `closed`.
- `function close_semaphore(@s: Semaphore) -> ()?`, called `ipc.close_semaphore(@s)`: Closes `s` in this process and empties the place; the semaphore stays as `close_memory` says memory stays. Fails `closed`.
- `function remove_semaphore(name: str) -> ()?`, called `ipc.remove_semaphore(name)`: Takes the name `name` from its semaphore, as `remove_memory` does for memory, Windows' rule the same. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `record Lock(handle: hero_ipc.Lock, name: str)`: A lock shared by name, held by one thread of one process at a time, which `open_lock` answers and `close_lock` closes; every copy reaches the same lock.
- `variant Acquired = .clean | .abandoned`: How `acquire_lock` took a lock.
- `function open_lock(name: str, permission: i64) -> Lock?`, called `ipc.open_lock(name, permission)`: The lock named `name`, made where no process has it yet. Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function acquire_lock(l: Lock, within: time.Duration) -> Acquired?`, called `ipc.acquire_lock(l, within)`: Takes `l` for the calling thread, waiting while another holds it, and answers how. Fails `timeout`, `invalid`, `stopped`, `closed`.
- `function release_lock(l: Lock) -> ()?`, called `ipc.release_lock(l)`: Releases `l`, held by the calling thread. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function close_lock(@l: Lock) -> ()?`, called `ipc.close_lock(@l)`: Closes `l` in this process and empties the place, releasing it first where the calling thread holds it. Fails `closed`.
- `function remove_lock(name: str) -> ()?`, called `ipc.remove_lock(name)`: Takes the name `name` from its lock: on POSIX its file is removed, so a process that opens the name later has another lock than one that has it open; remove a lock once no process uses it. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.


### audio

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/audio`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/audio/).

Sound for a program: frames of samples held in memory, converted between encodings, channel counts and rates, read from WAV files and written to them; and the system's devices, listed with their formats, a sound played on one and frames recorded from one, paused, resumed, stopped and its end told, a stream waited on in a `poll.Set`, the microphone's permission asked, and the system's beep.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an argument the call refuses: a format whose rate, channels or channel mask is out of its range, a sound whose bytes are no whole number of frames, bytes that are no WAV file, a length below zero.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a WAV file of a kind this package does not read: a compressed encoding, RIFX, a float of another width; and of a machine with no sound system this package reaches.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a device that is not there: `default_output` and `default_input` where the system names none, `open` where an identifier names no device.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a microphone the person refused this program, or has not been asked for: `open` and `ask_permission` fail with it.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a stream past what the layer holds, or a system with no memory, thread or descriptor left: `open`, `open_with`, `play` and `add_to` fail with it.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a wait whose limit passed: `write`, `finish`, `read`, `wait` and `ask_permission` fail with it.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The code of a wait the program's stop ended: `write`, `read`, `wait` and `ask_permission` fail with it.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a stream that is closed, has ended, or whose device went away: every function that takes a `Stream` fails with it.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of a refusal of the system's that no other code names, its words in the message: every function that reaches a device fails with it.
- `constant MAX_RATE: i64`, value `2147483647`: The most frames a second a format may have, the largest `i32`: past every rate a device runs at and every rate a radio's recording is kept at.
- `constant MAX_CHANNELS: i64`, value `65535`: The most channels a frame may have, the most a WAV file can say.
- `variant Encoding = .pcm8 | .pcm16 | .pcm24 | .pcm32 | .float32 | .float64`: How one sample is written as bytes, little-endian.
- `record Format(encoding: Encoding, rate: i64, channels: i64, speakers: i64)`: What the frames of a sound are: the encoding of a sample, the rate and the channels of a frame, and where each channel's speaker stands.
- `record Sound(format: Format, data: [u8])`: A sound held whole in memory: its format, and its frames one after another, each its channels' samples in order.
- `function width_of(encoding: Encoding) -> i64`, called `audio.width_of(encoding)`: The bytes one sample of `encoding` takes.
- `function frames_of(s: Sound) -> i64`, called `audio.frames_of(s)`: The frames of `s`: its bytes divided by a frame's.
- `function duration_of(s: Sound) -> time.Duration`, called `audio.duration_of(s)`: How long `s` plays at its rate: its frames over its rate, cut to the nanosecond below.
- `function to_samples(s: Sound) -> [f64]?`, called `audio.to_samples(s)`: The samples of `s`, interleaved as its frames hold them, each a number from -1 to 1: an integer sample divided by 2 to the power of its bits less one, around its zero, so the most negative is exactly -1 and the most positive one step short of 1; a float as it stands, past 1, a NaN or an infinity included. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_samples(format: Format, values: [f64]) -> Sound?`, called `audio.from_samples(format, values)`: A sound of `format` whose samples are `values`, interleaved, written as `format.encoding` writes them: an integer encoding takes the nearest step, ties to the even one, a value past -1 or 1 held there and a NaN silent; a float takes the value as it stands, `float32` rounded to the nearest. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_encoding(s: Sound, encoding: Encoding) -> Sound?`, called `audio.to_encoding(s, encoding)`: `s` with its samples written in `encoding`, each as `from_samples` writes it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_channels(s: Sound, channels: i64) -> Sound?`, called `audio.to_channels(s, channels)`: `s` with frames of `channels` channels, frame for frame: the mean of every channel where one is asked; the one channel in each where `s` has one; a fold where two are asked of more, each channel taken by where its speaker stands (`Format.speakers`), the front pair whole, a centre and the surrounds 3 dB down into the side they stand on, both sides for one in the middle, the low-frequency channel left out, and the whole scaled so a frame full in every channel stays full; and else each channel kept in its place, a channel added silent and one past the count left out. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_rate(s: Sound, rate: i64) -> Sound?`, called `audio.to_rate(s, rate)`: `s` at `rate` frames a second, by band-limited interpolation: a sinc under a Kaiser window, its cutoff at 95% of the lower rate's Nyquist frequency, so what the new rate cannot hold is let go, never folded back. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_format(s: Sound, format: Format) -> Sound?`, called `audio.to_format(s, format)`: `s` in `format`: its channels as `to_channels` makes them, then its rate as `to_rate` does, then its encoding, every step on the samples as numbers, so no step rounds to an integer between two others; and `format`'s channel mask. Fails `invalid`.
- `function silence(format: Format, length: time.Duration) -> Sound?`, called `audio.silence(format, length)`: A sound of `format` that is silent for `length`: every sample zero, 128 for `pcm8`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function tone(format: Format, hz: f64, amplitude: f64, length: time.Duration) -> Sound?`, called `audio.tone(format, hz: hz, amplitude: amplitude, length)`: A sound of `format` that is a sine of `hz` for `length`, the same in every channel, starting at zero and rising: frame `k` is `amplitude` times the sine of 2 pi `hz` `k` over the rate. Fails `invalid`.
- `function decode_wav(data: [u8]) -> Sound?`, called `audio.decode_wav(data)`: The sound the WAV file `data` holds: integer PCM of 1 to 32 bits a sample, in the fewest whole bytes that hold them, and IEEE floats of 32 and 64 bits, any number of channels, under a plain `fmt ` chunk or WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE, in a RIFF or an RF64 file. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_wav(s: Sound) -> [u8]?`, called `audio.encode_wav(s)`: The bytes of a WAV file holding `s`: a plain `fmt ` chunk for 8 and 16-bit integers and for floats in one or two channels with no channel mask, WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE for the rest, as Microsoft asks; a `fact` chunk with the frame count for floats and the extensible form; RF64 where the file would pass what a 32-bit size holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_wav(path: str) -> Sound?`, called `audio.read_wav(path)`: The sound the WAV file at `path` holds, as `decode_wav` reads it. Fails as `fs.read_bytes` does where the file cannot be read, and as `decode_wav` does on what it holds.
- `function write_wav(path: str, s: Sound) -> ()?`, called `audio.write_wav(path, s)`: Writes `s` as a WAV file at `path`, as `encode_wav` makes it, replacing the file that stood there. Fails as `encode_wav` does on `s`, and as `fs.write_bytes` does where the file cannot be written.
- `record WavReader(stream: io.Stream, format: Format, frames_left: i64)`: A WAV file read from a stream a piece at a time: its frames' format and how many are still to come, the stream standing at the next.
- `record WavWriter(stream: io.Stream, format: Format, frames: i64)`: A WAV file written to a stream a piece at a time: its frames' format and how many were written.
- `function wav_reader(s: io.Stream) -> WavReader?`, called `audio.wav_reader(s)`: A reader of the WAV file `s` holds, its chunks read in order up to its first frame, so its frames are read as the program asks, by `read_frames`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function read_frames(@r: WavReader, frames: i64) -> Sound?`, called `audio.read_frames(@r, frames)`: Up to `frames` of the next frames of `r`, fewer where the file ends first, none once it has. Fails `invalid`.
- `function wav_writer(s: io.Stream, format: Format) -> WavWriter?`, called `audio.wav_writer(s, format)`: A writer of a WAV file of `format` on `s`, its header written with its sizes unknown, which a reader reads to the end, until `finish_wav` writes them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_frames(@w: WavWriter, s: Sound) -> ()?`, called `audio.write_frames(@w, s)`: Writes the frames of `s` after those `w` wrote. Fails `invalid`.
- `function finish_wav(w: WavWriter) -> ()?`, called `audio.finish_wav(w)`: Finishes the file `w` wrote: its pad byte, and its header written again with its sizes, as RF64 where 32 bits cannot hold them; the stream is left at its end. Fails where `io.write` or `io.seek` fails, with its code: a stream that cannot seek, a pipe, keeps the sizes unknown, which `decode_wav` and `wav_reader` read to the end.
- `constant NULL_DEVICE: str`, value `"heroes:null"`: The identifier of the null device, which `null_device` gives.
- `variant Direction = .output | .input`: Which way a device's frames go.
- `record Device(id: str, name: str, direction: Direction, is_default: bool, format: Format)`: A device of the system's, or the null device, as `devices` lists it.
- `function system() -> str?`, called `audio.system()`: The name of the sound system this machine's devices are reached through: "CoreAudio" on macOS, "WASAPI" on Windows, and on Linux "PulseAudio" or "PipeWire", as the server reached names itself. Fails `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function devices() -> [Device]?`, called `audio.devices()`: Every output and input device the system has, each with the format it runs at, in the system's order. Fails `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function default_output() -> Device?`, called `audio.default_output()`: The device the system plays on when nothing else is asked. Fails `not_found`.
- `function default_input() -> Device?`, called `audio.default_input()`: The device the system records from when nothing else is asked. Fails `not_found`.
- `function null_device(direction: Direction, format: Format) -> Device`, called `audio.null_device(direction, format)`: The null device of `direction` at `format`: an output that plays nothing, at its stream's rate, and an input that records a sine of 440 Hz at half the full scale in every channel, frame `k` being 0.5 times the sine of 2 pi 440 `k` over the rate, rounded to an `f32`.
- `constant BUFFER_MS: i64`, value `500`: The span of frames a stream holds between the program and the device when `open` makes it: half a second.
- `record Stream(handle: hero_audio.Stream, device: Device, format: Format, pending: [f32], rates: resample.Resampler)`: Frames on their way to a device or from one: an output plays the sounds the program writes, an input records the sounds the program reads.
- `variant State = .running | .paused | .ended | .lost`: What a stream is doing.
- `function open(device: Device, format: Format) -> Stream?`, called `audio.open(device, format)`: A stream on `device` of sounds of `format`, started, holding `BUFFER_MS` of frames between the program and the device. Fails as `open_with` does.
- `function open_with(device: Device, format: Format, buffer: time.Duration) -> Stream?`, called `audio.open_with(device, format, buffer)`: A stream as `open` makes it, holding `buffer` of frames between the program and the device: a longer one plays on through a program's pause and records on while it does not read, and a shorter one plays a written sound sooner. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `not_found`, `permission`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function play(device: Device, s: Sound) -> Stream?`, called `audio.play(device, s)`: An output on `device` playing `s` whole, finished, so its end is told once it has played: `wait` waits for it, `pause`, `resume` and `stop` change it, and `close` ends it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write(@stream: Stream, s: Sound, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `audio.write(@stream, s, limit)`: Writes `s` to the output `s`'s device, converted to its format, waiting up to `limit` for room as the device plays. Fails `timeout`, `invalid`, `closed`, `stopped`.
- `function finish(@stream: Stream, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `audio.finish(@stream, limit)`: Says that no more sounds will be written to the output `stream`: the frames it still holds are handed to the device, waiting up to `limit` for room, and its end is told once the device has played them. Fails `timeout`, `limit`.
- `function read(@stream: Stream, limit: time.Duration) -> Sound?`, called `audio.read(@stream, limit)`: The frames the input `stream` has recorded since the last read, as a sound of its format, waiting up to `limit` for the first. Fails `timeout`, `limit`, `closed`, `invalid`, `stopped`.
- `function wait(stream: Stream, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `audio.wait(stream, limit)`: Waits up to `limit` for `stream` to end: an output finished and played out, or a stream stopped. Fails `timeout`, `closed`, `stopped`.
- `function pause(stream: Stream) -> ()?`, called `audio.pause(stream)`: Pauses `stream`: it keeps its frames, an output plays nothing and an input records nothing until `resume`. Fails `closed`, `failed`.
- `function resume(stream: Stream) -> ()?`, called `audio.resume(stream)`: Resumes `stream` where `pause` left it. Fails as `pause` does.
- `function stop(stream: Stream) -> ()?`, called `audio.stop(stream)`: Stops `stream` at once: an output drops the frames it holds and an input records no more, its frames still read. Fails `closed`.
- `function set_volume(stream: Stream, volume: f64) -> ()?`, called `audio.set_volume(stream, volume)`: Sets the gain every sample of `stream` is multiplied by on its way. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function state_of(stream: Stream) -> State?`, called `audio.state_of(stream)`: What `stream` is doing. Fails `closed`.
- `function position_of(stream: Stream) -> time.Duration?`, called `audio.position_of(stream)`: How much of `stream` the device has taken (an output) or given (an input) since it opened, at the device's rate: what has been played or recorded, silence played for want of frames not counted. Fails `closed`.
- `function dropped_of(stream: Stream) -> i64?`, called `audio.dropped_of(stream)`: The frames, at the device's rate, an input dropped because the program did not read them in time, or an output played as silence while running with nothing written and not finished. Fails `closed`.
- `function close(@stream: Stream) -> ()?`, called `audio.close(@stream)`: Closes `stream` and empties the place it is handed: the device's stream ended, an output's frames not yet played dropped. Fails `closed`.
- `function add_to(set: poll.Set, stream: Stream) -> i64?`, called `audio.add_to(set, stream)`: Adds `stream` to the set `set` and answers the entry's key: a wait on the set tells the key readable while an output has room for a frame or an input holds one, and once either has ended. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function ask_permission(limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `audio.ask_permission(limit)`: Asks whether this program may record from a microphone, and where the person has not been asked yet, asks them, the system showing its own dialog, waiting up to `limit` for their answer. Fails `permission`, `timeout`, `stopped`.
- `function beep() -> ()?`, called `audio.beep()`: Sounds the system's alert, the one the person chose where the system lets them, and answers without waiting for it to end. Fails `unsupported`, `failed`.


### mdns

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/mdns`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/mdns/).

Multicast DNS (RFC 6762) and DNS-based service discovery (RFC 6763): the devices, printers and peers of the local network found by name, and a program's own service made known to them.

- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `failure.NOT_FOUND`: A name that names nothing found in the time given, an instance not published, or an interface that does not exist.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `failure.INVALID`: A service type, an instance name, a host name, an attribute, a port or a number is not what the function takes; the message says which.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `failure.NOT_TEXT`: A label heard is not UTF-8.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `failure.EXISTS`: The service's instance name is published already.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `failure.LIMIT`: The names tried for a service were all held by other hosts.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `failure.UNSUPPORTED`: The platform has no such thing.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `failure.FAILED`: The system refused: a socket, a group, a send; the message carries its words.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `failure.TIMEOUT`: Nothing happened in the time given.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `failure.STOPPED`: The program was asked to stop while the call waited.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `failure.CLOSED`: A browser or a responder used after it was closed.
- `record Attribute(key: str, value: [u8]?)`: One attribute of a service, a key and, where it has one, a value (RFC 6763 § 6).
- `record Service(instance: str, type: str, subtypes: [str], host: str, port: i64, priority: i64, weight: i64, addresses: [net.Host], attributes: [Attribute])`: One instance of a service: what a browse finds, and what `publish` takes.
- `function service(instance: str, type: str, port: i64) -> Service`, called `mdns.service(instance: instance, type: type, port)`: A service to publish: `instance` of `type` on `port`, the machine's own host name and addresses, no attributes and no subtypes.
- `function name_of(s: Service) -> str?`, called `mdns.name_of(s)`: The name `s` goes by in the records, `Joe's Printer._ipp._tcp.local.`, a dot or a backslash in the instance written after a backslash. Fails `invalid`.
- `function attribute_of(attributes: [Attribute], key: str) -> [u8]?`, called `mdns.attribute_of(attributes, key)`: The value of the attribute `key` of `attributes`, its key compared without regard to case. Fails `not_found`.
- `function decode_attributes(texts: [[u8]]) -> [Attribute]`, called `mdns.decode_attributes(texts)`: The attributes the strings of a TXT record hold (RFC 6763 § 6): `key=value`, `key=` and `key`.
- `function encode_attributes(attributes: [Attribute]) -> [[u8]]?`, called `mdns.encode_attributes(attributes)`: The strings of the TXT record that holds `attributes`: the one empty string where there are none, as RFC 6763 § 6.1 asks. Fails `invalid`.
- `function browse(type: str, wait: time.Duration, interfaces: [str]) -> [Service]?`, called `mdns.browse(type, wait, interfaces)`: The instances of the service type `type` found on the network, each with its host, port, addresses and attributes. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `failed`, `stopped`.
- `function browse_types(wait: time.Duration, interfaces: [str]) -> [str]?`, called `mdns.browse_types(wait, interfaces)`: The service types offered on the network, as `_ipp._tcp` (RFC 6763 § 9). Fails as `browse` fails.
- `function resolve(instance: str, type: str, wait: time.Duration, interfaces: [str]) -> Service?`, called `mdns.resolve(instance: instance, type: type, wait, interfaces)`: The instance `instance` of `type`, with its host, port, addresses and attributes, asked for and waited for until its addresses are known. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `function lookup_addresses(name: str, wait: time.Duration, interfaces: [str]) -> [net.Host]?`, called `mdns.lookup_addresses(name, wait, interfaces)`: The addresses of the host `name` under `local.`, asked for and waited for until one is heard. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function lookup_reverse(address: net.Host, wait: time.Duration, interfaces: [str]) -> [str]?`, called `mdns.lookup_reverse(address, wait, interfaces)`: The names the host `address` goes by on the network, asked of the network by its reverse name (RFC 6762 § 4). Fails `not_found`.
- `record Watch(state: watching.Watch)`: A browser that keeps listening: it asks for a service type again and again, asks for each record again as its time runs down (RFC 6762 § 5.2), and tells what appears, changes and goes.
- `variant Change = .appeared(service: Service) | .changed(service: Service) | .disappeared(service: Service)`: What `next_change` tells about one instance.
- `function watch(type: str, interfaces: [str]) -> Watch?`, called `mdns.watch(type, interfaces)`: A browser on the service type `type`, on the interfaces `interfaces` names, the usual ones where it names none. Fails as `browse` fails.
- `function next_change(@w: Watch, wait: time.Duration) -> Change?`, called `mdns.next_change(@w, wait)`: The next change of the instances of the watched type, waiting for one. Fails `timeout`, `stopped`, `failed`, `closed`.
- `function close_watch(@w: Watch) -> ()?`, called `mdns.close_watch(@w)`: Closes the browser's sockets. Fails `closed`, `failed`.
- `record Responder(state: hosting.State)`: A responder: the sockets of a program that publishes services, and the services it publishes.
- `function responder(interfaces: [str]) -> Responder?`, called `mdns.responder(interfaces)`: A responder on the interfaces `interfaces` names, the usual ones where it names none. Fails as `browse` fails.
- `function publish(@r: Responder, s: Service) -> Service?`, called `mdns.publish(@r, s)`: Publishes `s`: its instance and host names are probed for three times, 250 ms apart, and where another host holds either the next name is tried (`Name (2)`, `Name (3)`; `host-2`), then the service is announced twice, a second apart (RFC 6762 §§ 8 and 9). Fails `exists`, `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function serve(@r: Responder, wait: time.Duration) -> [Service]?`, called `mdns.serve(@r, wait)`: Serves for `wait` milliseconds: every query heard about a published service is answered, with what the querier does not hold already, multicast or to the querier alone where it asks that or is a resolver of the old kind. Fails `stopped`, `failed`, `closed`.
- `function update(@r: Responder, s: Service) -> Service?`, called `mdns.update(@r, s)`: Changes what is published about a service already published: its port, priority, weight, addresses and attributes. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function withdraw(@r: Responder, instance: str, type: str) -> ()?`, called `mdns.withdraw(@r, instance: instance, type: type)`: Withdraws the service `instance` of `type`: a goodbye is multicast, which tells every cache to drop it (RFC 6762 § 10.1), and it is answered for no more. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function close_responder(@r: Responder) -> ()?`, called `mdns.close_responder(@r)`: Says goodbye for every service published and closes the responder's sockets. Fails `closed`, `failed`.


### ui

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/ui`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ui/).

Windows holding the system's own widgets, in the manner of wxWidgets: a button is an `NSButton` on macOS, a Win32 button on Windows, a GTK button on Linux, never one this package draws, so a program looks and behaves as the system's own programs do, its keys, its accessibility and its languages included.

- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `failure.CLOSED`: The app is closed, or the widget's life has ended: destroyed, its window or its box destroyed, or its app closed; and a headless app whose injected inputs are spent while no timer runs.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `failure.INVALID`: An argument the call cannot take: a size or a weight outside its range, a text holding a zero byte, a widget of another app or of a kind the call does not set, an index past the items.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `failure.TIMEOUT`: Nothing happened in the time `wait` was given.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `failure.UNSUPPORTED`: The system has no native user interface this package reaches, or the call came from a thread other than `main`'s.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `failure.EXISTS`: A native app is open already in this process.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `failure.LIMIT`: The system has no memory or no room for what was asked.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `failure.FAILED`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names; the message carries its words.
- `constant MOST_SIZE: i64`, value `1000000`: The most points a size, a position, a spacing, a padding or a margin takes, on both axes: a million, past every screen.
- `constant MOST_STRETCH: i64`, value `1000`: The highest weight a widget, a column or a row stretches by.
- `variant Backend = .automatic | .native | .headless`: Which side an app opens on.
- `record App(handle: hero_ui.App, number: i64, native: bool, table: model.Model, icon: desk.Icon, clipboard: Clip, inputs: [Input], events: [Event], answers: [Answer], choices: [Choice], prints: [PrintChoice], shown: [dialogs.Shown], dialogs_made: i64, docked: bool, notices: [desk.Notice], appearance: Appearance, quits_held: i64, identity: str, windowed: bool, claimed: bool, clock: i64, opened: time.Mark)`: An open user interface: its windows, its widgets and their state, made by `open` and ended by `close`.
- `function open(backend: Backend) -> App?`, called `ui.open(backend)`: A new app on `backend`. Fails `unsupported`, `exists`, `limit`.
- `function close(@app: App) -> ()?`, called `ui.close(@app)`: Closes `app`: every window and widget it holds is destroyed, every queue emptied, and the place emptied, so every later call through it fails `closed`. Fails `closed`.
- `function is_native(app: App) -> bool`, called `ui.is_native(app)`: Whether `app` stands on the system's own widgets.
- `record Widget(app: i64, id: i64)`: A widget, a box, a window, a menu, a menu item or a timer of an app: a number its app gave it, which every event about it names.
- `variant Kind = .window | .row | .column | .grid | .label | .button | .text_field | .text_area | .checkbox | .radio_group | .list | .combo | .progress | .slider | .picture | .menu | .menu_item | .menu_separator | .timer | .webview | .tabs | .page | .scrolled | .split | .pane | .table | .tree | .context_menu | .tray | .separator | .group | .editable_combo | .spin | .toolbar | .status_bar | .date_picker | .time_picker | .date_time_picker | .color_well | .font_button | .canvas | .calendar`: What a widget is.
- `function kind_of(app: App, widget: Widget) -> Kind?`, called `ui.kind_of(app, widget)`: What `widget` is. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function destroy(@app: App, widget: Widget) -> ()?`, called `ui.destroy(@app, widget)`: Destroys `widget` and everything it holds: a window's widgets and menus, a box's widgets, a menu's items; a timer stops. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `record Rect(x: i64, y: i64, width: i64, height: i64)`: A rectangle in a window's content, or a page's, a scrolled box's or a pane's, in points from its top-left corner, the y axis down.
- `function rect_of(@app: App, widget: Widget) -> Rect?`, called `ui.rect_of(@app, widget)`: Where `widget` stands in its window's content, or in the content of the page, scrolled box or pane it stands in, laid out first where anything changed; for a window, its content's size at 0, 0; for a page or a pane, where its tabs or its split shows it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function window(@app: App, title: str, width: i64, height: i64) -> Widget?`, called `ui.window(@app, title, width: width, height: height)`: A new window, titled `title`, its content `width` by `height` points or what it needs if that is more. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `function set_size(@app: App, widget: Widget, width: i64, height: i64) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_size(@app, widget, width: width, height: height)`: Gives window `widget` a content of `width` by `height` points, or what it needs if that is more. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function set_resizable(@app: App, widget: Widget, on: bool) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_resizable(@app, widget, on)`: Lets the person resize window `widget`, or keeps its size. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `record Screen(area: Rect, work: Rect, scale: i64)`: A screen of the system: its whole area and its work area, the whole less the menu bar, the Dock or the task bar, in the desktop's points, whose origin is the top-left corner of the system's main screen and whose y axis goes down; and its scale.
- `record Frame(screen: i64, x: i64, y: i64, width: i64, height: i64)`: Where a window stands: the screen it stands on most, and its frame on that screen, its title bar and its border included.
- `variant WindowState = .normal | .minimized | .maximized | .full_screen`: The state a window stands in.
- `variant Backdrop = .plain | .translucent`: What stands behind a window's widgets.
- `function screens(app: App) -> [Screen]?`, called `ui.screens(app)`: Every screen of the system, the main one first (on macOS the one holding the menu bar, on Windows the primary monitor), in the order the system lists them. Fails `closed`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function frame_of(@app: App, widget: Widget) -> Frame?`, called `ui.frame_of(@app, widget)`: Where window `widget` stands: the screen it stands on most and its frame there, laid out and shown first as `wait` would. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_position(@app: App, widget: Widget, screen: i64, x: i64, y: i64) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_position(@app, widget, screen: screen, x: x, y: y)`: Moves window `widget` so its frame's top-left corner stands at `x`, `y` on screen `screen`. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function center(@app: App, widget: Widget) -> ()?`, called `ui.center(@app, widget)`: Centres window `widget` in the work area of the screen it stands on. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function center_over(@app: App, widget: Widget, over: Widget) -> ()?`, called `ui.center_over(@app, widget: widget, over: over)`: Centres window `widget` over window `over`'s frame, kept within the work area of the screen `over` stands on: a dialog over its document. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_state(@app: App, widget: Widget, to: WindowState) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_state(@app, widget, to)`: Brings window `widget` to `state`, leaving the one it stands in first, and returns once the system has made it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function state_of(app: App, widget: Widget) -> WindowState?`, called `ui.state_of(app, widget)`: The state window `widget` stands in now, as the system holds it, the person's last act included. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_on_top(@app: App, widget: Widget, on: bool) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_on_top(@app, widget, on)`: Keeps window `widget` above every other application's windows, or lets it stand among them, as a new window does. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_framed(@app: App, widget: Widget, on: bool) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_framed(@app, widget, on)`: Gives window `widget` its frame, a title bar with its buttons and a border, as a new window has, or takes them away, its content keeping its size; a window with no frame is moved by a drag on its background. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function set_opacity(@app: App, widget: Widget, opacity: i64) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_opacity(@app, widget, opacity)`: Sets how opaque window `widget` is, its widgets with it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function set_backdrop(@app: App, widget: Widget, backdrop: Backdrop) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_backdrop(@app, widget, backdrop)`: Puts `backdrop` behind window `widget`'s widgets. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_icon(@app: App, img: image.Image) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_icon(@app, img)`: Gives the app its icon: the one the Dock shows on macOS, and every window's and the task bar's on Windows. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_modal(@app: App, widget: Widget, on: bool) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_modal(@app, widget, on)`: Makes window `widget` modal: until the program ends it or destroys the window, the person acts on it alone and the app's other windows take no input, as a dialog of the program's own needs. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function row(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.row(@app, into)`: A new box in `into` that lays its children out side by side, from the left, `model.SPACING` points between two. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function column(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.column(@app, into)`: A new box in `into` that lays its children out one under another, from the top, `model.SPACING` points between two. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function grid(@app: App, into: Widget, columns: i64) -> Widget?`, called `ui.grid(@app, into, columns)`: A new box in `into` that lays its children out in cells, `columns` to a row, row after row; each column as wide as its widest child, each row as high as its highest. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function set_span(@app: App, widget: Widget, columns: i64) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_span(@app, widget, columns)`: Has a child of a grid take `columns` of its columns from its cell rightwards, as wxWidgets' `wxGBSpan` in a `wxGridBagSizer`: a field as wide as a label and its neighbour, a row of buttons under a form. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function tabs(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.tabs(@app, into)`: New tabs in `into`: pages one at a time, each chosen by its tab, as a settings window shows them, wxWidgets' `wxNotebook`. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function page(@app: App, into: Widget, title: str) -> Widget?`, called `ui.page(@app, into, title)`: A new page of tabs `into`, at the end, whose tab reads `title`: a box that lays its children out one under another, as a column does, with a window's padding. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function scrolled(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.scrolled(@app, into)`: A new box in `into` whose content scrolls up and down, as a settings panel longer than its window, wxWidgets' `wxScrolledWindow`: it lays its children out one under another, as a column does, as wide as its inside and as high as they need, and the person scrolls it where they need more than it has. - `function split(@app: App, into: Widget, side_by_side: bool) -> Widget?`, called `ui.split(@app, into, side_by_side)`: A new split in `into`: two panes and the divider between them, which the person drags, as a file manager's sidebar beside its files, wxWidgets' `wxSplitterWindow`. - `function pane(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.pane(@app, into)`: A new pane of split `into`, the first made the left or the top one: a box that lays its children out one under another, as a column does. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.

- `record Fit(stretch: i64, fill: bool, align: Align, min_width: i64, min_height: i64, margin: i64)`: How a widget, or a box, takes room in the box holding it.

- `function set_fit(@app: App, widget: Widget, fit: Fit) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_fit(@app, widget, fit)`: Gives `widget` the fit `fit` in the box holding it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function set_spacing(@app: App, box: Widget, spacing: i64, padding: i64) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_spacing(@app, box, spacing: spacing, padding: padding)`: Gives box or window `box` `spacing` points between two of its children and `padding` points inside its edges. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function set_grid_stretch(@app: App, widget: Widget, columns: [i64], rows: [i64]) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_grid_stretch(@app, widget, columns: columns, rows: rows)`: Gives grid `widget`'s columns and rows their weights for the room it has left, one weight a column and one a row, in order. - `function separator(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.separator(@app, into)`: A new separator in `into`, as wxWidgets' `wxStaticLine`: the system's thin line between the widgets of a box, across a column or a window and down a row, filling its box that way. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function group(@app: App, into: Widget, title: str) -> Widget?`, called `ui.group(@app, into, title)`: A new group box in `into`, as wxWidgets' `wxStaticBox`: a frame with `title` above it around the widgets made in it, which it lays out one under another as a column does, in its own content. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function toolbar(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.toolbar(@app, into)`: A new toolbar in window `into`, as wxWidgets' `wxToolBar`: the common commands of a window as a row of controls above its content, drawn by the system. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function status_bar(@app: App, into: Widget) -> Widget?`, called `ui.status_bar(@app, into)`: A new status bar in window `into`, as wxWidgets' `wxStatusBar`: a bar across the foot of the window for a count or a state. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`, `unsupported`.

- `function set_picked(@app: App, widget: Widget, at: time.DateTime) -> ()?`, called `ui.set_picked(@app, widget, at)`: Puts picker `widget` at `at`, as `date_picker` does for a new one; no event comes of it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.

- `function picked_font(app: App, widget: Widget) -> Font?`, called `ui.picked_font(app, widget)`: The font `widget` shows now, as the program put it or the person picked it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.

- `variant Choice = .cancelled | .chosen(paths: [str])`: What the person did in a file dialog.
- `variant PrintChoice = .cancelled | .chosen(settings: printing.Settings)`: What the person did in a print or a page-setup dialog.
- `record Dialog(app: i64, id: i64)`: A dialog an app showed: a message box, a box of the program's words, a file, a folder, a print or a page-setup dialog, which `wait` names in its answer.
- `function message(@app: App, over: Widget, title: str, text: str, tone: Tone, buttons: Buttons) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.message(@app, over, title: title, text: text, tone, buttons)`: Shows a message box over window `over` and answers at once with it, as wxWidgets' `wxMessageDialog::ShowWindowModal` and GTK 4's `gtk_alert_dialog_choose`: the button the person presses comes later from `wait`, `.dialog_answered` naming the box, while the program's timers fire and its other windows answer. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function open_files(@app: App, over: Widget, title: str, filters: [Filter], multiple: bool) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.open_files(@app, over, title, filters, multiple)`: Shows the system's dialog to open files over window `over` and answers at once with it: what the person chooses comes later from `wait`, `.files_chosen` naming the dialog. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function save_file(@app: App, over: Widget, title: str, name: str, filters: [Filter]) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.save_file(@app, over, title: title, name: name, filters)`: Shows the system's dialog to save a file over window `over`, proposing the name `name`, and answers at once with it: the path the person chooses comes later from `wait`, `.files_chosen` naming the dialog. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function open_folders(@app: App, over: Widget, title: str, multiple: bool) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.open_folders(@app, over, title, multiple)`: Shows the system's dialog to choose a folder over window `over`, as wxWidgets' `wxDirDialog`, and answers at once with it: the folders the person chooses come later from `wait`, `.files_chosen` naming the dialog. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function print_dialog(@app: App, over: Widget, settings: printing.Settings) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.print_dialog(@app, over, settings)`: Shows the system's print dialog over window `over`, its fields first set from `settings`, as Qt's `QPrintDialog::open` does, and answers at once with it: the settings the person chooses come later from `wait`, `.print_chosen` naming the dialog, which holds `.cancelled` where they cancelled. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function page_dialog(@app: App, over: Widget, settings: printing.Settings) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.page_dialog(@app, over, settings)`: Shows the system's page-setup dialog (the paper and the orientation) over window `over` the way `print_dialog` shows the print dialog: its fields first set from `settings`, the answer at once with the dialog, the choice later from `wait`, `.print_chosen` naming it. Fails as `print_dialog` does.
- `function add_set(@app: App, set: poll.Set) -> i64?`, called `ui.add_set(@app, set)`: Makes the app's wait watch `set`, so that `wait` ends with `.ready` naming the answer where an entry of the set is ready (a socket readable, a stream at its end, a timer due, a mailbox that holds a value), whichever thread or timer made it so. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `function add_mailbox<T>(@app: App, m: (mailbox T)) -> i64?`, called `ui.add_mailbox(@app, m)`: Makes the app's wait watch the mailbox `m`, so that `wait` ends with `.ready` naming the answer while a receive on it would not wait: a value another thread sent, the mailbox closed or stopped. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`, `failed`. What each call must give its type parameters: `T` reaches no `ptr` and no `cstr`: `(mailbox T)` makes it cross between threads, line 3282; `T` is not `()`: `(mailbox T)` is a mailbox of it, line 3282.
- `function remove_source(@app: App, key: i64) -> ()?`, called `ui.remove_source(@app, key)`: Takes the set or the mailbox `add_set` or `add_mailbox` answered `key` for out of the app's wait; the set stays the program's and the mailbox keeps its values. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function ask(@app: App, over: Widget, title: str, text: str, tone: Tone, buttons: [str], cancel: i64) -> Dialog?`, called `ui.ask(@app, over, title: title, text: text, tone, buttons, cancel)`: Shows a message box over window `over` whose buttons say the program's own words, as "Save", "Don't Save" and "Cancel" before a document closes, and answers at once with it: the button the person presses comes later from `wait`, `.dialog_answered` naming the box, its answer `.button` and the button's index. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function render(@app: App) -> [str]?`, called `ui.render(@app)`: Every window of `app` as text, laid out first where anything changed: a line for each window, then each widget it holds, two spaces deeper for each box or menu around it, in the order made. Fails `closed`.


### ical/vcard

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/ical/vcard`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ical/vcard/).

vCard (RFC 6350, and RFC 2426's version 3.0): a contact read from and written as the `VCARD` components of a document, over the content lines `ical` reads and writes.

- `record Field(group: str?, value: str, types: [str], params: [ical.Param])`: A property with a text value: a telephone number, an address, a title, a note.
- `record Name(group: str?, family: [str], given: [str], additional: [str], prefixes: [str], suffixes: [str], params: [ical.Param])`: The name, `N`: five lists of values, each possibly empty.
- `record Address(group: str?, types: [str], po_box: [str], extended: [str], street: [str], locality: [str], region: [str], postal_code: [str], country: [str], params: [ical.Param])`: An address, `ADR`: seven lists of values, each possibly empty.
- `record Organization(group: str?, name: str, units: [str], params: [ical.Param])`: An organization, `ORG`: a name and the units under it.
- `record Card(version: str, formatted_names: [Field], name: Name?, nicknames: [Field], birthday: Field?, telephones: [Field], emails: [Field], addresses: [Address], organizations: [Organization], titles: [Field], roles: [Field], urls: [Field], notes: [Field], categories: [str], uid: str?, revision: str?, extra: [ical.Line])`: A contact, `VCARD`.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a document that is not a vCard, or has no usable `VERSION`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a version this package does not read, 2.1.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of bytes that are not UTF-8.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a document nested past `ical.MAX_DEPTH`.
- `function parse_cards(text: str) -> [Card]?`, called `vcard.parse_cards(text)`: The cards of a document: every `VCARD` at its top. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_cards(data: [u8]) -> [Card]?`, called `vcard.decode_cards(data)`: The cards of a document read from bytes. Fails `not_text`.
- `function format_cards(contacts: [Card]) -> str?`, called `vcard.format_cards(contacts)`: The cards written as a document. Fails `invalid`.
- `function encode_cards(contacts: [Card]) -> [u8]?`, called `vcard.encode_cards(contacts)`: The cards written as bytes. Fails as `format_cards` does.
- `function card_from(c: ical.Component) -> Card?`, called `vcard.card_from(c)`: The card a `VCARD` component holds. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function card_to(contact: Card) -> ical.Component?`, called `vcard.card_to(contact)`: The component of a card. Fails as `format_cards` does.
- `function card(formatted_name: str) -> Card`, called `vcard.card(formatted_name)`: A card of version 4.0 with a formatted name and nothing else; a program adds what it has, `c.telephones @ [field("+39 06 1234567")]`.
- `function field(value: str) -> Field`, called `vcard.field(value)`: A property with a value and nothing else.


### ssh

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/ssh`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ssh/).

A client of SSH 2 (RFC 4250 to 4254): a server reached, its host key checked against a `known_hosts` file the program names, a sign-in by a key or a password, programs run with their output, errors and exit status, a shell or a subsystem in a terminal or without, and connections forwarded both ways; with SSH's key formats, public key lines, OpenSSH's private key files and `known_hosts` lines, read and written.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: Bytes, a key, a line or a message that are not what they must be, and a host key that changed or is revoked: the readers, `connect`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A host the `known_hosts` file does not name, where the options do not add it: `connect`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: A sign-in, a channel or a request the server refused: the `sign_in_*` functions, `open_session`, `dial`, the requests.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection or the channel is closed: every call on a client.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The wait ran out: every call on a client.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A channel holds 2 MiB of output nobody read: `wait_exit`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A key type, an algorithm or a key file this package does not take.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system failed, its words in the message.
- `record PublicKey(key_type: str, blob: [u8], comment: str)`: A public key as SSH writes it.
- `record PrivateKey(key: keypairs.PrivateKey, public: PublicKey)`: A private key to sign in with, made by `parse_private_key`, `generate_key` or `private_key_of`.
- `variant KeyKind = .ed25519 | .ecdsa_p256 | .ecdsa_p384 | .rsa(bits: i64)`: Which kind of key `generate_key` makes.
- `function parse_public_key(line: str) -> PublicKey?`, called `ssh.parse_public_key(line)`: The public key a line of `authorized_keys` or a `.pub` file holds: a key type, the blob in base 64 and an optional comment. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_public_key(key: PublicKey) -> str`, called `ssh.format_public_key(key)`: `key` as a line of `authorized_keys`: its type, its blob in base 64 and its comment where it has one.
- `function decode_public_key(blob: [u8]) -> PublicKey?`, called `ssh.decode_public_key(blob)`: The public key `blob`, its wire form, holds, with no comment. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fingerprint(key: PublicKey) -> str`, called `ssh.fingerprint(key)`: `key`'s fingerprint as `ssh-keygen -l` prints it: `SHA256:` and the digest of its blob in base 64 with no padding.
- `function fingerprint_md5(key: PublicKey) -> str`, called `ssh.fingerprint_md5(key)`: `key`'s fingerprint as OpenSSH printed it before 6.8: `MD5:` and the digest's bytes in hexadecimal joined by colons.
- `function parse_private_key(text: str) -> PrivateKey?`, called `ssh.parse_private_key(text)`: The private key `text` holds: OpenSSH's own file, `-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----` with no passphrase, or PKCS #8, `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function format_private_key(key: PrivateKey) -> str?`, called `ssh.format_private_key(key)`: `key` written as OpenSSH's own file with no passphrase, as `ssh-keygen` writes one, its comment the public key's. Fails as the system fails to hand the key's bytes.
- `function generate_key(kind: KeyKind, comment: str) -> PrivateKey?`, called `ssh.generate_key(kind, comment)`: A new key of `kind` drawn by the system, with `comment`. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function private_key_of(@key: keypairs.PrivateKey, comment: str) -> PrivateKey?`, called `ssh.private_key_of(@key, comment)`: `key`, a key of `crypto/keypairs`, as a key to sign in with. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function close_key(@key: PrivateKey) -> ()?`, called `ssh.close_key(@key)`: Closes `key`, overwriting its secret. Fails `closed`.
- `function sign(key: PrivateKey, data: [u8]) -> [u8]?`, called `ssh.sign(key, data)`: `key`'s signature of `data` as SSH writes one: the algorithm's name and the signature, Ed25519's, ECDSA's over SHA-256 or SHA-384 by its curve, or RSA's over SHA-512. Fails `closed`.
- `function verify(key: PublicKey, data: [u8], signature: [u8]) -> bool?`, called `ssh.verify(key, data: data, signature: signature)`: Whether `signature`, a signature as SSH writes one, is `key`'s of `data`. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `variant HostKnown = .known | .unknown | .changed(line: i64) | .revoked(line: i64)`: What a `known_hosts` file says of a host's key.
- `function check_known_host(text: str, host: str, port: i64, key: PublicKey) -> HostKnown`, called `ssh.check_known_host(text: text, host: host, port, key)`: What `text`, a `known_hosts` file's contents, says of `key` for `host` at `port`, as OpenSSH reads the file: patterns with `*`, `?` and `!`, `[host]:port` for a port other than 22, hashed names, `@revoked` lines; names compared in lower case.
- `function known_host_line(host: str, port: i64, key: PublicKey, hashed: bool) -> str?`, called `ssh.known_host_line(host, port, key, hashed)`: The line of `known_hosts` that names `key` for `host` at `port`, with no line end. Fails where the system draws no salt.
- `variant UnknownHosts = .refuse | .add | .add_hashed`: What `connect` does with a host its `known_hosts` file does not name.
- `record Options(host: str, port: i64, user: str, known_hosts: str, unknown_hosts: UnknownHosts, wait: time.Duration)`: How a client connects and signs in.
- `function options(host: str, user: str, known_hosts: str) -> Options`, called `ssh.options(host: host, user: user, known_hosts: known_hosts)`: The options to reach `host` on port 22 as `user`, its key checked against `known_hosts`, an unknown host refused, each call waiting 30 seconds.
- `record Client(state: session.Session, user: str)`: A client connected to a server: its transport, its channels, its sign-in.
- `function connect(opts: Options) -> Client?`, called `ssh.connect(opts)`: A client connected to `opts.host`, the server's host key checked against `opts.known_hosts` before anything is sent under the keys agreed, and the sign-in service asked for: the next call signs in. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function fetch_host_key(host: str, port: i64, wait: time.Duration) -> PublicKey?`, called `ssh.fetch_host_key(host, port, wait)`: The host key `host` at `port` presents, fetched by a key exchange and the connection closed: what a program shows a person before adding a host to `known_hosts`, as `ssh-keyscan` does. Fails as `connect` does, never for the key itself.
- `function host_key(c: Client) -> PublicKey`, called `ssh.host_key(c)`: The host key `c`'s server presented and `known_hosts` trusted.
- `function banner(c: Client) -> str`, called `ssh.banner(c)`: The text of the banners the server sent while `c` signed in, empty for none: what a server shows before a login, a warning or a notice.
- `function set_wait(@c: Client, wait: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `ssh.set_wait(@c, wait)`: Sets how long each later call on `c` may wait. Fails `closed`.
- `function close(@c: Client) -> ()?`, called `ssh.close(@c)`: Closes `c`: a DISCONNECT sent, the connection and its keys closed. Fails as closing the connection fails; the client is closed either way.
- `function sign_in_methods(@c: Client) -> [str]?`, called `ssh.sign_in_methods(@c)`: The methods the server takes for `c`'s user, asked by the `none` method; empty where the server let the user in with none, `c` then signed in. Fails as the connection fails.
- `function sign_in_with_key(@c: Client, key: PrivateKey) -> ()?`, called `ssh.sign_in_with_key(@c, key)`: Signs `c` in with `key` by the `publickey` method: the key offered, then the session signed where the server takes it. Fails `permission`.
- `function sign_in_with_password(@c: Client, password: str) -> ()?`, called `ssh.sign_in_with_password(@c, password)`: Signs `c` in with `password` by the `password` method, or by `keyboard-interactive` answering its one hidden prompt where the server takes that alone, as a server checking passwords through PAM does. Fails `permission`.
- `function is_signed_in(c: Client) -> bool`, called `ssh.is_signed_in(c)`: Whether `c` has signed in.
- `record Channel(number: i64)`: A channel of a client: a session, a forwarded connection.
- `record Terminal(term: str, columns: i64, rows: i64)`: A terminal asked for a session (RFC 4254 § 6.2).
- `record Output(output: [u8], errors: [u8], status: i64?, signal: str?)`: What a program run by `run` gave.
- `record Exit(status: i64?, signal: str?)`: How a channel's program ended.
- `function open_session(@c: Client) -> Channel?`, called `ssh.open_session(@c)`: A new session channel of `c`, before any program runs in it: the place to ask a terminal and set variables before `exec`, `shell` or `subsystem`. Fails `permission`.
- `function ask_terminal(@c: Client, channel: Channel, terminal: Terminal) -> ()?`, called `ssh.ask_terminal(@c, channel, terminal)`: Asks a terminal of `terminal`'s type and size for `channel`, before its program starts. Fails `permission`.
- `function set_env(@c: Client, channel: Channel, name: str, value: str) -> ()?`, called `ssh.set_env(@c, channel, name: name, value: value)`: Sets the variable `name` to `value` for `channel`'s program, before it starts. Fails `permission`.
- `function exec(@c: Client, channel: Channel, command: str) -> ()?`, called `ssh.exec(@c, channel, command)`: Runs `command` in `channel`, through the user's shell on the server. Fails `permission`.
- `function shell(@c: Client, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `ssh.shell(@c, channel)`: Starts the user's shell in `channel`. Fails `permission`.
- `function subsystem(@c: Client, channel: Channel, name: str) -> ()?`, called `ssh.subsystem(@c, channel, name)`: Starts the subsystem `name` in `channel`, such as `sftp`. Fails `permission`.
- `function start(@c: Client, command: str) -> Channel?`, called `ssh.start(@c, command)`: A session running `command`, its output to read: `open_session` and `exec` in one call. Fails as `open_session` and `exec` do.
- `function run(@c: Client, command: str) -> Output?`, called `ssh.run(@c, command)`: `command` run to its end with no input: its output, its errors and its exit status, the channel closed. Fails as `start` does.
- `function write(@c: Client, channel: Channel, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `ssh.write(@c, channel, data)`: `data` written to `channel`'s program, waiting while the server's window for it is spent. Fails `closed`.
- `function read(@c: Client, channel: Channel, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `ssh.read(@c, channel, n)`: Up to `n` bytes of `channel`'s output, waiting for one: empty once the server sent its end and nothing is left. Fails `timeout`, `closed`.
- `function read_errors(@c: Client, channel: Channel, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `ssh.read_errors(@c, channel, n)`: Up to `n` bytes of what `channel`'s program wrote to its errors, waiting for one: empty once the server sent its end and nothing is left. Fails as `read` does.
- `function close_write(@c: Client, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `ssh.close_write(@c, channel)`: Tells `channel`'s program that its input has ended: the EOF it reads. Fails as the connection fails.
- `function resize(@c: Client, channel: Channel, terminal: Terminal) -> ()?`, called `ssh.resize(@c, channel, terminal)`: Tells `channel`'s terminal its new size. Fails as the connection fails.
- `function send_signal(@c: Client, channel: Channel, name: str) -> ()?`, called `ssh.send_signal(@c, channel, name)`: Sends the signal `name` to `channel`'s program (RFC 4254 § 6.9), which OpenSSH delivers since 8.0. Fails as the connection fails.
- `function wait_exit(@c: Client, channel: Channel) -> Exit?`, called `ssh.wait_exit(@c, channel)`: Waits until the server closes `channel` and tells how its program ended; its output and errors not read are kept for `read`. Fails `limit`.
- `function close_channel(@c: Client, channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `ssh.close_channel(@c, channel)`: Closes `channel` and waits for the server's close; what it held unread is dropped. Fails as the connection fails.
- `function dial(@c: Client, host: str, port: i64) -> Channel?`, called `ssh.dial(@c, host, port)`: A channel to `host` at `port` as the server reaches them (RFC 4254 § 7.2, `direct-tcpip`): what `ssh -L` forwards one connection through. Fails `permission`.
- `record Forwarded(channel: Channel, origin_host: str, origin_port: i64)`: A connection the server forwarded, accepted.
- `function listen_remote(@c: Client, host: str, port: i64) -> i64?`, called `ssh.listen_remote(@c, host, port)`: Asks the server to listen on `host` at `port` and forward each connection to this client (RFC 4254 § 7.1, `tcpip-forward`): what `ssh -R` asks. Fails `permission`.
- `function accept_remote(@c: Client) -> Forwarded?`, called `ssh.accept_remote(@c)`: The next connection the server forwarded for `listen_remote`, accepted, waiting for one. Fails `timeout`.
- `function cancel_remote(@c: Client, host: str, port: i64) -> ()?`, called `ssh.cancel_remote(@c, host, port)`: Asks the server to stop listening on `host` at `port` for this client. Fails `permission`.


### syslog

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/syslog`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/syslog/).

The system's own log: a daemon's lines where the system keeps its log and its tools read it.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a name, a line or a socket the package refuses.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a log this system does not have.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a socket nothing answers at, or a source nobody registered.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a system that refuses the program: a socket's permission, the registry's.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a log whose queue is full, or a line longer than it takes.
