- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a source registered already.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of any other refusal of the system, its words and number told.
- `constant JOURNAL_SOCKET: str`, value `"/run/systemd/journal/socket"`: The journal's socket, where systemd's journal listens.
- `constant SYSLOG_SOCKET: str`, value `"/dev/log"`: The classic syslog socket.
- `constant NAME_MOST: i64`, value `64`: The most bytes of a name.
- `variant Level = .emergency | .alert | .critical | .error | .warning | .notice | .info | .debug`: How serious a line is: RFC 5424's severities, from the most.
- `variant Destination = .journal | .syslog | .unified_log | .event_log`: Where a log's lines go.
- `record Log(name: str, destination: Destination, socket: str)`: A program's log: the name its lines are filed under and where they go.
- `function level_number(level: Level) -> i64`, called `syslog.level_number(level)`: RFC 5424's number of `level`: 0 for `emergency` to 7 for `debug`.
- `function is_name(name: str) -> bool`, called `syslog.is_name(name)`: Whether `name` is a name lines can be filed under on every system: 1 to 64 bytes of ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.
- `function open(name: str) -> Log?`, called `syslog.open(name)`: The system's log, the lines filed under `name`: the journal on a Linux that runs it, else `/dev/log`; the unified log on macOS; the Event Log on Windows. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function open_socket(name: str, destination: Destination, socket: str) -> Log?`, called `syslog.open_socket(name: name, destination, socket: socket)`: A log whose lines go to the socket at `socket` in the journal's protocol or the syslog line, wherever it stands: a journal in a container, a syslog daemon of the program's own. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_journal(name: str, level: Level, line: str) -> [u8]?`, called `syslog.encode_journal(name: name, level, line: line)`: The bytes of the journal entry one line is, in the journal's native protocol: `MESSAGE`, `PRIORITY`, `SYSLOG_FACILITY` (3, a daemon's) and `SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER`, a line holding a newline in the protocol's binary form. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_syslog(name: str, level: Level, line: str, pid: i64, at: time.DateTime) -> str?`, called `syslog.format_syslog(name: name, level, line: line, pid, at)`: The classic syslog line one line is, as the C library's `syslog(3)` writes it to `/dev/log`: `<PRI>Mmm dd hh:mm:ss name[pid]: line`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write(log: Log, level: Level, line: str) -> ()?`, called `syslog.write(log, level, line)`: Writes `line` to `log` at `level`, never waiting. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `permission`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function install_source(name: str) -> ()?`, called `syslog.install_source(name)`: Registers `name` as a source of the Event Log's Application log, with `EventCreate.exe` as its message file, so the Event Viewer shows each line whole. Fails `invalid`, `exists`, `permission`, `unsupported`.
- `function remove_source(name: str) -> ()?`, called `syslog.remove_source(name)`: Removes what `install_source` registered. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `permission`, `unsupported`.


### service/manage

Layer 5, named `use <rebel>/service/manage`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/service/manage/).

A service of the system installed, started, stopped, asked and removed by another program: a systemd unit, `--user` or the system's, on Linux; a launchd agent of the user's or a daemon of the system's on macOS; a service of the Service Control Manager on Windows.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument out of its range: a name that is not 1 to `NAME_MOST` bytes of ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`; a text holding a zero byte, or a description or a setting systemd reads bare that it would change; a program or a folder that is not absolute; a variable's name that is no name; a restart delay out of range.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: A service of that name is installed or known to the manager already.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No service of that name is installed: no unit or job the manager knows, no file at `path_of`'s path for `remove`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The system refuses the program what the call does: a system service is installed, started and removed by an administrator (root on Linux and macOS).
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The service did not reach the state asked in the span given, or a manager's program did not answer in a minute.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system has no memory left for the call.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This system has no manager this package reaches, or the manager has no form for what is asked: a Linux not booted with systemd, a user's service or a working folder on Windows, a restart at every exit on Windows.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names; the message carries its own words.
- `constant NAME_MOST: i64`, value `247`: The longest service name, in bytes: systemd's longest unit name, 255 bytes with `.service` (measured with systemd 257 on 2026-11-24).
- `constant TEXT_MOST: i64`, value `32768`: The longest description, in bytes.
- `variant Scope = .system | .user`: Whose a service is.
- `variant Restart = .never | .on_failure | .always`: When the system starts a service again after it ended by itself.
- `record Definition(name: str, description: str, program: str, arguments: [str], dir: str, env: {str: str}, scope: Scope, at_boot: bool, restart: Restart, restart_delay: time.Duration)`: A service's definition: what `install` writes.
- `variant Manager = .systemd | .launchd | .windows`: The manager a system has.
- `variant State = .stopped | .starting | .running | .stopping | .pausing | .paused | .resuming | .failed(code: i64)`: Where a service stands, as `status_of` reads it.
- `record Status(state: State, pid: i64?, at_boot: bool)`: What `status_of` answers.
- `function definition(name: str, program: str, arguments: [str], scope: Scope) -> Definition`, called `manage.definition(name: name, program: program, arguments, scope)`: A definition of the service `name`, of `scope`, running `program` with `arguments`: no description, the manager's own folder, no variables, not started by itself, never restarted, a restart delay of a second.
- `function manager() -> Manager?`, called `manage.manager()`: The manager of the system this program runs on: systemd where Linux was booted with it (`/run/systemd/system` is a folder, `sd_booted(3)`'s test), launchd on macOS, the Service Control Manager on Windows. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function format_unit(d: Definition) -> str?`, called `manage.format_unit(d)`: The systemd unit file of `d`: `[Unit]` with its description, `[Service]` with `Type=exec`, the program and its arguments quoted, the folder, the variables in the order of their names, the restart and its delay, and `[Install]` with the target `install` enables it for. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_job(d: Definition) -> str?`, called `manage.format_job(d)`: The launchd property list of `d`, in XML as `plutil -convert xml1` writes one: `Label`, `ProgramArguments`, `WorkingDirectory`, `EnvironmentVariables`, `RunAtLoad`, `KeepAlive` and `ThrottleInterval`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function path_of(name: str, scope: Scope) -> str?`, called `manage.path_of(name, scope)`: Where `install` writes the definition of the service `name` of `scope` on this system: `/etc/systemd/system/<name>.service` or the user's `systemd/user` folder under `os.config_dir`; `/Library/LaunchDaemons` or the user's `Library/LaunchAgents`, `<name>.plist`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function install(d: Definition) -> ()?`, called `manage.install(d)`: Installs `d`, which the system then starts as `d` says, or when asked; the service does not start now. Fails `invalid`, `exists`, `permission`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `function remove(name: str, scope: Scope, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `manage.remove(name, scope, limit)`: Stops the service `name` of `scope`, waiting at most `limit`, and removes it. Fails `not_found`, `timeout`, `limit`.
- `function start(name: str, scope: Scope, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `manage.start(name, scope, limit)`: Starts the service `name` of `scope`, waiting at most `limit` until the system says it started; a service that runs already is left running. Fails `not_found`, `timeout`, `limit`, `failed`, `permission`, `unsupported`.
- `function stop(name: str, scope: Scope, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `manage.stop(name, scope, limit)`: Stops the service `name` of `scope`, waiting at most `limit` until its process has ended; a stopped service is left stopped. Fails `not_found`, `timeout`, `limit`, `permission`, `unsupported`.
- `function restart(name: str, scope: Scope, limit: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `manage.restart(name, scope, limit)`: Stops the service `name` of `scope` where it runs and starts it, waiting at most `limit` for both; a stopped one is started. Fails as `stop` and `start` do.
- `function status_of(name: str, scope: Scope) -> Status?`, called `manage.status_of(name, scope)`: Where the service `name` of `scope` stands, its main process and whether the system starts it by itself. Fails `not_found`, `permission`, `unsupported`, `failed`.


### service

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/service`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/service/).

The program as a service of the system that starts it.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument out of its range: a name empty, longer than `NAME_MOST` bytes or holding a slash or a backslash; a state a function does not report, or an exit code outside 0 to 4,294,967,295; a wait of less than zero.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: This program started a service already.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: No service stands: none was started, or `end` ran.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The system did not call the program in the time `start` allowed.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: Nothing is there: no supervisor's socket answers at the name `$NOTIFY_SOCKET` gives, no launchd socket has the name asked for, no watchdog supervises this program.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The system refuses the program what the call does.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while `wait` waited, after the controls queued before the stop were told.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The system has no thread, socket or memory left for what the call needs.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: This system has no services: it is not Windows.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names: the program was not started by the Service Control Manager, or the system refused a report; the message carries the system's own words.
- `constant NAME_MOST: i64`, value `256`: The longest service name `start` takes, in bytes.
- `record Service(name: str)`: The service of this program.
- `variant State = .stopped | .start_pending | .stop_pending | .running | .resume_pending | .pause_pending | .paused`: What a service is in: the state it reports to the system.
- `variant Accept = .stop | .pause_resume | .shutdown | .preshutdown | .param_change | .time_change | .power | .session`: A control the program says it accepts: the system sends no other.
- `variant Kind = .stop | .pause | .resume | .shutdown | .preshutdown | .param_change | .time_change | .power | .session | .user`: What the system asked of the program.
- `record Control(kind: Kind, event: i64, session: i64)`: One control, as the system sent it.
- `function is_supported() -> bool`, called `service.is_supported()`: Whether this system has services: true on Windows alone.
- `function is_service() -> bool`, called `service.is_service()`: Whether the Service Control Manager started this program, which a program that is a service and a console tool at once asks first: false for a program started from a console, by another program or a scheduled task, and on every system but Windows.
- `function start(name: str, limit: time.Duration) -> Service?`, called `service.start(name, limit)`: Makes this program the service `name`, once the Service Control Manager has called it, and answers the service, standing in `start_pending`. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `exists`, `failed`, `unsupported`.
- `function arguments(s: Service) -> [str]?`, called `service.arguments(s)`: The start parameters the system gave the service, which `sc start <name> <argument>...` writes after the name, in order; none where the program was started with none. Fails `closed`.
- `function report_running(s: Service, accepts: [Accept]) -> ()?`, called `service.report_running(s, accepts)`: Reports the service running, taking the controls `accepts`. Fails `closed`, `failed`.
- `function report_paused(s: Service, accepts: [Accept]) -> ()?`, called `service.report_paused(s, accepts)`: Reports the service paused, taking the controls `accepts`. Fails as `report_running` does.
- `function report_pending(s: Service, state: State, wait_hint: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `service.report_pending(s, state, wait_hint)`: Reports a pending state: the service is on its way, and the system is told how long to wait for the next report before it takes the service for hung. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function end(s: Service, exit_code: i64) -> ()?`, called `service.end(s, exit_code)`: Reports the service stopped and ends it: the system is told, the controls not taken are let go, the bell closed, and every call through a copy of the service fails `closed` from then on. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function wait(s: Service, limit: time.Duration) -> [Control]?`, called `service.wait(s, limit)`: The controls the system sent, in order, waiting until one comes, `limit` passes, or the program is asked to stop. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `stopped`, `closed`.
- `function wait_forever(s: Service) -> [Control]?`, called `service.wait_forever(s)`: The controls the system sent, waiting as long as it takes: until one comes or the program is asked to stop. Fails as `wait` does.
- `function count(s: Service) -> i64?`, called `service.count(s)`: How many controls wait, without waiting. Fails `closed`.
- `function add_to(set: poll.Set, s: Service) -> i64?`, called `service.add_to(set, s)`: Adds the service to the set `set` and answers the entry's key: a wait on the set tells the key readable while a control waits, and the program then takes the controls with `wait` and a limit of zero. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function state_name(state: State) -> str`, called `service.state_name(state)`: The state as a word the system's own tools use: `sc query` prints `STOP_PENDING` for `stop_pending`, and this prints `stop_pending`.
- `function format_control(c: Control) -> str`, called `service.format_control(c)`: The control as one line a person reads: its kind, and the event and session where the kind has them.
- `variant Notice = .ready | .reloading | .stopping | .status(text: str) | .errno(number: i64) | .main_pid(pid: i64) | .watchdog | .watchdog_trigger | .watchdog_timeout(span: time.Duration) | .extend_timeout(span: time.Duration) | .bus_error(name: str) | .varlink_error(name: str) | .exit_status(code: i64) | .notify_access(who: NotifyAccess) | .restart_reset`: What a program tells the manager that supervises it, one case for each of systemd's assignments (`sd_notify(3)`).
- `variant NotifyAccess = .none | .main | .exec | .all`: Which processes of a service the manager takes notices from: the values of `NotifyAccess=` in `systemd.service(5)`.
- `function can_notify() -> bool`, called `service.can_notify()`: Whether this system has systemd's notice socket: POSIX does, and Windows does not.
- `function format_notices(notices: [Notice], monotonic: time.Duration) -> str?`, called `service.format_notices(notices, monotonic)`: The notices as the datagram one `notify` sends: their assignments, a line for each, with no newline at the end. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_notices(text: str) -> [Notice]?`, called `service.parse_notices(text)`: The notices a datagram holds, in order: what a supervisor reads of `format_notices`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function notify(notices: [Notice]) -> bool?`, called `service.notify(notices)`: Tells the manager the notices, as one datagram to the socket `$NOTIFY_SOCKET` names: true where it went, false where no manager named a socket, as when the program is started by hand. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `not_found`, `permission`, `limit`.
- `function watchdog_timeout() -> time.Duration?`, called `service.watchdog_timeout()`: The time the manager's watchdog allows between two `watchdog` notices, from `$WATCHDOG_USEC`: the program sends one about every half of it. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `variant Handed = .listener(socket: net.Listener) | .connection(conn: net.Conn) | .datagram(socket: net.UdpSocket) | .local_listener(socket: ipc.Listener) | .local_connection(stream: io.Stream) | .fifo(stream: io.Stream) | .special(stream: io.Stream) | .other(words: str)`: What a manager handed the program: a socket of `net` where it is one, the words for what it is where it is not.
- `record Inherited(name: str, handed: Handed)`: One descriptor handed over, with the name its unit gave it.
- `function is_booted_by_systemd() -> bool`, called `service.is_booted_by_systemd()`: Whether the system was booted with systemd as its init, which is what `sd_booted(3)` asks: the directory `/run/systemd/system/` exists.
- `function can_inherit() -> bool`, called `service.can_inherit()`: Whether this system has systemd's socket activation: POSIX does.
- `function can_inherit_launchd() -> bool`, called `service.can_inherit_launchd()`: Whether this system has launchd's socket activation: macOS does.
- `function inherit() -> [Inherited]?`, called `service.inherit()`: The sockets and files systemd handed this program, from descriptor 3 on (`$LISTEN_PID`, `$LISTEN_FDS`, `$LISTEN_FDNAMES`), in order, each set close-on-exec and made a value of `net`, of `ipc` or of `io`. Fails `exists`, `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function inherit_launchd(name: str) -> [Inherited]?`, called `service.inherit_launchd(name)`: The sockets launchd hands the job under `name` (`launch_activate_socket`), as `inherit` makes them, each named `name`. launchd hands a name's sockets over once. Fails `not_found`, `exists`, `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.


### http

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/http`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/http/).

HTTP/1.1, client and server, over `net` and over `tls`: a request and a response as values, read from and written to an `io.Stream` by RFC 9112; a client that sends a request to an `http://` or `https://` URL and follows its redirects; and a server that answers each request of each connection, plain or TLS, with a function of the program.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A message or a value that is not what HTTP/1.1 allows, a target that is no URL among them; the message says what and where.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A message past one of its `Limits`, or a client past its redirects.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: What this package does not do: a scheme other than `http` and `https`, a transfer coding other than chunked, an HTTP version other than 1.x; and TLS on a Linux machine with no OpenSSL, as `tls` fails.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A field, a status's text or a form that is not there; and, from `net`, a host name with no address.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection ended: the peer closed it, or nothing listens where a client connects, or a stream ended before a message began.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The time a connection was allowed ran out.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program asked to stop (`os.catch_stop`, `os.ask_stop`) while a call waited.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused the connection for a reason no other code names, the message carrying its own words; and a status of 400 or more made a failure by `require_success`, the message naming it.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: A body, a form or credentials whose bytes are not text in their charset.
- `constant DOES_NOT_FIT: str`, value `"does_not_fit"`: An HTTP date outside what a `time.Instant` holds.
- `constant METHOD_GET: str`, value `"GET"`: The method that asks for a representation of the target.
- `constant METHOD_HEAD: str`, value `"HEAD"`: The method that asks for what `METHOD_GET` would, without its body.
- `constant METHOD_POST: str`, value `"POST"`: The method that hands the target a body to process.
- `constant METHOD_PUT: str`, value `"PUT"`: The method that replaces the target with the body.
- `constant METHOD_PATCH: str`, value `"PATCH"`: The method that changes part of the target by the body.
- `constant METHOD_DELETE: str`, value `"DELETE"`: The method that removes the target.
- `constant METHOD_CONNECT: str`, value `"CONNECT"`: The method that opens a tunnel; this package's server answers it 501.
- `constant METHOD_OPTIONS: str`, value `"OPTIONS"`: The method that asks what the target allows.
- `constant METHOD_TRACE: str`, value `"TRACE"`: The method that asks the request back, as the server received it.
- `record Header(name: str, value: str)`: One field of a message's header: a name and its value.
- `function value_of(headers: [Header], name: str) -> str?`, called `http.value_of(headers, name)`: The value of the first field of `headers` named `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function values_of(headers: [Header], name: str) -> [str]`, called `http.values_of(headers, name)`: The value of every field of `headers` named `name`, in their order.
- `function has_header(headers: [Header], name: str) -> bool`, called `http.has_header(headers, name)`: Whether a field of `headers` is named `name`.
- `function with_header(headers: [Header], name: str, value: str) -> [Header]`, called `http.with_header(headers, name: name, value: value)`: A copy of `headers` with one field `name: value` where every field of that name was.
- `function without_header(headers: [Header], name: str) -> [Header]`, called `http.without_header(headers, name)`: A copy of `headers` without any field named `name`.
- `function canonical_name(name: str) -> str`, called `http.canonical_name(name)`: `name` as a header's name is written by custom: the first letter and each letter after a `-` upper case, the others lower case.
- `record Request(method: str, url: url.Url, headers: [Header], body: [u8], closing: bool, remote: str)`: A request: what a client sends and a server's handler reads.
- `record Response(status: i64, reason: str, headers: [Header], body: [u8], closing: bool)`: A response: what a server's handler answers and a client reads.
- `record Credentials(user: str, password: str)`: A user and a password, as a request's `Authorization: Basic` carries them.
- `record Part(name: str, filename: str, content_type: str, data: [u8])`: One part of a `multipart/form-data` body, as `with_multipart` writes it: a form's field, or a file.
- `function request(method: str, target: str) -> Request?`, called `http.request(method: method, target: target)`: A request with no field and no body, to send to `target`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_query(r: Request, pairs: [url.Pair]) -> Request`, called `http.with_query(r, pairs)`: A copy of `r` whose target's query has `pairs` after what it held.
- `function with_body(r: Request, content_type: str, body: [u8]) -> Request`, called `http.with_body(r, content_type, body)`: A copy of `r` with `body`, typed `content_type`.
- `function with_text(r: Request, text: str) -> Request`, called `http.with_text(r, text)`: A copy of `r` whose body is `text`, typed `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.
- `function with_json(r: Request, value: json.Value) -> Request?`, called `http.with_json(r, value)`: A copy of `r` whose body is `value` as JSON, typed `application/json`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function with_form(r: Request, pairs: [url.Pair]) -> Request`, called `http.with_form(r, pairs)`: A copy of `r` whose body is the form `pairs`, typed `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
- `function with_multipart(r: Request, parts: [Part]) -> Request`, called `http.with_multipart(r, parts)`: A copy of `r` whose body is `parts` as `multipart/form-data`, RFC 7578.
- `function query_of(r: Request) -> [url.Pair]?`, called `http.query_of(r)`: The keys and values of the query of `r`'s target, in their order. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function form_of(r: Request) -> [url.Pair]?`, called `http.form_of(r)`: The keys and values of `r`'s body, a form sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, in their order. Fails `not_found`, `not_text`.
- `function basic_auth_of(r: Request) -> Credentials?`, called `http.basic_auth_of(r)`: The user and the password `r`'s `Authorization: Basic` field carries. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function cookie_of(r: Request, name: str) -> str?`, called `http.cookie_of(r, name)`: The value of the cookie `name` that `r` sends, the first of that name, as Go's `Request.Cookie` answers. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function bearer_token_of(r: Request) -> str?`, called `http.bearer_token_of(r)`: The token `r` carries in an `Authorization: Bearer` field, RFC 6750. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function with_basic_auth(r: Request, user: str, password: str) -> Request`, called `http.with_basic_auth(r, user: user, password: password)`: A copy of `r` carrying `user` and `password` in an `Authorization: Basic` field, every `Authorization` before replaced.
- `function with_bearer_auth(r: Request, token: str) -> Request`, called `http.with_bearer_auth(r, token)`: A copy of `r` carrying `token` in an `Authorization: Bearer` field, RFC 6750, every `Authorization` before replaced.
- `function respond(status: i64, content_type: str, body: [u8]) -> Response`, called `http.respond(status, content_type, body)`: A response of `status` with `body`, typed `content_type`.
- `function respond_text(status: i64, text: str) -> Response`, called `http.respond_text(status, text)`: A response of `status` whose body is `text`, typed `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.
- `function respond_json(status: i64, value: json.Value) -> Response?`, called `http.respond_json(status, value)`: A response of `status` whose body is `value` as JSON, typed `application/json`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function respond_status(status: i64) -> Response`, called `http.respond_status(status)`: A response of `status` alone: no body, no field.
- `function respond_redirect(status: i64, location: str) -> Response`, called `http.respond_redirect(status, location)`: A response sending the client to `location`.
- `function respond_moved_to(base: str, r: Request) -> Response`, called `http.respond_moved_to(base, r)`: The answer that sends `r` to the same path and query under `base`: 308, so the method and the body are kept, as a site that moved, or an `http://` server sending every client to `https://`, answers.
- `function respond_not_found(r: Request) -> Response`, called `http.respond_not_found(r)`: The answer to `r` where its target names nothing, as Go's `NotFound` answers: 404 and the text `404 page not found`.
- `function respond_trace(r: Request) -> Response`, called `http.respond_trace(r)`: The answer RFC 9110 § 9.3.8 gives a `TRACE`: 200 and the request as it was read, typed `message/http`, for a handler to answer with.
- `function text_of(response: Response) -> str?`, called `http.text_of(response)`: The body of `response` as text, read by the `charset` of its `Content-Type`. Fails `not_text`, `unsupported`.
- `function json_of(response: Response) -> json.Value?`, called `http.json_of(response)`: The body of `response` as a JSON value. Fails as `text_of` and `json.parse` do.
- `function require_success(response: Response) -> Response?`, called `http.require_success(response)`: `response` where its status is below 400, what `requests` calls raising for the status. Fails `failed`.
- `function decode_body(response: Response, limit: i64) -> Response?`, called `http.decode_body(response, limit)`: A copy of `response` with its `Content-Encoding` undone, RFC 9110 § 8.4: gzip, `x-gzip`, deflate and identity, the last applied first, `deflate` read as zlib and, where zlib refuses it, as raw DEFLATE, as some servers send it. Fails `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function with_compression(response: Response, r: Request) -> Response`, called `http.with_compression(response, r)`: A copy of `response` compressed as gzip, or as deflate (zlib) where `r` accepts deflate and not gzip, where `r`'s `Accept-Encoding` accepts one, RFC 9110 § 12.5.3; else `response` as it is.
- `record Cookie(name: str, value: str, domain: str, host_only: bool, path: str, expires: time.Instant, persistent: bool, secure: bool, http_only: bool, same_site: str)`: A cookie, RFC 6265: what a `Set-Cookie` field gives a client to keep, and what a `Cookie` field sends back.
- `function parse_set_cookie(s: str, now: time.Instant) -> Cookie?`, called `http.parse_set_cookie(s, now)`: The cookie the `Set-Cookie` field's value `s` sets, RFC 6265 § 5.2. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_set_cookie(c: Cookie) -> str`, called `http.format_set_cookie(c)`: The value of a `Set-Cookie` field setting `c`.
- `function parse_cookie(s: str) -> [Cookie]?`, called `http.parse_cookie(s)`: The cookies the `Cookie` field's value `s` sends, in their order, each a name and a value. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_cookie(list: [Cookie]) -> str`, called `http.format_cookie(list)`: The value of a `Cookie` field sending `list`: each name and value, `; ` between them.
- `function matching_cookies(jar: [Cookie], target: url.Url, now: time.Instant) -> [Cookie]`, called `http.matching_cookies(jar, target, now)`: The cookies of `jar` a request to `target` sends at `now`, RFC 6265 § 5.4: its host matched by each cookie's domain, its path by each cookie's path, none ended, and a secure one only to an `https://` target.
- `function store_cookies(@jar: [Cookie], target: url.Url, response: Response, now: time.Instant)`, called `http.store_cookies(@jar, target, response, now)`: Keeps in `jar` each cookie `response`'s `Set-Cookie` fields set, for a request to `target`, RFC 6265 § 5.3.
- `function store_cookies_by(@jar: [Cookie], target: url.Url, response: Response, now: time.Instant, is_public_suffix: (function(str) -> bool))`, called `http.store_cookies_by(@jar, target, response, now, is_public_suffix)`: Keeps in `jar` each cookie `response`'s `Set-Cookie` fields set, as `store_cookies` keeps them, a `Domain` that `is_public_suffix` says is a public suffix refused, RFC 6265 § 5.3's step 5.
- `function is_single_label(domain: str) -> bool`, called `http.is_single_label(domain)`: Whether `domain` is a single label, `com` or `localhost`: the public suffixes this package knows without a list, as a session's `is_public_suffix` asks by default.
- `record Limits(head_bytes: i64, field_count: i64, body_bytes: i64)`: How much of a message is read before it fails `limit`: what keeps a peer from holding a program's memory.
- `function default_limits() -> Limits`, called `http.default_limits()`: The usual limits: a head of 65,536 bytes, as Python's line limit, 100 fields, as Python's, and a body of 10 MiB.
- `function read_request(@reader: io.Reader, limits: Limits) -> Request?`, called `http.read_request(@reader, limits)`: The next request `reader` holds, its head and its body, by RFC 9112. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function parse_target(method: str, target: str) -> url.Url?`, called `http.parse_target(method: method, target: target)`: The URL a request's first line names, `target` as written, for a request of `method`: `*` for `OPTIONS`, else as `url.parse_request_target` reads it. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function write_request(s: io.Stream, r: Request) -> ()?`, called `http.write_request(s, r)`: Writes `r` to `s` as HTTP/1.1: its first line, `Host`, its fields, its framing and its body. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_response(@reader: io.Reader, method: str, limits: Limits) -> Response?`, called `http.read_response(@reader, method, limits)`: The next final response `reader` holds, by RFC 9112, the informational ones before it skipped. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function write_response(s: io.Stream, response: Response, method: str) -> ()?`, called `http.write_response(s, response, method)`: Writes `response` to `s` as HTTP/1.1: its status line, its fields, its framing and its body. Fails `invalid`.
- `constant USER_AGENT: str`, value `"heroes-rebel-http/0.1.0"`: The `User-Agent` `default_client` sends, one product as RFC 9110 § 10.1.5 writes it: Heroes' library Rebel, its package `http`, and Rebel's version.
- `record Retries(count: i64, statuses: [i64], backoff: retries.Backoff)`: When a request is sent again, and how long the client waits first.
- `record Client(max_redirects: i64, deadline: time.Duration, limits: Limits, roots: str, retries: Retries, proxy: Proxy, user_agent: str)`: How a client sends: made by `default_client`, its fields changed by the program.
- `function default_client() -> Client`, called `http.default_client()`: The usual client: 10 redirects, as Go and Python follow, a time limit of 30 seconds, `default_limits()`, the system's own authorities, no retry, whose waits would be 100 ms doubled up to 10 s, no proxy: the environment's are read only where the program asks, `proxy_from_env()`; and `USER_AGENT` sent, as Go and Python send their own.
- `record Session(client: Client, headers: [Header], base: str, cookies: [Cookie], is_public_suffix: (function(str) -> bool))`: What a program keeps between requests, as `requests`' session does: how they are sent, the fields each carries, the URL a path is read against, and the cookies the server set.
- `function default_session() -> Session`, called `http.default_session()`: A session with `default_client()`, no field, no base, no cookie, and the public suffixes of one label alone.
- `function fetch(@s: Session, r: Request) -> Response?`, called `http.fetch(@s, r)`: The response to `r`, sent as `send` sends it, through `s`: its target resolved against `s.base`, `s.headers` added where `r` has none of the name, the cookies of `s` sent and those set kept, on every redirect. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_once(@s: Session, r: Request) -> Response?`, called `http.fetch_once(@s, r)`: The response to `r` through `s`, its redirects not followed: one request, sent again as `s.client.retries` says, its target resolved and its fields added as `fetch` does, the cookies of `s` sent and those set kept. Fails as `send` does.
- `function send(c: Client, r: Request) -> Response?`, called `http.send(c, r)`: The response to `r`, sent to the `http://` or `https://` URL it names on a connection of its own, its redirects followed and the cookies set on the way sent on. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`, `limit`, `timeout`.
- `function get(c: Client, target: str) -> Response?`, called `http.get(c, target)`: The response to a `GET` of `target`, as `send` answers it. Fails as `request` and `send` do.
- `function head(c: Client, target: str) -> Response?`, called `http.head(c, target)`: The response to a `HEAD` of `target`, as `send` answers it: no body. Fails as `request` and `send` do.
- `function post(c: Client, target: str, content_type: str, body: [u8]) -> Response?`, called `http.post(c, target: target, content_type: content_type, body)`: The response to a `POST` of `body` to `target`, as `send` answers it. Fails as `request` and `send` do.
- `function post_form(c: Client, target: str, pairs: [url.Pair]) -> Response?`, called `http.post_form(c, target, pairs)`: The response to a `POST` of the form `pairs` to `target`, as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, as `send` answers it. Fails as `request` and `send` do.
- `function round_trip(@reader: io.Reader, r: Request, limits: Limits) -> Response?`, called `http.round_trip(@reader, r, limits)`: The response to `r`, written on the connection `reader` reads and read back through `reader`: one exchange on a connection the program holds, so several may follow one another on it. Fails as `write_request` and `read_response` do.
- `record Proxy(http: str, https: str, bypass: [str])`: The proxies a client's requests go through: one for `http://` targets, one for `https://` targets, and the hosts reached directly.
- `function no_proxy() -> Proxy`, called `http.no_proxy()`: No proxy: every request sent directly, as `default_client` sends them.
- `function proxy_from_env() -> Proxy`, called `http.proxy_from_env()`: The proxies the environment names, as curl and Python read them: `http_proxy` or `HTTP_PROXY`, `https_proxy` or `HTTPS_PROXY`, and `no_proxy` or `NO_PROXY` parted by commas, the lower case name first.
- `function proxy_from_system() -> Proxy?`, called `http.proxy_from_system()`: The proxies the environment names where it names any, else the ones the system's own settings name: on macOS the proxies of the active network service (System Settings, Network), on Windows the current user's Internet Options, as Python's `getproxies` reads them. Fails `failed`, `limit`.
- `function proxy_for(p: Proxy, target: url.Url) -> str?`, called `http.proxy_for(p, target)`: The proxy a request to `target` goes through by `p`: its `https` proxy for an `https://` target, its `http` one for any other. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Opened(response: Response, reader: io.Reader)`: A request sent on a connection of its own, the head of its answer read and its body left on the connection: what `open_stream` makes.
- `function open_stream(c: Client, r: Request) -> Opened?`, called `http.open_stream(c, r)`: Sends `r` on a connection of its own, through the proxy `c.proxy` names for it, and reads the head of the answer, leaving the body on the connection. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`, `limit`, `timeout`, `failed`.
- `function tunnel(proxy: str, host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration) -> io.Stream?`, called `http.tunnel(proxy: proxy, host: host, port, deadline)`: A TCP connection to `host` at `port` through the proxy `proxy` names, the stream a tunnel the proxy opened: `CONNECT` for an `http://` proxy, the SOCKS handshake for a `socks4://`, `socks4a://`, `socks5://` or `socks5h://` one, written as `Proxy`'s fields write them. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `failed`, `permission`.
- `record BodyReader(state: streaming.Body)`: A response's body read piece by piece as it comes, where `read_response` holds it whole: made by `body_reader` from a head `read_response_head` read, and read by `read_piece` until it answers an empty list.
- `function read_response_head(@reader: io.Reader, method: str, limits: Limits) -> Response?`, called `http.read_response_head(@reader, method, limits)`: The head of the next final response `reader` holds, the informational ones before it skipped, its body left unread on the connection: what a client reads before a body that comes as it is made, an event stream's. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function body_reader(response: Response, method: str, limits: Limits) -> BodyReader?`, called `http.body_reader(response, method, limits)`: How the body of `response` is read as it comes, before a byte of it. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function read_piece(@reader: io.Reader, @body: BodyReader, most: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `http.read_piece(@reader, @body, most)`: The next piece of a body, at most `most` bytes: what `reader` holds of it, or what comes next, waiting only where it holds none. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function write_response_head(s: io.Stream, response: Response) -> ()?`, called `http.write_response_head(s, response)`: Writes the head of `response` to `s` for a body the program writes as it is made and ends by closing the connection: the status line, its fields, a `Date` where it has none, and `Connection: close`, with no length, which RFC 9112 § 6.3 lets end a body and every HTTP/1.x client reads. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Framing = .none | .length(bytes: i64) | .chunked | .to_end`: How a body ends, as a message relayed as it comes is framed: what `framing_of` reads of a body being read, and what `write_request_head` and `write_response_head_framed` write.
- `record BodyWriter(state: relaying.Owed)`: What writes a body relayed as it comes: answered by `write_request_head` and `write_response_head_framed` with the head they wrote, and moved on by `write_piece` and `end_pieces`, so a piece past a length and an end before it are refused rather than sent.
- `function request_body_reader(h: RequestHead, limits: Limits) -> BodyReader?`, called `http.request_body_reader(h, limits)`: How the body of the request `h` heads is read as it comes, before a byte of it: what a gateway reads to pass a body on without holding it whole. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function framing_of(body: BodyReader) -> Framing`, called `http.framing_of(body)`: How the body `body` reads ends, as it was framed before a byte of it was read: the framing a relay writes it on in.
- `function write_request_head(s: io.Stream, r: Request, framing: Framing) -> BodyWriter?`, called `http.write_request_head(s, r, framing)`: Writes the head of `r` to `s` for a body that follows in `framing`, written piece by piece with `write_piece` and ended by `end_pieces`: the request line with `url.request_target(r.url)`, `Host` as `r` names it or else as its URL does, the fields but the framing's, `Connection: close` where `r.closing`, and the framing's own field. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_response_head_framed(s: io.Stream, response: Response, framing: Framing) -> BodyWriter?`, called `http.write_response_head_framed(s, response, framing)`: Writes the head of `response` to `s` for a body that follows in `framing`, written piece by piece with `write_piece` and ended by `end_pieces`: the status line, the fields but the framing's, a `Date` where it has none, `Connection: close` where `response.closing` or the body runs to the connection's end, and the framing's own field. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_piece(s: io.Stream, @body: BodyWriter, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `http.write_piece(s, @body, data)`: Writes `data` to `s` as the next piece of the body `body` frames: the bytes themselves, or one chunk holding them; nothing for no bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function end_pieces(s: io.Stream, @body: BodyWriter) -> ()?`, called `http.end_pieces(s, @body)`: Ends the body `body` frames on `s`: the last chunk with an empty trailer for chunks, nothing else. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_switch_head(@reader: io.Reader, method: str, limits: Limits) -> Response?`, called `http.read_switch_head(@reader, method, limits)`: The head of the next response `reader` holds that is final or a 101, the other informational ones before it skipped, its body left unread: what a gateway reads after passing on a request that asked to switch protocols (`Upgrade`). Fails as `read_response_head` does, 101 aside.
- `function write_continue(s: io.Stream) -> ()?`, called `http.write_continue(s)`: Writes `100 Continue` to `s`, RFC 9110 § 15.2.1: what a server writes before reading the body of a request whose head asked for it with `Expect: 100-continue`, the client then sending it. Fails as `io.write` does.
- `record Event(name: str, data: str, id: str)`: An event of a `text/event-stream` body, as the WHATWG HTML standard dispatches it: read by `read_event` and `events_of`, and written by the package `web`.
- `record EventReader(last_id: str, retry: time.Duration, state: streaming.Events)`: An event stream being read: what a client keeps of it between two events.
- `function event_reader(response: Response, limits: Limits) -> EventReader?`, called `http.event_reader(response, limits)`: The reader of the event stream `response`'s body holds, before a byte of it, as a browser's `EventSource` reads one. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function read_event(@reader: io.Reader, @events: EventReader) -> Event?`, called `http.read_event(@reader, @events)`: The next event of the stream `events` reads, waiting for it: its lines read by the WHATWG HTML standard's algorithm, a line ended by a carriage return and a line feed, a line feed or a carriage return, a leading byte order mark dropped, a comment skipped, `retry` taken where it is digits alone, an `id` holding a zero byte ignored, bytes that are not UTF-8 read as U+FFFD. Fails `closed`, `limit`.
- `function events_of(response: Response) -> [Event]?`, called `http.events_of(response)`: The events of an event stream `response` holds whole, as `send` reads a stream the server ends: each ended by an empty line, read as `read_event` reads them; an event left unfinished at the end is dropped. Fails as `event_reader` fails on the status, the type and the coding.
- `record Server(limits: Limits, deadline: time.Duration)`: How a server serves: made by `default_server`, its fields changed by the program.
- `function default_server() -> Server`, called `http.default_server()`: The usual server: `default_limits()` and connections of 30 seconds at most.
- `function serve(s: Server, l: net.Listener, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> ()?`, called `http.serve(s, l, handler)`: Serves every connection `l` accepts with `handler`, one connection at a time, until the program asks to stop. Fails `timeout`, `closed`.
- `function serve_tls(s: Server, l: tls.Listener, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> ()?`, called `http.serve_tls(s, l, handler)`: Serves every TLS connection `l` accepts with `handler`, one connection at a time, until the program asks to stop: `serve` over `tls`. Fails `timeout`, `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function serve_conn(s: Server, c: net.Conn, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http.serve_conn(s, c, handler)`: Serves the requests of the connection `c` with `handler`, one after another, and answers how many were answered.
- `function serve_stream(s: Server, stream: io.Stream, remote: str, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http.serve_stream(s, stream, remote, handler)`: Serves the requests that come on `stream` with `handler`, one after another, as `serve_conn` serves a connection's, and answers how many were answered: the same work over any stream, a TLS one `tls.accept` answered among them.
- `function serve_with<S>(s: Server, l: net.Listener, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response)) -> ()?`, called `http.serve_with(s, l, state, handler)`: `serve` with `state` handed to `handler` beside each request: how a handler reads the program's routes, settings or data, since a function value holds none of its own. Fails where `serve` fails, with its code.
- `function serve_tls_with<S>(s: Server, l: tls.Listener, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response)) -> ()?`, called `http.serve_tls_with(s, l, state, handler)`: `serve_tls` with `state` handed to `handler` beside each request, as `serve_with` hands it. Fails where `serve_tls` fails, with its code.
- `function serve_stream_with<S>(s: Server, stream: io.Stream, remote: str, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http.serve_stream_with(s, stream, remote, state, handler)`: `serve_stream` with `state` handed to `handler` beside each request, as `serve_with` hands it, and how many were answered.
- `record RequestHead(request: Request, minor: i64)`: A request's head read apart from its body: what `read_request_head` answers and `read_request_body` reads on from.
- `function read_request_head(@reader: io.Reader, limits: Limits) -> RequestHead?`, called `http.read_request_head(@reader, limits)`: The head of the next request `reader` holds, its body left unread: what a server's own loop reads to decide before the body comes. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function read_request_body(@reader: io.Reader, h: RequestHead, limits: Limits) -> Request?`, called `http.read_request_body(@reader, h, limits)`: The request `h` begins, its body read from `reader`, `100 Continue` written first where an HTTP/1.1 client asked for it and a body follows. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function failure_status(code: str, in_head: bool) -> i64?`, called `http.failure_status(code, in_head)`: The status a server answers a request it failed to read with, RFC 9110 § 15: 400 for `invalid`, 431 for `limit` in the head and 413 in the body, 505 for `unsupported` in the head (a version) and 501 in the body (a transfer coding). Fails `not_found`, `closed`, `timeout`, `stopped`.
- `function refusal_of(h: RequestHead) -> i64?`, called `http.refusal_of(h)`: The status a server answers a well-formed head it will not serve with: 501 for `CONNECT`, which asks for a tunnel, and 417 for an `Expect` other than `100-continue`, RFC 9110 § 10.1.1. Fails `not_found`.
- `function next_request(@reader: io.Reader, limits: Limits) -> Request?`, called `http.next_request(@reader, limits)`: The next request `reader` holds, read whole as a server reads it: every refusal RFC 9112 asks for answered on `reader`'s stream first, closing, its reason the body, and `100 Continue` written where it is asked for. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function write_answer(s: io.Stream, r: Request, response: Response) -> ()?`, called `http.write_answer(s, r, response)`: Writes `response` to `s` as a server's answer to `r`, RFC 9112: a `Date` field where it has none, no body for `HEAD`, `Connection: close` where `r` or `response` closes, and `Connection: keep-alive` where `r` asked to keep the connection and it is kept, as an HTTP/1.0 client must be told. Fails as `io.write` does.
- `variant Ready = .request(request: Request) | .waiting`: What `read_ready` answers: a request whole, or none yet.
- `record RequestReader(reader: io.Reader, pending: RequestHead?, progress: ready.Progress)`: A connection's requests read as their bytes come, for a server that waits on many connections at once with `poll` and never waits on one: what `read_ready` reads from and keeps between its calls.
- `function request_reader(reader: io.Reader) -> RequestReader`, called `http.request_reader(reader)`: A reader of the requests `reader` brings, nothing of them read yet.
- `function read_ready(@requests: RequestReader, limits: Limits) -> Ready?`, called `http.read_ready(@requests, limits)`: The next request `requests` holds whole, read with at most one read of its stream: what a server waiting on many connections with `poll` calls when `poll` tells a connection is readable, so a client that sends a request slowly, or half of one, holds no other client back. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function to_h2_request(r: Request) -> http2.Request?`, called `http.to_h2_request(r)`: `r` as `http2` sends it: its method, its URL's scheme, authority and path with its query, its fields with names in lower case, those of HTTP/1.1's connection left out and `Host` carried as `:authority`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function from_h2_request(r: http2.Request, remote: str) -> Request?`, called `http.from_h2_request(r, remote)`: A request `http2` read, as a handler of this package reads one: its path and query as its URL, its fields, its `:authority` as a `Host` field where it sent none. Fails `invalid`.
- `function to_h2_response(response: Response, method: str) -> http2.Response`, called `http.to_h2_response(response, method)`: `response` as `http2` writes it in answer to a request of `method`: its fields with names in lower case, those of HTTP/1.1's connection and its framing left out, a `date` where it has none, and no body for `HEAD`, 204 or 304.
- `function from_h2_response(r: http2.Response) -> Response`, called `http.from_h2_response(r)`: A response `http2` read, as this package's: no reason, its fields as they came, its trailers dropped as HTTP/1.1's are.
- `function round_trip_h2(@c: http2.Conn, r: Request, limits: Limits) -> Response?`, called `http.round_trip_h2(@c, r, limits)`: The response to `r` on an HTTP/2 connection the program holds: many requests on one connection, one after another, as `round_trip` sends them on an HTTP/1.1 one. Fails `limit`.
- `function serve_h2(s: Server, @c: http2.Conn, remote: str, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http.serve_h2(s, @c, remote, handler)`: Serves the requests of an HTTP/2 connection with `handler`, one after another, until the client closes it or sends GOAWAY, and answers how many were answered: what `serve_stream` does over a TLS stream that chose `h2`.
- `function serve_h2_with<S>(s: Server, @c: http2.Conn, remote: str, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response)) -> i64`, called `http.serve_h2_with(s, @c, remote, state, handler)`: `serve_h2` with `state` handed to `handler` beside each request.
- `record FormPart(name: str, filename: str, is_file: bool, content_type: str, headers: [Header], data: [u8])`: One part of a `multipart/form-data` body as a server reads it, RFC 7578: a form's field, or a file.
- `record PartLimits(parts: i64, head_bytes: i64, part_bytes: i64, body_bytes: i64)`: How much of a multipart body is read before it fails `limit`: what keeps a client from holding a server's memory with many parts or long heads.
- `function default_part_limits() -> PartLimits`, called `http.default_part_limits()`: The usual limits: 1,000 parts, as Go's `multipartmaxparts` and werkzeug's `max_form_parts`; heads of 16,384 bytes; a part and a body of 10 MiB, the body `default_limits` reads.
- `function parts_of(r: Request, limits: PartLimits) -> [FormPart]?`, called `http.parts_of(r, limits)`: The parts of `r`'s body, a form sent as `multipart/form-data`, in their order. Fails `not_found`.
- `function decode_multipart(body: [u8], content_type: str, limits: PartLimits) -> [FormPart]?`, called `http.decode_multipart(body, content_type, limits)`: The parts of `body`, a multipart body, RFC 2046 § 5.1, in their order. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `not_text`.
- `function part_of(parts: [FormPart], name: str) -> FormPart?`, called `http.part_of(parts, name)`: The first part of `parts` whose form name is `name`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function negotiate_type(r: Request, offered: [str]) -> str?`, called `http.negotiate_type(r, offered)`: The media type of `offered` that `r`'s `Accept` fields weigh highest, RFC 9110 § 12.5.1. Fails `not_found`.
- `function negotiate_language(r: Request, offered: [str]) -> str?`, called `http.negotiate_language(r, offered)`: The language tag of `offered` that `r`'s `Accept-Language` fields weigh highest, RFC 9110 § 12.5.4. Fails `not_found`.
- `function negotiate_encoding(r: Request, offered: [str]) -> str?`, called `http.negotiate_encoding(r, offered)`: The content coding of `offered` that `r`'s `Accept-Encoding` fields weigh highest, RFC 9110 § 12.5.3. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Directive(name: str, value: str)`: One directive of a `Cache-Control` field, RFC 9111 § 5.2: `max-age=60`, `no-store`.
- `function parse_cache_control(value: str) -> [Directive]?`, called `http.parse_cache_control(value)`: The directives of `value`, a `Cache-Control` field's value, in their order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_cache_control(directives: [Directive]) -> str`, called `http.format_cache_control(directives)`: `directives` written as a `Cache-Control` value, `, ` between them.
- `function directive_of(directives: [Directive], name: str) -> str?`, called `http.directive_of(directives, name)`: The value of the directive `name` among `directives`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function has_etag(value: str, etag: str, strong: bool) -> bool`, called `http.has_etag(value: value, etag: etag, strong)`: Whether the entity tag `etag` stands in the list `value`, an `If-Match` or `If-None-Match` field's value, or the list is `*`, RFC 9110 § 8.8.3.2.
- `function is_not_modified(r: Request, response: Response) -> bool`, called `http.is_not_modified(r, response)`: Whether `r` holds a copy of what `response` answers, so `response` may be answered 304, RFC 9110 § 13.2.2.
- `function respond_not_modified(response: Response) -> Response`, called `http.respond_not_modified(response)`: `response` turned into the 304 that answers a request holding its copy, RFC 9110 § 15.4.5, as Go's `ServeContent` writes one.
- `constant TEST_REMOTE: str`, value `"192.0.2.1:1234"`: What `to_served` gives a request's `remote`: RFC 5737's documentation address and port 1234, as Go's `httptest.NewRequest` gives one.
- `constant TEST_HOST: str`, value `"example.com"`: The host `to_served` writes for a request whose target and fields name none, as Go's `httptest.NewRequest` writes it.
- `function to_served(r: Request, limits: Limits) -> Request?`, called `http.to_served(r, limits)`: `r` as a server reads it once a client has written it to a connection: its head written by `write_request`'s rules and read back by `read_request_head`'s, no network touched. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function to_received(r: Request, response: Response) -> Response`, called `http.to_received(r, response)`: `response` as a client reads it once a server has written it in answer to `r`, as `write_answer` writes it, no network touched.
- `function exchange(r: Request, handler: (function(Request) -> Response)) -> Response?`, called `http.exchange(r, handler)`: The response `handler` gives `r`, carried both ways in memory as a connection would carry them: a handler tried with no network, as Go's `httptest` and Flask's `test_client` try one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function exchange_with<S>(r: Request, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response)) -> Response?`, called `http.exchange_with(r, state, handler)`: `exchange` with `state` handed to `handler` beside the request, as `serve_with` hands it. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Served(connections: i64, answered: i64, cut: i64)`: What `serve_until_stopped` and `serve_stream_until_stopped` served, and what the stop cut.
- `function serve_until_stopped<S>(s: Server, l: net.Listener, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response), grace: time.Duration) -> Served?`, called `http.serve_until_stopped(s, l, state, handler, grace)`: Serves every connection `l` accepts with `handler`, one at a time, until the program asks to stop, and then ends gracefully, as Go's `Server.Shutdown` ends: no connection accepted after the stop, a connection idle at it closed, and a request whose bytes have come answered with `Connection: close` within `grace`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function serve_stream_until_stopped<S>(s: Server, stream: io.Stream, remote: str, state: S, handler: (function(S, Request) -> Response), grace: time.Duration) -> Served`, called `http.serve_stream_until_stopped(s, stream, remote, state, handler, grace)`: Serves the requests that come on `stream`, one after another, until the client or the stop ends them, and ends gracefully at the stop as `serve_until_stopped` does: what a program serving connections on its own threads calls on each, then joins them.
- `function format_date(t: time.Instant) -> str`, called `http.format_date(t)`: `t` as HTTP writes a date, RFC 9110's IMF-fixdate: `Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 GMT`.
- `function parse_date(s: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `http.parse_date(s)`: The instant `s` writes as an HTTP date: IMF-fixdate, the obsolete RFC 850 form or C's asctime form, as RFC 9110 asks a reader to accept. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `constant STATUS_CONTINUE: i64`, value `100`: The status 100, "Continue".
- `constant STATUS_SWITCHING_PROTOCOLS: i64`, value `101`: The status 101, "Switching Protocols".
- `constant STATUS_PROCESSING: i64`, value `102`: The status 102, "Processing".
- `constant STATUS_EARLY_HINTS: i64`, value `103`: The status 103, "Early Hints".
- `constant STATUS_OK: i64`, value `200`: The status 200, "OK".
- `constant STATUS_CREATED: i64`, value `201`: The status 201, "Created".
- `constant STATUS_ACCEPTED: i64`, value `202`: The status 202, "Accepted".
- `constant STATUS_NON_AUTHORITATIVE_INFORMATION: i64`, value `203`: The status 203, "Non-Authoritative Information".
- `constant STATUS_NO_CONTENT: i64`, value `204`: The status 204, "No Content".
- `constant STATUS_RESET_CONTENT: i64`, value `205`: The status 205, "Reset Content".
- `constant STATUS_PARTIAL_CONTENT: i64`, value `206`: The status 206, "Partial Content".

- `constant STATUS_ALREADY_REPORTED: i64`, value `208`: The status 208, "Already Reported".

### sql/migrate

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/sql/migrate`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sql/migrate/).

Numbered migrations of a database's schema: read from the SQL files of a folder or given as values, checked against a table of the versions already applied, and planned as steps, each applying or undoing one migration in its own transaction, that the program runs with its driver.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a file named almost as a migration, two migrations of one version, a migration whose up script changed after it ran, an older one found after a newer ran, or an option refused: `read_migrations`, `status`, `step` and the plans.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a version no migration has, and of a step back with no down script: `plan_up_to`, `plan_down`, `plan_down_to`, `step`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a lock SQLite has no form for: `lock_statement`, `unlock_statement`.
- `constant DEFAULT_TABLE: str`, value `"applied_migrations"`: The table of applied versions unless `Options` names another.
- `constant NO_TRANSACTION: str`, value `"-- no-transaction"`: The first line of a script that runs outside a transaction, for a statement neither database runs inside one; `step` reads it.
- `record Migration(version: i64, name: str, up: str, down: str?)`: A change to a database's schema, with the way back where there is one.
- `function read_migrations(dir: str) -> [Migration]?`, called `migrate.read_migrations(dir)`: The migrations in the folder `dir`, in the order of their versions. Fails `invalid`.
- `function checksum_of(script: str) -> str`, called `migrate.checksum_of(script)`: The checksum the table of versions keeps of `script`: its SHA-256, in 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
- `record Options(dialect: build.Dialect, table: str, allow_out_of_order: bool, ignore_missing: bool)`: How a database keeps its versions.
- `function options(dialect: build.Dialect) -> Options`, called `migrate.options(dialect)`: The options of a database of `dialect`, its versions in `DEFAULT_TABLE`, refusing an out-of-order or a missing migration.
- `record Applied(version: i64, name: str, checksum: str, applied_at: time.Instant)`: A version recorded in the table, as `applied_of` reads it.
- `function create_table_statement(opts: Options) -> build.Statement?`, called `migrate.create_table_statement(opts)`: The statement that makes the table of versions where it is not there: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, with the columns `version`, `name`, `checksum` and `applied_at`, the version its primary key. Fails `invalid`.
- `function select_applied_statement(opts: Options) -> build.Statement?`, called `migrate.select_applied_statement(opts)`: The query of every version applied, in the order of the versions. Fails as `create_table_statement` does.
- `function applied_of(rows: sql.Rows) -> [Applied]?`, called `migrate.applied_of(rows)`: The versions in `rows`, as `select_applied_statement`'s query answers them. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function current_version(applied: [Applied]) -> i64?`, called `migrate.current_version(applied)`: The version a database stands at: the largest applied. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Status(applied: [Migration], pending: [Migration])`: Which migrations a database has applied and which wait.
- `function status(migrations: [Migration], applied: [Applied], opts: Options) -> Status?`, called `migrate.status(migrations, applied, opts)`: The migrations applied and waiting, each applied version checked against its migration. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `variant Direction = .up | .down`: Which way a step goes.
- `record Step(version: i64, name: str, direction: Direction, script: str, in_transaction: bool, version_statement: build.Statement)`: One migration applied or undone: what the program runs, in order.
- `function step(migration: Migration, direction: Direction, opts: Options) -> Step?`, called `migrate.step(migration, direction, opts)`: The step that applies or undoes `migration`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function plan_up(migrations: [Migration], applied: [Applied], opts: Options) -> [Step]?`, called `migrate.plan_up(migrations, applied, opts)`: The steps that apply every migration waiting, the oldest first. Fails as `status` does.
- `function plan_up_to(migrations: [Migration], applied: [Applied], version: i64, opts: Options) -> [Step]?`, called `migrate.plan_up_to(migrations, applied, version, opts)`: The steps that apply every migration waiting up to `version`, it included. Fails `not_found`.
- `function plan_down(migrations: [Migration], applied: [Applied], opts: Options) -> [Step]?`, called `migrate.plan_down(migrations, applied, opts)`: The step that undoes the last migration applied; none where none is. Fails `not_found`.
- `function plan_down_to(migrations: [Migration], applied: [Applied], version: i64, opts: Options) -> [Step]?`, called `migrate.plan_down_to(migrations, applied, version, opts)`: The steps that undo every migration applied above `version`, the newest first. Fails `not_found`.
- `function format_plan(steps: [Step]) -> str`, called `migrate.format_plan(steps)`: `steps` as the text of a dry run: for each, a comment naming it, `BEGIN;` where it runs in a transaction, its script, its version statement with its parameters in a comment, and `COMMIT;`.
- `function lock_statement(opts: Options) -> build.Statement?`, called `migrate.lock_statement(opts)`: The statement that waits until no other program migrates the database and keeps it so until `unlock_statement`: PostgreSQL's `pg_advisory_lock`, its key taken from the table's name. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function unlock_statement(opts: Options) -> build.Statement?`, called `migrate.unlock_statement(opts)`: The statement that lets another program migrate again, after `lock_statement`'s: PostgreSQL's `pg_advisory_unlock`. Fails `unsupported`.


### grpc

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/grpc`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/grpc/).

gRPC over HTTP/2: calls of the four kinds (unary, a stream from the server, a stream from the client, and both ways at once), client and server, as the gRPC over HTTP/2 protocol writes them: each message framed by its length, a call's status and its message in the trailers, metadata as header fields (`-bin` keys carried in base 64), a deadline sent as `grpc-timeout`, and messages compressed by gzip where both ends allow it.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An argument refused: a method's path, a status code, a metadata key.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A message past `Options.max_message_bytes`.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The channel, the server's connection or the call has ended.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A method no schema or list names: `proto_method_of`, `status_name`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A peer's message compressed by an encoding other than gzip.
- `record Status(code: i64, message: str, details: [u8])`: How a call ended: a status code, a message for a person, and the details gRPC's rich error model carries as bytes (a `google.rpc.Status` as `protobuf.encode` writes it, sent as `grpc-status-details-bin`).
- `function status_name(code: i64) -> str?`, called `grpc.status_name(code)`: The name gRPC gives a status code: `"DEADLINE_EXCEEDED"` for 4. Fails `not_found`.
- `function status_of_http(status: i64) -> i64`, called `grpc.status_of_http(status)`: The status gRPC gives an HTTP status that came with no `grpc-status`: 400 is `STATUS_INTERNAL`, 401 `STATUS_UNAUTHENTICATED`, 403 `STATUS_PERMISSION_DENIED`, 404 `STATUS_UNIMPLEMENTED`, 429, 502, 503 and 504 `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`, every other `STATUS_UNKNOWN`.
- `function status_of_reset(error: i64) -> i64`, called `grpc.status_of_reset(error)`: The status gRPC gives a stream reset by an HTTP/2 error: `CANCEL` is `STATUS_CANCELLED`, `REFUSED_STREAM` `STATUS_UNAVAILABLE`, `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` `STATUS_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `INADEQUATE_SECURITY` `STATUS_PERMISSION_DENIED`, every other `STATUS_INTERNAL`.
- `function format_status_message(message: str) -> str`, called `grpc.format_status_message(message)`: `message` as `grpc-message` carries it: every byte outside space to `~`, and `%`, written as `%` and two capital hexadecimal digits.
- `function parse_status_message(s: str) -> str`, called `grpc.parse_status_message(s)`: The text `grpc-message` carries, its `%` escapes undone; an escape that is none is kept as it came, and bytes that make no UTF-8 are replaced, as gRPC's libraries read it.
- `record Entry(key: str, value: [u8])`: One entry of a call's metadata: a key and its value.
- `function is_binary_key(key: str) -> bool`, called `grpc.is_binary_key(key)`: Whether `key` carries bytes: whether it ends in `-bin`.
- `function value_of(metadata: [Entry], key: str) -> [u8]?`, called `grpc.value_of(metadata, key)`: The value of the first entry of `metadata` keyed `key`. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Framed(compressed: bool, data: [u8])`: One message as the wire carries it: whether it is compressed, and its bytes.
- `record Frames(messages: [Framed], rest: [u8])`: What `decode_frames` answers: the whole messages, and the bytes of one cut short.
- `function encode_frame(message: [u8], compressed: bool) -> [u8]`, called `grpc.encode_frame(message, compressed)`: A message framed for the wire: a byte that says whether it is compressed, its length in four bytes, then its bytes.
- `function decode_frames(data: [u8], most: i64) -> Frames?`, called `grpc.decode_frames(data, most)`: The messages `data` frames, in order, and the bytes of one cut short. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function format_timeout(d: time.Duration) -> str`, called `grpc.format_timeout(d)`: `d` as `grpc-timeout` carries it: at most eight digits and a unit, the finest unit that holds it (`n`, `u`, `m`, `S`, `M`, `H`).
- `function parse_timeout(s: str) -> time.Duration?`, called `grpc.parse_timeout(s)`: The time `grpc-timeout` says is left. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Options(http2: http2.Options, max_message_bytes: i64, compress: bool, user_agent: str)`: How an end runs its calls.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `grpc.default_options()`: The usual options: `http2.default_options()`, messages of 4 MiB as gRPC's libraries receive, sent uncompressed, the user agent `grpc-heroes/0.1`.
- `record Channel(conn: http2.Conn, authority: str, scheme: str, options: Options)`: A channel to one server: an HTTP/2 connection whose calls go to one authority.
- `record Reply(status: Status, messages: [[u8]], headers: [Entry], trailers: [Entry])`: What a call answers once it has ended: its status, the messages it received and its metadata.
- `record Call(stream: i64, path: str, deadline_at: i64, headers: [Entry], held: [u8], gzip_in: bool, gzip_out: bool, ended: bool, status: Status, trailers: [Entry], pending: [[u8]])`: A call in progress, made by `start_call`: a stream of the channel's connection, read and written by `send`, `receive`, `close_send` and `cancel`.
- `variant Incoming = .message(data: [u8]) | .end(status: Status, trailers: [Entry])`: What `receive` answers: the next message, or the call's end.
- `function connect(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, roots: str, options: Options) -> Channel?`, called `grpc.connect(host: host, port, deadline, roots: roots, options)`: A channel to `host` at `port` over TLS, ALPN choosing `h2`. Fails as `http2.connect` fails.
- `function connect_plain(host: str, port: i64, deadline: time.Duration, options: Options) -> Channel?`, called `grpc.connect_plain(host, port, deadline, options)`: A channel to `host` at `port` in plain text, HTTP/2 by prior knowledge. Fails as `http2.connect_plain` fails.
- `function new_channel(conn: http2.Conn, authority: str, scheme: str, options: Options) -> Channel`, called `grpc.new_channel(conn, authority: authority, scheme: scheme, options)`: A channel over an HTTP/2 connection the program made.
- `function close(@channel: Channel) -> ()?`, called `grpc.close(@channel)`: Closes the channel: GOAWAY, then its connection closed. Fails as `http2.close` does.
- `function call(@channel: Channel, path: str, request: [u8], metadata: [Entry], timeout: time.Duration) -> Reply?`, called `grpc.call(@channel, path, request, metadata, timeout)`: A unary call, or a call whose server answers a stream: `request` sent, every response read, the call's status answered. Fails `invalid`, `timeout`, `closed`.
- `function call_many(@channel: Channel, path: str, requests: [[u8]], metadata: [Entry], timeout: time.Duration) -> Reply?`, called `grpc.call_many(@channel, path, requests, metadata, timeout)`: A call whose client sends a stream: every request sent, the stream closed, every response read. Fails as `call` does.
- `function start_call(@channel: Channel, path: str, metadata: [Entry], timeout: time.Duration) -> Call?`, called `grpc.start_call(@channel, path, metadata, timeout)`: A call started, its head sent: what a call that streams both ways needs, its messages sent and read one by one. Fails as `call` does.
- `function send(@channel: Channel, @c: Call, message: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `grpc.send(@channel, @c, message)`: Sends one message on a call. Fails `limit`, `closed`.
- `function close_send(@channel: Channel, c: Call) -> ()?`, called `grpc.close_send(@channel, c)`: Tells the server this end sends no more messages on the call. Fails `closed`.
- `function receive(@channel: Channel, @c: Call) -> Incoming?`, called `grpc.receive(@channel, @c)`: The next message of the call, or its end with its status. Fails `closed`, `unsupported`.
- `function cancel(@channel: Channel, @c: Call)`, called `grpc.cancel(@channel, @c)`: Cancels a call: the stream reset with `CANCEL`, the call ended `STATUS_CANCELLED`.
- `function proto_method_of(schema: protobuf.Schema, path: str) -> protobuf.Method?`, called `grpc.proto_method_of(schema, path)`: The method a path names in `schema`: `/shop.Shop/GetOrder` is the method `GetOrder` of the service `shop.Shop`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function path_of(m: protobuf.Method) -> str`, called `grpc.path_of(m)`: The path a method is called by: `/` and its service's full name, `/` and its name.
- `record ProtoReply(status: Status, messages: [protobuf.Message], headers: [Entry], trailers: [Entry])`: What `call_proto` answers: the call's status, its responses decoded.
- `function call_proto(@channel: Channel, schema: protobuf.Schema, path: str, request: protobuf.Message, metadata: [Entry], timeout: time.Duration) -> ProtoReply?`, called `grpc.call_proto(@channel, schema, path, request, metadata, timeout)`: A call described by a `.proto`: `request` checked against the method's input type and encoded, the call made as `call` makes it, each response decoded as the output type. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Method(path: str, client_streaming: bool, server_streaming: bool)`: A method a server answers: its path and whether each side streams.
- `function methods_of(service: protobuf.Service) -> [Method]`, called `grpc.methods_of(service)`: The methods of a service, as `protobuf` read them from its `.proto`.
- `variant Health = .unknown | .serving | .not_serving | .service_unknown`: The health of a service, as the health checking service `grpc.health.v1.Health` answers it.
- `record Server(conn: http2.Conn, options: Options, health: {str: Health}, reflection: [str], watchers: {i64: str})`: A server's end of one HTTP/2 connection: the calls on it found and answered.
- `record ServerCall(stream: i64, path: str, method: i64, metadata: [Entry], deadline_at: i64, held: [u8], gzip_in: bool, gzip_out: bool, half_closed: bool, started: bool, finished: bool, pending: [[u8]])`: A call a server reads and answers, made by `next_call`.
- `function server(@stream: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Server?`, called `grpc.server(@stream, options)`: A server's end of the HTTP/2 connection `stream` carries: one `tls.accept` answered with `h2` chosen, or a plain one with prior knowledge. Fails as `http2.server` does.
- `function close_server(@s: Server) -> ()?`, called `grpc.close_server(@s)`: Closes a server's connection: GOAWAY, then the stream closed. Fails as `http2.close` does.
- `function next_call(@s: Server, methods: [Method]) -> ServerCall?`, called `grpc.next_call(@s, methods)`: The next call of one of `methods`, its head read: a call of another path is answered `STATUS_UNIMPLEMENTED`, and a health check or a reflection's request is answered where `s` enables them, and the next one is read. Fails `closed`.
- `function read_request(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall) -> Incoming?`, called `grpc.read_request(@s, @c)`: The next request of a call, or its end where the client sent its last. Fails `closed`, `limit`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function write_headers(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall, metadata: [Entry]) -> ()?`, called `grpc.write_headers(@s, @c, metadata)`: Sends the call's first metadata, before any response; sent with no entries by the first `write_response` where the program sends none. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function write_response(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall, message: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `grpc.write_response(@s, @c, message)`: Sends one response on a call. Fails `limit`, `closed`.
- `function finish(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall, status: Status, trailers: [Entry]) -> ()?`, called `grpc.finish(@s, @c, status, trailers)`: Ends a call with `status` and its trailing metadata; a call with no response sent ends with one header block, gRPC's trailers-only answer. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function answer_health(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall) -> ()?`, called `grpc.answer_health(@s, @c)`: Answers a call of the health checking service's `Check`: the service its request names looked up in `s.health`, its status answered, or `STATUS_NOT_FOUND` where it is not there. Fails as `read_request` and `finish` do.
- `function watch_health(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall) -> ()?`, called `grpc.watch_health(@s, @c)`: Answers a call of the health checking service's `Watch`: the status now, or `.service_unknown`, then each change `set_health` makes, the call kept open until the client cancels it. Fails as `read_request` and `write_response` do.
- `function answer_reflection(@s: Server, @c: ServerCall) -> ()?`, called `grpc.answer_reflection(@s, @c)`: Answers a call of server reflection, version 1 or 1alpha: each request answered as it comes, the list of `s.reflection`'s services where it asks for it and `NOT_FOUND` to a question about a file, until the client sends its last. Fails as `read_request`, `write_response` and `finish` do.
- `function left_ms(c: ServerCall) -> i64`, called `grpc.left_ms(c)`: The milliseconds left before the client's deadline, 0 where it has passed, -1 where the call has none.
- `function set_health(@s: Server, service: str, status: Health)`, called `grpc.set_health(@s, service, status)`: Sets the health of a service, telling every health `Watch` of it.
