- `constant STATUS_OK: i64`, value `0`: OK: the call succeeded.
- `constant STATUS_CANCELLED: i64`, value `1`: CANCELLED: the call was cancelled, usually by its caller.
- `constant STATUS_UNKNOWN: i64`, value `2`: UNKNOWN: an error no other code describes, or a status from a space this end does not know.
- `constant STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT: i64`, value `3`: INVALID_ARGUMENT: the caller gave an argument the server refuses whatever the system's state.
- `constant STATUS_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: i64`, value `4`: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the deadline passed before the call ended.
- `constant STATUS_NOT_FOUND: i64`, value `5`: NOT_FOUND: an entity the call names was not found.
- `constant STATUS_ALREADY_EXISTS: i64`, value `6`: ALREADY_EXISTS: an entity the call would create exists already.
- `constant STATUS_PERMISSION_DENIED: i64`, value `7`: PERMISSION_DENIED: the caller may not do this.
- `constant STATUS_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: i64`, value `8`: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: a resource ran out, a quota or a size among them.
- `constant STATUS_FAILED_PRECONDITION: i64`, value `9`: FAILED_PRECONDITION: the system is not in the state the call needs.
- `constant STATUS_ABORTED: i64`, value `10`: ABORTED: the call was aborted, a conflict among others.
- `constant STATUS_OUT_OF_RANGE: i64`, value `11`: OUT_OF_RANGE: the call went past a valid range.
- `constant STATUS_UNIMPLEMENTED: i64`, value `12`: UNIMPLEMENTED: the server does not offer the method.
- `constant STATUS_INTERNAL: i64`, value `13`: INTERNAL: an invariant broke inside the server or the protocol.
- `constant STATUS_UNAVAILABLE: i64`, value `14`: UNAVAILABLE: the service cannot be reached now; the call may be tried again.
- `constant STATUS_DATA_LOSS: i64`, value `15`: DATA_LOSS: data was lost or corrupted beyond repair.
- `constant STATUS_UNAUTHENTICATED: i64`, value `16`: UNAUTHENTICATED: the call carries no valid credentials.


### xlsx

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/xlsx`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/xlsx/).

Spreadsheets of Office Open XML, the `.xlsx` files of Excel, read and written.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a file that is not a workbook, the message naming the part and what was wrong there; of a name, a cell, an area or a value a sheet cannot hold; and of text that is no cell name or area.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a file past a bound its `ReadOptions` set, and of rows that would pass the `limit` `rows_of` is given.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a name the workbook does not hold: `sheet_of`, `cell_at`, `dimension_of` and `format_code_of` fail with it.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a value the format has no form for, a NaN, an infinity or a date before the epoch, and of a workbook this package does not read: one encrypted with a password, or a binary `.xlsb`.
- `constant MAX_ROWS: i64`, value `1048576`: The rows a sheet holds: 1,048,576, so the last row is 1,048,575.
- `constant MAX_COLUMNS: i64`, value `16384`: The columns a sheet holds: 16,384, so the last column, `XFD`, is 16,383.
- `constant MAX_TEXT_CHARS: i64`, value `32767`: The characters one cell's text may hold: 32,767, Excel's own bound.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES: i64`, value `67108864`: The bytes `default_read_options` lets a file's parts hold once decompressed, the text of its cells counted with them: 64 MiB.
- `constant DEFAULT_MAX_CELLS: i64`, value `1048576`: The cells `default_read_options` lets a file's sheets hold together: 1,048,576.
- `variant Value = .empty | .number(v: f64) | .text(v: str) | .boolean(v: bool) | .date(v: time.DateTime) | .error(v: str)`: What a cell holds.
- `record Cell(row: i64, column: i64, value: Value, formula: str, style: i64)`: One cell: where it stands, what it holds, its formula and its style.
- `record Area(first_row: i64, first_column: i64, last_row: i64, last_column: i64)`: A rectangle of cells, its corners included: `B2:C3` is rows 1 to 2 and columns 1 to 2.
- `record Position(row: i64, column: i64)`: Where one cell stands, as `parse_cell_name` reads it.
- `record ColumnFormat(first: i64, last: i64, width: f64, hidden: bool)`: The width of a run of columns, and whether they are hidden.
- `record RowFormat(row: i64, height: f64, hidden: bool)`: The height of one row, and whether it is hidden.
- `record Frozen(rows: i64, columns: i64)`: The rows at the top and the columns at the left that stay in view while the rest of a sheet scrolls; 0 and 0 where nothing is frozen.
- `record Link(area: Area, target: str, location: str, tooltip: str, display: str)`: A link from a cell, or an area of cells, to a web address, a file, or a place in the workbook.
- `variant Visibility = .visible | .hidden | .very_hidden`: Whether a sheet's tab is shown.
- `record Sheet(name: str, visibility: Visibility, cells: [Cell], merged: [Area], column_formats: [ColumnFormat], row_formats: [RowFormat], frozen: Frozen, links: [Link])`: One sheet of cells.
- `variant Epoch = .from_1900 | .from_1904`: Which day a serial number counts from: Excel's two epochs.
- `record DefinedName(name: str, refers_to: str, sheet: str, hidden: bool)`: A name defined over a workbook or one of its sheets: a cell, an area, a formula.
- `record Properties(title: str, subject: str, creator: str, keywords: str, description: str, last_modified_by: str, category: str, created: str, modified: str)`: What the document says of itself, its core properties; empty text where it says nothing.
- `record Workbook(sheets: [Sheet], styles: [Style], epoch: Epoch, names: [DefinedName], active: i64, properties: Properties)`: A workbook: its sheets, the styles its cells name, its epoch, its defined names and its properties.
- `variant Underline = .none | .single | .double | .single_accounting | .double_accounting`: How a line under a font is drawn.
- `record Font(name: str, size: f64, color: str, bold: bool, italic: bool, underline: Underline, strike: bool)`: A font.
- `variant Pattern = .none | .solid | .gray_0625 | .gray_125 | .light_gray | .medium_gray | .dark_gray | .dark_horizontal | .dark_vertical | .dark_down | .dark_up | .dark_grid | .dark_trellis | .light_horizontal | .light_vertical | .light_down | .light_up | .light_grid | .light_trellis`: How a cell's background is filled.
- `record Fill(pattern: Pattern, color: str, background: str)`: A cell's fill: a pattern of one colour over another.
- `variant Line = .none | .thin | .medium | .thick | .dashed | .dotted | .double | .hair | .medium_dashed | .dash_dot | .medium_dash_dot | .dash_dot_dot | .medium_dash_dot_dot | .slant_dash_dot`: How one edge of a cell is drawn.
- `record Edge(line: Line, color: str)`: One edge of a cell.
- `record Border(left: Edge, right: Edge, top: Edge, bottom: Edge)`: The four edges of a cell.
- `variant Horizontal = .general | .left | .center | .right | .fill | .justify | .center_continuous | .distributed`: Where a cell's content stands across it.
- `variant Vertical = .bottom | .center | .top | .justify | .distributed`: Where a cell's content stands up and down it.
- `record Style(font: Font, fill: Fill, border: Border, horizontal: Horizontal, vertical: Vertical, wrap: bool, number_format: str)`: A cell's style: the small set this package reads and writes.
- `record ReadOptions(max_bytes: i64, max_cells: i64)`: How much of a file reading may spend: a file past either bound fails `limit`.
- `function default_read_options() -> ReadOptions`, called `xlsx.default_read_options()`: The options `load` reads with: `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` and `DEFAULT_MAX_CELLS`.
- `function load(path: str) -> Workbook?`, called `xlsx.load(path)`: The workbook in the file at `path`, read with `default_read_options`. Fails as `read` does, and as `fs.open` fails.
- `function load_with(path: str, options: ReadOptions) -> Workbook?`, called `xlsx.load_with(path, options)`: The workbook in the file at `path`, read within the bounds `options` set. Fails as `read` does, and as `fs.open` fails.
- `function read(from: io.Stream, options: ReadOptions) -> Workbook?`, called `xlsx.read(from, options)`: The workbook in `from`, every sheet read whole. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode(data: [u8], options: ReadOptions) -> Workbook?`, called `xlsx.decode(data, options)`: The workbook whose file's bytes are `data`, read as `read` reads a file. Fails as `read` does.
- `function save(workbook: Workbook, path: str) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.save(workbook, path)`: Writes `workbook` to a new file at `path`, or over the file there. Fails as `write` does, and as `fs.create` fails.
- `function write(workbook: Workbook, to: io.Stream) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.write(workbook, to)`: Writes `workbook` to `to` as an `.xlsx` file: its sheets, cells, styles, names and properties. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode(workbook: Workbook) -> [u8]?`, called `xlsx.encode(workbook)`: `workbook` as the bytes of an `.xlsx` file, the same bytes `write` writes. Fails as `write` does but for the stream's failures.
- `function new_workbook() -> Workbook`, called `xlsx.new_workbook()`: A workbook with no sheet, the default style alone, the 1900 epoch, no name and no property.
- `function new_sheet(name: str) -> Sheet`, called `xlsx.new_sheet(name)`: An empty sheet named `name`, shown, with no cell and nothing frozen.
- `function add_sheet(@workbook: Workbook, s: Sheet) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.add_sheet(@workbook, s)`: Adds `s` after the sheets of `workbook`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function default_style() -> Style`, called `xlsx.default_style()`: The style of a cell `default_style` answers: Calibri of 11 points, no fill, no border, aligned by default, the number format `General`.
- `function add_style(@workbook: Workbook, style: Style) -> i64`, called `xlsx.add_style(@workbook, style)`: The index in `wb.styles` of a style equal to `style`, added at the end where none is.
- `function add_name(@workbook: Workbook, name: DefinedName) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.add_name(@workbook, name)`: Adds a defined name to `workbook`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_value(@s: Sheet, row: i64, column: i64, value: Value) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.set_value(@s, row: row, column: column, value)`: Sets the value of the cell at `row` and `column` of `s`, made where it is not there; its formula and its style are kept. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function set_formula(@s: Sheet, row: i64, column: i64, formula: str) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.set_formula(@s, row: row, column: column, formula)`: Sets the formula of the cell at `row` and `column` of `s`, made where it is not there; its value is kept as the value last computed. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_style(@s: Sheet, row: i64, column: i64, style: i64) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.set_style(@s, row: row, column: column, style: style)`: Sets the style of the cell at `row` and `column` of `s`, made where it is not there; its value and its formula are kept. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_row(@s: Sheet, values: [Value]) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.add_row(@s, values)`: Writes `values` into the row after the last row of `s` that holds a cell, from column 0; into row 0 of a sheet with none. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function merge(@s: Sheet, area: Area) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.merge(@s, area)`: Merges the cells of `area` of `s` into one, which shows the value of its top-left cell. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_column_width(@s: Sheet, first: i64, last: i64, width: f64) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.set_column_width(@s, first: first, last: last, width)`: Sets the width of the columns `first` to `last` of `s`, splitting or replacing the runs already set over them. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_row_height(@s: Sheet, row: i64, height: f64) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.set_row_height(@s, row, height)`: Sets the height of the row `row` of `s`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function freeze(@s: Sheet, rows: i64, columns: i64) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.freeze(@s, rows: rows, columns: columns)`: Freezes the first `rows` rows and the first `columns` columns of `s`; 0 and 0 unfreezes it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add_link(@s: Sheet, link: Link) -> ()?`, called `xlsx.add_link(@s, link)`: Adds `link` to the links of `s`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sheet_of(workbook: Workbook, name: str) -> Sheet?`, called `xlsx.sheet_of(workbook, name)`: The sheet of `workbook` named `name`, its name compared byte for byte. Fails `not_found`.
- `function sheet_names(workbook: Workbook) -> [str]`, called `xlsx.sheet_names(workbook)`: The names of the sheets of `workbook`, in the order their tabs stand.
- `function cell_at(s: Sheet, row: i64, column: i64) -> Cell?`, called `xlsx.cell_at(s, row: row, column: column)`: The cell of `s` at `row` and `column`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function is_before(a: Cell, b: Cell) -> bool`, called `xlsx.is_before(a: a, b: b)`: Whether `a` stands before `b` in a sheet's order: by row, then by column.
- `function value_at(s: Sheet, row: i64, column: i64) -> Value`, called `xlsx.value_at(s, row: row, column: column)`: The value of the cell of `s` at `row` and `column`, `.empty` where there is none.
- `function rows_of(s: Sheet, limit: i64) -> [[Value]]?`, called `xlsx.rows_of(s, limit)`: The values of `s` as rows from row 0 to its last row holding a value or a formula, every row from column 0 to the last column any such cell reaches; `.empty` where no value is. Fails `limit`.
- `function dimension_of(s: Sheet) -> Area?`, called `xlsx.dimension_of(s)`: The smallest area that holds every cell of `s` with a value or a formula. Fails `not_found`.
- `function parse_cell_name(s: str) -> Position?`, called `xlsx.parse_cell_name(s)`: The position the cell name `s` names, `B3` as row 2 and column 1. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_cell_name(row: i64, column: i64) -> str?`, called `xlsx.format_cell_name(row: row, column: column)`: The name of the cell at `row` and `column`: row 2 and column 1 is `B3`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_column_name(s: str) -> i64?`, called `xlsx.parse_column_name(s)`: The column the letters `s` name, `A` as 0 and `AA` as 26. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_column_name(column: i64) -> str?`, called `xlsx.format_column_name(column)`: The letters of `column`: 0 is `A`, 26 is `AA`, 16,383 is `XFD`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_area(s: str) -> Area?`, called `xlsx.parse_area(s)`: The area `s` names: `A1:C3`, or one cell `B2`, the corners in either order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_area(a: Area) -> str?`, called `xlsx.format_area(a)`: The name of `a`: `A1:C3`, or `B2` for an area of one cell. Fails `invalid`.
- `function serial_of(date: time.DateTime, epoch: Epoch) -> f64?`, called `xlsx.serial_of(date, epoch)`: The serial number Excel holds for `date` by `epoch`: the days since the epoch, the time of day their fraction. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function date_of(serial: f64, epoch: Epoch) -> time.DateTime?`, called `xlsx.date_of(serial, epoch)`: The moment the serial number `serial` names by `epoch`, rounded to the millisecond. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_date_format(code: str) -> bool`, called `xlsx.is_date_format(code)`: Whether the number format `code` shows a date or a time: a `y`, `m`, `d`, `h` or `s` outside quotes, brackets and escapes, or `AM/PM`.
- `function format_code_of(id: i64) -> str?`, called `xlsx.format_code_of(id)`: The code of the built-in number format numbered `id`: 14 is `mm-dd-yy`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function format_value(v: Value) -> str`, called `xlsx.format_value(v)`: `v` as plain text: a number in the fewest digits that read back as it, a whole one with no point; `TRUE` or `FALSE`; a date as `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss`, with milliseconds where it has any; an error as Excel writes it; nothing for `.empty`.


### jobs/postgres_store

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/jobs/postgres_store`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jobs/postgres_store/).

Jobs kept in PostgreSQL, in a table of the program's own database, as river keeps them: a job enqueued in the program's own transaction is kept exactly where that transaction commits, a worker claims the next job ready with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so any number of workers each claim a job once without waiting on each other, and a job completed in the program's own transaction is completed exactly where the work it did commits.

- `function schema() -> str`, called `postgres_store.schema()`: The script that makes the store's tables and indexes where they are not, for a program that keeps its schema in migrations: run it once with `postgres.exec_script`, or as the up script of a migration.
- `function install(@db: postgres.Db) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.install(@db)`: Makes the store's tables and indexes where they are not, in the first schema of the connection's `search_path`. Fails `permission`.
- `function enqueue(@db: postgres.Db, job: jobs.Job) -> i64?`, called `postgres_store.enqueue(@db, job)`: Enqueues `job` and answers its id. Fails `exists`.
- `function enqueue_many(@db: postgres.Db, batch: [jobs.Job]) -> [i64]?`, called `postgres_store.enqueue_many(@db, batch)`: Enqueues every job of `batch`, all or none, and answers their ids in its order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function find_unique(@db: postgres.Db, key: str) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.find_unique(@db, key)`: The job not finished, waiting or running, that holds the unique key `key`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function claim(@db: postgres.Db, worker: jobs.Worker) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.claim(@db, worker)`: Claims the next job ready in `worker`'s queues and answers it running, its lease held for `worker.lease`: the first by priority, then by when it became due, then by id, in any queue of the worker that is not paused. Fails `not_found`.
- `function complete(@db: postgres.Db, claimed: jobs.Info, output: json.Value) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.complete(@db, claimed, output)`: Marks the claimed attempt done, the job completed, keeping `output`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function fail_attempt(@db: postgres.Db, worker: jobs.Worker, claimed: jobs.Info, error: str) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.fail_attempt(@db, worker, claimed, error)`: Marks the claimed attempt failed with `error`, and answers the job as it now stands: waiting a wait of `worker.backoff` before its next attempt, or failed for good where it had no attempt left, or cancelled where its cancellation was asked while it ran. Fails `not_found`.
- `function fail_attempt_with(@db: postgres.Db, claimed: jobs.Info, error: str, wait: time.Duration) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.fail_attempt_with(@db, claimed, error, wait)`: Marks the claimed attempt failed with `error`, as `fail_attempt` does, the job waiting `wait` before its next attempt where it has one left: the wait the program computed itself, `jobs.retry_wait_with` over a fraction it drew from a generator it seeded, so its waits repeat run after run. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function discard(@db: postgres.Db, claimed: jobs.Info, error: str) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.discard(@db, claimed, error)`: Marks the claimed attempt failed with `error` and the job failed for good, whatever attempts it had left: for an error no retry can mend, a payload the program cannot read. Fails `not_found`.
- `function snooze(@db: postgres.Db, claimed: jobs.Info, wait: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.snooze(@db, claimed, wait)`: Gives the claimed attempt back uncounted, the job to run again after `wait`: for work that must wait for something else, a resource busy, a limit of calls. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function extend(@db: postgres.Db, worker: jobs.Worker, claimed: jobs.Info) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.extend(@db, worker, claimed)`: Renews the claimed attempt's lease for `worker.lease` from now, and answers the job: a job that runs longer than its lease calls it before the lease ends, and so learns whether its cancellation was asked. Fails `stopped`, `not_found`.
- `function rescue(@db: postgres.Db) -> i64?`, called `postgres_store.rescue(@db)`: Gives back every running job whose lease ran out, its worker gone or stalled, and answers how many: each attempt counts as failed with the store's words, and the job is ready again at once, or failed for good where it had no attempt left, or cancelled where that was asked. Fails with the database's failure.
- `function purge(@db: postgres.Db, state: jobs.State, older_than: time.Duration) -> i64?`, called `postgres_store.purge(@db, state, older_than)`: Removes every job of `state` that finished more than `older_than` ago, and answers how many. Fails `invalid`.
- `function pause(@db: postgres.Db, queue: str) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.pause(@db, queue)`: Pauses `queue`: no worker claims from it until `resume`, and its jobs wait. Fails `invalid`.
- `function resume(@db: postgres.Db, queue: str) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.resume(@db, queue)`: Resumes `queue`, paused or not. Fails `invalid`.
- `function paused_queues(@db: postgres.Db) -> [str]?`, called `postgres_store.paused_queues(@db)`: The queues paused, in the order of their names' bytes. Fails with the database's failure.
- `function get(@db: postgres.Db, id: i64) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.get(@db, id)`: The job `id`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function list(@db: postgres.Db, queue: str, state: jobs.State, offset: i64, limit: i64) -> [jobs.Info]?`, called `postgres_store.list(@db, queue, state, offset: offset, limit: limit)`: The jobs of `queue` in `state`, at most `limit` after the first `offset`: for `available` in the order they would be claimed, those ready first; for `running` the lease that runs out first first; for the finished the newest first. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function counts(@db: postgres.Db) -> [jobs.Count]?`, called `postgres_store.counts(@db)`: How many jobs stand in each queue and state, those with none left out, in the order of the queues' names, then of the states' names. Fails with the database's failure.
- `function cancel(@db: postgres.Db, id: i64) -> jobs.State?`, called `postgres_store.cancel(@db, id)`: Cancels job `id` and answers its state after: `cancelled` where it waited or was cancelled already; `running` where it runs, its cancellation asked, which its worker learns from `extend` and which a failed attempt then carries out. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function retry(@db: postgres.Db, id: i64) -> jobs.Info?`, called `postgres_store.retry(@db, id)`: Makes job `id` ready to run now, and answers it: a job failed, cancelled or completed runs again, with one attempt more where it had none left; a job waiting is made ready at once. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `exists`.
- `function delete(@db: postgres.Db, id: i64) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.delete(@db, id)`: Removes job `id`, whatever it stands in but `running`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function enqueue_due(@db: postgres.Db, schedules: [jobs.Periodic]) -> [i64]?`, called `postgres_store.enqueue_due(@db, schedules)`: Enqueues the job of each schedule of `schedules` whose run is due, and answers the ids enqueued: any number of programs may call it, as often as they like, and each due run is enqueued once. Fails `not_found`.
- `function set_limit(@db: postgres.Db, name: str, every: time.Duration, burst: i64) -> jobs.Bucket?`, called `postgres_store.set_limit(@db, name, every, burst)`: Makes the limit `name` full, a token every `every` and a burst of `burst`, or gives the limit of that name this rate and burst, holding the tokens it held, as many as the new burst allows, a debt kept: `jobs.bucket` and `jobs.with_rate` kept in the store, where every worker of the database takes from the one limit. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function remove_limit(@db: postgres.Db, name: str) -> ()?`, called `postgres_store.remove_limit(@db, name)`: Removes the limit `name`; a worker that asks it next fails `not_found`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function limit_named(@db: postgres.Db, name: str) -> jobs.Bucket?`, called `postgres_store.limit_named(@db, name)`: The limit `name` as it stands now, its `seen` the server's time of the reading: `jobs.tokens(limit, at: limit.seen)` is what it holds then. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function allow(@db: postgres.Db, name: str, n: i64) -> jobs.Allowed?`, called `postgres_store.allow(@db, name, n)`: Whether `n` tokens of the limit `name` are there now, taking them where they are, as `jobs.allow` does of a bucket the program holds; any number of workers on any number of connections take from it, and none more than it holds. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function reserve(@db: postgres.Db, name: str, n: i64) -> jobs.Reservation?`, called `postgres_store.reserve(@db, name, n)`: Takes `n` tokens of the limit `name` now even if they are not there, and tells how long to wait for them: reservations of every worker queue, each behind the ones before, as `jobs.reserve` does. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function reserve_within(@db: postgres.Db, name: str, n: i64, within: time.Duration) -> jobs.Reservation?`, called `postgres_store.reserve_within(@db, name, n, within)`: `reserve`, the tokens taken only where the wait for them is no longer than `within`, as `jobs.reserve_within` does. Fails `timeout`.
- `function cancel_reservation(@db: postgres.Db, name: str, taken: jobs.Reservation) -> jobs.Bucket?`, called `postgres_store.cancel_reservation(@db, name, taken)`: Gives the reservation `taken` of the limit `name` back, as far as no later taking of any worker has used what it took, as `jobs.cancel` does, and answers the limit after. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.


### jobs/redis_store

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/jobs/redis_store`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jobs/redis_store/).

Jobs kept in Redis, as Sidekiq, asynq and RQ keep them: each job a hash, each queue sorted sets of the jobs ready, waiting, running and finished, and every change a Lua script the server runs whole, so any number of workers each claim a job once and never see one half moved.

- `constant PREFIX: str`, value `"rebel_jobs:"`: The prefix of every key the store writes: `rebel_jobs:job:<id>` for a job's fields, `rebel_jobs:ready:<queue>` and the other sets of a queue, `rebel_jobs:unique:<key>`, `rebel_jobs:periodic:<name>`, `rebel_jobs:limit:<name>` for a limit workers share.
- `function enqueue(@c: redis.Client, job: jobs.Job) -> i64?`, called `redis_store.enqueue(@c, job)`: Enqueues `job` and answers its id. Fails `exists`.
- `function enqueue_many(@c: redis.Client, batch: [jobs.Job]) -> [i64]?`, called `redis_store.enqueue_many(@c, batch)`: Enqueues every job of `batch`, all or none, in one script, and answers their ids in its order. Fails as `enqueue` fails for the first job refused, the message naming its place in `batch`, and then keeps none of them.
- `function find_unique(@c: redis.Client, key: str) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.find_unique(@c, key)`: The job not finished, waiting or running, that holds the unique key `key`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function claim(@c: redis.Client, worker: jobs.Worker) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.claim(@c, worker)`: Claims the next job due in `worker`'s queues and answers it running, its lease held for `worker.lease`: the first by priority, then by when it became due, then by id, in any queue of the worker that is not paused. Fails `not_found`.
- `function complete(@c: redis.Client, claimed: jobs.Info, output: json.Value) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.complete(@c, claimed, output)`: Marks the claimed attempt done, the job completed, keeping `output`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function fail_attempt(@c: redis.Client, worker: jobs.Worker, claimed: jobs.Info, error: str) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.fail_attempt(@c, worker, claimed, error)`: Marks the claimed attempt failed with `error`, and answers the job as it now stands: waiting a wait of `worker.backoff` before its next attempt, or failed for good where it had no attempt left, or cancelled where its cancellation was asked while it ran. Fails `not_found`.
- `function fail_attempt_with(@c: redis.Client, claimed: jobs.Info, error: str, wait: time.Duration) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.fail_attempt_with(@c, claimed, error, wait)`: Marks the claimed attempt failed with `error`, as `fail_attempt` does, the job waiting `wait` before its next attempt where it has one left: the wait the program computed itself, `jobs.retry_wait_with` over a fraction it drew from a generator it seeded, so its waits repeat run after run. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function discard(@c: redis.Client, claimed: jobs.Info, error: str) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.discard(@c, claimed, error)`: Marks the claimed attempt failed with `error` and the job failed for good, whatever attempts it had left: for an error no retry can mend, a payload the program cannot read. Fails `not_found`.
- `function snooze(@c: redis.Client, claimed: jobs.Info, wait: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.snooze(@c, claimed, wait)`: Gives the claimed attempt back uncounted, the job to run again after `wait`: for work that must wait for something else, a resource busy, a limit of calls. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function extend(@c: redis.Client, worker: jobs.Worker, claimed: jobs.Info) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.extend(@c, worker, claimed)`: Renews the claimed attempt's lease for `worker.lease` from now, and answers the job: a job that runs longer than its lease calls it before the lease ends, and so learns whether its cancellation was asked. Fails `stopped`, `not_found`.
- `function rescue(@c: redis.Client) -> i64?`, called `redis_store.rescue(@c)`: Gives back every running job whose lease ran out, its worker gone or stalled, and answers how many: each attempt counts as failed with the store's words, and the job is ready again at once, or failed for good where it had no attempt left, or cancelled where that was asked. Fails as `redis.call` fails.
- `function purge(@c: redis.Client, state: jobs.State, older_than: time.Duration) -> i64?`, called `redis_store.purge(@c, state, older_than)`: Removes every job of `state` that finished more than `older_than` ago, and answers how many. Fails `invalid`.
- `function pause(@c: redis.Client, queue: str) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.pause(@c, queue)`: Pauses `queue`: no worker claims from it until `resume`, and its jobs wait. Fails `invalid`.
- `function resume(@c: redis.Client, queue: str) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.resume(@c, queue)`: Resumes `queue`, paused or not. Fails `invalid`.
- `function paused_queues(@c: redis.Client) -> [str]?`, called `redis_store.paused_queues(@c)`: The queues paused, in the order of their names' bytes. Fails as `redis.call` fails.
- `function get(@c: redis.Client, id: i64) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.get(@c, id)`: The job `id`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function list(@c: redis.Client, queue: str, state: jobs.State, offset: i64, limit: i64) -> [jobs.Info]?`, called `redis_store.list(@c, queue, state, offset: offset, limit: limit)`: The jobs of `queue` in `state`, at most `limit` after the first `offset`: for `available` in the order they would be claimed, those ready first; for `running` the lease that runs out first first; for the finished the newest first. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function counts(@c: redis.Client) -> [jobs.Count]?`, called `redis_store.counts(@c)`: How many jobs stand in each queue and state, those with none left out, in the order of the queues' names, then of the states' names. Fails as `redis.call` fails.
- `function cancel(@c: redis.Client, id: i64) -> jobs.State?`, called `redis_store.cancel(@c, id)`: Cancels job `id` and answers its state after: `cancelled` where it waited or was cancelled already; `running` where it runs, its cancellation asked, which its worker learns from `extend` and which a failed attempt then carries out. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function retry(@c: redis.Client, id: i64) -> jobs.Info?`, called `redis_store.retry(@c, id)`: Makes job `id` ready to run now, and answers it: a job failed, cancelled or completed runs again, with one attempt more where it had none left; a job waiting is made ready at once. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `exists`.
- `function delete(@c: redis.Client, id: i64) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.delete(@c, id)`: Removes job `id`, whatever it stands in but `running`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function enqueue_due(@c: redis.Client, schedules: [jobs.Periodic]) -> [i64]?`, called `redis_store.enqueue_due(@c, schedules)`: Enqueues the job of each schedule of `schedules` whose run is due, and answers the ids enqueued: any number of programs may call it, as often as they like, and each due run is enqueued once. Fails `not_found`.
- `function set_limit(@c: redis.Client, name: str, every: time.Duration, burst: i64) -> jobs.Bucket?`, called `redis_store.set_limit(@c, name, every, burst)`: Makes the limit `name` full, a token every `every` and a burst of `burst`, or gives the limit of that name this rate and burst, holding the tokens it held, as many as the new burst allows, a debt kept: `jobs.bucket` and `jobs.with_rate` kept in the store, where every worker of the server takes from the one limit. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function remove_limit(@c: redis.Client, name: str) -> ()?`, called `redis_store.remove_limit(@c, name)`: Removes the limit `name`; a worker that asks it next fails `not_found`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function limit_named(@c: redis.Client, name: str) -> jobs.Bucket?`, called `redis_store.limit_named(@c, name)`: The limit `name` as it stands now, its `seen` the server's time of the reading: `jobs.tokens(limit, at: limit.seen)` is what it holds then. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function allow(@c: redis.Client, name: str, n: i64) -> jobs.Allowed?`, called `redis_store.allow(@c, name, n)`: Whether `n` tokens of the limit `name` are there now, taking them where they are, as `jobs.allow` does of a bucket the program holds; any number of workers on any number of connections take from it, and none more than it holds. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function reserve(@c: redis.Client, name: str, n: i64) -> jobs.Reservation?`, called `redis_store.reserve(@c, name, n)`: Takes `n` tokens of the limit `name` now even if they are not there, and tells how long to wait for them: reservations of every worker queue, each behind the ones before, as `jobs.reserve` does. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `does_not_fit`.
- `function reserve_within(@c: redis.Client, name: str, n: i64, within: time.Duration) -> jobs.Reservation?`, called `redis_store.reserve_within(@c, name, n, within)`: `reserve`, the tokens taken only where the wait for them is no longer than `within`, as `jobs.reserve_within` does. Fails `timeout`.
- `function cancel_reservation(@c: redis.Client, name: str, taken: jobs.Reservation) -> jobs.Bucket?`, called `redis_store.cancel_reservation(@c, name, taken)`: Gives the reservation `taken` of the limit `name` back, as far as no later taking of any worker has used what it took, as `jobs.cancel` does, and answers the limit after. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `does_not_fit`.


### ui/webview

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/ui/webview`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/ui/webview/).

A web page as a program's interface, in the manner of Tauri: the system's own web view, shown as a widget of a `ui` app, whose page is the HTML, CSS and scripts the program carries, and the program its logic, the two speaking through a bridge of texts and through nothing else.

- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `failure.CLOSED`: The app is closed, or the web view's life has ended.
- `constant INVALID: str`, value `failure.INVALID`: An argument the call cannot take: a path, a content type, a policy, an origin or a text the web view refuses, a widget of another kind or of another app, a text that is no framed call.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The table holds no asset at the path given.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `failure.LIMIT`: The table holds as many assets or as many bytes as it takes, the web view allows as many origins as it takes, or as many texts wait for a page that loads as it keeps.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `failure.UNSUPPORTED`: The system has no web view this program reaches, or a value the framing has no form for (a `nan` in an answer).
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `failure.FAILED`: The system refused for a reason none of the above names; the message carries its words.
- `constant ORIGIN: str`, value `"app://localhost"`: The app's own origin, which every web view serves its assets at.
- `constant DEFAULT_POLICY: str`, value `"default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'"`: The content security policy every response carries where the program set none: everything from the app's own origin and nothing else, an image also from a `data:` URL, no plug-in, no `<base>`, no form sent anywhere, and the page framed by nobody.
- `constant MESSAGE_MOST: i64`, value `16777216`: The most bytes one text takes, either way across the bridge: 16 MiB.
- `constant ASSET_MOST: i64`, value `67108864`: The most bytes one asset's body holds: 64 MiB.
- `constant ASSETS_MOST: i64`, value `4096`: The most assets one web view's table holds.
- `constant BYTES_MOST: i64`, value `268435456`: The most bytes the bodies of one web view's table hold in all: 256 MiB.
- `function webview(@app: ui.App, into: ui.Widget) -> ui.Widget?`, called `webview.webview(@app, into)`: A new web view in `into`, showing no page until `navigate` or `load_html`, at the size the layout gives it: 320 by 240 points, or the room `ui.set_fit` lets it take. Fails `unsupported`, `closed`, `invalid`, `limit`, `failed`.
- `record Asset(path: str, content_type: str, body: [u8])`: A file the web view serves at its path, with its content type and its bytes.
- `function asset(path: str, body: [u8]) -> Asset?`, called `webview.asset(path, body)`: The asset at `path` holding `body`, its content type the one its extension takes (`content_type_of`). Fails `invalid`.
- `function content_type_of(path: str) -> str`, called `webview.content_type_of(path)`: The content type a file at `path` is served with, by its extension: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and every text with `charset=utf-8`, JSON, the image, font, audio and video formats a page loads, and `application/octet-stream`, which no page runs or shows, for an extension none of them is.
- `function put_asset(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, file: Asset) -> ()?`, called `webview.put_asset(@app, view, file)`: Puts `asset` into `view`'s table, replacing the one at its path; the page reads it at its next request. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function remove_asset(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, path: str) -> ()?`, called `webview.remove_asset(@app, view, path)`: Takes the asset at `path` out of `view`'s table: the page's next request for it is 404. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function assets_of(app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget) -> [str]?`, called `webview.assets_of(app, view)`: The paths of the assets `view`'s table holds, in the order first put. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function load_html(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, html: str) -> ()?`, called `webview.load_html(@app, view, html)`: Puts `html` into `view`'s table as `/index.html` and shows it, at `ORIGIN` + `/`: a page written whole by the program, its scripts and styles assets of their own or none. Fails as `put_asset` and `navigate` do.
- `function set_policy(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, policy: str) -> ()?`, called `webview.set_policy(@app, view, policy)`: Sets the content security policy every response of `view` carries from its next request; "" puts `DEFAULT_POLICY` back. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function policy_of(app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget) -> str?`, called `webview.policy_of(app, view)`: The content security policy `view`'s responses carry now. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function allow_origin(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, origin: str) -> ()?`, called `webview.allow_origin(@app, view, origin)`: Lets `view`'s page go to `origin`: shown in the web view, never heard by the bridge. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function allows(app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, url: str) -> bool?`, called `webview.allows(app, view, url)`: Whether a frame of `view`'s page may go to `url`: the app's own origin, `about:blank` and `about:srcdoc`, and an origin the program allowed, as the native side's web view decides it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function navigate(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, path: str) -> ()?`, called `webview.navigate(@app, view, path)`: Has `view` show the page at `path` of `ORIGIN`; it loads at the next `ui.wait`, and the texts posted from now wait for it. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function page_of(app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget) -> str?`, called `webview.page_of(app, view)`: The path `view` was last asked to show, "" before the first. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `record Response(status: i64, content_type: str, length: i64, policy: str)`: What the page of `view` is answered for a request of `method` to `url`.
- `function response_of(app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, method: str, url: str) -> Response?`, called `webview.response_of(app, view, method: method, url: url)`: What `view` answers its page's request of `method` to `url`, as the native side's web view answers it: 200 with the asset's type and length for `GET` or `HEAD` of a path its table holds, a folder's `index.html` for a path ending in `/`, the query ignored; 404 for another origin or a path it does not hold; 405 for another method. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function post(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, text: str) -> ()?`, called `webview.post(@app, view, text)`: Posts `text` to `view`'s page: handed to the function the page gave `heroes.receive`, in the order posted, once a page of `ORIGIN` has loaded; never to a page of another origin. Fails `invalid`, `limit`, `closed`, `failed`.
- `function print_page(@app: ui.App, view: ui.Widget, settings: printing.Settings, ask: bool) -> ui.Dialog?`, called `webview.print_page(@app, view, settings, ask)`: Prints the page `view` shows, as Qt's `QWebEnginePage::print` does, and answers at once with the dialog the print is: its outcome comes later from `ui.wait`, `.print_chosen` naming it, which holds the settings the page was printed with once the page is the system's, or `.cancelled` where the person cancelled or the system could not print it. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `unsupported`, `failed`.
- `record Call(id: i64, name: str, args: json.Value)`: A call the page made by `heroes.invoke`.
- `function parse_call(text: str) -> Call?`, called `webview.parse_call(text)`: The call `text` holds, a text the page sent by `heroes.invoke`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_answer(call: Call, value: json.Value) -> str?`, called `webview.format_answer(call, value)`: The text that resolves `call`'s promise with `value`, for `post`. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function format_refusal(call: Call, code: str, msg: str) -> str`, called `webview.format_refusal(call, code: code, msg: msg)`: The text that rejects `call`'s promise with an `Error` whose `code` is `code` and whose message is `msg`, for `post`.
- `function format_event(name: str, data: json.Value) -> str?`, called `webview.format_event(name, data)`: The text of the event `name` with `data`, which calls every function the page gave `heroes.on` for `name`, for `post`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.


### xmldsig

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/xmldsig`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/xmldsig/).

XML Signature, checked and made: a `ds:Signature` of XML Signature 1.1 (W3C, 2013) read and checked against the key a program trusts, its references to the document itself digested over Canonical XML, and an enveloped or detached signature made by a key pair or an HMAC secret.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A signature not of the schema, a digest or a value that does not hold, two elements of one identifier, a key of another kind: `check`, `sign`, `sign_hmac`, `certificates_of`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A reference naming no element: `check`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: An algorithm, a transform or a reference not read here: `check`, `sign`.
- `constant SPACE: str`, value `"http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#"`: The namespace of XML Signature's elements.
- `variant Method = .rsa_sha256 | .rsa_sha384 | .rsa_sha512 | .rsa_pss_sha256 | .rsa_pss_sha384 | .rsa_pss_sha512 | .ecdsa_sha256 | .ecdsa_sha384 | .ed25519 | .hmac_sha256 | .hmac_sha384 | .hmac_sha512`: How a signature is made.
- `variant Digest = .sha256 | .sha384 | .sha512 | .sha3_256 | .sha3_512`: The digest of a reference.
- `function method_uri(method: Method) -> str`, called `xmldsig.method_uri(method)`: The identifier XML Signature writes for `method`.
- `function digest_uri(digest: Digest) -> str`, called `xmldsig.digest_uri(digest)`: The identifier XML Signature writes for `digest`.
- `variant Verifier = .certificate(v: x509.Certificate) | .public_key(der: [u8]) | .secret(key: [u8])`: What a signature is checked by: the key a program trusts, never one the signature carries.
- `record CheckOptions(id_attributes: [str])`: How `check` finds the element a reference names.
- `function default_check_options() -> CheckOptions`, called `xmldsig.default_check_options()`: The options that read `ID`, `Id` and `id` as identifiers.
- `record Signed(uri: str, whole: bool, place: [i64], element: xml.Element)`: One element a signature covers, as `check` found it.
- `record Checked(method: str, signed: [Signed])`: What a signature that holds covers.
- `function signature_places(doc: xml.Document) -> [[i64]]`, called `xmldsig.signature_places(doc)`: The places of every `ds:Signature` element of `doc`, in document order.
- `function check(doc: xml.Document, signature: [i64], verifier: Verifier, options: CheckOptions) -> Checked?`, called `xmldsig.check(doc, signature, verifier, options)`: What the signature at `signature` in `doc` covers, once its value holds for `verifier` and every reference's digest matches. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function certificates_of(doc: xml.Document, signature: [i64]) -> [x509.Certificate]?`, called `xmldsig.certificates_of(doc, signature)`: The certificates the signature at `signature` carries in its `KeyInfo`, in order: what the signer says it signed with, which proves nothing until the program matches one to a key it trusts. Fails `invalid`.
- `record SignOptions(method: Method, digest: Digest, canonical: xml.CanonicalOptions, id_attribute: str, certificates: [x509.Certificate])`: How `sign` and `sign_hmac` make a signature.
- `function default_sign_options(method: Method) -> SignOptions`, called `xmldsig.default_sign_options(method)`: The options of `method` with SHA-256, the exclusive form without comments, identifiers in `ID` and no certificate: what SAML 2.0 signs with.
- `function sign(doc: xml.Document, parent: [i64], before: i64, signed: [[i64]], key: keypairs.PrivateKey, options: SignOptions) -> xml.Document?`, called `xmldsig.sign(doc, parent, before, signed, key, options)`: `doc` with a signature by `key` of the elements at `signed` put in as child `before` of the element at `parent`: enveloped where it stands inside an element it signs, detached where beside it. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function sign_hmac(doc: xml.Document, parent: [i64], before: i64, signed: [[i64]], secret: [u8], options: SignOptions) -> xml.Document?`, called `xmldsig.sign_hmac(doc, parent, before, signed, secret, options)`: `doc` with an HMAC signature under `secret` of the elements at `signed` put in as child `before` of the element at `parent`, as `sign` puts one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sign_bytes(message: [u8], key: keypairs.PrivateKey, method: Method) -> [u8]?`, called `xmldsig.sign_bytes(message, key, method)`: The signature of `message` by `key` under `method`, its value as XML Signature writes one: an ECDSA value as its two halves side by side, not DER. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function check_bytes(message: [u8], value: [u8], method: str, verifier: Verifier) -> ()?`, called `xmldsig.check_bytes(message: message, value: value, method, verifier)`: Succeeds where `value` is a signature of `message` that holds for `verifier` under the method whose identifier is `method`, as a query of SAML's HTTP-Redirect binding names it in `SigAlg`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.


### x509/pkcs12

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/x509/pkcs12`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/x509/pkcs12/).

PKCS #12 (RFC 7292), the `.pfx` and `.p12` files Windows, macOS, Java, OpenSSL and load balancers import and export a key and its certificates in, read and written: the keys, the certificates, the revocation lists and the secrets of a file, each with its name and its key identifier; the key and the chain that belong together; and a file made of a key and its chain, or of trusted certificates alone, as Java's trust stores are.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A file that is not what RFC 7292 says, the message saying which part; a file with no MAC given to `decode`; an argument refused by `encode`.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: No key in the file, or no certificate that is the key's: `identities_of`.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The password does not open the file: its MAC does not hold, or, where it has none, a content does not decipher.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A scheme, a digest or a mode this package does not read, the message naming it; an iteration count above `MAX_ITERATIONS`.
- `constant MAX_ITERATIONS: i64`, value `derive.MAX_ITERATIONS`: The most iterations a file is read or written with, ten million: a count is the writer's and the time is the reader's.
- `constant MIN_ITERATIONS: i64`, value `writing.MIN_ITERATIONS`: The fewest iterations `encode` writes with, RFC 8018 § 4.2's 1000.
- `constant ANY_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE: str`, value `writing.ANY_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE`: The purpose Java trusts a certificate of a trust store for, `anyExtendedKeyUsage`, `2.5.29.37.0`.
- `record Attribute(oid: str, values: [asn1.Value])`: An attribute of a bag this package does not read into a field.
- `record Key(der: [u8], name: str, id: [u8], attributes: [Attribute])`: A private key a file holds.
- `record Entry(certificate: x509.Certificate, name: str, id: [u8], trusted_for: [str], attributes: [Attribute])`: A certificate a file holds.
- `record Secret(kind: str, value: asn1.Value, name: str, id: [u8], attributes: [Attribute])`: A secret a file holds, a SecretBag.
- `variant Integrity = .none | .hmac(digest: crypto.Algorithm, iterations: i64) | .pbmac1(digest: crypto.Algorithm, iterations: i64)`: What told that a file is unchanged.
- `record Contents(keys: [Key], certificates: [Entry], crls: [x509.RevocationList], secrets: [Secret], integrity: Integrity)`: What a file holds, in the order it holds it.
- `function decode(der: [u8], password: str) -> Contents?`, called `pkcs12.decode(der, password)`: What the file `der` holds, opened by `password`. Fails `permission`, `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_without_integrity(der: [u8], password: str) -> Contents?`, called `pkcs12.decode_without_integrity(der, password)`: What the file `der` holds, opened by `password`, whether it writes a MAC or not: a MAC written is checked all the same. Fails `permission`.
- `record Identity(key: [u8], chain: [x509.Certificate])`: A key and the certificates that belong to it.
- `function identities_of(contents: Contents) -> [Identity]?`, called `pkcs12.identities_of(contents)`: Each key of `contents` with its chain: its certificate, then the ones of the file that issued it (`x509.chain_of`). Fails `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function chain_pem(identity: Identity) -> str`, called `pkcs12.chain_pem(identity)`: The PEM of `identity`'s chain, the key's certificate first: `tls.Server`'s `chain`.
- `function key_pem(identity: Identity) -> str`, called `pkcs12.key_pem(identity)`: The PEM of `identity`'s key, `PRIVATE KEY` (PKCS #8): `tls.Server`'s `key`.
- `variant Protection = .aes256 | .triple_des`: How a file is written.
- `record Options(protection: Protection, iterations: i64)`: The protection and the iterations a file is written with.
- `function default_options() -> Options`, called `pkcs12.default_options()`: `aes256` with 10000 iterations, Java's count.
- `function encode(key: keypairs.PrivateKey, chain: [x509.Certificate], name: str, password: str, options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `pkcs12.encode(key, chain, name: name, password: password, options)`: The file of `key` and its `chain`, named `name`, under `password`: the key shrouded, the certificates in one enciphered safe, a MAC over both, as OpenSSL lays them out. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function encode_trust_store(certificates: [x509.Certificate], names: [str], password: str, options: Options) -> [u8]?`, called `pkcs12.encode_trust_store(certificates, names, password, options)`: A trust store of `certificates`, as Java's: each certificate trusted for `ANY_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE` and named, all in one enciphered safe, a MAC over it, and no key. Fails `invalid`.


### sftp

Layer 6, named `use <rebel>/sftp`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/sftp/).

A client of SFTP, the SSH File Transfer Protocol version 3 (draft-ietf-secsh-filexfer-02) as OpenSSH's `sftp-server` speaks it, over a channel of an `ssh` client: files opened, read and written, their attributes read and set, folders listed, made and removed, paths renamed, linked and resolved, with OpenSSH's extensions where the server announces them, each checked by the version OpenSSH's `PROTOCOL` gives it: `posix-rename@openssh.com`, `hardlink@openssh.com`, `fsync@openssh.com`, `lsetstat@openssh.com`, `statvfs@openssh.com`, `fstatvfs@openssh.com`, `limits@openssh.com`, `expand-path@openssh.com`, `copy-data`, `home-directory` and `users-groups-by-id@openssh.com`.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `conn.INVALID`: An argument outside its range, or an answer the protocol does not allow: a malformed packet, a status `BAD_MESSAGE`; the message says where.
- `constant FILE_NOT_FOUND: str`, value `conn.FILE_NOT_FOUND`: A path that names nothing, the language's own code: the status `NO_SUCH_FILE`.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: A name already taken: a folder made, a file made new, a link or a name given where one stands.
- `constant NOT_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `"not_a_directory"`: A path that names something other than a folder where one was owed.
- `constant IS_A_DIRECTORY: str`, value `"is_a_directory"`: A path that names a folder where a file was owed.
- `constant NOT_EMPTY: str`, value `"not_empty"`: A folder removed while it holds something.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `conn.PERMISSION`: The server refused: the status `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `wire.NOT_TEXT`: A name the server holds that is not UTF-8, the language's own code.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `conn.CLOSED`: The session, its channel or its connection ended.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `conn.TIMEOUT`: The client's wait ran out.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `conn.UNSUPPORTED`: The server does not offer what was asked: an extension it did not announce, the status `OP_UNSUPPORTED`, a version older than 3.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `conn.FAILED`: The server failed and its status, `FAILURE`, names no reason; its words are in the message.
- `record Session(state: conn.State)`: An SFTP session on a channel of an `ssh` client.
- `record File(handle: [u8], path: str)`: A file open on the server: the handle the server gave and the path it was opened by.
- `record Attributes(kind: fs.Kind?, size: i64?, permission: i64?, user: i64?, group: i64?, written: time.Instant?, read: time.Instant?, extended: {str: [u8]})`: The attributes of what a path names, as the server gave them at one moment.
- `record Listed(name: str, long_name: str, attributes: Attributes)`: One entry of a folder on the server.
- `record Volume(total: i64, free: i64, available: i64, block_size: i64, files: i64, files_free: i64, files_available: i64, id: i64, read_only: bool, no_setuid: bool, name_max: i64)`: The facts of the volume a path stands on (`statvfs@openssh.com`): its space in bytes and its files.
- `function start(@c: ssh.Client) -> Session?`, called `sftp.start(@c)`: A session of SFTP on a new channel of `c`: the subsystem `sftp` started, the version agreed, the server's extensions and bounds read. Fails `permission`, `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function close(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session) -> ()?`, called `sftp.close(@c, @s)`: Ends `s` and closes its channel; the server closes the files and folders left open. Fails as the connection fails.
- `function extensions(s: Session) -> [str]`, called `sftp.extensions(s)`: The names of the extensions the server announced, in its order.
- `function has_extension(s: Session, name: str) -> bool`, called `sftp.has_extension(s, name)`: Whether the server announced the extension `name`, any version of it.
- `function open(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> File?`, called `sftp.open(@c, @s, path)`: The file `path` names, open to read. Fails `file_not_found`, `permission`.
- `function create(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> File?`, called `sftp.create(@c, @s, path)`: The file `path` names, open to write from its start: made where it is not there, emptied where it is, its permission 0o666 less the server's mask. Fails as `open_with` does.
- `function open_with(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, access: fs.Access, permission: i64) -> File?`, called `sftp.open_with(@c, @s, path, access, permission)`: The file `path` names, open as `access` says, made with `permission` where `access` makes it. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `exists`, `file_not_found`.
- `function close_file(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File) -> ()?`, called `sftp.close_file(@c, @s, file)`: Closes `file` on the server. Fails `failed`.
- `function read(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File, offset: i64, n: i64) -> [u8]?`, called `sftp.read(@c, @s, file, offset: offset, n: n)`: Up to `n` bytes of `file` from `offset`: fewer only where the file ends first, empty at or past its end. Fails `invalid`, `is_a_directory`.
- `function write(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File, offset: i64, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `sftp.write(@c, @s, file, offset, data)`: Writes `data` to `file` at `offset`, where a file is longer it is overwritten and where shorter it grows. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function read_bytes(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> [u8]?`, called `sftp.read_bytes(@c, @s, path)`: The bytes of the file at `path`, all of them. Fails `file_not_found`, `is_a_directory`.
- `function write_bytes(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `sftp.write_bytes(@c, @s, path, data)`: Writes `data` as the whole of the file at `path`: made where it is not there, its permission 0o666 less the server's mask, and emptied first where it is. Fails as `create` and `write` do.
- `function file_info(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File) -> Attributes?`, called `sftp.file_info(@c, @s, file)`: The attributes of the open `file`. Fails where the server refuses.
- `function sync(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File) -> ()?`, called `sftp.sync(@c, @s, file)`: Asks the server to write `file`'s bytes to its disk before answering (`fsync@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function truncate_file(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File, length: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.truncate_file(@c, @s, file, length)`: Makes the open `file` `length` bytes long: shorter, it loses its end; longer, its new bytes are zero. Fails `invalid`.
- `function set_file_permission(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File, permission: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_file_permission(@c, @s, file, permission)`: Sets the permission bits of the open `file`. Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function set_file_owner(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File, user: i64, group: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_file_owner(@c, @s, file, user: user, group: group)`: Gives the open `file` to the user and the group of those numbers, -1 leaving either as it is. Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function set_file_times(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File, written: time.Instant, accessed: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_file_times(@c, @s, file, written: written, accessed: accessed)`: Sets the times of the last write and the last read of the open `file`, in whole seconds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function info(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> Attributes?`, called `sftp.info(@c, @s, path)`: The attributes of what `path` names, every link followed. Fails `file_not_found`.
- `function link_info(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> Attributes?`, called `sftp.link_info(@c, @s, path)`: The attributes of what `path` names, of the link itself where it names one. Fails as `info` does.
- `function set_permission(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, permission: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_permission(@c, @s, path, permission)`: Sets the permission bits of what `path` names, every link followed. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `file_not_found`.
- `function set_owner(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, user: i64, group: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_owner(@c, @s, path, user: user, group: group)`: Gives what `path` names, every link followed, to the user and the group of those numbers, -1 leaving either as it is. Fails `invalid`, `permission`, `file_not_found`.
- `function set_times(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, written: time.Instant, accessed: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_times(@c, @s, path, written: written, accessed: accessed)`: Sets the times of the last write and the last read of what `path` names, every link followed, in whole seconds. Fails `invalid`, `file_not_found`.
- `function truncate(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, length: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.truncate(@c, @s, path, length)`: Makes the file `path` names, every link followed, `length` bytes long: shorter, it loses its end; longer, its new bytes are zero. Fails `invalid`, `file_not_found`, `is_a_directory`.
- `function read_dir(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> [Listed]?`, called `sftp.read_dir(@c, @s, path)`: The entries of the folder `path`, sorted by their names' bytes, `.` and `..` never among them; a link is listed as a link. Fails `file_not_found`, `not_a_directory`, `not_text`.
- `function make_dir(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.make_dir(@c, @s, path)`: Makes the folder `path`, its permission 0o777 less the server's mask. Fails `exists`, `file_not_found`, `permission`.
- `function make_dir_with(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, permission: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.make_dir_with(@c, @s, path, permission)`: Makes the folder `path` with the permission `permission`, less the server's mask. Fails `invalid`, `permission`.
- `function make_dir_all(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.make_dir_all(@c, @s, path)`: Makes the folder `path` and every folder above it that is not there. Fails `not_a_directory`.
- `function remove(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.remove(@c, @s, path)`: Removes the file or the link at `path`; a link is removed, never what it names. Fails `file_not_found`, `is_a_directory`, `permission`.
- `function remove_dir(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.remove_dir(@c, @s, path)`: Removes the empty folder `path`. Fails `file_not_found`, `not_a_directory`, `not_empty`, `permission`.
- `function remove_all(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.remove_all(@c, @s, path)`: Removes `path` with everything it holds; a link inside is removed, never followed. Fails `file_not_found`.
- `function rename(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, from: str, to: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.rename(@c, @s, from: from, to: to)`: Gives `from` the name `to`, where nothing is at `to`: SFTP's own rename, which never replaces. Fails `exists`, `file_not_found`, `permission`.
- `function posix_rename(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, from: str, to: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.posix_rename(@c, @s, from: from, to: to)`: Gives `from` the name `to` as POSIX's `rename` does, at once, a file at `to` replaced (`posix-rename@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`, `file_not_found`.
- `function read_link(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> str?`, called `sftp.read_link(@c, @s, path)`: The text the link `path` holds. Fails `file_not_found`, `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function symlink(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, target: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.symlink(@c, @s, target: target, name: name)`: Makes `name` a symbolic link holding `target`. Fails `exists`, `file_not_found`.
- `function hard_link(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, existing: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `sftp.hard_link(@c, @s, existing: existing, name: name)`: Makes `name` a second name of the file `existing` names, a hard link (`hardlink@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`, `exists`, `file_not_found`.
- `function resolve(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> str?`, called `sftp.resolve(@c, @s, path)`: The absolute path `path` names on the server, cleaned, every link followed: `resolve(".")` is the folder the session starts in. Fails `file_not_found`, `not_text`.
- `function volume(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> Volume?`, called `sftp.volume(@c, @s, path)`: The facts of the volume `path` stands on (`statvfs@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`, `file_not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function set_link_permission(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, permission: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_link_permission(@c, @s, path, permission)`: Sets the permission bits of the link itself where `path` names one, and of what it names where it names no link (`lsetstat@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function set_link_owner(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, user: i64, group: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_link_owner(@c, @s, path, user: user, group: group)`: Gives the link itself where `path` names one, and what it names where it names no link, to the user and the group of those numbers, -1 leaving either as it is (`lsetstat@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function set_link_times(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str, written: time.Instant, accessed: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `sftp.set_link_times(@c, @s, path, written: written, accessed: accessed)`: Sets the times of the last write and the last read of the link itself where `path` names one, and of what it names where it names no link, in whole seconds (`lsetstat@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`.
- `function expand(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, path: str) -> str?`, called `sftp.expand(@c, @s, path)`: The path `path` names with a leading `~` or `~user` expanded to a home folder, made absolute and cleaned as `resolve` does (`expand-path@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`, `file_not_found`, `not_text`.
- `function home(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, user: str) -> str?`, called `sftp.home(@c, @s, user)`: The home folder of the user `user` on the server (`home-directory`). Fails `unsupported`, `failed`, `not_text`.
- `function copy_range(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, from: File, from_offset: i64, n: i64, to: File, to_offset: i64) -> ()?`, called `sftp.copy_range(@c, @s, from: from, from_offset: from_offset, n: n, to: to, to_offset: to_offset)`: Copies `n` bytes of `from` at `from_offset` to `to` at `to_offset`, the server reading and writing them itself, so they never cross the network (`copy-data`). Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function user_names(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, users: [i64]) -> {i64: str}?`, called `sftp.user_names(@c, @s, users)`: The names of the users whose numbers are `users`, as the server's system knows them (`users-groups-by-id@openssh.com`). Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`.
- `function group_names(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, groups: [i64]) -> {i64: str}?`, called `sftp.group_names(@c, @s, groups)`: The names of the groups whose numbers are `groups`, as the server's system knows them (`users-groups-by-id@openssh.com`). Fails as `user_names` does.
- `function file_volume(@c: ssh.Client, @s: Session, file: File) -> Volume?`, called `sftp.file_volume(@c, @s, file)`: The facts of the volume the open `file` stands on (`fstatvfs@openssh.com`). Fails as `volume` does.


### web

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/web`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/web/).

Routes for an HTTP server in the manner of Go's Echo: explicit routes, values, no magic.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a pattern, a prefix or a name that is not one; of a request's body that is not what a step reads; and of a path whose escapes do not read.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a request no route takes, of a name no route has, of a parameter, a cookie or a token the request does not hold.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a route whose method and shape a router holds already, and of a name given to a second pattern.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a cookie that would pass `MOST_COOKIE_BYTES`.
- `record Route(method: str, pattern: str, name: str, groups: [str], steps: [str])`: One route a router holds, as `add` made it.
- `variant ErrorForm = .text | .json`: How this package writes an error's body.
- `record Router(prefix: str, groups: [str], routes: [Route], redirect_slash: bool, errors: ErrorForm, index: routing.Index, steps: [str])`: A set of routes and how a request no route takes is answered.
- `function new_router() -> Router`, called `web.new_router()`: An empty router: no prefix, no group, no step, errors written as text, no slash redirected.
- `function new_group(parent: Router, name: str, prefix: str) -> Router?`, called `web.new_group(parent, name: name, prefix: prefix)`: An empty router for the group `name`, whose routes take `prefix` after the prefix of `parent`, to be mounted into `parent` once its routes are added. Fails `invalid`.
- `function add(@router: Router, method: str, pattern: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `web.add(@router, method: method, pattern: pattern, name: name)`: Adds to `router` the route `name` for `method` and `pattern`. Fails `invalid`, `exists`.
- `function add_any(@router: Router, pattern: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `web.add_any(@router, pattern: pattern, name: name)`: Adds to `router` the route `name` for every method on `pattern`. Fails as `add` does.
- `function mount(@router: Router, group: Router) -> ()?`, called `web.mount(router: @router, group: group)`: Adds to `router` every route of `group`, which `new_group` made from it. Fails `exists`.
- `function path_for(router: Router, name: str, params: [Param]) -> str?`, called `web.path_for(router, name, params)`: The path of the route named `name`, its parameters filled from `params`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `record Param(name: str, value: str)`: One parameter of a route as a request fills it.
- `record Found(name: str, pattern: str, groups: [str], params: [Param], steps: [str])`: The route that takes a request, and what its parameters hold.
- `function route(router: Router, r: http.Request) -> Found?`, called `web.route(router, r)`: The route of `router` that takes `r`, and its parameters. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function allowed_of(router: Router, r: http.Request) -> [str]`, called `web.allowed_of(router, r)`: The methods a route of `router` takes on `r`'s path, sorted by their bytes: what an `Allow` field says.
- `function not_routed(router: Router, r: http.Request) -> http.Response`, called `web.not_routed(router, r)`: The answer to `r` where `route` found no route: what the client should be told.
- `function param_of(found: Found, name: str) -> str`, called `web.param_of(found, name)`: The value of the parameter `name` of `found`, which its route's pattern declares: a value every request the route takes holds, so it is read with no failure to answer.
- `function is_in_group(found: Found, name: str) -> bool`, called `web.is_in_group(found, name)`: Whether `found` was added in the group `name`, or in a group inside it.
- `function json_of(r: http.Request) -> json.Value?`, called `web.json_of(r)`: The body of `r` as a JSON value. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function error_response(form: ErrorForm, status: i64, message: str) -> http.Response`, called `web.error_response(form, status, message)`: A response of `status` whose body says `message` in `form`.
- `function render(status: i64, t: template.Template, name: str, value: json.Value) -> http.Response?`, called `web.render(status, t, name, value)`: A response of `status` whose body is the template `name` of `t` made of `value`. Fails as `template.render_named` does.
- `function with_disposition(response: http.Response, filename: str, download: bool) -> http.Response`, called `web.with_disposition(response, filename, download)`: A copy of `response` that a browser saves as the file `filename`, or shows in the page under that name.
- `record Folder(root: str, index: str, listing: bool, hidden: bool)`: Where `serve_folder` answers from, and how.
- `function default_folder(root: str) -> Folder`, called `web.default_folder(root)`: The usual way to answer from `root`: `index.html` for a folder, no listing, no hidden name.
- `function serve_folder(r: http.Request, folder: Folder, rest: str) -> http.Response`, called `web.serve_folder(r, folder, rest)`: The answer to `r` from the file of `folder` that `rest` names.
- `function serve_file(r: http.Request, file: str) -> http.Response`, called `web.serve_file(r, file)`: The answer to `r` from the file `file`.
- `function sniff(data: [u8]) -> str`, called `web.sniff(data)`: The media type the first bytes of `data` show, by the WHATWG's rules as Go reads them: `application/octet-stream` where they show none.
- `variant Step = .go_on(request: http.Request) | .answer(response: http.Response)`: What a step before a handler answers: go on with the request, or answer here.
- `function before(r: http.Request, steps: [(function(http.Request) -> Step)]) -> Step`, called `web.before(r, steps)`: Runs `steps` on `r` in their order, until one answers.
- `function after(r: http.Request, response: http.Response, steps: [(function(http.Request, http.Response) -> http.Response)]) -> http.Response`, called `web.after(r, response, steps)`: Runs `steps` on `response` in their order, each given `r` and what the one before answered.
- `function before_with<S>(r: http.Request, state: S, steps: [(function(S, http.Request) -> Step)]) -> Step`, called `web.before_with(r, state, steps)`: `before` with `state` handed to each step beside the request: how a step reads the server's keys, settings or data, since a function value holds none of its own (spec § 9).
- `function after_with<S>(r: http.Request, response: http.Response, state: S, steps: [(function(S, http.Request, http.Response) -> http.Response)]) -> http.Response`, called `web.after_with(r, response, state, steps)`: `after` with `state` handed to each step beside the request and the response, as `before_with` hands it.
- `function limit_body(r: http.Request, most_bytes: i64) -> Step`, called `web.limit_body(r, most_bytes)`: Refuses `r` 413 where its body is longer than `most_bytes`.
- `function require_basic(r: http.Request, realm: str, accepts: (function(http.Credentials) -> bool)) -> Step`, called `web.require_basic(r, realm, accepts)`: Refuses `r` 401 unless its Basic credentials are ones `accepts` takes.
- `function require_basic_with<S>(r: http.Request, realm: str, state: S, accepts: (function(S, http.Credentials) -> bool)) -> Step`, called `web.require_basic_with(r, realm, state, accepts)`: `require_basic` with `state` handed to `accepts` beside the credentials: how a program checks them against its own accounts.
- `function challenge_basic(realm: str) -> http.Response`, called `web.challenge_basic(realm)`: The answer 401 that asks for Basic credentials in `realm`.
- `function require_bearer(r: http.Request, realm: str, accepts: (function(str) -> bool)) -> Step`, called `web.require_bearer(r, realm, accepts)`: Refuses `r` unless its Bearer token is one `accepts` takes, as RFC 6750 answers: 401 where it has none or `accepts` refuses it, 400 where the field is no token.
- `function require_bearer_with<S>(r: http.Request, realm: str, state: S, accepts: (function(S, str) -> bool)) -> Step`, called `web.require_bearer_with(r, realm, state, accepts)`: `require_bearer` with `state` handed to `accepts` beside the token: how a program checks a token against its own signing key or its own store.
- `function challenge_bearer(realm: str, error: str) -> http.Response`, called `web.challenge_bearer(realm: realm, error: error)`: The answer that asks for a Bearer token in `realm`, RFC 6750: 401, or 400 for `invalid_request`.
- `record Cors(origins: [str], methods: [str], headers: [str], exposed: [str], credentials: bool, max_age: time.Duration)`: Which other origins a browser may let read the answers, and how, by the Fetch standard's CORS.
- `function default_cors(origins: [str]) -> Cors`, called `web.default_cors(origins)`: The usual CORS for `origins`: the methods `GET`, `HEAD`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `POST` and `DELETE`, the fields the browser asks, no credentials, no age.
- `function preflight(r: http.Request, cors: Cors) -> Step`, called `web.preflight(r, cors)`: Answers `r` 204 where it is a CORS preflight, and lets every other request go on.
- `function with_cors(r: http.Request, response: http.Response, cors: Cors) -> http.Response`, called `web.with_cors(r, response, cors)`: A copy of `response` carrying what lets the page of `r`'s origin read it.
- `function with_request_id(r: http.Request) -> http.Request?`, called `web.with_request_id(r)`: A copy of `r` whose `X-Request-Id` holds an identifier: the one the client sent, or a new one. Fails as `uuid.new_v4` does.
- `function copy_request_id(r: http.Request, response: http.Response) -> http.Response`, called `web.copy_request_id(r, response)`: A copy of `response` carrying `r`'s `X-Request-Id`, where it has one.
- `function log_request(logger: log.Logger, r: http.Request, response: http.Response, started: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `web.log_request(logger, r, response, started)`: Writes one line about `r` and its `response` through `logger`. Fails as `log.write` does.
- `function recover(logger: log.Logger, r: http.Request, answer: http.Response?, form: ErrorForm) -> http.Response`, called `web.recover(logger, r, answer, form)`: The response `answer` holds, or, where it is a failure, 500 and a line through `logger` saying the failure.
- `function gzip(r: http.Request, response: http.Response, min_bytes: i64) -> http.Response`, called `web.gzip(r, response, min_bytes)`: A copy of `response` with its body compressed by gzip, where `r` accepts it and it is worth it: `http.with_compression`, by gzip alone and past a size.
- `function gunzip_body(r: http.Request, most_bytes: i64) -> Step`, called `web.gunzip_body(r, most_bytes)`: Lets `r` go on with its body decompressed where its `Content-Encoding` is `gzip`, and refuses it where that body does not read.
- `function refuse_cross_origin(r: http.Request, trusted: [str]) -> Step`, called `web.refuse_cross_origin(r, trusted)`: Refuses 403 a request of a method that changes something, sent by a page of another origin, as Go's `CrossOriginProtection` does.
