- `function require_type(r: http.Request, types: [str]) -> Step`, called `web.require_type(r, types)`: Refuses `r` 415 where it has a body whose type is none of `types`.
- `constant METHOD_FIELD: str`, value `"_method"`: The form field in which a `POST` names the method it stands for: `_method`, which `override_method` reads where no `X-HTTP-Method-Override` field is sent.
- `function override_method(r: http.Request) -> Step`, called `web.override_method(r)`: Lets a `POST` go on as the method it stands for, for a client that can send only `GET` and `POST`: the method its `X-HTTP-Method-Override` field names, as Echo's `MethodOverride` reads it, or its form's `METHOD_FIELD`, which is how an HTML form names one, since a form sends `GET` and `POST` alone and sets no field of the header.
- `function format_event(event: http.Event) -> str?`, called `web.format_event(event)`: The text of `event` in the `text/event-stream` format of the WHATWG HTML standard: an `id` line where its id is not "", an `event` line where its name is not "", one `data` line for each line of its data, and the empty line that makes a reader dispatch it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function start_events(s: io.Stream, headers: [http.Header]) -> ()?`, called `web.start_events(s, headers)`: Writes to `s` the head of an event stream kept open: 200, `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache` where `headers` sets none, and `Connection: close`, the stream running to the connection's end. Fails as `http.write_response_head` does.
- `function write_event(s: io.Stream, event: http.Event) -> ()?`, called `web.write_event(s, event)`: Writes `event` to the event stream `s` carries, as `format_event` writes it, at once. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function write_retry(s: io.Stream, ms: i64) -> ()?`, called `web.write_retry(s, ms)`: Writes to the event stream `s` carries a `retry` line: the milliseconds a client waits before it connects again once the stream ends. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_comment(s: io.Stream, text: str) -> ()?`, called `web.write_comment(s, text)`: Writes to the event stream `s` carries a comment, which a reader skips: a line opening with a colon for each line of `text`, what keeps a proxy from closing a connection where no event is said for long. Fails as `io.write` fails.
- `function respond_events(events: [http.Event]) -> http.Response?`, called `web.respond_events(events)`: A response holding `events` whole as an event stream, for a handler that cannot keep a connection open: the client reads them, and connects again once the response ends, after its `retry`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Limiter(rate: f64, burst: i64, most_keys: i64, buckets: {str: limiting.Bucket})`: The token buckets of many clients, one per key, as golang.org/x/time/rate documents one: a bucket holds up to `burst` tokens, refills at `rate` tokens a second, and each request takes one.
- `function new_limiter(rate: f64, burst: i64, most_keys: i64) -> Limiter?`, called `web.new_limiter(rate, burst: burst, most_keys: most_keys)`: A limiter of `rate` tokens a second and `burst` at once, for at most `most_keys` clients at once, every bucket full. Fails `invalid`.
- `function allow(@limiter: Limiter, key: str, now: time.Instant) -> bool`, called `web.allow(@limiter, key, now)`: Takes a token from the bucket of `key` and answers true where it holds one at `now`; else takes none, leaves the bucket as it was and answers false: Go's `Limiter.AllowN` for one.
- `function wait_of(limiter: Limiter, key: str, now: time.Instant) -> time.Duration`, called `web.wait_of(limiter, key, now)`: How long from `now` until the bucket of `key` holds a token: zero where it holds one, so `allow` would answer true.
- `function limit_rate(@limiter: Limiter, r: http.Request, key: str, now: time.Instant, form: ErrorForm) -> Step`, called `web.limit_rate(@limiter, r, key, now, form)`: Lets `r` go on where the bucket of `key` holds a token at `now`, taking it; else answers 429 with `Retry-After`, the whole seconds until it holds one, rounded up.
- `function serve(server: http.Server, l: net.Listener, router: Router, handler: (function(Router, http.Request) -> http.Response)) -> ()?`, called `web.serve(server, l, router, handler)`: Serves every connection `l` accepts, one at a time, until the program asks to stop, each request answered by `handler` with `router`: `http.serve_with` with the router as the program's value. Fails as `http.serve_with` does.
- `function serve_tls(server: http.Server, l: tls.Listener, router: Router, handler: (function(Router, http.Request) -> http.Response)) -> ()?`, called `web.serve_tls(server, l, router, handler)`: `serve` over the TLS connections `l` accepts: `http.serve_tls_with` with the router as the program's value. Fails as `http.serve_tls_with` does.
- `function serve_stream(server: http.Server, stream: io.Stream, remote: str, router: Router, handler: (function(Router, http.Request) -> http.Response)) -> i64`, called `web.serve_stream(server, stream, remote, router, handler)`: Serves the requests that come on `stream`, one after another, and answers how many were answered: `http.serve_stream_with` with the router as the program's value.
- `constant MOST_COOKIE_BYTES: i64`, value `4096`: The most bytes a `Set-Cookie` value this package writes may hold, as gorilla/securecookie bounds its own: a browser keeps 4,096 bytes of a cookie at least (RFC 6265 § 6.1) and no more is promised.
- `record CookieOptions(name: str, path: str, domain: str, max_age: time.Duration, secure: bool, http_only: bool, same_site: str, keys: [[u8]], sealing: [seal.Key])`: How a cookie this package signs or seals is written and read.
- `function default_cookie_options(name: str, ring: [[u8]]) -> CookieOptions`, called `web.default_cookie_options(name, ring)`: Options for a cookie named `name` signed by `ring`: the path `/`, 30 days, `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax`, nothing sealed.
- `function sign_value(ring: [[u8]], name: str, value: str, expires: time.Instant) -> str`, called `web.sign_value(ring, name: name, value: value, expires)`: `value` signed for the cookie `name` with the first of `ring`, valid before `expires`: the value and the end in the clear, and an HMAC-SHA256 tag over the name, the value and the end.
- `function verify_value(ring: [[u8]], name: str, signed: str, now: time.Instant) -> str?`, called `web.verify_value(ring, name: name, signed: signed, now)`: The value `signed` holds for the cookie `name`, as `sign_value` wrote it. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`.
- `function seal_value(ring: [seal.Key], name: str, value: str, expires: time.Instant) -> str?`, called `web.seal_value(ring, name: name, value: value, expires)`: `value` sealed for the cookie `name` under the first of `ring`, valid before `expires`: encrypted and authenticated by `crypto/seal`, the name bound beside it, as gorilla/securecookie's encrypted form keeps a value from the client's eyes. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function open_value(ring: [seal.Key], name: str, sealed: str, now: time.Instant) -> str?`, called `web.open_value(ring, name: name, sealed: sealed, now)`: The value `sealed` holds for the cookie `name`, as `seal_value` wrote it. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `closed`, `not_text`.
- `function secure_cookie_of(r: http.Request, options: CookieOptions, now: time.Instant) -> str?`, called `web.secure_cookie_of(r, options, now)`: The value of the cookie `options.name` that `r` sends, verified or opened as `options` says. Fails `not_found`.
- `function with_secure_cookie(response: http.Response, options: CookieOptions, value: str, now: time.Instant) -> http.Response?`, called `web.with_secure_cookie(response, options, value, now)`: A copy of `response` setting the cookie `options.name` to `value`, signed or sealed as `options` says, for `options.max_age` from `now`. Fails `limit`.
- `function without_cookie(response: http.Response, options: CookieOptions) -> http.Response`, called `web.without_cookie(response, options)`: A copy of `response` that makes the browser forget the cookie `options.name`: an empty value, `Max-Age=0` and an end in 1970.
- `record Session(values: {str: str}, is_new: bool)`: A session kept in a cookie: values the server gave the client to send back, signed or sealed so it cannot change them, as Flask's and gorilla's cookie stores keep one.
- `function new_session() -> Session`, called `web.new_session()`: An empty session, new.
- `function session_of(r: http.Request, options: CookieOptions, now: time.Instant) -> Session?`, called `web.session_of(r, options, now)`: The session `r`'s cookie holds, as `with_session` wrote it. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function with_session(response: http.Response, session: Session, options: CookieOptions, now: time.Instant) -> http.Response?`, called `web.with_session(response, session, options, now)`: A copy of `response` writing `session` into its cookie, as `with_secure_cookie` writes one, its values as a JSON object. Fails `limit`.
- `constant CSRF_FIELD: str`, value `"csrf_token"`: The form field a CSRF token is read from: `csrf_token`.
- `constant CSRF_HEADER: str`, value `"X-CSRF-Token"`: The header field a CSRF token is read from, gorilla/csrf's: `X-CSRF-Token`.
- `constant CSRF_KEY: str`, value `"_csrf"`: The key of `Session.values` under which `csrf_secret` keeps a session's secret.
- `function new_csrf_secret() -> str?`, called `web.new_csrf_secret()`: A new secret for CSRF tokens: 32 bytes from the system's generator, in URL-safe base 64, which the server keeps, in the session or in a signed cookie of its own, and never writes into a page. Fails as `os.random_bytes` does.
- `function csrf_secret(@session: Session) -> str?`, called `web.csrf_secret(@session)`: The CSRF secret `session` keeps, made and kept in it where it has none: the synchronizer token pattern, the secret living as long as the session. Fails as `new_csrf_secret` does.
- `function mask_csrf(secret: str) -> str?`, called `web.mask_csrf(secret)`: The token a page writes in its form, or a script sends in `CSRF_HEADER`, for `secret`: masked anew at each call, so a compressed page never repeats the secret's bytes, as Django and gorilla/csrf mask theirs against BREACH. Fails `invalid`.
- `function csrf_token_of(r: http.Request) -> str?`, called `web.csrf_token_of(r)`: The CSRF token `r` sends: its `CSRF_HEADER` field, else its form's `CSRF_FIELD`, a form sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or as `multipart/form-data`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function check_csrf(r: http.Request, secret: str) -> Step`, called `web.check_csrf(r, secret)`: Refuses `r` 403 where it changes something and its CSRF token does not unmask to `secret`; a safe method goes on.
- `record SecurityHeaders(content_security_policy: str, strict_transport_security: str, content_type_options: str, frame_options: str, referrer_policy: str, permissions_policy: str, opener_policy: str, resource_policy: str, origin_agent_cluster: str, others: [http.Header])`: The fields a response carries against framing, sniffing, leaking its address and loading what it did not mean to: helmet's set, each field "" where it is not written.
- `function default_security_headers() -> SecurityHeaders`, called `web.default_security_headers()`: helmet's defaults, as helmet 8.3.0 answered on 2026-11-17: a policy of `self` for everything, `object-src 'none'`, `upgrade-insecure-requests`; HSTS for a year with subdomains; `nosniff`; `SAMEORIGIN`; `no-referrer`; `same-origin` for both cross-origin policies; `?1`; and its older fields `X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off`, `X-Download-Options: noopen`, `X-Permitted-Cross-Domain-Policies: none` and `X-XSS-Protection: 0`.
- `function minimal_security_headers() -> SecurityHeaders`, called `web.minimal_security_headers()`: Three fields that cost no page anything, each written where a response has none: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, against a page sniffed, framed by another site or followed with its full address; every other field "".
- `function format_hsts(max_age: time.Duration, subdomains: bool, preload: bool) -> str`, called `web.format_hsts(max_age, subdomains: subdomains, preload: preload)`: A `Strict-Transport-Security` value, RFC 6797 § 6.1.
- `function with_security_headers(response: http.Response, headers: SecurityHeaders) -> http.Response`, called `web.with_security_headers(response, headers)`: A copy of `response` carrying each field of `headers` that is not "", where `response` has none of that name, so a handler's own field wins.
- `record Forwarded(address: str, scheme: str, host: str, proxies: i64)`: What a request says of its client once the proxies the program trusts are read through: made by `forwarded_of`.
- `function trusted_networks(list: [str]) -> [net.Network]?`, called `web.trusted_networks(list)`: The networks of `list`, each an address, `10.0.0.1` or `::1`, or a network, `10.0.0.0/8` or `fd00::/8`: the proxies a program trusts. Fails `invalid`.
- `function forwarded_of(r: http.Request, trusted: [net.Network]) -> Forwarded`, called `web.forwarded_of(r, trusted)`: The client of `r`, read through the proxies `trusted` holds: from RFC 7239's `Forwarded` where `r` sends one, else from `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto` and `X-Forwarded-Host`.
- `function etag_of(body: [u8], weak: bool) -> str`, called `web.etag_of(body, weak)`: A strong entity tag for `body`, or a weak one: the first 16 bytes of its SHA-256 in hexadecimal, quoted, `W/` before it where `weak`.
- `function with_etag(r: http.Request, response: http.Response) -> http.Response`, called `web.with_etag(r, response)`: A step after the handler: `response` given a strong `ETag` of its body where it is a 200 to `GET` or `HEAD` with none, then answered 304 where `r` holds its copy, by `If-None-Match` or by `If-Modified-Since` against its `Last-Modified`.
- `function require_acceptable(r: http.Request, offered: [str]) -> Step`, called `web.require_acceptable(r, offered)`: A step that refuses `r` 406 where it accepts none of `offered`, by its `Accept` fields, saying what is offered.
- `function exchange(r: http.Request, router: Router, handler: (function(Router, http.Request) -> http.Response)) -> http.Response?`, called `web.exchange(r, router, handler)`: The response `handler` gives `r` with `router`, carried both ways in memory as a connection would carry them: `http.exchange_with` with the router as the program's value, as Go's `httptest` and Flask's `test_client` try a handler. Fails as `http.exchange_with` does.
- `function serve_until_stopped(server: http.Server, l: net.Listener, router: Router, handler: (function(Router, http.Request) -> http.Response), grace: time.Duration) -> http.Served?`, called `web.serve_until_stopped(server, l, router, handler, grace)`: Serves every connection `l` accepts, one at a time, until the program asks to stop, and ends gracefully: `http.serve_until_stopped` with the router as the program's value. Fails as `http.serve_until_stopped` does.
- `record Check(name: str, outcome: ()?)`: One check a program ran for its health or its readiness: its name and what it found.
- `function health_response(r: http.Request, checks: [Check], detail: bool) -> http.Response`, called `web.health_response(r, checks, detail)`: The answer of a health, liveness or readiness endpoint, `/healthz`, `/livez` or `/readyz` as Kubernetes names them, for the checks a program ran: 200 where every check passed, 503 where one did not.
- `function default_webhook_tolerance() -> time.Duration`, called `web.default_webhook_tolerance()`: How far a webhook's timestamp may stand from the clock that reads it, either way: five minutes, as the specification's libraries allow.
- `function new_webhook_secret() -> str?`, called `web.new_webhook_secret()`: A new secret for signing webhooks: `whsec_` and the standard base 64 of 32 bytes the system's generator draws. Fails as `os.random_bytes` does.
- `function webhook_signature(secret: str, id: str, sent: time.Instant, payload: [u8]) -> str?`, called `web.webhook_signature(secret: secret, id: id, sent, payload)`: The `webhook-signature` of `payload` sent as `id` at `sent`, by the Standard Webhooks specification: `v1,` and the standard base 64 of the HMAC-SHA256 of `id`, `.`, the decimal of `sent`'s Unix seconds, `.` and the payload, keyed by the secret's bytes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function sign_webhook(secret: str, id: str, sent: time.Instant, payload: [u8]) -> [http.Header]?`, called `web.sign_webhook(secret: secret, id: id, sent, payload)`: The three header fields a webhook is sent with, by the Standard Webhooks specification: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function verify_webhook(headers: [http.Header], payload: [u8], secrets: [str], now: time.Instant, tolerance: time.Duration) -> str?`, called `web.verify_webhook(headers, payload, secrets, now, tolerance)`: The id of the webhook `headers` and `payload` carry, where one of `secrets` signed it as the Standard Webhooks specification says and it was sent within `tolerance` of `now`. Fails `invalid`.


### websocket

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/websocket`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/websocket/).

WebSocket (RFC 6455), client and server: a connection that carries whole messages of text or of bytes both ways, framed and masked as the RFC asks, compressed by permessage-deflate (RFC 7692) where both ends agree, and ended by its closing handshake.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A frame, a handshake or an argument that is not what RFC 6455 or RFC 7692 allows; the message says what was found and where.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A frame past `Settings.frame_bytes`, a message past `Settings.message_bytes`, a handshake's head past its limits, or more redirects than a `Client` follows.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: A text message, a text part or a close's reason that is not UTF-8, the language's own code.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection is closed: by its closing handshake, by `drop`, by a failure, or by the peer ending its stream; and, from `net` and `tls`, nothing listening at the address.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The time allowed ran out: a `Client`'s `deadline_ms`, or a deadline `set_deadline` placed.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The program was asked to stop while a call waited (`os.catch_stop`, `os.ask_stop`).
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A host name with no address, from `net`; a close asked of a connection still open, by `closing_of`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A scheme other than `ws` and `wss`, and TLS on a machine with no TLS library, as `tls` fails.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The system refused for a reason none of the codes above names, from `net`, `tls` and `io`; the message carries the system's own words.
- `constant CLOSE_NORMAL: i64`, value `1000`: The close code of a purpose fulfilled: the connection ends as it should.
- `constant CLOSE_GOING_AWAY: i64`, value `1001`: The close code of an end going away: a server going down, a browser leaving a page.
- `constant CLOSE_PROTOCOL_ERROR: i64`, value `1002`: The close code of a frame the RFC refuses, which this package sends with `invalid`.
- `constant CLOSE_UNSUPPORTED_DATA: i64`, value `1003`: The close code of a message of a kind the end does not take, text where it takes bytes alone.
- `constant CLOSE_NO_STATUS: i64`, value `1005`: The code `closing_of` gives a close frame that carried no code.
- `constant CLOSE_ABNORMAL: i64`, value `1006`: The code `closing_of` gives a connection that ended with no close frame received.
- `constant CLOSE_INVALID_PAYLOAD: i64`, value `1007`: The close code of a message whose data does not match its kind, text that is not UTF-8, which this package sends with `not_text`.
- `constant CLOSE_POLICY_VIOLATION: i64`, value `1008`: The close code of a message that breaks the end's policy, where no other code says more.
- `constant CLOSE_MESSAGE_TOO_BIG: i64`, value `1009`: The close code of a message too big to take, which this package sends with `limit`.
- `constant CLOSE_MANDATORY_EXTENSION: i64`, value `1010`: The close code a client sends where the server did not agree an extension the client needs.
- `constant CLOSE_INTERNAL_ERROR: i64`, value `1011`: The close code of a server that met a condition it could not serve.
- `constant CLOSE_SERVICE_RESTART: i64`, value `1012`: The close code of a server restarting: the client may connect again.
- `constant CLOSE_TRY_AGAIN_LATER: i64`, value `1013`: The close code of a server overloaded for now: the client may connect again later.
- `constant CLOSE_BAD_GATEWAY: i64`, value `1014`: The close code of a gateway that had a bad answer from the server behind it.
- `constant CLOSE_TLS_HANDSHAKE: i64`, value `1015`: The code `closing_of` gives a connection whose TLS handshake failed.
- `function is_close_code(code: i64) -> bool`, called `websocket.is_close_code(code)`: Whether `code` may stand in a close frame: 1000 to 1003, 1007 to 1014, and 3000 to 4999, the codes registered for libraries and for private use.
- `function close_name(code: i64) -> str?`, called `websocket.close_name(code)`: The name of a close code as IANA's registry writes it: `Normal Closure` for 1000. Fails `not_found`.
- `variant Message = .text(text: str) | .binary(data: [u8])`: A message of data: what `read_message` answers and `write_message` writes.
- `variant Kind = .text | .binary`: The two kinds of a message of data, as a `Part` names them.
- `record Part(kind: Kind, data: [u8], last: bool)`: One fragment of a message, as `read_part` answers it and `write_part` writes it: a message too long to hold whole, or one written as it is made.
- `function data_of(m: Message) -> [u8]`, called `websocket.data_of(m)`: The bytes `m` holds: a text's UTF-8, or the bytes.
- `function kind_of(m: Message) -> Kind`, called `websocket.kind_of(m)`: The kind of `m`.
- `record Settings(frame_bytes: i64, message_bytes: i64, fragment_bytes: i64, close_wait: time.Duration)`: How much a connection reads, and how it writes and waits: made by `default_settings`, its fields changed by the program at any time.
- `function default_settings() -> Settings`, called `websocket.default_settings()`: The usual settings, as Python's `websockets` sets them: frames and messages of 1 MiB at most, every message in one frame, and 10 seconds for the peer's close.
- `record Compression(enabled: bool, level: i64, min_bytes: i64, server_no_context_takeover: bool, client_no_context_takeover: bool, server_max_window_bits: i64, client_max_window_bits: i64)`: Whether and how messages are compressed, by permessage-deflate (RFC 7692): what a client offers and a server accepts.
- `function default_compression() -> Compression`, called `websocket.default_compression()`: Compression turned off, its other fields at their usual values: level 6, every message compressed, both ends keeping their windows, of 15 bits.
- `record Client(settings: Settings, compression: Compression, protocols: [str], origin: str, headers: [http.Header], tls: tls.Client, deadline: time.Duration, redirects: i64, head: http.Limits, proxy: http.Proxy)`: What a client offers and how it connects: made by `default_client`, its fields changed by the program.
- `function default_client() -> Client`, called `websocket.default_client()`: The usual client: `default_settings`, no compression, no subprotocol and no origin, the system's own authorities, 10 seconds to connect, and 10 redirects at most, as Python's `websockets`.
- `record Server(settings: Settings, compression: Compression, protocols: [str], origins: [str], every_origin: bool, headers: [http.Header])`: What a server accepts in an opening request and answers it: made by `default_server`, its fields changed by the program.
- `function default_server() -> Server`, called `websocket.default_server()`: The usual server: `default_settings`, no compression, no subprotocol, and the request's own origin alone, as Go's gorilla and coder take it.
- `variant Role = .client | .server`: Which end of a connection this is: a client masks every frame it writes and reads none masked; a server the other way.
- `record Conn(stream: io.Stream, role: Role, protocol: str, extensions: str, headers: [http.Header], settings: Settings, state: engine.State)`: A WebSocket connection: made by `connect`, `client_over`, `upgrade` or `conn_of`, read and written by this package's functions.
- `record Closing(code: i64, reason: str, sent: i64)`: How a connection ended, as `closing_of` answers it.
- `function is_open(c: Conn) -> bool`, called `websocket.is_open(c)`: Whether `c` is open: no close sent or received, no failure, not dropped.
- `function closing_of(c: Conn) -> Closing?`, called `websocket.closing_of(c)`: The close frames `c` received and sent, once it is no longer open. Fails `not_found`.
- `function pongs_of(c: Conn) -> i64`, called `websocket.pongs_of(c)`: How many pongs `c` has received, an answer to its `write_ping` or one the peer sent unasked.
- `function last_pong_of(c: Conn) -> [u8]`, called `websocket.last_pong_of(c)`: The bytes of the last pong `c` received, none before the first: what a program compares with the ping it wrote.
- `function connect(target: str, client: Client) -> Conn?`, called `websocket.connect(target, client)`: A connection to `target`, opened by the opening handshake: a TCP connection for `ws://`, TLS for `wss://`. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function client_over(@stream: io.Stream, target: str, client: Client) -> Conn?`, called `websocket.client_over(@stream, target, client)`: A connection opened by the opening handshake over `stream`, a stream the program already holds connected to the server of `target`: through a proxy's tunnel, or over a pipe in a test. Fails as `connect` does once the connection is made, a redirect included, since nothing is followed here; and as `io.read` and `io.write` fail.
- `function new_key() -> str?`, called `websocket.new_key()`: A new `Sec-WebSocket-Key`: sixteen bytes of the system's generator for keys, as base 64. Fails as `os.random_bytes` does.
- `function accept_key(key: str) -> str`, called `websocket.accept_key(key)`: The `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` a server answers the `Sec-WebSocket-Key` `key` with: the base 64 of the SHA-1 of the key and RFC 6455's own GUID.
- `function is_upgrade(r: http.Request) -> bool`, called `websocket.is_upgrade(r)`: Whether `r` asks to become a WebSocket connection: a `GET` whose `Connection` holds `upgrade` and whose `Upgrade` holds `websocket`, in any case.
- `function protocols_of(r: http.Request) -> [str]`, called `websocket.protocols_of(r)`: The subprotocols `r` offers, in its order: every value of its `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` fields, split at their commas.
- `function upgrade(@reader: io.Reader, r: http.Request, server: Server) -> Conn?`, called `websocket.upgrade(@reader, r, server)`: The connection `r` asks for, its `101` answer written on `reader`'s stream: how a server that read and routed `r` itself turns it into a WebSocket. Fails `invalid`.
- `function conn_of(@stream: io.Stream, role: Role, settings: Settings) -> Conn`, called `websocket.conn_of(@stream, role, settings)`: A connection over `stream`, whose opening handshake is done already or was never needed: no subprotocol, no extension.
- `function read_message(@c: Conn) -> Message?`, called `websocket.read_message(@c)`: The next message of data `c` receives, waiting for it: its fragments joined, decompressed and checked. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `not_text`, `limit`, `timeout`, `stopped`.
- `function held_of(c: Conn) -> i64`, called `websocket.held_of(c)`: How many frames `c` holds whole, read from its stream and not taken yet: what a program waiting with `poll` asks before it waits, as this package's head says.
- `function read_ready(@c: Conn) -> [Message]?`, called `websocket.read_ready(@c)`: The messages of data `c` completes with what it holds and at most one read of its stream: what a program serving many connections on one thread calls where `poll` tells the stream readable or `held_of` is above 0, as this package's head says, so it never waits there. Fails as `read_message` does.
- `function read_part(@c: Conn) -> Part?`, called `websocket.read_part(@c)`: The next fragment of a message of data `c` receives, waiting for it: a message read as it comes, never held whole. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_json(@c: Conn) -> json.Value?`, called `websocket.read_json(@c)`: The JSON value the next message of data `c` receives holds, text or bytes. Fails `not_text`.
- `function write_message(@c: Conn, m: Message) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_message(@c, m)`: Writes `m` to `c`, compressed where the two ends agreed it and it is long enough, in fragments where `c`'s settings say. Fails `closed`, `invalid`.
- `function write_text(@c: Conn, text: str) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_text(@c, text)`: Writes the text `text` to `c` as one message, as `write_message` does. Fails as `write_message` does.
- `function write_binary(@c: Conn, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_binary(@c, data)`: Writes the bytes `data` to `c` as one message, as `write_message` does. Fails as `write_message` does.
- `function write_part(@c: Conn, part: Part) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_part(@c, part)`: Writes `part` to `c` as the next frame of a message written as it is made: the first part begins it, the one with `last` ends it. Fails `invalid`, `not_text`, `closed`.
- `function write_json(@c: Conn, value: json.Value) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_json(@c, value)`: Writes `value` to `c` as a message of text, as `json.format` writes it. Fails as `json.format` and `write_message` fail.
- `function write_ping(@c: Conn, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_ping(@c, data)`: Writes a ping holding `data` to `c`; the peer answers with a pong holding the same bytes, which a read counts (`pongs_of`). Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function write_pong(@c: Conn, data: [u8]) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_pong(@c, data)`: Writes a pong holding `data` to `c`, unasked: a heartbeat the peer does not answer. Fails as `write_ping` does.
- `record Prepared(message: Message, frame: [u8])`: A message framed once, to be written to many connections: what a server sending one message to all its clients prepares.
- `function prepare(m: Message) -> Prepared`, called `websocket.prepare(m)`: `m` framed once, as `write_prepared` writes it.
- `function write_prepared(@c: Conn, p: Prepared) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_prepared(@c, p)`: Writes the prepared message `p` to `c`: its frame as it is where `c` is a server writing neither compressed nor in fragments, else framed for `c` as `write_message` frames it. Fails as `write_message` does.
- `function write_close(@c: Conn, code: i64, reason: str) -> ()?`, called `websocket.write_close(@c, code, reason)`: Writes `c`'s close frame and goes on: the closing handshake begun, which a read ends when the peer's close comes. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function close(@c: Conn, code: i64, reason: str) -> ()?`, called `websocket.close(@c, code, reason)`: Ends `c` by the closing handshake: its close written, the peer's awaited for `close_wait_ms` (the messages before it read and dropped), then its stream closed. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function drop(@c: Conn) -> ()?`, called `websocket.drop(@c)`: Closes `c`'s stream at once, with no closing handshake: the peer sees the connection end abnormally (1006). Fails `closed`.
- `function set_deadline(c: Conn, deadline: time.Duration) -> ()?`, called `websocket.set_deadline(c, deadline)`: Makes every later and waiting read and write of `c`'s stream end by `deadline` from now, failing `timeout`: a read so ended loses nothing, and the next read goes on. Fails `invalid`, `closed`, `unsupported`.


### oauth2

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/oauth2`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/oauth2/).

An OAuth 2.0 client (RFC 6749 as RFC 9700 hardens it) and OpenID Connect: the authorization code grant with PKCE, the client credentials, device authorization (RFC 8628), JWT bearer (RFC 7523) and refresh grants, a token's revocation (RFC 7009) and introspection (RFC 7662), an authorization server's metadata (RFC 8414, OpenID Connect Discovery), a protected resource's (RFC 9728), resource indicators (RFC 8707), the issuer of a redirect checked (RFC 9207), a client's metadata document whose URL is its id, and an ID token verified through `jose`.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: An answer or an argument not of its form, a redirect's state or issuer not the one expected, an ID token refused.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A member, a well-known document, or a challenge's parameter absent.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The server answered an OAuth error (RFC 6749 § 5.2): its `error`, its `error_description` and its `error_uri` in the message.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The user denied a device its authorization (`access_denied`).
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: A device code expired before the user answered (`expired_token`).
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: What `jose` or the platform lacks: an ID token signed by an algorithm this platform cannot verify.
- `variant Authentication = .basic | .post | .none | .private_key_jwt(key: jose.Key, algorithm: jose.Algorithm)`: How a client proves itself at the token endpoint (RFC 6749 § 2.3, RFC 7523 § 2.2).
- `record Config(client_id: str, client_secret: str, authentication: Authentication, authorization_endpoint: str, token_endpoint: str, device_authorization_endpoint: str, revocation_endpoint: str, introspection_endpoint: str, redirect_uri: str, scopes: [str], resources: [str], transport: http.Client)`: A client of one authorization server: who it is, how it authenticates, where the server's endpoints are and what it asks.
- `function default_config(client_id: str) -> Config`, called `oauth2.default_config(client_id)`: A client of `client_id` with no secret (`.none`), no endpoint, no scope and `http.default_client()`.
- `function config_from(metadata: Metadata, client_id: str) -> Config`, called `oauth2.config_from(metadata, client_id)`: A client of `client_id` whose endpoints are those `metadata` names.
- `function new_verifier() -> str?`, called `oauth2.new_verifier()`: A new PKCE code verifier (RFC 7636 § 4.1): 32 bytes from the system's generator in base64url, 43 characters. Fails as `random.secure_token_base64_url` does.
- `function challenge_of(verifier: str) -> str`, called `oauth2.challenge_of(verifier)`: The S256 challenge of `verifier` (RFC 7636 § 4.2): the base64url of its SHA-256.
- `function new_state() -> str?`, called `oauth2.new_state()`: A new state or nonce: 32 bytes from the system's generator in base64url, which a redirect or an ID token must give back. Fails as `random.secure_token_base64_url` does.
- `function authorization_url(c: Config, state: str, challenge: str, extra: [url.Pair]) -> str?`, called `oauth2.authorization_url(c, state: state, challenge: challenge, extra)`: The URL the user's browser is sent to (RFC 6749 § 4.1.1): the authorization endpoint with `response_type=code`, the client's id, its redirect, its scopes, `state`, the S256 `challenge`, its resources, then `extra`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_redirect(target: str, state: str, issuer: str) -> str?`, called `oauth2.parse_redirect(target: target, state: state, issuer: issuer)`: The authorization code the redirect `target` carries, its state and issuer checked first. Fails `invalid`, `failed`, `permission`.
- `function exchange_code(c: Config, code: str, verifier: str) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.exchange_code(c, code: code, verifier: verifier)`: The tokens `code` is exchanged for at the token endpoint, with the PKCE `verifier` and the client's redirect and resources. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function post_form(c: Config, endpoint: str, form: [url.Pair]) -> http.Response?`, called `oauth2.post_form(c, endpoint, form)`: The response of `endpoint` to `form` POSTed with the client authenticated as `c` says: the one request every grant, a revocation and an introspection send, for an endpoint this package has no function for (a pushed authorization request, a token exchange). Fails `invalid`.
- `function token_of(r: http.Response, now: time.Instant) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.token_of(r, now)`: The token a token endpoint's response `r` holds, received at `now`. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function client_credentials(c: Config) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.client_credentials(c)`: A token for the client itself (RFC 6749 § 4.4), its scopes and resources asked. Fails as `exchange_code` does.
- `function refresh(c: Config, token: Token) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.refresh(c, token)`: `token` renewed by its refresh token (RFC 6749 § 6), the refresh token kept where the server sends none. Fails `invalid`.
- `function renewed(c: Config, token: Token, now: time.Instant) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.renewed(c, token, now)`: `token` itself where it has not expired at `now`, else `refresh`'s answer. Fails as `refresh` does.
- `function exchange_assertion(c: Config, assertion: str) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.exchange_assertion(c, assertion)`: A token for the JWT `assertion` given as the grant (RFC 7523 § 2.1): `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`. Fails as `exchange_code` does.
- `function request_token(c: Config, form: [url.Pair]) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.request_token(c, form)`: A token asked of the token endpoint with `form` as its parameters, the client authenticated as `c` says: any grant, token exchange (RFC 8693) among them. Fails as `exchange_code` does.
- `record DeviceAuthorization(device_code: str, user_code: str, verification_uri: str, verification_uri_complete: str, expiry: time.Instant, interval: time.Duration)`: What a device authorization answers (RFC 8628 § 3.2).
- `function start_device(c: Config) -> DeviceAuthorization?`, called `oauth2.start_device(c)`: The codes a device asks (RFC 8628 § 3.1), its scopes and resources asked. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function poll_device(c: Config, device: DeviceAuthorization) -> Token?`, called `oauth2.poll_device(c, device)`: The token the user's approval gives, the token endpoint asked at the interval `device` names (RFC 8628 § 3.4), five seconds more after each `slow_down`, until `device` expires. Fails `permission`, `timeout`, `failed`.
- `record Token(access_token: str, token_type: str, refresh_token: str, expiry: time.Instant, scopes: [str], id_token: str, members: {str: json.Value})`: A token endpoint's answer (RFC 6749 § 5.1).
- `function is_expired(token: Token, now: time.Instant) -> bool`, called `oauth2.is_expired(token, now)`: Whether `token` has expired at `now`, counting ten seconds early, as Go's `Token.Valid` does, so a request does not carry one that expires on the way.
- `function authorize(r: http.Request, token: Token) -> http.Request`, called `oauth2.authorize(r, token)`: `r` with `Authorization: Bearer` and `token`'s access token, any other `Authorization` replaced.
- `function revoke(c: Config, token: str, hint: str) -> ()?`, called `oauth2.revoke(c, token: token, hint: hint)`: Revokes `token` at the revocation endpoint (RFC 7009). Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `record Introspection(active: bool, scopes: [str], client_id: str, username: str, subject: str, audiences: [str], issuer: str, expiry: time.Instant, members: {str: json.Value})`: What the server says of `token` (RFC 7662).
- `function introspect(c: Config, token: str, hint: str) -> Introspection?`, called `oauth2.introspect(c, token: token, hint: hint)`: What the introspection endpoint answers of `token` (RFC 7662). Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `record Metadata(issuer: str, authorization_endpoint: str, token_endpoint: str, jwks_uri: str, userinfo_endpoint: str, revocation_endpoint: str, introspection_endpoint: str, device_authorization_endpoint: str, registration_endpoint: str, scopes_supported: [str], grant_types_supported: [str], code_challenge_methods_supported: [str], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: [str], id_token_signing_alg_values_supported: [str], authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: bool, client_id_metadata_document_supported: bool, members: {str: json.Value})`: An authorization server's metadata (RFC 8414 § 2, OpenID Connect Discovery § 3): its endpoints and what it supports.
- `function metadata_url(issuer: str) -> str?`, called `oauth2.metadata_url(issuer)`: Where RFC 8414 puts `issuer`'s metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` between its host and its path. Fails `invalid`.
- `function openid_configuration_url(issuer: str) -> str?`, called `oauth2.openid_configuration_url(issuer)`: Where OpenID Connect Discovery puts `issuer`'s configuration: its URL with `/.well-known/openid-configuration` after its path. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_metadata(text: str, issuer: str) -> Metadata?`, called `oauth2.parse_metadata(text: text, issuer: issuer)`: The metadata `text` holds, its `issuer` required to be `issuer`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_metadata(transport: http.Client, issuer: str) -> Metadata?`, called `oauth2.fetch_metadata(transport, issuer)`: `issuer`'s metadata, asked at `metadata_url`, then at `openid_configuration_url` and at OpenID Connect's well-known path inserted as RFC 8414 inserts its own, the first that answers. Fails `not_found`.
- `record ResourceMetadata(resource: str, authorization_servers: [str], jwks_uri: str, scopes_supported: [str], bearer_methods_supported: [str], resource_name: str, members: {str: json.Value})`: A protected resource's metadata (RFC 9728 § 2).
- `function resource_metadata_url(resource: str) -> str?`, called `oauth2.resource_metadata_url(resource)`: Where RFC 9728 puts `resource`'s metadata: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` between its host and its path. Fails `invalid`.
- `function resource_metadata_of(r: http.Response) -> str?`, called `oauth2.resource_metadata_of(r)`: The metadata URL a 401's `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge names in its `resource_metadata` (RFC 9728 § 5.1). Fails `not_found`.
- `function parse_resource_metadata(text: str, resource: str) -> ResourceMetadata?`, called `oauth2.parse_resource_metadata(text: text, resource: resource)`: The metadata `text` holds, its `resource` required to be `resource`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_resource_metadata(transport: http.Client, resource: str, location: str) -> ResourceMetadata?`, called `oauth2.fetch_resource_metadata(transport, resource: resource, location: location)`: `resource`'s metadata, asked at `location`, or at `resource_metadata_url` where `location` is "". Fails `not_found`.
- `function format_resource_metadata(m: ResourceMetadata) -> str?`, called `oauth2.format_resource_metadata(m)`: `m` as the JSON document a resource serves at its `resource_metadata_url`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_challenge(location: str, scope: str) -> str`, called `oauth2.format_challenge(location: location, scope: scope)`: The `WWW-Authenticate` value a resource answers a request without a valid token with: `Bearer resource_metadata="..."`, and the scope where given.
- `record ClientMetadata(client_id: str, client_name: str, client_uri: str, logo_uri: str, redirect_uris: [str], grant_types: [str], token_endpoint_auth_method: str, jwks_uri: str, members: {str: json.Value})`: A client's metadata (RFC 7591 § 2) as a document served at the URL that is its `client_id` (OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents).
- `function format_client_metadata(m: ClientMetadata) -> str?`, called `oauth2.format_client_metadata(m)`: `m` as the JSON document a client serves at its `client_id`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_client_metadata(text: str, client_id: str) -> ClientMetadata?`, called `oauth2.parse_client_metadata(text: text, client_id: client_id)`: The client metadata `text` holds, its `client_id` required to be the URL `client_id` it was fetched from. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_client_metadata(transport: http.Client, client_id: str) -> ClientMetadata?`, called `oauth2.fetch_client_metadata(transport, client_id)`: The metadata document at the URL `client_id`, as a server reads a client it has never seen. Fails `invalid`.
- `record IdTokenRules(issuer: str, client_id: str, nonce: str, algorithms: [jose.Algorithm], leeway: time.Duration, now: time.Instant, max_age: time.Duration, access_token: str)`: What an ID token must answer (OpenID Connect Core § 3.1.3.7).
- `function id_token_rules(metadata: Metadata, client_id: str, nonce: str) -> IdTokenRules?`, called `oauth2.id_token_rules(metadata, client_id: client_id, nonce: nonce)`: Rules for an ID token of `metadata`'s issuer to `client_id` with `nonce`: the algorithms the provider names that `jose` knows, `RS256` where it names none, a leeway of a minute, the wall clock's time. Fails `failed`.
- `function verify_id_token(id_token: str, trusted: [jose.Key], rules: IdTokenRules) -> jose.Token?`, called `oauth2.verify_id_token(id_token, trusted, rules)`: The ID token `id_token` verified by one of `trusted` and checked by `rules`: its signature, `iss`, `aud`, `azp`, `exp`, `iat`, `nonce`, `auth_time` and `at_hash`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function fetch_key_set(transport: http.Client, jwks_uri: str) -> [jose.Key]?`, called `oauth2.fetch_key_set(transport, jwks_uri)`: The keys of the JWK set at `jwks_uri`, as `jose.parse_key_set` reads them. Fails `failed`.
- `function fetch_userinfo(transport: http.Client, endpoint: str, token: Token, subject: str) -> {str: json.Value}?`, called `oauth2.fetch_userinfo(transport, endpoint: endpoint, token, subject: subject)`: The claims the UserInfo endpoint answers for `token` (OpenID Connect Core § 5.3), its `sub` required to be `subject`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `failed`.


### saml

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/saml`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/saml/).

SAML 2.0's service provider (OASIS, 2005): a program signs its users in through a company's identity server.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a message not of SAML's form, or a rule that does not hold.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of an element or an endpoint a message or metadata lacks.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of a form of SAML this package does not read.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of a status other than success, answered by the identity provider.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a message longer than `MOST_BYTES`.
- `constant MOST_BYTES: i64`, value `4194304`: The most bytes a message read from a binding may hold, once inflated or decoded.
- `constant HTTP_POST: str`, value `"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST"`: The HTTP-POST binding's identifier.
- `constant HTTP_REDIRECT: str`, value `"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect"`: The HTTP-Redirect binding's identifier.
- `constant PERSISTENT: str`, value `"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent"`: The format of a name the identity provider keeps for one user and one service provider, opaque and lasting.
- `constant TRANSIENT: str`, value `"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:transient"`: The format of a name made for one session alone.
- `constant EMAIL_ADDRESS: str`, value `"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress"`: The format of a name that is a mail address.
- `constant DEFAULT_SKEW_SECONDS: i64`, value `120`: The clock skew `response_options` allows between the two providers, in seconds.
- `record ServiceProvider(entity_id: str, acs_url: str, logout_url: str, name_id_format: str, certificates: [x509.Certificate])`: The service provider a program is: what its metadata says and what a response is checked against.
- `function service_provider(entity_id: str, acs_url: str) -> ServiceProvider`, called `saml.service_provider(entity_id: entity_id, acs_url: acs_url)`: A service provider of entity identifier `entity_id` and consumer service `acs_url`, with no logout service, no format asked and no certificate.
- `record Endpoint(binding: str, location: str, response_location: str)`: One endpoint of an identity provider.
- `record IdentityProvider(entity_id: str, sso: [Endpoint], logout: [Endpoint], certificates: [x509.Certificate], want_requests_signed: bool, name_id_formats: [str])`: An identity provider, as its metadata describes it.
- `variant Source = .signed(by: xmldsig.Verifier) | .trusted`: How far a metadata document is trusted.
- `function parse_metadata(text: str, entity_id: str, source: Source, now: time.Instant) -> IdentityProvider?`, called `saml.parse_metadata(text: text, entity_id: entity_id, source, now)`: The identity provider `entity_id` as the metadata `text` describes it. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function format_metadata(sp: ServiceProvider) -> str?`, called `saml.format_metadata(sp)`: The metadata of `sp`: an `EntityDescriptor` with its `SPSSODescriptor`, its signing certificates, its logout service by both bindings where it has one, the format it asks, and its consumer service by HTTP-POST, asking signed assertions. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Outgoing(id: str, parameter: str, binding: str, destination: str, doc: xml.Document)`: A message a service provider sends, built and not yet signed.
- `record RequestOptions(force_authn: bool, is_passive: bool, allow_create: bool, authn_contexts: [str])`: What an authentication request asks beyond its identity.
- `function default_request_options() -> RequestOptions`, called `saml.default_request_options()`: Options asking nothing more and letting a name be made.
- `function authn_request(sp: ServiceProvider, idp: IdentityProvider, binding: str, options: RequestOptions, now: time.Instant) -> Outgoing?`, called `saml.authn_request(sp, idp, binding, options, now)`: An authentication request of `sp` to `idp`, sent by `binding`, its response asked by HTTP-POST at `sp.acs_url`; its identifier is drawn from the system's generator. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function endpoint_of(list: [Endpoint], binding: str, response: bool, what: str) -> str?`, called `saml.endpoint_of(list, binding: binding, response, what: what)`: The location of the first endpoint of `binding` in `list`, its response location where `response` asks one and it writes one. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `variant Signer = .key(v: keypairs.PrivateKey, method: xmldsig.Method) | .unsigned`: Who signs a message sent.
- `function redirect_url(m: Outgoing, relay_state: str, signer: Signer) -> str?`, called `saml.redirect_url(m, relay_state, signer)`: The URL that sends `m` by HTTP-Redirect: its message deflated and in base 64 (SAML Bindings § 3.4.4.1), `relay_state` beside it where not empty, and signed over the query's bytes where `signer` is a key. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function post_page(m: Outgoing, relay_state: str, signer: Signer) -> str?`, called `saml.post_page(m, relay_state, signer)`: The page that posts `m` by HTTP-POST (SAML Bindings § 3.5.4), signed inside where `signer` is a key: the signature enveloped after its `Issuer`, over exclusive Canonical XML and SHA-256. Fails as `redirect_url` fails, for a message of the other transport.
- `record ResponseOptions(now: time.Instant, skew_seconds: i64, request_id: str, want_assertions_signed: bool)`: What a response is checked against beyond the two providers.
- `function response_options(request_id: str, now: time.Instant) -> ResponseOptions`, called `saml.response_options(request_id, now)`: Options for the response to the request `request_id`, checked at `now` with `DEFAULT_SKEW_SECONDS`, its assertion signed.
- `function unsolicited_options(now: time.Instant) -> ResponseOptions`, called `saml.unsolicited_options(now)`: Options for a response no request of the program asked (SAML Profiles § 4.1.5), which must then answer none.
- `record Seen(until: {str: i64})`: The assertions already read and when each expires, so a bearer assertion is read once (SAML Profiles § 4.1.4.5).
- `function new_seen() -> Seen`, called `saml.new_seen()`: A record of no assertion read.
- `record Attribute(name: str, name_format: str, friendly_name: str, values: [str])`: One attribute the identity provider says of the user.
- `record Login(issuer: str, name_id: str, name_id_format: str, name_qualifier: str, sp_name_qualifier: str, session_index: str, session_ends: bool, session_end: time.Instant, authn_instant: time.Instant, authn_context: str, attributes: [Attribute], assertion_id: str, response_id: str, in_response_to: str, one_time_use: bool)`: Who signed in, as a response that holds says.
- `function check_response(saml_response: str, sp: ServiceProvider, idp: IdentityProvider, options: ResponseOptions, @seen: Seen) -> Login?`, called `saml.check_response(saml_response, sp, idp, options, @seen)`: Who signed in, once the response the browser posted holds. Fails `failed`, `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function values_of(login: Login, name: str) -> [str]`, called `saml.values_of(login, name)`: The values of the attributes of `login` whose `Name` or `FriendlyName` is `name`, in order; empty where none is.
- `variant Incoming = .redirect(query: str) | .post(message: str)`: A logout message received, as the binding brought it.
- `record LogoutOrder(id: str, name_id: str, name_id_format: str, session_indexes: [str])`: A logout the identity provider asks of the service provider.
- `function logout_request(sp: ServiceProvider, idp: IdentityProvider, login: Login, binding: str, now: time.Instant) -> Outgoing?`, called `saml.logout_request(sp, idp, login, binding, now)`: A logout request of `sp` for the session `login` holds, sent to `idp`'s first single logout endpoint of `binding`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function check_logout_response(incoming: Incoming, sp: ServiceProvider, idp: IdentityProvider, request_id: str, now: time.Instant) -> ()?`, called `saml.check_logout_response(incoming, sp, idp, request_id, now)`: Succeeds where the identity provider's answer to the logout request `request_id` holds and says it succeeded. Fails `invalid`, `failed`, `limit`.
- `function check_logout_request(incoming: Incoming, sp: ServiceProvider, idp: IdentityProvider, now: time.Instant) -> LogoutOrder?`, called `saml.check_logout_request(incoming, sp, idp, now)`: The logout the identity provider asks, once its request holds. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `limit`.
- `function logout_response(sp: ServiceProvider, idp: IdentityProvider, order: LogoutOrder, binding: str, now: time.Instant) -> Outgoing?`, called `saml.logout_response(sp, idp, order, binding, now)`: The answer of `sp` to the logout `order`, success, sent to `idp`'s first single logout endpoint of `binding`, at its response location where it writes one. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.


### s3

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/s3`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/s3/).

The S3 API spoken over HTTP and HTTPS with Signature Version 4: objects put, read whole or by a range, asked about, copied, deleted and listed; buckets made, listed and removed; uploads in parts; presigned URLs and browser forms; checksums; and any other request of the API signed and sent.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an argument this package refuses before sending (a bucket's name, a key, a region, a part's number), and of a server's 400 and 416 and an answer not of the API's shape.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a bucket, a key, an upload or a version the server does not hold, and of credentials or a profile nobody wrote.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a bucket made that is there already, and of a put that `PutOptions.if_none_match` refused because the object exists.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: The code of a request the server refuses to these credentials: denied, signed by an unknown key, a wrong secret or an expired token.
- `constant NOT_EMPTY: str`, value `"not_empty"`: The code of a bucket deleted while it holds objects or versions.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a server that asks the client to slow down after every retry, and of an answer past `Client.limits`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of an operation the server does not implement (501).
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of every other refusal: a condition not met (412), an object not modified (304), a status no other code names.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a connection the server closed before it answered.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a request that passed `Client.deadline`.
- `constant STOPPED: str`, value `"stopped"`: The code of a request the program was asked to stop while it waited.
- `record Credentials(access_key_id: str, secret_access_key: str, session_token: str)`: The keys a request is signed with.
- `variant SharedFile = .credentials | .config`: Which of the two shared files a text is: they name a profile's section differently.
- `function credentials_from_env() -> Credentials?`, called `s3.credentials_from_env()`: The credentials the environment holds: `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function credentials_from_text(text: str, profile: str, kind: SharedFile) -> Credentials?`, called `s3.credentials_from_text(text: text, profile: profile, kind)`: The credentials the profile `profile` holds in `text`, a shared file's. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function credentials_from_files(profile: str) -> Credentials?`, called `s3.credentials_from_files(profile)`: The credentials of the profile `profile` in the shared files: the credentials file first, then the config file. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function default_credentials() -> Credentials?`, called `s3.default_credentials()`: The credentials a program finds by itself, as botocore looks: the environment's, then the shared files' for the profile `profile_name` names. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function profile_name() -> str`, called `s3.profile_name()`: The profile a program uses: `AWS_PROFILE`, else `AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, else `default`.
- `function format_credentials(c: Credentials) -> str`, called `s3.format_credentials(c)`: `c` written for a person, with no secret: the key's id with its last four characters alone shown, whether a secret is held, and whether a token is.
- `variant Addressing = .auto | .path | .virtual_host`: How a client reaches its buckets: by host name, by path, or as this package chooses.
- `record Profile(region: str, endpoint_url: str, addressing: Addressing)`: What a profile of the config file says of S3: its region, its endpoint and its addressing.
- `function profile_from_text(text: str, profile: str) -> Profile?`, called `s3.profile_from_text(text: text, profile: profile)`: The profile `profile` of `text`, a config file's. Fails `invalid`.
- `function profile_from_files(profile: str) -> Profile?`, called `s3.profile_from_files(profile)`: The profile `profile` of the config file, `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` or `~/.aws/config`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Client(credentials: Credentials, region: str, endpoint: str, addressing: Addressing, dualstack: bool, accelerate: bool, sign_payload: bool, deadline: time.Duration, limits: http.Limits, roots: str, max_attempts: i64)`: How every request is sent: to whom, as whom, and within what.
- `function aws_client(region: str, credentials: Credentials) -> Client`, called `s3.aws_client(region, credentials)`: A client of Amazon S3 in `region`.
- `function minio_client(endpoint: str, credentials: Credentials) -> Client`, called `s3.minio_client(endpoint, credentials)`: A client of a MinIO server, or of any server of the S3 API, at `endpoint`.
- `function r2_client(account_id: str, credentials: Credentials) -> Client`, called `s3.r2_client(account_id, credentials)`: A client of Cloudflare R2 for the account `account_id`.
- `function backblaze_client(region: str, credentials: Credentials) -> Client`, called `s3.backblaze_client(region, credentials)`: A client of Backblaze B2's S3 API in `region`.
- `function client_from_env() -> Client?`, called `s3.client_from_env()`: The client the environment and the shared files describe, as botocore reads them: `default_credentials`, the region of `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` or the profile, `us-east-1` where none names one, and the endpoint of `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` or the profile. Fails as `default_credentials` and `profile_from_files` do.
- `function object_url(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str) -> str?`, called `s3.object_url(c, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: The URL of the object `key` in `bucket`, unsigned, as `c` reaches it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function is_bucket_name(name: str) -> bool`, called `s3.is_bucket_name(name)`: Whether `name` may name a new bucket, by S3's rules: 3 to 63 bytes of lower-case letters, digits, `.` and `-`, a letter or a digit at each end, no `..`, no `.-` or `-.`, and not written as an IPv4 address.
- `constant UNSIGNED_PAYLOAD: str`, value `"UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD"`: The payload's hash a request sends when its body is not signed.
- `constant EMPTY_PAYLOAD_SHA256: str`, value `"e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"`: The hexadecimal SHA-256 of no bytes, the hash of an empty payload.
- `constant MAX_EXPIRES_SECONDS: i64`, value `604_800`: The longest a presigned URL may live: 604,800 seconds, seven days.
- `record Signature(request: http.Request, canonical_request: str, string_to_sign: str, signature: str)`: What a signature was made from, for a program that shows or checks it.
- `function format_amz_date(t: time.Instant) -> str`, called `s3.format_amz_date(t)`: The instant `t` as SigV4 writes it: `20150830T123600Z`.
- `function parse_amz_date(s: str) -> time.Instant?`, called `s3.parse_amz_date(s)`: The instant `s` writes as SigV4's date, `20150830T123600Z`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function uri_encode(s: str, keep_slash: bool) -> str`, called `s3.uri_encode(s, keep_slash)`: `s` URI-encoded as SigV4 asks: every byte but a letter, a digit, `-`, `.`, `_` and `~` written as `%` and two upper-case hexadecimal digits.
- `function canonical_request(r: http.Request, payload_hash: str, s3: bool) -> str?`, called `s3.canonical_request(r, payload_hash, s3)`: The canonical request of `r`, the text a signature is made over. Fails `invalid`.
- `function signing_key(secret: str, at: time.Instant, region: str, service: str) -> [u8]`, called `s3.signing_key(secret: secret, at, region: region, service: service)`: The key a signature is made with: the secret, then the day, the region, the service and `aws4_request`, each an HMAC-SHA256 of the one before.
- `function sign_request(r: http.Request, credentials: Credentials, region: str, service: str, at: time.Instant) -> Signature?`, called `s3.sign_request(r, credentials, region: region, service: service, at)`: `r` signed for `service` in `region` at `at`, in its header: `Host` where it has none, `X-Amz-Date`, `X-Amz-Security-Token` where the credentials hold a token, and `Authorization`, the fields of those names it held replaced. Fails `invalid`.
- `function presign_request(r: http.Request, credentials: Credentials, region: str, service: str, at: time.Instant, expires: time.Duration) -> Signature?`, called `s3.presign_request(r, credentials, region: region, service: service, at, expires)`: `r` presigned: its target given the query that signs it, so whoever holds the URL may send `r` until it expires. Fails `invalid`.
- `variant Checksum = .none | .crc32 | .crc32c | .crc64nvme | .sha1 | .sha256`: A checksum S3 keeps beside an object, sent as `x-amz-checksum-<name>` and checked by the server.
- `function checksum_of(data: [u8], algorithm: Checksum) -> str`, called `s3.checksum_of(data, algorithm)`: The checksum of `data` by `algorithm`, as S3 writes it: its bytes, big endian, in base 64.
- `function format_checksum(algorithm: Checksum) -> str`, called `s3.format_checksum(algorithm)`: The name S3 gives `algorithm`: `CRC32`, `CRC32C`, `CRC64NVME`, `SHA1`, `SHA256`; "" for `none`.
- `function parse_checksum(s: str) -> Checksum?`, called `s3.parse_checksum(s)`: The checksum S3 names `s`, in any case. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Operation(method: str, bucket: str, key: str, query: [url.Pair], headers: [http.Header], body: [u8])`: One request of the S3 API, before it is signed: what `send` sends and every function below makes.
- `function operation(method: str, bucket: str, key: str) -> Operation`, called `s3.operation(method: method, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: An operation `method` on `key` of `bucket`, with no query, no field and no body.
- `function prepare(c: Client, op: Operation, at: time.Instant) -> http.Request?`, called `s3.prepare(c, op, at)`: The request `op` makes for `c`, signed at `at`: its URL by `c`'s addressing, its fields, and its signature. Fails `invalid`.
- `function send(c: Client, op: Operation) -> http.Response?`, called `s3.send(c, op)`: The response to `op`, signed now and sent as `c` says, its status from 200 to 299. Fails with the code S3's own error code maps to (the face's comment names them), the message opening with S3's code, or with the status where S3 answered no error document, and naming the method, the bucket and the key; and as `prepare` and the connection fail.
- `record Meta(name: str, value: str)`: One piece of an object's metadata, sent as `x-amz-meta-<name>`.
- `record Tag(key: str, value: str)`: One tag of an object, a key and its value.
- `record PutOptions(content_type: str, cache_control: str, content_disposition: str, content_encoding: str, content_language: str, expires: str, metadata: [Meta], tags: [Tag], storage_class: str, acl: str, server_side_encryption: str, kms_key_id: str, checksum: Checksum, if_none_match: str, if_match: str)`: How an object is put: its fields, its metadata, its checksum and its conditions.
- `function default_put_options() -> PutOptions`, called `s3.default_put_options()`: Put options with no field, no metadata, no tag and no condition, the checksum CRC-32 as botocore sends by default.
- `function headers_of(options: PutOptions) -> [http.Header]?`, called `s3.headers_of(options)`: The fields a put of `options` sends: what a presigned PUT's sender must send too. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Stored(etag: str, version_id: str, checksum: str)`: What S3 answers to a put, a copy or an upload completed.
- `function put_object(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, data: [u8], options: PutOptions) -> Stored?`, called `s3.put_object(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, data, options)`: Puts `data` as the object `key` of `bucket`, replacing any of that key. Fails `exists`, `failed`.
- `variant Range = .whole | .from(first: i64) | .between(first: i64, last: i64) | .suffix(count: i64)`: Which bytes of an object a read asks for.
- `record GetOptions(span: Range, version_id: str, if_match: str, if_none_match: str, if_modified_since: str, if_unmodified_since: str, part_number: i64, verify_checksum: bool)`: How an object is read: which bytes, which version, on which conditions.
- `function default_get_options() -> GetOptions`, called `s3.default_get_options()`: Get options for the whole of the newest version, no condition, no part, no check.
- `function range_header(span: Range) -> str?`, called `s3.range_header(span)`: The `Range` field `span` asks for: `bytes=0-9`, `bytes=100-`, `bytes=-10`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function get_operation(bucket: str, key: str, options: GetOptions) -> Operation?`, called `s3.get_operation(bucket: bucket, key: key, options)`: The operation `get_object_with` sends: the version and the part in the query, the range, the conditions and the checksum's mode in the fields. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Info(key: str, size: i64, total_size: i64, etag: str, last_modified: time.Instant, content_type: str, cache_control: str, content_disposition: str, content_encoding: str, content_language: str, expires: str, metadata: [Meta], version_id: str, storage_class: str, checksum_algorithm: Checksum, checksum: str, server_side_encryption: str, parts_count: i64, headers: [http.Header])`: What S3 says of an object: its size, its fields, its metadata.
- `record Object(info: Info, data: [u8])`: An object read: what S3 says of it and its bytes.
- `function info_of(r: http.Response, key: str) -> Info?`, called `s3.info_of(r, key)`: What the fields of `r`, S3's answer about the object `key`, say of it. Fails `invalid`.
- `function get_object(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str) -> Object?`, called `s3.get_object(c, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: The object `key` of `bucket`, whole. Fails `not_found`, `limit`.
- `function get_object_with(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, options: GetOptions) -> Object?`, called `s3.get_object_with(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, options)`: The object `key` of `bucket`, read as `options` say. Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function get_object_to(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, options: GetOptions, s: io.Stream) -> Info?`, called `s3.get_object_to(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, options, s)`: Writes the object `key` of `bucket`, read as `options` say, to `s` as it comes: an object of any size. Fails as `get_object_with` does, and as `io.write` fails; a failure past the first byte leaves those written.
- `function head_object(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str) -> Info?`, called `s3.head_object(c, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: What S3 says of the object `key` of `bucket`, without its bytes. Fails `not_found`.
- `function object_exists(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str) -> bool?`, called `s3.object_exists(c, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: Whether `bucket` holds an object of the key `key`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function delete_object(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str) -> ()?`, called `s3.delete_object(c, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: Deletes the object `key` of `bucket`; deleting one that is not there succeeds, as S3 answers. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function delete_object_version(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, version_id: str) -> ()?`, called `s3.delete_object_version(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, version_id: version_id)`: Deletes the version `version_id` of the object `key` of `bucket` for good. Fails as `send` fails.
- `record NotDeleted(key: str, code: str, message: str)`: One object a `delete_objects` did not delete, and why.
- `function delete_objects(c: Client, bucket: str, names: [str]) -> [NotDeleted]?`, called `s3.delete_objects(c, bucket, names)`: Deletes every object of `names` from `bucket`, a thousand to a request. Fails as `send` fails, where a request as a whole is refused.
- `function copy_object(c: Client, from_bucket: str, from_key: str, to_bucket: str, to_key: str) -> Stored?`, called `s3.copy_object(c, from_bucket: from_bucket, from_key: from_key, to_bucket: to_bucket, to_key: to_key)`: Copies the object `from_key` of `from_bucket` to `to_key` of `to_bucket`, its metadata and fields kept. Fails `not_found`.
- `function copy_object_with(c: Client, from_bucket: str, from_key: str, to_bucket: str, to_key: str, options: PutOptions) -> Stored?`, called `s3.copy_object_with(c, from_bucket: from_bucket, from_key: from_key, to_bucket: to_bucket, to_key: to_key, options)`: Copies the object `from_key` of `from_bucket` to `to_key` of `to_bucket`, its metadata and fields replaced by those of `options`. Fails as `copy_object` does.
- `function get_object_tags(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str) -> [Tag]?`, called `s3.get_object_tags(c, bucket: bucket, key: key)`: The tags of the object `key` of `bucket`, in their order. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function put_object_tags(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, tags: [Tag]) -> ()?`, called `s3.put_object_tags(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, tags)`: Sets the tags of the object `key` of `bucket` to `tags`, every one before replaced. Fails `invalid`.
- `record ListOptions(prefix: str, delimiter: str, start_after: str, continuation_token: str, max_keys: i64)`: How a page of objects is asked for.
- `function default_list_options() -> ListOptions`, called `s3.default_list_options()`: List options for every key, the first page, the server's page size.
- `record Summary(key: str, size: i64, etag: str, last_modified: time.Instant, storage_class: str)`: One object of a listing.
- `record Listing(objects: [Summary], prefixes: [str], truncated: bool, next_token: str)`: One page of a listing.
- `function list_objects(c: Client, bucket: str, options: ListOptions) -> Listing?`, called `s3.list_objects(c, bucket, options)`: One page of the objects of `bucket`, by the API's version 2. Fails `not_found`.
- `function list_all_objects(c: Client, bucket: str, prefix: str) -> [Summary]?`, called `s3.list_all_objects(c, bucket: bucket, prefix: prefix)`: Every object of `bucket` whose key begins with `prefix`, page after page. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Version(key: str, version_id: str, is_latest: bool, delete_marker: bool, size: i64, etag: str, last_modified: time.Instant)`: One version of an object, or a delete marker, in a bucket that keeps versions.
- `function list_object_versions(c: Client, bucket: str, prefix: str) -> [Version]?`, called `s3.list_object_versions(c, bucket: bucket, prefix: prefix)`: Every version and delete marker of the objects of `bucket` whose key begins with `prefix`, page after page. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Bucket(name: str, created: time.Instant, region: str)`: One bucket of a listing.
- `function list_buckets(c: Client) -> [Bucket]?`, called `s3.list_buckets(c)`: The buckets the credentials own, in the order answered. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function create_bucket(c: Client, bucket: str) -> ()?`, called `s3.create_bucket(c, bucket)`: Makes the bucket `bucket` in `c`'s region. Fails `invalid`, `exists`.
- `function delete_bucket(c: Client, bucket: str) -> ()?`, called `s3.delete_bucket(c, bucket)`: Deletes the bucket `bucket`, which must be empty. Fails `not_empty`, `not_found`.
- `function bucket_exists(c: Client, bucket: str) -> bool?`, called `s3.bucket_exists(c, bucket)`: Whether the bucket `bucket` is there and the credentials may reach it. Fails `permission`, `not_found`.
- `function bucket_region(c: Client, bucket: str) -> str?`, called `s3.bucket_region(c, bucket)`: The region the bucket `bucket` stands in, as `GetBucketLocation` answers: `us-east-1` where S3 answers no location. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function get_bucket_config(c: Client, bucket: str, name: str) -> str?`, called `s3.get_bucket_config(c, bucket: bucket, name: name)`: The configuration `name` of the bucket `bucket`, the document S3 answers. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function put_bucket_config(c: Client, bucket: str, name: str, document: str) -> ()?`, called `s3.put_bucket_config(c, bucket: bucket, name: name, document: document)`: Sets the configuration `name` of the bucket `bucket` to `document`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function delete_bucket_config(c: Client, bucket: str, name: str) -> ()?`, called `s3.delete_bucket_config(c, bucket: bucket, name: name)`: Deletes the configuration `name` of the bucket `bucket`. Fails as `get_bucket_config` does.
- `constant MIN_PART_SIZE: i64`, value `5_242_880`: The least size of every part but the last: 5 MiB.
- `constant MAX_PARTS: i64`, value `10_000`: The most parts an upload holds: 10,000.
- `constant MAX_PART_SIZE: i64`, value `5_368_709_120`: The largest part, and the largest object of one put: 5 GiB.
- `record Upload(bucket: str, key: str, upload_id: str, checksum: Checksum)`: An upload in parts begun: where it goes and the id S3 gave it.
- `record Part(number: i64, etag: str, size: i64, checksum: str)`: One part uploaded.
- `function create_multipart_upload(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, options: PutOptions) -> Upload?`, called `s3.create_multipart_upload(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, options)`: Begins an upload in parts of the object `key` of `bucket`. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function upload_part(c: Client, upload: Upload, number: i64, data: [u8]) -> Part?`, called `s3.upload_part(c, upload, number, data)`: Uploads `data` as the part `number` of `upload`. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `function upload_part_copy(c: Client, upload: Upload, number: i64, from_bucket: str, from_key: str, span: Range) -> Part?`, called `s3.upload_part_copy(c, upload, number, from_bucket: from_bucket, from_key: from_key, span)`: Copies the bytes `span` names of the object `from_key` of `from_bucket` as the part `number` of `upload`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function complete_multipart_upload(c: Client, upload: Upload, parts: [Part]) -> Stored?`, called `s3.complete_multipart_upload(c, upload, parts)`: Ends `upload` by joining `parts` into its object. Fails `invalid`.
- `function abort_multipart_upload(c: Client, upload: Upload) -> ()?`, called `s3.abort_multipart_upload(c, upload)`: Ends `upload` without an object, its parts deleted. Fails `not_found`.
- `function list_parts(c: Client, upload: Upload) -> [Part]?`, called `s3.list_parts(c, upload)`: Every part of `upload` uploaded so far, page after page, by number. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function list_multipart_uploads(c: Client, bucket: str, prefix: str) -> [Upload]?`, called `s3.list_multipart_uploads(c, bucket: bucket, prefix: prefix)`: Every upload in parts of `bucket` begun and not ended whose key begins with `prefix`, page after page. Fails as `send` fails.
- `function put_object_in_parts(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, data: [u8], part_size: i64, options: PutOptions) -> Stored?`, called `s3.put_object_in_parts(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, data, part_size, options)`: Puts `data` as the object `key` of `bucket` in parts of `part_size` bytes, the last smaller, as AWS's upload managers do. Fails `invalid`.
- `function put_object_from(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, s: io.Stream, part_size: i64, options: PutOptions) -> Stored?`, called `s3.put_object_from(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, s, part_size, options)`: Puts what `s` holds until its end as the object `key` of `bucket`, read and uploaded a part of `part_size` bytes at a time, so an object of any size is put holding one part in memory. Fails `limit`.
- `function presign_url(c: Client, method: str, bucket: str, key: str, headers: [http.Header], at: time.Instant, expires: time.Duration) -> str?`, called `s3.presign_url(c, method: method, bucket: bucket, key: key, headers, at, expires)`: A URL that sends `method` to the object `key` of `bucket` until it expires, with no key: what a browser or another program fetches. Fails `invalid`.
- `function presign_get(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, expires: time.Duration) -> str?`, called `s3.presign_get(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, expires)`: A URL that reads the object `key` of `bucket` for `expires` from now. Fails `failed`.
- `function presign_put(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, expires: time.Duration) -> str?`, called `s3.presign_put(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, expires)`: A URL that puts the object `key` of `bucket` for `expires` from now; the sender sends no field the URL did not sign. Fails as `presign_get` does.
- `record PostForm(target: str, fields: [url.Pair])`: A form a browser POSTs to put an object: the URL it goes to and the fields it holds before the file, as `presign_post` makes them.
- `function presign_post(c: Client, bucket: str, key: str, content_type: str, max_size: i64, at: time.Instant, expires: time.Duration) -> PostForm?`, called `s3.presign_post(c, bucket: bucket, key: key, content_type: content_type, max_size, at, expires)`: A form that lets a browser, or any program with no key, put the object `key` of `bucket` by POST until it expires: S3's signed policy. Fails `invalid`.
