### jsonrpc

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/jsonrpc`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/jsonrpc/).

JSON-RPC 2.0, exactly as its specification of 2013-01-04 writes it: requests, notifications, answers and errors with their codes, batches, and ids of every kind the specification allows, read from text and written as text; carried over a stream one message a line (as MCP's standard streams and JSON Lines carry it) or each after a `Content-Length` header (as the Language Server Protocol carries it), and over HTTP through `http`.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text, a frame or a value that is no message, and of a method or a parameter a server refuses.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of a method no `add_method` described, and of a parameter a found call does not hold.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a message, a frame or a batch past what `Limits` allows.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of an answer that is an error, its code and message in the failure's message: what `value_of` fails with.
- `constant NOT_TEXT: str`, value `"not_text"`: The code of a frame whose bytes are not UTF-8.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of an HTTP method other than `POST`, and of a frame's charset other than UTF-8.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The code of a stream that ends before a message begins, or whose other end is gone.
- `constant EXISTS: str`, value `"exists"`: The code of a method `add_method` was given already.
- `constant PARSE_ERROR: i64`, value `-32700`: The text received is not JSON: answered with a `null_id`.
- `constant INVALID_REQUEST: i64`, value `-32600`: The JSON received is not a request: answered with a `null_id`.
- `constant METHOD_NOT_FOUND: i64`, value `-32601`: No method of that name.
- `constant INVALID_PARAMS: i64`, value `-32602`: The parameters are not those the method takes.
- `constant INTERNAL_ERROR: i64`, value `-32603`: The server failed while it answered.
- `constant SERVER_ERROR_FIRST: i64`, value `-32099`: The lowest of the codes the specification leaves to a server's own errors, -32099 to -32000.
- `constant SERVER_ERROR_LAST: i64`, value `-32000`: The highest of the codes the specification leaves to a server's own errors.
- `constant MAX_EXACT_ID: i64`, value `9007199254740991`: The largest number an id may be in either direction, 2^53 - 1: past it two ids written differently read as one `f64`, so a request bearing one is refused as `INVALID_REQUEST`.
- `variant Id = .absent | .null_id | .number(v: f64) | .text(v: str)`: What names a request, so that its answer can name it back: a string, a number, `null`, or nothing for a notification.
- `record Error(code: i64, message: str, data: json.Value)`: An error an answer carries.
- `variant Reply = .result(value: json.Value) | .error(error: Error)`: What answers a request: its result, or an error.
- `variant Message = .request(id: Id, method: str, params: json.Value) | .notification(method: str, params: json.Value) | .response(id: Id, reply: Reply)`: One JSON-RPC message.
- `record Received(messages: [Message?], batch: bool)`: What one text received holds: one message, or a batch of them.
- `function answer_result(id: Id, value: json.Value) -> Message`, called `jsonrpc.answer_result(id, value)`: The answer to the request `id` names: `value` as its result.
- `function answer_error(id: Id, code: i64, message: str) -> Message`, called `jsonrpc.answer_error(id, code, message)`: The answer to the request `id` names: an error with `code` and `message` and no data.
- `function answer_outcome(id: Id, outcome: json.Value?) -> Message`, called `jsonrpc.answer_outcome(id, outcome)`: The answer to the request `id` names, made from what the program's own handler answered.
- `function answer_refusal(id: Id, code: str, msg: str) -> Message`, called `jsonrpc.answer_refusal(id, code: code, msg: msg)`: The answer to a request `method_of` refused.
- `function answer_parse_error(why: str) -> Message`, called `jsonrpc.answer_parse_error(why)`: The answer to a text that is not JSON: `PARSE_ERROR`, its id `.null_id`.
- `function answer_invalid_request(why: str) -> Message`, called `jsonrpc.answer_invalid_request(why)`: The answer to a value that is no request: `INVALID_REQUEST`, its id `.null_id`, as the specification asks where the id could not be read.
- `function value_of(reply: Reply) -> json.Value?`, called `jsonrpc.value_of(reply)`: The value of `reply`'s result. Fails `failed`.
- `function format_id(id: Id) -> str`, called `jsonrpc.format_id(id)`: `id` as JSON writes it: `1`, `"a"`, `null`, or "" for `.absent`.
- `record Limits(message_bytes: i64, batch_items: i64, depth: i64)`: What a server and a client allow a text received to hold.
- `function default_limits() -> Limits`, called `jsonrpc.default_limits()`: The usual limits: 16 MiB a message, 1,000 elements a batch, and `json.DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`.
- `function parse(text: str, limits: Limits) -> Received?`, called `jsonrpc.parse(text, limits)`: The message or the batch `text` holds. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function format(m: Message) -> str?`, called `jsonrpc.format(m)`: `m` as JSON on one line. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function format_batch(messages: [Message]) -> str?`, called `jsonrpc.format_batch(messages)`: `messages` as one JSON array on one line: a batch. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function message_of(v: json.Value) -> Message?`, called `jsonrpc.message_of(v)`: The message the JSON value `v` writes, as `parse` reads each element. Fails `invalid`.
- `function message_json(m: Message) -> json.Value`, called `jsonrpc.message_json(m)`: `m` as the JSON value `format` writes.
- `variant Framing = .lines | .content_length`: How messages follow each other on a stream.
- `function read_text(@reader: io.Reader, framing: Framing, limits: Limits) -> str?`, called `jsonrpc.read_text(@reader, framing, limits)`: The text of the next message `reader` holds, its framing taken off. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `limit`, `unsupported`, `not_text`.
- `function read_message(@reader: io.Reader, framing: Framing, limits: Limits) -> Message?`, called `jsonrpc.read_message(@reader, framing, limits)`: The next message `reader` holds, read and parsed: what a client reads from its peer, which writes one message at a time. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_text(s: io.Stream, text: str, framing: Framing) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.write_text(s, text, framing)`: Writes `text`, one message or batch, to `s` with its framing, in one write. Fails `invalid`.
- `function write_message(s: io.Stream, m: Message, framing: Framing) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.write_message(s, m, framing)`: Writes `m` to `s`, as `format` writes it and `write_text` frames it. Fails as `format` and `write_text` fail.
- `function write_answers(s: io.Stream, answers: [Message], batch: bool, framing: Framing) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.write_answers(s, answers, batch, framing)`: Writes the answers to one text received: one answer alone, a batch's as one array, and nothing where there is none, as when every message was a notification. Fails as `format` and `write_text` fail.
- `record Method(name: str, params: [str], required: i64)`: A method a server takes: its name and its parameters' names.
- `record Methods(by_name: {str: Method})`: The methods a server takes, by name.
- `record Found(method: str, params: {str: json.Value})`: What `method_of` answers: the method a request names, and its parameters by name.
- `function new_methods() -> Methods`, called `jsonrpc.new_methods()`: A table of no methods.
- `function add_method(@methods: Methods, name: str, params: [str], required: i64) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.add_method(@methods, name, params, required)`: Adds the method `name` to `methods`. Fails `invalid`, `exists`.
- `function method_of(methods: Methods, method: str, params: json.Value) -> Found?`, called `jsonrpc.method_of(methods, method, params)`: The method of `methods` that `method` names, and `params` by name. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.
- `function param_of(found: Found, name: str) -> json.Value?`, called `jsonrpc.param_of(found, name)`: The parameter `name` of `found`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function dispatch(text: str, methods: Methods, limits: Limits, handler: (function(Found) -> json.Value?)) -> str?`, called `jsonrpc.dispatch(text, methods, limits, handler)`: The answer to `text`, as a server with no state of its own answers it: each request found in `methods` and handed to `handler`, each notification handed to it and its answer dropped. Fails `unsupported`.
- `record Client(reader: io.Reader, writer: io.Stream, framing: Framing, limits: Limits, next_id: i64, inbox: [Message], waiting: deque.Deque)`: A client of one peer over a stream: where it writes its calls, where it reads what answers them, and what came meanwhile.
- `record Call(method: str, params: json.Value, notification: bool)`: A call of a batch: a method and its parameters, and whether it asks for an answer.
- `function new_client(reading: io.Stream, writing: io.Stream, framing: Framing, limits: Limits) -> Client`, called `jsonrpc.new_client(reading: reading, writing: writing, framing, limits)`: A client that writes to `writing` and reads from `reading`.
- `function call(@c: Client, method: str, params: json.Value) -> Reply?`, called `jsonrpc.call(@c, method, params)`: Calls `method` with `params` and waits for its answer. Fails `invalid`, `closed`.
- `function notify(c: Client, method: str, params: json.Value) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.notify(c, method, params)`: Writes the notification `method` with `params`, which nothing answers. Fails `invalid`.
- `function call_batch(@c: Client, calls: [Call]) -> [Reply]?`, called `jsonrpc.call_batch(@c, calls)`: Calls every one of `calls` in one batch and waits for every answer. Fails `invalid`.
- `function next_message(@c: Client) -> Message?`, called `jsonrpc.next_message(@c)`: The next message from the peer: the oldest one kept in the inbox, else the next one read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function send(c: Client, m: Message) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.send(c, m)`: Writes `m` to the peer: an answer to one of its requests, or any message. Fails as `write_message` fails.
- `function check_params(params: json.Value) -> ()?`, called `jsonrpc.check_params(params)`: Fails `invalid` where `params` is neither a list, an object nor `.null_value`, the three forms a call's parameters take. Fails `invalid`.
- `function read_http(r: http.Request, limits: Limits) -> Received?`, called `jsonrpc.read_http(r, limits)`: The message or the batch an HTTP request carries, as a server reads it. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function respond_http(answers: [Message], batch: bool) -> http.Response?`, called `jsonrpc.respond_http(answers, batch)`: The HTTP response that carries the answers to one request's body: 200 with the answer or the batch's array as `application/json`, or 204 with no body where nothing answers it. Fails as `format` fails.
- `function refusal_http(code: str, msg: str) -> http.Response`, called `jsonrpc.refusal_http(code: code, msg: msg)`: The HTTP response to a body `read_http` refused.
- `function exchange_http(transport: http.Client, r: http.Request, messages: [Message]) -> [Message]?`, called `jsonrpc.exchange_http(transport, r, messages)`: Sends `messages` in one `POST` and reads what answers them. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function call_http(transport: http.Client, target: str, method: str, params: json.Value) -> Reply?`, called `jsonrpc.call_http(transport, target: target, method: method, params)`: Calls `method` with `params` over HTTP, the id 1, and answers its reply. Fails `invalid`.


### acme

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/acme`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/acme/).

A client of ACME, RFC 8555: the directory read, an account made, found, changed or deactivated, an order placed for names, its authorizations answered by HTTP-01 or DNS-01, the order finalized with a certificate request, and the certificate chain downloaded, revoked, or asked when to renew (RFC 9773).

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an answer of the server that is not what RFC 8555 writes, and of an argument refused.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of an account looked for and not there: `find_account`.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a server's `rateLimited`.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: The code of a wait that ran out: `wait_authorization`, `wait_order`.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of what the server's directory does not offer: `new_authorization` without `newAuthz`, `fetch_renewal_info` without `renewalInfo`.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of every other refusal of the server, and of an authorization or an order that turned `invalid`: the problem's type and detail are in the message.
- `record Directory(new_nonce: str, new_account: str, new_order: str, new_authz: str, revoke_cert: str, key_change: str, renewal_info: str, terms_of_service: str, website: str, caa_identities: [str], external_account_required: bool, profiles: {str: str})`: What a server's directory names (RFC 8555 § 7.1.1).
- `record Client(directory: Directory, session: wire.Session)`: A client of one ACME server, with one account key.
- `function connect(directory_url: str, key: jose.Key, transport: http.Client) -> Client?`, called `acme.connect(directory_url, key, transport)`: A client of the server whose directory is at `directory_url`, signing with `key`: the directory read. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_directory(text: str) -> Directory?`, called `acme.parse_directory(text)`: The directory the JSON `text` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Account(url: str, status: str, contacts: [str], orders: str)`: An account, as the server answers it (RFC 8555 § 7.1.2).
- `function new_account(@client: Client, contacts: [str], agree_terms: bool) -> Account?`, called `acme.new_account(@client, contacts, agree_terms)`: The account of `client`'s key, made where none is; `client` signs as it from then on. Fails `failed`.
- `function new_account_bound(@client: Client, contacts: [str], agree_terms: bool, key_id: str, hmac_key: [u8]) -> Account?`, called `acme.new_account_bound(@client, contacts, agree_terms, key_id, hmac_key)`: The account of `client`'s key made and bound to an account the CA keeps (external account binding, RFC 8555 § 7.3.4). Fails as `new_account` does.
- `function find_account(@client: Client) -> Account?`, called `acme.find_account(@client)`: The account of `client`'s key, none made. Fails `not_found`.
- `function update_account(@client: Client, contacts: [str]) -> Account?`, called `acme.update_account(@client, contacts)`: `client`'s account with its contacts replaced. Fails `invalid`.
- `function deactivate_account(@client: Client) -> Account?`, called `acme.deactivate_account(@client)`: `client`'s account deactivated: it can do nothing more, for ever. Fails `invalid`.
- `function change_key(@client: Client, key: jose.Key) -> ()?`, called `acme.change_key(@client, key)`: `client`'s account moved to `key`, which signs from then on (RFC 8555 § 7.3.5). Fails `invalid`, `failed`.
- `function parse_account(text: str, url: str) -> Account?`, called `acme.parse_account(text: text, url: url)`: The account the JSON `text` writes, at `url`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Identifier(kind: str, value: str)`: What a certificate is for: a domain name or an IP address.
- `record Problem(kind: str, detail: str, status: i64, identifier: Identifier, subproblems: [Problem])`: A problem the server reports (RFC 7807 and RFC 8555 § 6.7).
- `function parse_problem(text: str) -> Problem?`, called `acme.parse_problem(text)`: The problem the JSON `text` writes: its type, detail, status, identifier and subproblems, these read one level deep. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Order(url: str, status: str, expires: time.Instant?, identifiers: [Identifier], not_before: time.Instant?, not_after: time.Instant?, authorizations: [str], finalize: str, certificate: str, profile: str, problems: [Problem])`: An order (RFC 8555 § 7.1.3).
- `record OrderRequest(identifiers: [Identifier], not_before: time.Instant?, not_after: time.Instant?, profile: str)`: What `new_order` asks for.
- `function order_for(names: [str]) -> OrderRequest`, called `acme.order_for(names)`: An order of a certificate for `names`, each a domain name, "*." before a wildcard; the validity and profile left to the server.
- `function new_order(@client: Client, request: OrderRequest) -> Order?`, called `acme.new_order(@client, request)`: An order placed. Fails `invalid`, `failed`, `limit`.
- `function fetch_order(@client: Client, url: str) -> Order?`, called `acme.fetch_order(@client, url)`: The order at `url`, read again. Fails `failed`.
- `function parse_order(text: str, url: str) -> Order?`, called `acme.parse_order(text: text, url: url)`: The order the JSON `text` writes, at `url`. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Challenge(url: str, kind: str, status: str, token: str, validated: time.Instant?, problems: [Problem])`: A challenge of an authorization (RFC 8555 § 7.1.5 and § 8).
- `record Authorization(url: str, status: str, identifier: Identifier, expires: time.Instant?, challenges: [Challenge], wildcard: bool)`: An authorization: the account's proof of control of one identifier.
- `function fetch_authorization(@client: Client, url: str) -> Authorization?`, called `acme.fetch_authorization(@client, url)`: The authorization at `url`. Fails `failed`.
- `function new_authorization(@client: Client, identifier: Identifier) -> Authorization?`, called `acme.new_authorization(@client, identifier)`: An authorization asked before any order, where the server offers it. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function deactivate_authorization(@client: Client, url: str) -> Authorization?`, called `acme.deactivate_authorization(@client, url)`: The authorization at `url` given up: deactivated, so the account must prove control again. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function parse_authorization(text: str, url: str) -> Authorization?`, called `acme.parse_authorization(text: text, url: url)`: The authorization the JSON `text` writes, at `url`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_challenge(text: str) -> Challenge?`, called `acme.parse_challenge(text)`: The challenge the JSON `text` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function challenge_of(authorization: Authorization, kind: str) -> Challenge?`, called `acme.challenge_of(authorization, kind)`: The challenge of `authorization` whose type is `kind`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function key_authorization(client: Client, token: str) -> str?`, called `acme.key_authorization(client, token)`: The key authorization of `token`: the token, a dot, and the account key's thumbprint (RFC 8555 § 8.1). Fails `invalid`.
- `function http01_path(token: str) -> str`, called `acme.http01_path(token)`: The path an HTTP-01 answer is served at, on port 80 of the name: "/.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>".
- `function http01_body(client: Client, token: str) -> str?`, called `acme.http01_body(client, token)`: The body an HTTP-01 answer is served with, as `text/plain`: the key authorization. Fails as `key_authorization` does.
- `function dns01_name(domain: str) -> str`, called `acme.dns01_name(domain)`: The name a DNS-01 answer is published under: "_acme-challenge." before the identifier, a wildcard's "*." left out.
- `function dns01_value(client: Client, token: str) -> str?`, called `acme.dns01_value(client, token)`: The TXT record a DNS-01 answer publishes: SHA-256 of the key authorization, in base 64 for URLs without padding. Fails as `key_authorization` does.
- `function accept_challenge(@client: Client, challenge: Challenge) -> Challenge?`, called `acme.accept_challenge(@client, challenge)`: `challenge` answered: the server told the answer is in place and asked to validate it. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function wait_authorization(@client: Client, url: str, timeout: time.Duration) -> Authorization?`, called `acme.wait_authorization(@client, url, timeout)`: The authorization at `url` once it settles: read again, the waits as the server's `Retry-After` asks, a second where it says none, until it is no longer "pending". Fails `failed`, `timeout`, `invalid`.
- `function finalize(@client: Client, order: Order, csr: [u8]) -> Order?`, called `acme.finalize(@client, order, csr)`: `order` finalized with the certificate request `csr`. Fails `failed`.
- `function wait_order(@client: Client, url: str, timeout: time.Duration) -> Order?`, called `acme.wait_order(@client, url, timeout)`: The order at `url` once it settles: read again until it is neither "pending" nor "processing", waiting as `wait_authorization` does. Fails `failed`, `timeout`, `invalid`.
- `record Chain(pem: str, alternates: [str])`: A certificate chain downloaded.
- `function download(@client: Client, url: str) -> Chain?`, called `acme.download(@client, url)`: The certificate chain at `url`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function revoke(@client: Client, certificate: [u8], reason: i64) -> ()?`, called `acme.revoke(@client, certificate, reason)`: The certificate `certificate` revoked, signed by the account. Fails `failed`.
- `record RenewalInfo(start: str, end: str, explanation: str)`: When the CA suggests renewing a certificate (RFC 9773).
- `function renewal_id(certificate: [u8]) -> str?`, called `acme.renewal_id(certificate)`: The identifier RFC 9773 names a certificate by: its authority key identifier and its serial number's bytes, each in base 64 for URLs without padding, joined by a dot. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_renewal_info(client: Client, certificate: [u8]) -> RenewalInfo?`, called `acme.fetch_renewal_info(client, certificate)`: The renewal window of `certificate`, asked of the server. Fails `unsupported`.


### x509/ocsp

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/x509/ocsp`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/x509/ocsp/).

OCSP (RFC 6960): whether a certificate is revoked, asked of the responder its issuer names and the answer checked.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A request or a response that is not what RFC 6960 says, or a signature, a signer, a nonce or a moment that does not hold, the message saying which.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A response that says nothing of the certificate asked about; a certificate that names no responder: `status_of`, `check`.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: A responder's error status, or an HTTP status other than 200: the message carries it.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: A CertID's hash, a response's type or a signature's algorithm not read here.
- `record CertId(hash: crypto.Algorithm, issuer_name_hash: [u8], issuer_key_hash: [u8], serial: big.Integer)`: How a request and a response name one certificate (RFC 6960 § 4.1.1).
- `function id_of(certificate: x509.Certificate, issuer: x509.Certificate, hash: crypto.Algorithm) -> CertId?`, called `ocsp.id_of(certificate: certificate, issuer: issuer, hash)`: The CertID of `certificate`, issued by `issuer`, by `hash`. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function is_issued_by(id: CertId, issuer: x509.Certificate) -> bool`, called `ocsp.is_issued_by(id, issuer)`: Whether `id` names a certificate `issuer` issued: its hashes are of the issuer's name and key, by the hash it names.
- `record Request(ids: [CertId], nonce: [u8], signed: bool, der: [u8])`: A request read.
- `function new_nonce() -> [u8]?`, called `ocsp.new_nonce()`: A nonce of 32 bytes, the most RFC 8954 § 2.1 allows, drawn from the system's source. Fails as `os.random_bytes` fails.
- `function create_request(asked: [CertId], nonce: [u8]) -> [u8]?`, called `ocsp.create_request(asked, nonce)`: The DER of a request for `asked`, with `nonce` where it is not []. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function decode_request(der: [u8]) -> Request?`, called `ocsp.decode_request(der)`: The request `der` holds. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function get_url(base: str, request: [u8]) -> str`, called `ocsp.get_url(base, request)`: The URL of a GET of `request` from the responder at `base` (RFC 6960 appendix A.1): `base`, a `/` where it ends in none, and the request in base 64 with `+`, `/` and `=` escaped.
- `variant ResponseStatus = .successful | .malformed_request | .internal_error | .try_later | .sig_required | .unauthorized`: How a responder answered (RFC 6960 § 4.2.1).
- `variant Status = .good | .revoked(at: time.DateTime, reason: x509.Reason?) | .unknown`: What a response says of a certificate.
- `record Single(id: CertId, status: Status, this_update: time.DateTime, next_update: time.DateTime?, extensions: [x509.Extension])`: What a response says of one certificate.
- `variant ResponderId = .by_name(name: x509.Name) | .by_key(hash: [u8])`: How a response names its signer.
- `record Basic(tbs: [u8], responder: ResponderId, produced_at: time.DateTime, responses: [Single], nonce: [u8], extensions: [x509.Extension], signature_algorithm: x509.Algorithm, signature: [u8], certificates: [x509.Certificate])`: A basic response (RFC 6960 § 4.2.1), what a `successful` one holds.
- `record Response(status: ResponseStatus, basic: Basic?, der: [u8])`: A response read.
- `function format_response_status(status: ResponseStatus) -> str`, called `ocsp.format_response_status(status)`: The name RFC 6960 gives `status`.
- `function decode_response(der: [u8]) -> Response?`, called `ocsp.decode_response(der)`: The response `der` holds, as a responder sends it or a TLS server staples it. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`, `not_found`.
- `record Options(at: time.Instant, nonce: [u8], nonce_required: bool, skew: time.Duration, max_age: time.Duration)`: What a response is checked against.
- `function default_options(at: time.Instant, nonce: [u8]) -> Options`, called `ocsp.default_options(at, nonce)`: The options of the moment `at` and the nonce `nonce`: five minutes of skew and an hour of age, a response without a nonce taken on its freshness.
- `function signer_of(basic: Basic, issuer: x509.Certificate, at: time.Instant) -> x509.Certificate?`, called `ocsp.signer_of(basic, issuer, at)`: The certificate that signed `basic`, for the certificates `issuer` issued: the issuer itself, or a responder it delegated to, which `basic` carries, which `issuer` signed for `x509.OCSP_SIGNING`, whose key usage, where it is written, allows a signature, and which is valid at `at` (RFC 6960 § 4.2.2.2). Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function status_of(response: Response, certificate: x509.Certificate, issuer: x509.Certificate, options: Options) -> Single?`, called `ocsp.status_of(response, certificate: certificate, issuer: issuer, options)`: What `response` says of `certificate`, issued by `issuer`, once every check of this module's comment holds. Fails `failed`, `invalid`, `not_found`, `unsupported`.
- `function check(certificate: x509.Certificate, issuer: x509.Certificate, client: http.Client) -> Single?`, called `ocsp.check(certificate: certificate, issuer: issuer, client)`: The status of `certificate`, issued by `issuer`, asked of the responders its `authorityInfoAccess` names, in their order until one answers: a request by SHA-1 with a fresh nonce sent by POST, the response checked at the moment it is read by `status_of` with `default_options`. Fails `not_found`, `failed`.
- `record Answer(id: CertId, status: Status, this_update: time.DateTime, next_update: time.DateTime?)`: What a responder says of one certificate.
- `record ResponseTemplate(answers: [Answer], produced_at: time.DateTime, nonce: [u8], by_key: bool, certificates: [x509.Certificate])`: What a response says, and how it names its signer.
- `function create_response(template: ResponseTemplate, signer: x509.Certificate, key: keypairs.PrivateKey, scheme: keypairs.Scheme) -> [u8]?`, called `ocsp.create_response(template, signer, key, scheme)`: The DER of a successful response of `template`, signed by `signer`'s `key` by `scheme`: the issuer's own key, or a delegated responder's. Fails `invalid`, `unsupported`.
- `function create_error_response(status: ResponseStatus) -> [u8]?`, called `ocsp.create_error_response(status)`: The DER of a response answering the error `status`, with no responseBytes. Fails `invalid`.


### llm/anthropic

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/llm/anthropic`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/llm/anthropic/).

Claude's Messages API spoken over `http`, with no SDK: a conversation sent and its answer read whole or as it streams, tools whose calls the program runs itself, tokens counted, batches of requests, the models listed, and every failure the API answers told with its status, its type, its request id and the wait it advises.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A request or an argument not of the API's form (400, 422), and an answer not of the shape the API documents.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: A key refused or a resource it may not use (401, 402, 403), and a request the model refused (`stop_reason` `refusal`, by `require_complete`).
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A model, a batch or a path the API does not know (404), and a key set nowhere.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A request too large (413), a rate limit or a spend cap reached (429), the API overloaded (529), and an answer cut at `max_tokens` or at the model's context window (`require_complete`).
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: A request the API gave up on (408, 504), and the client's deadline passed.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: Every other status the API answers (409, 500, and the 5xx it does not name): the message carries its type and its words.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection closed before an answer was whole, or a stream read past its end.
- `constant API_VERSION: str`, value `"2026-10-21"`: The version of the API this package speaks, sent as `anthropic-version`.
- `constant BASE_URL: str`, value `"https://api.anthropic.com"`: The address of the Claude API.
- `constant STOP_END_TURN: str`, value `"end_turn"`: The model reached a natural stopping point.
- `constant STOP_MAX_TOKENS: str`, value `"max_tokens"`: The answer reached the request's `max_tokens`, or the model's most.
- `constant STOP_STOP_SEQUENCE: str`, value `"stop_sequence"`: The answer met one of the request's `stop_sequences`, which `Message.stop_sequence` names.
- `constant STOP_TOOL_USE: str`, value `"tool_use"`: The model called one or more tools, which `tool_calls_of` hands out.
- `constant STOP_PAUSE_TURN: str`, value `"pause_turn"`: The API paused a long turn of server tools: the answer is sent back as it is, by `with_reply`, and the model goes on.
- `constant STOP_REFUSAL: str`, value `"refusal"`: The model declined the request; `Message.stop_details` says why.
- `constant STOP_CONTEXT_WINDOW: str`, value `"model_context_window_exceeded"`: The answer filled the model's context window.
- `constant BATCH_IN_PROGRESS: str`, value `"in_progress"`: A batch whose requests are still being processed.
- `constant BATCH_CANCELING: str`, value `"canceling"`: A batch whose cancelling has begun.
- `constant BATCH_ENDED: str`, value `"ended"`: A batch whose every request has ended, and whose results can be read.
- `record Client(api_key: str, auth_token: str, base_url: str, version: str, betas: [str], headers: [http.Header], max_retries: i64, max_wait: time.Duration, deadline: time.Duration, roots: str, limits: http.Limits)`: How requests reach the API: the credentials, the address, the version, and how a request is sent again.
- `function default_client(api_key: str) -> Client`, called `anthropic.default_client(api_key)`: A client of the Claude API with the key `api_key`: version `API_VERSION`, 2 retries waiting at most a minute each, 10 minutes for an attempt, as the official SDKs wait, and `http`'s limits.
- `function client_from_env() -> Client?`, called `anthropic.client_from_env()`: A client as `default_client` makes one, its key read from the environment: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, else `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` as a token, and its address from `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` where that is set. Fails `not_found`.
- `record Turn(role: str, content: [json.Value])`: One turn of a conversation: who speaks, and the content blocks said.
- `record Tool(name: str, description: str, input_schema: json.Value, strict: bool, eager_input_streaming: bool)`: A tool the model may call, which the program runs itself.
- `record Request(model: str, max_tokens: i64, system: str, turns: [Turn], tools: [Tool], server_tools: [json.Value], fields: {str: json.Value})`: What is sent to make a message: the fields every request has, and every other parameter by name.
- `function new_request(model: str, max_tokens: i64, turns: [Turn]) -> Request`, called `anthropic.new_request(model, max_tokens, turns)`: A request to `model` for at most `max_tokens` tokens, holding `turns` and nothing else.
- `function user(text: str) -> Turn`, called `anthropic.user(text)`: A user's turn holding the text `text`.
- `function assistant(text: str) -> Turn`, called `anthropic.assistant(text)`: An assistant's turn holding the text `text`, for a conversation written by hand; an answer's own turn is `turn_of`'s.
- `function text_block(text: str) -> json.Value`, called `anthropic.text_block(text)`: A text block: `{"type": "text", "text": ...}`.
- `function image_block(media_type: str, data: [u8]) -> json.Value`, called `anthropic.image_block(media_type, data)`: An image block of `data` in base 64.
- `function document_block(data: [u8]) -> json.Value`, called `anthropic.document_block(data)`: A document block of the PDF `data` in base 64.
- `function cached(block: json.Value, ttl: str) -> json.Value`, called `anthropic.cached(block, ttl)`: `block` marked as the end of a prefix the API caches: its `cache_control` set to `{"type": "ephemeral"}`, with `ttl` where it is not "".
- `function with_field(r: Request, name: str, value: json.Value) -> Request`, called `anthropic.with_field(r, name, value)`: A copy of `r` with the parameter `name` set to `value`, replacing one of that name.
- `function with_effort(r: Request, effort: str) -> Request`, called `anthropic.with_effort(r, effort)`: A copy of `r` whose `output_config.effort` is `effort`, the rest of its `output_config` kept.
- `function with_turn(r: Request, turn: Turn) -> Request`, called `anthropic.with_turn(r, turn)`: A copy of `r` with `turn` after its turns.
- `function request_json(r: Request) -> json.Value?`, called `anthropic.request_json(r)`: The body `create` sends for `r`, as the API reads it: `model`, `max_tokens`, `messages`, `system` and `tools` where set, `tools` holding `r.tools` then `r.server_tools`, then `r.fields` in their order. Fails `invalid`, `does_not_fit`.
- `record Usage(input_tokens: i64, output_tokens: i64, cache_creation_input_tokens: i64, cache_read_input_tokens: i64)`: The tokens an answer counted.
- `record Message(id: str, model: str, role: str, content: [json.Value], stop_reason: str, stop_sequence: str, stop_details: json.Value, usage: Usage, inputs: {str: str})`: A message the model answered: what `create` reads, what a stream builds, and what a batch's result holds.
- `variant Block = .text(text: str) | .thinking(thinking: str, signature: str) | .redacted_thinking(data: str) | .tool_use(id: str, name: str, input: json.Value) | .server_tool_use(id: str, name: str, input: json.Value) | .other(kind: str, value: json.Value)`: A content block of an answer, read by `blocks_of`.
- `record ToolCall(id: str, name: str, input_json: str)`: A call of a tool of the program's, as `tool_calls_of` hands it out.
- `function message_of(v: json.Value) -> Message?`, called `anthropic.message_of(v)`: The message the JSON `v` holds, as the API writes one. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_message(text: str) -> Message?`, called `anthropic.parse_message(text)`: The message the JSON text `text` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function blocks_of(m: Message) -> [Block]`, called `anthropic.blocks_of(m)`: The content blocks of `m` as a variant, in order.
- `function text_of(m: Message) -> str`, called `anthropic.text_of(m)`: The text of `m`'s text blocks, joined with nothing between them.
- `function require_complete(m: Message) -> Message?`, called `anthropic.require_complete(m)`: `m` where it stopped as a turn ends: at its end, at a stop sequence, to call tools, or paused for the program to send it back. Fails `permission`, `limit`.
- `function turn_of(m: Message) -> Turn`, called `anthropic.turn_of(m)`: The assistant's turn `m` is, its blocks unchanged, to send back.
- `function with_reply(r: Request, reply: Message) -> Request`, called `anthropic.with_reply(r, reply)`: A copy of `r` with the answer `reply` after its turns: what goes back after `pause_turn`.
- `function tool_calls_of(m: Message) -> [ToolCall]`, called `anthropic.tool_calls_of(m)`: The calls of the program's tools `m` holds, in order: what the program runs where `stop_reason` is `tool_use`.
- `function input_of(call: ToolCall) -> json.Value?`, called `anthropic.input_of(call)`: The input of `call`, checked whole: a JSON object. Fails `invalid`.
- `function tool_result(tool_use_id: str, content: str, is_error: bool) -> json.Value`, called `anthropic.tool_result(tool_use_id: tool_use_id, content: content, is_error)`: The block that answers the call `tool_use_id`: `content` as its text, and `is_error` where the tool failed.
- `function with_tool_results(r: Request, reply: Message, results: [json.Value]) -> Request`, called `anthropic.with_tool_results(r, reply, results)`: A copy of `r` with the answer `reply` and then one user turn holding `results`: the next request of a tool loop, every result of one turn in one message, as the API asks.
- `record ApiError(status: i64, kind: str, message: str, request_id: str, retryable: bool, wait: time.Duration)`: A failure the API answered, as `failure_of` reads it from a message.
- `function failure_of(msg: str) -> ApiError?`, called `anthropic.failure_of(msg)`: The failure the API answered that `msg` tells, as every call of this package writes one: `[429 rate_limit_error req_01 1500] words`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function send_raw(c: Client, method: str, path: str, body: json.Value) -> http.Response?`, called `anthropic.send_raw(c, method: method, path: path, body)`: The answer of any endpoint of the API, read whole, with this client's key, version, betas and retries: what this package does not wrap, the Files and Skills APIs and the betas, reached by hand. Fails as the API answers, each status with its code and its `ApiError` in the message, and as `http.send` fails.
- `function create(c: Client, r: Request) -> Message?`, called `anthropic.create(c, r)`: The message the model answers to `r`, read whole. Fails `invalid`.
- `function count_input_tokens(c: Client, r: Request) -> i64?`, called `anthropic.count_input_tokens(c, r)`: The input tokens `r` would cost, as the API counts them before it is sent: its turns, its system prompt and its tools. Fails as `create` fails.
- `record Stream(state: streaming.State)`: A message being read as its events come, made by `stream`: what has arrived, and the connection it arrives on.
- `variant Event = .message_start(message: Message) | .block_start(index: i64, block: json.Value) | .text_delta(index: i64, text: str) | .thinking_delta(index: i64, thinking: str) | .signature_delta(index: i64, signature: str) | .input_delta(index: i64, partial_json: str) | .citation_delta(index: i64, citation: json.Value) | .block_stop(index: i64, block: json.Value) | .message_delta(stop_reason: str, usage: Usage) | .message_stop | .ping | .other(name: str, data: json.Value)`: One event of a stream, as `next_event` reads it.
- `function stream(c: Client, r: Request) -> Stream?`, called `anthropic.stream(c, r)`: A stream of the message the model answers to `r`, its head read and no event yet. Fails `invalid`.
- `function next_event(@s: Stream) -> Event?`, called `anthropic.next_event(@s)`: The next event of `s`, waiting for it, added to the message so far. Fails `closed`, `limit`, `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `function message_so_far(s: Stream) -> Message?`, called `anthropic.message_so_far(s)`: The message of `s` as far as it has arrived: the blocks ended whole, the open one as far as it has come, a tool's input read as far as it is JSON. Fails `invalid`.
- `function final_message(@s: Stream) -> Message?`, called `anthropic.final_message(@s)`: The whole message of `s`, its remaining events read: what the SDKs call the final message. Fails as `next_event` fails, before the message is whole.
- `function input_so_far(s: Stream) -> json.Partial?`, called `anthropic.input_so_far(s)`: What the input of the tool call streaming now holds so far, read as `json.parse_partial` reads a text still arriving. Fails `not_found`.
- `function close_stream(@s: Stream)`, called `anthropic.close_stream(@s)`: Closes the connection of `s`; a stream not read to its end is cut there.
- `record ModelInfo(id: str, display_name: str, created_at: time.Instant?, max_input_tokens: i64, max_tokens: i64, raw: json.Value)`: A model the API serves, as the Models API describes it.
- `record Cursor(after_id: str, before_id: str, limit: i64)`: Where a page of a list begins, and how long it is.
- `record ModelPage(models: [ModelInfo], has_more: bool, first_id: str, last_id: str)`: A page of models.
- `function first_page() -> Cursor`, called `anthropic.first_page()`: The first page of a list, of 20 items.
- `function model_info_of(v: json.Value) -> ModelInfo?`, called `anthropic.model_info_of(v)`: The model the JSON `v` describes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function list_models(c: Client, cursor: Cursor) -> ModelPage?`, called `anthropic.list_models(c, cursor)`: A page of the models the API serves. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_model(c: Client, id: str) -> ModelInfo?`, called `anthropic.fetch_model(c, id)`: The model whose id or alias is `id`. Fails `not_found`.
- `record BatchRequest(custom_id: str, request: Request)`: One request of a batch, named so its result can be found.
- `record RequestCounts(processing: i64, succeeded: i64, errored: i64, canceled: i64, expired: i64)`: How many requests of a batch stand in each state.
- `record Batch(id: str, processing_status: str, request_counts: RequestCounts, created_at: time.Instant?, ended_at: time.Instant?, expires_at: time.Instant?, cancel_initiated_at: time.Instant?, archived_at: time.Instant?, results_url: str)`: A batch of requests the API answers within a day, at half the price.
- `record BatchPage(batches: [Batch], has_more: bool, first_id: str, last_id: str)`: A page of batches.
- `variant Outcome = .succeeded(message: Message) | .errored(error: ApiError) | .canceled | .expired`: How one request of a batch ended.
- `record BatchResult(custom_id: str, outcome: Outcome)`: The result of one request of a batch.
- `function batch_of(v: json.Value) -> Batch?`, called `anthropic.batch_of(v)`: The batch the JSON `v` describes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function create_batch(c: Client, requests: [BatchRequest]) -> Batch?`, called `anthropic.create_batch(c, requests)`: Sends `requests` as one batch. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_batch(c: Client, id: str) -> Batch?`, called `anthropic.fetch_batch(c, id)`: The batch `id` as it stands now: what a program polls until it has ended. Fails `not_found`.
- `function list_batches(c: Client, cursor: Cursor) -> BatchPage?`, called `anthropic.list_batches(c, cursor)`: A page of the workspace's batches. Fails `invalid`.
- `function cancel_batch(c: Client, id: str) -> Batch?`, called `anthropic.cancel_batch(c, id)`: Begins cancelling the batch `id`; the requests not yet sent end `canceled`. Fails as `fetch_batch` fails.
- `function delete_batch(c: Client, id: str) -> ()?`, called `anthropic.delete_batch(c, id)`: Deletes the ended batch `id` and its results. Fails as `fetch_batch` fails.
- `function batch_result_of(line: json.Value) -> BatchResult?`, called `anthropic.batch_result_of(line)`: The result one line of a batch's results holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_batch_results(text: str) -> [BatchResult]?`, called `anthropic.parse_batch_results(text)`: The results a batch's `.jsonl` text holds, one object a line, in the order written: not the order of the requests, so a program finds each by its `custom_id`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function batch_results(c: Client, id: str) -> [BatchResult]?`, called `anthropic.batch_results(c, id)`: The results of the ended batch `id`, read a line at a time as they come. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.


### llm/openai

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/llm/openai`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/llm/openai/).

OpenAI's Chat Completions and Responses APIs spoken over `http`, with no SDK, and every server that speaks them: Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp's and LM Studio's servers, reached by their base URL.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: A request or an argument not of the API's form (400, 422), and an answer not of the shape the API documents.
- `constant PERMISSION: str`, value `"permission"`: A key refused or a resource it may not use (401, 402, 403), and an answer the model refused or a filter cut (`require_finished`, `require_complete`).
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: A model or a path the server does not know (404), and a variable of the environment unset.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: A request too large (413), a rate limit or a quota reached (429), a model overloaded (503), and an answer cut at its ceiling of tokens.
- `constant TIMEOUT: str`, value `"timeout"`: A request the server gave up on (408, 504), and the client's deadline passed.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: Every other status (409, 500, and the 5xx not named): the message carries the server's type, code and words, and a response that failed.
- `constant CLOSED: str`, value `"closed"`: The connection closed before an answer was whole, or a stream read past its end.
- `constant BASE_URL: str`, value `"https://api.openai.com/v1"`: The address of OpenAI's API, its version in its path.
- `constant OLLAMA_URL: str`, value `"http://localhost:11434/v1"`: The address of a local Ollama, where `OLLAMA_HOST` says none.
- `constant FINISH_STOP: str`, value `"stop"`: A choice that reached a natural stop or a stop sequence.
- `constant FINISH_LENGTH: str`, value `"length"`: A choice cut at the request's ceiling of tokens.
- `constant FINISH_TOOL_CALLS: str`, value `"tool_calls"`: A choice that calls tools, which `tool_calls_of` hands out.
- `constant FINISH_CONTENT_FILTER: str`, value `"content_filter"`: A choice whose content a filter left out.
- `constant STATUS_COMPLETED: str`, value `"completed"`: A response whose output is whole.
- `constant STATUS_INCOMPLETE: str`, value `"incomplete"`: A response cut short; `Response.incomplete_reason` says why.
- `constant STATUS_FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: A response that failed; `Response.error` says why.
- `constant STATUS_IN_PROGRESS: str`, value `"in_progress"`: A response still being made, in the background.
- `constant STATUS_QUEUED: str`, value `"queued"`: A response waiting to be made, in the background.
- `constant STATUS_CANCELLED: str`, value `"cancelled"`: A response cancelled before its end.
- `record Client(api_key: str, base_url: str, organization: str, project: str, headers: [http.Header], max_retries: i64, max_wait: time.Duration, deadline: time.Duration, roots: str, limits: http.Limits)`: How requests reach a server: the key, the address, and how a request is sent again.
- `function default_client(api_key: str) -> Client`, called `openai.default_client(api_key)`: A client of OpenAI's API with the key `api_key`: 2 retries waiting at most a minute each, 10 minutes for an attempt, as the official SDKs wait.
- `function client_from_env() -> Client?`, called `openai.client_from_env()`: A client as `default_client` makes one, read from the environment: the key from `OPENAI_API_KEY`, the address from `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, the organization from `OPENAI_ORG_ID` and the project from `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID`, each where set. Fails `not_found`.
- `function local_client(base_url: str) -> Client`, called `openai.local_client(base_url)`: A client of a server of the program's that speaks the format, sending no key: vLLM, llama.cpp's server, LM Studio.
- `function ollama_client() -> Client?`, called `openai.ollama_client()`: A client of the Ollama `OLLAMA_HOST` names, `OLLAMA_URL` where it is unset: a host, a host and a port, or a URL, its port 11434 where it names none and `0.0.0.0` read as the loopback, as Ollama's own clients read it. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Function(name: str, description: str, parameters: json.Value, strict: bool)`: A function the model may call, which the program runs itself; the same for both APIs.
- `record ToolCall(id: str, name: str, arguments: str)`: A call of a function of the program's, as an answer holds it.
- `function arguments_of(call: ToolCall) -> json.Value?`, called `openai.arguments_of(call)`: The arguments of `call`, checked whole: a JSON object. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Usage(input_tokens: i64, output_tokens: i64, total_tokens: i64, cached_tokens: i64, reasoning_tokens: i64)`: The tokens an answer counted, by either API.
- `record ApiError(status: i64, kind: str, code: str, message: str, request_id: str, retryable: bool, wait: time.Duration)`: A failure the server answered, as `failure_of` reads it from a message.
- `function failure_of(msg: str) -> ApiError?`, called `openai.failure_of(msg)`: The failure the server answered that `msg` tells, as every call of this package writes one: `[429 requests rate_limit_exceeded req_1 1500] words`. Fails `not_found`.
- `function send_raw(c: Client, method: str, path: str, body: json.Value) -> http.Response?`, called `openai.send_raw(c, method: method, path: path, body)`: The answer of any endpoint of the server, read whole, with this client's key and retries: what this package does not wrap, files, batches, moderations, reached by hand. Fails as the server answers, each status with its code and its `ApiError` in the message, and as `http.send` fails.
- `record ChatRequest(model: str, messages: [json.Value], tools: [Function], fields: {str: json.Value})`: What is sent to make a chat completion: the fields every request has, and every other parameter by name.
- `record Choice(index: i64, finish_reason: str, message: json.Value, content: str, refusal: str, tool_calls: [ToolCall])`: One choice of a chat completion.
- `record Completion(id: str, model: str, created: time.Instant?, choices: [Choice], usage: Usage)`: A chat completion: what `chat` reads and a chat stream builds.
- `function chat_request(model: str, messages: [json.Value]) -> ChatRequest`, called `openai.chat_request(model, messages)`: A request to `model` holding `messages` and nothing else.
- `function system_message(text: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.system_message(text)`: The instructions of the system, read first.
- `function developer_message(text: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.developer_message(text)`: The instructions of the developer, which newer models read in place of the system's.
- `function user_message(text: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.user_message(text)`: What a user says.
- `function user_parts(parts: [json.Value]) -> json.Value`, called `openai.user_parts(parts)`: A user's message of several parts: text and images.
- `function text_part(text: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.text_part(text)`: A part of text.
- `function image_part(image_url: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.image_part(image_url)`: A part holding the image at `image_url`.
- `function assistant_message(text: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.assistant_message(text)`: What the assistant said, for a conversation written by hand; an answer's own message is `Choice.message`.
- `function tool_message(tool_call_id: str, content: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.tool_message(tool_call_id: tool_call_id, content: content)`: The answer to the call `tool_call_id`.
- `function with_chat_field(r: ChatRequest, name: str, value: json.Value) -> ChatRequest`, called `openai.with_chat_field(r, name, value)`: A copy of `r` with the parameter `name` set to `value`, replacing one of that name.
- `function with_message(r: ChatRequest, message: json.Value) -> ChatRequest`, called `openai.with_message(r, message)`: A copy of `r` with `message` after its messages.
- `function with_tool_messages(r: ChatRequest, reply: Completion, results: [json.Value]) -> ChatRequest`, called `openai.with_tool_messages(r, reply, results)`: A copy of `r` with the first choice of `reply` and then `results`: the next request of a tool loop.
- `function chat_request_json(r: ChatRequest) -> json.Value?`, called `openai.chat_request_json(r)`: The body `chat` sends for `r`: `model`, `messages`, `tools` where set, then `r.fields` in their order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function completion_of(v: json.Value) -> Completion?`, called `openai.completion_of(v)`: The chat completion the JSON `v` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_completion(text: str) -> Completion?`, called `openai.parse_completion(text)`: The chat completion the JSON text `text` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function text_of(done: Completion) -> str`, called `openai.text_of(done)`: The text of the first choice of `done`, "" where it has none.
- `function tool_calls_of(done: Completion) -> [ToolCall]`, called `openai.tool_calls_of(done)`: The calls of the program's functions the first choice of `done` holds.
- `function require_finished(done: Completion) -> Completion?`, called `openai.require_finished(done)`: `done` where its first choice finished as a turn ends: a stop or tool calls. Fails `permission`, `limit`, `invalid`.
- `function chat(c: Client, r: ChatRequest) -> Completion?`, called `openai.chat(c, r)`: The chat completion the model answers to `r`, read whole. Fails `invalid`.
- `record ChatStream(state: chat_chunks.State)`: A chat completion being read as its chunks come, made by `chat_stream`.
- `record ToolCallDelta(index: i64, id: str, name: str, arguments: str)`: A piece of a tool call, as a chunk carries it.
- `record ChunkChoice(index: i64, content: str, refusal: str, tool_calls: [ToolCallDelta], finish_reason: str)`: A choice's piece, as a chunk carries it.
- `record Chunk(id: str, model: str, choices: [ChunkChoice], usage: Usage)`: One chunk of a chat stream.
- `function chat_stream(c: Client, r: ChatRequest) -> ChatStream?`, called `openai.chat_stream(c, r)`: A stream of the chat completion the model answers to `r`, its head read and no chunk yet; the usage is asked for in a last chunk. Fails `invalid`.
- `function next_chunk(@s: ChatStream) -> Chunk?`, called `openai.next_chunk(@s)`: The next chunk of `s`, waiting for it, added to the completion so far. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `function completion_so_far(s: ChatStream) -> Completion?`, called `openai.completion_so_far(s)`: The completion of `s` as far as it has arrived: each choice's text, refusal and calls joined, their arguments as far as they came. Fails `invalid`.
- `function final_completion(@s: ChatStream) -> Completion?`, called `openai.final_completion(@s)`: The whole completion of `s`, its remaining chunks read. Fails `closed`.
- `function close_chat_stream(@s: ChatStream)`, called `openai.close_chat_stream(@s)`: Closes the connection of `s`; a stream not read to its end is cut there.
- `record ResponseRequest(model: str, input: [json.Value], instructions: str, tools: [Function], previous_response_id: str, fields: {str: json.Value})`: What is sent to make a response: the fields every request has, and every other parameter by name.
- `record Response(id: str, model: str, status: str, output: [json.Value], usage: Usage, error: json.Value, incomplete_reason: str)`: A response of the Responses API.
- `function response_request(model: str, input: [json.Value]) -> ResponseRequest`, called `openai.response_request(model, input)`: A request to `model` holding `input` and nothing else.
- `function input_message(role: str, text: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.input_message(role: role, text: text)`: An input message of `role` holding `text`.
- `function function_output(call_id: str, output: str) -> json.Value`, called `openai.function_output(call_id: call_id, output: output)`: The output of the call `call_id`, an input item.
- `function with_response_field(r: ResponseRequest, name: str, value: json.Value) -> ResponseRequest`, called `openai.with_response_field(r, name, value)`: A copy of `r` with the parameter `name` set to `value`.
- `function with_function_outputs(r: ResponseRequest, reply: Response, outputs: [json.Value]) -> ResponseRequest`, called `openai.with_function_outputs(r, reply, outputs)`: A copy of `r` with the output of `reply` and then `outputs` after its input: the next request of a tool loop that keeps no state on the server.
- `function response_request_json(r: ResponseRequest) -> json.Value?`, called `openai.response_request_json(r)`: The body `create_response` sends for `r`: `model`, `input`, `instructions`, `tools` and `previous_response_id` where set, then `r.fields` in their order. Fails `invalid`.
- `function response_of(v: json.Value) -> Response?`, called `openai.response_of(v)`: The response the JSON `v` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function parse_response(text: str) -> Response?`, called `openai.parse_response(text)`: The response the JSON text `text` holds. Fails `invalid`.
- `function output_text_of(r: Response) -> str`, called `openai.output_text_of(r)`: The text of `r`'s messages: every `output_text` part, joined with nothing between them, what the SDKs call `output_text`.
- `function function_calls_of(r: Response) -> [ToolCall]`, called `openai.function_calls_of(r)`: The calls of the program's functions `r` holds, in order.
- `function require_complete(r: Response) -> Response?`, called `openai.require_complete(r)`: `r` where it completed and refused nothing. Fails `failed`, `limit`, `permission`, `invalid`.
- `function create_response(c: Client, r: ResponseRequest) -> Response?`, called `openai.create_response(c, r)`: The response the model makes for `r`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_response(c: Client, id: str) -> Response?`, called `openai.fetch_response(c, id)`: The response `id` as the server keeps it: one made in the background polled until it ends. Fails `not_found`.
- `function cancel_response(c: Client, id: str) -> Response?`, called `openai.cancel_response(c, id)`: Cancels the response `id`, made in the background. Fails as `fetch_response` fails.
- `function delete_response(c: Client, id: str) -> ()?`, called `openai.delete_response(c, id)`: Deletes the response `id` the server keeps. Fails as `fetch_response` fails.
- `function count_input_tokens(c: Client, r: ResponseRequest) -> i64?`, called `openai.count_input_tokens(c, r)`: The input tokens `r` would cost, as the API counts them before it is sent: its input, its instructions and its tools. Fails as `create_response` fails.
- `record ResponseStream(state: response_events.State)`: A response being read as its events come, made by `response_stream`.
- `variant ResponseEvent = .created(response: Response) | .item_added(output_index: i64, item: json.Value) | .item_done(output_index: i64, item: json.Value) | .text_delta(item_id: str, output_index: i64, content_index: i64, delta: str) | .text_done(item_id: str, output_index: i64, content_index: i64, text: str) | .arguments_delta(item_id: str, output_index: i64, delta: str) | .arguments_done(item_id: str, output_index: i64, arguments: str) | .refusal_delta(item_id: str, output_index: i64, delta: str) | .completed(response: Response) | .incomplete(response: Response) | .failed(response: Response) | .other(name: str, data: json.Value)`: One event of a response stream, as `next_response_event` reads it.
- `function response_stream(c: Client, r: ResponseRequest) -> ResponseStream?`, called `openai.response_stream(c, r)`: A stream of the response the model makes for `r`, its head read and no event yet. Fails `invalid`.
- `function next_response_event(@s: ResponseStream) -> ResponseEvent?`, called `openai.next_response_event(@s)`: The next event of `s`, waiting for it. Fails `closed`, `invalid`, `timeout`.
- `function response_so_far(s: ResponseStream) -> Response?`, called `openai.response_so_far(s)`: The response of `s` as far as it has arrived: whole after its last event, else its items with their text and arguments as far as they came. Fails `invalid`.
- `function final_response(@s: ResponseStream) -> Response?`, called `openai.final_response(@s)`: The response of `s` as its last event holds it, its remaining events read. Fails as `next_response_event` fails before the last event.
- `function close_response_stream(@s: ResponseStream)`, called `openai.close_response_stream(@s)`: Closes the connection of `s`; a stream not read to its end is cut there.
- `record EmbeddingRequest(model: str, inputs: [str], dimensions: i64)`: What is sent to embed texts.
- `record Embeddings(vectors: [[f32]], model: str, usage: Usage)`: The vectors of an embedding request.
- `function embedding_request(model: str, inputs: [str]) -> EmbeddingRequest`, called `openai.embedding_request(model, inputs)`: A request to embed `inputs` with `model`, each vector of the model's own length.
- `function embed(c: Client, r: EmbeddingRequest) -> Embeddings?`, called `openai.embed(c, r)`: The vectors of `r`'s inputs, as `f32`s, in the inputs' order. Fails `invalid`.
- `record Model(id: str, owned_by: str, created: time.Instant?)`: A model the server serves.
- `function list_models(c: Client) -> [Model]?`, called `openai.list_models(c)`: The models the server serves. Fails `invalid`.
- `function fetch_model(c: Client, id: str) -> Model?`, called `openai.fetch_model(c, id)`: The model `id`. Fails `not_found`, `invalid`.


### graphql

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/graphql`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/graphql/).

GraphQL, as its specification of October 2021 writes it and as its working draft has settled since (`@oneOf` input objects, Unicode escapes past U+FFFF, the check that an operation's kind exists): a document's text parsed into operations and fragments, a schema's text parsed into a schema, a document validated against a schema by every rule of the specification's section 5, and an operation executed with the program answering every field, its result and its errors the specification's JSON response.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of a text that does not parse, a schema or a document that breaks a rule, and a request or a message that is not what GraphQL sends.
- `constant LIMIT: str`, value `"limit"`: The code of a text past what `Limits` allows.
- `constant NOT_FOUND: str`, value `"not_found"`: The code of an operation name a document does not hold, and of a response's `data` where execution never began.
- `constant UNSUPPORTED: str`, value `"unsupported"`: The code of an HTTP method or a media type a server refuses.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of an answer over HTTP whose status is not a success: what `call_http` fails with.
- `constant QUERY: str`, value `"query"`: The kind of an operation that reads.
- `constant MUTATION: str`, value `"mutation"`: The kind of an operation that writes, its root fields run one after another.
- `constant SUBSCRIPTION: str`, value `"subscription"`: The kind of an operation that answers each event of a stream.
- `record Limits(bytes: i64, tokens: i64, depth: i64, aliases: i64, directives: i64, fields: i64, errors: i64, introspection: bool)`: What a document may hold and ask, so that a text built to exhaust a server is refused before it runs.
- `function default_limits() -> Limits`, called `graphql.default_limits()`: The usual limits: a text of at most 1 MiB and 20,000 tokens, 64 levels, 500 aliases, 50 directives on one place, 20,000 fields and 100 errors, and introspection allowed.
- `record Location(line: i64, column: i64)`: A place in a text: where an error was found.
- `record Error(message: str, locations: [Location], path: [json.Value], extensions: json.Value)`: An error as a GraphQL response carries it.
- `record Schema(model: model.Model)`: A schema: its types, its directives and its roots, checked by every rule of the specification's type system.
- `function parse_schema(text: str, limits: Limits) -> Schema?`, called `graphql.parse_schema(text, limits)`: The schema `text` writes, in the schema definition language. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function extend_schema(schema: Schema, text: str, limits: Limits) -> Schema?`, called `graphql.extend_schema(schema, text, limits)`: `schema` with the definitions and extensions of `text` added. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function format_schema(schema: Schema) -> str`, called `graphql.format_schema(schema)`: `schema` written in the schema definition language, as graphql-js's `printSchema` writes it: the types the program defined in their order, the specified scalars, directives and the introspection types left out.
- `function introspection_of(schema: Schema) -> json.Value`, called `graphql.introspection_of(schema)`: What the specification's introspection query answers about `schema`: the `data` of a response to `introspection_query`, as graphql-js's `introspectionFromSchema` answers it.
- `function schema_from_introspection(data: json.Value, limits: Limits) -> Schema?`, called `graphql.schema_from_introspection(data, limits)`: The schema an answer to `introspection_query` describes, as a client builds it from a server's answer: graphql-js's `buildClientSchema`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function introspection_query() -> str`, called `graphql.introspection_query()`: The introspection query of graphql-js's `getIntrospectionQuery` with every option on: descriptions, the schema's own, `specifiedByURL`, repeatable directives and deprecated arguments and input fields.
- `record Document(tree: tree.Tree)`: A document parsed: its operations, its fragments and any other definition it holds, kept with its text so that an error can name its line.
- `record Operation(kind: str, name: str, variables: [Variable])`: What `operations_of` answers about one operation.
- `record Variable(name: str, type: str, has_default: bool)`: A variable an operation defines.
- `function parse(text: str, limits: Limits) -> Document?`, called `graphql.parse(text, limits)`: The document `text` writes. Fails `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function format(document: Document) -> str`, called `graphql.format(document)`: `document` written as graphql-js's `print` writes it: two spaces a level, one selection a line, the definitions a blank line apart, the comments and the commas left out.
- `function operations_of(document: Document) -> [Operation]`, called `graphql.operations_of(document)`: The operations `document` holds, in their order.
- `function validate(schema: Schema, document: Document, limits: Limits) -> [Error]`, called `graphql.validate(schema, document, limits)`: The errors of `document` against `schema` by every rule of the specification's section 5, in graphql-js's words and order: none where it is valid.
- `function validate_with(schema: Schema, document: Document, limits: Limits, rules: [str]) -> [Error]`, called `graphql.validate_with(schema, document, limits, rules)`: The errors of `document` against `schema` by the rules `rules` names alone.
- `function rule_names() -> [str]`, called `graphql.rule_names()`: The names of the rules `validate` runs, in the order it runs them.
- `record Request(query: str, operation_name: str, variables: json.Value, extensions: json.Value)`: What a client asks of a server: the parameters GraphQL over HTTP names.
- `record Response(data: json.Value?, errors: [Error], extensions: json.Value)`: What a server answers: the specification's response.
- `function parse_request(text: str) -> Request?`, called `graphql.parse_request(text)`: The request a JSON body writes, as GraphQL over HTTP sends it by `POST`. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_request(r: Request) -> str?`, called `graphql.format_request(r)`: `r` written as the JSON body GraphQL over HTTP sends, its members in the order `query`, `operationName`, `variables`, `extensions`, each but `query` left out where it is empty. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function parse_response(text: str) -> Response?`, called `graphql.parse_response(text)`: The response a JSON text writes, as a client reads a server's answer. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_response(response: Response) -> str?`, called `graphql.format_response(response)`: `response` written as JSON, its members in the order graphql-js writes them: `errors` where there are any, `data` where execution began, then `extensions`; each error's `message`, `locations`, `path` and `extensions`. Fails `unsupported`.
- `function request_of(v: json.Value) -> Request?`, called `graphql.request_of(v)`: The request the JSON value `v` writes, as `parse_request` reads a body: what a transport reads that carries requests inside its own messages. Fails `invalid`.
- `function request_json(r: Request) -> json.Value`, called `graphql.request_json(r)`: `r` as a JSON value, as `format_request` writes it.
- `function response_of(v: json.Value) -> Response?`, called `graphql.response_of(v)`: The response the JSON value `v` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function response_json(response: Response) -> json.Value`, called `graphql.response_json(response)`: `response` as a JSON value, its members in graphql-js's order: `errors` where there are any, `data` where execution began, then `extensions`.
- `function error_of(v: json.Value) -> Error?`, called `graphql.error_of(v)`: The error the JSON value `v` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function error_json(e: Error) -> json.Value`, called `graphql.error_json(e)`: `e` as a JSON value: `message`, then `locations`, `path` and `extensions` where it has them.
- `record Execution(state: exec.State)`: An operation being executed: what is answered so far and what waits.
- `record Field(id: i64, type_name: str, field_name: str, arguments: {str: json.Value}, parent: json.Value, path: [json.Value], return_type: str)`: A field the program is asked to resolve.
- `variant Step = .resolve(fields: [Field]) | .done(response: Response)`: What `next_step` answers: fields to resolve, or the response.
- `function start(schema: Schema, r: Request, root: json.Value, limits: Limits) -> Execution`, called `graphql.start(schema, r, root, limits)`: An execution of the operation `r` asks for, its document parsed and validated and its variables coerced.
- `function start_document(schema: Schema, document: Document, operation_name: str, variables: json.Value, root: json.Value, limits: Limits) -> Execution`, called `graphql.start_document(schema, document, operation_name, variables: variables, root: root, limits)`: An execution of an operation of a document already parsed, as a server that keeps its documents (persisted queries) runs it: validated, its variables coerced.
- `function next_step(@e: Execution) -> Step`, called `graphql.next_step(@e)`: The next step of `e`: the fields ready to be resolved, or the response.
- `function answer(@e: Execution, answers: [json.Value?])`, called `graphql.answer(@e, answers)`: Gives `e` the answers to the fields of its last step.
- `function selected_of(e: Execution, field: Field) -> [str]`, called `graphql.selected_of(e, field)`: The names of the fields selected below `field`, so that its resolver loads only what is asked: each once, in the order the document selects them, `__typename` among them, over every type an interface's or a union's value can be.
- `function execute(schema: Schema, r: Request, root: json.Value, limits: Limits, resolver: (function(Field) -> json.Value?)) -> Response`, called `graphql.execute(schema, r, root, limits, resolver)`: The response to `r`, every field `resolver` must answer handed to it.
- `function execute_with<S>(schema: Schema, r: Request, root: json.Value, limits: Limits, state: S, resolver: (function(S, Field) -> json.Value?)) -> Response`, called `graphql.execute_with(schema, r, root, limits, state, resolver)`: The response to `r`, every field handed to `resolver` with the program's own value.
- `variant Subscribed = .stream(field_name: str, arguments: {str: json.Value}) | .refused(response: Response)`: What `subscribe` answers: the source stream to open, or why none opens.
- `function subscribe(schema: Schema, r: Request, limits: Limits) -> Subscribed`, called `graphql.subscribe(schema, r, limits)`: The source stream a subscription asks for: its root field and its arguments, the specification's `CreateSourceEventStream`.
- `function start_event(schema: Schema, r: Request, event: json.Value, limits: Limits) -> Execution`, called `graphql.start_event(schema, r, event, limits)`: An execution of the subscription `r` asks for over one event of its stream, the specification's `ExecuteSubscriptionEvent`: the root field is resolved with `event` as its parent.
- `function read_http(r: http.Request, limits: Limits) -> Request?`, called `graphql.read_http(r, limits)`: The request an HTTP request carries, as GraphQL over HTTP writes it: by `GET`, its parameters in the query; by `POST`, a JSON body. Fails `unsupported`, `invalid`, `limit`.
- `function respond_http(r: http.Request, response: Response) -> http.Response`, called `graphql.respond_http(r, response)`: The HTTP response that carries `response`, in the media type `r` accepts: `application/graphql-response+json`, whose status is 200 where execution began and 400 where the request was refused, or `application/json`, whose status is 200 either way.
- `function refusal_http(r: http.Request, code: str, msg: str) -> http.Response`, called `graphql.refusal_http(r, code: code, msg: msg)`: The HTTP response to a request `read_http` refused.
- `function serve_http<S>(r: http.Request, schema: Schema, root: json.Value, limits: Limits, state: S, resolver: (function(S, Field) -> json.Value?)) -> http.Response`, called `graphql.serve_http(r, schema, root, limits, state, resolver)`: The answer of a GraphQL server to an HTTP request, every field handed to `resolver` with the program's own value: `read_http`, `execute_with` and `respond_http` in one call.
- `function call_http(transport: http.Client, target: str, r: Request) -> Response?`, called `graphql.call_http(transport, target, r)`: Sends `r` to the server at `target` by `POST` and reads its response. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `constant WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL: str`, value `"graphql-transport-ws"`: The subprotocol a WebSocket carrying `Message`s names.
- `variant Message = .connection_init(payload: json.Value) | .connection_ack(payload: json.Value) | .ping(payload: json.Value) | .pong(payload: json.Value) | .subscribe(id: str, request: Request) | .next(id: str, response: Response) | .error(id: str, errors: [Error]) | .complete(id: str)`: A message of the `graphql-transport-ws` protocol, a text frame each.
- `function parse_message(text: str) -> Message?`, called `graphql.parse_message(text)`: The message `text` writes. Fails `invalid`.
- `function format_message(m: Message) -> str?`, called `graphql.format_message(m)`: `m` written as a text frame's text. Fails `unsupported`.


### otlp

Layer 7, named `use <rebel>/otlp`, [its reference](https://heroes-lang.org/rebel/otlp/).

OpenTelemetry's protocol, OTLP 1.x over HTTP with protobuf: the attributes, the resource and the instrumentation scope every signal's request carries; an exporter, which posts a request to a collector and sends it again as OTLP's specification asks; and the pieces a signal's request is written with, on `protobuf`'s wire, so the bytes are those Python's `opentelemetry-proto` writes for the same message.

- `constant INVALID: str`, value `"invalid"`: The code of an environment variable that is not the format, and of a collector's answer that is no protobuf message: `resource_from_env`, `exporter_from_env`, `export`.
- `constant FAILED: str`, value `"failed"`: The code of a collector that answered a status other than 2xx after every retry: `export`.
- `variant AttributeValue = .text(v: str) | .boolean(v: bool) | .integer(v: i64) | .number(v: f64) | .texts(v: [str])`: What an attribute holds, as OTLP's `AnyValue` does.
- `record Attribute(key: str, value: AttributeValue)`: An attribute: a key and its value, `service.name` and `checkout`, of a resource, a span, an event, a link or a log record.
- `record Scope(name: str, version: str)`: The instrumentation scope a request names: the library or program that recorded what it carries.
- `function resource_from_env(service: str) -> [Attribute]?`, called `otlp.resource_from_env(service)`: A resource as OpenTelemetry's environment variables describe it: `service.name` from `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, else from `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, else `service`; then every other `key=value` pair of `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, between commas, trimmed and percent-decoded, each a text, as Python's SDK reads them. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `variant Signal = .metrics | .traces | .logs`: Which of OTLP's signals an exporter sends, and so the path it posts to.
- `constant METRICS_URL: str`, value `"http://localhost:4318/v1/metrics"`: The URL OTLP's metrics are posted to where nothing else says: the collector on this machine.
- `constant TRACES_URL: str`, value `"http://localhost:4318/v1/traces"`: The URL OTLP's spans are posted to where nothing else says.
- `constant LOGS_URL: str`, value `"http://localhost:4318/v1/logs"`: The URL OTLP's log records are posted to where nothing else says.
- `record Exporter(client: http.Client, url: str, headers: [http.Header], gzip: bool, retries: http.Retries)`: Where and how OTLP requests are sent over HTTP.
- `function exporter_to(target: str) -> Exporter`, called `otlp.exporter_to(target)`: An exporter posting to `target`, uncompressed, with no field of its own, sending again 3 times after a status of 429, 502, 503 or 504, from 1 second doubled up to 30, as OTLP's specification asks.
- `function exporter_from_env(signal: Signal) -> Exporter?`, called `otlp.exporter_from_env(signal)`: An exporter of `signal` as OpenTelemetry's environment variables describe it: `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT` (or `_TRACES_`, `_LOGS_`) taken whole, or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` with `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/traces` or `/v1/logs` after it, or the signal's URL on this machine; the fields of `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` and its kin of the signal, `key=value` pairs between commas, each percent-decoded; gzip where `_COMPRESSION` or its kin says `gzip`; and the milliseconds of `_TIMEOUT` or its kin as the client's deadline. Fails `invalid`, `not_found`.
- `record Exported(rejected: i64, message: str)`: The outcome of an export a collector accepted: how much of it it refused none the less, and why.
- `function export(exporter: Exporter, body: [u8]) -> Exported?`, called `otlp.export(exporter, body)`: Posts `body`, an OTLP request, to `exporter`'s URL as `application/x-protobuf`, and sends it again as `exporter.retries` says. Fails `failed`, `invalid`.
- `function value_bytes(value: AttributeValue, length: i64) -> [u8]`, called `otlp.value_bytes(value, length)`: `value` as OTLP's `AnyValue`, the bytes a log record's body is written as, and an attribute's value.
- `function attribute_bytes(a: Attribute, length: i64) -> [u8]`, called `otlp.attribute_bytes(a, length)`: `a` as OTLP's `KeyValue`, its value an `AnyValue`, the bytes a signal's request writes for an attribute of its resource, a span, an event, a link, a log record or a point.
